pages.title: Base Designs
pages.body:
# Base Designs

How to pick, size, and judge a base in current-era (2025–2026) Rust. This folder covers the whole arc of a wipe: [[Starter Bases]] → [[Solo Bases]] / [[Duo Bases]] / [[Trio Bases]] / [[Group Bases]] → [[Expansion and Compound Design]]. Core concepts live in [[Open Core vs Closed Core]] and [[Bunkers]]; where to put the thing is [[Base Locations]].

## The three numbers that matter

Every design is judged on:

1. **Build cost** — can you actually farm it on day 1–2?
2. **Daily upkeep** — can you sustain it *every day* without playing Farming Simulator?
3. **Raid cost** — how much sulfur does a raider burn to reach your loot?

> A manageable 2x2 you can consistently upkeep beats a 3x3 that starts decaying mid-wipe because farming fell behind.

Rules of thumb (2026 meta):
- A good **solo** base costs ~60–120 stone/hour in upkeep, takes **30+ rockets** to crack from any angle, and has at least one [[Bunkers|bunker]] so a "successful" raid still doesn't pay.
- A 1x1 runs ~60 stone/hr upkeep, a 2x1 ~120/hr, a 2x2 hits 200+/hr. Size to your farming capacity, not your ambition.

## Building tiers — HP, cost, raid cost (re-verified Jun 13 2026)

> Cross-checked against the live **"Built Different" patch (Jun 4 2026)** — a player-model / ballistic-armor / M16A2 update that **changed no building HP, upgrade cost, door HP, or explosive damage**. Every number below is current for the June 2026 wipe.


| Wall tier | HP | Build cost | Upkeep/day | Rockets | C4 | Satchels | Explo 5.56 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stone | 500 | 300 stone | 30–99 stone | 4 | 2 | 10 (4 soft-side) | 185 |
| Sheet Metal | 1,000 | 200 frags | 20–66 frags | 8 | 4 | 23 | 400 |
| Armored | 2,000 | 25 HQM | 2–8 HQM | 15 | 8 | 46 | 799 |

Sulfur cost of one breach (rocket path): stone wall ≈ 5,600 sulfur, sheet metal wall ≈ 10,175 sulfur, armored wall ≈ 21,000 sulfur. Soft-side stone is the classic cheap entry (4 satchels) — always face hard side out and check soft sides on honeycomb.

Wood tier exists but is a day-1-only material: it burns, and its soft side can be melee'd down. Get to stone before your first sleep.

## Doors (verified vs rusthelp.com)

| Door | HP | Cost | WB tier | Cheapest kill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Sheet Metal Door]] | 250 | 150 frags | none | 1 C4 / 2 rockets / 4 satchels / 63 explo ammo |
| [[Garage Door]] | 600 | 300 frags + 2 gears | T2 | 2 C4 (4,400 sulfur) / 3 rockets / 150 explo ammo (3,750 sulfur) |
| [[Armored Door]] | 1,000 | 20 HQM + 5 gears | T3 | 3 C4 (6,600 sulfur) / 5 rockets / 250 explo ammo |

Garage doors are the workhorse: no weak side, 600 HP, cheap. Armored doors go on TC room and core last.

## Upkeep and decay (the tax system)

- The [[Tool Cupboard]] (craft: **1,000 wood**) drains materials every 24h proportional to what your base is made of.
- Small bases (≤~15 building blocks) pay **~10%** of build cost per day. Past ~16 blocks the rate climbs, scaling up to **~33%** for very large bases (rusthelp's per-block upkeep ranges — e.g. 30–99 stone on a 300-stone wall — confirm the 10%→33% spread). A ~68-block base lands around a **14% effective rate**.
- When TC runs dry, decay starts: **twig 1h, wood 3h, stone 5h, sheet metal 8h, armored 12h** to fully collapse (official wiki).
- If raiders destroy a stocked TC, up to 24h of stored upkeep is consumed as grief protection — your base doesn't instantly start rotting.

**Practical upshot:** armored honeycomb is an upkeep trap (HQM/day) for small groups. Standard meta is stone shell, metal core/key walls, armored only on TC room and bunker cell.

## Choosing a design — decision table

| You are | Hours/day | Build | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anyone, hour 0 of wipe | — | 2x1 with airlock | [[Starter Bases]] |
| Solo, casual | 1–3 | 2x1/2x2 bunker, closed core | [[Solo Bases]] |
| Solo, sweaty | 4+ | 2x1 open core w/ shooting floor | [[Solo Bases]], [[Open Core vs Closed Core]] |
| Duo | 2–4 | 2x2 open core or stability bunker | [[Duo Bases]] |
| Trio | 3+ | 2x2/3x3 hybrid, Frustrator-style loot rooms | [[Trio Bases]] |
| 4–8 players | farm team | Multi-TC fortress + compound | [[Group Bases]], [[Expansion and Compound Design]] |

## What changed since 2023 (if you're returning)

- **Mortars (May 2026 update):** Workbench T2 HE/fragmentation mortars lob shells **over** [[High External Stone Wall|high external walls]] from outside your TC bubble. Tall-wall compounds are no longer a hard shield; compact bases and roofed walkways are in. See [[Expansion and Compound Design]].
- **Explosive protection is capped at 75%** (May 2025) — no more unkillable raid tanks.
- **Auto turret interference:** max **12 active turrets within a 40 m radius** (vanilla `sentry.maxinterference`). Turret walls are dead; smart placement isn't.
- **Open core** became the dominant active-player meta (defend from height, not wall count) — see [[Open Core vs Closed Core]].
- Siege weapons (Feb 2025: Catapult, Ballista, Battering Ram, Siege Tower) added a third raid path besides boom and door-camping; many 2025+ designs advertise "anti-siege" rooflines.
- [[Backpacks]] drop on death — raid defense now showers loot; hoppers (Mar 2025) auto-collect it.

## Sources

rusthelp.com (wall/door/turret stat pages), wiki.facepunch.com (Tool Cupboard), switchbladegaming.com, xgamingserver.com, corrosionhour.com, cobaltlab.tech, rustbases.gg, rustbaselab.com, frozen-rust.com, bisecthosting.com, Evil Wurst's base catalog (sites.google.com/view/evilwurstsbases).

pages.title: Base Locations
pages.body:
# Base Locations

Where you build matters as much as what you build. A perfect [[Solo Bases|solo design]] on the beach gets door-camped to death by everyone who spawns; a mediocre one tucked into a forest cliff survives the wipe. This page covers biome trade-offs, the **T1-monument ring** concept, terrain spots, and the placement mistakes that end wipes early. Pairs with [[Base Designs]] (what to build) and [[Expansion and Compound Design]] (how to grow once placed).

> [!note] Returning-player context
> **World Update 2.0 (Oct 2024)** regenerated all terrain — new cliffs, canyons, lakes, oases. The **Jungle biome (May 2025)** added a whole new low-tier zone. Rivers everywhere are wider/deeper now (you swim to cross). So old "spots" you remember from 2023 are gone; learn the map each wipe.

## The core trade-off

Every location balances two opposing pressures:

| Pull toward... | Because | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Near a monument** | Fast loot, fast recycler runs, quick scrap | High foot traffic = you're seen, scouted, raided |
| **Away from everything** | Stealth, fewer raiders, peaceful farm | Long runs to loot; if found while offline, no neighbors to deter the raid |

For a returning solo/duo/trio, the sweet spot is the **T1 ring**: close enough to a *low-tier* monument to farm components efficiently, far enough from *high-tier* monuments and the map's open core that you're not in everyone's path.

## The monument-tier ring concept

Build near monuments that match your skill and threat tolerance:

| Tier | Monuments | Who farms there | Build nearby if... |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 (low)** | [[Gas Station]], [[Supermarket]], [[Mining Outpost]], [[Lighthouse]], small [[Harbor]] | Fresh spawns, solos | You want safe early components + recycler — the returning-player default |
| **T2 (mid)** | [[Water Treatment]], [[Train Yard]], [[Power Plant]], [[Airfield]], [[Sewer Branch]] | Geared solos/duos | You can fight for it; better comps, more traffic |
| **T3 (high)** | [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Arctic Research Base]], [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] | Squads, sweats | You're a confident group looking for endgame loot + keycard runs |

> The T2 recycler now runs a **5s cycle at 120% yield** vs the safe-zone recycler's **8s / 80%** (May 2024 split) — building near a monument recycler is faster *and* more efficient than running to [[Outpost]]. That raised the value of a T1-ring spot.

## Biome trade-offs

### Snow (Arctic)
- **Pros:** Metal and sulfur nodes are denser than elsewhere; lower population = often peaceful. **Ice lakes** are perfectly flat — they fit any footprint.
- **Cons:** Cold damage without clothing/fire; scarce food; resources spread out; boats don't spawn in winter. Ice lakes draw big groups; **icebergs** are defensible (water moat) but cramped past a trio.
- **Verdict:** strong **stealth solo** biome if you can manage cold. Build at the snow/forest edge for food access.

### Desert
- **Pros:** Great stone and metal; low player traffic; **hoodoo rock formations** give natural camouflage for hidden bases; pigs (furnace fuel/food) are common.
- **Cons:** Historically wood-scarce (QoL has eased this); open sightlines mean a found base has no cover.
- **Verdict:** best **balance of resources + low encounters**; a solid solo/duo pick. Build against a hoodoo or cliff, not in the open dunes.

### Temperate / Forest
- **Pros:** Best wood; dense trees hide bases and let you camouflage; mountain-base spots give wood + stone in one farm circuit.
- **Cons:** Competitors harvest the same wood; easy to lose your own base in thick woods (note coordinates!).
- **Verdict:** the all-rounder. **Base of a mountain near woods** is the classic balanced spot.

### Jungle (May 2025, tier-0 zones)
- **Pros:** Dense canopy hides bases from ground *and* air; **riverbank crocodiles/predators** deter water approaches; scarce nodes mean enemies don't loiter; [[Ziggurat]] + [[Jungle Ruins]] nearby for loot.
- **Cons:** Predators (tigers, panthers, snakes) are a real PvE threat — prep before settling; low resource density means longer farm runs.
- **Verdict:** novel **stealth** option; the predator AI works *for* you defensively.

## Terrain spot types

| Spot | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| **Cliffside / overhang** | Hidden, foundation tucked into rock denies raid angles | Limited footprint; weak online defense (fewer peeks); 1x1/2x1 only |
| **Mountain base** | Wood + stone in one circuit; cover | Can be summit-camped from above |
| **Waterfront** | Boat/[[Tugboat]] access, endgame water content, [[Cargo Ship]] | Obvious target; **submarine torpedo** + naval-cannon raid vector since the Feb 2026 Naval Update |
| **Summit** | Visibility, roof-camp angles | MLRS-vulnerable; brutal travel; assumes you roof-camp |
| **Cave** | Cheap early shelter | High foot traffic, expensive food, tiny build radius |
| **Island** | Isolated, harder to reach | Limited resources; offline-raid magnet; [[Cargo Ship]] exposure |
| **Roadside / train track** | Fast resource/road loot | High visibility; door-camp central; never sleep here |

## Placement rules

1. **Never the open beach or a road.** You will be door-camped by every spawn. The single most common returning-player death.
2. **Put a wall or cliff at your back** — denies raiders a 360° approach and cuts the faces they can splash.
3. **Check sightlines to nearby monuments** — you want to *see* people coming, not have a sniper tower overlooking your loot room.
4. **Water within a short run** (Mar 2025 food spoilage + drinking) but not *on* the shore unless you want naval raids.
5. **Leave a 15% expansion buffer** — don't wedge into a gap you can't grow out of ([[Expansion and Compound Design]]).
6. **Don't build under a recycler/safe-zone** sightline where roof campers farm you.
7. **Stealth beats walls early.** A base nobody finds is never raided; a visible base is raided eventually regardless of rocket cost.

## Solo/duo/trio TL;DR for Josia

- **Stealth solo:** snow edge or jungle riverbank, cliff at your back, [[Solo Bases|2x1 bunker]].
- **Efficient duo:** desert hoodoo or forest mountain in the **T1 ring** (Gas Station / Mining Outpost), [[Duo Bases|2x2]].
- **Aggressive trio:** forest near a **T2** (Water Treatment / Train Yard) you intend to fight over, [[Trio Bases|open-core 2x2]] — but only if you'll be online to hold it.

## Sources
CorrosionHour building-location guide, GamerRant best-build-spots, ScalaCube location guide, FalconRust base-spots guide; biome/recycler/naval changes cross-checked against the 2023→2026 returning-player brief.

pages.title: Building Basics
pages.body:
# Building Basics

How you go from nothing to a metal box: the Building Plan, the Hammer, and the upgrade-grade ladder.

## The two core tools

| Tool | Craft cost | What it does |
|------|-----------|--------------|
| **Building Plan** | 20 wood | Places building blocks (foundations, walls, floors, frames, roofs, stairs). You select the piece from a radial menu, then place it as **twig**. Costs the listed twig material per piece. |
| **Hammer** | 100 wood | Upgrades placed pieces through the grade ladder, rotates/picks up freshly placed pieces (10-minute window), and shows stability/info on hover. |

Both are craftable from the start with no workbench. The **Garry's Mod-style** flow: place with the Plan, then walk around hitting pieces with the Hammer and selecting the grade.

## The building-block primer

Building blocks (the structural pieces, not deployables) are placed via the Building Plan and snap to a grid:

- **Foundation** — the ground piece everything snaps to. Square or **triangle**. Foundations are 100% stability (see [[Stability]]).
- **Wall** — vertical block on a foundation edge. Has a [[Soft Side|hard side and a soft side]].
- **Floor / Ceiling** — horizontal block; doubles as the ceiling of the room below and floor of the room above.
- **Wall Frame** — a wall with a hole you fill (door, window, garage, embrasure — see [[Doors and Locks]] and [[Windows Shutters and Frames]]).
- **Doorway** — a wall with a person-sized opening, fits a door.
- **Window** — a wall with a window slot.
- **Roof** — sloped triangular/square top piece for [[Roof Access and Peaks|peaks]].
- **Stairs** — L-shape, U-shape, and **spiral** stairs for vertical movement.

## The grade ladder (verified HP and upgrade cost)

Every block starts as **twig** and is upgraded with the Hammer. HP values are for a standard **wall**; foundations/floors are in the same ballpark per grade. Upgrade cost is a **range** because larger pieces (square wall vs triangle, foundation vs floor) cost different amounts — the table shows the per-piece range.

| Grade | Wall HP | Upgrade cost (per piece range) | Decay time (no upkeep) | Notes |
|-------|--------:|-------------------------------|-----------------------:|-------|
| **Twig** | 10 | free (placed by Building Plan) | ~1 hour | Raidable by hand/hatchet. Never leave twig overnight. |
| **Wood** | 250 | 50–200 wood | 3 hours | First real upgrade. Still cheap to raid (fire/satchels). |
| **Stone** | 500 | 75–300 stone | 5 hours | The standard early-wipe wall. Has a meaningful [[Soft Side|soft side]]. |
| **Sheet Metal** | 1000 | 50–200 metal fragments | 8 hours | Mid-wipe standard. Near-immune to melee from the hard side. |
| **Armored** | 2000 | 7–25 HQM (High Quality Metal) | 12 hours | Endgame. Explosives only realistically. |

A **stone wall** = 300 stone to upgrade (the high end of the range, since it's a full square wall). A **stone foundation** is in the same 75–300 band. Triangles cost roughly 50% of the square equivalent.

### How damage scales

Each grade roughly doubles the HP of the last, but the **raid cost scales much faster than HP** because explosives have a damage type that armored/sheet metal resist. This is why armored is worth the HQM despite "only" 2x the HP of sheet metal — see [[Raid Costs]] for the rocket/C4/satchel tables per grade.

## Workflow tips

- **Upgrade in order**: you cannot skip grades — you go twig -> wood -> stone -> sheet -> armored, paying each step. Plan resources accordingly (going straight to stone on a 1x1 = ~3000 stone for the shell).
- **Pick-up window**: a freshly placed block can be picked back up with the Hammer for ~10 minutes if it's still twig and you have building privilege. After upgrading, you can no longer pick it up — only demolish (and demolish is only allowed within ~10 min of placement, or never on most vanilla servers).
- **Twig is a planning tool**: place your whole base in twig first to check the layout and [[Stability]], then mass-upgrade.
- Always keep the **soft side inward** ([[Soft Side]]) and drop a stocked **[[Tool Cupboard]]** before you log off.

## Related

[[Upkeep and Decay]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Stability]] · [[Soft Side]] · [[Doors and Locks]] · [[Base Designs]] · [[Raid Costs]]

pages.title: Building Mechanics
pages.body:
# Building Mechanics

The construction system in Rust: how you place, upgrade, support, defend, and maintain a base. This folder is the durable reference for everything structural. For finished base layouts see [[Base Designs]]; for how raiders break in see [[Raiding]] and [[Raid Costs]].

## Pages in this folder

- [[Building Basics]] — Building Plan, Hammer, grade ladder (twig -> wood -> stone -> sheet metal -> armored) with HP and upgrade cost per grade.
- [[Upkeep and Decay]] — exact upkeep tax brackets, per-grade decay timers, the 24h grief-protection grace period.
- [[Tool Cupboard]] — building privilege, authorization, 16m clearance, 24 upkeep slots, how upkeep is paid.
- [[Soft Side]] — hard vs soft side, which placements expose the weak face, the melee-raid implications.
- [[Stability]] — how blocks lose stability with height/unsupported span, what holds a structure up, collapse.
- [[Doors and Locks]] — every door type with HP/cost/raid cost, Code Lock vs Key Lock.
- [[Windows Shutters and Frames]] — wall frames and the five fillings (bars, glass, embrasures, shutters), window frame items.
- [[Deployables]] — storage boxes, furnaces, shelves, lockers, sleeping bags, and the 2024+ additions (backpacks, wallpaper, mini fridge, hoppers).
- [[Bunkers]] — the bunker catalog: which designs still work in 2026 and which are patched.
- [[Roof Access and Peaks]] — roof peaks, anti-roof-camp design, non-ladderable holes, peek-downs.

## The 30-second mental model

1. Place a **foundation** with the [[Building Basics|Building Plan]], then walls/floors snapping off it. New pieces start as **twig** (free-ish, 10 HP, raidable by hand).
2. Hit each piece with the **Hammer** and upgrade it through the grade ladder. **Stone** (500 HP) is the standard early-wipe wall; **sheet metal** (1000 HP) is mid-wipe; **armored** (2000 HP) is endgame.
3. Drop a **[[Tool Cupboard]]** inside and fill it with materials — without a stocked TC the base decays immediately. The TC also gates who can build/upgrade/pick up within ~16m.
4. Keep the **[[Soft Side]]** of every wall facing **inward**. A soft-sided exterior wall can be melee-raided for a fraction of the cost.
5. Use **[[Stability]]** rules to keep upper floors from collapsing, and **[[Roof Access and Peaks]]** design so nobody can ladder/boost onto your roof.

## Returning-player note (2023 -> 2026)

Core building HP and grades are unchanged. What changed around building:
- **Blueprint Fragments** gate Workbench tiers now (see [[Getting Started]] / [[Progression]]) — but the building-block BPs themselves are default/cheap to research after the Nov 2025 cost cut.
- **Wallpaper** (Sep 2024) is now a deployable on walls. **Mini Fridge** (18 slots) and **hoppers** (auto-loot) were added with the Mar 2025 Crafting Update.
- **Armored Triangle Ladder Hatch** added Apr 2026 (Spring Clean) — top-tier vertical-access piece.
- **Naval Update** (Feb 2026) added water-placed Boat Building Stations and modular ship hull blocks — a parallel build system, covered under [[Vehicles]], not here.
- Garage doors and bunkers still work, but **explosive protection is now capped at 75%** (May 2025), which changes raid math more than build math.

_Numbers on these pages are verified against rusthelp.com (RustLabs successor), wiki.facepunch.com, and current 2026 guides. Where two sources disagree (e.g. Armored Door HP), the page flags it._

pages.title: Bunkers
pages.body:
# Bunkers

A **bunker** is any sealed room with **no walkable door** — the only way in is to **drop through a hatch** or **briefly remove a floor/wall piece** that you put back behind you. The point: a raider can't door-camp or just blow one door to reach your [[Tool Cupboard|TC]]/loot. To raid a true bunker you must break the **shell** (lots of explosives), not pick a lock. This is the backbone of modern solo/duo/trio defense in 2026.

## What makes a bunker work

- The core room has **no door** — entry is vertical (hatch) or a **removable block**.
- The TC and loot sit inside, surrounded by [[Soft Side|honeycomb]] so no [[Soft Side|soft side]] is reachable from outside.
- Getting in is a small ritual (open hatch / pop a block) that an attacker can't replicate without first breaking through.

## Bunker types — and 2026 status

| Type | How it works | 2026 status |
|------|--------------|-------------|
| **Garage-door bunker** | A 1x1 (or vehicle bay) sealed by a **[[Doors and Locks|garage door]]** in a wall frame; you roll it up to enter, it rolls flush with no gap and **can't be splash-damaged through the adjacent walls**. Often a vehicle bay sitting inside the TC bubble but outside the main honeycomb. | **WORKS.** Standard, intended mechanic. The reliable, no-exploit bunker. |
| **Hatch / floor-drop bunker** | Core room reached by a **ladder hatch** in the ceiling/floor; you drop in, hatch closes. Modern version uses the **Armored Triangle Ladder Hatch** (Apr 2026, Spring Clean) for max durability. | **WORKS.** Intended. The Apr 2026 hatch makes this stronger than ever. |
| **Triangle drop-down / jump-up bunker** | Two half-walls + a **triangle floor drop-down**; you drop through a triangle gap into the sealed core and climb back via half-walls/furnaces as jump-ups. (Rocketnode's 2026 "spiral stair bunker" is a variant — half walls + triangle drop + spiral staircase to seal.) | **WORKS** as a build pattern in 2026 guides — but exact viability shifts patch-to-patch as Facepunch adjusts jump-up heights. Verify the half-wall/jump-up combo in-game on the current patch. |
| **Wall-stack / "shoot-through honeycomb" bunker** | Triple-honeycomb cores (e.g. the 2026 "DICEPT" triple bunker) bury the core behind multiple wall layers with a removable-block entry. | **WORKS** — current meta for solo/duo open-core anti-door-camp bases. |
| **Stability bunker (old)** | Abused [[Stability]]: place a block, remove its support so stability lets you pick it up / drop a "lid," sealing a room with no door. | **MOSTLY PATCHED / unreliable.** Facepunch has repeatedly nerfed pick-up windows and stability tricks. Do **not** rely on a classic stability bunker in 2026 — use a garage-door or hatch bunker instead. |
| **TC-less / no-cupboard exploit (very old)** | Building without a TC to dodge upkeep/auth rules. | **DEAD.** Patched years ago; a TC-less base decays immediately ([[Upkeep and Decay]]). |

**Bottom line for a 2026 returning player:** build a **garage-door bunker** or an **(armored triangle) ladder-hatch bunker** — both are intended mechanics and rock-solid. Treat any "stability/pick-up trick" bunker from old YouTube videos as suspect until you test it on the live patch.

**Patch check (Jun 13 2026):** the current live patch is **"Built Different" (Jun 4 2026)** — a player-model / ballistic-armor / M16A2 update with **no changes to stability, hatches, garage doors, or any bunker-relevant mechanic**. Garage-door and ladder-hatch bunkers are confirmed intended and unaffected this patch. The only standing caution is the recurring **stability-trick / "God Bunker" cycle** (those get nerfed unpredictably on first-Thursday building passes), so the verify-on-a-build-server rule still applies before every wipe.

## Anti-door-camp angle

The reason bunkers dominate solo/duo play: a normal door lets an enemy **camp your doorway** and kill you every time you peek out. A bunker has **no exterior door to camp** — you enter from inside the shell, and an "open core" design lets you shoot out at campers from multiple angles. Pair with [[Roof Access and Peaks|peek-downs]] for a base that's miserable to camp.

## Build cautions

- **Honeycomb the core fully** — a bunker is worthless if a raider can [[Soft Side|soft-side]] the floor/wall of the core from an adjacent gap.
- **Protect the TC room specifically** — once a raider reaches the [[Tool Cupboard]] they Clear-list and own the base. The TC should be the deepest, most-honeycombed point.
- **Mind the new raid tools**: since Apr 30 2026, **HE/fragmentation mortars unlock at WB2** and can **lob shells over a compound wall from outside your TC bubble** — bunkers protect against entry but not against artillery raining on exposed roofs/walls. See [[Raiding]].
- **Explosive protection is capped at 75%** (May 2025) — you can't make a wall functionally unraidable, only expensive. Bunkers raise the *cost/time* to reach loot, they don't make you immune.

## Related

[[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Soft Side]] · [[Stability]] · [[Doors and Locks]] · [[Roof Access and Peaks]] · [[Raiding]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Bunkers
pages.body:
# Bunkers

> **Patch status (Jun 13 2026):** the live **"Built Different" patch (Jun 4 2026)** touched no stability, hatch, garage-door or pixel-gap mechanic. Garage-door and ladder-hatch (incl. the Apr 2026 armored triangle hatch) bunkers are confirmed intended and working this wipe; stability-trick / "God Bunker" cells remain the patch-volatile category — verify those on a build server every first Thursday. For the mechanic-level overview see the building-folder [[Bunkers]] page.

A **bunker** is any sealed room with no walkable door — the only way in is to drop through a hatch or briefly open/remove a structural piece that outsiders can't. The point: even a fully successful door-raid becomes a **partial raid**. Your blueprints, boom stash, and a re-kit survive, and you're back in the fight the same evening. Every serious 2025–2026 design ([[Solo Bases]] through [[Group Bases]]) carries at least one; Crow's CTHULHU runs three, Limi Lab's NYXAR seven.

## The economics

A bunker forces raiders to pay **twice**: once to reach the cell, once to open it — and the second payment is usually an [[Base Designs|armored wall (15 rockets / ~21,000 sulfur)]] or a full floor/ceiling set with no door to cheese. Most raids are budgeted to the gram of sulfur; the bunker is what makes them leave with half.

## Families of bunker (current era)

### 1. Stability bunkers

Exploit the stability system: the bunker cell is sealed by a wall/floor piece whose **support chain you control**. To open, you demolish or destroy a cheap "key" piece (often a twig or low-tier block elsewhere), which makes the sealing piece lose stability and collapse; to close, you rebuild the key piece. Classic implementations seal the TC/loot room behind a wall that has no hammer access from outside.

- Used by: Evil Wurst's Serenity, Viking, "Stability 2x2" (with underground basement cell)
- Cost to operate: one cheap block per open/close
- Risk: stability rules are **the most patched system in the game** — verify on a build server every month

### 2. Drop-down / sealed-hatch bunkers

A cell reachable only from above through a ladder hatch or drop chute, with the vertical path sealed or trap-rigged.

- **Ladder Hatch** (verified rusthelp.com): 250 HP, WB T2, costs 1 wooden ladder + 300 frags + 3 gears, research 60 scrap. Dies to 1 C4 — so good designs put it *inside* the protected envelope, not as the outer skin.
- The Frustrator family ([[Trio Bases]]) is the weaponized version: drop chutes rigged with undrainable shotgun traps, so descending into the loot room is itself the raid cost.

### 3. Roof bunkers

Cells built into the roof structure, opened by a stability trick from the roofline. Favored by group designs because multiple cells fit one roof: Evil Wurst's Waterloo (4 separated roof bunkers) and Tycho (3 splash-separated roof bunkers — spaced so one rocket's splash can't damage two cells).

### 4. Pixel-gap / wide-gap bunkers

Geometry tricks: pieces placed so a human can't pass but you can interact/shoot through, or gaps closed by a conditional roof piece. The "9 Bunkers That Still Work in 2026" genre of build videos tracks which survive each patch — treat any specific pixel gap as **patch-volatile**.

### 5. TC ("god") bunkers

Sealing the [[Tool Cupboard]] itself so it can't be reached even after full base clear — periodically killed and revived by patches ("God Bunker is BACK" cycles on build channels, including a 2026 revival). Powerful but the most likely to be patched mid-wipe; never make it your only TC protection.

## Rules for living with bunkers

1. **Test on a build server every single wipe.** Facepunch patches building exploits monthly (first Thursday — see [[Updates]]); a patched bunker either seals you out of your own loot or quietly stops sealing at all.
2. **Bunker contents:** BPs/[[Workbench]] access kit, boom stash, 2–3 full kits, spare TC + lock. Not your daily-driver loot — opening the bunker often should be unnecessary.
3. **Wrap the cell in solid honeycomb on every face** including floor/ceiling, so a raider who breaches the level above still faces a full wall set.
4. **Don't advertise.** External texture should be indistinguishable from normal honeycomb; raiders eyeballing your base count layers.
5. **Splash-separate multiple bunkers** (Tycho pattern) — spacing is what makes cell #2 cost full price.
6. Armored tier on the cell only — 25 HQM/wall to build, 2–8 HQM/day each in upkeep ([[Base Designs]]).

## Counters (know thine enemy)

Raiders beat bunkers by: raiding **during your online window** and following you in; mapping stability chains and shooting the key block themselves (bad bunkers have externally-damageable keys); or simply taking the unbunkered 80% and leaving. A bunker is loss-limitation, not invincibility — the [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open-core shooting floor]] is what actually stops raids.

pages.title: Deployables
pages.body:
# Deployables

Deployables are placed **inside** a base (not part of the structural grid): storage, smelting, sleeping, decoration, automation. They require [[Tool Cupboard|building privilege]] to place. This page is the durable catalog of the ones that matter for base interiors, including the 2024–2026 additions a returning player won't know.

## Storage

| Item | Slots | Craft cost | Notes |
|------|------:|-----------|-------|
| **Wood Storage Box** | 18 | 100 wood | Cheap early box. Place several in a [[Bunkers|loot room]]. |
| **Large Wood Box** | 48 | 250 wood + 50 metal frags | The workhorse storage box; ~2.7x a small box. |
| **Mini Fridge** | 18 | (Crafting Update item) | Pauses **food spoilage** for items inside when powered — see [[Farming]] / Crafting Update. Added Mar 2025. |
| **Locker** | 18 (gear) | military components | Quick-swap full kits (armor+weapons in one click). Loot-room staple. |
| **Coffin / Vending Machine** | varies | — | Vending machines double as **hidden loot storage** (face inward into a triangle) and as a shop. |

### Shelves (reworked)

Storage shelves let you **stack boxes vertically** in a tight footprint — important because compact bases pay less [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]]. Used heavily in modern loot-room design to cram storage into a small honeycombed core.

## Smelting and processing

| Item | Slots | Notes |
|------|------:|-------|
| **Furnace** | 6 (3x furnace = ~18 across slots) | Smelts ore -> metal frags / HQM, cooks food, makes charcoal. |
| **Large Furnace** | 18 | 3x a normal furnace's throughput; for bulk smelting. |
| **Cooking Workbench** | — | Added Mar 2025 Crafting Update — cooks the **8 buff pies** and recipes. New since 2023. |
| **Refinery / Mixing Table / Workbench T1–T3** | — | Crafting stations; T1–T3 gate what you can build (see [[Getting Started]]). |
| **Hopper** | — | Auto-loots/transfers items between containers (Mar 2025). Automation glue for furnaces/output. |

## Sleeping and respawn

- **Sleeping Bag**: respawn point, ~5 min cooldown. **Capped at 15 respawn points** per player (Jun 2023 change — you can't carpet the map in bags anymore). Place spares in your base and a hidden spawn nearby.
- **Bed**: faster respawn cooldown than a bag, fixed location.

## 2024–2026 additions (returning-player catch-up)

- **Backpacks** (Feb 2024): **Small** = 12 slots (craft 50 cloth + 5 sewing kits, T1); **Large** = 28 slots (military loot only). **They drop on death** — a raider gets your pack. Not a base deployable but core inventory.
- **Wallpaper** (Sep 2024): decorative deployable applied to interior walls.
- **Mini Fridge** (Mar 2025): 18 slots, pauses food spoilage when powered.
- **Hoppers, Chicken Coops, Bee boxes** (Mar 2025 Crafting Update): automation + [[Farming]] deployables.
- **Digital Clock / Seismic Sensor / Tin Can Alarm** (May 2026): raid alarms — the **Seismic Sensor** detects nearby explosions/building damage and can trigger alerts; the **Tin Can Alarm** is a throwable tripwire-style rig.
- **Water Wheel** (Apr 2026): river-placed power generator (see [[Electricity]]).

## Practical loot-room layout

1. Put the **[[Tool Cupboard]]** and best loot in the most-protected room (behind the most [[Soft Side|honeycomb]] / a [[Bunkers|bunker]]).
2. Use **shelves + large boxes + lockers** to pack storage tightly (compact = cheap [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]]).
3. Keep a **Mini Fridge** for cooked food so it doesn't spoil.
4. Spread **sleeping bags** (you get 15) across the base + a hidden offsite spawn.
5. Don't store everything in one box — **spread loot** so a single wall break doesn't expose your whole stash.

## Related

[[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Building Basics]] · [[Farming]] · [[Electricity]] · [[Getting Started]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Doors and Locks
pages.body:
# Doors and Locks

Doors go in **doorways** or **wall frames** ([[Windows Shutters and Frames]]) and are how you actually get in and out of a sealed base. A door is only as good as its **lock** — an unlocked door opens for anyone.

## Door types (verified HP, cost, raid cost)

Raid costs below are the **cheapest explosive method** to destroy the door outright. Full tables live on [[Raid Costs]].

| Door | HP | Craft cost | Workbench | Cheapest raid | Notes |
|------|---:|-----------|:---------:|---------------|-------|
| **Wooden Door** | 200 | 200 wood | none | satchels / fire | First-night door. Fine until people have explosives. Flammable. |
| **Sheet Metal Door** | 250 | 150 metal frags | none | **1 C4** (or 2 rockets / 4 satchels) | The standard door for ~80% of a wipe. |
| **Garage Door** | 600 | 300 metal frags + 2 gears | WB2 | **2 C4** (or 3 rockets / 9 satchels) | Rolls **up** — no swing arc, no gap. Needs a garage-door wall frame. Key bunker/airlock piece; can't be splash-damaged through walls. |
| **Armored Door** | 800 (rusthelp lists 1000)* | 20 HQM + 5 gears | WB3 | **2–3 C4** (or 5 rockets / ~12–15 satchels) | Toughest door. Has a hatch to peek/shoot out. Endgame core door. |

\* **HP discrepancy**: most 2026 guides (WikiRust, Falcon Rust) cite **800 HP / ~12 satchels**; rusthelp.com lists **1000 HP / 5 rockets / 3 C4 / 15 satchels**. Likely a recent rebalance — verify in-game on the current "Built Different" patch before betting a raid defense on it. Either way it's the strongest door and explosives-only.

### Double-door variants

Wooden, Sheet Metal, and Armored come in **double-door** versions that fill a **double-door wall frame** (wider opening, e.g. for vehicles/loot flow). HP is per-leaf similar to the single door; you raid them like two doors or blow the frame. The **Garage Door always uses a double-door frame** by design.

## Locks

A door with **no lock opens for anybody.** Always lock external doors.

| Lock | Craft cost | How it works | Weakness |
|------|-----------|--------------|----------|
| **Code Lock** | 100 metal frags | Set a 4-digit code; anyone who knows the code opens it. Can set a **guest code** for visitors. | Anyone who learns/shoulder-surfs the code. Can be shot off? No — but the **door** can be blown. |
| **Key Lock** | 75 wood | Creates a physical **key** item; you must craft/hold the key. | If you **die and a raider loots the key**, they walk into your base. Rarely used past the first hour. |

**Code Lock is the standard** for essentially every door past the opening minutes. Key Locks are a stopgap when you don't have 100 metal frags yet. Locks themselves aren't really "raided" — raiders blow the **door**, not the lock.

## Airlocks and door stacking

- **Airlock**: two doors in series (a tiny chamber between) so you're never one door from the outside. Standard for any base you care about. A garage door + sheet door airlock is common.
- **Door + window/embrasure**: pair a door with a [[Windows Shutters and Frames|metal embrasure]] beside it to shoot attackers while staying behind the door.
- Doors can be placed in [[Windows Shutters and Frames|wall frames]] as well as doorways, giving flexible placement.

## Returning-player note

Door HP and lock mechanics are essentially the same as 2023. The bigger raid-math change is the **75% explosive-protection cap** (May 2025) — relevant to walls, not doors, but it shifts whether raiders go through your [[Doors and Locks|door]] or your [[Soft Side|wall/soft-side]]. Garage doors remain a top defensive piece for [[Bunkers|bunkers]] because they can't be splash-damaged through adjacent walls.

## Related

[[Windows Shutters and Frames]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Raiding]] · [[Building Basics]]

pages.title: Duo Bases
pages.body:
# Duo Bases

> Re-checked Jun 13 2026 vs the live **"Built Different" patch (Jun 4 2026)** — no building/raid rebalance, so the creator-published upkeep and raid-cost figures below stand. Per-wall breach math: [[Raid Costs]]; tier table: [[Base Designs]].

Two players doubles farm rate, which buys either a bigger raid-cost sponge or a real [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open core]] with two defenders on the shooting floor. The 2026 duo standard is a **2x2 core** (sometimes 2x1 early) with one of: a stability [[Bunkers|bunker]], an open core, or Frustrator-style trap loot rooms. Budget class: ~9k stone / 8k frags / ~75 HQM daily upkeep for a full endgame duo base.

## Named current designs

### The Solara (2025) — duo/trio open core

- **Footprint:** 2x2 core, open core
- **Type:** the widely-copied "best duo/trio" tutorial build of 2025 — open core with shooting floor above, honeycombed exterior, bunkered TC
- **Bunker type:** **bunkered TC** (sealed-cell TC, not a full loot bunker) — the TC survives a door clear; main loot is open-core honeycombed
- **Raid cost to loot:** open-core honeycomb makes the raider cross multiple stone/metal layers (~2 C4 / 5,600 sulfur per stone wall, 4 C4 / ~10,200 per sheet wall) before reaching the floor; the bunkered TC then forces a second armored-tier breach (~8 C4 / 21,000 sulfur) to fully own the base
- **Why it works for duos:** open core needs bodies on the shooting floor; two players can actually man it. Build it if you both play evenings; build a Crow bunker base if you don't.

### The Super Simple Vanilla Egg — Crow

- **Build cost:** 37,000 stone / 29,000 metal frags / 261 HQM
- **Upkeep:** 9,000 stone / 8,000 frags / 74 HQM per day
- **Bunker type:** distributed sealed loot cells (three) rather than one big bunker
- **Features:** integrated airlock, **three loot rooms**, egg/circle footprint
- **Raid cost to loot:** the three loot rooms are honeycomb-separated, so a breach into one (~4 C4 / 8,800 sulfur through a metal-cored cell) exposes at most a third of the stash; clearing all three is roughly **3x** that. There is no cheap face — see "why circles" below.
- **Why circles:** round (triangle-mix) footprints have no flat wall for raiders to set up splash damage on, and every honeycomb cell costs the same to breach — there's no "cheapest face." Circle/egg footprints are a defining 2025–2026 duo trend.

### The Bobo — Lackii (Jul 2025)

- Marketed as the design that "reinvents the solo/duo meta" — compact hybrid with bunkered loot and open-core-style peeks. Lackii's builds favor low upkeep over maximum rocket count; good for duos who raid more than they defend.

### Evil Wurst's duo set (creator-published numbers)

| Design | Size | Upkeep/day | Raid cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Serenity V1 | 1–2, 2x2 | 1.5–5.8k stone / 2.2–3.6k frags / 54–69 HQM | — | **Stability bunker**; scales from early to endgame in place |
| Chad Shed V2 | 1–3, 2x2 | 574 stone / 1,640 frags / 50 HQM | — | Grows step-by-step from a 1x1 — best "starter that becomes the main" |
| Phoenix V3 | 1–2 | 3.1k stone / 2.7k frags / 72 HQM | **27 rockets** | Floor-stacked bunker, double ceiling layers |
| Leech V2 | 1–2, 2x1 | 2.6k stone / 1.8k frags / 19 HQM | — | T3 workbench in a 2x1; minimal upkeep |
| Hell Maw | 1–2 | 3.4k stone / 3.3k frags / 29 HQM | 27 rockets | Minicopter hangar + electric turrets |

(Evil Wurst's catalog at sites.google.com/view/evilwurstsbases — designs predate the 2025 siege/mortar updates; shells hold up, but check rooflines against catapult/[[Mortar]] arcs on a build server.)

## Duo-specific layout advice

- **Two bags, two airlocks.** A second entrance (with its own airlock) means a door camper can't lock both of you out; it's also your counter-raid sally port. Keep it garage-doored.
- **Split the loot.** Two+ loot rooms in separate honeycomb cells (Vanilla Egg's three rooms): a 4-rocket breach should never see more than half your boom.
- **Furnace room ≠ loot room.** Furnaces leak light and noise; keep smelting on the outer ring so deep raids pay full price. Post-mortar, keep furnaces **inside** the footprint, not in a courtyard ([[Expansion and Compound Design]]).
- **Turret budget:** with 10 HQM each, a duo can run 4–6 [[Auto Turret]]s by day 3 — airlock interior, core approach, and one covering the roof. Stay under the 12-in-40m interference cap with room for compound turrets later.
- **Upkeep split:** one player's daily farm run (~10–15k stone with a T2 pick or jackhammer) should fully cover TC; if it doesn't, the base is too big — see [[Base Designs]] decision table.

Upgrade path from a [[Starter Bases|starter 2x1]]: place the 2x2 core around or beside the starter at ~8k stone banked, move TC last, then let the shack decay or convert it to an external. Trio version of all this: [[Trio Bases]].

pages.title: Expansion and Compound Design
pages.body:
# Expansion and Compound Design

How a base grows from a [[Starter Bases|starter]] into something with a perimeter, a shooting floor, and turret coverage — and how the 2026 [[Mortar]] meta changed all of it. Read this *after* [[Base Designs]] and [[Open Core vs Closed Core]]; expansion is the third raid path (boom and door-camping are the other two) and the easiest place to over-build yourself into an [[Upkeep]] death spiral.

> [!warning] The mortar problem (the single biggest 2026 change)
> Since the **Apr 30 2026 update**, HE and fragmentation **[[Mortar]]s unlock at [[Workbench Level 2]]** and can lob shells **over a compound wall from outside your [[Tool Cupboard]] bubble**. Tall external walls used to *hide* you; now they create a **predictable arc** a mortar crew drops shells into, and they raise your profile. The whole "stack high walls and hide behind them" compound meta is dead. Modern compounds are **lower-profile, roofed over internal walkways, with furnaces pulled indoors**.

## When (and whether) to expand

Expand only when **all** of these are true:
1. You can **upkeep** the bigger footprint with your current farm output (see [[Base Designs]] tax math — honeycomb and externals tax daily, forever).
2. You have the **bodies to defend** the new space online — an empty compound is just more wall for a raider to grub against.
3. You're staying on this server/spot long enough to amortize the build cost.

Honeycomb layers are almost always a better spend than footprint or a compound for a solo/duo: each honeycombed stone wall adds ~5,600 sulfur to the raid for ~300 stone + daily tax, no new space to defend.

## Compounds — the outer perimeter

A **compound** is an outer ring of [[High External Stone Wall|high external walls]] around your core. It forces raiders to breach the perimeter before they touch the base, and — critically — **stops grubbing** (a raider building their own twig/honeycomb against your wall to set up [[Satchel Charge|satchels]] or a [[Siege Tower]]). The space between the wall and your base is the **kill zone**.

### High external walls (verified stats)

| Wall | HP | ~Height | Rockets to break | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High External **Wooden** Wall | 500 | ~4 m | melee/fire vulnerable | early-wipe only; **can now be upgraded to stone in place** (Jan 2026) |
| High External **Stone** Wall | 500 | ~4 m | **4 rockets** (3 MLRS) | the standard; **now craftable** (no longer kit-only); fire-resistant |
| High External **Stone Gate** | 500 | ~4 m | 4 rockets | your one entry point — put an [[Airlock]] *behind* it, never rely on the gate alone |

Walls also die to enough melee on wood, or [[Battering Ram]]/[[Catapult]] siege from the Feb 2025 update. **Stack them in pairs** (double-walled compound) at high-value bases so a single rocket line doesn't open the perimeter — but mind the [[Upkeep]] and the mortar profile.

### Compound rules
- **One gate, airlocked.** Multiple gates = multiple breach points and grub spots.
- **External [[Tool Cupboard|TCs]]** placed inside the compound deny raiders the ability to build (ladders, towers, honeycomb) in your kill zone. This is the *main* reason to run a compound. Honeycomb each external TC into a small armored cell so it can't be cheaply destroyed.
- **Keep the gap wide enough to shoot across** but **narrow enough to deny a [[Siege Tower]] landing** — and roof internal walkways so a [[Mortar]] can't shell people crossing the kill zone.
- **Pull furnaces, sleeping bags, and farm stations off open ground** post-mortar; an HE shell over the wall kills an exposed furnace line.

## Shooting floors (the heart of modern defense)

A **shooting floor** is an elevated platform from which defenders fire **down** into the kill zone / core through floor gaps. Combined with [[Auto Turret]]s below, that space becomes nearly impossible for raiders to hold. This is the defensive backbone of every [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open-core]] design and most good compounds.

- **Wide gaps:** misaligned floor/wall slots you can shoot through but raiders can't jump through.
- **Peek-downs:** floor-level slots for side angles — **outer** peek-downs cover the compound/kill zone, **inner** peek-downs cover the core. Good designs have both (e.g. Evil Wurst's Concord, [[Trio Bases]]).
- **Roof floor:** a second layer above for vertical coverage and anti-siege.

A raider who spends 20 rockets into your core then steps into open ground under a manned shooting floor has bought the worst fight in the game — and their dropped [[Backpack]] feeds your hoppers.

## Auto turret coverage (plan it before you build)

- [[Auto Turret]]: 1,000 HP, costs 10 HQM + targeting computer + CCTV camera, draws **10 power**. Each needs an [[Electricity|electrical]] feed.
- **Interference cap:** a maximum of **12 active turrets within a 40 m radius** (vanilla `sentry.maxinterference`); over the cap they shut off. Turret-wall spam is dead — overlap **arcs**, not raw count.
- **A 3x3 room is too large for one turret** to cover; budget **2–3 turrets with overlapping arcs** and a single inside toggle so you can power them down to reload/repair.
- **Turret pods** (a small recessed external box with a turret behind a wide gap) hidden in a compound wall can instakill grubbers — a current meta external defense.
- Big bases run **switched banks** wired to [[Seismic Sensor]]s / detectors so they stay under the interference cap until a raid trips them on.

## Anti-siege roofline (Feb 2025+)

Siege weapons (Catapult, Ballista, Battering Ram, Siege Tower + shields) added a raid path that punishes flat, low, climbable rooflines:
- **Step your roofline** so a Siege Tower can't deposit players on a flat surface adjacent to your core.
- **Shield-wall peeks** (shielded firing slots) let you fight siege crews without eating their counter-fire — 2025+ designs (Naxos, Ixion) advertise this.
- **Mortars (May 2026)** out-range high walls entirely; the only real answer is **compactness + roofed internals**, not more height.

## Expansion order (practical)

1. Starter → main core (honeycomb the core first; see [[Starter Bases]]).
2. Add **internal honeycomb layers** before any footprint or compound — cheapest sulfur-per-stone.
3. Add a **shooting floor / peek-downs** over the core once you have bodies to man it.
4. Add **external TCs** in the future compound footprint to lock down build privilege early.
5. **Then** the [[High External Stone Wall|high external wall]] ring with one airlocked gate — last, because it's the highest upkeep and the mortar liability.
6. **Turrets** wired in with overlapping arcs, under the 40 m cap.

> Don't run two full bases. When the starter's done its job, convert it to an external/furnace shack inside the compound or let it decay — paying [[Upkeep]] on two TCs is the classic over-extension that starves your main into decay.

## Sources
RustBases.gg compound guide, XGamingServer 2026 base designs, Switchblade Gaming (mortar/compound meta), CorrosionHour, wiki.facepunch + WikiRust (high external wall HP/rockets); mortar/siege/turret changes cross-checked against the 2023→2026 returning-player brief.

pages.title: Group Bases
pages.body:
# Group Bases

Quad and up. At this scale the base is an economy: the published numbers below make the point that a clan fortress costs **3–4 dedicated farmers per day** just to not decay. Groups that can't staff that should run a fat [[Trio Bases|trio-class]] core plus compound instead. Josia's solo/duo/trio reality: this page is mostly threat intel — know what you're (not) raiding.

## Named current designs

### The Ixion (2025 META 6-man)

- **Group:** ~6 | **Type:** [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open core]] with multiple [[Bunkers|bunkers]], explicitly **anti-siege** (rooflines and shielded peeks designed against Catapult/Ballista/Siege Tower, post-Feb-2025)
- The reference "modern 6-man": open core for online fights, bunkered loot for offlines.

### The Conquest (2025, 4–6 man)

- **Type:** open core + **wide-gap** shooting floor + **seawall** (water-facing compound wall) — built for shoreline plots where boat/sub raids are a vector ([[Base Locations]]).

### The Prophecy — Dust (4+ players)

- **Build:** 97,000 stone / 78,000 frags / 650 HQM
- **Upkeep:** 20,000 stone / 15,000 frags / 160 HQM per day
- Dust is one of the defining open-core builders (with Zypic/spinky); the Prophecy is the mid-size clan standard.

### The Osmium — Meano (large clan)

- **Build:** 124,000 stone / 381,000 metal frags / 340 HQM
- **Upkeep:** 32,000 stone / 101,000 frags / 340 HQM per day (3–4 full-time farmers)
- **Raid cost:** **900+ rockets minimum ≈ 1.26 million sulfur**
- The "you are not raiding this" tier. Frag-heavy shell = sheet-metal honeycomb everywhere (1,000 HP/wall, 7 rockets each — see [[Base Designs]]).

### Evil Wurst's group set (creator-published numbers)

| Design | Size | Upkeep/day | Raid cost | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Waterloo | 4–8 | 18k stone / 17k frags / 313 HQM | — | **4 separated roof bunkers**, multi-TC fortress |
| The Alamo | 4+ | 8k stone / 15k frags / 198 HQM | — | Expandable battlements + shooting floor |
| The Tycho | 3–6 | 6k stone / 9k frags / 150 HQM | — | 3 **splash-separated** roof bunkers |
| The Retaliator | 3+ | 10.8k stone / 7.6k frags / 123 HQM | — | **4 TCs**, peek-downs, integrated compound |
| Das Bunker | — | 4.3k stone / 4.1k frags / 41 HQM | **31 rockets** | Hidden underground bunker |
| The Exasperator | — | 2.2–4.2k stone / 3.2–4.3k frags / 34–128 HQM | **30 rockets** | Armored bunker, drop-down loot, "spiderman" entrance |

## Group doctrine (what makes clan bases different)

- **Multi-TC is mandatory.** 3–4 TC zones (Waterloo/Retaliator pattern) mean raiders can't seal one cupboard and own the base; each wing keeps building privilege if another falls. Place each TC in its own armored, honeycombed cell.
- **Distributed loot.** Per-player loot rooms in splash-separated cells (Tycho's "splash-separated bunkers"): rocket splash (radius hits multiple walls) is the clan-raid economizer, so cells are spaced to deny double-hits.
- **Shell composition:** stone outer honeycomb (cheap to repair), **sheet-metal mid layers** (the real sponge), armored only on TC/bunker cells — HQM upkeep at 340/day is already brutal at Osmium scale.
- **Compound + shooting floor** does the online work: wide-gap turret pods, overlapping [[Auto Turret]] coverage (cap: 12 active per 40 m — big bases run switched banks on detectors), external TCs in gatehouses. Full treatment in [[Expansion and Compound Design]].
- **Post-mortar (May 2026):** tall-wall compounds are arcable by WB2 [[Mortar]]s — large clans now roof their internal walkways, drop some perimeter walls to deny predictable arcs, and pull furnaces indoors.
- **Defense showers loot:** dead raiders drop [[Backpacks]]; hoppers under the shooting floor auto-collect during fights (Mar 2025 QoL).

## Raiding-them math (for the solo/trio reader)

Door-path is always cheaper than wall-path on these: [[Garage Door]] 600 HP (2 C4 / 4,400 sulfur) vs sheet wall 1,000 HP (4 C4 / 8,800 sulfur) vs armored wall (8 C4 / ~21k sulfur). Clan bases die to **online** TC rushes and gatehouse sealing, not to honest boom — or just don't; farm the [[Trio Bases|trios]] instead.

pages.title: Open Core vs Closed Core
pages.body:
# Open Core vs Closed Core

The central design question of 2025–2026 base building. **Closed core** = the traditional model: loot at the center, wrapped in as many honeycomb wall layers as you can afford. **Open core** = skip the honeycomb around the core and **defend from height instead** — raiders who get inside stand in an open kill-box under your shooting floor.

> "Closed core is better when you're offline for long stretches. Open core is better when you're fighting." — rustbases.gg

## How an open core works

Instead of wall layers, the core is a tall open room. Defenders fight from:

- **Shooting floor** — the elevated platform ringing the core's airspace; defenders shoot down through gaps
- **Wide gaps** — deliberately misaligned floors/walls (built by placing and demolishing scaffolding foundations) leaving slots you can shoot through but can't be jumped through
- **Peek-downs** — floor-level slots giving side angles down exterior walls and into the core (**inner** peek-downs cover the core, **outer** peek-downs cover the compound — good designs have both, e.g. Evil Wurst's Concord)
- **Roof floor** — a second elevated layer above the shooting floor for vertical coverage and anti-siege work

A raider who spends 20 rockets getting into the core has bought a fight on the worst terrain in the game: open ground, defenders above with hard cover, [[Auto Turret]]s in the gaps, and their dropped [[Backpacks]] feeding your hoppers.

## The trade, honestly

| | Open core | Closed core |
|---|---|---|
| Online raid | Very strong — height + angles | Weak sightlines from inside |
| Offline raid | **Cheaper to crack** (fewer walls) | Expensive (every layer is 4–15 rockets) |
| Build cost | Usually cheaper | Expensive honeycomb |
| Upkeep | Lower | Higher (walls tax daily — see [[Base Designs]]) |
| Skill floor | Needs bodies online + PvP ability | Works while you sleep |
| Group size | Duo+ to man the floor (solo possible) | Any |

**Decision rule:** count your offline hours. Offline 20h/day → closed core, maximum honeycomb, multiple [[Bunkers|bunkers]]. Online every evening with a duo/trio → open core wins fights and saves upkeep.

## The hybrid (what most good 2025–2026 designs actually are)

Pure open core is an offline-raid donation. The current standard is **bunkered open core**:

- Open core + shooting floor for the online game
- Sealed [[Bunkers|bunker]] cells (in the honeycomb ring or under the core) holding BPs, boom, and best kits for the offline game
- Honeycomb only where it protects the bunkers and TC, not blanket layers

Examples across the size range: RustLogic's Perfect Open Core 2x1 ([[Solo Bases]]), The Solara ([[Duo Bases]]), The Naxos's bunkered-starter open core ([[Trio Bases]]), The Ixion ([[Group Bases]]). Key creators of the school: **Zypic** (The Agitator), **Dust** (The Prophecy), **spinky** (The Onyx).

## Why open core took over (timeline)

1. **Upkeep economics** — honeycomb taxes daily forever; height is free after construction.
2. **Aimcone overhaul (May 2024)** made defended angles meaningfully stronger for the entrenched shooter.
3. **Siege weapons (Feb 2025)** punished static wall stacks; open designs added anti-siege rooflines and shield-wall peeks instead.
4. **Explosive protection cap at 75% (May 2025)** — raid tanks die to shooting-floor fire again.
5. **[[Mortar]]s (May 2026)** arc over compound walls; the open core's answer (compact footprint, roofed floors) survives where wall-farms don't ([[Expansion and Compound Design]]).

## Build-server homework

Wide gaps, peek-down geometry, and bunker seals are placement-precise and get silently changed by monthly patches. Rebuild your design on a build/creative server **every wipe** before trusting it — a patched wide gap is a free ladder for raiders, and a patched bunker is a sealed-off loot piñata. See [[Bunkers]] for what's currently stable.

pages.title: Roof Access and Peaks
pages.body:
# Roof Access and Peaks

Your roof is a raid surface. **Top-down raiding is more common than ever** in 2026 — if an attacker can ladder, boost, or build onto your roof, they reach the [[Soft Side|soft underside]] of your loot-room floor and break **down** into your core for ~10x melee damage. Good roof design makes the roof **non-ladderable and unfallable** while giving **you** safe firing positions (peaks/peek-downs).

## The threats you're designing against

1. **Roof camping**: an attacker sits on your roof and kills you whenever you exit ([[Bunkers|bunkers]] help by removing the exterior door).
2. **Ladder access**: a ladder placed on a flat/low-angle surface lets them walk up. Steep roof pieces stop ladders.
3. **Boosting**: one player crouches, another jumps off them onto a ledge. Flat ledges and shallow steps enable boosts.
4. **Building onto your base**: outside your [[Tool Cupboard|TC]] bubble, raiders can place their **own** twig steps/foundations to climb up — so extend privilege over your immediate exterior.
5. **Top-down breach**: once on the roof, they break **down** through the soft floor underside ([[Soft Side]]) into the loot room.

## Roof peaks — the core defensive idea

A **peak** is a raised roof structure (square + triangle roof pieces, or wall stacks) that creates **steep, ladder-proof, un-boostable geometry** while giving you **peek-downs**: small gaps/embrasures you shoot **out and down** through from a protected position, then duck back behind a floor/wall.

- **Combine square and triangle roof pieces** so coverage gaps are too steep to ladder and too high/awkward to fall or boost into.
- **Peek-downs**: build the peak so there's a gap you can shoot your own doorways/roof/core through, while floor pieces and [[Windows Shutters and Frames|embrasures]] keep you covered. Lets you punish a roof camper or a raider at your door **from above**.
- **Avoid door-based peaks**: old peaks that used a doorway to climb are **too easily boosted/door-camped**. Modern guidance is to use roof/floor geometry and embrasures instead of a door you climb through.

## Anti-roof-camp / anti-ladder rules

- **Make the outer roof steep** — triangle/peaked roof pieces at angles ladders can't grab.
- **No flat ledges or shallow steps** on the exterior that enable a boost up.
- **Ensure large roof holes are non-ladderable AND unfallable** — a gap should be either fully sealed or too steep to place a ladder / land in.
- **Extend [[Tool Cupboard|building privilege]] over your immediate perimeter** so attackers can't twig-step up the outside (privilege blocks their placement within ~16 m of your outer blocks).
- **Honeycomb above the loot room** so even a roof-breacher hits layers of [[Soft Side|honeycomb]] instead of the soft floor underside directly.
- **Roof loot defenses**: vending machines (face inward) can store loot on the roof; turrets + a SAM Site make the roof hostile to campers and air. (Auto turrets have a **40 m interference cap** — Oct 2023 — so don't cluster too many.)

## Vertical access for YOU (without giving it to them)

- **Ladder Hatch / Armored Triangle Ladder Hatch** (the latter added Apr 2026): a code-/privilege-gated hatch is the clean way to reach your own roof from inside — see [[Bunkers]]. Raiders can't use it without privilege.
- **Spiral / U-stairs inside the shell** to climb without an exterior ladder.
- Keep your own access **internal** — never leave an external ladder or shallow exterior steps a raider can reuse.

## 2026 watch-out: mortars

Since **Apr 30 2026**, HE/fragmentation **mortars unlock at WB2** and can **lob shells over a compound wall from outside your TC bubble** onto exposed roofs. A peaked, ladder-proof roof still helps against climbers, but **don't leave thin/twig roof pieces exposed** — armor the top and don't assume height alone protects you. See [[Raiding]].

## Related

[[Soft Side]] · [[Stability]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Windows Shutters and Frames]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Raiding]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Soft Side
pages.body:
# Soft Side

Every stone/metal/armored building block has a **hard side** and a **soft side**. The soft side takes **far more melee and tool damage**. Building with a soft side facing outward is the single most common beginner mistake — it lets raiders pickaxe through your wall for almost nothing instead of spending explosives.

## How to tell them apart

- **Hard side (strong)**: rougher, darker texture. On stone it has the **dark brick outlines / mortar lines**. This is the side that faces a raider, the walkable top of a foundation, the top of a floor.
- **Soft side (weak)**: lighter, smoother, flat grey. On stone it's the plain light-grey face. This is the side that should always face **inward / into your base**.

When you place a wall, the **hard side automatically faces outward from the foundation** — but you can rotate pieces, and certain placements force the soft side out. **Always check** by looking at the texture from outside.

## The damage difference (why it matters)

Melee/tool damage is dramatically higher against the soft side:

| Wall grade | Hard side (pickaxe) | Soft side (pickaxe) |
|------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| Stone | ~1 dmg per **8** hits (500 HP = a LOT of hits) | ~1.2 dmg per hit -> **~7 pickaxes** to break a wall |
| Sheet Metal | near-immune from outside | ~1 dmg per **2** hits + takes tool damage |

In rough terms, the soft side takes on the order of **10x melee damage** and **~2x firearm damage** compared to the hard side. A soft-sided stone wall can be silently pickaxed down for the cost of a few pickaxes — no explosives, no noise — which completely defeats the point of upgrading.

## Which placements expose the soft side (the rules)

This is the part people get wrong. The **soft side is always the "underside / inside" face**:

- **Walls**: soft side is the **inner** face. Default placement puts hard side out — good. But a wall placed on the wrong edge, or stacked oddly, can flip it.
- **Foundations**: the **top** (the surface you walk on) is the hard side. The **bottom/sides** are soft. A foundation edge exposed at the base of a cliff can be soft-side raided from below/side.
- **Floors / Ceilings**: the **top** is hard (you walk on it), the **underside is soft**. This is the classic loot-room weakness — **if a raider gets directly below your loot room, they break upward through the soft underside of the floor for ~10x melee / ~2x firearm damage**. This is exactly how "soft-side the loot room from below" raids work.
- **Triangle floors / roofs**: same rule — top hard, underside soft.

### Design consequences

1. **Never leave a wall with its soft side outward.** Rotate and re-check every external wall.
2. **Honeycomb under and around the loot room** so a raider can't reach the soft underside of your floor. The classic exploit is breaking up through an unhoneycombed floor.
3. **Don't build a loot room on the ground floor with empty space beneath an adjacent foundation** — they tunnel sideways then up through the soft floor.
4. On a **bunker** ([[Bunkers]]), the whole point is that the soft underside of the core floor is unreachable without first breaking the outer shell.

## Quick check before you log off

Walk the **outside** of your base. Every wall should show the **dark, bricked, rough** face. Any pale flat-grey wall = soft side out = re-rotate it. Then make sure no floor's soft underside is exposed to open air a raider can stand in.

## Related

[[Building Basics]] · [[Stability]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Raiding]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Solo Bases
pages.body:
# Solo Bases

> Numbers re-checked Jun 13 2026 against the live **"Built Different" patch (Jun 4 2026)** — no building/raid rebalance this wipe, so creator-published upkeep and rocket counts below stand. Rocket counts are "to reach loot from any angle"; cross-reference per-wall costs in [[Raid Costs]] and the tier table in [[Base Designs]].

What "good" looks like for one player in 2025–2026: a 2x1 or 2x2 core, **30+ rockets to the loot from any angle**, at least one [[Bunkers|bunker]], and upkeep you can pay with one farm run (~60–120 stone/hour class; see [[Base Designs]] for the tax math). The solo meta has split into two schools — closed-core bunker bases for low-hour players, and compact [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open-core]] bases with shooting floors for players who'll be online to defend.

## Named current designs

### Perfect Open Core Solo/Duo — RustLogic (May 2026)

- **Footprint:** 2x1 core, open core with airlock + honeycomb
- **Upkeep (creator-published):** 10,300 stone / 9,600 metal frags / 37 HQM per 24h, plus 2 external TCs
- **Bunker type:** none — open core relies on the shooting floor, not a sealed cell (HQM line stays cheap because armored is core-cell only)
- **Raid cost to loot:** open-core honeycomb forces a multi-wall path; the design's selling point is that it's defended live rather than offline-proof, so treat the **2 external TCs** as the real "double-pay" tax — a raider must clear core + both externals to fully own it (~2 C4 / 5,600 sulfur per stone-wall layer crossed)
- **Verdict:** the current "default" sweaty solo/duo build; cheap HQM line because armored is limited to core cell. Tutorial on rustbaselab.com.

### The Agitator — Zypic

- **Footprint:** 2x1, solo
- **Type:** open core; highlighted by rustbases.gg as the flagship 2x1 solo open-core design of the era
- **Key features:** shooting floor over an open core, wide gaps, peek-downs. Pairs the smallest viable footprint with online-defense angles. Zypic, Dust, and spinky are the names to search for current-patch versions.

### The Onyx — spinky (Apr 2026)

- **Footprint:** 2x2
- **Type:** "meta build" snowball-to-endgame base — designed to be built from starter stage and grown in place rather than rebuilt
- **Why it's listed everywhere:** it's the 2026 answer to "one base for the whole wipe" for solo/duo.

### Crow's line — TIRAMISU / RAZOR MINI / CTHULHU

- **CTHULHU (Dec 2025):** **triple [[Bunkers|bunker]]** (sealed-cell type), "cozy & cheap" — the budget bunker pick. Three splash-separated cells mean opening loot room #1 (one wall/floor set) doesn't touch #2 or #3 — a raider pays the breach cost **three times** to clear everything.
- **TIRAMISU / RAZOR MINI (Apr 2026):** dual/double **bunker** designs with **shield walls** (post-siege-update feature: shielded peeks vs [[Mortar]]/Ballista). Two sealed cells = pay-twice loot.
- Crow's designs emphasize multiple sealed [[Bunkers|bunker]] cells so a raid that opens one loot room pays again for the next. **Reach-loot rule:** each sealed cell behind armored honeycomb costs ~**8 C4 / 15 rockets / ~21,000 sulfur per wall** to crack, multiplied by the number of cells the raider wants.

### Limi Lab's line — THICKET / NEOTEK / ANT / NYXAR / FEROS

- **THICKET (Jan 2026):** closed/hybrid core, "strong & cheap," **80+ rockets to reach loot** (~112,000 sulfur of rockets to fully clear)
- **NEOTEK (Feb 2026):** turret-heavy shell, **90+ rockets to clear** (~126,000 sulfur) — turrets force the raider to spend boom/ammo before even starting the wall path
- **ANT (Jul 2025):** **4 [[Bunkers|bunkers]]** (sealed-cell), smart turrets, low upkeep — the efficiency pick; pay-4x loot
- **NYXAR (Nov 2025):** **7 bunkers**, huge shell — solo-buildable but group-tier raid cost (clearing all 7 cells is a several-hundred-rocket commitment, i.e. raid-deterrent by sheer cell count)
- **FEROS (Sep 2025):** **open core** (no sealed bunker) with internal courtyard and "insane peaks" — defended live, not offline
- Limi Lab designs are rocket-sponge closed/hybrid cores: high offline security, higher upkeep. The rocket counts are creator-published "to reach loot from any angle" figures; honeycomb depth, not wall tier alone, drives them.

### Mini Frustrator — Evil Wurst

- **Group:** 1–2 | **Upkeep:** 2,600 stone / 1,300 frags / 17 HQM per day
- **Type:** drop-down loot rooms rigged with shotgun traps (the Frustrator mechanic — loot is reached by chutes raiders can't safely descend; traps are undrainable). Fits a T3 workbench despite the tiny footprint. The classic "my loot room fights back" solo base; full family on the trio page ([[Trio Bases]]).

### Hydra V2 — Faded (big-solo option)

- **Build:** 67,000 stone / 35,000 frags / 360 HQM
- **Upkeep:** 13,000 stone / 7,200 frags / 101 HQM per day
- **Features:** multiple separated loot rooms, hidden TC
- **Verdict:** only take this on if you play 6+ hours/day — the upkeep alone is a daily farm session. For most solos a THICKET/Onyx-class base banks more and loses less.

## Solo design checklist

- [ ] 2x1 or 2x2 core — every extra foundation is upkeep you pay forever
- [ ] [[Bunkers|Bunker]] cell holding BPs + best loot (a successful raid should still miss your [[Workbench]] T3 kit)
- [ ] Offset/L-shaped airlock, [[Garage Door]]s on the path to core, [[Armored Door]] on core only
- [ ] Stone shell, metal core walls, armored TC cell only (HQM upkeep discipline)
- [ ] Roof access for counter-play; ladder hatch (250 HP, T2, 300 frags + ladder + 3 gears) sealing vertical paths
- [ ] 1–2 [[Auto Turret]]s inside the airlock/core approach (1,000 HP, 10 HQM + targeting computer + CCTV, 10 power)
- [ ] External TC(s) if you compound later — [[Expansion and Compound Design]]
- [ ] Build it once on a build server (`/creative` servers) before wipe day

## Closed vs open core for solos

If you're offline 20h/day: closed core, maximum honeycomb, multiple bunkers (Limi Lab/Crow school). If you're online and want to win the fight: compact open core with a shooting floor (Zypic/RustLogic school). Full trade-off analysis: [[Open Core vs Closed Core]].

Where to put it matters as much as the design: snow and deep forest for stealth solos, T1-monument ring for farm efficiency — [[Base Locations]].

pages.title: Stability
pages.body:
# Stability

Rust enforces a soft "physics" rule: every building block has a **stability percentage**. If a piece is too far from solid support — too high, or spanning too far horizontally with nothing under it — its stability drops, and at **0% it collapses and is destroyed** (instantly on placement, or it falls if support is removed later).

## The core rule

- **Foundations sit on the ground at ~100% stability.** They are the anchor — everything's stability is ultimately measured by distance back to a foundation.
- **Stability decreases as you move away from ground/support** — both **upward** (each floor up) and **outward** (each tile of unsupported horizontal span).
- **Walls and pillars carry stability upward**; **floors carry it outward** but lose a chunk per tile.
- When you hover a placed block at melee range with the [[Building Basics|Hammer]], it shows the **stability %**. Use this constantly while building tall.

So: a wall directly on a foundation is rock-solid; a floor cantilevered three tiles past its last support is shaky; a wall placed on the far edge of that floor inherits the floor's weak stability and may read ~15% or refuse to place.

## What gives support

- **Foundations** = 100% anchor.
- **Walls / wall frames / window frames** = the main vertical supports. Adding a wall under an upper floor dramatically restores its stability — this is the standard fix for "this floor keeps collapsing."
- **Pillars** = cheap vertical support for open floors (e.g. under a big roof or platform).
- **Floors** propagate stability outward but each successive unsupported tile loses more, so wide open rooms need internal walls or pillars.

If a block can't reach enough support, you'll see it tinted/red on placement and it won't place, or it places at low % and is vulnerable to **collapse if its support is later destroyed**.

## Height limits

There is no hard "max floors" number, but stability falls off with height, so a tower of floors needs walls stacked beneath each level to keep stability above 0. In practice you can build very tall **as long as each level is supported by walls below it** — unsupported overhangs and floating rooms are what the system prevents.

## Why it matters for defense and raiding

- **Collapse raiding**: because removing support can drop everything above it, raiders sometimes destroy a **load-bearing wall/foundation** to collapse an upper structure instead of breaking every wall. Distribute support so no single block holds up your whole roof or loot room.
- **Stability bunkers** ([[Bunkers]]) historically abused this — sealing a room by placing a block that's then unsupported so it can be picked up, or using stability to drop a "lid." Verify current status on the [[Bunkers]] page.
- **Don't over-rely on cantilevers** for [[Roof Access and Peaks|roof peaks]] — a peak supported only by a thin stack can be collapsed.

## Practical building tips

1. **Build the shell in twig first** and watch stability before committing resources.
2. If an upper floor reads low %, **drop a wall or pillar under it**.
3. **Stack walls vertically** when going tall — don't try to float upper rooms on cantilevered floors.
4. Keep **load-bearing pieces honeycombed/armored** so they can't be popped to collapse the structure above.
5. Internal walls do double duty: they add stability **and** add [[Soft Side|honeycomb]] for raid defense.

## Related

[[Building Basics]] · [[Soft Side]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Roof Access and Peaks]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Starter Bases
pages.body:
# Starter Bases

The hour-0 to day-2 base: cheap, fast, and just strong enough that the first guy with 4 satchels doesn't end your wipe. The goal is **full stone, an airlock, and a protected TC by your first log-off**, then you snowball into a real design ([[Solo Bases]], [[Duo Bases]], [[Trio Bases]]).

## Day-1 targets

- Full **stone** shell (wood burns and its soft side can be melee'd through — stone soft-side still takes 4 satchels, which nobody has in hour 2)
- **Airlock** (two doors, never both open)
- TC out of door-line, honeycombed as soon as you have spare stone
- A [[Sheet Metal Door]] on the outer slot ASAP — it needs **no workbench**, costs **150 metal frags**, and stops every melee tool

## The 2x1 (the canonical starter)

Two square foundations, one of them your loot/TC room, one your entrance with airlock. Total cost lands around **1,600–2,000 stone** for a 1x1-with-airlock and slightly more for a 2x1; budget ~2,500–3,500 stone gathered to have upgrade spare.

**Per-grade upgrade cost (per square wall, verified — see [[Building Basics]]):** wood = 50–200 wood, **stone = 300 stone**, sheet metal = 200 frags, armored = 25 HQM. A 2x1 stone shell of ~6 walls + 2 floors + frames runs the ~1,600–2,000 stone above because triangles and frames cost less than full squares. **Upkeep:** a small (≤~15-block) starter pays ~**10%** of build cost per 24h, so a 2x1 stone starter is roughly **160–200 stone/day** — one quick farm run.

**Build order (twig first, upgrade after placement):**

1. Craft Building Plan (20 wood) + Hammer (100 wood). Place 2 square foundations in twig.
2. Wall the perimeter in twig, leave one doorway facing cover (not a road).
3. Place [[Tool Cupboard]] (**1,000 wood**) in the back corner, behind where your internal wall will be. Lock it... the TC is the base.
4. Ceiling on, then hammer-upgrade everything to **stone** (300/wall — see [[Base Designs]] tier table).
5. Internal wall + doorway splitting the two foundations: front cell = airlock, back cell = TC + loot.
6. Doors: wooden door immediately (300 wood), replace outer with sheet metal the moment you've recycled 150 frags. Code locks (100 metal frags each) over key locks, always.
7. Drop a sleeping bag inside (30 cloth) and a furnace.

**Raid cost when finished:** ~5,600 sulfur (4 rockets / 2 C4 through one stone wall) — enough that you're not free loot on night 1.

### Why the airlock matters

Two doors with a dead space between them mean a deep-door camper or a rusher who catches one door open still hits a second locked door. Never place doors so both can be seen/opened from outside at once. L-shaped (offset) airlocks beat straight ones — no direct rocket line to the core.

## The 2x2 step-up (day 1–3)

Once you've banked **~8,000 stone**, rebuild or expand into a 2x2: **8,000–10,000 stone + 1,500–3,000 metal frags** gets you four rooms — airlock, furnace room, loot room, TC room — with one honeycomb layer started. Raid cost jumps to **16,800–22,400 sulfur** (3–4 stone walls soft-side). This is the standard solo/duo platform for the rest of the wipe; most named designs in [[Solo Bases]] and [[Duo Bases]] are a 2x2 core with tricks bolted on.

**Upgrade triggers (verified meta guidance):**
- Day 1–3: 1x1/2x1 → 2x2 at ~8k stone banked
- Mid-wipe: add honeycomb layers **before** adding footprint (each honeycombed stone wall adds ~5,600 sulfur to the raid)
- Metal-core the loot room when frags allow — roughly **doubles** raider cost vs stone
- TC room walls → armored eventually (**15 rockets / ~21,000 sulfur per wall**)
- If farming falls behind: **downsize**. Decay eats over-built bases (stone collapses 5h after TC empties)

## Starter mistakes that end wipes

- **Building on the beach/roadside.** You will be door-camped by everyone who spawns. See [[Base Locations]].
- **Key locks.** Death = lost key = raiders walk in. Code locks only.
- **TC visible from the doorway.** One door breach should never give TC access (TC = they can seal you out and take everything).
- **Skipping the airlock to save 2 walls.** It's ~600 stone for the single highest-value defensive feature in the game.
- **Sleeping in wood.** 250 HP walls, flammable, soft-side meleeable.
- **Loot above ground floor with twig stairs left in.** Raiders use your own twig.

When the starter has done its job, keep it as a [[Expansion and Compound Design|external/furnace shack]] or let it decay — don't keep paying upkeep on two bases ([[Base Designs]] upkeep math).

pages.title: Tool Cupboard
pages.body:
# Tool Cupboard
