The single most important deployable in the game. The **Tool Cupboard (TC)** establishes **building privilege** over an area, pays [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]] to stop decay, and gates who can build, upgrade, or pick up pieces near it. No TC = no base.

## Craft and stats

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Craft cost | 1000 wood |
| Workbench | None (craftable from start) |
| Inventory | **24 upkeep slots** + **4 tool slots** (28 total) |
| Building privilege radius | ~16 m out from each outer building component, up to ~6 floors high |
| Placement clearance | Cannot place within ~16 m of another TC |
| Max authorized players | 10 (vanilla) |

The 24 upkeep slots hold the materials it burns for [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]]; the 4 tool slots are a small extra storage area (often used to stash a key/tools).

## Building privilege

When a TC is placed, you become **authorized** to it automatically. Inside the privilege zone, only authorized players can:

- Place new building blocks
- Upgrade blocks with the [[Building Basics|Hammer]]
- Pick up / rotate freshly placed pieces
- Place most deployables (boxes, turrets, etc.)

Unauthorized players see "**Building Blocked**" and can do none of the above. This is what stops a raider from sealing themselves into your base or walling you in.

**Important nuance:** privilege radius is projected ~16 m from each **outer building component**, not from the cupboard itself. So a long base extends privilege along its whole footprint. A standalone TC with no attached building projects a fixed sphere.

## Authorization

- **Authorize**: hold E on the TC -> "Authorize." You're now on the list.
- **Deauthorize me**: removes only you.
- **Clear list**: anyone with access can wipe **all** authorized players at once — common after a raid to lock everyone out, or to remove a backstabbing teammate. **A raider who reaches your TC will Clear the list and authorize themselves, taking the base.** Protecting the TC room is the whole point of a [[Bunkers|bunker]] / honeycomb.
- Up to **10 players** can be authed on vanilla. The [[Getting Started|party system]] (Jul 2025) auto-teams friends but does **not** auto-authorize them — you still hold E on the TC.

## How upkeep is paid

The TC continuously consumes materials from its 24 slots to cover the [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep tax]] of every block in privilege. It burns the **matching material per grade**:

- Wood blocks -> wood
- Stone blocks -> stone
- Sheet metal -> metal fragments
- Armored -> HQM

If a needed material runs out, **only that material's blocks decay** — your stone shell can survive while your sheet-metal core melts, or vice versa. The TC display (and the on-screen privilege HUD) shows "**protected for X**." Keep all relevant materials stocked.

## When the TC is destroyed or empty

- **Empty TC**: blocks begin decaying right away (outer pieces first).
- **Destroyed TC**: a **24-hour grace buffer** (`decay.upkeep_grief_protection`) keeps paying upkeep, so the base doesn't instantly collapse. After 24h, normal [[Upkeep and Decay|decay timers]] start.
- **No TC at all**: immediate decay — never rely on a TC-less base.

## Placement strategy

- **Bury it deep.** The TC should be in the most protected room — behind the most walls, ideally a [[Bunkers|bunker]] or behind an [[Doors and Locks|armored door]]. Whoever owns the TC owns the base.
- **One TC per base.** The 16 m clearance means you usually can't (and shouldn't) place a second. Compounds connect their footprints to share one privilege zone.
- **Hide a backup base's TC** away from the main, since you can't place two close together.
- 2026 cosmetic skins exist (Retro, Shockbyte) — purely visual, no stat change.

## Related

[[Upkeep and Decay]] · [[Building Basics]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Doors and Locks]] · [[Raiding]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Trio Bases
pages.body:
# Trio Bases

> Re-checked Jun 13 2026 vs the live **"Built Different" patch (Jun 4 2026)** — no building/raid rebalance, so the creator-published upkeep and raid-cost figures below stand. Per-wall breach math: [[Raid Costs]].

Three players is the sweet spot: enough farm for a serious shell and enough guns for an [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open core]] to actually function, while still small enough to dodge zerg attention. Trio designs are 2x2–3x3 cores with **multiple separated loot rooms** (so one breach ≠ wipe) and usually a shooting floor.

## Named current designs

### The Naxos (2025 META trio)

- **Type:** open core with a **bunkered starter** — you build the bunker cell first as your day-1 base, then the open-core shell grows around it
- **Group:** trio | **Core:** open, with shooting floor + peek-downs
- **Bunker type:** sealed-cell bunkered starter (the original day-1 cell becomes the permanent deep loot/BP bunker)
- **Raid cost to loot:** the open-core shell forces a multi-layer wall path before the floor; the inner bunkered-starter cell is then a second armored breach (~8 C4 / 21,000 sulfur). A door clear of the open core never reaches the bunkered starter — that's the pay-twice guarantee.
- **Why it's the reference trio build:** the bunkered-starter pattern solves the classic trio problem of being raidable during the awkward hours between starter and main. Tutorial circulates on YouTube/rustbaselab ("The Naxos — 2025 META Rust Trio Base Design").

### The Frustrator family — Evil Wurst (the trap-loot classic)

- **Mechanic:** loot rooms reached only by **drop-down chutes rigged with undrainable shotgun traps**, surrounding a central core — every door raid turns into a trap gauntlet
- **Raid cost:** fully upgraded, **25+ rockets to reach TC from any angle**; the three loot rooms are spaced so opening all of them costs **~40 rockets**
- **Upkeep:** Frustrator V2 ≈ 4,300 frags/day class; **V3: 8k stone / 7k frags / 111 HQM** per day
- **Variants:** Mini Frustrator (solo/duo — see [[Solo Bases]]), **Aggravator** (1–3 players, ~2/3 the upkeep: 2.9k stone / 2.6k frags / 47 HQM, 3 shotgun-protected loot rooms)
- Arguably the most successful base-design family ever published; the trap-chute idea is now generic across 2025-era designs.

### The BEAST — Faded (Mar 2026)

- **Group:** solo/duo/trio | billed "super strong" current-patch build from one of the biggest build channels (Faded also publishes [[Solo Bases|Hydra V2]]). Closed-core rocket sponge school — take it if your trio logs off early.

### Evil Wurst's trio set (creator-published numbers)

| Design | Size | Footprint | Upkeep/day | Raid cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Concord | 1–3 | 2x1 | 7.5k stone / 6k frags / 75 HQM | — | Honeycombed, **shooting floor with inner + outer peek-downs** — mini open core |
| Viking | 1–3 | compact | 3.4k stone / 1.4k frags / 41 HQM | **27 rockets** | Needs **no blueprints** to build; roof + stability bunkers |
| Valkyrie | 2–3 | — | 4k stone / 2.3k frags / 22 HQM | 27 rockets | Reinforced-glass bunker, 2 loot rooms |
| Trinity | 1–3 | multi-TC | 5k stone / 1.5k frags / 7 HQM | — | Early-wipe PvP tower, 3 TCs |

## Trio layout doctrine

- **Three loot rooms minimum, separated by full honeycomb** so splash can't open two at once (the Frustrator/Vanilla-Egg principle). Each member "owns" a room — a raid never gets all three kits.
- **Shooting floor with both inner and outer peek-downs** (Concord pattern): outer peeks fight the compound, inner peeks shoot raiders who get inside the core. This is the heart of the current meta — details in [[Open Core vs Closed Core]].
- **Bunker the BPs.** One sealed [[Bunkers|bunker]] cell with workbench + BP stash means even a 40-rocket clear doesn't reset your progression (BPs are per-player but the T3 + boom stock is the real loss).
- **Multi-TC from day 3:** external TCs honeycombed into wings/compound make sealing-and-taking-over your base far more expensive and protect against TC-rush online raids ([[Expansion and Compound Design]]).
- **Roofline anti-siege:** post-Feb-2025, check that a Siege Tower or Catapult can't land players on a flat low roof; 2025+ designs (Naxos, Ixion-style) use stepped rooflines and shielded peeks. [[Mortar]]s (May 2026) out-range high external walls — compactness is protection.
- **Upkeep budget:** a trio sustains ~8k stone / 7k frags / ~100 HQM daily (Frustrator V3 class) comfortably with one farmer per day rotating. Past that you're a [[Group Bases|group base]] with two players missing.

pages.title: Upkeep and Decay
pages.body:
# Upkeep and Decay

Why your base needs a stocked [[Tool Cupboard]], how much it costs per day, and how fast it falls apart if you let it run dry.

## The two systems

1. **Decay** — passive HP loss on building blocks. Without a TC (or with an empty one), blocks decay starting almost immediately and disappear after a per-grade timer.
2. **Upkeep** — a resource "tax" the TC pays continuously to **prevent** decay. As long as the TC has the right materials, nothing decays.

## Decay timers (no upkeep / empty TC)

Once a block has no upkeep protecting it, it loses HP until it's gone, on this schedule:

| Grade | Time to fully destroy |
|-------|----------------------:|
| Twig | ~1 hour |
| Wood | 3 hours |
| Stone | 5 hours |
| Sheet Metal | 8 hours |
| Armored | 12 hours |

These are the same timers listed on the [[Building Basics]] grade table. Decay damages **outer/unconnected pieces first**. Note these are short — a weekend away with no upkeep means even an armored base is gone in half a day.

## Upkeep cost: the tax-bracket system

Upkeep is **10% of the base build cost per day at the lowest bracket**, but it scales **non-linearly** — the more building blocks you own, the higher the percentage tax on each additional block. Brackets (verified vs Corrosion Hour decay variables):

| Bracket | Block count | Tax rate |
|---------|-------------|---------:|
| 0 | blocks 1–15 | **10%** (0.10) |
| 1 | blocks 16–65 | **15%** (0.15) |
| 2 | blocks 66–190 | **20%** (0.20) |
| 3 | blocks 191+ | **33.3%** (0.333) |

The final upkeep cost shown in the TC is the **sum of every block's cost x its bracket rate**, rounded up. In practice the game averages across all your blocks, so a small base pays ~10% of its build cost per day and a sprawling clan base pays up to ~33% per day. **Lesson: compact bases are far cheaper to maintain** — every extra honeycomb wall pushes you toward the expensive brackets.

### Rough per-day numbers

The TC consumes the same material the blocks are made of (wood for wood blocks, stone for stone, metal frags for sheet, HQM for armored). Ballpark, in the cheap bracket:

- A **stone foundation** ~ 8 stone/day; a **stone wall** ~ 5 stone/day.
- A small stone 2x1 sits comfortably in the 10–15% brackets — a few hundred stone covers a day.
- A mixed stone-shell + sheet-metal-core base needs **stone, metal fragments, and HQM all stocked** simultaneously; missing any one material means that material's blocks decay while the others survive.

## The grace period (TC destroyed)

If your TC is **destroyed** (or you remove it), the game keeps paying upkeep from a buffer for up to **24 hours** (`decay.upkeep_grief_protection = 1440` minutes). This stops raiders from instantly collapsing your base by popping the TC. After 24h with no TC, normal decay timers begin. This is also why a raided base with a broken TC still stands for a day before melting.

## Practical maintenance rules

- **Always over-stock the TC** before logging off. Fill all 24 upkeep slots ([[Tool Cupboard]]) with surplus stone/metal/HQM.
- **Match materials to your grades** — an all-armored core needs HQM in the TC, not just stone.
- **Keep it compact** — staying under ~65 blocks keeps you in the 10–15% brackets. Honeycomb adds defense but also upkeep.
- **Check the timer** — hovering the TC (or standing in privilege) shows "protected for X hours/days." If it reads hours, top up.
- A base with **no TC at all** decays immediately — never build a "TC-less" structure expecting it to last.

## Related

[[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Building Basics]] · [[Stability]] · [[Base Designs]] · [[Economy]]

pages.title: Windows Shutters and Frames
pages.body:
# Windows Shutters and Frames

**Wall frames** and **window frames** are building blocks with a hole you fill with a chosen insert. They let you make peek-holes, shooting ports, glass, and door/garage openings — without leaving an open gap.

## Frames vs walls

- A **wall** is solid.
- A **window** is a wall with a fixed window-sized slot near the top (good for peeking/shooting from cover).
- A **wall frame** is a wall that's almost entirely open — you fill it with one of: a **door**, **double door**, **garage door**, **window bars/glass**, **embrasure**, or **shutters**. Wall frames are the flexible workhorse for designing peeks, airlocks, and shooting floors.

Both window frames and wall frames are placed with the [[Building Basics|Building Plan]] and upgraded through the grade ladder like any block.

## Window/frame fillings (verified)

The five main fillings for a frame, with craft cost / HP / workbench:

| Insert | Craft cost | HP | WB | What it does |
|--------|-----------|---:|:--:|--------------|
| **Wooden Window Bars** | 100 wood | 250 | none | Cheap bars — blocks bodies, you can shoot out (and they can shoot in). Early game. |
| **Metal Window Bars** | 150 metal frags | 500 | WB1 | Reinforced bars; blocks players, lets projectiles through both ways. Standard cheap peek. |
| **Wood Shutters** | 200 wood | 200 | WB1 | Open/close wooden shutters — sight/shooting port you can close. Flammable. |
| **Metal Horizontal Embrasure** | 200 metal frags | 500 | WB1 | A barred horizontal slot you shoot **out** of while protected — classic defensive shooting port. |
| **Metal Vertical Embrasure** | 200 metal frags | 500 | WB1 | Vertical-slot version of the above. |
| **Strengthened Glass Window** | 50 metal frags | 350 | WB2 | See through, but **cracks/breaks** under fire and bodies can't pass; cheaper glass. |
| **Reinforced Glass Window** | 4 HQM | 500 | WB3 | See out, **nobody can shoot through either direction**. Great for safe loot-room sightlines. |

(Embrasures and metal bars are the bread-and-butter for **shooting floors** and **peek-defense**; reinforced glass is for **watching** without exposing a shooting hole.)

## Garage-door frame

The **Garage Door** ([[Doors and Locks]]) requires a **garage-door wall frame** (`wall.frame.garagedoor`, WB2). It's the standard piece for vehicle bays and [[Bunkers|garage-door bunkers]] because it rolls up flush with no swing gap and resists splash damage through adjacent walls.

## Design uses

- **Shooting floor / peek**: a ring of metal embrasures around your second floor lets you shoot down on raiders while behind walls.
- **Airlock window**: a metal-bars frame in an airlock lets you shoot anyone trapped in the chamber.
- **Loot-room sightline**: reinforced glass so you can watch a corridor without giving raiders a hole to shoot through.
- **Cheap early defense**: wooden/metal window bars cover gaps before you can afford embrasures.

## Returning-player note

Window/frame items are largely unchanged from 2023. The notable adjacent additions are **[[Deployables|Wallpaper]]** (Sep 2024, decorates walls) and the ongoing relevance of embrasure peeks given the **Sep 2025 gunshot-audibility** change (shots heard 400/500/600 m by weapon class) — peeking from an embrasure now gives away your position at range.

## Related

[[Doors and Locks]] · [[Building Basics]] · [[Soft Side]] · [[Roof Access and Peaks]] · [[Base Designs]]

pages.title: Ammo Recipes
pages.body:
# Ammo Recipes

Every ammunition recipe in **Rust** (2026), plus the gunpowder math everything is built on. Ammo is crafted at a **Mixing Table** (for the gunpowder-heavy types) or at a [[Workbenches|workbench]]. Costs verified June 2026.

## Gunpowder — the base of all ammo

| Recipe | Output |
|---|---|
| **30 Charcoal + 20 Sulfur** | **10 Gunpowder** (2s craft) |

Charcoal comes free from burning wood in furnaces/campfires; sulfur from sulfur ore or sulfur nodes. Gunpowder is then the main ingredient in nearly every bullet and explosive. See [[Explosive Recipes]] for the raiding side.

## Bullet recipes

| Ammo | Recipe | Output | Tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pistol Bullet** | 10 metal frags + 5 gunpowder | 4 | T1 |
| **5.56 Rifle Ammo** | 10 metal frags + 5 gunpowder | 3 | T2 |
| **HV 5.56 Rifle Ammo** | 10 metal frags + 20 gunpowder | 2 | T3 |
| **Explosive 5.56 Ammo** | metal frags + gunpowder + sulfur (mixing table) | varies | T3 |
| **12 Gauge Buckshot** | 6 metal frags + 4 gunpowder | (per craft) | T1 |
| **12 Gauge Slug** | 10 metal frags + 5 gunpowder | — | T2 |
| **Handmade Shell** | 4 metal frags + 6 gunpowder + 4 stone | — | primitive |
| **Nailgun Nails** | metal frags | — | T1 |
| **Incendiary 5.56** | 5.56 + sulfur + low-grade | — | T3 |
| **Incendiary Pistol** | pistol bullet + sulfur + low-grade | — | T2 |
| **HV Pistol Ammo** | metal frags + extra gunpowder | — | T2 |

> [!note] Explosive 5.56 is the cheap raiding ammo
> Explosive 5.56 ("explo ammo") is a primary soft-side raiding tool — fired from an AK/Semi to chew doors and walls. It's crafted at a mixing table after learning the Explosives BP. Cost and raid efficiency are detailed in [[Explosive Recipes]] and the raiding agent's raid-cost page.

## Arrows & primitive ammo

| Ammo | Recipe |
|---|---|
| **Wooden Arrow** | 25 wood + 10 stone -> 2 |
| **Bone Arrow** | 10 wood + 10 bone fragments -> 2 |
| **High Velocity Arrow** | 5 wood + 5 metal frags |
| **Fire Arrow** | wooden arrow + cloth + low-grade |

## The gunpowder bottleneck

Because every meaningful bullet needs gunpowder, **sulfur is the real currency of PvP**. A solo planning to PvP/raid should be mining sulfur and running a mixing table constantly. Rough mental math:

- 1 gunpowder = ~2 sulfur-equivalent (20 sulfur -> 10 GP).
- A stack of 5.56 (128) at 5 GP per 3 rounds â‰ˆ 213 GP â‰ˆ 426 sulfur for a full stack.

## Returning-player notes

- **Mixing Table** consolidated ammo/gunpowder crafting (you don't hand-mix in inventory for the gunpowder-heavy stuff).
- New since 2023: ammo for the **High Calibre Revolver** uses 5.56; **Handmade SMG** uses pistol ammo. Plan sulfur accordingly.

## Related

[[Explosive Recipes]] · [[Weapon Recipes]] · [[Crafting Basics]] · [[Tech Tree]]

pages.title: Blueprint Fragments
pages.body:
# Blueprint Fragments

**Blueprint Fragments** are a crafting ingredient added in the **Oct 2025 "Meta Shift"** update and kept in **Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die."** They are *the* gate on workbench progression now: no amount of scrap will build you a [[Workbench Level 2]] or [[Workbench Level 3]] without them. This is the single biggest structural change a 2023 returner runs into.

There are two kinds:

| Fragment | Used for | Tier of source |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic Blueprint Fragment** | [[Workbench Level 2]] (needs **5**) | green/blue card puzzle monuments, low/mid crates |
| **Advanced Blueprint Fragment** | [[Workbench Level 3]] (needs **5**) | elite crates, red-card / top-tier monuments, hackable crates |

**Conversion:** 20 Basic Fragments craft into 1 Advanced Fragment. So a WB3's 5 Advanced Fragments = 100 Basic Fragments if you grind the long way (you almost never should — go to elite monuments instead).

## Where to find Basic Blueprint Fragments

"Damaged diagrams" for a T2 bench. Guaranteed spawns at green/blue puzzle monuments:

| Source | Approx. yield |
|---|---|
| [[Underwater Labs]] | ~4 |
| [[Power Plant]] | ×3 |
| [[Train Yard]] | ×3 |
| [[Water Treatment Plant]] | ×3 |
| [[Airfield]] | ×2 |
| [[Arctic Research Base]] | ×2 |
| [[Airdrop\|Supply Drop]] | ×2 |
| Lower-tier monuments ([[Ferry Terminal]], [[Radtown]], [[Harbor]]) | 1 each |
| **[[Metal Detector]]** on roads/rails | 6.1% chance per dig |
| Recycling a [[Workbench Level 2]] | 2-3 (recycler type dependent) |

A WB2 needs only **5 Basic Fragments** — that's typically one or two monument runs. Don't overthink it.

**Metal Detector dig table (roads/rails, verified vs [[rusthelp.com]] June 2026)** — the fragment is the rare hit, but the dig is also a quiet scrap/HQM faucet:

| Dig result | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| Metal Fragments | 20–25 | 30.3% |
| Road Signs | 4–5 | 30.3% |
| High Quality Metal | 3–5 | 18.2% |
| [[Scrap]] | 7–13 | 9.1% |
| **Basic Blueprint Fragment** | 1 | **6.1%** |
| Road Sign Jacket / Gloves | 1 | 3% each |

So ~1 in 16 successful digs yields a Basic Fragment — a viable low-PvP supplement for a solo, but slower than a single puzzle-monument loot room (×3 guaranteed).

## Where to find Advanced Blueprint Fragments

Tied to top-tier monuments and elite loot. Guaranteed in **Hackable Crate** events; common in **Elite Crates**:

- [[Launch Site]]
- [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] (red keycard)
- [[Underwater Labs]] (elite crates)
- [[Military Tunnels]]
- [[Small Oil Rig]] / [[Large Oil Rig]] (hackable crate guarantees one)

A WB3 needs **5 Advanced Fragments**. Realistically that's a few oil rig / launch site runs, or buying time at a [[Bradley APC]] / heli farm to fund the elite-monument trips.

## How they work

- Fragments are a normal stackable inventory item — they drop on death like anything else.
- They are **not** the same as learning a blueprint. You still pay scrap (tech tree / [[Research Table]]) to learn the *items*. Fragments only build the *bench*.
- They survive a wipe? No — everything wipes monthly, fragments included. Each wipe you re-farm.

## Returning-player gotcha

In 2023 you'd dump ~500-1,250 scrap to upgrade a bench. In 2026 scrap does nothing for that — you **must** do a monument puzzle run to get fragments. If you're sitting on scrap wondering why the WB2 craft is greyed out, that's why: you're missing the 5 Basic Fragments.

## Related

[[Workbenches]] · [[Workbench Level 2]] · [[Workbench Level 3]] · [[Blueprints]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Blueprints
pages.body:
# Blueprints

A **blueprint (BP)** is the permanent knowledge of how to craft an item. You can have every resource for an Assault Rifle in your inventory, but without the blueprint learned you can't craft it. This page covers what's free, how you learn BPs, and the rules that bit returning players hardest in 2025-2026.

## The two big changes since 2023

1. **Blueprints force-wipe every month.** Since the Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die" update, the first-Thursday wipe resets **both the map and every player's blueprints** (it used to be map-only on most "blueprint wipe optional" servers — now the official cycle wipes BPs every wipe). You re-learn everything from scratch each wipe. This was confirmed again with the June 2026 "Built Different" wipe.
2. **Research costs were slashed** to make re-learning painless: 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 scrap by rarity (down from 20 / 75 / 125 / 500). See [[Tech Tree]].

> [!note] Why the change
> Facepunch wanted the meta to "pivot" each wipe instead of zerg clans snowballing identical loadouts. Cheap research + monthly BP wipe means everyone re-progresses, but fast.

## Three ways to learn a blueprint

| Method | Cost | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **[[Tech Tree]]** | scrap (15/30/60/120 by rarity) | unlocks for you only | cheapest if you follow a path; needs the matching [[Workbenches\|workbench]] |
| **[[Research Table]]** | scrap (per-rarity 15/30/60/120 since Nov 2025 — same scale as the tech tree now; old 75/250/500 per-tier is dead) + 1 copy of the item | a **shareable** paper blueprint | destroys the item; the BP can be handed to a teammate |
| **Default** | free | always known | basic survival/building tier (see below) |

You do **not** combine these for one item — pick whichever is cheaper/available. Tech tree is almost always cheaper per item; research table is for when you found a gun you can't yet path to, or want to share a BP with your duo/trio.

## What's default-craftable (no BP needed)

These are known from spawn every wipe — the "naked-to-base" essentials:

- **Tools:** Rock, Torch, Stone Hatchet, Stone Pickaxe, Salvaged tools require BPs but the stone tier is free
- **Building:** Building Plan + Hammer, Wood/Stone/sheet upgrades, [[Tool Cupboard]], wooden door, wooden barricades, sleeping bag, campfire, furnace, small stash
- **Workbench Level 1 itself** — free recipe (you just need 500 wood + 100 metal frags)
- **Early weapons:** Bow, Wooden/Stone spear, Salvaged tools (no — these need BP), Bone Knife/Club, Hunting Bow
- **Basic clothing:** burlap set, bandage, basic medical

Everything beyond this — guns, components, T2/T3 tools, explosives, electricity, most armor — must be re-learned each wipe via tech tree or research.

## The Blueprint Fragment layer (separate from learning BPs)

Do not confuse *learning a blueprint* with *building a higher workbench*. They're separate gates:

- **Learning a BP** = scrap (tech tree / research table).
- **Tiering up your bench** = **[[Blueprint Fragments]]** (a physical crafting ingredient), not scrap. WB2 needs 5 Basic Fragments; WB3 needs 5 Advanced Fragments.

You need the right **workbench tier present** to *research* tier-locked items too — so you can't research a T3 gun until you have a [[Workbench Level 3]] built.

## Tips for the monthly grind

- Hoard scrap the day before wipe is pointless (it wipes). Hoard nothing — plan your *route* instead. See [[Progression Route]].
- The cheap research costs mean a single [[Bradley APC]] or heli loot run funds most of your T3 unlocks.
- In a duo/trio, use the [[Research Table]] for the 2-3 key guns so one person researches and hands paper BPs to the others — saves total scrap vs. everyone tech-treeing separately.

## Related

[[Tech Tree]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Progression Route]] · [[Crafting Basics]]

pages.title: Building Recipes
pages.body:
# Building Recipes

Craft costs for **Rust** building blocks, deployables, and base-security items (2026). Building blocks are placed with the Hammer + Building Plan and then **upgraded** in tiers (twig -> wood -> stone -> sheet metal -> armored). This page covers the deployables and locks that gate your base; for raid-defense numbers see the building/raiding agent pages.

## Core base deployables

| Item | Recipe | Tier | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tool Cupboard (TC)** | 1,000 wood | default | the base's privilege/decay anchor — place first |
| **Workbench Level 1** | 500 wood + 100 metal frags | default | see [[Workbench Level 1]] |
| **Workbench Level 2** | 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + 5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments\|frags]] | T1 | see [[Workbench Level 2]] |
| **Workbench Level 3** | 1,000 metal frags + 100 HQM + 5 Advanced frags | T2 | see [[Workbench Level 3]] |

| **Small Stash** | 10 cloth | default | hideable cache |
| **Wood Storage Box** | 100 wood | default | 12 slots |
| **Large Wood Box** | 250 wood | default | 30 slots / 48 slots |
| **Furnace** | 200 wood + 100 stone + 50 low-grade | default | smelting |
| **Large Furnace** | 600 stone + 400 wood + 50 low-grade | T1 | bulk smelting |
| **Campfire** | 5 wood | default | cooking/heat |

## Doors & locks (base security)

| Item | Recipe | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| **Wooden Door** | 300 wood | default |

## QoL & storage (new-ish)

## Raid-alarm & defense (May 2026 additions)
