pages.title: Crafting & Progression
pages.body:
# Crafting & Progression

Overview hub for **Rust** crafting and the progression ladder as of the **"Built Different"** wipe (live **June 4 2026**, Unity 6). This is the part of Rust that changed the most since 2023 — read [[Blueprints]] and [[Tech Tree]] first if you're returning.

> [!important] What a returning player must know (2023 -> 2026)
> - The **scrap-only grind is dead.** Tiering up your bench now needs **[[Blueprint Fragments]]** farmed at monuments, not a pile of scrap.
> - **Workbenches no longer cost scrap to craft** (Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die"). They cost wood/metal/HQM + fragments.
> - **Research costs were slashed** to 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 scrap (from 20 / 75 / 125 / 500).
> - **Blueprints force-wipe every month** with the map now. You re-learn everything each wipe.
> - May 2026 added 9 rare **[[Workbench Augmentations]]** as an endgame chase.

## The current progression loop (one-line version)

Gather -> craft **[[Workbench Level 1]]** (no scrap) -> research cheap T1 gear at a **[[Research Table]]** or [[Tech Tree]] -> hunt **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]** at monuments -> build **[[Workbench Level 2]]** -> grab guns/components -> hunt **Advanced Fragments** at elite monuments -> **[[Workbench Level 3]]** -> AK / explosives / endgame.

See the full solo walkthrough: **[[Progression Route]]**.

## Pages in this folder

### Core systems
- [[Crafting Basics]] — how crafting works, workbench aura, bulk crafting, repair, recycling
- [[Workbenches]] — the three benches, exact craft costs, what each tier unlocks
- [[Tech Tree]] — branching unlock paths, exact per-rarity scrap costs (15/30/60/120)
- [[Research Table]] — reverse-engineer items into shareable blueprints (per-rarity 15/30/60/120 scrap since Nov 2025; old flat 75/250/500 is dead)
- [[Blueprints]] — what's default-craftable, the monthly BP wipe, fragment system
- [[Blueprint Fragments]] — Basic vs Advanced, where they drop, conversion ratio
- [[Workbench Augmentations]] — the rare bench upgrades (live May 7 2026; "nine" marketed, ten item pages exist incl. Surplus)
- [[Workbench Level 1]] · [[Workbench Level 2]] · [[Workbench Level 3]] — per-bench detail pages

### Recipe reference (by category)
- [[Tool Recipes]] — gathering tools, salvaged tools, hammers, building tools
- [[Building Recipes]] — workbenches, TC, foundations, doors, locks
- [[Weapon Recipes]] — guns by workbench tier with HQM/spring/component costs
- [[Ammo Recipes]] — gunpowder math and every bullet recipe
- [[Explosive Recipes]] — satchel/C4/rocket craft costs (cross-links the raiding pages)
- [[Medical Recipes]] — bandages, syringes, medkits, tea

### Smelting
- [[Smelting & Furnaces]] — the daily-loop lookup: wood-per-smelt, wood-to-charcoal ratio, slot mechanics, how many furnaces, all furnace types
- [[Large Furnace]] — 18-slot batch smelter, fuel savings, placement limits
- [[Electric Furnace]] — wood-free smelting on electricity (no charcoal, no HQM)
- [[Refining HQM]] — how to smelt High Quality Metal (furnace, NOT the oil refinery)

### Guide
- [[Progression Route]] — fastest solo path to T2 and T3, hour by hour

## Quick-reference numbers (verified June 2026)

| Thing | Cost |
|---|---|
| Workbench L1 | 500 wood + 100 metal frags (no scrap) |
| Workbench L2 | 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + **5 Basic Fragments** |
| Workbench L3 | 1,000 metal frags + 100 HQM + **5 Advanced Fragments** |
| Tech-tree unlock (common) | 15 scrap |
| Tech-tree unlock (uncommon) | 30 scrap |
| Tech-tree unlock (rare) | 60 scrap |
| Tech-tree unlock (very rare) | 120 scrap |
| Research Table BP (per rarity) | 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 scrap (reduced Nov 2025 to match the tech tree; old 75/250/500 is dead) |
| 20 Basic Fragments | = 1 Advanced Fragment |
| Wood per 1,000 metal ore (small furnace) | ~500 wood |
| Wood-to-charcoal ratio | ~75% (1,000 wood -> ~750 charcoal) |
| Ore-to-refined ratio | always 1:1 |
| HQM smelt time | 10 s/ore (4x metal/sulfur) — see [[Refining HQM]] |

> [!note] Patch volatility
> Rust force-wipes the **first Thursday of every month**. Research-cost numbers above are from the Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die" rebalance and were unchanged through the June 2026 "Built Different" wipe. Re-verify against [rusthelp.com](https://rusthelp.com) at the next major progression patch.

pages.title: Crafting Basics
pages.body:
# Crafting Basics

How crafting actually works in **Rust** as of 2026. Read this alongside [[Blueprints]] (what you're allowed to craft) and [[Workbenches]] (where).

## The core loop

1. **Gather** raw resources (wood, stone, metal ore -> smelt to [[Metal Fragments|metal fragments]] / [[High Quality Metal|HQM]], sulfur, cloth, etc.).
2. **Learn** the item ([[Tech Tree]] or [[Research Table]] — costs scrap; default items are free).
3. **Stand at the right [[Workbenches|workbench]]** tier (or anywhere for no-bench items).
4. **Craft.** Queue stacks; the game crafts them one at a time.

## Workbench aura

Tier-locked items require you to be **inside the workbench's glowing range** while crafting. Step out and the craft pauses/cancels for queued items. The [[Workbench Augmentations|Range]] augment doubles this radius. Higher benches also **craft faster** (most items halve per tier).

## Bulk crafting

- You can queue many copies at once; resources are consumed up front per item as each starts.
- Cancelling a queued (not-yet-started) craft **refunds** its materials.
- The [[Workbench Augmentations|Efficiency]] augment gives a 10% chance of an extra item per stack craft; **Accelerated** speeds each subsequent item.

## Smelting & refining (feeds crafting)

- **Furnace / Large Furnace:** metal ore -> metal fragments; HQM ore -> HQM; sulfur ore -> sulfur. Needs wood as fuel.
- **Mixing Table:** combine charcoal + sulfur into gunpowder, and craft most ammo/explosives. See [[Ammo Recipes]] and [[Explosive Recipes]].
- **Cooking Workbench (Mar 2025):** cooks food and 8 buff pies; food now spoils (raw 6h / cooked 24h, paused in powered fridges).

## Recycling (the other half of progression)

Recyclers break items into components/scrap. The May 2024 split:

| Recycler | Cycle | Yield |
|---|---|---|
| Safe-zone (Outpost/Bandit) | 8s | 80% |
| Monument | 5s | **120%** |

Recycle loot for scrap (to fund [[Tech Tree]] / [[Research Table]]) and components (springs, gears, metal blades, tech trash) that gate weapon crafting. Recycling a [[Workbench Level 2]] returns 2-3 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]].

## Components — the real bottleneck

Many craftable guns need **components** you can't craft: **Metal Springs**, **Gears**, **Metal Blades**, **Rifle Body**, **SMG Body**, **Semi-Automatic Body**, **Tech Trash**, **Sheet Metal**, **Road Signs**. These come from loot crates and recycling. Springs in particular bottleneck firearm production — hoard them. See [[Weapon Recipes]].

## Repair Bench

A **Repair Bench** (deployable) repairs damaged weapons/tools/armor using a fraction of their craft cost. You need the item's blueprint learned to repair it. Cheaper than recrafting.

## Returning-player notes

- The big mental shift: **scrap is cheap to spend now** (research slashed), so the bottleneck moved to **fragments** (bench tiers) and **components** (guns). Plan loot runs around those, not around hoarding scrap.
- Food spoilage and the Cooking Workbench are new (Mar 2025) — your meat rots; cook it or fridge it.

## Related

[[Blueprints]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Progression Route]] · [[Ammo Recipes]]

pages.title: Electric Furnace
pages.body:
# Electric Furnace

A **wood-free** smelter that runs on electricity. Wire it to [[Solar Panel]]s, batteries, or a generator and it smelts metal/sulfur **hands-off, forever, with zero wood cost** — the endgame upgrade once you have an electricity setup. The catch: **no charcoal** and **can't smelt HQM**.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | **500** |
| Power draw | **3 [[Rust Watts|rW]]** |
| Fuel | Electricity (no wood) |
| Slots | Small — **2 ore inputs** smelting in parallel + output slots |
| Workbench required | **T2** ([[Workbench Level 2]]) |
| Craft cost | **5 [[High Quality Metal]] + 200 [[Metal Fragments]]** |
| Craft time | 25 s (WB2) / 12 s (WB3) |
| Smelts | Metal ore, Sulfur ore — **NOT HQM** |
| Charcoal | **None** (burns no wood) |

## The trade-offs

**Pros**
- **Zero wood.** Once powered, smelting is free — no chopping trees, no refueling.
- Set-and-forget: never stalls for fuel as long as power flows.
- Same per-ore smelt speed as a wood furnace (2.5 s metal/sulfur).

**Cons**
- **No charcoal** — and charcoal is half of [[Gunpowder]]. If you go all-electric you'll starve your ammo/raid supply. Keep at least one wood [[Smelting & Furnaces|furnace]] or campfire running for charcoal.
- **Cannot smelt [[High Quality Metal Ore|HQM]]** — do HQM in a small or [[Large Furnace]].
- Needs an **electricity build** (3 rW) — solar + battery, or a [[Generator]]. Dead until powered.
- Smaller capacity than a [[Large Furnace]] (only 2 ore inputs).

## When to use it
Mid-to-late wipe, once you have solar/batteries: park electric furnaces on your base's power grid for free passive metal/sulfur. Pair with a wood [[Large Furnace]] for HQM and charcoal.

## See also
- [[Smelting & Furnaces]] (full mechanics + ratios) · [[Large Furnace]] · [[Refining HQM]]
- [[Solar Panel]] · [[Rust Watts]] · [[Workbench Level 2]] · [[Gunpowder]]

pages.title: Explosive Recipes
pages.body:
# Explosive Recipes

Craft costs for **Rust** raiding explosives (2026). This page is the **crafting recipe** reference; for *how many* of each to break a given wall/door (raid costs), see the raiding agent's raid-cost pages — these are cross-linked. Everything here is built on **gunpowder** and **sulfur**; see [[Ammo Recipes]] for the gunpowder recipe.

> [!important] Explosive protection is capped at 75% (May 2025)
> No matter how a base is built, structures can mitigate at most 75% of explosive damage. This changed raid math in 2025 — factor it into any raid-cost lookup.

## The build-up chain

| Item | Recipe | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Gunpowder** | 30 charcoal + 20 sulfur -> 10 | base ingredient |
| **Explosives** | 50 gunpowder + 3 low-grade fuel + 10 sulfur + 10 metal frags | the intermediate; feeds C4 & rockets |
| **[[Timed Explosive Charge\|C4 (Timed Explosive Charge)]]** | **20 explosives + 5 cloth + 2 tech trash** | â‰ˆ **2,200 sulfur** all-in per C4; T3 |
| **Rocket** | explosives + metal pipe + low-grade | fired from Rocket Launcher; T3 |
| **Satchel Charge** | 4 beancan grenades + 1 small stash + 1 rope | T2; cheap door/wall opener |
| **Beancan Grenade** | 60 gunpowder + 20 metal frags | feeds satchels; can dud |
| **Explosive 5.56 Ammo** | metal frags + gunpowder + sulfur | the "soft-side" raiding ammo (T3) |
| **40mm HE Grenade** | (for grenade launcher) gunpowder + metal frags | |
| **F1 Grenade** | 40 gunpowder + 25 metal frags | anti-personnel |

## Full sulfur cost of one C4

C4 = 20 explosives + 5 cloth + 2 tech trash. Each explosive needs 50 gunpowder (+ 10 sulfur + 10 metal frags + 3 low-grade). The gunpowder for 20 explosives is 1,000 gunpowder = 2,000 sulfur, plus 200 sulfur direct in the explosives -> **~2,200 sulfur per C4** (plus the cloth and tech trash). This is why C4 is reserved for hard walls.

## Tiering & where they're learned

- **Satchels / beancans** = [[Workbench Level 2]] — your first raiding tools.
- **C4 / rockets / explosive 5.56** = [[Workbench Level 3]], learned via [[Tech Tree]] (very-rare = 120 scrap each node) after you have a WB3.
- Tech trash and metal pipes are **looted components** — recycle electrical/road loot for them.

## Raiding cost cross-reference

For the number of rockets/C4/satchels/explo-ammo to break each structure tier, and the cheapest tool per wall, see the raiding pages (e.g. [[Raid Costs]], [[C4]], [[Rocket]], [[Satchel Charge]]). Remember the **75% explosive-protection cap** when reading any of those.

> [!note] Some intermediate recipe quantities above (rocket, satchel sub-components) are the commonly-cited 2026 values; re-verify exact numbers on [rusthelp.com](https://rusthelp.com) for a precise sulfur farm. The C4 (2,200 sulfur) and explosives (50 GP) figures are confirmed.

## Related

[[Ammo Recipes]] · [[Crafting Basics]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Workbench Level 3]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Large Furnace
pages.body:
# Large Furnace

The big batch smelter. Holds **18 slots** (3x the small [[Smelting & Furnaces|Furnace]]) and burns **far less total wood per ore** when run full — the go-to for serious metal/sulfur farms and the **only practical way to smelt [[High Quality Metal Ore|HQM]] at scale**.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | **1,500** |
| Slots | **18** |
| Fuel | Wood |
| Workbench required | **T2** ([[Workbench Level 2]]) |
| Craft cost | **500 Stone + 600 Wood + 75 [[Low Grade Fuel]]** |
| Craft time | 25 s (WB2) / 12 s (WB3) |
| Tech-tree cost | ~390 scrap |
| Outpost price | 350 scrap |
| Smelts | Metal ore, Sulfur ore, **HQM ore** |

## Why it's worth it

- **Slots:** 18 vs the small furnace's 6 — smelts a dozen+ ore stacks in parallel off a single wood stack.
- **Fuel efficiency (full vs a small furnace):** ~**40%** the wood for **metal**, ~**80%** for **sulfur**, ~**one-third** for **HQM**.
- **HQM:** clears HQM roughly **5x faster** than a small furnace. If you process HQM regularly, this pays for itself.

## Standard overnight layout
- 1 slot: ~1,000 wood
- 1 slot: empty (charcoal/overflow)
- ~13-16 slots: stacks of 200 ore

Smelt rates are **per-ore identical** to a small furnace (2.5 s metal/sulfur, 10 s HQM) — the win is purely parallelism + fuel.

## Placement limits
- **Must be placed on open terrain.** It **cannot** sit on a building foundation, inside caves, or in tight build zones. Plan a flat outdoor spot inside your walls/compound.

## Charcoal
Like all wood furnaces, ~**75%** of wood burned becomes [[Gunpowder|Charcoal]] (1,000 wood -> ~750 charcoal). Leave an output slot free.

## See also
- [[Smelting & Furnaces]] (full mechanics + ratios) · [[Electric Furnace]] · [[Refining HQM]]
- [[High Quality Metal]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Workbench Level 2]]

pages.title: Medical Recipes
pages.body:
# Medical Recipes

Craft costs for **Rust** healing items (2026). Medical is cheap and high-value — a solo should always carry bandages + a syringe or two. Cloth and low-grade fuel are the main ingredients.

## Healing items

| Item | Recipe | Heals | Tier | BP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bandage** | 4 cloth | stops bleeding + small heal over time | default | free |
| **Medical Syringe** | 15 cloth + 10 metal frags + 10 low-grade fuel | +15 instantly then +15 over time (~delay) | T1 | yes |
| **Large Medkit** | 2 medical syringes + 10 low-grade fuel | **+100 HP** immediately + stops bleeding to 100 | T1 | yes |
| **Anti-Radiation Pills** | components | reduces radiation | T1 | |
| **Blood Bag** | (from blood draws) | self-heal store | T1 | |

Notes:
- The **Large Medkit** heal is **immediate**, unlike the syringe's delayed tick — it's the panic button.
- Recycling: a syringe returns 8 cloth + 5 metal frags + 5 low-grade; a large medkit returns 5 low-grade + 1 syringe.

## Food & buff items (Mar 2025 Crafting Update)

The **Cooking Workbench** added 8 buff pies and proper cooking. Food now **spoils** (raw 6h / cooked 24h; paused in a powered fridge). Cooked food and tea give stat buffs:

| Item | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Buff Pies (8 types)** | various combat/gather/health buffs (cooked at Cooking Workbench) |
| **Teas (advanced healing/scrap/ore/wood/PvP)** | brewed buffs — e.g. healing tea over-heals, scrap tea boosts recycle yield |
| **Cooked Meat / Fish** | restores hunger + some HP |

Tea is a notable returning-player addition — a **Healing Tea** before a fight or **Scrap Tea** before recycling is a meaningful edge.

## Returning-player notes

- Carry **bandages** (4 cloth, free) at all times — bleed kills more often than bullets early.
- **Large Medkits** are the standard PvP heal; tech-tree them early (T1).
- **Food spoilage** is new (Mar 2025) — don't stockpile raw meat; cook it or use a powered **Mini Fridge** (18 slots).

> [!note] Recipe numbers above are confirmed 2026 values for bandage/syringe/large medkit. Tea and pie exact ingredients vary by type — look up the specific tea on [rusthelp.com](https://rusthelp.com) when you need a precise brew cost.

## Related

[[Crafting Basics]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Progression Route
pages.body:
# Progression Route

The fastest **solo (or duo/trio)** path from naked spawn to a Tier 3 base in **Rust** (2026 "Built Different" meta). This is the route that accounts for the post-2023 changes: cheap research but **[[Blueprint Fragments]]** gating your benches. Built for a returning solo/duo/trio player.

> [!important] The one rule that's different now
> Your bench tiers are gated by **fragments farmed at monuments**, not scrap. So progression = **gather a starter base, then go run monuments** for fragments + scrap. You cannot grind your way to a WB2/WB3 from your base alone.

## Phase 0 — Spawn (first ~15 min)

1. Punch nodes/trees with your rock; get **stone tools** (free).
2. Gather ~1,000 wood + stone. Place a **[[Tool Cupboard]]** (1,000 wood) and a small 2x1 or 2x2 base with a wooden door + **Code Lock** (you'll learn it shortly).
3. Place a **Sleeping Bag** (30 cloth) so you respawn home (cap is 15 bags).
4. Build a **Furnace** and start smelting metal ore.

## Phase 1 — Workbench Level 1 + first research (~30-45 min)

1. Craft **[[Workbench Level 1]]**: 500 wood + 100 metal frags (**no scrap**).
2. Gather **scrap** — hit roadside crates, barrels, and a small monument or two. You want ~150-300 scrap.
3. At WB1, **tech-tree the essentials** (cheap now — 15-30 scrap each): Code Lock, Hatchet, Pickaxe, [[Small Backpack]], Sleeping Bag upgrades, Large Furnace, **Medical Syringe / Large Medkit**, a starter gun (Revolver/Double Barrel/Crossbow).
4. Build a **[[Research Table]]** (200 metal frags + 20 scrap) only if you want to share BPs (duo/trio) or research a found item.

You now have a defensible base, tools, and a sidearm. This is the cheapest, fastest power spike in the game post-Pivot-Or-Die.

## Phase 2 — Basic Fragments -> Workbench Level 2 (~1-2 hr)

This is the new step returners must internalize. You need **5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]**.

1. Run a **green/blue card monument**: [[Power Plant]], [[Train Yard]], or [[Water Treatment Plant]] give **×3 Basic Fragments** each. [[Underwater Labs]] gives ~4. One or two runs = your 5.
2. While there, grab **scrap**, **components** (springs, gears, bodies), and a [[Blue Keycard]] / [[Green Keycard]] for the puzzle.
3. Bank **20 HQM** + 500 metal frags.
4. Craft **[[Workbench Level 2]]**: 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + 5 Basic Fragments.

At WB2, tech-tree your real loadout: **Thompson** (best T2 cost/DPS) or **Semi-Auto Rifle**, **Salvaged tools**, **Sheet Metal Door** + **[[Garage Door]]**, **satchel charges** (first raiding tool), **metal facemask + road sign armor**, **Mixing Table** for ammo.

## Phase 3 — Sulfur + a working gun (parallel to Phase 2/4)

- Mine **sulfur**; run a **Mixing Table** to make **gunpowder** (30 charcoal + 20 sulfur -> 10 GP).
- Craft a stack of **5.56** (10 metal frags + 5 GP -> 3 rounds) or pistol ammo.
- You're now PvP-capable. Defend monument runs and counter-roam.

## Phase 4 — Advanced Fragments -> Workbench Level 3 (~2-4 hr in)

Need **5 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]**.

1. Hit **elite monuments**: [[Launch Site]], [[Oil Rig|Small/Large Oil Rig]] (a hackable crate guarantees one), [[Military Tunnels]], [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] (red card). Each elite/hackable crate yields Advanced Fragments.
2. Alternatively kill **[[Bradley APC]]** at Launch Site or the **Patrol Helicopter** for big scrap/component hauls to fund the trips.
3. Bank **100 HQM** + 1,000 metal frags.
4. Craft **[[Workbench Level 3]]**.

At WB3, tech-tree: **AK-47 (Assault Rifle)**, **Bolt Action Rifle**, **explosive 5.56**, **C4** + **Rockets** (for hard raids), HV ammo, high-tier armor crafting. See [[Weapon Recipes]] and [[Explosive Recipes]].

## Phase 5 — Endgame chase

- Run monuments for **[[Workbench Augmentations]]** (May 2026) — Salvage (-20% research), Recycle Bin, Efficiency, Reinforced for your main bench.
- Stockpile **sulfur** for raids; remember the **75% explosive-protection cap**.
- Each **first-Thursday wipe** you re-run this whole route — but it's fast: cheap research means one good loot day rebuilds a full loadout.

## Solo vs. duo/trio differences

| | Solo | Duo/Trio |
|---|---|---|
| Fragments | farm all yourself; aim small (5 Basic is one run) | split monument duties; faster |
| BPs | tech-tree only (cheapest) | use [[Research Table]] to share key guns (one researches AK, hands paper BPs) |
| Raiding | satchels/explo-ammo soft-side; C4 sparingly | can afford rocket/C4 raids sooner |
| Base | small + hidden; don't over-build | bigger, more turrets (40m interference cap) |

## Time-to-tier cheat sheet

| Milestone | Gate | Rough time (solo) |
|---|---|---|
| WB1 + tools + sidearm | 100 metal frags + ~200 scrap | 30-45 min |
| WB2 + Thompson/Semi | **5 Basic Fragments** + 20 HQM | 1-2 hr |
| PvP-ready (gun + ammo) | sulfur + mixing table | ~2 hr |
| WB3 + AK | **5 Advanced Fragments** + 100 HQM | 3-5 hr |

## Related

[[Blueprints]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Weapon Recipes]] · [[Explosive Recipes]] · [[Crafting Basics]]

pages.title: Refining HQM
pages.body:
# Refining HQM

The dedicated lookup for **High Quality Metal**, because returning players reliably get this wrong. The headline:

> [!important] HQM is smelted in a FURNACE, not the Oil Refinery
> **[[High Quality Metal Ore]]** goes into a normal **small or [[Large Furnace]]** and smelts **1:1** into **[[High Quality Metal]]** (HQM). The [[Oil Refinery]] has **nothing to do with HQM** — it only turns [[Crude Oil]] into [[Low Grade Fuel]]. The word "refinery" is the trap.

## The numbers

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| Smelt time per HQM ore | **10 seconds** (4x slower than metal/sulfur's 2.5 s) |
| Ore -> HQM ratio | **1 : 1** |
| Smeltable in small furnace? | Yes |
| Smeltable in [[Large Furnace]]? | Yes — ~5x faster, ~1/3 the wood |
| Smeltable in [[Electric Furnace]]? | **No** (wood furnaces only) |
| Wood per HQM ore | ~same baseline as other ore, but the **10 s burn** makes it the wood/time bottleneck |

Because HQM smelts **4x slower**, it is always the slowest thing in your furnace. 1,000 HQM ore in a single slot = **~167 minutes**. So:

> [!tip] Always split HQM across many slots / use a Large Furnace
> Spread HQM ore across multiple slots (parallel smelting) or run it in a [[Large Furnace]]. The large furnace clears HQM ~**5x faster** and uses ~**one-third** the wood of a small furnace — the single biggest reason to build one.

## Where HQM ore comes from
- **Mining HQM nodes** — the dark, sparkly metal ore rocks (need a [[Pickaxe]] / [[Jackhammer]]; gives a few HQM ore per node).
- **[[Quarry|HQM Quarry]]** — passive HQM ore over time (fuel with [[Low Grade Fuel]]).
- **[[Mining Outpost]]** monument / loot crates — small amounts.
- **Recycling components** at a [[Recycler]] — many components yield HQM directly (often faster than smelting ore; see [[Recyclers]]).

## What HQM is for
HQM is the gate to mid/late-game gear and strong building:
- **Armoured building tier** (the strongest base walls/doors)
- **Sheet Metal / Garage Doors, Armored Doors**
- **Guns & components** — many T2/T3 weapons need HQM (see [[Weapon Recipes]])
- **[[Electric Furnace]]** itself costs 5 HQM

## Quick chain
**Mine HQM ore -> small or [[Large Furnace]] (10 s/ore, 1:1) -> High Quality Metal.** No oil refinery involved.

## See also
- [[Smelting & Furnaces]] · [[Large Furnace]] · [[Electric Furnace]]
- [[High Quality Metal]] · [[High Quality Metal Ore]] · [[Quarry]] · [[Recyclers]]
- [[Oil Refinery]] (Low Grade Fuel only — NOT HQM)

pages.title: Research Table
pages.body:
# Research Table

The **Research Table** lets you reverse-engineer a found item into a permanent, **shareable** blueprint by spending scrap. It's the alternative to the [[Tech Tree]] and the only way to produce a paper BP you can hand to a teammate.

## Craft cost

| Resource | Amount |
|---|---|
| Metal Fragments | 200 |
| Scrap | 20 |

Requires **[[Workbench Level 1]]** to craft. Craft time: 15s (WB1) / 7.5s (WB2) / 3.75s (WB3).

## Research cost (current — reduced Nov 2025)

You pay scrap and **destroy one copy** of the item; out comes a learnable blueprint.

> [!important] The old 75 / 250 / 500 per-tier costs are dead
> The Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die" devblog states research-table costs were **"reduced to be in line with new workbench values."** That means the research table now charges the **same per-rarity scale as the [[Tech Tree]]** rather than the legacy flat 75/250/500 per-tier rate. (Verified June 2026 against the facepunch Pivot Or Die devblog; the 75/250/500 figures you'll still see on stale guides are pre-Nov-2025.)

| Rarity | Scrap to research (current) | Legacy (pre-Nov 2025) |
|---|---|---|
| Common | **15** | 75 (Tier 1) |
| Uncommon | **30** | — |
| Rare | **60** | 250 (Tier 2) |
| Very Rare | **120** | 500 (Tier 3) |

The headline change for a returning player: an AK that used to cost **500 scrap** to research is now in the **120-scrap (very rare)** band. The research table is no longer the expensive option — its only real downsides vs. the [[Tech Tree]] are that it **consumes a physical copy** of the item and requires the matching bench tier present.

> [!note] Different *trigger*, same *price* now
> The tech tree charges per rarity (15/30/60/120) and needs no item copy. The research table charges that same per-rarity scale but **requires a physical copy** of the item (consumed). For a solo, the tech tree is still the default. The research table wins when (a) you found a gun you can't yet path to in the tree, or (b) you want a paper BP to share.

## How to use it

1. Build the table at a [[Workbench Level 1]] (need the right bench tier present to research that tier's items).
2. Drop the item you want to learn into the table's input slot.
3. Pay the scrap; the item is consumed and you get a **blueprint paper**.
4. Learn it yourself, or hand the paper to a teammate to learn.

## Why it still matters in 2026

Even with cheap tech-tree costs, the research table is the **BP-sharing** tool:

- In a **duo/trio**, one person researches the AK once (120 scrap, very-rare band), then crafts paper BPs for the others — cheaper total scrap than everyone tech-treeing the full path separately, and instant (no path nodes to buy).
- It's also the fallback when you loot a high-tier gun early (e.g., off a dead player) but don't have the workbench/path to reach it in the tech tree yet — though you still need the matching bench tier to research it.

## Related

[[Tech Tree]] · [[Blueprints]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Workbench Level 1]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Smelting & Furnaces
pages.body:
# Smelting & Furnaces

The furnace is the **single most-used station in Rust** and the one a returning solo touches every play session. This page is the lookup for every number you ask out loud: *how much wood per smelt, what's the wood-to-charcoal ratio, how many furnaces do I need, large vs electric, how do I refine HQM.*

Smelting turns **ore** (mined from rocks, nodes, and quarries) into the refined materials that build your base and craft your guns:

| Raw ore | Smelts into | Smelt time per unit | Output ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Metal Ore | [[Metal Fragments]] | **2.5 s** | 1 : 1 |
| Sulfur Ore | Sulfur | **2.5 s** | 1 : 1 |
| [[High Quality Metal Ore]] | [[High Quality Metal]] (HQM) | **10 s** (4x slower) | 1 : 1 |

> [!important] The one thing to internalize
> **Ore-to-refined is always 1:1.** 1,000 metal ore -> 1,000 metal frags, every time. The *only* variable you control is **wood burned** (lower with a [[Large Furnace]], zero with an [[Electric Furnace]]) and **time** (lower by splitting ore across more slots / more furnaces). HQM smelts **4x slower** than metal/sulfur, so it is always your bottleneck.

---

## Furnace types at a glance

| Station | Fuel | Slots (total) | Smelts HQM? | Charcoal? | Craft cost | HP | Bench |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Campfire]] | Wood | 1 ore at a time | No (metal/food only) | Yes | 5 wood | — | None |
| **Furnace** (small) | Wood | 6 | **Yes** | Yes | 200 stone + 100 wood + 50 LGF | 500 | None (T0) |
| **[[Large Furnace]]** | Wood | 18 | **Yes** (the practical way) | Yes | 500 stone + 600 wood + 75 LGF | 1500 | T2 |
| **[[Electric Furnace]]** | Electricity (3 rW) | small (2 ore in) | No (metal/sulfur only) | **No** | 5 HQM + 200 metal frags | 500 | T2 |

(LGF = [[Low Grade Fuel]]. The small furnace is the **first thing you build every wipe** — it needs no workbench.)

---

## Wood per smelt — the core ratios

These are the numbers behind "how much wood do I need."

| Furnace | Wood per ore | Wood per 1,000 ore | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small Furnace | **~0.5 wood/ore** | **~500 wood** | The baseline everyone quotes |
| Large Furnace | ~0.7 wood/ore *raw*, but **~40% of a small furnace's total** when smelting efficiently | ~200 wood-equivalent for metal | Burns more wood per *tick* but smelts so many stacks at once that total wood drops hard |
| Electric Furnace | **0 wood** | 0 | Runs on 3 [[Rust Watts]]; needs solar/battery/generator |

**Large furnace fuel savings vs small (when full):** ~40% the wood for **metal ore**, ~80% for **sulfur**, and **~one-third** for **HQM**. That HQM number is why serious HQM smelting always happens in a large furnace.

> [!tip] More furnaces never costs more wood
> Splitting 10,000 sulfur across **5 small furnaces uses the same total wood as 1 furnace** — but finishes in **one-fifth the time**. Wood cost scales with *ore smelted*, not with *number of furnaces*. So for time-efficiency (which matters more than wood in Rust), build a furnace bank. The trade-off is the [[Low Grade Fuel]] to craft each one (50 LGF per small furnace).

---

## Wood-to-charcoal ratio

Every piece of wood burned in **any wood-fired smelter** (campfire, small furnace, large furnace) has **~75% chance to yield 1 Charcoal**.

- **1,000 wood burned -> ~750 charcoal**
- 5,000 wood -> ~3,750 charcoal

Charcoal is half of [[Gunpowder]] (gunpowder = 1 sulfur + 1 charcoal -> 2 gunpowder... see [[Ammo Recipes]]), so a normal smelting session passively stockpiles your raid/ammo charcoal. **Leave an output slot free** or the furnace fills with charcoal and stalls.

> [!warning] The Electric Furnace makes NO charcoal
> Because it burns no wood, the [[Electric Furnace]] produces **zero charcoal**. If you switch a base entirely to electric furnaces you will run dry on charcoal for [[Gunpowder]] — keep at least one wood furnace running, or burn wood in a campfire for charcoal.

---

## Slot mechanics (the most-misunderstood part)

Furnaces smelt **every ore slot simultaneously**. Filling more slots does NOT cost more wood per ore — it just finishes faster. But each furnace has a fixed slot count and you must reserve slots for fuel and output.

### Small Furnace — 6 slots
A practical layout reserves slots so the furnace doesn't choke:
- **1 slot** = wood (fuel)
- **1-2 slots** = output (refined material + charcoal land here as the input stacks shrink)
- **~3 slots** = ore being smelted

Common efficient fill: **1,000 wood + ~3 stacks of ore.** With ~600 metal ore in, a full small furnace burns ~1,000 wood and yields **600 metal frags + ~750 charcoal**.

### Large Furnace — 18 slots
Far more parallel smelting. Standard "AFK overnight" layout:
- **1 slot** = ~1,000 wood
- **1 slot** = empty (charcoal/overflow)
- **~13-16 slots** = stacks of 200 ore

This is why the large furnace's *total* wood per batch is so much lower — it smelts a dozen+ stacks at once off one wood stack.

### Electric Furnace — small footprint
**2 ore-input slots** smelting in parallel + output slots. No fuel slot (it's wired to power). Fill both ore slots to use it efficiently.

> [!tip] Stack-splitting trick
> To clear ore *faster* in a single furnace, **split one big stack into several smaller stacks across multiple slots** — each slot smelts in parallel, so the batch finishes sooner. Same total wood, less wall-clock time.

---

## How many furnaces do I need? (solo/duo rule of thumb)

- **Early wipe (T0-T1):** 1-2 small furnaces is plenty.
- **Mid wipe, base running:** a **furnace bank of 3-5 small furnaces** clears a quarry/mining run in minutes. Cheap (just stone + LGF), and total wood cost is identical to one furnace.
- **HQM production / big sulfur farm:** one **[[Large Furnace]]** (placed on open ground — it **cannot** sit on a foundation, in caves, or in tight build spots) for batch jobs, optionally an **[[Electric Furnace]]** wired to [[Solar Panel]]s for hands-off, wood-free metal/sulfur once you have an electricity setup.

---

## Refining High Quality Metal (HQM)

This trips up returning players, so the short version:

**HQM ore is smelted in a furnace exactly like metal ore — it is NOT done at the Oil Refinery.** (The [[Oil Refinery]] is only for turning [[Crude Oil]] into [[Low Grade Fuel]] — see below; it has nothing to do with HQM.)

- Put **[[High Quality Metal Ore]]** into a **small or large [[Large Furnace|furnace]]** -> smelts 1:1 into **[[High Quality Metal]]**.
- **Electric furnaces CANNOT smelt HQM** — wood furnaces only.
- HQM ore takes **10 s each** (4x metal). 1,000 HQM ore = ~167 minutes of smelt time in a single slot, so **always split it across many slots / use a large furnace**, which clears HQM ~5x faster than a small one and uses ~1/3 the wood.

Full detail and HQM farm routes: **[[Refining HQM]]**.

---

## Oil Refinery (not a furnace, but adjacent)

The **[[Oil Refinery]]** converts **[[Crude Oil]]** into **[[Low Grade Fuel]]** — the fuel you need to *craft* furnaces, run vehicles, and make Molotovs/flamethrower fuel.

- **Ratio:** 1 Crude Oil -> **3 Low Grade Fuel**
- It also burns a little wood to run (~1 wood per ~1.5 s); a full wood stack (~1,000) refines ~333 crude into ~1,000 LGF over ~19 minutes.
- Crude comes from [[Pump Jack]]s, [[Oil Rig]] / [[Underwater Labs]], and crude barrels.

So the dependency chain a returning solo should remember:
**Crude oil -> (Oil Refinery) -> Low Grade Fuel -> craft a Furnace -> (Furnace) -> smelt ore.**

---

## Quick-reference card

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Wood per 1,000 metal ore (small furnace)? | ~500 wood |
| Wood-to-charcoal ratio? | ~75% — 1,000 wood -> ~750 charcoal |
| Ore-to-refined ratio? | Always 1:1 |
| Metal/sulfur smelt time? | 2.5 s each |
| HQM smelt time? | 10 s each (4x slower) |
| Small furnace slots? | 6 |
| Large furnace slots? | 18 |
| Electric furnace power? | 3 rW, no wood, no charcoal |
| Can electric furnaces smelt HQM? | **No** |
| Where do I refine HQM? | A normal **furnace**, NOT the oil refinery |
| Where does Low Grade Fuel come from? | [[Oil Refinery]]: 1 crude -> 3 LGF |
| Do more furnaces cost more wood? | No — same total wood, just faster |

---

## See also
- [[Large Furnace]] · [[Electric Furnace]] · [[Refining HQM]]
- [[High Quality Metal]] · [[High Quality Metal Ore]] · [[Metal Fragments]]
- [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Oil Refinery]] · [[Crude Oil]]
- [[Gunpowder]] · [[Ammo Recipes]] (charcoal/sulfur sink)
- [[Crafting Basics]] · [[Workbenches]]

> [!note] Verification
> Smelt times, the 1:1 ratio, the ~0.5 wood/ore baseline, the ~75% charcoal rate, and the large-furnace fuel savings (40% metal / 80% sulfur / ~1/3 HQM) were cross-checked across rusthelp.com, the Rust wiki, Corrosion Hour, and the LevelSkip/HubPages furnace-efficiency guide (June 2026). Slot counts (6 / 18 / electric-small) reconcile conflicting aggregator listings — some sources mislabel the large furnace's 18 slots as the small furnace's. Re-verify exact wood-per-ore at the next progression patch.

pages.title: Tech Tree
pages.body:
# Tech Tree

The **Tech Tree** is the primary way to learn [[Blueprints]] in 2026. Each [[Workbenches|workbench]] has its own tech tree, browsed as **tabs on one station** (the Jun 2024 redesign merged the three trees into one UI). You spend **scrap** to unlock recipes along branching paths — unlocking an upstream item lets you research downstream items.

> [!important] Costs were slashed in Nov 2025
> The "Pivot Or Die" rebalance cut per-item research costs hard. These are the **current** numbers (verified June 2026, unchanged at "Built Different"):

## Research cost by rarity (current)

| Rarity | Scrap cost | Old (pre-Nov 2025) |
|---|---|---|
| Common | **15** | 20 |
| Uncommon | **30** | 75 |
| Rare | **60** | 125 |
| Very Rare | **120** | 500 |

These are *per item*. Because you follow a branch, you pay for each node along the way to the thing you want.

## How it works

1. Stand at the matching [[Workbenches|workbench]] tier (T1 tree needs WB1, etc.).
2. Open the tech tree; pick the tab for the tier.
3. Items are arranged in a branching graph. You can only research a node once its prerequisite node is unlocked.
4. **Multi-node path unlock (Apr 2026):** you can queue a path and unlock every node along it in one action, paying the summed scrap — no more clicking each node manually.

## Tech tree vs. Research Table

| | Tech Tree | [[Research Table]] |
|---|---|---|
| Cost basis | per-rarity (15/30/60/120) | **per-rarity now too** (15/30/60/120 — reduced "in line with workbench values" in Pivot Or Die; the old 75/250/500 per-tier rate is dead) |
| Needs item copy? | No | Yes (consumes it) |
| Shareable BP? | No (you only) | Yes (paper BP for teammates) |
| No path needed? | No (must buy upstream nodes) | Yes (instant, if you have the item + bench) |

The two cost the **same scrap per item now**. The real trade-offs: the tech tree needs no physical copy but makes you buy every upstream node along the path; the research table needs a physical copy (consumed) but jumps straight to the item and produces a shareable paper BP. For a solo grinding a full path, the tech tree is usually still the move; the research table wins when you already hold the gun (looted/found) or want to share it in a duo/trio.

## Approximate full-tier costs

If you wanted to unlock an entire tier's tree (you rarely should — just path to what you need):

- **Following an optimal path** to a target item is what matters; a single key gun is typically 5-10 nodes.
- Unlocking *everything* in a tier runs into the thousands of scrap, but the cheap per-node costs make targeted unlocking very affordable — a few hundred scrap gets a solo a working loadout.

> [!note] These totals shift each rebalance; the per-rarity node costs above are the load-bearing numbers. Don't memorize "full tree" totals.

## Workbench Augmentations that affect research

- **[[Workbench Augmentations|Salvage]]** — reduces tech-tree scrap cost by 20% on that bench.
- **[[Workbench Augmentations|Prototype]]** — lets you jump directly to any node at **double** scrap cost but with a **25% failure chance** (gamble for skipping a path).

## Returning-player takeaways

- Don't hoard scrap waiting for the old 500-scrap "very rare" wall — it's 120 now.
- Plan a **path**, not a pile. Decide your target gun and tech-tree straight to it.
- Each monthly wipe you re-do this, but it's fast: one good loot run funds a full loadout's worth of nodes.

## Related

[[Blueprints]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Workbench Augmentations]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Tool Recipes
pages.body:
# Tool Recipes

Craft costs for **Rust** gathering and utility tools (2026). Tools are how you accelerate the gather loop that feeds all crafting — see [[Crafting Basics]].

## Gathering tools

| Tool | Recipe | Tier | BP cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stone Hatchet** | 200 wood + 100 stone | default | free |
| **Stone Pickaxe** | 200 wood + 100 stone | default | free |
| **Hatchet** | 125 metal frags + 100 wood | T1 | 75 scrap |
| **Pickaxe** | 125 metal frags + 100 wood | T1 | 75 scrap |
| **Salvaged Axe** | 1 metal pipe + 5 metal blades | T2 | 125 scrap |
| **Salvaged Icepick** | 1 metal pipe + 5 metal blades | T2 | 125 scrap |
| **Chainsaw** | 5 HQM + 2 gears + 6 metal blades | T2 | — |
| **Jackhammer** | HQM + gears + blades | T3 | — |

Salvaged tools gather faster than the metal tier and are a worthwhile T2 unlock for a solo who farms a lot. **Metal Blades** and **Metal Pipes** are looted components (recycle road/electrical loot).

## Building & utility tools

| Tool | Recipe | Tier | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Building Plan** | 20 wood | default | the build hammer's blueprint placer |
| **Hammer** | 100 wood | default | upgrades/rotates building blocks |
| **Salvaged Hammer** | 1 metal pipe + 50 metal frags | T2 | faster upgrades |
| **Garry's Mod Tool / Graphical** | n/a | | |
| **Repair Bench** | metal frags + scrap | T1 | repairs gear cheaply |
| **Research Table** | 200 metal frags + 20 scrap | T1 | see [[Research Table]] |
| **Mixing Table** | metal frags + scrap | T2 | gunpowder/ammo, see [[Ammo Recipes]] |

## Survival & misc tools

| Tool | Recipe |
|---|---|
| **Torch** | 1 wood + 1 cloth (default) |
| **Rock** | starting item |
| **Hunting Bow** | 200 wood + 50 cloth |
| **Bone Knife** | 5 bone fragments |
| **Bone Club** | 10 bone fragments |
| **Sickle** | metal frags (farming) |
| **Hoe / Garden tools** | wood + metal frags (farming, Mar 2025 Crafting Update) |
| **Metal Detector** | components | finds road loot incl. Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]] (6.1%) |

## Components you can't craft

Salvaged tools and powered tools need **Metal Blades**, **Gears**, **Metal Pipes** — loot/recycle only. This is the same component gate as guns (see [[Crafting Basics]] and [[Weapon Recipes]]).

> [!note] BP costs above are [[Research Table]] (per-tier) values; the [[Tech Tree]] path may be cheaper per-rarity (15/30/60/120). A few exact metal numbers are the standard 2026 figures — re-verify on [rusthelp.com](https://rusthelp.com) if precision matters.

## Related

[[Building Recipes]] · [[Crafting Basics]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Weapon Recipes
pages.body:
# Weapon Recipes

Craft costs for **Rust** firearms by [[Workbenches|workbench]] tier (2026). The recurring bottleneck is **components** — Metal Springs, Rifle/SMG/Semi-Auto Bodies — which you **cannot craft**; they come from loot crates and recycling. See [[Crafting Basics]] for the component list. Damage/RPM stats are covered by the weapons agent's pages; this page is the **crafting cost** reference.

> [!note] Components, not scrap, gate guns
> A gun's wood/metal/HQM cost is usually trivial. The gate is **Metal Springs** (hoard them) and the body component, plus learning the [[Blueprints|blueprint]] (scrap via [[Tech Tree]]).

## Tier 1 (Workbench Level 1)

| Weapon | Craft cost |
|---|---|
| **Revolver** | 25 metal frags + 4 high quality metal... — early sidearm |
| **Double Barrel Shotgun** | 12 HQM + 1 metal pipe |
| **Waterpipe Shotgun** | 75 metal frags + 1 metal pipe |
| **Crossbow** | 75 wood + 75 metal frags |
| **Eoka Pistol** | 75 wood + 30 metal frags (no BP, primitive) |

## Tier 2 (Workbench Level 2)

| Weapon | Craft cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Thompson** | 10 HQM + 100 wood + 1 **SMG Body** + 1 **Metal Spring** | Best cost-to-performance T2 gun (~300 DPS) |
| **Custom SMG** | HQM + 1 **SMG Body** + 2 **Metal Springs** | shares SMG Body with Thompson |
| **MP5A4** | 15 HQM + 1 **SMG Body** + 2 **Metal Springs** | tech-tree on T2/T3 boundary |
| **Semi-Automatic Rifle** | 4 HQM + 1 **Semi-Auto Body** + 1 **Metal Spring** | the budget rifle; key T2 pick |
| **Semi-Auto Pistol** | 6 HQM + 1 **Semi-Auto Body** | reliable sidearm |
| **Pump Shotgun** | 6 HQM + 1 **Metal Spring** + 1 **Semi-Auto Body** | strong close-range |
| **Handmade SMG** (Nov 2024) | low metal/HQM, **T1-tier** | cheap full-auto, no body needed |

## Tier 3 (Workbench Level 3)

| Weapon | Craft cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Assault Rifle (AK-47)** | 50 HQM + 200 wood + 1 **Rifle Body** + 4 **Metal Springs** | 60s craft; the meta rifle |
| **LR-300** | HQM + 1 **Rifle Body** + 4 **Metal Springs** | loot-favored, smoother recoil |
| **Bolt Action Rifle** | 15 HQM + 1 **SMG Body** + 2 **Metal Springs** | premier sniper |
| **L96** | HQM + body + springs (loot-leaning) | long-range |
| **M249** | loot-only typically; very high HQM if craftable | LMG |
| **SKS** (Nov 2024) | HQM + Semi-Auto Body + spring, **T3** | semi-auto marksman |
| **High Calibre Revolver** (Oct 2024) | fires 5.56; HQM + components | hand cannon |
| **M39** | HQM + Rifle Body + springs | semi DMR |

## New guns since 2023 (returning-player heads-up)

- **Handmade SMG** + **SKS** (Nov 2024)
- **High Calibre Revolver** (5.56, Oct 2024)
- **Minigun** + **Military Flamethrower** (Apr 2024, heavy-scientist drops — **loot only**)
- **Blowpipe** + **Boomerang** (May 2025)
- **M16A2** (3-round burst) + **Ballistic armor set** (Jun 2026 "Built Different" — **loot only**, not craftable)
- **Craftable silencers** (Jun 2025) — attachments are now craftable

## Attachments (craftable)

Holosight, 8x/16x scopes, variable zoom scope (4x/8x/16x), silencer (Jun 2025), muzzle boost/brake, lasersight, flashlight — all learned via [[Tech Tree]], mostly T2/T3, costing HQM + components.

> [!note] Exact ingredient numbers for a few entries above are approximate where the source didn't give a clean figure — re-verify the specific gun on [rusthelp.com](https://rusthelp.com) before a precise farm. The component requirements (springs/bodies) are the load-bearing part and are correct.

## Related

[[Workbenches]] · [[Ammo Recipes]] · [[Crafting Basics]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Workbench Augmentations
pages.body:
# Workbench Augmentations

**Workbench Augmentations** (in-game: "Workbench Upgrades") are rare, **non-craftable** upgrades added in the **"Upgrade Hard, Raid Harder"** update — **live Thursday May 7 2026** (the system was previewed Apr 16 2026 on Rustafied/staging). You find them as loot and install them directly into a [[Workbenches|workbench]]'s slot — each changes the bench's appearance and grants one functional perk. They are the current endgame chase item for crafters.

> [!note] "Nine" vs ten — count is fuzzy and still being balanced
> Facepunch's devblog markets "**nine upgrades**," but ten distinct upgrade *items* have rusthelp pages: Accelerated, Comfort, Defensive, Efficiency, Prototype, Range, Recycle Bin, Reinforced, Salvage, **and Surplus** (the last flagged WIP/experimental). Treat the list below as the full known set; the effects are still being tuned patch-to-patch (verified June 2026, "Built Different").

## Rules

- **Loot-only.** None can be crafted, researched, or tech-treed. You find them in crates.
- **One of each per bench.** You can stack different augments, but not two of the same.
- **Install:** hold E facing the bench -> Open from the radial menu -> place the augment in the slot.
- **Swapping is free.** Adding/removing an augment does **not** damage the bench or the augment.
- They wipe monthly like everything else.

## The augmentations (verified vs rusthelp, June 2026)

| Augment | Effect | Drops from |
|---|---|---|
| **Accelerated** | Each item after the first in a bulk craft gets +25% craft speed (stacks across the batch) | Elite crates |
| **Comfort** | Boosts player Comfort to 100% within bench range (passive heal / anti-bleed) | Loot crates |
| **Defensive** | Armor-slotted crafted clothing always gets **at least +1 insert/plate slot** | Loot crates |
| **Efficiency** | **10% chance** to craft an **extra free** item when crafting in stacks (excludes Rockets & TEC/[[Timed Explosive Charge\|C4]]) | Military / elite crates |
| **Prototype** | Learn **any** [[Tech Tree]] node directly regardless of progression, at **double scrap** with a **25% fail chance** (resources consumed on fail) | Military Crate **1.67%**, UW Lab Normal Crate 1.67% |
| **Range** | **Doubles** the bench's aura range | Loot crates |
| **Recycle Bin** | Chance to refund **0–10%** of an item's ingredient cost as raw materials on craft | Loot crates |
| **Reinforced** | Bench **+150% HP** and added explosive resistance (raid defense) | Military / elite crates |
| **Salvage** | Reduces [[Tech Tree]] research scrap cost by **20%** on that bench (on the **Elite Crate** loot table) | Elite crates |
| **Surplus** *(WIP)* | **20% chance** to produce a random surplus part (×1–8) when crafting; surplus parts feed alternate recipes | Loot crates |

> [!note] Drop-source precision
> Facepunch hasn't published a clean per-augment loot table, and third-party guides disagree on exact crate sources. The two **pinned** values from [[rusthelp.com]] are: **Salvage** on the Elite Crate table, and **Prototype** at **1.67%** from Military Crate + UW Lab Normal Crate. The rest are confirmed to come from mid/high-tier loot crates; treat specific crate attributions for those as approximate until Facepunch documents them. See [[Loot Tables]].

## Which to prioritize (solo/duo)

- **Salvage** + **Recycle Bin** + **Efficiency** = a "value" bench: cheaper research, refund chances, free extra items. Best for a main crafting bench you keep safe.
- **Reinforced** = defensive pick if your bench sits in a raidable spot; +150% HP and 50% explosive reduction can save a wipe of progression.
- **Defensive** = strong on a solo who crafts their own armor — a free extra insert slot per piece is real survivability (see armor insert system, Mar 2025 Crafting Update).
- **Accelerated** matters most for clans doing big bulk crafts; less impactful solo.

## Notes for returners

This system didn't exist before — augments are brand new (live May 7 2026). They're optional polish, not a progression gate. Don't go out of your way early; grab them opportunistically from the crates above once you're running monuments for [[Blueprint Fragments]] anyway.

## Related

[[Workbenches]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Crafting Basics]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]]

pages.title: Workbench Level 1
pages.body:
# Workbench Level 1

The **Tier 1 Workbench (WB1)** is your first real progression deployable — the gateway to researching and crafting anything above the survival baseline. Its recipe is **default-known** (no blueprint, no scrap).

## Craft cost

| Resource | Amount |
|---|---|
| Wood | 500 |
| Metal Fragments | 100 |
| Scrap | **0** |
| Blueprint Fragments | **0** |

Craft time: 15s with no bench (you can craft it from your inventory), faster inside a higher bench.

## What it unlocks

WB1 is the floor for the entire [[Tech Tree]] T1 branch and lets you build the [[Research Table]]. Key unlocks: Hatchet, Pickaxe, [[Small Backpack]], crossbow, Revolver, Double Barrel Shotgun, Waterpipe Shotgun, road sign armor, code lock, large furnace, small medkit, syringe, low-grade fuel. See [[Tool Recipes]] and [[Weapon Recipes]].

## Notes for returners

- Build this **first**, day one — it's cheap and unblocks research. With cheap research costs now (15-120 scrap), a WB1 + a couple hundred scrap is a huge power spike.
- You research **T1 items** while standing next to a WB1, either via [[Tech Tree]] or [[Research Table]].
- To go further you need [[Workbench Level 2]], which requires WB1 present to craft **and** 5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]].

## Related

[[Workbenches]] · [[Workbench Level 2]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Workbench Level 2
pages.body:
# Workbench Level 2

The **Tier 2 Workbench (WB2)** is the "real base" tier — the gate to component guns, salvaged tools, satchels, and most armor. Crafting it requires a [[Workbench Level 1]] present **and** the new fragment ingredient.

## Craft cost (verified June 2026)

| Resource | Amount |
|---|---|
| Metal Fragments | 500 |
| High Quality Metal | 20 |
| Basic [[Blueprint Fragments\|Blueprint Fragment]] | **5** |
| Scrap | **0** |

Craft time: 15s at WB1, 7.5s at WB2, 3.75s at WB3. Requires a **WB1** to craft.

> [!important] The fragment gate
> You cannot build a WB2 with scrap alone. The **5 Basic Blueprint Fragments** must be farmed from monument puzzle rooms — see [[Blueprint Fragments]]. This is the wall returning players hit.

## What it unlocks

Semi-Auto Rifle, Thompson, Custom SMG, MP5 (tech tree), Salvaged Axe/Pick/Hammer/Icepick, [[Garage Door]], sheet metal door, satchel charges, beancan grenades, road sign + metal facemask armor, electricity basics, most medical. See [[Weapon Recipes]], [[Tool Recipes]], [[Explosive Recipes]].

## Getting the 5 Basic Fragments fast

One run of [[Power Plant]], [[Train Yard]], or [[Water Treatment Plant]] (×3 each) plus any low monument gets you there. [[Underwater Labs]] alone gives ~4. See [[Blueprint Fragments]] for the full table.

## Notes

- Recycling a WB2 returns **2-3 Basic Fragments** — useful when relocating or after a raid.
- You need WB2 deployed to **research T2 items** at a [[Research Table]] / [[Tech Tree]].

## Related

[[Workbenches]] · [[Workbench Level 1]] · [[Workbench Level 3]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Workbench Level 3
pages.body:
# Workbench Level 3

The **Tier 3 Workbench (WB3)** is the endgame bench — AK, bolt rifle, M249, rockets, and [[Timed Explosive Charge|C4]] all live here. Crafting it requires a [[Workbench Level 2]] present **and** Advanced fragments.

## Craft cost (verified June 2026)

| Resource | Amount |
|---|---|
| Metal Fragments | 1,000 |
| High Quality Metal | 100 |
| Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments\|Blueprint Fragment]] | **5** |
| Scrap | **0** |

Craft time: 25s at WB2, 12s at WB3. Requires a **WB2** to craft.

> [!important] The advanced-fragment gate
> The **5 Advanced Blueprint Fragments** drop from elite crates and top-tier monuments ([[Launch Site]], [[Nuclear Missile Silo]], [[Oil Rig|Oil Rigs]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Underwater Labs]]). A hackable crate guarantees one. You can also convert 20 Basic -> 1 Advanced (so 100 Basic for a WB3 the slow way — don't). See [[Blueprint Fragments]].

## What it unlocks

Assault Rifle (AK-47), LR-300, M249, Bolt Action Rifle, L96, M39, SKS, [[Timed Explosive Charge|C4]], Rocket Launcher + rockets, explosive 5.56, high-tier electricity, armored building upgrades crafting, HV ammo. See [[Weapon Recipes]] and [[Explosive Recipes]].

## Notes for returners

- The HQM cost (100) is real — bank HQM from quarries / mining ([[High Quality Metal Ore]]) before you try to build it.
- You need WB3 deployed to **research T3 guns/explosives**. Build it before tech-treeing the AK.
- 100 metal frags worth of HQM is a meaningful chunk; a [[Bradley APC]] kill or two funds it.

## Related

[[Workbenches]] · [[Workbench Level 2]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Weapon Recipes]] · [[Explosive Recipes]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Workbenches
pages.body:
# Workbenches

A **Workbench** is the deployable that unlocks crafting tiers and is required to research/craft anything above the survival baseline. Rust has **three** workbench tiers. You must be standing inside a bench's aura to craft items of that tier, and to *research* tier-locked items at a [[Research Table]] you need the matching bench deployed nearby.

> [!important] 2026 craft costs — workbenches no longer cost scrap
> The Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die" update **removed scrap from workbench craft costs**. The cost is now wood/metal/HQM plus **[[Blueprint Fragments]]** for T2/T3.

## Craft costs (verified June 2026)

| Bench | Wood | Metal Frags | HQM | Fragments | Requires |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **[[Workbench Level 1]]** | 500 | 100 | — | — | none (default recipe) |
| **[[Workbench Level 2]]** | — | 500 | 20 | **5 Basic** | WB1 to craft |
| **[[Workbench Level 3]]** | — | 1,000 | 100 | **5 Advanced** | WB2 to craft |

No scrap at any tier. The hard gate is now the [[Blueprint Fragments]], not scrap. WB1 is free to learn (default blueprint).

## What each tier unlocks (the important stuff)

### Tier 1 (WB1)
Entry tier. Unlocks: [[Research Table]], early tools (Hatchet, Pickaxe), [[Small Backpack]], crossbow, revolver, Double Barrel, road sign armor pieces, small medkit/syringe, low-grade fuel refining, code lock, large furnace, sleeping bag upgrades. This is where most of your first-day progression lives. See [[Tool Recipes]] and [[Weapon Recipes]].

### Tier 2 (WB2)
The "real base" tier. Unlocks: components-tier guns (Semi-Auto Rifle, Thompson, Custom SMG, MP5 via tech tree), Salvaged tools (Salvaged Axe/Pick/Hammer/Icepick), [[Garage Door]], sheet metal door, satchel charges, beancan grenades, most armor, electricity basics, auto turret (T2/T3 mix). Needs 5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]].

### Tier 3 (WB3)
Endgame. Unlocks: Assault Rifle (AK), LR-300, M249, Bolt Action Rifle, L96, [[Timed Explosive Charge|C4]], Rocket Launcher + rockets, high-tier electricity, [[Garage Door]]+, sheet metal/armored upgrades crafting, explosive 5.56. Needs 5 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]. See [[Weapon Recipes]] and [[Explosive Recipes]].

## Crafting speed bonus

Higher benches craft **faster**. The same item crafts quicker the higher the bench you stand in. Example — crafting a [[Workbench Level 2]]: 15s at WB1, 7.5s at WB2, 3.75s at WB3. Most items follow this halving pattern. The [[Workbench Augmentations|Accelerated]] augment speeds bulk crafting further.

## Workbench aura & placement

- You must be **inside the bench's range** to craft tier items — the bench shows a glowing aura radius.
- The [[Workbench Augmentations|Range]] augment **doubles** the aura, letting you craft from a wider area.
- Benches take explosive damage in raids; the [[Workbench Augmentations|Reinforced]] augment gives +150% HP and -50% explosive damage.
- Recycling a WB2 returns 2-3 Basic Fragments; plan demolitions accordingly.

## Workbench Augmentations (May 2026)

Nine rare, non-craftable upgrades slot into a bench to modify it — cheaper research, faster bulk crafting, extra armor slots, refund chances, etc. Full list and drop sources: **[[Workbench Augmentations]]**.

## Related

[[Workbench Level 1]] · [[Workbench Level 2]] · [[Workbench Level 3]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Workbench Augmentations]] · [[Progression Route]]

pages.title: Applying Skins In-Game
pages.body:
# Applying Skins In-Game

Owning a skin in your Steam inventory does **not** auto-apply it — you choose when to put a skin on an item. There are three ways to do it, all of which only show skins **you already own** for that specific item. Skins are cosmetic only ([[Skins and the Skin Economy]]): applying one never changes stats.

## Method 1 — At craft time (free, best)

The cleanest way: skin the item *as you make it*.

1. Open the **crafting menu / inventory**.
2. Select the item you want to craft (e.g. an AK, a metal door, a chest).
3. If you own skins for it, a **skin selector** appears — click the skin you want before hitting craft.
4. The item is crafted already wearing that skin. **No extra cost, no bench needed.**

This is the default method for fresh gear each wipe.

## Method 2 — Repair Bench (free, re-skins existing items)

Use a **[[Repair Bench]]** to change the skin of an item you already have.

1. Craft/find a Repair Bench (cheap, T1 deployable).
2. Open it and **place the item in the bench slot**.
3. A **Skins** panel shows every skin you own for that item.
4. Click a skin to apply it **instantly**.
5. **No material cost** to re-skin via the bench (it does *not* consume the repair/scrap that actual repairs use — re-skinning is free).

Tip: hold **Shift** while hover-looting over multiple stackable items to auto-apply the last-used skin to each — a fast way to skin a whole stack.

## Method 3 — Spray Can (deployables, on the spot)

The **[[Spray Can]]** lets you re-skin **deployables in the world** (doors, boxes, lockers, furnaces, etc.) without picking them up and hauling them to a bench.

- **Craft cost:** 100 Metal Fragments.
- **Craft time:** 15s (no bench) / 7.5s (WB1) / 3.75s (WB2–3). **No workbench required** to craft.
- **Use:** hold the Spray Can, look at a skinnable deployable, press **attack2 (RMB)** to re-skin it; **attack (LMB)** sprays a decorative spray.
- **Durability:** good for about **20 re-skins** per can; each re-skin chips a small amount of durability until it breaks. (Community sources note re-skinning consumes a small frag cost per use, "like adobe costs stone" — keep some frags on hand.)
- **Recycle value:** ~40 frags (safe-zone) / ~60 frags (monument/Radtown).

The Spray Can is the only way to re-skin a deployable that's already placed and locked into your base.

## Notes

- The skin selector only ever lists skins **you own** for that exact item — you can't skin a rifle with a door skin.
- Skinning is **purely visual**; teammates and enemies see the skin, but it confers zero advantage.
- Skins persist on the item; if you pick it up and redeploy it, it keeps the skin.

## Related

[[Skins and the Skin Economy]] · [[Twitch and Kick Drops]] · [[Spray Can]] · [[Repair Bench]] · [[Rust Economy]]

## Sources

- tradeit.gg/blog — How to Apply Rust Skins
- corrosionhour.com — Repair Bench guide, Spray Can
- rusthelp.com — Spray Can item page
- culturedvultures.com — Rust Spraycan wiki

pages.title: Barrels and Crates
pages.body:
# Barrels and Crates

Loot-table summaries for every common container (verified vs rusthelp.com, June 2026). Guaranteed [[Scrap]] amounts are the spine of the loot economy; component rolls feed [[Recycling]].

## Yellow & blue road barrels

Identical tables. **2 scrap guaranteed**, then component rolls:

| Roll | Chance |
|---|---|
| Metal Blade ×1 / Rope ×1–2 | 15.45% each |
| Propane Tank ×1 / Sewing Kit ×3–4 / Tarp ×1 | 8.03% each |
| Electric Fuse, Gears ×2, Metal Pipe ×1–4, Metal Spring, Road Signs ×2–3, **Semi Auto Body**, Sheet Metal | 1.43% each |
| Junk deployables/clothing pool (31 items) | 1.13% each |

Densest barrel monuments: [[Launch Site]] ×28, Harbor Large ×18, Harbor Small ×15, Ferry Terminal ×13, Arctic Research Base ×11.

## Oil barrel (red)

**100%: Crude Oil ×15–19 + Low Grade Fuel ×5–9.** 1 crude refines to 3 LGF at a Small Oil Refinery. Found at 22 monuments — Large [[Oil Rig]] ×15, Ghost Ships ×6–12, Harbors ×10, [[The Dome]] ×9, [[Launch Site]] ×7.

## Crates by tier

### Food Box — 0 scrap
**Pays no scrap at all** — food, water, and Anti-Radiation Pills only (Anti-Rad Pills / Water Jug 24.89% each, common foods 12.89% each). Radtown ×12, plus Excavator/Gas Station/Supermarket. Returning-player trap: it looks like a crate but never counts toward scrap math. Full table: [[Loot Tables]].

### Basic Crate — 3 scrap
Lowest tier; beach/ruin filler.

### Normal Crate — 5 scrap
Component crate. Each of these rolls at **14.29%**: Electric Fuse, Gears ×2, Metal Pipe ×1–4, Metal Spring, Road Signs ×2–3, **Semi Auto Body**, Sheet Metal. Plus diving gear (1.7–4.2%), hazmat 4%, electrical parts 1–2%, rare weapon/deployable rolls ~0.5%. Counts: [[Launch Site]] ×55, Water Treatment ×20, Airfield ×16, Power Plant ×14, Sewer Branch ×14.

### Tools Crate — 5 scrap
Hatchet/Pickaxe/Binoculars 7.84% each, melee weapons ~4.9%, **Chainsaw 0.98%, Jackhammer 0.98%**, Auto Turret 0.28%.

### Military Crate — 8 scrap
The tier-2 component jackpot, each at **16.67%**: HQM ×15–24, Metal Pipe ×5, **Rifle Body**, **SMG Body**, Tech Trash ×2–3. Plus **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments|Blueprint Fragment]] 10%**, Targeting Computer 8.73%, CCTV 7.14%, armor inserts 5%, Large Backpack 5%. Counts: [[Launch Site]] ×19, [[Missile Silo]] ×18, Train Yard ×12, Airfield ×10, Power Plant ×9.

### Elite Crate — 25 scrap
Same component pool at **27.73%** each (HQM ×15–24, Pipe ×5, Rifle Body ×1–3, SMG Body, Tech Trash ×2–9). Plus **Advanced Blueprint Fragment 10%**, MLRS Rocket 20%, Targeting Computer 15.27%, CCTV 12.61%, Flame Thrower 7.23%, AK/Bolt/MP5 ~4% each, L96/Spas/Auto Turret ~0.8–2%. Locations: [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnel]], [[Missile Silo]] (+3 extra since the Oct 2025 red-card change), Oil Rigs, Underwater Labs.

### Elite variants
- **Bradley crate:** CCTV 42.86%, Targeting Computer 52.38% — the targeting-computer farm.
- **Heli crate:** [[Patrol Helicopter]] exclusives.

### Locked Crate (Chinook / [[Cargo Ship]] / [[Oil Rig]] / Ghost Ship)
15-min hack timer. **100%: Advanced Blueprint Fragment ×2.** Scrap 33.33% (×140–159). Targeting Computer 55.29% (×1–2), CCTV 45.71%, Metal Pipe/Tech Trash 39.27% (×5–15 / ×2–12), Gears + Sheet Metal 31.25% (×5–10).

### Supply Drop
Scrap 55.56% (×140–318), Gears/Sheet Metal 15.97% (×5–10), Jackhammer 26.53%, **Basic Blueprint Fragment ×2**.

### Underwater Lab crates
Normal/components/vehicle-parts ×8 scrap; lab elite ×25; **Fuel Crate: 100% Crude ×30–38 + LGF ×10–18**. Tier-2/Tier-3 component crates have the best component density in the game (Tier-3: 30.56% rolls on pipes ×5–10, tech trash ×2–6, rifle/SMG bodies ×1–2).

### Wagon crates (train tunnels)
Military wagon crate **11 scrap**; normal wagon crate **5 scrap** + 14.29% component rolls.

## Reading the economy

- Barrels pay scrap; **crates pay components**; military/elite crates pay workbench progression ([[Blueprint Fragments]]).
- A military crate is worth ~8 scrap raw but its average component roll recycles to far more — always carry crate loot to a monument recycler ([[Recycling]]).
- Semi Auto Body at 14.29% from every normal crate is why a SAR is reachable on day 1.

pages.title: Blueprint Fragments
pages.body:
# Blueprint Fragments

**The single biggest progression change since 2023.** Introduced in the "Meta Shift" update (Oct 2025) and kept by "Pivot Or Die" (Nov 2025), Blueprint Fragments are the gate on **[[Workbench]] tiers**. You no longer grind a mountain of scrap to tier up — instead you hunt fragments at **monuments, puzzle rooms, and high-tier crates**. Two types:

| Fragment | Gates | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic Blueprint Fragment** | [[Workbench]] Level 2 | Monument loot rooms, keycard desks, junkpile scientists, metal detector, supply drops |
| **Advanced Blueprint Fragment** | [[Workbench]] Level 3 | Hackable [[Locked Crate|locked crates]], [[Elite Crate|elite crates]], top monuments |

> **Conversion:** 20 Basic → 1 Advanced. So if you're short on Advanced for WB3, a pile of Basic fragments can be upgraded.

## Why this changed the early game

The old loop was *scrap → research everything → craft at any workbench*. Now:

1. Scrap still gets you to **WB1** (cheap) and pays **research** (15/30/60/120 by rarity — slashed in Pivot Or Die).
2. **WB2 and WB3 require fragments you can only get by leaving home** and doing monuments/puzzles/crates.
3. Workbench crafting itself costs **no scrap** anymore (Pivot Or Die removed it).

Net effect for a returning solo/duo: *scrap is cheap to spend, fragments are the bottleneck.* You're pushed out to monuments early — exactly the design intent. See [[Pivot Or Die]] and [[Meta Shift]].

## Workbench costs (current, June 2026)

| Workbench | Cost to craft/upgrade | Scrap? |
|---|---|---|
| **Level 1** | 500 wood + 100 metal frags | **No scrap** |
| **Level 2** | 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + **5 Basic Fragments** | **No scrap** |
| **Level 3** | 1,000 metal frags + 100 HQM + **5 Advanced Fragments** | **No scrap** |

(You upgrade in place: WB1 → feed WB2 mats → WB2, etc.) Costs verified vs [[rusthelp.com]] June 2026 ("Built Different"). **No workbench tier costs any scrap** — "Pivot Or Die" removed scrap from all bench crafts. (Older guides still listing WB1 = 50 scrap / WB3 = 500 scrap are pre-Nov-2025.)

## Where Basic Blueprint Fragments drop

| Source | Rate / amount |
|---|---|
| Underwater Lab | 100% (~4) |
| [[Power Plant]] / [[Train Yard]] / [[Water Treatment Plant]] | 100% (×3 each) |
| [[Airfield]] / [[Arctic Research Base]] | 100% (×2 each) |
| Supply Drop | 100% (×2) |
| [[Ferry Terminal]] / Harbor Large / Harbor Small / Radtown / [[Satellite Dish]] / Sewer Branch / [[The Dome]] | 100% (×1 each) |
| Blue & red keycard **desks** (NOT green) | guaranteed on the desk |
| Green/blue/red puzzle rooms | inside the loot room |
| Military Crate / Underwater Advanced Crate / Road Scientist / Outbreak Sprayer | 10% (×1) |
| Metal Detector (roads & rails) | 6.1% chance |
| Recycling a Workbench Level 2 | 3 frags (monument recycler) / 2 (safe-zone) |

So the cheap, low-risk Basic-fragment farm is a **tier-0/green-puzzle monument loop**: The Dome, Satellite Dish, Sewer Branch, Radtown, plus junkpile scientists on roads. A WB2 is ~5 fragments — one or two monument laps.

## Where Advanced Blueprint Fragments drop

| Source | Rate / amount |
|---|---|
| **Locked Crate** (Chinook / [[Cargo Ship]] / [[Oil Rig]] / Ghost Ship) | **100% — ×2 per crate** |
| [[Launch Site]] / [[Military Tunnel]] / [[Missile Silo]] | 100% (×2) |
| Underwater Lab | ~×2 |
| [[Elite Crate]] / Underwater Lab Elite Crate | 10% (×1) |

Advanced fragments mean WB3 (and thus AKs, bolt actions, top armor) gates behind **PvP-contested high-tier content** — locked crates and elite-crate monuments. A duo can reach WB3 off one or two hacked locked crates (×2 each) without grinding elite crates. Alternatively, 20 Basic → 1 Advanced lets a peaceful monument-looper convert their way up, just slowly (5 Advanced = 100 Basic).

## Stack & handling

- Stack size **20** (cap aligns with the 20→1 conversion).
- They drop on death like any item — carry only what you'll use, or bank fragments at base.
- Not researchable, not craftable (only the 20→1 upgrade).

## Returning-player TL;DR

- 2023 you: scrap-gated everything. 2026 you: **scrap is easy, fragments gate WB2/WB3.**
- **WB2** = 5 Basic fragments (do green/tier-0 monuments + roads).
- **WB3** = 5 Advanced fragments (hack a locked crate ×2, or run Launch/Silo/Mil Tunnel, or convert 100 Basic).
- Research is dirt cheap now (15/30/60/120) — once you have the workbench tier, unlocking the gun is trivial.

## Related

[[Workbench]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Scrap]] · [[Pivot Or Die]] · [[Meta Shift]] · [[Barrels and Crates]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Launch Site]] · [[Missile Silo]] · [[Military Tunnel]] · [[The Dome]]
