pages.body:
# Components

Non-craftable (mostly) intermediate items that gate weapon/deployable crafting. Everything below is verified against rusthelp.com (June 2026). Recycle yields are given as **Monument / Safe-zone** (the May 2024 recycler split — monument recyclers pay ~50% more; see [[Recycling]]).

Quick reference — scrap per component when recycled:

| Component | Monument recycler | Safe-zone recycler |
|---|---|---|
| Rifle Body | 30 + 1 HQM (80% +1 HQM) | 20 + 1 HQM (20% +1) |
| Tech Trash | 24 + 1 HQM (20% +1) | 16 (80% HQM) |
| Electric Fuse | 24 | 16 |
| SMG Body | 18 + 1 HQM (80% +1) | 12 + 1 HQM (20% +1) |
| Semi Auto Body | 18 + 90 frags + 1 HQM (80% +1) | 12 + 60 frags + 1 HQM (20% +1) |
| Gears | 12 + 15 frags | 8 + 10 frags |
| Metal Spring | 12 + 1 HQM (20% +1) | 8 (80% HQM) |
| Sheet Metal | 9 + 120 frags + 1 HQM (20% +1) | 6 + 80 frags (80% HQM) |
| Metal Pipe | 6 + 1 HQM (20% +1) | 4 (80% HQM) |
| Road Signs | 6 + 1 HQM (20% +1) | 4 (80% HQM) |
| Metal Blade | 2 + 18 frags | 1 + 12 frags |
| Empty Propane Tank | 1 + 60 frags | 80% 1 + 40 frags |

---

## Gears
- **Where:** Locked Crates 31.25% (×5–10), UW Lab Tier-2 components 26.53% (×2–4), Supply Drop 15.97% (×5–10), normal crates ×2 @14.29%, barrels 1.43% (×2).
- **Recycle:** 15 frags + 12 scrap / 10 frags + 8 scrap.
- **Crafts:** armored doors & ladder hatches (5–6), shotgun trap (2), flame turret (1), chainsaw + HMLMG (2), generators/wind turbine (2–3), elevators/hoppers/water wheel (1–2), siege weapons (1).
- **Buy:** [[Outpost]] 125 scrap.

## Metal Spring
- **Where:** UW Lab Tier-2 26.53% (×1–2), normal crates 14.29%, tunnel/lab dwellers 7.43% (×1–3), scientists 4.73%, barrels 1.43%.
- **Recycle:** 1 HQM + 12 scrap (20% extra HQM) / 8 scrap (80% HQM).
- **Crafts:** every spring gun — AK (4), HMLMG (3), MP5/SKS (2), SAR/Thompson/Custom SMG (1) etc., Pressure Pad (1).
- **Buy:** [[Outpost]] 60 scrap.

## Metal Pipe
- **Where:** roadside Roadsign objects 100% (×1, harvest them), Locked Crate 39.27% (×5–15), Elite Crate 27.73% (×5–15), UW Lab Tier-3 30.56% (×5–10).
- **Recycle:** 1 HQM + 6 scrap (20% +HQM) / 4 scrap (80% HQM).
- **Craftable:** yes — 2 HQM + 20 scrap @ WB3.
- **Crafts:** all rockets, mortar shells, salvaged tools, Flame Thrower (6), Homing Missile Launcher (3), Bolt Action (3).
- **Buy:** [[Outpost]] 30 scrap.

## Rope
- **Where:** Tackleboxes 100%, jungle/underwater basic crates ~38–42% (×1–6), barrels 15.45% (×1–2).
- **Recycle:** 18 cloth / 12 cloth.
- **Crafts:** ladders (3), compound bow/crossbow (2), shotgun trap (2), sewing kit (3).
- **Buy:** [[Outpost]] for 30 **cloth**.

## Tarp
- **Where:** underwater crates 20–38%, dwellers 15.42%, barrels 8.03%.
- **Recycle:** 60 cloth / 40 cloth (best cloth-per-slot in the game).
- **Crafts:** Hazmat Suit (5), parachute (2), composter (2), planters/water catchers (1–2), Boat Building Station (1).

## Tech Trash
- **Where:** Locked Crate 39.27% (×2–12), Elite Crate 27.73% (×2–9), UW Lab Tier-3 30.56% (×2–6). Also produced by recycling Targeting Computers (2–3) and CCTV (1+).
- **Recycle:** 1 HQM + 24 scrap (20% +HQM) / 16 scrap (80% HQM).
- **Crafts:** 20+ top-end items — Night Vision Goggles (2), Industrial Crafter (2), Homing Missile (1 per 2), timed explosives line.

## Rifle Body
- **Where:** Elite Crate 27.73% (×1–3), Military Crate 16.67% (×1), UW Lab Tier-3 30.56% (×1–2), PT Boat scientist drybox 25.99%.
- **Recycle:** 1 HQM + **30 scrap** (80% +HQM) / 1 HQM + 20 scrap (20% +HQM). Highest scrap component.
- **Crafts:** AK (1 + 50 HQM + 200 wood + 4 springs), Bolt Action (1 + 20 HQM + 3 pipes + 1 spring), HMLMG (1 + 60 HQM + 3 springs + 2 gears), M39/LR via tech tree.
- **Buy:** Travelling Vendor ~161 scrap (floats).

## SMG Body
- **Where:** Elite Crate 27.73% (×1–3), RHIB scientist drybox 26.53%, UW Lab Tier-3 30.56%.
- **Recycle:** 1 HQM + 18 scrap (80% +HQM) / 1 HQM + 12 scrap (20% +HQM).
- **Crafts:** Custom SMG (1 + 8 HQM + 1 spring), Thompson (1 + 10 HQM + 100 wood + 1 spring), MP5A4 (1 + 15 HQM + 2 springs).
- **Buy:** Travelling Vendor ~104 scrap (floats).

## Semi Automatic Body
- **Where:** Mil Tunnel/PT/RHIB scientists 36.34% (×1–3), road scientists 23.61% (×1–2), normal crates 14.29%, UW Lab Tier-2 26.53%.
- **Recycle:** 90 frags + 1 HQM + 18 scrap (80% +HQM) / 60 frags + 1 HQM + 12 scrap (20% +HQM).
- **Crafts:** Semi-Auto Pistol (1 + 4 HQM + 1 pipe), SAR (1 + 1 spring + 450 frags + 4 HQM), SKS (1 + 2 springs + 200 frags + 12 HQM).

## Road Signs
- **Where:** roadside Roadsign objects 100% (×1), normal crates 14.29% (×2–3), dwellers 7.43% (×2–9), metal detector finds 30.3% (×4–5).
- **Recycle:** 1 HQM + 6 scrap (20% +HQM) / 4 scrap (80% HQM).
- **Crafts:** Roadsign armor set (1–2 + leather + sewing kits), roadsign horse armor (4), reinforced wooden shield, salvaged cleaver.

## Sheet Metal
- **Where:** Locked Crate 31.25% (×5–10), Supply Drop 15.97% (×5–10), normal crates 14.29% (×1), UW Lab Tier-2 26.53%.
- **Recycle:** 120 frags + 1 HQM + 9 scrap (20% +HQM) / 80 frags + 6 scrap (80% HQM).
- **Crafts:** heavy plate armor (1–2), high external stone wall (1), wind turbine (3), siege weapons (2), beehive (1).
- **Buy:** [[Outpost]] 30 scrap.

## CCTV Camera
- **Where:** Locked Crate 45.71% (×1–2), **Bradley crate 42.86%**, Elite Crate 12.61% (×1–3), Military Crate 7.14%.
- **Recycle:** yields Tech Trash (1 + 80% chance extra at monument).
- **Crafts:** Auto Turret (1 CCTV + 1 Targeting Computer + 10 HQM), Computer Station cameras.
- Stack ×64; no longer sold at Outpost.

## Targeting Computer
- **Where:** Locked Crate 55.29% (×1–2), **Bradley crate 52.38%**, Elite Crate 15.27% (×1–3), Military Crate 8.73%.
- **Recycle:** 60 frags + 1 HQM + **3 Tech Trash** (20% +HQM) / 40 frags + 2 Tech Trash (80% HQM).
- **Crafts:** Auto Turret, Computer Station.

## Metal Blade
- **Where:** underwater/jungle crates 38–63%, dwellers 28.51%, barrels 15.45%.
- **Recycle:** 18 frags + 2 scrap / 12 frags + 1 scrap.
- **Craftable:** 30 frags + 10 scrap @ WB2.
- **Crafts:** Salvaged Axe (5), Chainsaw (6), Longsword (2), Metal Barricade (2).
- **Buy:** [[Outpost]] 15 scrap.

## Empty Propane Tank
- **Where:** underwater crates 21–38%, dwellers 15.42%, barrels 8.03%.
- **Recycle:** 60 frags + 1 scrap / 40 frags (80% scrap).
- **Crafts:** Flame Thrower (2), Flame Turret (2), Propane Bomb (1), Speargun (1), Water Purifier (1).

## Sewing Kit
- **Where:** barrels 8.03% (×3–4), dwellers 15.42% (×3–8), underwater crates up to 37.73% (×3–12).
- **Craftable:** 20 cloth + 3 rope @ WB3.
- **Recycle:** 12 cloth + 1 rope (80% +rope) / 8 cloth + 1 rope (20% +rope).
- **Crafts:** 25+ recipes — backpacks, parachute, bed, hazmat variants, roadsign armor.

## Electric Fuse
- **Where:** normal crates 14.29%, barrels 1.43%. Consumed by monument puzzle fuse boxes (see [[Monument Puzzles]]).
- **Recycle:** 24 scrap / 16 scrap — recycle spares only if you're done puzzling; fuses are the eternal bottleneck for keycard runs ([[Blue Keycard]], [[Green Keycard]]).

pages.title: Diesel Fuel
pages.body:
# Diesel Fuel

The fuel that runs all of Rust's **mass-production mining**: the [[Giant Excavator Pit]], the static [[Excavator and Quarries|quarries]] (Stone/Sulfur/HQM), and the [[Pump Jack]]. **One diesel = ~2 minutes of run time** on any of those machines. It is **not craftable** — you either buy it or loot it, which makes diesel the real cost of bulk mining.

- **Stack size: 20.** (The Excavator's tank also holds exactly 20 — a full looted stack is a full run.)
- Cannot be crafted, cannot be researched.
- Consumed only by the Excavator, quarries, and Pump Jack.

## Where to get it

| Source | Amount |
|---|---|
| **[[Outpost]] vending** | Buy for **300 Low Grade Fuel** each (the reliable supply) |
| [[Junkyard]] | ~3 |
| [[Water Treatment Plant]] | ~3 |
| [[Large Oil Rig]] / Small Oil Rig | ~3 / ~2 |
| [[The Dome]] | ~2 |
| [[Power Plant]] | ~2 |
| Radtown | ~1 |
| Travelling Vendor | Occasionally (demand-priced — see [[Vending and Shops]]) |

## The 300-LGF math

Buying diesel at Outpost costs **300 LGF** apiece. That sounds steep until you see the output:

| Machine | 1 diesel buys you |
|---|---|
| Excavator (HQM run) | **100 HQM** |
| Excavator (sulfur run) | **2,000 sulfur ore** |
| Excavator (stone) | **10,000 stone** |
| Stone Quarry | 5,000 stone + 1,000 metal ore |
| Sulfur Quarry | 1,000 sulfur ore |
| HQM Quarry | 50 HQM ore |
| [[Pump Jack]] | 60 crude + 170 LGF (≈ break-even LGF + free crude) |

So 300 LGF → 100 HQM at the Excavator is wildly positive (100 HQM hand-mined is dozens of node hits). The constraint is **carrying enough diesel and holding the monument**, not the LGF price.

## Funding the LGF

You pay for diesel in low grade fuel, so the early-game chain is:

- **Animal fat → LGF:** 3 fat + 1 cloth = 4 LGF (bears/boars on the way to a monument).
- **Crude → LGF:** 1 crude refines to 3 LGF at a Small Oil Refinery. Crude comes from red oil barrels (15–19 each) and the [[Pump Jack]].
- A single Pump Jack run hands you 170 LGF + 60 crude (=180 more LGF) — over half a diesel's buy-in back per cycle.

## Returning-player note

In 2023 quarries ran on **low grade fuel directly**. They were all converted to **diesel** in the "Big Quality of Life" update. If you remember pouring LGF into a quarry, that's why your old habit doesn't work — buy/loot diesel now, then feed the machine.

## Related

[[Excavator and Quarries]] · [[Giant Excavator Pit]] · [[Pump Jack]] · [[Outpost]] · [[Vending and Shops]] · [[Gathering]]

pages.title: Excavator and Quarries
pages.body:
# Excavator and Quarries

Mass-production mining: the [[Giant Excavator Pit]] and the static monument quarries turn **[[Diesel Fuel]]** into bulk stone, metal frags, sulfur ore, HQM ore, and crude oil — far faster than swinging a [[Gathering|Jackhammer]] at nodes. All of it runs on diesel now (the old low-grade quarries were converted in the "Big Quality of Life" update), so the real cost of mass mining is **getting diesel**. Verified vs rusthelp / Corrosion Hour, June 2026.

> One number to remember: **1 Diesel = ~2 minutes of run time** on every machine below. Stock up on diesel, then drain a whole tank in one sitting.

## Diesel Fuel — the bottleneck

Diesel is **not craftable**. Sources:

| Source | How |
|---|---|
| Buy at [[Outpost]] | **300 Low Grade Fuel** per diesel (vending) — the reliable supply |
| [[The Dome]] | Diesel barrels / crates inside |
| [[Large Oil Rig]] / Oil Rigs | Diesel in crates |
| Loot crates at the Excavator | A few diesel spawn on-site each reset |
| Travelling Vendor | Occasionally stocks it (price floats) |

300 LGF per diesel means diesel is effectively "raw LGF you carry to a machine." A [[Pump Jack]] (below) or animal-fat/crude refining funds the LGF; see [[Gathering]] and [[Vending and Shops]].

---

## Giant Excavator Pit

A huge contested monument machine. Insert diesel in the **Engine Room** (tank holds **20 diesel max** = a full 40-minute run), then pick ONE resource in the **Control Room** by the spinning head. Output drops at two points: a **conveyor belt to a rail car** and a **pile by the bulldozer**.

### Output per diesel (pick one resource per run)

| Resource selected | Per diesel | Full 20-diesel tank (40 min) |
|---|---|---|
| Stone | **10,000** | 200,000 |
| Metal Fragments | **5,000** | 100,000 |
| Sulfur Ore | **2,000** | 40,000 |
| High Quality Metal | **100** | 2,000 |

- One diesel burns every **2 minutes**; you can only mine **one** resource type per run, so plan (a sulfur run before a raid, a frags/HQM run before a base upgrade).
- The Excavator also periodically **requests** and spawns **loot/scrap crates** on-site while running — extra reason it's camped. Treat it as a PvP event, not a quiet farm.
- It is a [[Monuments|monument]] with a recycler (see [[Recycling]]) and oil/road barrels, so a sulfur run doubles as a scrap stop.

**Value read:** a single HQM run (2,000 HQM for 20 diesel = ~6,000 LGF of buy-in) is enormous — that's most of a stone base's worth of sheet metal. Sulfur runs fund raids fast (40,000 sulfur ≈ ~80 rockets of gunpowder-equivalent). The Excavator is the single best sulfur/HQM faucet in the game *if you can hold it*.

---

## Static monument quarries

Three indestructible quarries sit at fixed monuments and run on diesel. Each takes **2 min 9 sec per diesel**. Lower throughput than the Excavator but **uncontested-er** and you can leave them running.

| Quarry | Per diesel | Biome / location |
|---|---|---|
| **Stone Quarry** ([[Mining Outpost]]) | **5,000 Stone + 1,000 Metal Ore** | Temperate / Mining Outpost |
| **Sulfur Quarry** | **1,000 Sulfur Ore** | Desert |
| **HQM Quarry** | **50 HQM Ore** | Snow/Arctic |

- Ore is **ore**, not refined — you still need a furnace to smelt metal ore → frags and HQM ore → HQM. Stone is usable raw.
- These are walk-up public machines: load diesel, come back later, collect from the output box.

## Pump Jack (crude oil)

Indestructible objects near **[[Power Plant]], [[Train Yard]], and [[Water Treatment Plant]]**. Diesel-powered like the quarries:

- **1 Diesel → 60 Crude Oil + 170 Low Grade Fuel**, per ~2 min 9 sec.
- This is a near-break-even LGF machine (170 LGF out vs the 300 LGF you'd pay for the diesel at Outpost) **but** you also get 60 crude on top — net it's a crude faucet, and crude refines 1:3 into more LGF at a Small Oil Refinery. Effectively: diesel → 170 + (60×3 =180) = ~350 LGF, slightly positive plus you can run the Excavator's frags/HQM with the surplus.
- The Pump Jack used to be a deployable; it is now monument-only.

## Placeable Mining Quarry (deployable, vanilla but rare-BP)

Player-placeable quarries still exist on some servers/maps:

1. Throw a **Survey Charge** on the ground. It shows resource abundance in a radius of ~2.5–3.5 foundations — **0 to 5 each** of Stone, Metal Ore, Metal Fragments, Sulfur. A good crater = a good spot.
2. Place the **Mining Quarry** there (it can't be picked up once placed). It always yields Rocks plus the surveyed resource.
3. Feed it diesel; collect output.

Survey-and-place is mostly a clan/large-group play and the BP is uncommon — solos/duos lean on the static quarries and the Excavator instead.

## Returning-player notes

- **Everything is diesel now.** The 2023-era low-grade quarries are gone — if you remember pouring LGF into a quarry, that's the old system. Budget diesel (= 300 LGF each at [[Outpost]]).
- The Excavator out-produces a hand-mined node run by an order of magnitude per minute, but you pay diesel and PvP risk. For a solo, the **static Sulfur/HQM quarries** are the safer bulk play; for a duo+ holding map control, the **Excavator** is unmatched.
- See [[Gathering]] for hand-mining node yields, [[Scrap Runs]] for diesel-stop routing, and [[Vending and Shops]] for the diesel buy price.

## Related

[[Giant Excavator Pit]] · [[Mining Outpost]] · [[Power Plant]] · [[Train Yard]] · [[Water Treatment Plant]] · [[Gathering]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Vending and Shops]] · [[Outpost]]

pages.title: Gathering
pages.body:
# Gathering

Node, tree and tool numbers (verified vs rusthelp.com node pages, June 2026). Hit the moving **hotspot** (sparkle) every swing — it's both a yield bonus per hit and a massive speed multiplier (see duration columns).

## Ore nodes — yield per node by tool

### Stone node
| Tool | Stone | Time (spam) | Time (hotspots) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jackhammer | **1,000** | 4s | 3s |
| Salvaged Icepick | 1,000 | 14s | 8s |
| Pickaxe | 1,000 | 27s | 12s |
| Stone Pickaxe | 794 | 25s | 11s |
| Salvaged Hammer | 536 | 20s | 9s |
| Bone Club | 450 | 55s | 20s |
| Rock | 375 | 64s | 25s |

### Metal node
| Tool | Metal Ore | HQM Ore | Time (hotspots) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jackhammer | **600** | 2 | 3s |
| Salvaged Icepick | 600 | 2 | 8s |
| Pickaxe | 600 | 2 | 12s |
| Stone Pickaxe | 485 | 2 | 11s |
| Salvaged Hammer | 358 | — | 9s |
| Rock | 250 | — | 25s |

### Sulfur node
| Tool | Sulfur Ore | Time (hotspots) |
|---|---|---|
| Jackhammer | **300** | 3s |
| Salvaged Icepick | 300 | 8s |
| Pickaxe | 300 | 12s |
| Stone Pickaxe | 257 | 11s |
| Rock | 100 | 25s |

**Rules of thumb:** anything below a Pickaxe wastes sulfur (only Jackhammer/Icepick/Pickaxe hit the full 300). Jackhammer mines a whole node in ~3–4 seconds — it has no real competitor. Snow and jungle/forest cliffsides spawn the densest node runs.

## The Jackhammer

- **Buy, don't craft:** [[Outpost]] **150 scrap** (10s restock). Travelling Vendor ~92, Floating Cities ~172 (prices float).
- Repairs **free** at WB1/repair bench (−5% max condition per repair) — one jackhammer lasts most of a wipe.
- Drops: Supply Drop 26.53%, Tools Crate 0.98%.
- Recycles to 3 blades + 36 scrap (monument) if you loot spares.

## Wood

- Trees give **500 / 750 / 1,000 wood** depending on species/size. Always collect the fallen-tree bonus and hit the moving X mark.
- **Hatchet:** 30 wood/hit. **Salvaged Axe:** 50 wood/hit (~28 wood/sec sustained).
- **Chainsaw:** same total per tree but ~2.3× faster than a Salvaged Axe in practice (test: 15,500 wood in 2:30 vs 5:50). Runs on low grade fuel, needs a rev-up, and is loud.
- Chainsaw: craft 5 HQM + 2 Gears + 6 Metal Blades @ WB2, or buy at [[Outpost]] **125 scrap**.

## Other gathering

- **Roadside Roadsign objects:** harvest with any blade for guaranteed Metal Pipe ×1 + Road Signs ×1 (see [[Components]]).
- **Animal fat → fuel:** 3 animal fat + 1 cloth craft **4 low grade fuel** — bears/boars fund early chainsaw/jackhammer fuel.
- **Crude → LGF:** 1 crude refines to **3 LGF** at a Small Oil Refinery (wood-fired).
- **Jungle biome** (since May 2025): tier-0 but predator-heavy (tigers, crocs, snakes) — great untouched node runs if you can survive it; see [[Jungle]].
- Mass production beats nodes mid-game: see [[Excavator and Quarries]].

## Early-wipe gather plan (solo)

1. Rock → 1 stone node (375) → Stone Pickaxe + Hatchet.
2. Farm to Pickaxe ASAP (full 300-sulfur nodes from then on).
3. First ~150 scrap → [[Outpost]] Jackhammer; next 125 → Chainsaw. From there a single fuel-stocked farm lap fills a small base.

pages.title: Locked Crate
pages.body:
# Locked Crate

The **Locked Crate** (a.k.a. Hackable Crate) is the single best **endgame loot piñata** in Rust and the **only guaranteed source of Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]**. You start the hack by swiping/holding it, which begins a **~15-minute (900s) timer**; when it finishes, the crate unlocks for anyone nearby — so it's a magnet for PvP. It appears at [[Cargo Ship]], the [[Oil Rig]]s (the locked crate is the reward for the rig puzzle), [[Chinook CH47]] drop sites, and Ghost Ships.

## Loot table (verified vs [[rusthelp.com]], June 2026 "Built Different")

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| **Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments|Blueprint Fragment]]** | 2 | **100.00%** |
| **Metal Armor Insert** | 1 | **100.00%** |
| Targeting Computer | 1 | 55.29% |
| Metal Facemask / Metal Chest Plate | 1 | 52.78% each |
| MLRS Aiming Module | 1 | 50.00% |
| Metal Pipe / Tech Trash | 5–15 / 2–12 | ~39% |
| [[Scrap]] | 140–159 | ~33.33% |
| Gears + Sheet Metal | 5–10 | ~31% |
| 5.56 Rifle Ammo (all variants) | — | ~30% |
| **Assault Rifle** | 1 | 28.45% |
| **LR-300** | 1 | 24.24% |
| **Bolt Action Rifle** | 1 | 22.73% |
| Computer Station / Drone / electrical / building | 1 | ~1.34% |

## Why it matters

- **Fastest WB3 in the game:** the guaranteed **×2 Advanced Fragments** means hacking **one** locked crate gets you to over half of a [[Workbench Level 3]] (needs 5 Advanced), and two crates fully clear it — no elite-crate grind required. See [[Blueprint Fragments]].
- **Guaranteed metal armor insert** + ~50%+ chances at a full metal-armor set make it a kit-up in one open.
- **AK at 28.45%** is the best single-container chance of looting a finished Assault Rifle anywhere.

## Returning-player tactics

- The **15-min hack** is loud and visible — expect company. On the [[Oil Rig]]s, hack timing draws boats; on [[Cargo Ship]], it announces your presence to anyone watching the ship.
- Solo play: hack it, then **hold the crate room / hide and wait** rather than standing on it. Greening the card on a rig also spawns scientists.
- Don't conflate this with the **Bradley/Heli crates** (different tables — those carry C4, this carries fragments + armor + rifles).

## Related

[[Loot Tables]] · [[Barrels and Crates]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Oil Rig]] · [[Cargo Ship]] · [[Scrap]] · [[Loot Table Reverse Lookup]] · [[rusthelp.com]]

pages.body:
# Loot Table Reverse Lookup

The flip side of [[Loot Tables]]: instead of *"what's in this crate"*, this answers **"I want item X — which container drops it, and at what odds?"** Percentages are per-slot roll chances from [[rusthelp.com]] (verified June 2026). For the full per-container breakdowns see [[Loot Tables]].

> Quick legend: a single crate has several random slots, so the *chance you see the item in one open* is higher than the per-slot % shown. Treat these as relative odds for "where do I farm this."

---

## Explosives & raiding tools

| Item | Best sources (per-slot %) |
|---|---|
| **Timed Explosive Charge (C4)** | Heli Crate 25% · Bradley Crate 36% · Supply Drop 26.53% · Hackable Locked Crate (in pool) · NOT in standard Elite Crate |
| **Satchel Charge** | Supply Drop 48.98% (×2) |

| Homing Missile / MLRS Aiming Module | Bradley & Heli crates · Locked Crate (Aiming Module 50%) |
| Supply Signal | Military Crate 1% |

The cheapest path to raid explosives as a solo/duo is still **crafting** (research [[Satchel Charge]]/[[Timed Explosive Charge|C4]] via the now-cheap [[Tech Tree]]) rather than crate-farming — but **Bradley + Heli kills** are the fastest loot-only explosives.

## Rifles & high-tier guns

## Weapon bodies (craft-your-own-gun components)

This is the core returning-player insight: you don't *need* to loot the finished AK — farm **Rifle Bodies** at military/elite crates and craft it once you have **WB3** ([[Blueprint Fragments]]).

## [[Blueprint Fragments]]

pages.title: Loot Tables
pages.body:
# Loot Tables

**The canonical "what drops from what, and at what odds" lookup.** This is the page you hit when you ask *"is C4 in elite crates?"*, *"what's the fragment drop chance from a military crate?"*, or *"is it worth hacking a locked crate for the AK?"* — answered with real percentages instead of vibes.

How Rust loot works (the part that makes the tables make sense):

- Every container has **guaranteed slots** (e.g. scrap is always there) plus a number of **random slots**, each of which independently rolls an item from a weighted pool.
- The percentages below are **per-slot roll chances** as published by [[rusthelp.com]] (RustLabs successor). A crate with several slots can roll the same high-% item more than once, so the *expected number per open* of a 16.67% item over (say) 3 slots is higher than 16.67%.
- Containers pay one of two currencies: **barrels pay [[Scrap]]**, **crates pay [[Components]]** (which you then [[Recycling|recycle]] into more scrap + raw mats). Military/elite crates additionally pay **[[Blueprint Fragments]]** = [[Workbench]] progression.

Companion pages: [[Barrels and Crates]] (quick summary), [[Loot Table Reverse Lookup]] (where does item X drop), [[Blueprint Fragments]] (the fragment economy in depth), [[Components]], [[Recycling]].

---

## At-a-glance: container tier ladder

| Container | Guaranteed scrap | Pays | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Barrels and Crates\|Road Barrel]] (yellow/blue) | 2 | low components | roads, monuments | ~15% chance of a useful component |
| Oil Barrel (red) | 0 | Crude + LGF | beaches, monuments | 100% fuel, no scrap |
| Food Box | **0** | food + water + rad pills | radtown, roadside | **no scrap at all** — sustenance only |
| Basic Crate | 3 | junk deployables | tier-0 monuments | worst crate; near-pure scrap |
| Normal Crate | 5 | tier-1 components | most monuments | **Semi Auto Body 14.29%** — day-1 SAR |
| Tools Crate | 5 | tools | monuments | Chainsaw/Jackhammer 0.98% each |
| Military Crate | 8 | tier-2 components | mid/high monuments | **Basic Fragment 10%**, Rifle/SMG Body 16.67% |
| Elite Crate | 25 | tier-2 comps + guns | top monuments | **Advanced Fragment 10%**, AK 4% |
| Bradley Crate | — | guns + MLRS rockets | [[Launch Site]] (Bradley kill) | targeting-computer farm; MLRS Rocket 100% |
| Heli Crate | — | guns + rockets | [[Patrol Helicopter]] wreck | best gun density per crate |
| Hackable Locked Crate | ~140–159 | endgame everything | Chinook/[[Cargo Ship]]/[[Oil Rig]]/Ghost Ship | **Advanced Fragment ×2 @ 100%**, 15-min hack |
| Supply Drop | 140–159 | explosives + guns + ammo | airdrop / supply signal | **Basic Fragment ×2 @ 100%**, Satchel ×2 49% |

---

## Road Barrel (yellow & blue — identical)

**Guaranteed: 2 [[Scrap]].** Then one component slot rolls:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| Metal Blade | 1 | 15.45% |
| Rope | 1–2 | 15.45% |
| Empty Propane Tank | 1 | 8.03% |
| Sewing Kit | 3–4 | 8.03% |
| Tarp | 1 | 8.03% |
| Electric Fuse | 1 | 1.43% |
| Gears | 2 | 1.43% |
| Metal Pipe | 1–4 | 1.43% |
| Metal Spring | 1 | 1.43% |
| Road Signs | 2–3 | 1.43% |
| **Semi Automatic Body** | 1 | 1.43% |
| Sheet Metal | 1 | 1.43% |
| Junk deployable/clothing pool (26 items: barricades, water bucket, leather gloves, igniter, guitar, hats, rugs, signs, shelves, binoculars…) | 1 | 1.13% each |

Densest barrel monuments: [[Launch Site]] ×28, Harbor Large ×18, Harbor Small ×15, [[Ferry Terminal]] ×13, Arctic Research Base ×11.

## Oil Barrel (red)

**100%: Crude Oil ×15–19 + Low Grade Fuel ×5–9.** No scrap. 1 Crude → 3 LGF at a Small Oil Refinery. See [[Diesel Fuel]]. Found at 22 monuments — Large [[Oil Rig]] ×15, Ghost Ships ×6–12, Harbors ×10, [[The Dome]] ×9, [[Launch Site]] ×7.

---

## Basic Crate

**Guaranteed: 3 [[Scrap]].** Random slot rolls one of ~31 junk deployables/clothing at **4.79% each**: stone/wooden barricades, water bucket, leather gloves, igniter, stone fireplace, acoustic guitar, beenie/boonie/baseball cap, mailbox, balaclava, bandana mask, paddle, shorts, planter boxes, rugs, salvaged shelves, tank top, wood shutters, signs, floor spikes, spinning wheel, table, binoculars, tuna can lamp, water barrel.

**Effectively a 3-scrap crate** — the component value is near-zero. Only at Giant Excavator Pit ×6, Mining Outpost ×4, [[Oxum's Gas Station|Gas Station]] ×3, Abandoned Supermarket ×2.

## Normal Crate

**Guaranteed: 5 [[Scrap]].** Tier-1 component pool, each slot at **14.29%**:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| Electric Fuse | 1 | 14.29% |
| Gears | 2 | 14.29% |
| Metal Pipe | 1–4 | 14.29% |
| Metal Spring | 1 | 14.29% |
| Road Signs | 2–3 | 14.29% |
| **Semi Automatic Body** | 1 | 14.29% |
| Sheet Metal | 1 | 14.29% |
| Diving Mask | 1 | 4.17% |
| Hazmat Suit | 1 | 4.00% |
| Large Solar Panel | 1 | 1.55% |
| Electrical switches/components (HBHF sensor, smart switch, splitter, blocker…) | 1 | 0.83–1.27% |
| Tesla Coil / RF Transmitter / rare deployables | 1 | 0.14% |

**Why it matters:** the Semi Auto Body at 14.29% per slot is the reason a [[Semi-Automatic Rifle]] is reachable on day 1 from a single monument lap. Top spawns: [[Launch Site]] ×55, [[Water Treatment Plant]] ×20, [[Airfield]] ×16, [[Power Plant]] ×14, Sewer Branch ×14, [[Missile Silo]] ×13, Radtown ×12, [[Train Yard]] ×12.

## Tools Crate

**Guaranteed: 5 [[Scrap]].**

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| Hatchet / Pickaxe / Binoculars | 1 | 7.84% each |
| Pants / Longsleeve Tee / Wood armor set | 1 | 6.54% each |
| Bone+Fire arrows / Hunting Bow / Mace / Salvaged Cleaver / Salvaged Sword | — | 4.90% each |
| Hoodie | 1 | 3.27% |
| Targeting Computer | 1 | 3.08% |
| Diving Mask | 1 | 2.72% |
| CCTV Camera | 1 | 2.52% |
| Crossbow / Combat Knife | 1 | 2.45% each |
| Salvaged Axe / Salvaged Icepick | 1 | 1.96% each |
| Diving Tank | 1 | 1.63% |
| **Chainsaw** (+20–39 LGF) | 1 | 0.98% |
| **Jackhammer** | 1 | 0.98% |
| Wetsuit / Diving Fins | 1 | 1.09% each |
| **Auto Turret** | 1 | 0.28% |
| Ammo variants (5.56, incendiary, HV, explosive) | various | 0.13–1.47% |

The Tools Crate is the **only non-elite source of Chainsaw/Jackhammer** outside the [[Tech Tree]] — but at ~1% each, don't farm it for them.

---

## Military Crate

**Guaranteed: 8 [[Scrap]].** The tier-2 component jackpot. Core pool, each slot at **16.67%**:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| High Quality Metal | 15–24 | 16.67% |
| Metal Pipe | 5 | 16.67% |
| **Rifle Body** | 1 | 16.67% |
| **SMG Body** | 1 | 16.67% |
| Tech Trash | 2–3 | 16.67% |
| **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments\|Blueprint Fragment]]** | 1 | **10.00%** |
| Targeting Computer | 1 | 8.73% |
| CCTV Camera | 1 | 7.14% |
| Metal Armor Insert | 1 | 5.00% |
| Large Backpack | 1 | 5.00% |
| Workbench upgrade (Efficiency/Prototype/Reinforced) | 1 | 1.67% each |
| Auto Turret | 1 | 1.21% |
| Supply Signal | 1 | 1.00% |
| ~80 rare items (Rocket Launcher, Pump Shotgun, Heavy Plate set, Tesla Coil, batteries, building pieces) | 1 | 0.42% each |

**No C4, no rockets in the guaranteed pool** — the Rocket Launcher is part of the 0.42% rare tail, so military crates are *not* a reliable explosives source. They ARE the best **Rifle/SMG Body** source (a duo can craft an AK off bodies + WB3). Top spawns: [[Launch Site]] ×19, [[Missile Silo]] ×18, [[Train Yard]] ×12, [[Airfield]] ×10, [[Power Plant]] ×9, Large [[Oil Rig]] ×8, Ghost Ships ×8, [[Military Tunnel]] ×5, [[Water Treatment Plant]] ×5, [[The Dome]] ×4.

## Elite Crate

**Guaranteed: 25 [[Scrap]].** Same tier-2 component pool but richer, **27.73% per core slot**, plus a real gun pool:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| High Quality Metal | 15–24 | 27.73% |
| Metal Pipe | 5 | 27.73% |
| Rifle Body | 1–3 | 27.73% |
| SMG Body | 1 | 27.73% |
| Tech Trash | 2–9 | 27.73% |
| **MLRS Rocket** | 1 | 20.00% |
| Targeting Computer | 1 | 15.27% |
| CCTV Camera | 1 | 12.61% |
| **Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments\|Blueprint Fragment]]** | 1 | **10.00%** |
| Flame Thrower (+35 LGF) | 1 | 7.23% |
| F1 Grenade / Flashbang / Molotov / SAP (Semi-Auto Pistol) | — | 7.23% each |
| **Assault Rifle** (+12 ×5.56) | 1 | 4.00% |
| **Bolt Action Rifle** (+8 ×5.56) | 1 | 4.00% |
| **MP5A4** (+30 pistol) | 1 | 4.00% |
| L96 / Spas-12 / Auto Turret / heavier kit | 1 | 0.78–2.8% |

**Is C4 in elite crates? No.** Timed Explosive Charge (C4) is *not* in the standard elite crate pool — it's in the **Bradley/Heli crates and Supply Drops**, not the monument elite crate. Elite crates DO have an AK at 4% per slot and an Advanced Fragment at 10%. Locations: [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnel]], [[Missile Silo]] (+3 extra elite crates since the Oct 2025 red-keycard change), Oil Rigs, Underwater Labs.

---

## Bradley Crate (kill the [[Bradley APC]] at [[Launch Site]])

The Bradley drops 1–3 of these. Loot leans guns + raid tools:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| **MLRS Rocket** | — | 100.00% |
| Targeting Computer | 1 | 52.38% |
| Lasersight + 8× Scope + Burst Module + Ext. Mag | — | 50.00% |
| CCTV Camera | 1 | 42.86% |
| **Timed Explosive Charge** (C4) | — | 36.00% |
| Armored Door / Ladder Hatch | 1 | 30.00% each |
| Tech Trash | 10–11 | 25.00% |
| 5.56 ammo (all variants) | 120–250 | 19.00% |
| Rockets (Incendiary/HV/MLRS/Homing) | mixed | 19.00% |
| Armored Double Door | 1 | 15.00% |
| **L96** (+ Variable Zoom + ammo) | 1 | 8.68% |
| **M249** (+50 ×5.56) | 1 | 8.33% |
| Auto Turret | 1 | 4.76% |
| M92 / Prototype 17 / misc rifles & SMGs | 1 | 0.35–0.87% |

**The targeting-computer + C4 farm.** Bradley crates are one of the few non-locked-crate sources of C4 (36%).

## Heli Crate (kill the [[Patrol Helicopter]])

Best **gun density per crate** in the game. The Heli drops 4–6 crates on death:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| **Timed Explosive Charge** (C4) + Rocket | 2 + 3 | 25.00% |
| 5.56 ammo (all variants) | 120+60+30+40 | 15.00% |
| Rockets (Incendiary/HV/MLRS/Homing) | 5+3+2+4 | 15.00% |
| **M249** (+50 ×5.56) | 1 | 10.00% |
| Lasersight + 8× Scope + Burst + Ext. Mag | — | 7.50% |
| AK / Bolt / MP5A4 (+ammo) | 1 | 2.26% each |
| M92 / Prototype 17 / Custom SMG / Thompson | 1 | 1.56% each |
| LR-300 / M39 / M4 Shotgun / armor / doors / HMLMG | 1 | 0.63–0.94% |

---

## Hackable Locked Crate (Chinook / [[Cargo Ship]] / [[Oil Rig]] / Ghost Ship)

**Hack timer ~15 minutes** (900s) once you swipe the green card / start the hack. The single best **endgame loot piÃ±ata**, and the *only guaranteed Advanced Fragment source*:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| **Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments\|Blueprint Fragment]]** | 2 | **100.00%** |
| Metal Armor Insert | 1 | 100.00% |
| Targeting Computer | 1 | 55.29% |
| Metal Facemask / Metal Chest Plate | 1 | 52.78% each |
| MLRS Aiming Module | 1 | 50.00% |
| [[Scrap]] | 140–159 | ~33.33% |
| 5.56 Rifle Ammo (all variants) | — | ~30% |
| **Assault Rifle** | 1 | 28.45% |
| **LR-300** | 1 | 24.24% |
| **Bolt Action Rifle** | 1 | 22.73% |
| Metal Pipe / Tech Trash | 5–15 / 2–12 | ~39% |
| Gears + Sheet Metal | 5–10 | ~31% |
| Computer Station / Drone / electrical / building | 1 | ~1.34% |

A duo can hit WB3 off **one hacked locked crate** (Advanced ×2) without ever touching an elite crate. See [[Blueprint Fragments]].

## Supply Drop (airdrop / [[Supply Signal]])

The **explosives + ammo crate.** Comes from a free airdrop or a crafted/looted Supply Signal:

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments\|Blueprint Fragment]]** | 2 | **100.00%** |
| Pistol Bullet | 15 | 82.20% |
| 12 Gauge Buckshot | 6 | 70.00% |
| HQM | 32–39 | 55.56% |
| [[Scrap]] | 140–159 | 55.56% |
| 5.56 Rifle Ammo | 12 | 50.67% |
| 12 Gauge Incendiary / Slug | 4–7 / 4 | 50.00% each |
| **Satchel Charge** | 2 | 48.98% |
| **F1 Grenade** | 6–9 | 48.98% |
| Road-sign / bucket / coffee-can armor | 1 | 36–43% |
| Chainsaw / Jackhammer / **Timed Explosive Charge** (C4) | 1 | 26.53% each |
| SAR / Pump Shotgun / Custom SMG / Thompson | 1 | 23.44% each |
| M92 / M39 / Spas-12 / MP5A4 | 1 | 18.31% each |
| Ballistic armor pieces | 1 | 8.33% |
| **LR-300** | 1 | 3.81% |

A supply signal popped on a roof is a strong early-wipe spike: guaranteed 2 Basic fragments + ~half-chance of Satchels/C4 + a gun.

---

## Food Box (the "no scrap" container)

**Guaranteed scrap: ZERO.** A common returning-player misconception is that food boxes pay scrap like crates — they don't. The food box is a pure-sustenance container (verified on [[rusthelp.com]], June 2026):

| Item | Qty | Chance |
|---|---|---|
| Anti-Radiation Pills | 1 | 24.89% |
| Water Jug | 1 | 24.89% |
| Apple / Bread Loaf / Can of Beans / Can of Tuna / Chocolate Bar / Corn / Granola Bar / Honeycomb / Pickles (×1-2) / Potato / Small Water Bottle | 1 | 12.89% each |

Most common at **Radtown ×12**, plus Giant Excavator Pit, [[Oxum's Gas Station|Gas Station]], and Abandoned Supermarket. Loot it for early radiation pills + water on a scrap run, but never count it toward your scrap math. (There is a separate **Normal Crate - Food** wagon variant in train tunnels that mirrors the normal-crate scrap; the loose roadside/radtown *food box* is the zero-scrap one.)

## Underwater Lab & wagon crates (quick)

- **UW Lab Fuel Crate:** 100% Crude ×30–38 + LGF ×10–18 — best single fuel grab in the game.
- **UW Lab Tier-3 component crate:** densest components anywhere — 30.56% rolls on Metal Pipe ×5–10, Tech Trash ×2–6, Rifle/SMG Body ×1–2.
- **UW Lab Elite Crate:** mirrors the surface Elite Crate (25 scrap, Advanced Fragment 10%).
- **Train tunnel wagon crates:** Military Wagon Crate **11 scrap**; Normal Wagon Crate **5 scrap** + 14.29% tier-1 rolls (same pool as Normal Crate).

---

## Fragment drop odds (the question everyone asks)

| Source | Fragment | Rate |
|---|---|---|
| Hackable Locked Crate | Advanced | **×2 @ 100%** |
| Supply Drop | Basic | **×2 @ 100%** |
| Top monuments ([[Launch Site]]/[[Military Tunnel]]/[[Missile Silo]]) loot rooms | Advanced | ×2 @ 100% |
| Underwater Lab | Basic ~×4 / Advanced ~×2 | 100% |
| Tier-1 monuments ([[Power Plant]]/[[Train Yard]]/[[Water Treatment Plant]]) | Basic | ×3 @ 100% |
| [[Airfield]] / Arctic Research Base | Basic | ×2 @ 100% |
| Military Crate | Basic | **10% per slot** |
| Elite Crate | Advanced | **10% per slot** |
| Metal Detector (roads/rails) | Basic | 6.1% chance |
| Conversion bench | 20 Basic → 1 Advanced | n/a |

Full fragment economy, workbench costs, and farming routes: **[[Blueprint Fragments]]**.

---

## Returning-player TL;DR

- **Barrels = scrap; crates = components; elite/military/locked = fragments + guns.**
- **C4 (Timed Explosive Charge)** is NOT in standard elite crates — get it from **Bradley (36%)**, **Heli (25%)**, **Supply Drops (26.5%)**, or **Locked Crates**.
- **AK (Assault Rifle):** 4% per elite-crate slot, 28% per locked crate, 2.26% per heli crate — or just craft it off **Rifle Bodies** (16.67% per military-crate slot) once you have WB3.
- **Fastest WB3:** hack one **Locked Crate** → guaranteed Advanced Fragment ×2.
- **Day-1 gun:** Normal Crates drop **Semi Auto Body at 14.29%** — one monument lap = a SAR.

## Verification note

All container scrap and drop-chance numbers on this page were re-checked against [[rusthelp.com]] (RustLabs successor) in **June 2026**, current as of the **"Built Different"** wipe (Jun 4 2026). Confirmed exact: Basic 3 / Normal 5 / Tools 5 / Military 8 / Elite 25 guaranteed scrap; Military core pool 16.67% + Basic Fragment 10%; Elite core pool 27.73% + Advanced Fragment 10% + AK/Bolt/MP5 4% + MLRS Rocket 20%; Locked Crate Advanced Fragment ×2 @ 100% + Metal Armor Insert 100% + Targeting Computer 55.29% + AK 28.45% + LR-300 24.24% + Bolt 22.73% + scrap ×140-159 @ 33.33%; Oil Barrel Crude ×15-19 + LGF ×5-9 @ 100% (no scrap); Food Box = no scrap.

pages.title: Pump Jack
pages.body:
# Pump Jack

A diesel-powered crude-oil machine. Once a deployable, the Pump Jack is now an **indestructible monument object** found near **[[Power Plant]], [[Train Yard]], and [[Water Treatment Plant]]**. Feed it [[Diesel Fuel]] and it pumps crude oil + low grade fuel.

## Output

| Per 1 Diesel (~2 min 9 sec) | Yield |
|---|---|
| Crude Oil | **60** |
| Low Grade Fuel | **170** |

### Is it worth the diesel?

Diesel costs **300 LGF** at [[Outpost]]. One pump cycle returns **170 LGF directly + 60 crude**, and crude refines 1:3 into LGF at a Small Oil Refinery (60 crude → 180 LGF). So:

- Total LGF-equivalent out: 170 + 180 = **~350 LGF** for a 300-LGF diesel = **slightly positive**, plus you keep flexibility (crude can fuel furnaces/refineries directly, or be sold at [[Bandit Camp]]).
- The Pump Jack is therefore a **near-break-even crude/LGF faucet** — useful for stocking the fuel you need to *also* run the [[Giant Excavator Pit]] for frags/HQM, not a standalone profit engine.

## How to use

1. Bring diesel ([[Diesel Fuel]] — buy at Outpost for 300 LGF, or loot at the Dome/Oil Rig/etc.).
2. Walk up to the Pump Jack at Power Plant / Train Yard / Water Treatment.
3. Load diesel; collect crude oil + LGF from the output.

It's a public, walk-up machine — no survey charge, no placement, no BP needed (unlike the rare placeable [[Excavator and Quarries|Mining Quarry]]).

## Returning-player note

The Pump Jack used to be a **placeable deployable** you'd survey-and-drop like a quarry. It's now **monument-only and indestructible** — you can't own one, you share the public ones. Pair it with the static [[Excavator and Quarries|quarries]] and the [[Giant Excavator Pit]] for a full diesel-mining loop.

## Related

[[Diesel Fuel]] · [[Excavator and Quarries]] · [[Giant Excavator Pit]] · [[Power Plant]] · [[Train Yard]] · [[Water Treatment Plant]] · [[Gathering]] · [[Vending and Shops]]

pages.title: Recycling
pages.body:
# Recycling

Recyclers break [[Components]] and items back into [[Scrap]] and raw materials. **Since May 2 2024 there are two recycler classes** — this is the single most important economy change for a returning 2023 player:

| | Safe-zone recycler | Monument ("Radtown") recycler |
|---|---|---|
| Cycle time | **8s** per stack | **5s** per stack |
| Yield | **−20%** vs old baseline | **+20%** vs old baseline |
| Risk | None (safe zone) | Full PvP, camp-able |
| Where | [[Outpost]] (×3), [[Bandit Camp]] (×2) | 19 monuments, 24 recyclers |

Net effect: a monument recycler returns **~50% more** material than a safe-zone one (120 vs 80) and runs ~40% faster. Community shorthand: monument ≈ 60% of an item's craft cost back, safe-zone ≈ 40%.

> Source: the May 2 2024 "Meta Madness" change, per Facepunch's own post — *"Recyclers in Safe Zones... cycle time has increased to 8 seconds and they now yield 80% of what they used to. Recyclers found at Monuments have the same cycle time as before but now yield 120%."* So the split is literally **80% @ 8s (safe-zone)** vs **120% @ 5s (monument)**. The per-component table below is the *monument (120%)* yield in the left column.

## Monument recycler locations (24 total)

Power Plant ×3, Sewer Branch ×2, Airfield ×2, and ×1 each at: Abandoned Supermarket, Arctic Research Base, Ferry Terminal, [[Giant Excavator Pit]], Harbor (Large), Harbor (Small), [[Junkyard]], [[Launch Site]], Lighthouse, [[Military Tunnel]], Mining Outpost, Oxum's Gas Station, Radtown, Satellite Dish, Train Yard, Water Treatment Plant.

Low-traffic, low-rad picks for solos: **Oxum's, Mining Outpost, Supermarket, Lighthouse** — tier-0, no hazmat needed, fast in-and-out.

## Mechanics

- 6 input slots; processes top-to-bottom, one stack "bundle" per cycle.
- No fuel needed.
- You can stop it mid-run; outputs accumulate in the bottom grid.
- Recyclers are the #1 ambush spot in the game. Drop a [[Sleeping Bag]] nearby, don't stand still, and clear audio cues first.

## Scrap per component (monument / safe-zone)

| Component | Monument | Safe-zone |
|---|---|---|
| Rifle Body | **30** (+1 HQM, 80% +1) | 20 (+1 HQM) |
| Tech Trash | **24** (+1 HQM) | 16 |
| Electric Fuse | 24 | 16 |
| SMG Body | 18 (+1 HQM, 80% +1) | 12 (+1 HQM) |
| Semi Auto Body | 18 (+90 frags +1 HQM) | 12 (+60 frags +1 HQM) |
| Gears | 12 (+15 frags) | 8 (+10 frags) |
| Metal Spring | 12 (+1 HQM) | 8 |
| Sheet Metal | 9 (+120 frags +1 HQM) | 6 (+80 frags) |
| Metal Pipe | 6 (+1 HQM) | 4 |
| Road Signs | 6 (+1 HQM) | 4 |
| Metal Blade | 2 (+18 frags) | 1 (+12 frags) |
| Propane Tank | 1 (+60 frags) | (+40 frags) |

Material-focused recycles: **Tarp → 60/40 cloth**, **Rope → 18/12 cloth**, **Sewing Kit → 12/8 cloth + rope**. A Small Oil Refinery recycles to 150/100 low grade fuel.

> Pinned vs [[rusthelp.com]] (June 2026, "Built Different"): **Rifle Body = 30 scrap monument / 20 safe-zone** (+1 HQM both; 80% bonus-HQM monument vs 20% safe-zone), **Tech Trash = 24 / 16**. These are the two highest-value common recyclables and the spine of every scrap-run loop — don't ever recycle bodies/tech trash at a safe zone if a monument recycler is reachable.

## Strategy

1. **Never dump components at Outpost out of habit.** The 2023 reflex is wrong now — a full inventory of bodies/tech trash is worth ~50% more two grid squares away at a monument recycler.
2. **Recycle for HQM early.** Springs, pipes, road signs and sheet metal are the early HQM faucet (80%/20% bonus rolls) before you have a furnace economy.
3. **Keep, don't recycle:** springs + semi bodies (SAR/SKS crafting), rifle bodies until you've crafted your AK, 1–2 fuses for [[Monument Puzzles]], tarp if you need a Hazmat.
4. **Junk weapons recycle well** — e.g. a looted Jackhammer recycles to 3 metal blades + 36 scrap at a monument recycler (2 + 24 safe-zone).

See [[Scrap Runs]] for full recycle-loop routes and [[Barrels and Crates]] for what feeds the loop.

pages.title: Rust Economy
pages.body:
# Rust Economy

The loot-and-scrap economy is the backbone of every wipe: barrels and crates drop [[Scrap]] and [[Components]], recyclers convert components into more scrap and raw materials, and scrap buys research, vehicles, and gear. Since the Oct/Nov 2025 progression rework ("Meta Shift" + "Pivot Or Die"), scrap is **cheap to spend** (research costs slashed to 15/30/60/120) but workbench tiering now runs on [[Blueprint Fragments]] hunted at monuments — so the economy loop is: *farm scrap early → WB1 → monument runs for fragments + components → recycle at monument recyclers → research everything cheaply.*

## Pages in this folder

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [[Scrap]] | Every scrap source ranked, amounts per container, everything scrap buys |
| [[Components]] | Section per component: where it drops, recycle yields, what it crafts |
| [[Recycling]] | Safe-zone vs monument recycler yields (the May 2024 split), locations, per-component tables |
| [[Scrap Runs]] | Best scrap/hour routes — roads, tunnels, junkyard shredder, monument loops, solo vs duo |
| [[Barrels and Crates]] | Loot table summaries for every barrel and crate tier |
| [[Loot Tables]] | **Master drop-rate reference** — full per-container tables (every item + %) for every barrel/crate/drop, plus the fragment-odds table |
| [[Loot Table Reverse Lookup]] | "Where does item X drop, and at what odds" — reverse index by item (C4, AK, fragments, components, armor) |
| [[Gathering]] | Tools, node yields, hotspots, wood rates, jackhammer/chainsaw math |
| [[Excavator and Quarries]] | Giant Excavator + static quarry yields per diesel |
| [[Diesel Fuel]] | The mining fuel: where to get it, the 300-LGF math, what it powers |
| [[Pump Jack]] | Crude oil + LGF per diesel at Power Plant / Train Yard / Water Treatment |
| [[Blueprint Fragments]] | The new tiering currency: where Basic/Advanced fragments drop, workbench costs |
| [[Vending and Shops]] | Outpost/Bandit Camp price lists, Air Wolf vehicles, dynamic pricing |
| [[Skins and the Skin Economy]] | Cosmetic-only skins, Steam Market vs real-money cashout, Workshop creator pipeline |
| [[Applying Skins In-Game]] | Craft-time skin selector, Repair Bench re-skin, Spray Can on deployables |
| [[Twitch and Kick Drops]] | Free account-bound skins: linking, watch-time tiers, claiming on Twitch + Kick |

## Headline numbers (verified June 2026)

- Research costs: **15 / 30 / 60 / 120 scrap** by rarity (Pivot Or Die, Nov 2025). Workbenches cost **no scrap** to craft.
- Recyclers: safe-zone = **8s/stack, −20% yield**; monument = **5s/stack, +20% yield** (May 2024 split). Monument recyclers give **~50% more** output than safe-zone ones.
- Barrel = **2 scrap** + ~15% chance of a component. Crate scrap (guaranteed): Basic **3** · Normal/Tools **5** · Military **8** · Elite **25** · Locked Crate **140-159 @ 33%**. **Food Box = 0 scrap** (food/water only — a returning-player trap). All re-verified vs [[rusthelp.com]] June 2026.
- Giant Excavator: 1 diesel = 2 min = **10,000 stone** or **5,000 metal frags** or **2,000 sulfur ore** or **100 HQM ore**.
- Official servers now **wipe blueprints monthly** (since Nov 2025).

## Related (other folders)

[[Outpost]] · [[Bandit Camp]] · [[Junkyard]] · [[Launch Site]] · [[Missile Silo]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Workbench]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Minicopter]]

pages.title: Scrap
pages.body:
# Scrap

The universal currency. Used at the [[Research Table]] (research blueprints), [[Tech Tree]] (unlock paths), every NPC vending machine, and a handful of high-tier craft recipes. **Stack size ×1,000**, despawns in 20 minutes (item ID -932201673).

Since "Pivot Or Die" (Nov 2025) scrap is much cheaper to spend: research costs are **15 / 30 / 60 / 120** scrap by rarity tier (down from 20/75/125/500), and **workbenches no longer cost any scrap** — tiering up runs on [[Blueprint Fragments]] instead. Scrap is no longer the bottleneck; fragments are.

## Every source, ranked (guaranteed drops unless noted)

| Source | Scrap | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Supply Drop | ×140–318 (55.56% chance) | Biggest single hit in the game |
| Locked Crate (Chinook / [[Oil Rig]] / Ghost Ship) | ×140–159 (33.33%) | Plus 2 guaranteed Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] |
| Elite Crate | ×25 | [[Launch Site]], [[Missile Silo]], [[Military Tunnel]], labs |
| Underwater Lab Elite Crate | ×25 | |
| Wagon Military Crate | ×11 | Train tunnels |
| Military Crate | ×8 | 100% |
| Underwater Lab crates (normal/components/vehicle parts) | ×8 | 100% |
| Vehicle Parts crate | ×8 | Roadside / [[Junkyard]] |
| Normal Crate / Tools Crate / Jungle Crate / Wagon Normal | ×5 | 100% |
| Basic Crate | ×3 | 100% |
| **Yellow & blue road barrels** | **×2** | 100% — the bread-and-butter early source |
| Military Tunnel / PT Boat / RHIB scientists | ×8–33 (36.34%) | Best NPC scrap |
| Road scientists / Outbreak Sprayer | ×8–22 (23.61%) | |
| Fish (catfish, salmon, orange roughy, small shark) | ×6 (20%) | Gutting fish — passive fish-trap farms work |

> Not a scrap source: the **Food Box** (radtown/roadside) pays **zero scrap** — food, water, and rad pills only. Don't count it in scrap math. See [[Loot Tables]].

Indirect sources (often bigger than direct drops):
- **Recycling [[Components]]** — a rifle body is 30 scrap at a monument recycler; see [[Recycling]].
- **[[Junkyard]] shredder** — 200 scrap per [[Minicopter]], 500 per [[Attack Helicopter]]; see [[Scrap Runs]].
- **Selling at [[Bandit Camp]]/Outpost vending** — crude oil, excess components, etc. See [[Vending and Shops]].

## What scrap buys

| Sink | Cost |
|---|---|
| Research (per item, by rarity) | **15 / 30 / 60 / 120** scrap |
| [[Tech Tree]] unlocks | Same rarity costs, path-based (multi-node path-unlock since Apr 2026) |
| [[Research Table]] research (per item, by rarity) | **15 / 30 / 60 / 120** scrap (reduced to match the tech tree in Nov 2025; old flat 75/250/500 is dead) + consumes a copy |
| [[Research Table]] (craft the table itself) | 200 metal frags + **20 scrap** (WB1) |
| Metal Pipe (craft) | 2 HQM + **20 scrap** (WB3) |
| Metal Blade (craft) | 30 frags + **10 scrap** (WB2) |
| [[Outpost]] components | Gears 125 · Spring 60 · Pipe 30 · Sheet Metal 30 · Blade 15 |
| [[Outpost]] tools | Jackhammer **150** · Chainsaw **125** |
| Low Grade Fuel ([[Outpost]]) | 20 LGF for 10 scrap |
| Air Wolf ([[Bandit Camp]]) | Hot Air Balloon **150** · [[Minicopter]] **750** · Scrap Transport Heli **1,250** · [[Attack Helicopter]] **2,250** |
| Boats (Fishing Village) | Rowboat **125** · RHIB **300** |
| Outpost deployables (range) | ×5 (Sprinkler) up to ×500 (Wind Turbine, SAM Site, LR-300) |

> NPC vending prices **float with demand** since Jul 2024 — Travelling Vendor and Floating City prices drift (e.g. jackhammer ~92–172 scrap depending on vendor/demand). Outpost core prices above are the stable reference. See [[Vending and Shops]].

## Early-wipe rule of thumb

A road barrel is 2 scrap + ~15% component odds; ~25 barrels ≈ WB1-era research money plus a pocket of components. Don't recycle at safe zones unless contested — monument recyclers pay ~50% more (see [[Recycling]]).

pages.title: Scrap Runs
pages.body:
# Scrap Runs

Best scrap-per-hour routes as of June 2026, ranked for solo/duo/trio play. Per-hour figures are community estimates (rustmods 2026 guide) — treat as relative rankings, not guarantees. All routes assume you end at a **monument recycler** (see [[Recycling]] — +50% over safe zones).

## The ranking

| Method | Scrap/hr | Group size | Risk | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Train tunnels + recycler loop | **~1,500–2,000** | Solo+ | Med | SAR/revolver, ~100 rounds |
| [[Launch Site]] loop | ~1,500–2,000 | Duo+ | High | Hazmat, [[Blue Keycard]]/[[Red Keycard]] |
| Arctic Research Base | ~2,500–3,000 | Trio | High | Guns, kits |
| [[Missile Silo]] | ~1,200+ | Solo+ | Med-High | Red keycard run |
| Fishing (passive traps) | ~1,500–2,000 overnight | Solo | None | Fish traps; gut fish (20% ×6 scrap each) |
| [[Junkyard]] shredder | **800–1,500** | Solo | Low-Med | Low grade fuel |
| Sea trash / ocean barrel run | 800–1,200 | Solo | Low | Boat or [[DPV]] |
| Road barrel farming | low but instant | Solo | Low | A rock and patience |

## Route notes

### Road farming (hour 0 of wipe)
Every yellow/blue barrel = **2 scrap** + ~15% component roll + ~1.4% jackpot roll (gears, semi body, etc. — see [[Barrels and Crates]]). Ring road on a [[Pedal Bike]]/[[Motorbike]] beats walking 3:1. Smash roadside **Roadsign objects** too — guaranteed metal pipe ×1 and road signs ×1 per sign.

### Train tunnels (the solo workhorse)
Underground rail network under every monument: tunnel dwellers (7.43% springs, 15.42% tarp/propane, 28.51% blades/rope each) + wagon crates (military wagon crate = **11 scrap**) + military crates. Loop: clear a station → loot → ride work cart to next station → surface at a monument with a recycler. ~1.5–2k/hr with recycling. Bring 100+ rounds; dwellers rush in melee packs.

### Junkyard shredder
Crane costs **20 low grade/minute** to operate; magnet-drop vehicles into the shredder:
- [[Attack Helicopter]] **500** scrap · Scrap Transport Heli **300** · [[Minicopter]] **200**
- Chassis: large **150** / medium **125** / small **75**
- Junk pickup trucks around the yard: **50 scrap + 50 frags** each (usually 5–10 spawned)
- Snowmobile 50 · Motorbike(+sidecar) 40 · Trike 30 · Bicycle 25
- Modules shred to 25–87 frags + wood, armored/engine modules add 1–2 HQM

Shred value scales with vehicle HP (50% health = 50% scrap). Junkyard has its own recycler + yellow barrels, so it chains into a recycle loop: **800–1,500/hr solo**. Stealing a parked heli and shredding it is real money.

### Monument recycle loop (duo classic)
Harbor → Ferry Terminal → Radtown (or your local 3-monument triangle): barrels on the way, crates inside, fragments for [[Blueprint Fragments]] progress, recycle everything on-site at each monument recycler. A duo splits: one loots, one holds the recycler.

### Big-game scrap
- **Locked Crates** (Cargo/Oil Rig/Chinook): 33.33% chance of **140–159 scrap** plus 2 guaranteed Advanced fragments and 31–55% rolls on top components.
- **Supply Drops**: 55.56% chance of **140–318 scrap** — contest every airdrop you can reach.
- [[Cargo Ship]] and [[Oil Rig]] are scrap-dense but contested; treat as PvP events, not farm routes (Oil Rig floods with radiation 30 min after the crate hack now).

## Solo vs duo vs trio

- **Solo:** tunnels + junkyard + sea trash. Avoid Arctic/Launch unless the server's dead. Passive fish traps overnight.
- **Duo:** monument triangle loop with a recycler guard; Launch Site barrel yard (28 yellow + blue barrels) is now efficient.
- **Trio:** Arctic Research Base (~2.5–3k/hr) and Locked Crate contests become first-class options.

Spend plan for what you farm: see [[Scrap]] ("what scrap buys") and [[Blueprint Fragments]] for why monuments beat pure barrel scrap now.

pages.title: Skins and the Skin Economy
pages.body:
# Skins and the Skin Economy

Skins in Rust are **purely cosmetic re-textures** of items, weapons, deployables, clothing, and tools. They change appearance only — **no skin affects damage, recoil, durability, capacity, range, or any gameplay stat** (Facepunch has held this rule since skins launched in 2015; there is no pay-to-win in the official skin system). The one thing skins *do* have is real-money value: many are tradeable Steam Marketplace items, which makes Rust one of the larger skin economies on Steam alongside CS2.

This page covers where skins come from, how the economy works, and whether you can turn them into real money. For *applying* a skin in-game see [[Applying Skins In-Game]]; for free skins from streams see [[Twitch and Kick Drops]].

## TL;DR for a returning player

- Skins are cosmetic only. They never affect stats. Run them freely.
- You apply them **for free** at craft time, or for free at a [[Repair Bench]], or on deployables with a [[Spray Can]] (100 metal frags).
- **Steam Marketplace selling = Steam Wallet credit only**, never real cash out. To get actual money you must use third-party trade sites (with fees + risk).
- **Drops skins (Twitch/Kick) and most Twitch-only / store "limited" skins are account-bound** — not tradeable, no market value.
- Owning a skin on Steam = it's usable on **every server** automatically; no need to re-buy per wipe.

## Where skins come from

| Source | Tradeable? | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Rust Item Store** (in-game / Steam store) | Most yes; some marked limited | Real money (~$0.50–$5 typical) | Rotating store of community workshop skins Facepunch approved |
| **Steam Community Market** | Yes (marketable ones) | Steam Wallet | Buy/sell between players; 7-day trade hold on freshly bought |
| **Twitch / Kick Drops** | **No — account-bound** | Free (watch time) | See [[Twitch and Kick Drops]] |
| **Twitch streamer redemption / promo skins** | Usually no | Free | Limited promo skins, often non-marketable |
| **Workshop "accepted" skins** | Yes once in store | Real money | Community-made, voted up, then sold |

## The Steam Workshop creator pipeline

Anyone can make a Rust skin and submit it to the **[[Steam Workshop]]**. Facepunch's in-game workshop tool (no Unity install required anymore — you preview in-game) lets creators upload alternate textures for items and weapons. Players vote; the most popular skins get **accepted into the Rust Item Store** as premium cosmetics.

- When an accepted skin sells, the **creator gets a revenue share** of the sale.
- Facepunch has paid out **over $1,000,000** to community skin creators (cumulative, per PCGamesN; an earlier milestone cited $250,000).
- Standard Steam Workshop creator share is **25%** of the sale (Valve/Facepunch split), consistent with other Workshop economies; exact Rust percentage isn't published but tracks that norm.

## Can you sell Rust skins for real money?

Short answer: **not through Steam directly.**

### Official Steam Community Market

- You can list marketable skins on the **Steam Community Market** and sell them to other players.
- **Proceeds land in your Steam Wallet** — usable for games, DLC, or buying other skins. **You cannot withdraw Steam Wallet to a bank/card.** It is locked to the Steam ecosystem.
- Steam takes a **15% fee** on each sale (5% Steam + 10% game-specific transaction fee).
- Freshly traded/purchased items carry a **7-day Steam trade hold** before they can move again.

### Third-party trade/cashout sites (real cash, but caveats)

To convert skins into **actual money** (crypto, bank transfer, debit card), people use third-party marketplaces. Commonly named in 2026: **Skinport, Tradeit.gg, ShadowPay, SkinSwap, Skin.Land, SkinsMonkey**. General flow: log in with Steam → select skins → pick payout (BTC/ETH/USDT, bank, or card) → trade completes → you get cash.

**Caveats (state these to any returning player before they cash out):**
- These sites are **third-party, not endorsed by Steam/Facepunch.** Using them can risk your account (Steam ToS gray area for selling for cash; scam risk).
- They take a **cut/spread** (often 10–30% under "real" value).
- Payout values are well below in-game "shown" prices.
- Scams, fake sites, and trade-hijack bots are common — verify the domain.

## What's tradeable vs not

- **Tradeable / marketable:** most Item Store skins and Workshop-accepted skins.
- **Account-bound (no value, can't sell):** all **Twitch/Kick Drops** skins, most promo/redemption skins, and some store skins explicitly flagged "limited / not marketable."
- A skin you only got from Drops can still be **applied freely in-game forever**, but it will never appear on the Steam Market.

## Economy facts to remember

- Skins are **per-account, cross-server, persistent through wipes.** Once you own it on Steam, it's available on every official/community server, every wipe, no re-buy.
- A skin does **not** need to be re-purchased when blueprints wipe — skins live in your **Steam inventory**, separate from in-game progression.
- Rust's skin market is one of Steam's most active; rare/discontinued skins (e.g., old limited drops, "Glory" AK, early metalwork sets) can trade for **hundreds of dollars**.

## Related

[[Applying Skins In-Game]] · [[Twitch and Kick Drops]] · [[Spray Can]] · [[Repair Bench]] · [[Steam Workshop]] · [[Rust Economy]] · [[Vending and Shops]]

## Sources

- rusthelp.com — Spray Can, Repair Bench item pages
- tradeit.gg/blog — How to Apply Rust Skins
- psxextreme.com — How to Sell Rust Skins for Real Money 2026
- skinport.com / shadowpay.com — third-party marketplace listings
- pcgamesn.com — Rust skin creators paid $1M
- steamcommunity.com/workshop/about (appid 252490) — Rust Workshop

pages.title: Twitch and Kick Drops
pages.body:
# Twitch and Kick Drops

**Drops are free, account-bound skins you earn by watching Rust streams** that have the *Drops Enabled* tag. Facepunch runs them on **two platforms now**: Twitch (long-running) and **Kick** (added 2025/2026). They are the main way to get free cosmetics. The catch: Drops skins are **account-bound — not tradeable and worth $0 on the market** ([[Skins and the Skin Economy]]). They are still nice cosmetics you can apply forever via [[Applying Skins In-Game]].

You do **not** need Twitch Prime or any paid subscription to earn Drops — just a free Twitch/Kick account and Rust on Steam.

## How Drops work (both platforms)

1. **Own Rust on Steam** — you can't receive any Drop item without it.
2. **Link your accounts.** Connect your Steam account and your Twitch (or Kick) account on the Facepunch Drops page:
   - Twitch: the official Rust Twitch Drops linking page (twitch.facepunch.com / via twitch.tv settings → Connections).
   - Kick: **kick.facepunch.com** → link Steam + Kick.
3. **Watch Drops-Enabled streams.** Find Rust streams tagged *Drops Enabled*. Watch time **accumulates across sessions and across streams**, but **only one stream counts at a time** — multi-boxing tabs does NOT stack progress.
4. **Claim manually.** Earned ≠ claimed. Go to your inventory page and **click Claim** for each drop:
   - Twitch: `twitch.tv/drops/inventory` — confirm it shows **Claimed**.
   - Kick: the Kick Drops Inventory page.
5. **Drops unlock in sequence** — you must claim the lower-tier drop before progress counts toward the next.
6. **Delivery to Rust:** items appear in your in-game inventory on next login.
   - Kick: ~10 min, up to ~30 min.
   - Twitch: usually fast, but Steam delivery can take **up to 7 days** during big rounds.

## Watch-time tiers (typical round)

A standard round has **4–6 skins**, each gated behind a **cumulative** watch-time threshold; finishing a whole round needs **~6–8 hours** total. Example structure from the April 2026 "Peanut's Wasteland" Twitch round:

| Reward | Item type | Cumulative watch time |
|---|---|---|
| TheBurntPeanut Rock | Rock skin | 2 hours |
| The Nutsack | Sleeping bag skin | 4 hours |
| TheBurntPeanut Door | Garage door skin | 6 hours |
| TheBurntPeanut L96 | [[L96]] rifle skin | 8 hours |

**Round cadence:** new Twitch Drops rounds run roughly monthly, usually paired with the **first-Thursday force wipe** ([[Wipe Schedule]]). Round numbers are in the high 40s+ as of 2026 (e.g. "Round 48 Homebrewed 4.0").

## Kick Drops (the newer program)

Kick Drops are **separate** from Twitch — different platform, different streamers, different items. As of June 2026 the live one is the **Round 3 "Kick Off 2" event (through June 21, 2026)**.

Kick rounds split into two categories:

- **General drops** (any Drops-Enabled Kick stream):
  - Large Wood Box — 2 hours
  - Garage Door — 4 hours
  - Locker — 6 hours
- **Streamer-specific drops** — weapons/building/cosmetic skins, typically **2 hours per drop**, only earned watching that specific streamer.

You can earn on **both Twitch and Kick** in the same period to collect both sets.

## Practical tips

- Set your stream to a **low quality** and leave it running in a background tab to bank watch time (1 stream at a time still applies).
- You can watch on **PC, mobile, or other devices** — being logged in is what matters.
- **Claim before the round ends** — unclaimed drops can expire after the round closes.
- These skins **cannot be sold** — don't expect market value. They're for personal use only.
- For the **current round's exact items/dates**, check @playrust on Twitter, rust.facepunch.com/news, or kick.facepunch.com — rounds change monthly and details post 24–72h before going live.

## Related

[[Skins and the Skin Economy]] · [[Applying Skins In-Game]] · [[Wipe Schedule]] · [[Rust Economy]]

## Sources

- kick.facepunch.com — Kick Drops Round 3 (June 2026)
- lagofast.com — All Rust Twitch Drops 2026
- wiki.facepunch.com/rust/twitch-drops — official
- dmarket.com/blog — Rust Twitch Drops
- gamerant.com — April 2026 TheBurntPeanut round
- frozen-rust.com — Twitch Drops round history

pages.title: Vending and Shops
pages.body:
# Vending and Shops

Every NPC store and the player shopping systems, in one place. This is the **scrap sink** side of the economy — where farmed [[Scrap]] turns into tools, guns, vehicles, components, and keycards. The two safe-zone hubs are [[Outpost]] and [[Bandit Camp]]; the full per-machine price lists live on those monument pages — this page is the cross-monument reference plus the things that aren't tied to one shop (dynamic pricing, Drone Marketplace, Travelling Vendor, Fishing Village boats).

> **2026 headline:** NPC prices **float with demand** (since Jul 2024) and the **Blue Keycard is no longer sold at Outpost** — keycards moved to the Scrap 4 Sale vendor at Bandit Camp. Two big "but it used to be…" traps for a returning player.

## Dynamic (demand) pricing — read this first

Since July 2024, many NPC vendor prices **drift with how much players buy**. Heavily-bought items creep up; ignored items drift down. This hits the **Travelling Vendor** and **Floating City** shops hardest; the **Outpost / Bandit Camp core catalog** is much more stable (treat those as the reference prices). Example spread seen in 2026: a Jackhammer is **150 at Outpost**, ~92 from a Travelling Vendor on a good day, ~172 at a Floating City. So: **comparison-shop the floating vendors, but rely on Outpost/Bandit for predictable buys.**

## [[Outpost]] — the workshop hub

No-build safe zone with **3 recyclers** (safe-zone type — see [[Recycling]]), 2× WB1, research table, repair bench, drone marketplace, blackjack. Full price list on the [[Outpost]] page. Key buys:

| Category | Notable prices |
|---|---|
| **Tools** | Jackhammer **150** · Chainsaw **125** · Pickaxe 50 · Hatchet 40 |
| **Components** | Gears 125 · Spring 60 · Pipe 30 · Sheet Metal 30 · Blade 15 · Rope 30 **cloth** |
| **Resource exchange** | Stone ×1,000 = 50 · Wood ×1,000 = 20 · Frags ×250 = 25 · LGF ×20 = 10 |
| **Diesel Fuel** | **300 LGF** each — fuels [[Excavator and Quarries]] |
| **Defense** | Auto Turret 400 · SAM Site 500 · Flame Turret 250 · Shotgun Trap 150 |
| **Building** | Large Furnace 350 · Computer Station 300 · Small Oil Refinery 125 |

The wood/stone exchange machines make Outpost a **day-1 base-up shortcut**: recycle a road run's components for scrap, buy 1,000 stone for 50 scrap.

## [[Bandit Camp]] — vehicles, guns, keycards, gambling

Swamp-stilt safe zone with **2 recyclers**, the **casino**, **Air Wolf**, the black-market weapon vendor, and the keycard vendor. Full list on the [[Bandit Camp]] page. Highlights:

### Air Wolf (helicopters / aircraft)

| Vehicle | Price |
|---|---|
| Hot Air Balloon | 150 scrap |
| [[Minicopter]] | 750 scrap |
| Scrap Transport Helicopter | 1,250 scrap |
| [[Attack Helicopter]] | 2,250 scrap |

### Scrap 4 Sale — keycards (moved here from Outpost)

| Card | Price |
|---|---|
| [[Green Keycard]] | 15 scrap |
| [[Blue Keycard]] | 40 scrap |
| [[Red Keycard]] | 80 scrap |

(Older guides say red cards can't be bought — that changed with the 2026 reshuffle. Prices float.)

### Black-market weapons

LR-300 **500** · M39 **400** · M92 Pistol **250** · Spas-12 **250** · Night Vision Goggles **250** · Variable Zoom Scope **300** · F1 Grenade **8**.

### Casino

Big Wheel (house-edged, bet 1/3/5 only), 3 slots, 5 player-vs-player poker tables (the only +EV game if you're the better player), blackjack at Outpost / Floating Cities. The wheel/slots are **scrap sinks**; poker is a **scrap transfer**.

## Fishing Village — boats

Small NPC docks (no recycler combat-relevant utilities) selling watercraft:

| Boat | Price |
|---|---|
| Rowboat | 125 scrap |
| RHIB | 300 scrap |

Also sells fishing rods/bait and buys fish — fish gut into [[Scrap]] (~20% chance ×6), so passive fish-trap farms cash out here. See [[Scrap Runs]].

## Drone Marketplace (buy from any player vending machine)

Terminals at [[Outpost]] and [[Bandit Camp]]. Browse and buy from **any player-run vending machine on the map**; a delivery drone flies it to the marketplace pickup. This is how you buy from other players' shops without traveling to their base — and how you can sell map-wide if you run your own vending machines.

## Travelling Vendor

A mobile NPC truck that drives roads and stops at points of interest, selling a **rotating, demand-priced** stock — sometimes including **components, diesel, and the Jackhammer below Outpost price**. Worth flagging on the map and intercepting; stock and prices vary every spawn.

## Floating City casino / shops ([[Deep Sea]])

The Feb 2026 Naval/Deep Sea content added **Floating Cities with casinos** offshore. They carry vendor stock too, but at the **high end of the demand-pricing spread** — convenient when you're out at sea, not where you go for cheap staples.

## What to actually buy (returning-player priorities)

1. **Jackhammer (150)** — biggest single farming upgrade; buy before tech-treeing tools.
2. **Diesel (300 LGF)** for an [[Excavator and Quarries]] sulfur/HQM run when you have map control.
3. **Auto Turret (400)** / **SAM Site (500)** for base defense once you're established.
4. **Keycards at Bandit** only if you can't be bothered to puzzle — green/blue puzzles *award* cards + Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]] for free.
5. **Minicopter (750)** as soon as you can spare it — transport changes the whole game for a duo.

## Related

[[Outpost]] · [[Bandit Camp]] · [[Scrap]] · [[Components]] · [[Excavator and Quarries]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Minicopter]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Green Keycard]] · [[Blue Keycard]] · [[Red Keycard]] · [[Safe Zones]]

pages.title: Auto Turrets
pages.body:
# Auto Turrets

The backbone of automated base defense. A powered Auto Turret tracks and shoots targets on its own, day or night.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| HP | **1,000** |
| Power to run | **10 rW** (11 rW if using the signal outputs) |
| Range | **30 m** (10 foundations) |
| Ammo capacity | up to **1,536** 5.56 Rifle Ammo |
| Weapon | any gun you load + ammo (rifle, shotgun, etc.) |
| Outputs | Has Target / Low Ammo (â‰¤50) / No Ammo |
| Interference cap | **12 active turrets per 40 m** radius (13th won't power) |
| Craft | High Quality Metal + Gears + CCTV components, WB Level 2 |

## Modes

- **Peacekeeper** — only fires on players who are visibly aggressive (weapon out / shooting). Won't punish friendly randoms wandering by. Good for outpost-adjacent or public-facing bases.
- **Attack All / Hostile** — fires on anyone not authorized. Required if you want to **remote-control** the turret yourself. The standard for a defended main base.

**Authorization:** add yourself and teammates to the turret's authorized list (hold-E menu) or it'll shoot you. Authorize the whole team.

## Loadout

- Load a **weapon + ammo** into the turret's inventory. A turret is only as good as its gun — an AK or [[M249]] turret shreds; a turret with a Nailgun is a speed bump.
- **5.56 rifle ammo** is standard; up to 1,536 rounds.
- High-velocity / incendiary ammo changes behavior (incendiary applies burn, HV improves long-range hit).

## Placement meta

- **Mount on walls/ceilings above eye level** so raiders can't easily melee or shoot the turret base; force them to expose themselves to shoot up at it.
- **Interference:** never pack more than **12 turrets inside 40 m** — the 13th and beyond refuse to power and just spark. Spread a large wall across the radius limit or stagger heights.
- **Behind shooting-floor "turret nests"** (a turret peeking through a half-wall gap) survive longer than exposed ones.
- **Power the array from a [[Large Rechargeable Battery]]** so they stay armed when solar/wind drops — see [[Electrical Circuits]] circuit #2.

## Signal outputs (advanced)

Wiring the **Has Target** output (needs 11 rW total) lets you trigger other things when the turret acquires a target — e.g. fire a **Smart Alarm**, drop a [[Garage Door]], or light a flasher. **Low Ammo** (â‰¤50 rounds) and **No Ammo** outputs can warn you to resupply via the Rust+ app.

## Counters (how raiders beat them)

- **Soft-side raiding** the wall the turret can't cover.
- **Building cover** (twig walls / sheet metal) to advance under fire.
- **Explosives** thrown over walls (turrets can't shoot the floor directly below them — there's a dead zone).
- High ground / longer-range guns out to the 30 m edge.
- See [[Raiding]] and [[PvP]] for full counter-play.

## Related

- [[Electrical Components]] · [[Electrical Circuits]] · [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] · [[SAM Site]] · [[Traps]] · [[Raiding]]

pages.title: Electrical Circuits
pages.body:
# Electrical Circuits

Step-by-step recipes for the circuits a solo/duo/trio actually builds. Test any of these in the free simulator at [[rustrician.io]] before committing HQM. Remember the **1 rW pass-through loss** on nearly every component (see [[Electricity Basics]]).

---

## 1. Base power backbone (build this first)

The foundation every other circuit plugs into.

1. **Large Solar Panel** (roof, facing the sun) → input A of a **[[Root Combiner]]**.
2. **Wind Turbine** (highest open-air point) → input B of the Root Combiner.
3. Root Combiner output → **[[Large Rechargeable Battery]]** input.
4. Battery **Power Out** → a **[[Splitter]]** (3 outputs) or **[[Electrical Branch]]** chain.
5. From the splitter, run lines to your turrets, doors, lights, and [[Industrial]] gear.

Bury the battery and combiner deep. This gives you 24/7 power with no single point of failure.

---

## 2. Auto-turret array with battery backup + timer

Keeps turrets armed even when sources fail, and (optional timer leg) lets you arm the wall only on a schedule.

**Component list (8-turret wall):**
- 1x [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] (100 rW output, ~24,000 rWm capacity)
- 1x [[Root Combiner]] + your sources (Large Solar + Wind Turbine)
- Enough [[Splitter]]s / [[Electrical Branch]]es to fan out 8 lines (each Splitter = 3 outputs; chain them)
- 8x [[Auto Turret]]
- 1x Smart Switch (master kill, Rust+ controllable, costs 1 rW)
- *(optional)* 1x Timer for scheduled arming

**Wiring order:**
1. **Sources -> Root Combiner -> Large Battery** input (from circuit #1). Battery is your backup buffer.
2. Battery **Power Out (100 rW) -> Smart Switch** input. The Smart Switch is your single master kill / Rust+ remote arm.
3. Smart Switch output -> first **[[Splitter]]** (splits the line into 3 equal legs). Chain a second/third Splitter off one leg to reach all 8 lines, or use **Electrical Branches** set to 10 rW each for exact per-turret budgeting.
4. Each final leg -> one **[[Auto Turret]]** Power In. **A turret draws exactly 10 rW** (official Facepunch figure). Feed **11 rW** if you also wire the turret's **Has Target / Low Ammo / No Ammo** output ports into a circuit.
5. *(optional timer leg)* Insert a **Timer** between the Smart Switch and the splitter, looped to itself, if you want the wall to arm only during set windows. Most solos skip this and leave turrets always-on.

**Power budget:** 8 turrets x 10 rW = **80 rW**, +1 rW Smart Switch = **81 rW** continuous, inside the battery's 100 rW output. A full [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] (24,000 rWm) holds ~5 hours of an 80 rW draw with zero generation — your solar/wind should cover daytime and the battery bridges the night.

**Scaling:** A single Large Battery (100 rW out) comfortably runs **~9 turrets** (90 rW) before you hit its output ceiling. Beyond that, run a second battery on its own source/combiner — do **not** daisy-chain two batteries off one line expecting to sum outputs.

---

## 3. Smart raid alarm + Rust+ notification

Get a phone push the moment someone uninvited is at your base.

**Component list:**
- 1x [[HBHF Sensor]] (**1 rW**) — detects players by heartbeat within ~11 m
- 1x **Smart Alarm** (**1 rW**; passes input power minus 1)
- power from your [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] line

**Wiring order:**
1. Run a battery line (>=2 rW available) to the **[[HBHF Sensor]]** Power In. In its menu set **Exclude Authorized = ON, Include Others = ON** so it ignores you and TC-authed teammates and only fires on strangers.
2. HBHF **passthrough output** -> **Smart Alarm** Power In. The HBHF only outputs power equal to the number of unauthorized players it senses, so the alarm only powers up when an enemy is present.
3. The **Smart Alarm** pushes a notification to the **Rust+ companion app** on your phone and sounds an audible siren. Name the alarm in its menu (e.g. "Loot Room") so the phone alert is readable.
4. Total idle draw is just the HBHF's 1 rW (alarm stays dark until tripped).

**Multi-room version:** wire several HBHF sensors' outputs into a chain of **OR Switches** (0 rW each) so any one sensor tripping fires a single Smart Alarm. Keep one alarm per logical zone if you want to know *which* room was breached from the Rust+ alert name.

---

## 4. Garage-door bunker auto-trigger (with timer)

Classic "honeycomb bunker" — a hidden [[Garage Door]] that only opens when you stand on a secret spot, then auto-closes behind you.

**Component list:**
- 1x **Pressure Pad** (**1 rW**; pulses ~1 rW briefly when stood on — detects players *and* vehicles, works through half-height floors) **or** 1x [[HBHF Sensor]] (1 rW) if you want a no-visible-trigger version
- 1x **[[Door Controller]]** (**1 rW**) attached to the bunker [[Garage Door]]
- 1x **Memory Cell** (latches the open state)
- 1x **Timer** (set 3–5 s; holds the door open long enough to pass)
- power from your battery line

**Wiring order (timer auto-close):**
1. **Pressure Pad** output -> **Memory Cell** SET input. Stepping on the pad latches "open."
2. **Memory Cell** output -> **[[Door Controller]]** Power In. While latched, the Door Controller (1 rW) holds the [[Garage Door]] open.
3. **Memory Cell** output also -> **Timer** input; **Timer** output (after its 3–5 s delay) -> Memory Cell **RESET**. This auto-closes the door a few seconds after you trigger it, even if you've already walked off the pad.
4. Place the pad on the *inside* of the honeycomb cell so raiders standing outside can never trip it. With an [[HBHF Sensor]] version (Exclude Authorized ON), only you/teammates can open it at all.

**Simpler always-while-pressed version:** skip the Memory Cell and Timer — wire **Pressure Pad -> Door Controller** directly. The door is open only while you physically stand on the pad and shuts the instant you step off. Cheaper, but you can't pass through fast.

---

## 4b. Auto-door (sensor-triggered interior door)

A normal interior door that opens as you approach and closes behind you — convenience automation for a sorting room or shooting-floor entry (not a security door — raiders can walk through it too unless gated by an HBHF Exclude-Authorized check).

**Component list:** 1x [[HBHF Sensor]] (1 rW, set **Include Others OFF / Exclude Authorized OFF** if you want it to open for anyone, or Exclude-Authorized-style filtering for team-only) -> 1x **[[Door Controller]]** (1 rW) on the door.

**Wiring order:**
1. **[[HBHF Sensor]]** output -> **[[Door Controller]]** Power In.
2. Door Controller opens the door while the sensor reads a body; it closes a moment after you leave the ~11 m sensor range.
