3. Add a **Timer** (~2–3 s) between sensor and controller's reset path if the door slams too quickly behind you.

Total draw ~2 rW. Use a **Pressure Pad** instead of the HBHF for a cheaper "open while standing here" mat in front of the door.

---

## 5. Day/night automatic lights (solar latch)

Lights that turn **on at night** and off by day — no battery waste in daylight.

**Component list:** 1x Large Solar Panel (control signal) + 1x **Blocker** + your **Ceiling Lights** (**2 rW each**) on the battery line.

**Wiring order:**
1. **Large Solar Panel** -> the **Blocker's** side (control/"block") input.
2. Battery Power Out -> the Blocker's **main** input -> your **Ceiling Lights** (budget 2 rW per Ceiling Light).
3. Logic: while the sun is up the solar panel powers the Blocker, which **blocks** the line -> lights off. At night solar drops to 0, the Blocker releases -> lights turn on.
4. The Blocker (acting as a NOT gate) inverts the solar signal for you automatically. Five ceiling lights = 10 rW only at night.

---

## 6. Auto-on turrets only when enemies present (power saver)

Don't drain the battery 24/7 — only arm turrets when someone trips a sensor.

1. **[[HBHF Sensor]]** (Exclude Authorized) → **Memory Cell** SET input.
2. Memory Cell Output → turret Power In.
3. Wire a **Timer** (~30s) from the Memory Cell output back to its **RESET** input so turrets disarm 30s after the last detection.
4. Net effect: turrets sit dark (saving power) until an enemy is sensed, snap on, and time back off. Trade-off: a half-second arm delay — most solos keep turrets always-on instead and use this for [[Traps|trap]] banks.

---

## 7. Auto-furnace ignition (smelting without electric furnaces)

If you don't have [[Industrial]] electric furnaces, automate ignition of regular furnaces.

1. **Igniter** placed at the furnace mouth.
2. **Switch** or **Timer** → Igniter (1 rW; 2 rW with flame).
3. Flip the switch to light the furnace remotely, or use a Timer for a fixed burn. The Igniter wears out (~16–17 min) — replace periodically.
4. The full [[Industrial]] electric-furnace setup is strictly better if you have the parts.

---

## 8. Tesla-coil trap hallway

A passive raid deterrent in a loot-room approach (see [[Traps]]).

1. **[[HBHF Sensor]]** (Exclude Authorized) in the hallway → **Tesla Coil** Power In.
2. Feed the coil **35 rW** for max damage (it deals **1 HP/sec per rW**, capped at 35).
3. Coil only zaps within ~3.5 m, so line a 1-tile choke with several.
4. Power from a [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] — 35 rW per coil adds up fast.

---

## 9. Water pump + sprinkler farm (auto-watering)

Keep an indoor [[Farming|planter]] garden watered hands-free by lifting water from a source up to your grow room. See [[Water Systems]] for the plumbing side.

**Component list:**
- 1x **Electric Water Pump** (**5 rW**; has 3 sockets: 1 power, 2 for remote on/off) sitting in/at your water source
- water hose from the pump up to the grow room
- up to **4x Sprinkler** per pump (each **1 rW**, each draws 2 mL/s from the line and sprays 3 mL/s)
- power from your [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] line
- *(optional)* 1x Timer to pulse the system instead of running it 24/7

**Wiring + plumbing order:**
1. Place the **Water Pump** at/below your water source (ocean, river, or a fed [[Water Catcher]] / Water Barrel). A powered pump is required whenever the sprinklers sit **higher** than the source.
2. Power the pump's main socket with **5 rW** from the battery line. Collection rate is ~8.5 mL/s, output up to 12 mL/s.
3. Run a **water hose** from the pump output up to the grow room and into your **Sprinklers** (up to 4 per pump; 4 x 2 mL/s = 8 mL/s draw, within the pump's output).
4. Power each **Sprinkler** with **1 rW**. They spray the planters below them.
5. *(optional)* Insert a **Timer** on the pump's power leg so it runs in bursts (e.g. 30 s on every few minutes) rather than continuously — planters only need topping up, so this saves power and water.

**Power budget:** pump 5 rW + four sprinklers 4 rW = **9 rW**. Modest enough to share the turret battery line. For a bigger farm, add a second pump rather than overloading one (the 12 mL/s output caps how many sprinklers stay fed).

---

## Practice in the simulator

[[rustrician.io]] lets you drag-and-drop every component and watch power flow live — build and debug a circuit there for free before spending HQM in-game. It uses the **Test Generator** (100 rW infinite) as its source; swap it mentally for your real battery.

## Related

- [[Electrical Components]] · [[Auto Turrets]] · [[Traps]] · [[Water Systems]] · [[Industrial]]

pages.title: Electrical Components
pages.body:
# Electrical Components

The full parts list. Power figures verified against [[rustrician.io]] and rusthelp. Remember the universal rule: most components draw **1 rW** and pass through **`input âˆ’ 1`** rW (exceptions noted).

## Batteries (storage)

| Battery | Capacity (rWm) | Max Output (rW) | Efficiency | Craft | WB |
|---------|---------------|-----------------|-----------|-------|----|
| [[Small Rechargeable Battery]] | 150 | 10 | 80% | 5 HQM | 1 |
| [[Medium Rechargeable Battery]] | 9,000 | 50 | 80% | 5 HQM + 1 Tech Trash | 2 |
| [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] | 24,000 | 100 | 80% | 50 HQM | 2 |

- **80% input efficiency** — 20% of charging power is lost. Size sources ~25% over your draw.
- Needs **â‰¥5 seconds** of stored charge to discharge.
- Bidirectional (charge + supply simultaneously). Output capped at the rated max regardless of charge level.
- Large battery at 100 rW max output runs for **240 minutes** (4 hours) from full.

## Distribution

### Root Combiner
Sums **two inputs → one output** with no backflow. The clean way to merge two power sources (solar + wind) or source + battery. Craft: 2 HQM (WB1).

### Splitter
**One input → three outputs**, dividing power **evenly** across however many outputs are connected. 6 rW into a splitter with 3 outputs = 2 rW each. Craft: 1 HQM (WB1).

### Electrical Branch
**One input → two outputs: "Power Out" and "Branch Out."** You set a value on the Branch Out; it pulls exactly that much off the line, and the rest continues out Power Out. Subtle gotcha: an Electrical Branch set to N registers **N Active Usage on the battery but actually consumes N+1** (the extra 1 rW is its operating cost). Use it when you want a *fixed* amount to one device and the remainder elsewhere — more precise than a Splitter. Craft: 1 HQM (WB1).

## Switches & logic

| Component | Behavior | Power |
|-----------|----------|-------|
| **Switch** | Manual on/off, toggled by hand | passes `input âˆ’ 0`, free when off |
| **Smart Switch** | Toggle remotely from the **Rust+ companion app**; also has a wire input | 1 rW |
| **AND Switch** | Passes power only when **both** inputs are powered. Outputs the larger input. | **0 rW** (the exception) |
| **OR Switch** | Passes power if **either** input is powered; outputs the larger input âˆ’ 1 | 1 rW |
| **XOR Switch** | Passes power only when **exactly one** input is powered (blocks if both) | 1 rW |
| **RAND Switch** | 50% chance to pass/block each time it's set | 1 rW |
| **Blocker** | A NOT gate — **blocks** the main line whenever its side input receives a signal. Hides downstream Active Usage from the battery while blocking. | 1 rW |
| **Memory Cell** | Flip-flop with SET / RESET / TOGGLE inputs. SET routes to Output; RESET routes to Inverted Output; the state **latches** until changed. The core of every "stay-on-until-reset" circuit. | output = `input âˆ’ 1` |
| **Timer** | Passes power for a configured duration (0.25s up to ~2 weeks), then cuts off. Re-trigger on a new pulse. | 1 rW, output `input âˆ’ 1` |
| **Counter** | Counts up/down pulses on side inputs; passes power when count meets the target (1–100). Also doubles as a **digital readout** for storage monitors / numbers. | output `input âˆ’ 1` |

## Sensors & triggers

| Component | Range | Output | Power | Notes |
|-----------|-------|--------|-------|-------|
| **HBHF Sensor** | ~11 m (3.5 foundations) | **1 rW per person** detected | 1 rW | "Heartbeat Human Friend/Foe." Toggle Include/Exclude Authorized vs Others. The standard turret/alarm trigger. |
| **Laser Detector** | 4.5 m (1.5 foundations) | `input âˆ’ 1` when broken | 1 rW | Tripwire-style; pairs with doors/traps. |
| **Pressure Pad** | floor contact | pulses 1 rW then `input` | 1 rW | Place on floors/foundations only. Good for [[Garage Door]] bunker triggers. |
| **Storage Monitor** | — | reports box contents to Rust+ app | — | Read-only; also outputs a signal when a box has items. |
| **Tin Can Alarm** | tripwire | — | — | New May 2026 throwable rig — non-electric but pairs with raid-alarm logic. |
| **Seismic Sensor** | base-wide | signal on nearby explosions | — | New May 2026 raid-detection sensor. |

## RF (wireless)

- **RF Broadcaster** — transmits on a set frequency (1–9999 MHz) while powered. 1 rW.
- **RF Receiver** — outputs power when a matching-frequency broadcaster is on. 1 rW. Enables **wireless circuits** (e.g. roof button → base door, no wire run).
- **RF Transmitter / Detonator** — handheld; detonates RF-fused explosives (timed C4) on its frequency. Used in [[Raiding]].

## Utility / output devices

| Device | Power | Effect |
|--------|-------|--------|
| **Door Controller** | 1 rW | Opens/closes a wired door on signal. Works on single & double doors, [[Garage Door]]s, window shutters, gates. The bunker-base staple. |
| **Electrical Heater** | 3 rW | Heat source (~4 m sphere). Dries wet players; regulates crop temperature in greenhouses. |
| **Igniter** | 1 rW (2 rW with flame visual) | Ignites furnaces, fireplaces, fireworks, explosives. Wears out (~16–17 min lifespan). Used in auto-furnace and trap-burn circuits. |
| **Audio Alarm / Smart Alarm** | 1 rW | Audible siren (~42 m) and/or push notification to the **Rust+ app** — the standard raid alarm. |
| **Fogger-3000** | 1 rW | Fog machine; burns LGF (1/min active, 10/min on motion mode). Concealment / ambush. |
| **Snow Machine** | 1 rW | Snow patch (~3.5-foundation radius); burns LGF 1/min. |
| **Flasher Light / Siren Light / Strobe** | ~1 rW | Visual indicators — wire to an HBHF or alarm for a "someone's here" light. |
| **Simple Light / Ceiling Light / Search Light** | 1 rW | Base lighting; Search Light sweeps and is the brightest. |

## Related

- [[Electricity Basics]] — power sources & the 1 rW rule
- [[Electrical Circuits]] — these parts assembled into working circuits
- [[Auto Turrets]] · [[Traps]] · [[Industrial]] · [[Water Systems]]

pages.title: Electricity
pages.body:
# Electricity

Rust's electricity system powers turrets, traps, doors, lights, automated farms, and the entire [[Industrial]] crafting/sorting layer. Power is measured in **rW (Rust Watts)** for flow and **rWm (Rust Watt-minutes)** for stored battery charge. You wire components with the **Wire Tool** (craft: 1 Scrap, or buy at [[Outpost]]); industrial uses the separate **Pipe Tool** and water uses the **Hose Tool**.

This folder is the full electrical + industrial reference for solo/duo/trio bases.

## Pages

- [[Electricity Basics]] — how power flows, the Wire Tool, power sources (solar, wind, generators), root combiner, base wiring rules
- [[Electrical Components]] — every logic/control component: branch, splitter, batteries, switches, AND/OR/XOR, memory cell, blocker, timer, counter, sensors, RF, door controller
- [[Electrical Circuits]] — step-by-step recipes for the 8 most useful circuits (turret array w/ battery backup, smart alarm, garage-door bunker trigger, auto-lights, day/night solar latch)
- [[Auto Turrets]] — turret behavior, power, ammo, interference cap, peacekeeper vs attack, placement meta
- [[Traps]] — shotgun trap, flame turret, tesla coil, SAM site, landmines, igniter
- [[Industrial]] — conveyors, pipes, storage adaptors, splitters/combiners, industrial crafter, electric furnace, auto-sort + auto-smelt builds
- [[Water Systems]] — water catchers, pumps, sprinklers, purifiers for automated farming

## The one rule that confuses everyone

**Almost every component consumes 1 rW just to function, and passes through `input âˆ’ 1` rW.** Chain ten components in a line and you've lost ~10 rW before the last one even does its job. The exceptions: the **AND Switch** (0 rW), and power *sources* / batteries. Always budget for the loss when sizing a battery.

## Quick power-source cheat sheet

| Source | Output | Caveat |
|--------|--------|--------|
| [[Large Solar Panel]] | up to **20 rW** | Daytime only (~11AM–9PM), needs sun line-of-sight |
| Wind Turbine | **0–150 rW** (avg ~93 at 6th-floor height) | Fluctuates constantly; needs height + open air; 15m no-build zone |
| Small Generator | **40 rW** steady | Burns ~1 Low Grade Fuel / 45s |
| Test Generator | **100 rW** infinite | Creative/build-server only, not survival-craftable |

Pair a solar panel + elevated wind turbine into a [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] via a [[Root Combiner]] — their failure modes (night / no wind) don't overlap, giving 24/7 uptime.

## Related

- [[Outpost]] and [[Bandit Camp]] sell most components
- [[Tech Tree]] / research unlocks the electrical tier
- See [[Raiding]] and [[PvP]] for how raiders defeat turret/trap setups

pages.title: Electricity Basics
pages.body:
# Electricity Basics

Everything you need to start wiring a base: the tool, the units, the power sources, and the rules that govern how electricity flows.

## The Wire Tool

- **Craft:** 1 Scrap at any [[Workbench]] (or buy at [[Outpost]]). Default research tier 0 — available immediately.
- Equip it, then **left-click an output slot** on one component and **left-click an input slot** on another to draw a wire. Hold the click and add waypoints to route the wire cleanly.
- **Right-click** while holding the tool to delete a wire.
- Wire color is cosmetic only — set it in the tool's radial for organization.
- Wires can pass through walls/foundations freely (unlike the [[Industrial]] Pipe Tool).

> Companions: the **Hose Tool** wires [[Water Systems]]; the **Pipe Tool** wires [[Industrial]] containers. Same click-to-connect feel, different networks.

## Units

| Unit | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **rW** (Rust Watt) | Instantaneous power flow. A solar panel outputs 20 rW; a turret draws 10 rW. |
| **rWm** (Rust Watt-minute) | Stored energy in a battery. A [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] holds 24,000 rWm = 100 rW for 240 min. |

**Active Usage** is the live drain registered on a battery from everything currently powered downstream. If your Active Usage exceeds what your sources produce, the battery drains; if it's lower, the battery charges (at 80% efficiency).

## Power sources

### Large Solar Panel
- **Output: up to 20 rW**, scaling with the sun's intensity and the angle of light hitting the panel face.
- **Daytime only** — begins generating ~11 AM in-game, peaks at noon, falls to 0 by ~9 PM. Useless overnight without a battery buffer.
- **Craft:** 5 High Quality Metal + 1 Tech Trash, 15s at Workbench Level 1. **Buy at [[Outpost]] for 75 Scrap.** Drops from crates (~1.55%).
- Place facing south (in the northern map area) with clear line of sight to the horizon; elevation helps avoid shadows.
- One panel makes ~940–1,075 rWm across a full day depending on season.

### Wind Turbine
- **Output: 0–150 rW**, fluctuating constantly with simulated wind. Higher placement = more frequent peaks. **Average ~93 rW at 6th-floor height.**
- Large deployable with a **15-meter restricted build radius** around it — you can't place foundations too close, so plan roof/tower space.
- Needs **open air**: nearby cliffs, mountains, or tall builds choke output.
- More raidable than solar (exposed on the roof) but far higher ceiling. The solo/duo workhorse when you need 24/7 turret power.

### Small Generator
- **Output: 40 rW steady** while fueled.
- Burns **~1 Low Grade Fuel every 45 seconds** (~80 LGF/hour). Good for short bursts (raids, base defense windows) but expensive to run 24/7.
- No daylight/wind dependency — fully reliable as long as it has fuel.

### Test Generator
- **100 rW, infinite, free** — but only exists on **creative/build servers**. You cannot craft it in survival. Mentioned only so you don't confuse it with the Small Generator when copying circuit diagrams from [[rustrician.io]].

## Batteries — the buffer layer

See [[Electrical Components]] for the full battery table. Key facts:

- **All batteries charge at 80% efficiency** — 20% of incoming power is lost as heat. Size your sources ~25% above your draw to keep a battery topped.
- **Minimum 5 seconds of charge** before a battery can discharge.
- Batteries are **bidirectional**: they can take charge and supply load at the same time.
- A battery's **Power Out** caps at its rated max (10 / 50 / 100 rW) no matter how full it is.

| Battery | Capacity | Max Output | Craft | WB |
|---------|----------|-----------|-------|----|
| [[Small Rechargeable Battery]] | 150 rWm | 10 rW | 5 HQM | 1 |
| [[Medium Rechargeable Battery]] | 9,000 rWm | 50 rW | 5 HQM + 1 Tech Trash | 2 |
| [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] | 24,000 rWm | 100 rW | 50 HQM | 2 |

## The Root Combiner

You **cannot wire two power sources into the same input** — and you shouldn't backfeed power between sources. The **Root Combiner** solves both: it has two inputs and one output, summing two sources (e.g. solar + wind, or battery + generator) into one clean line with no backflow.

- **Craft:** 2 HQM at Workbench Level 1.
- Standard layout: `Solar + Wind → Root Combiner → Large Battery → (everything else)`.

## The 1 rW pass-through rule

This is the single most important wiring fact in Rust:

> **Nearly every component costs 1 rW to operate and outputs `input âˆ’ 1` rW on its main pass-through.**

So a [[Door Controller]] fed 10 rW passes 9 rW onward. Chain a Splitter → Branch → Timer → Door Controller and you've burned ~4 rW before the door even opens. **Budget the loss.** The only common exception is the **AND Switch** at 0 rW.

## Recommended starter wiring

1. **Solar panel** (roof) + **wind turbine** (tower) → **Root Combiner**.
2. Root Combiner → **Large Rechargeable Battery** input.
3. Battery **Power Out** → a [[Splitter]] or [[Electrical Branch]] to fan out to your loads ([[Auto Turrets]], lights, [[Door Controller]]s).
4. Keep batteries and the wiring hub deep inside your base — exposed batteries are a soft raid target.

## Related

- [[Electrical Components]] — the parts list
- [[Electrical Circuits]] — wiring recipes
- [[Industrial]] — the item-automation layer that runs on this power

pages.title: Industrial
pages.body:
# Industrial

The base-automation layer (added Jan 2023, "Industrial Update"). It moves items between containers and crafts/smelts automatically. It runs *alongside* [[Electricity Basics|electricity]] — most industrial parts need a small power feed (1 rW) plus the **Pipe Tool** to connect.

## The toolkit

| Component | Power | What it does |
|-----------|-------|--------------|
| **Pipe Tool** | — | Connects industrial entities (like the Wire Tool but for items). Cannot pass through building blocks or vending machines; **can** pass through deployables like doors. |
| **Storage Adaptor** | none | Snap onto any storage box / furnace / etc. to make it pipe-connectable. **1–4 adaptors per container** depending on type. |
| **Industrial Conveyor** | **1 rW** | The workhorse — moves & **filters** items between containers on a timer. |
| **Industrial Splitter** | passive | One input → up to **3 outputs**, dividing the item flow. |
| **Industrial Combiner** | passive | Up to **3 inputs → 1 output**, merging containers. |
| **Industrial Crafter** | **1 rW** | Auto-crafts an item from a loaded blueprint, pulling mats from a connected box. Must attach to the right [[Workbench]] (max **2 crafters per bench**). |
| **Electric Furnace** | **3 rW** | Smelts ore with power instead of wood; **~66% faster than a Small Furnace**; produces **no charcoal**. Takes up to **4 Storage Adaptors**. |

## The Industrial Conveyor in detail

This is the piece that actually does the sorting/moving.

- **The 5-second rule:** from power-on to first transfer is **5 seconds**, and each transfer after is every **5 seconds**.
- **Throughput:** up to **60 items/stack from 12 stacks per 5s** (stackables move in 60s; unstackables move 12 at a time).
- **Three outputs:** the **passthrough** (consumes the 1 rW), **Filter Pass** (free), **Filter Fail** (free).
- **Filters** (up to 12 items): set a per-item **MIN / MAX / BUFFER** and a mode of **ANY ITEM / REQUIRE ALL / EXCLUDE LISTED**:
  - **MAX** — stop moving an item once the destination hits the set count (cap a box at e.g. 1,000 stone).
  - **MIN** — only move the *surplus* above a kept minimum (always leave 100 LGF behind).
  - **BUFFER** — move in fixed chunks.
- **Limits:** max **32 storage adaptors per side**, and an **industrial max depth of 32 components** in a chain.

## Build 1 — auto-sorting conveyor (loot room, step by step)

Dump everything into one box; it sorts itself into labeled boxes every 5 seconds.

**Component list (sorts into 6 boxes):**
- 1x **dump box** (Large Wood/Metal Box) — your input
- 6x destination boxes (stone, metal frags, sulfur, HQM, components, scrap, etc.)
- **Storage Adaptors** — 1 on the dump box output, 1 on each destination box (Large Box accepts up to 4 if you need more pipes)
- 6x **Industrial Conveyor** (1 rW each) **or** 2x conveyor + **Industrial Splitters** to fan out
- **Pipe Tool** + power from your [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] line

**Build order:**
1. Snap a **Storage Adaptor** onto the dump box and onto each destination box.
2. Place an **Industrial Conveyor** between the dump box and each destination box. (To save conveyors: one conveyor -> an **Industrial Splitter** can fan one filtered stream to 3 boxes, but a conveyor-per-item gives cleaner filtering.)
3. On each conveyor's **filter**, add the **one item type** that box should receive, mode **ANY ITEM**, and set a **MAX** equal to the box cap (e.g. cap a stone box at the stack count you want). Up to 12 filter items per conveyor.
4. Power each conveyor with **1 rW** from your battery line — 6 conveyors = **6 rW**.
5. **Pipe Tool** every link. The conveyor moves up to **60 items/stack across 12 stacks per 5-second tick** (unstackables: 12 at a time). First transfer is 5 s after power-on, then every 5 s. Drop loot in the dump box and it auto-routes.

**Tip:** put one final "overflow" conveyor with mode **EXCLUDE LISTED** (everything you already sort) pointing to a junk box, so unexpected items never clog the dump box.

## Build 2 — auto-smelting furnace bank (step by step)

Ore in one box -> smelted ingots out another, hands-free.

**Component list (3 ore types):**
- 1x **ore box** (input) with Storage Adaptor
- 3x **Electric Furnace** (3 rW each, up to 4 Storage Adaptors each) — one per ore type
- 1x **ingot output box** with Storage Adaptor
- conveyors: at minimum 1 in (ore->furnaces) + 1 out (furnaces->ingot box); cleaner is 1 in + 1 out per furnace
- **Pipe Tool** + battery line

**Build order:**
1. **Ore box** (Storage Adaptor) -> **Industrial Conveyor** -> each **Electric Furnace** input slot. Filter the in-conveyor(s) to the ore types (metal ore, sulfur ore, HQM ore) so each ore lands in its own furnace. Use an **Industrial Splitter** to fan one ore stream if needed.
2. Power each **Electric Furnace with 3 rW** (no wood needed; ~66% faster than a Small Furnace; makes **no charcoal**). Three furnaces = **9 rW** for the furnaces.
3. **Electric Furnace output** (Storage Adaptor) -> **Industrial Conveyor** -> your **ingot storage box**. Set the out-conveyor filter to **only** move the finished ingot (metal fragments / sulfur / HQM), so unsmelted ore stays in the furnace until it cooks.
4. Net result: dump raw ore, walk away, collect ingots. No Igniter needed — electric furnaces self-heat from power.

**Power budget:** 3 furnaces (9 rW) + ~4 conveyors (4 rW) = **~13 rW** continuous. Note electric furnaces give **no charcoal**, so keep a couple of wood furnaces or an Igniter setup ([[Electrical Circuits]] #7) if you still want charcoal for gunpowder.

## Build 3 — auto-crafter (e.g. auto-ammo, auto-gunpowder)

**Component list:** 1x **Industrial Crafter** (1 rW; **max 2 per [[Workbench]]**) + material box + finished-goods box + 2 conveyors + Pipe Tool + battery line.

**Build order:**
1. Attach the **Industrial Crafter** to the correct **[[Workbench]]** (gunpowder/ammo = WB Level 1+). You can mount up to 2 crafters per bench.
2. **Material box** (e.g. sulfur + charcoal for gunpowder) -> **Industrial Conveyor** (1 rW) -> **Crafter input**.
3. Load the **blueprint** (e.g. Gunpowder) into the crafter's blueprint slot.
4. **Crafter output** -> **Industrial Conveyor** -> finished-goods box.
5. Power the crafter (**1 rW**). It crafts continuously as long as mats are supplied — turn raw sulfur/charcoal into a stockpile of gunpowder, then chain a second crafter (gunpowder + metal frags) into rifle/pistol ammo automatically.

**Power budget:** crafter 1 rW + 2 conveyors 2 rW = **3 rW** per craft line.

## Naval / boat industrial (Feb–Mar 2026)

Since March 2026, the new player-built **modular ships** ([[Naval Update]]) support **electricity and industrial IO** on the hull — you can run conveyors, crafters, and electrical components on a moving ship. Niche for solos but relevant for water bases.

## Related

- [[Electricity Basics]] (powers all this) · [[Electrical Components]] · [[Water Systems]] · [[Workbench]] · [[Economy]] (recyclers + auto-recycle setups)

pages.title: Large Rechargeable Battery
pages.body:
# Large Rechargeable Battery

The endgame power buffer — the heart of any base running a full [[Auto Turrets|turret]] wall, [[SAM Site]], or heavy [[Industrial]] automation.

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Capacity | **24,000 rWm** |
| Max Output | **100 rW** |
| Input efficiency | 80% (20% loss) |
| Runtime at max | 240 min (4 hrs) from full |
| Min charge to discharge | 5 seconds |
| Craft | **50 HQM**, WB Level 2 |
| HP | 100 |

## Use

100 rW supports ~10 [[Auto Turrets]] (10 rW each) or a turret cluster plus an [[Industrial]] auto-furnace farm. 24,000 rWm is hours of reserve — survives a full night plus dead-wind stretches.

### Charge math
- Charging is 80% efficient: to net +X rW into the battery you must feed `X Ã· 0.8` in.
- To merely **hold** charge against an Active Usage of A, your sources must produce `A Ã· 0.8`.
- Trickle reference: 1 rW of net input takes **~34 real-world days** to fill an empty Large battery — so undersized sources will never keep up with a turret wall. Pair with a properly elevated wind turbine.

## Standard wiring

`Solar Panel + Wind Turbine → [[Root Combiner]] → Large Battery → Splitter → turrets / doors / lights`

Keep it buried deep — a raided Large battery kills your whole defense grid.

## Related

- [[Electrical Components]] · [[Electricity Basics]] · [[Auto Turrets]] · [[SAM Site]] · [[Industrial]]

pages.title: Medium Rechargeable Battery
pages.body:
# Medium Rechargeable Battery

The mid-tier buffer — the sweet spot for solo/duo bases running a couple of turrets plus utility circuits.

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Capacity | **9,000 rWm** |
| Max Output | **50 rW** |
| Input efficiency | 80% (20% loss) |
| Runtime at max | 180 min (3 hrs) from full |
| Min charge to discharge | 5 seconds |
| Craft | **5 HQM + 1 Tech Trash**, WB Level 2 (25s) |
| HP | 100 |

## Use

50 rW comfortably runs **3–4 [[Auto Turrets]]** with signal outputs, or a turret + [[Industrial]] electric furnaces + [[Door Controller]]s. 9,000 rWm of storage rides out a night of no solar / dead wind without a problem.

Can be **wired in series** with other batteries to pool capacity. For most solo/duo defensive bases this is the battery to build first — a Large is overkill until you're running a turret wall.

## Related

- [[Electrical Components]] · [[Electricity Basics]] · [[Small Rechargeable Battery]] · [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] · [[Auto Turrets]]

pages.title: Small Rechargeable Battery
pages.body:
# Small Rechargeable Battery

The entry-level power buffer. Cheap enough to put behind every starter solar panel.

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Capacity | **150 rWm** |
| Max Output | **10 rW** |
| Input efficiency | 80% (20% loss) |
| Runtime at max | ~15 min from full |
| Min charge to discharge | 5 seconds |
| Craft | **5 High Quality Metal**, WB Level 1 |
| HP | 100 |

## Use

10 rW output is exactly enough for **one [[Auto Turret]]** (10 rW) or a few [[Door Controller]]s / lights — but with no headroom for the turret's signal outputs (which need 11 rW). For a real turret defense you want the [[Medium Rechargeable Battery]] or [[Large Rechargeable Battery]].

Best role: smoothing a single solar panel for a light, [[Door Controller]], or a low-draw sensor circuit overnight. 150 rWm is tiny — it buffers minutes, not hours.

## Related

- [[Electrical Components]] · [[Electricity Basics]] · [[Medium Rechargeable Battery]] · [[Large Rechargeable Battery]]

pages.title: Traps
pages.body:
# Traps

Passive and triggered base-defense devices. Most pair with an [[HBHF Sensor]] or [[Pressure Pad]] trigger (see [[Electrical Circuits]]). Stats verified against [[rustrician.io]] and rusthelp.

## Shotgun Trap

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| HP | **300** |
| Damage | **180** per shot (Handmade Shells) |
| Fire rate | 120 rounds/min (2 shots/sec) |
| Detection range | **4 m** (1.3 foundations) |
| Ammo | up to **384** Handmade Shells (= 192s continuous fire) |
| Power | none (mechanical) — but commonly **wired** to fire on a sensor signal |

The bread-and-butter hallway trap. Mounts on walls; fires when an unauthorized player enters its cone. Authorize yourself so it ignores you. Stack several down a 1-tile corridor for a kill hallway. **Wire to an [[HBHF Sensor]]** so it only fires on enemies, conserving shells.

## Flame Turret

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| HP | **300** |
| Damage | **8** per tick |
| Range | **5.6 m** (1.9 foundations), in a cone |
| Fuel | **Low Grade Fuel — ~30/min** while firing |
| Burst | sprays flames ~5s per trigger |
| Power | none — fuel-driven; wire a trigger to activate |

Area denial — the flame **inhibits movement** and applies stacking burn, brutal in a tight choke. Lower raw DPS than a shotgun trap but the slow + burn punishes anyone trying to push through. Combine flame + shotgun traps in the same hallway.

## Tesla Coil

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| HP | **250** |
| Damage | **1 HP/sec per rW**, up to **35 HP/sec** at 35 rW |
| Range | ~**3.5 m** (just over 1 foundation) |
| Power | **1–35 rW** (you choose; damage scales with input) |

The only *electric* trap that damages directly. Feed it **35 rW** for max output. Very short range, so it shines in 1-tile honeycomb chokes or stacked in a loot-room approach. Drains a lot of power per coil — budget your [[Large Rechargeable Battery]]. **Warning:** the coil zaps *anyone* unauthorized including you if you're not on its list, and it can chain to nearby players.

## SAM Site

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| HP | **1,000** |
| Power | **25 rW** (passes input âˆ’ 25) |
| Range | **150 m** (1 grid square) |
| Outputs | Has Target / Low Ammo (â‰¤10) |
| Ammo | SAM Site Ammo (craftable) |

Anti-air. Locks onto and fires homing rockets at the [[Attack Helicopter]], [[Minicopter]], [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]], and the patrol/event chopper. Essential if you fly or want to deny air-raids on your base. Set to **target players' vehicles** mode for base defense vs **target patrol heli** for farming the event heli. Burns ammo fast — wire the Low Ammo output to a Smart Alarm.

## Igniter

A 1 rW electrical component (not strictly a "trap") that **ignites anything flammable** — wire it to light furnaces remotely, or to ignite flammable traps/oil. Wears out after ~16–17 min. See [[Electrical Components]].

## Landmines

Buried explosive trap; detonates when a player (or animal) steps on it. Placed around base perimeters and on common approach lanes. Non-electric. One-time use, decent anti-personnel deterrent but easily spotted by careful raiders.

## Bear Trap

Cheap metal jaw trap; snares and damages whoever steps in it, holding them in place for a few seconds — enough for your turrets/traps to finish them. Non-electric, reusable after reset.

## Trap-hallway design

The classic kill-tunnel layered down a 1-wide corridor leading to your loot:
1. **[[Pressure Pad]] or [[HBHF Sensor]]** at the entrance → triggers everything.
2. **Shotgun Traps** on the side walls (high DPS).
3. **Flame Turret** mid-hall (slow + burn).
4. **Tesla Coils** in the final choke (constant electric damage).
5. **[[Auto Turrets]]** overwatching the exit.

Authorize your whole team on every device. Build it *behind* your [[Garage Door]] bunker so raiders must commit before they see it.

## Related

- [[Electrical Circuits]] (trap-hallway wiring) · [[Auto Turrets]] · [[Electrical Components]] · [[Raiding]] · [[PvP]]

pages.title: Water Systems
pages.body:
# Water Systems

The plumbing layer for automated [[Farming]] (sprinklers keep crops watered) and for drinking/medical water. Wired with the **Hose Tool** (not the Wire Tool). Some parts need [[Electricity Basics|electricity]] to pump uphill.

## Collection

| Source | Base yield | Stores | Notes |
|--------|-----------|--------|-------|
| **Small Water Catcher** | **3 mL/min** | up to its tank | Cheap; scales with rain/fog/biome. |
| **Large Water Catcher** | **8 mL/min** | up to its tank | Costs ~5× wood, 4× metal, 2× tarp of a small for ~2.5× yield. |
| **Water Barrel** | — (storage) | **20,000 mL**, outputs up to **12 mL/s** | The main buffer tank for a sprinkler farm. |

Catcher yield rises with weather: `base + (Rain × 100mL × biome) + (Fog × 20mL)` for a small catcher (×300/×60 for a large). Rain, snow, and fog all boost collection. New **Water Wheel** river generator (Apr 2026) also pulls water from rivers.

> **Rule of thumb:** small catchers are more cost-efficient per mL than large ones — but large ones save space/sockets. For a serious farm, run **at least 2 Large Water Catchers per Water Barrel**.

## Movement & power

| Component | Power | Behavior |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| **Water Pump** | **5 rW** | Pumps water (~**8.5 mL/s**) and **uphill** against gravity. Required when your sprinklers/tank sit *above* the source. |
| **Fluid Switch & Pump** | **1 rW** | Acts as a water valve/switch. **No power needed if gravity feeds water down** floors; needs power to push *up*. |
| **Powered Water Purifier** | **5 rW** | Converts **salt water → fresh** at a **2:1 ratio**, outputs up to **12 mL/s**. One purifier feeds ~7 pumps. |
| **Fluid Combiner / Splitter** | passive | Merge or split water evenly across 3 ports (like the [[Industrial]] item versions, but for liquid). |

## Sprinklers (the farming payoff)

- Each **Sprinkler consumes 2 mL/sec** and waters a **~3 m radius** patch.
- **Max throughput:** a source outputting only 6 mL/s supports **3 sprinklers** (6 Ã· 2). A full [[Water Barrel]] at 12 mL/s supports **6 sprinklers** — which is also the **chain limit (max 6 sprinklers in a chain, max depth 9 components)**.
- Place sprinklers above [[Planter Box]]es so the spray hits the soil. Powered sprinklers replace manual watering-can runs entirely.

## Build — fully automated sprinkler farm (step by step)

1. **2+ Large Water Catchers** on the roof → hose down into a **Water Barrel**.
2. If your **planters are below** the barrel, gravity feeds them — no pump needed; just hose Barrel → Sprinklers.
3. If your **planters are above** the source, insert a **Water Pump (5 rW)** to push water up; power it from your [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] line.
4. Hose the barrel/pump → up to **6 Sprinklers** arranged over your [[Planter Box]]es (each waters ~3 m).
5. Add **[[Electrical Heater]]s (3 rW)** in a greenhouse to regulate crop temperature, and **Ceiling Lights** for indoor growth.
6. Result: crops stay watered 24/7 with zero manual upkeep as long as it rains enough to refill the catchers.

## Drinking / salt water

- **Powered Water Purifier** turns ocean salt water into drinkable fresh water (2:1) — useful for a coastal/water base with no fresh source. Also produces **Salt** as a byproduct (used in food preservation since the Mar 2025 Crafting Update).

## Related

- [[Farming]] (genetics, planters, fertilizer, yields) · [[Electricity Basics]] · [[Electrical Components]] · [[Industrial]]

pages.title: Airdrop
pages.body:
# Airdrop

An **Airdrop** (Supply Drop) is a green loot crate parachuted in by a **Cargo Plane**. It contains guaranteed resources plus a roll of armor, explosives, and one or two weapons — often including rare items like **[[C4]]** and **Mining Quarries**. Airdrops are triggered either by a **server timer / population threshold** or manually by a player using a **[[Supply Signal]]**.

## How airdrops trigger

| Trigger | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **Server-wide drop** | The host/server spawns a Cargo Plane on a timer or when population hits a threshold. The plane crosses the map and drops one or more crates at fixed/random points. |
| **[[Supply Signal]]** | A player throws a Supply Signal grenade → **violet/purple smoke column** → a Cargo Plane flies in and drops a crate **at the signal's location**. |

The purple smoke is visible from far away, so any drop you call is effectively announced to nearby players.

## Supply Signal

- A **throwable smoke grenade** that calls in one airdrop to where it lands.
- **Where to find them:** rare drop in **[[Military Crate]]s** and **elite crates** (and from some loot sources). Not craftable in normal play.
- **Strategy:** pop it inside your walled compound, on a roof you control, or at a monument you're holding — never in the open, or you're just gifting the crate to whoever's nearby.

## Airdrop contents

Every Supply Drop is **guaranteed** to contain:

- Some **resources**
- **Armor**
- **Explosives**
- **One or two weapons**

Higher-value rolls can include **[[C4]]**, mining quarries, high-tier guns, components, and meds. It's a randomized military-tier table — one of the better ways to luck into explosives or a quarry early.

## Tactics

- **Contesting a server drop:** get there early, take an angle on the landing spot, and let others commit first — third-party the players fighting over it.
- **Calling your own:** secure the area first. The smoke is a beacon; assume company.
- The crate floats down slowly — you can sometimes shoot/reach it as it lands, or wait for it to settle.

## Related

- [[Chinook CH-47]] — the other aerial loot event (drops a [[Locked Crate]])
- [[C4]] — a prized airdrop roll
- [[Military Crate]] — where Supply Signals spawn
- [[Patrol Helicopter]], [[Cargo Ship]] — other contestable loot events

pages.title: Animals
pages.body:
# Animals

Rust's wildlife — a mix of harmless food animals and dangerous predators. They're an early-game food/cloth/fat source and a constant hazard, especially after the **Jungle Update (May 2025)** added the deadliest predators in the game. Animals are killed with melee, bows, or guns and harvested with a tool (a [[Bone Knife]]/[[Salvaged Cleaver]] gets the most resources).

## Standard animals

| Animal | HP | Damage / threat | Drops (harvest) | Where |
|--------|----|-----------------|-----------------|-------|
| **Chicken** | **25** | Harmless | Raw chicken breast, feathers, small fat | Temperate |
| **Boar** | **150** | Tusk melee, moderate | Pork, **animal fat**, leather/bone | All biomes |
| **Stag / Deer** | **150** | Antler melee (flees mostly) | Deer meat, fat, leather, bone | All biomes |
| **Wolf** | **100–150** | Bite + pack behavior, real stalking AI | Wolf meat, fat, **wolf skull**, bone | All biomes |
| **Boar/Stag/Wolf** are the staple food/fat/cloth animals early. | | | | |
| **Brown Bear** | **~325–400** | **Heavy bite + Bleeding**, dangerous | Bear meat, **lots of fat & leather**, bear skull | Forests/all biomes |
| **Polar Bear** | **420** | Same as bear, arctic | Same as bear | Arctic biome |
| **Shark** | **150** | Bite (in water/shipwrecks) | Shark meat | Ocean, near [[Cargo Ship]]/shipwrecks |
| **Horse** | tameable | Mount (not a threat) | — (ride it; saddlebags 12 slots) | Roads, Stables |

> Bear HP is sourced as **325** (Corrosion Hour bestiary) and **400** (Fandom/wiki); treat bears as ~400 effective and very dangerous. Both bears apply **bleed** — back off and patch up rather than tanking the hits.

## Jungle predators (Jungle Update, May 2025)

These spawn **only in the new jungle biome** (tier-0 zones) and are among the most lethal animals in Rust. They use real **stalking/ambush AI** — they sneak, wait, and commit only when they expect a kill.

| Animal | Behavior | Threat | Drops |
|--------|----------|--------|-------|
| **Tiger** | Stalks, **sneaks up from behind**, strikes when it's confident of a kill | Very high — one of the deadliest animals added | High meat/fat |
| **Panther** | Like the tiger but **stealthier**, rare black-coated, moves silently, fast strike | Very high, hardest to see coming | High meat/fat |
| **Crocodile** | River-dweller; **extremely fast in water**, slow on land; **drags prey into the water**; tanky and relentless | High near rivers — don't fight in water | Croc meat/fat, leather |
| **Snake** | Hides in underbrush, strikes fast; **poisons + slows you for ~5 seconds** | Moderate but the poison/slow can get you killed by something else | **5 raw snake meat, 10 animal fat, 4 snake venom** |

**Jungle survival:** keep your back to walls/cliffs (tigers/panthers ambush from behind), avoid fighting crocs in deep water, and watch the ground for snakes. A ranged weapon and a torch/light help spot stalkers. Vine-swinging traversal is part of the biome.

## Harvest notes

- **Animal Fat** (from boars, bears) is the key cooking/low-grade-fuel resource — boars are the most efficient fat source early.
- **Leather** comes from larger animals (bears, crocs); **bone** from most; **cloth** comes from hemp plants, not animals.
- Cook meat before eating — and note **food spoilage** now applies (raw 6h / cooked 24h, paused in a powered fridge; Crafting Update Mar 2025).
- Use a **[[Bone Knife]]** or better cutting tool for max yield; punching/shooting gives less.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- **Wolves (Nov 2024)** and **jungle predators (May 2025)** are new, all with real **stalking AI** — animals are far more dangerous than in 2023.
- **World Update 2.0 (Oct 2024)** added new terrain/biomes; the **Jungle biome (May 2025)** is where the big cats/crocs/snakes live.
- **Horses overhauled (Feb 2025):** they swim, tow siege weapons, and have **12-slot saddlebags**.
- **Sharks** appear around shipwrecks and the [[Deep Sea Event]] waters.

## Related

- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — the humanoid PvE threats
- [[Missions]] — Stables hunt missions target boars/deer; Fishing Village shark hunts
- [[Cooking Workbench]] — for the meat you harvest
- [[Deep Sea Event]] — sharks + ocean wildlife

pages.title: Bradley APC
pages.body:
# Bradley APC

The **Bradley APC** (the "tank") is a stationary-route armored vehicle that patrols [[Launch Site]] (and the rails/road there). It is **immune to everything except explosives** — bullets, melee, fire, and arrows do **zero** damage — so you need rockets, C4, or satchels to kill it. Destroying it drops three high-tier APC crates, making Launch Site a premium mid/late-wipe objective for teams that can afford the explosives.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| HP | **1,000** (verified) |
| Damage immunities | Everything **except explosives** (bullets/melee/fire = 0 dmg) |
| Machine guns | up to **~7 dmg/hit** (twin auto-cannons, suppressive) |
| Main cannon | **~25–30 dmg/shell** (the big "boom" turret) |
| Crates dropped | **3 APC crates** (verified) |
| Crate burn time | **~4 minutes** before lootable (debris must cool) |
| Respawn | **~1 hour** after each kill (verified) |
| Location | [[Launch Site]] (patrols set route) |

## Cost to destroy

| Explosive | Amount | Approx. sulfur |
|-----------|--------|----------------|
| **[[High Velocity Rocket]]** | **4 min** (bring 6–7 for misses) | ~800 (4) to ~1,400 (7) — ~200 sulfur each |
| **[[Rocket]]** | **8** | ~11,200 |
| **[[C4]]** (Timed Explosive Charge) | **3** | ~6,600 |
| **[[Satchel Charge]]** | **~20** | ~9,600 |
| **F1 Grenade** | **~40–50** | — |
| **Explosive 5.56 ammo** | **~500–600** | ~12,500–15,000 |

**Most cost-efficient:** **HV rockets** at ~200 sulfur each. The reliable kill is **4 HV minimum, bring 6–7** (re-verified Jun 2026): 4 land it with clean aim on the rear/treads, but bring spares because misses happen and Bradley is moving. HV rockets fly straight and fast, so they're easier to land on a moving target than standard rockets and cost a fraction of the 8-rocket or 3-C4 routes. The published "4 vs 7" spread is purely aim, not a balance change. See [[Raid Costs]] for the full table.

## How to fight it

1. **Aim at the main body/turret**, not the wheels — every explosive hit counts toward the 1,000 HP pool.
2. **Peek, fire 1–2 rockets, duck.** The cannon one-shots most early armor; do not stand in the open trading shots.
3. **Commit once you start.** If you damage it and then leave it alone for several minutes, **it repairs back to full** — there's no point chipping it across multiple trips.
4. Fight from elevation or behind hard cover at [[Launch Site]] (the rocket-factory building, the rocket itself, container stacks).
5. Watch the cannon's line of sight — it can't shoot what it can't see. Break LoS between volleys.

## Loot

A destroyed Bradley drops **3 APC crates** in burning wreckage. You must wait **~4 minutes** for the fire to die before looting. Contents are high military tier: assault rifles, [[LR-300]], [[M249]], explosives, high-tier components, ammo, and a chance at the **[[Minigun]]** / **Military Flamethrower** (shared exclusive pool with [[Patrol Helicopter]]).

> The kill is loud and the smoke is visible across the map — expect contesters. Have a plan to hold the crates for 4 minutes or to extract them fast.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- Core stats (1,000 HP, explosive-only, 3 crates, ~1h respawn) are unchanged since 2023.
- **Monument loot was reshuffled in late 2025/2026** for the first time in 5+ years — Launch Site's surrounding crate loot changed, but Bradley itself remains the headline reward.
- Explosive-protection on **armor** is now capped at **75%** (May 2025) — relevant when *defending* against Bradley/raids, not for killing it.
- There are now Bradley-style APCs reported at some other locations on certain maps/modes, but Launch Site is the canonical one.

## Related

- [[Launch Site]] — its home monument
- [[Patrol Helicopter]] — the other big AI loot event (no explosives needed)
- [[High Velocity Rocket]], [[Rocket]], [[C4]], [[Satchel Charge]] — kill costs
- [[Raid Costs]] — same explosives, different target

pages.title: Cargo Ship
pages.body:
# Cargo Ship

The **Cargo Ship** ("cargo") is a roaming ocean monument — a large freighter that spawns at the map edge, circles the ocean, and eventually leaves. It is guarded by scientists, packed with crates including **3 hackable [[Locked Crate]]s**, and since the Harbor rework it now **docks at a [[Harbor]]** during its route. It's a great mid-wipe loot run because it needs no explosives, just a way to board and the firepower to clear scientists.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Spawn frequency | Every **2–4 in-game days** (â‰ˆ a few real hours; server-tunable) |
| Scientists | **~12** heavily armed blue scientists (verified screenrant 2026) |
| [[Locked Crate]]s | **3** (verified) — fixed spawn zones at **bow / stern / mid**, each **15-minute** hack |
| Other crates | Multiple basic + military crates across decks/holds |
| Loot respawn | Replenishes every **10 minutes**, up to **3 times** |
| Departure | Triggers a **siren**, then **radiation** floods the deck to lethal — leave |
| Radiation respawn trick | **Survive ~2 minutes into the radiation** and the ship **respawns all 3 locked crates and stops the radiation** (verified) — a free second loot cycle if you can ride it out |
| Lifeboat | At the **back** of the ship for escape |

## Route & harbor docking (post-rework)

The Cargo Ship spawns at the edge of the map and travels across the ocean. Since the **Harbor rework (Apr 2024)** it will pick the **first [[Harbor]] it passes** and **dock there once**. While docked, the harbor **cranes load several red shipping containers onto the deck**. Those containers have openable doors — you can **hide inside one and get craned aboard**, a new stealth boarding route. The ship departs after a short dock window.

This means you can now **board from land** at a harbor instead of needing a boat, which is huge for solos without a [[RHIB]].

## How to board

| Method | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| **[[RHIB]] / boat** | Drive alongside, climb the rear ladder. Classic method. |
| **Harbor container** | Hide in a dock container before the crane loads it (post-rework). |
| **Swim + ladder** | Possible but slow and exposed; the ship moves. |
| **Parachute / [[Attack Helicopter]]** | Air-drop onto the deck (parachutes added; -20% durability per use). |

## Clearing & loot

- Push the decks killing scientists (MP5s, shotguns, LR-300s). Use corridors and containers for cover.
- Start the **3 [[Locked Crate]] hacks early** — each takes **15 minutes**, and the global map marker tells everyone you're there. Hack all three so they finish around the same time.
- Loot the regular crates; they **refill every 10 minutes up to 3 times**, so a long, defended hold pays off if you can keep the ship.
- When the **departure siren** sounds, radiation ramps to lethal. Either **leave immediately** via the rear **lifeboat**/your boat/parachute, **or** — if you have rad protection and meds — **tank ~2 minutes into the radiation**: the ship then **respawns all 3 locked crates and shuts off the radiation**, giving you a clean second loot run with no one else around.

Loot tier: rifles, components, ammo, plus the **3 locked crates** (elite-tier guns, [[C4]], high-end components). Among the better PvE loot runs available without explosives.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- **Harbor docking (Apr 2024)** is the big change vs. 2023 — board from land, hide in craned containers.
- The deparature **radiation timer is unchanged** in concept (siren → flood).
- **Deep Sea (Feb 2026):** note that **RHIBs are banned** from the new [[Deep Sea Event]] zone, but RHIBs are still fine for boarding the normal cargo ship.
- Gunshot audibility ranges (Sep 2025) mean clearing cargo draws attention from shore.

## Related

- [[Harbor]] — where it now docks
- [[Locked Crate]] — the 3 hackable crates aboard
- [[RHIB]], [[Attack Helicopter]] — boarding tools
- [[Deep Sea Event]] — the newer offshore loot zone
- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — the blue scientists aboard

pages.title: Chinook CH-47
pages.body:
# Chinook CH-47

The **Chinook CH-47** is a large twin-rotor transport helicopter with two roles in Rust:

1. **The loot event** — a Chinook flies over the map and drops a **single [[Locked Crate]]** at a random tier-1+ monument, which players then hack (15 min) and fight over.
2. **The Oil Rig defense** — when you hack the [[Locked Crate]] on an [[Oil Rig]], a Chinook flies in and **deploys heavy scientists** onto the helipad.

## Chinook loot event

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Frequency | Random / occasional (rarer than [[Airdrop]]s) |
| Drop | **1 [[Locked Crate]]** (the CH47 crate) |
| Drop location | A random **tier-1-or-higher monument** |
| Hack time | **15 minutes** |
| Marker | Crate location shown **globally** on the map during the hack |
| Reset | **Shooting the crate resets the hack timer** |

How it plays out:

1. The Chinook appears, circles, and drops a single locked crate at a monument (it may carry it slung underneath before placing it).
2. Approach and **start the hack** — 15-minute countdown, visible to the whole server.
3. Defend it for 15 minutes. **Do not shoot the crate** — taking damage resets the timer (a known troll/denial tactic).
4. It opens into elite-tier loot: high-end guns, [[C4]]/explosives, rare components.

You can also try to **shoot down the Chinook itself** for a bonus, but it has a large HP pool and the real prize is the crate.

## Chinook at Oil Rig

When you activate the locked crate on [[Small Oil Rig]] (L4) or [[Large Oil Rig]] (L6), a Chinook flies in and **fast-ropes heavy scientists** onto the helipad — **5 on Small Rig, 10 on Large Rig** (verified Corrosion Hour). See [[Oil Rig]] and [[NPCs & Scientists]] for heavy-scientist stats (**300 HP** verified, 5 headshots, four equal-chance loadout variants: [[M249]] / Minigun / Military Flamethrower / [[SPAS-12]]).

## Tips

- The free-roaming Chinook crate is one of the best "no explosives needed" loot grabs — but the global marker means you must be ready to **hold a monument for 15 minutes** against third parties.
- Bring a teammate to watch flanks while one defends the crate.
- Don't pre-damage the crate; let the timer run clean.

## Related

- [[Locked Crate]] — what it drops / what you hack
- [[Oil Rig]] — where it deploys heavy scientists
- [[Airdrop]] — the other aerial loot event
- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — heavy scientists it carries

pages.title: Christmas Event
pages.body:
# Christmas Event

Rust's annual winter event, branded "Rustmas" / "Merry Rustmas" / "Seasons Beatings." Facepunch turns it on in mid-December and it runs **all the way to the January force-wipe** — the longest of the three seasonal events. While live, **presents rain down around every player** on a jingle-bell timer, **stockings** you place refill with loot, and a **Santa sleigh** replaces the C130 [[Airdrop]]. See [[Seasonal Events]] for the shared skeleton.

## Schedule

| Year | Live | Ends |
|------|------|------|
| 2023 | mid-Dec | Jan force-wipe |
| 2024 ("Season's Beatings") | mid-Dec | Jan force-wipe |
| **2025** ("Silent Night, Violent Night") | **~Dec 16–18** | **Jan New Year force-wipe** |

Pattern: on ~Dec 16, runs to the first-Thursday January wipe. Longest seasonal window (~2+ weeks).

## Presents (the core mechanic)

Triggered automatically **at the start of each new in-game day**, announced by **jingle bells**.

- **Default: 2 gifts spawn per player** (`xmas.giftsperplayer`, default 2), within **~40–50 m** (`xmas.spawnrange`, default 50). Up to 5 spawn attempts (`xmas.spawnattempts`).
- You must **destroy/open the present** to get the loot inside.
- Presents come in **three sizes — Small, Medium, Large** — with loot scaling up sharply by size.

### Present loot by size

| Size | Loot tier |
|------|-----------|
| **Small** | Basic resources, low-grade fuel, small festive items, candy cane |
| **Medium** | Components, mid-tier weapons, festive cosmetics |
| **Large** | **Endgame** — high-tier weapons, **explosives (C4 / rockets)**, big resource stacks |

A Large present is comparable to a good [[Airdrop]] tier — they're worth fighting over.

### Present trade-up ladder

If you don't get a Large from RNG, ladder up: **collect 10 of a type → trade into 1 of the next tier up**, all the way to Large.

| Combine | → Get |
|---------|-------|
| 10 Small presents | 1 Medium present |
| 10 Medium presents | 1 Large present |

This is the Christmas analog to the Halloween candy → loot-bag ladder.

## Stockings

Craftable/placeable deployables you hang in your base. **Every time the jingle bells ring (each new in-game day), your stockings refill with loot.**

| Stocking | Loot quality | Lifespan |
|----------|--------------|----------|
| **Small Stocking** | Lower | ~**5–10 refills** then expires |
| **Large Stocking** | Higher chance of better items | ~**5–10 refills** then expires |

Hang several before logging off — they're passive free loot during the event. Refill is also forced server-wide via `xmas.refill`.

## Santa sleigh airdrops

During the event, the C130 sound is replaced by **sleigh bells** — **Santa and his reindeer** fly over and drop **giant gift-wrapped [[Airdrop]]s** trailing sparkles. These carry the normal airdrop loot **plus extra presents**, so they're even more worth chasing than a standard drop.

## Gingerbread houses (PvE dungeon)

Gingerbread houses spawn around the map (count scales with map size — e.g. ~**34** on a 4750 map, ~**14** on a 3100 map). Inside you fight **gingerbread men** enemies and loot **special presents** and crates. The Christmas equivalent of the Halloween portal dungeons.

## Event-only items & cosmetics

| Item | Type | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| **Snowball Launcher** | Weapon | Fires snowballs; festive joke gun |
| **Candy Cane Club** | Melee weapon | Festive melee |
| **Snowball** | Throwable | Snowball fights |
| **Santa Hat** | Cosmetic headwear | Free from presents |
| **Reindeer Antlers** | Cosmetic headwear | Free from presents |
| **Pookie Bear** | Cosmetic/companion item | Rare present drop |
| **Christmas Tree** | Deployable (decorable) | Craft: 100 wood, 20 cloth; 6 decoration types (stars, baubles, pinecones, gingerbread men, candy canes, tinsel/lights) |
| **Advent Calendar** | Deployable | Craft: 100 wood, 20 cloth |
| **Wooden Sled** | Vehicle/toy | Craft: 150 wood, 25 metal fragments |
| **Ice Walls / Snow Machine** | Building/decor | Ice wall ~300–3000 stone by height |
| **Gingerbread skin** | Free building skin | Applies to wood structures during event |

Plus **paid Christmas skins** in the Steam Item Store for the duration.

## Console
