pages.title: Deep Sea Event
pages.body:
# Deep Sea Event

The **Deep Sea** is an offshore **event zone** added in the **Naval Update (Feb 5, 2026)** — the biggest content drop in Rust's history. It opens at one cardinal direction per wipe and runs in timed windows, packing **Ghost Ships**, a **Floating City** safe-zone hub, **Tropical Islands**, and roaming **PT Boat / scientist patrols** with elite-tier loot. Crucially you need a **player-built boat or a captured PT Boat to get there** — RHIBs, rowboats, and submarines can't survive the trip — so it's a late-wipe objective.

## Access & timing

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Added | **Naval Update, Feb 5, 2026** |
| Location | One **cardinal direction** (N/S/E/W), fixed for the wipe |
| Event window | ~**3-hour** cycles (10,800s) then contents are destroyed |
| Warnings | Toast at **20 min** left; **radiation starts at 5 min**, overwhelming at **3 min** |
| Access craft | **Player-built boats** or **[[PT Boat]]** only (no [[RHIB]] / rowboat / sub) |
| Building | **No building, no sleeping bags** inside the zone |
| Loot | **First-come, first-served** — once looted it's gone until reset |

## What's inside

### Ghost Ships
Stationary wrecked vessels (about **4** total, visual variants Clean / Chum / Cargo Deck), each guarded by **~6 scientists** plus PT-boat patrols. Interiors hold brown/green crates, red toolboxes, and **2 [[Locked Crate]]s** per ship — and hacking those locked crates **triggers a patrol-boat attack**, like Oil Rig. Top-tier elite loot.

### Floating City
A **safe-zone hub** monument out in the Deep Sea with **vendors, turrets, and fishing spots** — and a **casino**. A place to trade and regroup mid-event.

### Tropical Islands
About **6** islands with mixed themes — some flat with **3–5 scientists**, others with ancient rune fortifications and more guards. Loaded with **fuel barrels (32+ per island documented)**, ore nodes (metal/sulfur), and metal-detecting spots with improved drop rates.

### PT Boat / scientist patrols
**Patrol fleets** roam the open water — typically **one [[PT Boat]]** (dual M249-equivalent gunners) flanked by **two RHIBs** of scientists. They aggressively engage players. Island scientists smoke-grenade and flank, dealing ~**18 dmg/bullet** vs. a Hazmat suit.

## Tactics

- **Build a boat first.** A player-built modular ship (or a stolen PT Boat) is the entry ticket — see [[Naval Update]] / boats. RHIB won't make it.
- Watch the clock: at **5 minutes left** radiation begins, so plan extraction with buffer.
- Hit **islands for fuel/ore** if you want resources; hit **Ghost Ships** for elite crates (and expect the patrol-attack on locked-crate hacks).
- Use the **Floating City** as a safe regroup/trade point, but it's contested PvP-adjacent.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

This entire system is **new since you last played** — the ocean was an afterthought in 2023. Naval Update (Feb 2026) added player-built ships with **cannons**, the Deep Sea zone, Ghost Ships, Floating Cities, and **[[PT Boat]]s**. As of March 2026 boats support **electricity/industrial IO**.

## Related

- [[PT Boat]] — patrol craft / access vehicle
- [[Locked Crate]] — Ghost Ship hackables
- [[Cargo Ship]], [[Oil Rig]] — the older naval events (RHIB-friendly)
- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — Deep Sea scientist patrols
- [[Naval Update]] — the parent content update

pages.title: Easter Event
pages.body:
# Easter Event

Rust's annual spring event. Facepunch turns it on in mid-April for a ~2-week window ending at the April force-wipe. Mechanically it's the **closest twin to the [[Halloween Event]]** — swap candy for **colored eggs** and scarecrows for nothing (Easter has no roaming NPCs), and you have the same hunt-scoreboard-and-upgrade loop. See [[Seasonal Events]] for the shared skeleton.

## Schedule

| Year | Live | Ends |
|------|------|------|
| **2025** | **Apr 10, 2025** | **Apr 24, 2025** |
| 2026 | mid-April (expected) | April force-wipe |

Pattern: turns on ~April 10, runs ~2 weeks to the next monthly wipe.

## Egg hunt (the scoreboard event)

- **Frequency:** the hunt refreshes roughly **every 24–38 in-game hours** (i.e. about once every other in-game day, like the other events).
- **Trigger:** cheerful music signals the hunt.
- **Mechanic:** colorful **Easter Eggs** spawn around every player.
- **Duration:** **3 minutes** to collect as many as possible.
- **Scoreboard:** server ranks all players; the **top 3** get prize eggs (which you then crack for loot):

| Rank | Reward |
|------|--------|
| 1st | **3 Silver Eggs** |
| 2nd | **1 Silver Egg** |
| 3rd | **1 Bronze Egg** |

Cracking a prize egg yields loot **ranging from scrap up to an M249** — same payout ceiling as the Halloween loot bags. Like Halloween, an active hunt is contestable PvP; geared players camp egg spawns near enemy bases.

## The egg upgrade ladder

Non-podium players still progress. The raw **Painted Eggs** you collect ladder up:

| Combine | → Get |
|---------|-------|
| 10 Painted Eggs | 1 **Bronze Egg** |
| 10 Bronze Eggs | 1 **Silver Egg** |
| 10 Silver Eggs | 1 **Gold Egg** |

Each higher tier cracks open for better loot — the same collect-10-to-upgrade pattern as Halloween candy and Christmas presents. A **Gold Egg** is the top tier.

## Eggs as loot containers

The colored eggs (Bronze / Silver / Gold) are **crackable loot containers**, not just trophies. Contents scale by color and can include tools (**jackhammers, chainsaws**), resources (stone, low-grade fuel), and weapons up to **double-barrel shotgun / M249**. Free cosmetics (Bunny Ears, Bunny Onesie) also drop from Bronze/Silver eggs.

## Event-only items & cosmetics

| Item | What it does | Source |
|------|--------------|--------|
| **Egg Basket** | **Instant egg pickup** (left-click grabs immediately instead of a per-egg wait) — major scoreboard edge | Event drop |
| **Bunny Ears** | Free cosmetic + "Egg Vision" (see more eggs) | Bronze/Silver eggs |
| **Bunny Onesie** | Free cosmetic + Egg Vision | Bronze/Silver eggs |
| **Bunny Hat / Nest Hat** | Cosmetic headwear | Steam Item Store |
| **Egg Suit / Chicken Costume** | Cosmetic full outfit | Steam Item Store |
| **Easter Horse Costumes** | Cosmetic for [[Horse]]s | Steam Item Store |

The **Egg Basket (fast pickup) + Bunny Onesie/Ears (egg vision)** combo is the Easter equivalent of Halloween's Pumpkin Basket + Scarecrow Wrap — wear both to win the scoreboard.

## Console

Easter uses the same general convar style as the other events (an `enabled` toggle and a manual-refresh command). Exact Easter convar names are not confirmed from a live event — see [[Seasonal Events]] for the documented Halloween/Christmas commands.

## Related

- [[Seasonal Events]] — shared event pattern + [[Halloween Event]] / [[Christmas Event]]
- [[Airdrop]] — closest year-round analog to the prize-egg loot
- [[Horse]] — Easter horse costumes
- [[Force Wipe]] — event ends at the April wipe

pages.title: Giant Excavator
pages.body:
# Giant Excavator

The **Giant Excavator** is a large industrial monument (the Giant Excavator Pit) you can **activate by feeding it [[Diesel Fuel]]** to mass-mine a chosen resource. It outputs roughly **twice a [[Mining Quarry]]'s rate** over the same time, making it the best bulk-resource event on the map — but running it is loud, marks you on the map, and invites contesters.

## How to run it

1. Climb up to the control platform on the excavator.
2. **Select the ore** at the control panel — it splits into **stone, sulfur, and high quality metal** outputs (plus metal). Pick the resource line you want.
3. **Add [[Diesel Fuel]]** to the fuel tank and start the engine with **Use (E)**.
4. It runs for about **2 minutes per diesel**, dumping the mined resource into output bins / onto the conveyor for you to collect.

## Output (per diesel)

| Resource | Yield per diesel (full run) |
|----------|------------------------------|
| **Stone** | ~**5,000** |
| **Metal Ore** | ~**1,000** |
| **Sulfur Ore** | ~**1,000** |
| **High Quality Metal** | ~**50** |

(You pick one line; the figures above are the per-diesel ceiling for that line. Output per diesel is roughly **2x a [[Mining Quarry]]** over the same timeframe.)

## Where to get diesel

**[[Diesel Fuel]]** is not bought from vendors in normal play — find it at:

- The top of **[[The Dome]]**
- **[[Junkyard]]**

Each diesel barrel powers one ~2-minute run, so stock up before committing.

## Tactics

- The excavator is **loud and visible** while running — it telegraphs your presence to the whole area. Bring a teammate to watch the approaches.
- Best run when server pop is low or you control the area; geared teams will third-party an active excavator.
- HQM line is the most valuable per-diesel relative to how slow HQM is to farm elsewhere.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- **Quarries & Pump Jacks were reworked to require [[Diesel Fuel]]** like the excavator (you can no longer just feed them low-grade fuel passively the old way) — they're now in line with the excavator's diesel model.
- **World Update 2.0 (Oct 2024)** regenerated terrain but the excavator monument and its mechanics are intact.

## Related

- [[Diesel Fuel]] — the fuel it needs
- [[The Dome]], [[Junkyard]] — diesel sources
- [[Mining Quarry]] — the smaller personal version
- [[Sulfur]], [[High Quality Metal]] — what you're after

pages.title: Halloween Event
pages.body:
# Halloween Event

Rust's annual spooky-season event. Facepunch flips it on for a ~2-week window and it auto-ends at the November force-wipe. While live, **scarecrows and mummies roam the map hunting players**, **portals to loot dungeons** appear, and a **trick-or-treat candy hunt** fires every other in-game day with a server scoreboard. See [[Seasonal Events]] for the shared event skeleton.

## Schedule

| Year | Live | Ends |
|------|------|------|
| 2023 | late Oct | Nov 2 |
| 2024 | late Oct | Nov force-wipe |
| **2025** | **Oct 23, 2pm EST** | **Nov 6, 2025** (mandatory patch to enable) |

Pattern: turns on ~Oct 23 via a mandatory patch, runs to early November / the next monthly wipe. Expect the same window each October.

## Trick-or-treat candy hunt (the scoreboard event)

- **Frequency:** about **once every other in-game day**.
- **Trigger:** announced by spooky music + a "Trick or Treat" countdown.
- **Mechanic:** when the countdown ends, **[[Halloween Candy]]** spawns on the ground around *every* player on the server.
- **Duration:** you have **3 minutes** to collect as much candy as possible.
- **Scoreboard:** server ranks every player by candy collected. At the end, the **top 3** are rewarded:

| Rank | Reward |
|------|--------|
| 1st | **3 Medium Loot Bags** |
| 2nd | **1 Medium Loot Bag** |
| 3rd | **1 Small Loot Bag** |

(Older posts described "top 5"/"special loot bags"; the verified 2025 payout is the top-3 table above.)

This is **contestable PvP** — geared players camp candy spawns near enemy bases, so treat an active hunt like a mini [[Airdrop]].

## Halloween Candy & the loot-bag ladder

[[Halloween Candy]] is both food and currency:

- **As food:** edible, **+25 calories, +1 HP** (negligible — don't rely on it).
- **Stack size 1,000; despawns in 5 min** on the ground.
- **As currency — the upgrade ladder:**

| Combine | → Get |
|---------|-------|
| 10 Halloween Candy | 1 **Small Loot Bag** |
| 10 Small Loot Bags | 1 **Medium Loot Bag** |
| 10 Medium Loot Bags | 1 **Large Loot Bag** |

**Loot bags** are the real prize. Contents scale by bag size and can include event cosmetics (Vampire Stake, Pumpkin Basket, Scarecrow Wrap), resources, and **weapons ranging from a Hunting Bow up to an M249**. A Large Loot Bag is endgame-tier — saving candy to ladder up is a legitimate solo strategy if you can't win the scoreboard.

## Scarecrows & Mummies (roaming NPCs)

- **HP:** **200 each**.
- **Population:** roughly **40** roaming a default-size map.
- **Behavior:** aggressive — they charge and chase players relentlessly.
- **Weapons:** chainsaws, sickles, machetes, beancan grenades.
- **Drops:** themed body parts (head / torso / legs, in heavy/medium/light variants) plus real loot — fuses, guitars, metal blades, sickles, **SAR bodies, F1 grenades**, and rare cosmetics (Ghost Sheet Costume, Frankenstein/Mummy Masks).

They're free XP-equivalent loot if you have any rifle, but the body parts feed the Frankenstein pet system below.

## Frankenstein pets

Build a **Frankenstein's Table**, feed it three body parts (head + torso + legs) dropped by scarecrows/mummies, and animate a combat pet.

- **Craft cost:** **200 metal fragments** at a [[Workbench Level 1]].
- **Part type sets the build:** **Light** (fast, low HP), **Medium** (balanced), **Heavy** (tanky, slow) — depending on which limb variants you use.
- **Limit:** **1 pet per player**.
- **Leash:** follows you up to **~100 m** before recalling.
- **Commands:** Idle, Follow, Combat, Assist, Guard, Move, Destroy. Bind with `bind <key> +pets` to open the pet wheel.

## Portals & dungeons

- Appear as **blue glowing doors** at random map locations (population set by `halloweendungeon.population`).
- Walk through to a small **underground dungeon** containing **2–5 scarecrow NPCs** guarding **normal + military crates**.
- Clear it, loot, and leave via the return portal. Low-effort loot if a portal spawns near you.

## Event-only items & cosmetics

| Item | What it does | Source / cost |
|------|--------------|---------------|
| **Pumpkin Basket** | **Instant candy pickup** (no per-candy delay) — huge scoreboard edge | Loot bag drop |
| **Scarecrow Wrap** | "Candy Vision" — reveals an extra candy vs other players | Scarecrow drop / loot bag |
| **Ghost Sheet Costume** | Wearable costume + Candy Vision | Rare scarecrow drop |
| **Frankenstein Mask / Mummy Mask** | Free cosmetic headwear during event | Kill scarecrows / mummies |
| **Vampire / Wooden Stake** | One-hit weapon vs the undead NPCs | Undead corpse drop |
| **Dracula Mask & Cape** | Cosmetic head armor | Craft: 10 cloth |
| Coffins, spider webs, graveyard fence, skull spikes | Decorative base deployables | Craft / loot |

Plus **paid Halloween skins** in the Steam Item Store for the duration.

## Console

- `halloween.enabled true/false` — toggle the event.
- `halloweendungeon.population <n>` — portal/dungeon spawn rate.
- `bind <key> +pets` — pet command wheel.

## Related

- [[Seasonal Events]] — shared event pattern + [[Christmas Event]] / [[Easter Event]]
- [[Halloween Candy]] — the hunt collectible + upgrade ladder
- [[Airdrop]] — closest year-round analog to the loot-bag rewards
- [[Workbench Level 1]] — needed to craft the Frankenstein's Table

pages.title: Missions
pages.body:
# Missions

**Missions** are repeatable quests handed out by NPCs at the safe-zone monuments ([[Outpost]], [[Bandit Camp]], [[Stables]], [[Fishing Village]]). They're low-risk "go there, bring this, come back" tasks that pay **scrap and tools** — a reliable, safe income stream that's great for solos early in a wipe and for topping up scrap without contesting events.

## How missions work

1. Talk to a mission NPC at a safe zone, pick an available mission.
2. Complete the objective (kill X animals, gather/turn in resources, visit a monument, fish, treasure-hunt).
3. Return to the NPC to claim the reward.
4. **Lock-out timers** apply — you can't immediately re-request the same mission after completing **or abandoning** it.

Missions are intentionally low-stakes: steady scrap/tools without the risk of [[Oil Rig]], [[Cargo Ship]], or PvP monuments. Stack several across different safe zones to keep them all on cooldown rotation.

## Mission givers by location

| Location | NPC | Missions |
|----------|-----|----------|
| **[[Bandit Camp]]** | **Lumberjack** | Lost Bottles, Collect Wood, Wildlife Cull |
| **[[Bandit Camp]]** | **Miner** | Mining/resource gathering tasks |
| **[[Outpost]]** | **CZ-721**, **Vagabond** | Gather / fetch / visit-monument tasks |
| **[[Stables]]** | **Hunter** | **Boar Hunt**, **Deer Hunt** |
| **[[Stables]]** | **Stablehand** | Horse/stable tasks |
| **[[Fishing Village]]** | **Dive Master** | **Shark Hunt**, **Underwater Bounty** |
| **[[Fishing Village]]** | **Fisherman** | **Tackle the Day**, **Go Fish**, **Oiled Up** |

## Mission types

- **Hunt** — kill a number of animals ([[Animals]]: boars, deer, sharks). Stables/Fishing Village.
- **Gather** — bring back specific resources (wood, ore, etc.). Bandit Camp/Outpost.
- **Fish** — catch fish / fishing-based objectives. Fishing Village.
- **Visit** — travel to a particular monument.
- **Treasure hunt** — find/dig up a reward at a location.

## Rewards

Missions pay **scrap and tools** primarily, plus occasional components/resources. The value is in **safety and reliability** — you'll never get an [[Oil Rig]]-tier payout, but you also won't lose your kit. Excellent for:

- Early-wipe scrap toward your first **[[Workbench]]** and **Blueprint Fragment** hunts.
- Solos who want income without PvP exposure.
- Topping up scrap between event runs.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- Missions and the safe-zone NPC vendors are mature systems by 2026.
- **[[Stables]]** is a mission hub now (Hunter + Stablehand), tied to the **horse overhaul (Feb 2025)** — saddlebags, swimming horses, siege-weapon towing.
- Safe-zone **vendor prices float with demand (Jul 2024)**, so the broader safe-zone economy around missions shifts over a wipe.
- Mission scrap feeds the **post-"Pivot Or Die" (Nov 2025)** progression where research is cheap (15/30/60/120 scrap) but you still need scrap + **Blueprint Fragments** to tier up workbenches.

## Related

- [[Outpost]], [[Bandit Camp]], [[Stables]], [[Fishing Village]] — safe-zone hubs
- [[Animals]] — hunt-mission targets
- [[Scrap]], [[Workbench]] — what the rewards feed into
- [[Recycler]] — the other safe-zone scrap source

pages.title: NPCs & Scientists
pages.body:
# NPCs & Scientists

Rust's hostile humanoid NPCs. **Scientists** guard monuments and events; **dwellers** patrol the underground tunnels and underwater labs; **heavy scientists** defend [[Oil Rig]] crate hacks. They drop scrap, components, meds, ammo, and sometimes weapons. Knowing their HP, headshot counts, and aggro ranges is the difference between farming them and dying to them.

## Scientist tiers (HP)

All HP values below are **verified against rusthelp.com / Facepunch wiki (2026-06-13)**. NPC HP varies by *spawn location* in Rust, so the "blue scientist" you fight is not one fixed number — a monument/Launch Site scientist is **150 HP** but the **Oil Rig scientist is 215 HP**.

| Tier | NPC | HP | Typical weapons | Where |
|------|-----|----|-----------------|-------|
| 1 | **Roaming / Roadside (Road) Scientist** | **115** | [[M92 Pistol]] | Roads, roadside crates |
| 2 | **[[Tunnel Dweller]]** | **125** (verified) | M92 / **M39** rifle | Underground train tunnels |
| 2 | **[[Underwater Dweller]]** (Lab Dweller) | **125** (verified) | M92 / **MP5** | Underwater Labs |
| 3 | **Monument / Launch Site Scientist (blue)** | **150** (verified) | **MP5** or **[[LR-300]]** | Most monuments, Launch Site, [[Cargo Ship]] |
| 3 | **Oil Rig Scientist (blue)** | **215** (verified) | MP5 / LR-300 | [[Oil Rig]] (the rig blues are tankier than monument blues) |
| 4 | **Military / NVG Scientist** | **175–300** | LR-300 or **[[SPAS-12]]** | Military Tunnels / Nuclear Missile Silo (flag: exact silo HP unverified) |
| 6 | **[[Heavy Scientist]]** | **300** (verified) | **[[M249]]** / **Minigun** / **Military Flamethrower** / **[[SPAS-12]]** | [[Oil Rig]] (Chinook event), [[Patrol Helicopter]]/[[Bradley APC]] drops |

> **Flagged unverified:** NVG/Silo and Military-Tunnel scientist exact HP (115/175/300 are community figures; rusthelp lists per-location variants but I confirmed only Road 115, Tunnel/Underwater Dweller 125, monument/Launch 150, Oil Rig 215, Heavy 300 directly). Dweller *weapon* loadouts (M39 vs M92, MP5 vs M92) are community-sourced and not individually verified on rusthelp.

**Headshot rule of thumb:** a standard **blue scientist dies to 3 headshots**; a **heavy scientist takes 5 headshots** (EOD/heavy armor). Body shots take many more — always aim for the head.

### The four Heavy Scientist loadout variants (verified 2026-06-13)

Heavy Scientists all share **300 HP** but spawn as one of **four named weapon variants**, and rusthelp lists each as its own entity for **both** the Oil Rig and Bradley spawn pools:

| Variant | Weapon | Oil Rig entity | Bradley entity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Heavy M249** | [[M249]] LMG | Oil Rig Heavy M249 Scientist | Bradley Heavy M249 Scientist |
| **Heavy Minigun** | Minigun | Oil Rig Heavy Minigun Scientist | Bradley Heavy Minigun Scientist |
| **Heavy Flamethrower** | Military Flamethrower | Oil Rig Heavy Flamethrower Scientist | Bradley Heavy Flamethrower Scientist |
| **Heavy SPAS-12** | [[SPAS-12]] shotgun | Oil Rig Heavy SPAS Scientist | Bradley Heavy SPAS Scientist |

The four variants are an **even split — ~25% chance each** per heavy spawned (community-standard understanding; rusthelp lists four equal-weight entity pools rather than a published per-spawn weight, so treat the 25%-each split as **community-sourced, not a published convar**). All four were re-added to the heavy loadout after the SPAS/M249 heavies returned in the Apr 2024 update (previously only Minigun + Flamethrower).

## Aggro & damage

- **Aggro distances** fall into ~**4 bands: 15m, 30m, 40m, 60m**, depending on the NPC tier and your gear/exposure. Crouching and breaking line of sight reduces detection.
- **Scientist bullets do full damage regardless of range** — but their **accuracy drops off sharply** at distance, so fighting them from far with a scoped rifle is much safer than close-quarters.
- Scientists throw **smoke grenades** and will **flank** when you crouch in cover (notably Deep Sea island scientists).
- Sample damage: Deep Sea island scientists deal **~18 HP per bullet** against a Hazmat suit.

## The dwellers (underground / underwater)

| NPC | HP | Weapons | Notes |
|-----|----|---------|-------|
| **[[Tunnel Dweller]]** | **125** (verified rusthelp 2026-06-13) | M92 pistol or **M39 rifle** (loadout community-sourced) | Patrol train-tunnel stations. The **M39 variant is accurate and dangerous**. Gas-masked, territorial, respawn at bad times. |
| **[[Underwater Dweller]]** (Underwater Lab Dweller) | **125** (verified rusthelp 2026-06-13) | M92 or MP5 (loadout community-sourced) | Patrol most of the Underwater Labs. Similar threat to tunnel dwellers; fight is in water/cramped rooms. |

Both are reclusive — they don't roam far from their stations, so you can often avoid or pick them off one at a time.

## Heavy Scientists (the real fight)

The **[[Heavy Scientist]]** is a reinforced, **300 HP** (verified), heavy-armored scientist that arrives via **[[Chinook CH-47]]** when you hack an [[Oil Rig]] locked crate (**5** at Small Rig, **10** at Large Rig — Corrosion Hour; some guides list 6 at Small, treat 5 as the canonical figure). They come in **four equal-chance loadout variants — M249, Minigun, Military Flamethrower, SPAS-12 (see table above)** — and drop the best NPC loot (incl. explosives + high-tier gear; the Minigun/Military Flamethrower are themselves rare drops). Bring an automatic rifle/LMG, a shotgun for the rush, and lots of meds; use doorways and railings as cover.

## Other NPCs

- **Scarecrows** and **Murderers** — melee zombies that appear at certain monuments / Halloween events (seasonal). Low threat, melee only.
- **PT Boat / Deep Sea scientists** — see [[Deep Sea Event]]; PT boats mount dual M249-equivalent gunners.

## Loot summary

| Tier | Typical drops |
|------|---------------|
| Roadside / dweller | Basic meds, low scrap, ammo, low-tier components (gears, springs) |
| Blue / military | Mid meds, rare components, SMG/AR parts, weapon bodies |
| NVG / heavy | Tech trash, rifle bodies, military-grade meds, explosives, high-tier gear |

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- **Monument loot reshuffle (late 2025/2026)** changed what crates/NPCs drop at several monuments — the NPC HP/headshot values here are current but contents shifted.
- New scientist deployments exist at the **Nuclear Missile Silo** (now [[Red Keycard]]) and across the **[[Deep Sea Event]]** zone (Feb 2026).
- Aggro-band and full-damage-at-range mechanics are unchanged.

## Related

- [[Oil Rig]], [[Cargo Ship]], [[Patrol Helicopter]], [[Bradley APC]] — where you fight these NPCs
- [[Chinook CH-47]] — delivers heavy scientists
- [[Animals]] — the non-humanoid PvE threats
- [[Deep Sea Event]] — newest scientist content

pages.title: Oil Rig
pages.body:
# Oil Rig

The **Oil Rig** monuments are stationary offshore platforms guarded by scientists, each with a top-floor **[[Locked Crate]]** that, when hacked, triggers a **[[Chinook CH-47]] heavy-scientist defense event**. There are two: **Small Oil Rig** and **Large Oil Rig**. They're a core mid-wipe loot source — clear the scientists, hack the crate, survive the heavy-scientist drop, take the loot.

You reach them by boat ([[RHIB]] recommended) or by swimming. No radiation on the rigs themselves (unlike [[Cargo Ship]]).

## Small Oil Rig

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Blue scientists | **~12–15** patrolling (**215 HP each**, verified); 5-headshot to torso-tank, aim head |
| Heavy scientists (event) | **5** (via [[Chinook CH-47]]; Corrosion Hour — some guides say 6) |
| Locked crate | On **Level 4**, **15-minute** hack (verified) |
| Loot containers | ~8–31 incl. **3 [[Green Keycard]]-locked** rooms + military/elite crates |
| Scientist respawn | **~24 minutes** (verified Corrosion Hour) |
| Puzzle | [[Green Keycard]] for the L3 locked rooms |

## Large Oil Rig

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Blue scientists | **23** (L0:2, L1:3, L2:2, L3:2, L4:4, L5:3, L6:7 — verified Corrosion Hour); **215 HP each** |
| Heavy scientists (event) | **10** (via [[Chinook CH-47]] — verified Corrosion Hour) |
| Locked crate | On **Level 6**, **15-minute** hack (verified) |
| Loot containers | ~62 across levels (L0:2, L2:13, L3:9, L4:10, L5:16, L6:14 — verified Corrosion Hour) |
| Scientist respawn | **~24 minutes** (verified Corrosion Hour) |
| Crate types | food, medical, standard, military, **elite**, barrels |

## The hack → Chinook event

1. Clear enough scientists to reach the locked crate (L4 Small, L6 Large).
2. Activate the **[[Locked Crate]]** — starts a **15-minute** timer **and** spawns a **[[Chinook CH-47]]** that drops **heavy scientists** onto the helipad (**5** on Small, **10** on Large).
3. **Heavy scientists** are heavy-armored, **300 HP** (verified), take **5 headshots** to drop (vs. 3 for a blue scientist), and come in **four equal-chance loadout variants — [[M249]], Minigun, Military Flamethrower, [[SPAS-12]]** (see [[NPCs & Scientists]]). Treat them as the real fight — they're far tougher than the patrol scientists. **Note the rig's own blue scientists are 215 HP** (verified rusthelp), tankier than the 150 HP monument blues.
4. Survive 15 minutes, the crate unlocks → elite-tier loot (guns, [[C4]], high-end components).

**Tip:** start the hack only when you're ready to fight the heavies, since the timer + global marker invites both the Chinook drop and human contesters. Bring an [[M249]]/[[Assault Rifle]], a shotgun for close heavies, and plenty of meds. Use doorways and the helipad railings as cover; heavies hit hard and the flamethrower denies space.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- **Monument loot reshuffle (late 2025/2026):** Oil Rig loot tables were part of the first big monument loot rework in 5+ years — exact crate contents shifted, but the structure (scientists → hack → Chinook heavies → locked crate) is intact.
- **Oil Rig flooding:** since an update, the rig **floods with radiation ~30 minutes after the crate is hacked** on some configurations — don't camp the rig indefinitely after looting.
- Heavy-scientist HP/headshot values (~300 HP, 5 headshots) are current.
- [[Green Keycard]] still gates the Small Rig L3 rooms.

## Related

- [[Chinook CH-47]] — drops the heavy scientists here
- [[Locked Crate]] — the hackable crate on the top level
- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — blue + heavy scientist stats
- [[Green Keycard]] — Small Rig puzzle
- [[Cargo Ship]], [[Deep Sea Event]] — other naval loot runs

pages.title: Patrol Helicopter
pages.body:
# Patrol Helicopter

The **Patrol Helicopter** (the "heli") is a roaming AI attack helicopter that spawns periodically and patrols monuments, machine-gunning and rocketing any player it considers a threat. Killing it drops some of the best non-explosive-gated loot in the game, and unlike [[Bradley APC]] you do **not** need explosives — a rifle and enough ammo will do it. This makes the heli one of the best early-to-mid wipe plays for a solo/duo.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body HP | **10,000** (verified) |
| Main (top) rotor HP | **900** (verified) |
| Tail rotor HP | **500** (verified) |
| Spawn frequency | Every **2–4 hours** (server default, verified Corrosion Hour) |
| Aggro drop (no line of sight) | Loses interest after ~**30 seconds** |
| Crash loot | **4 crates** = **1 Heli Crate (elite tier)** + **3 Heli Weapon Crates**, in burning gibs |

## How it picks targets (aggro)

The heli will engage you if you are "geared" — broadly, wearing **more than two clothing/armor pieces** or carrying a weapon more advanced than a bow. Naked-ish players with primitive tools are often ignored. Once it has a target it will:

- Strafe with twin door-gunner **machine guns** (sustained, accurate at range).
- Fire **rockets** that leave burning **napalm** on the ground — do not stand in the fire, it stacks damage fast and ignites wooden bases.
- Orbit and retreat to line up rocket runs.

Break line of sight (around a wall, into a building) and it deaggros after ~30 seconds. Use that to peek-shoot-hide.

## How to take it down

**The fast way — kill the rotors.** If you destroy **both** the top rotor (900 HP) and the tail rotor (500 HP), the heli crashes regardless of remaining body HP. That's only ~1,400 effective HP vs. 10,000 for the body, so always shoot rotors, not the hull.

- Best target order: **tail rotor first** (it's the smaller, easier pool and the heli flies erratically once it's gone), then the top rotor.
- The body-only method takes **200+ assault rifle rounds** — avoid unless you can't hit the rotors.

**Recommended loadout (solo/duo):**

| Weapon | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| **[[Assault Rifle]]** / [[LR-300]] + lots of 5.56 | Bread-and-butter. Bring 300+ rounds, focus rotors during strafe runs. |
| **[[Bolt Action Rifle]] / [[L96]]** + HV ammo | Long-range rotor pecking; great for the opening to draw aggro safely. |
| **[[Rocket]]s** | A few rockets to the rotors ends it fast, but you usually want those for [[Bradley APC]]/raids. |
| **[[Minigun]]** (heli/Bradley drop) | If you already have one, it shreds rotors. |

**Tactic:** fight near a monument with cover. Peek during its machine-gun strafe (when it's committed and predictable), dump into a rotor, then duck before the rocket run. Never fight it in the open. Keep medical supplies up — door-gun damage is high.

## Crash loot

On death the heli explodes into **4 crates** in burning gibs — **1 Heli Crate (elite tier, guaranteed top-tier weapon)** plus **3 Heli Weapon Crates** — that you cannot loot until the fire dies down (~couple minutes). Contents are high-tier: assault rifles, [[LR-300]], explosives ([[C4]], rockets), components, and a chance at the **[[Minigun]]** / **Military Flamethrower** (heli + Bradley are the only sources). The wreckage also leaves **scrap metal / high quality metal** to harvest.

> Warning: the burning gibs spread fire — clear the napalm before standing on them, and watch for third parties drawn by the gunfire and smoke.

## Returning-player notes (2023 → 2026)

- The heli's core stats (10,000 body / 900 top / 500 tail) are unchanged.
- **[[Homing Missile Launcher]]** exists now as a dedicated anti-air counter to both the heli and the new [[Attack Helicopter]] (the player-flown one bought at [[Bandit Camp]]).
- Note the name collision: **Patrol Helicopter** = the AI event heli (this page). **Attack Helicopter** = the player-pilotable vehicle added Sep 2023 (2,250 scrap, [[Bandit Camp]]).
- Gunshots are now audible by class at 400/500/600m (Sep 2025), so expect company when you start shooting the heli.

## Related

- [[Bradley APC]] — the other big AI loot piÃ±ata (explosive-only)
- [[Locked Crate]] — comparable loot tier
- [[Minigun]], [[Military Flamethrower]] — exclusive heli/Bradley drops
- [[NPCs & Scientists]], [[Animals]]

pages.title: Rust Events & PvE
pages.body:
# Rust Events & PvE

The roaming/spawning events and NPC-driven PvE content in Rust. These are the recurring "contestable" objectives that drive map movement and PvP — most players win wipes by controlling who gets the loot from these, not by farming nodes.

This folder covers the world events ([[Cargo Ship]], [[Patrol Helicopter]], [[Bradley APC]], [[Chinook CH-47]], [[Airdrop]], [[Oil Rig]], [[Giant Excavator]], [[Deep Sea Event]]) and the PvE actors ([[NPCs & Scientists]], [[Animals]], [[Missions]]).

## What to contest at each hour of wipe

A rough cadence for a solo/duo/trio on a force-wipe Thursday. Times are real-world after a fresh wipe; adjust for pop.

| Wipe hour | What's live / worth doing | Why |
|-----------|---------------------------|-----|
| **0:00–1:00** | Roads + [[Missions]] (Stables/Outpost), low monuments (Mining Outpost, Gas Station, Supermarket) | Build a base, get scrap + first WB. No heli/Bradley yet on most servers. |
| **1:00–2:00** | Recyclers, [[Junkyard]] heli shredding, green/blue card monuments. First [[Patrol Helicopter]] may spawn (every 2–4h). | Convert components to scrap, hunt **Blueprint Fragments** for WB2/WB3 (Meta Shift, Oct 2025). |
| **2:00–4:00** | [[Small Oil Rig]] (15 scientists), [[Cargo Ship]] when it spawns (every 2–4 in-game days), first [[Airdrop]]s. | Mid-tier guns + components. Oil Rig green-card loot. |
| **4:00–8:00** | [[Large Oil Rig]] (23 scientists), [[Bradley APC]] at [[Launch Site]] (needs explosives by now), [[Chinook CH-47]] locked crates. | Tier-3 gear, elite crates, [[Locked Crate]] hacks. |
| **8:00+** | [[Deep Sea Event]] (Feb 2026, needs a built boat), Nuclear Missile Silo (RED card), contest geared teams. | Endgame loot, [[Workbench Augmentation]] chase items. |

**General rule:** the heli and Bradley are the two events you can deny to the whole server if you have explosives — killing them and taking the crates is one of the highest scrap-per-minute plays once you can afford the rockets.

## Event quick-reference

| Event | Trigger | Key cost / requirement | Top reward |
|-------|---------|------------------------|------------|
| [[Patrol Helicopter]] | Auto, every 2–4h | A rifle + ammo (no explosives needed) | 4 [[Locked Crate]]-tier gibs of high-tier loot |
| [[Bradley APC]] | Patrols [[Launch Site]] | 7 HV rockets / 3 C4 (explosive-only) | 3 APC crates (military gear) |
| [[Cargo Ship]] | Every 2–4 in-game days | A boat / RHIB to board | 3 [[Locked Crate]]s + ship loot, 10-min respawn x3 |
| [[Chinook CH-47]] | Random, drops [[Locked Crate]] | 15-min hack | 1 [[Locked Crate]] (elite gear) |
| [[Airdrop]] | Server timer or [[Supply Signal]] | None (or 1 signal) | Guns, C4, components, armor |
| [[Small Oil Rig]] | Hack crate on L4 | Green card + a gun for heavies | Heavy scientist loot + locked crate |
| [[Large Oil Rig]] | Hack crate on L6 | Green card + serious firepower | 10 heavies, locked crate, elite crates |
| [[Giant Excavator]] | Feed diesel | Diesel fuel (Dome/Junkyard) | 5000 stone / 1000 ore / 50 HQM per diesel |
| [[Deep Sea Event]] | Opens 1 dir per wipe, 3h windows | A **built boat** or PT boat (no RHIB) | Ghost Ship elite crates, floating city |

## Pages in this folder

- [[Cargo Ship]] — roaming sea monument, docks at harbors, 3 locked crates
- [[Patrol Helicopter]] — the heli; 10,000 HP, rotor weak points, takeable solo
- [[Bradley APC]] — Launch Site tank; explosive-only, 7 HV rockets
- [[Chinook CH-47]] — drops a single locked crate at monuments
- [[Airdrop]] — supply drops via signal or server timer
- [[Oil Rig]] — small + large rig events, heavy scientists, locked crate
- [[Giant Excavator]] — diesel-powered mass resource event
- [[Deep Sea Event]] — Feb 2026 offshore event zone (Ghost Ships, Floating City)
- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — scientist tiers, tunnel/underwater dwellers, HP + aggro
- [[Animals]] — wildlife HP/damage/loot incl. jungle predators
- [[Missions]] — NPC quests at safe zones for scrap

## Seasonal events (calendar-driven holiday events)

These run every year for a ~2-week window around the holiday and end at the monthly force-wipe. They add event-only loot, NPCs, and a hunt-scoreboard mini-game.

- [[Seasonal Events]] — overview + shared event pattern (hunt -> scoreboard -> collect-10-to-upgrade ladder) and console toggles
- [[Halloween Event]] — scarecrows/mummies (200 HP), candy hunt, loot bags, Frankenstein pets, portal dungeons (~Oct 23 -> Nov wipe)
- [[Christmas Event]] — jingle-bell presents, stockings, Santa sleigh airdrops, snowball weapons, gingerbread houses (~Dec 16 -> Jan wipe)
- [[Easter Event]] — egg hunt, colored-egg upgrade ladder, bunny cosmetics (~Apr 10 -> Apr wipe)

## Related

- Monuments: [[Launch Site]], [[Junkyard]], [[The Dome]], [[Harbor]]
- Keycards: [[Green Keycard]], [[Blue Keycard]], [[Red Keycard]]
- Raiding: [[Raid Costs]], [[Rocket]], [[C4]]

pages.title: Seasonal Events
pages.body:
# Seasonal Events

Rust runs three recurring **real-world holiday events** every year. Unlike the roaming PvE events ([[Patrol Helicopter]], [[Cargo Ship]], [[Bradley APC]]), these are **calendar-driven**: Facepunch turns them on for a 2-week window around the holiday, they auto-end at the next monthly force-wipe, and they layer extra mechanics, NPCs, and **event-only loot** on top of whatever else is happening on the server. A returning player WILL log in during one and wonder why there are scarecrows / presents / eggs everywhere.

The three events:

| Event | Page | Typical window | Signature mechanic | Marquee loot |
|-------|------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| **Halloween** | [[Halloween Event]] | ~Oct 23 → Nov force-wipe | Trick-or-treat candy hunt + roaming scarecrows/mummies + portals | Loot bags (up to M249), Frankenstein pets, masks |
| **Christmas** ("Rustmas" / "Seasons Beatings") | [[Christmas Event]] | ~Dec 16 → Jan force-wipe | Jingle-bells present spawn + stockings + Santa sleigh airdrops | Snowball Launcher, Candy Cane Club, large presents (C4-tier) |
| **Easter** | [[Easter Event]] | ~Apr 10 → Apr force-wipe | Egg hunt + colored-egg upgrade ladder | Loot eggs (up to M249), bunny cosmetics, egg basket |

## How they all work (shared pattern)

All three events follow the **same skeleton** — once you understand one you understand all three:

1. **A collectible spawns around every player** on a timer (candy / presents / eggs).
2. **A timed "hunt" mini-game** fires roughly **once every other in-game day**, announced by themed music. You get **3 minutes** to grab as many collectibles as possible.
3. **A server scoreboard** ranks every player by how much they collected; the **top 3** get prize loot at the end of the hunt.
4. **A collect-10-to-upgrade ladder** lets non-winners convert raw collectibles into better loot tiers (e.g. 10 candy → small loot bag → medium → large; 10 painted eggs → bronze → silver → gold).
5. **A "vision" cosmetic + a "fast pickup" cosmetic** give a competitive edge in the hunt (Pumpkin Basket / Egg Basket = instant pickup; Scarecrow Wrap / Bunny Onesie = see extra collectibles).
6. **Free cosmetics** drop from event NPCs/collectibles; **paid cosmetics** appear in the Steam Item Store for the duration.

The key insight for a returning solo/duo/trio: **the loot is genuinely good** (large presents and 1st-place hunt bags can contain C4, rockets, and an M249), and **the hunt is contestable PvP** — geared players camp the candy/egg spawns around enemy bases. Treat the hunt like a mini [[Airdrop]].

## Console toggles

Server owners (and your own listen/local server) control these. Useful to know they exist:

| Command | Event | Effect |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `halloween.enabled true/false` | Halloween | Turn the event on/off |
| `xmas.enabled true/false` | Christmas | Turn the event on/off |
| `xmas.refill` | Christmas | Manually trigger a present spawn / stocking refill |
| `xmas.giftsperplayer 2` | Christmas | Gifts spawned per player (default 2) |
| `xmas.spawnrange 50` | Christmas | Spawn radius around each player, meters (default 50) |
| `halloweendungeon.population` | Halloween | Spawn rate of the Halloween portals/dungeons |

(Easter shares the same general convar style; there is no live event running to confirm exact Easter convar names — see gaps.)

## Pages in this folder (seasonal)

- [[Halloween Event]] — scarecrows, mummies, candy hunt, Frankenstein pets, portals, masks
- [[Christmas Event]] — presents, stockings, Santa sleigh, snowball weapons, gingerbread houses
- [[Easter Event]] — egg hunt, colored-egg upgrade ladder, bunny cosmetics

## Related

- [[Rust Events & PvE]] — the non-seasonal roaming events index
- [[Airdrop]] — the closest year-round analog to the hunt-scoreboard loot drops
- [[Force Wipe]] — seasonal events always end at the monthly force-wipe

pages.title: Animal Yields
pages.body:
# Animal Yields

The master harvest table — exactly what each animal drops when skinned with a good cutting tool ([[Bone Knife]] or better). Numbers are ranges because harvest amounts roll within a band; bigger/rarer animals give more. Values verified against rusthelp.com (current "Built Different" patch era). For tool efficiency see [[Harvest Tools]]; for the threat side see [[Animals]].

## Full harvest table (land animals)

| Animal | HP | Animal Fat | Leather | Bone Fragments | Cloth | Raw Meat |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Chicken** | 20-25 | tiny/none | none | 6-12 | 3-6 | Chicken Breast |
| **Boar** | 150 | 19-40 | 10-20 | 23-50 | 5-10 | Raw Pork |
| **Stag / Deer** | 150 | 5-10 | 24-50 | 24-50 | 12-25 | Raw Deer Meat |
| **Wolf** | 100-150 | 5-10 | 35-75 | 19-40 | 16-35 | Raw Wolf Meat |
| **Horse** | 200 | 5-10 | 24-50 | 24-50 | 12-25 | Horse Meat |
| **Bear (brown)** | ~400 | 46-100 | 46-100 | 69-150 | 23-50 | 10-20 Raw Bear Meat |
| **Polar Bear** | 420 | 55-120 | 58-125 | 78-170 | 23-50 | 10-22 Raw Bear Meat |
| **Tiger** (jungle) | high | 46-100 | 32-70 | 69-150 | 32-70 | high |
| **Panther** (jungle) | high | 46-100 | 46-100 | 69-150 | 23-50 | high |
| **Crocodile** (jungle) | high | 55-120 | 78-170 | 78-170 | 14-30 | Croc meat |
| **Snake** (jungle) | low | 5-10 | none | none | none | 5 Raw Snake Meat (+4 Snake Venom) |
| **Shark** (ocean) | 148-150 | 19-40 | 19-40 | 23-50 | 10-20 | Raw Fish |

> Tiger/Panther/Croc HP and meat counts aren't published as clean single numbers — they're among the deadliest, tankiest animals in the game ([[Animals]]). Their *resource* drops above are verified; treat them as the richest land harvest if you can kill them.

## Reading the table — the practical takeaways

- **Best fat per kill:** Crocodile and Polar Bear (55-120), then Bear/Tiger/Panther (46-100). Bears are the realistic top fat source for most players.
- **Best leather per kill:** Crocodile (78-170), Polar Bear (58-125), Bear/Panther (46-100). Boar is the *worst* leather animal (10-20) despite being a fat staple.
- **Best bone per kill:** Crocodile & Polar Bear (78-170), then Bear/Tiger/Panther (69-150). You rarely need to farm bone — one bear oversupplies your tool needs.
- **Best cloth per kill:** Tiger (32-70), then the bears (23-50). But cloth from animals is incidental — for *volume* cloth, farm [[Hemp]] (10/plant, scalable).
- **Safest early farm:** Boars and stags (both 150 HP, low threat). A boar = fat + bone; a stag = leather + bone. Mix them and you cover all four staples without touching a bear.

## Fish & aquatic fat (bonus source)

Caught fish ([[Fishing]]) and gutted aquatic animals also drop **animal fat**, handy if you live coastal:

| Fish | Animal Fat |
|---|---|
| Small Shark | 20 |
| Catfish / Orange Roughy | 18 |
| Salmon | 16 |
| Yellow Perch | 9 |
| Small Trout | 8 |
| Sardine | 5 |
| Anchovy / Herring | 1 |

Catfish, Orange Roughy, Salmon, and Small Shark also drop ~8 cloth (20% chance). Gut fish with a [[Bone Knife]] at a [[Fishing Village]] — see [[Fishing]].

## Other ways to get these resources (non-hunting)

- **Recycling** ([[Recycling]]): low grade fuel recycles *back* into animal fat; many decorative/cloth items recycle into cloth.
- **Barrels & crates** ([[Barrels and Crates]]): cloth, leather, and low grade fuel show up as loot.
- **[[Hemp]]:** the only *farmable* cloth (10/plant).
- **[[Chicken Coops]]:** farmed chicken meat + eggs without hunting.

## Related

- [[Hunting & Harvesting]] — the overview / how-to
- [[Harvest Tools]] — which tool maximizes these numbers
- [[Low Grade Fuel]] — what the fat turns into
- [[Raw Meat and Food Values]] — the food side of the meat column
- [[Animals]] — HP, aggro, and jungle predator AI

pages.title: Berries & Crops
pages.body:
# Berries & Crops

What you actually plant. Berries are the fuel for the entire [[Teas]] economy; hemp is your cloth supply; corn/potato/pumpkin/wheat are food; mushrooms are foraged filler. All can be grown in [[Farming Basics|planters]] and improved with [[Plant Genetics]].

## Berries — the six colors

Berries are foraged from wild bushes (each bush picked gives **1 berry + 1 seed**) and then farmed. Every berry color feeds specific [[Teas]] recipes:

| Berry | Feeds these teas |
|-------|------------------|
| **Red** | Healing Tea, Max Health Tea, Anti-Rad Tea, Wood Tea, Warming/Cooling Tea |
| **Blue** | Wood Tea, Ore Tea |
| **Yellow** | Ore Tea, **Scrap Tea**, Max Health Tea, Warming/Cooling Tea |
| **White** | **Scrap Tea** |
| **Green** | Anti-Rad Tea |
| **Black** | minor / niche recipes |

**For the meta:** the [[Pure Scrap Tea]] loop runs on **Yellow + White** berries — prioritize farming those two colors. A Pure Scrap Tea costs 32 Yellow + 32 White berries, so high-**Y (Yield)** genes pay off fast (see [[Plant Genetics]]).

## Hemp → Cloth

The most important non-food crop. Hemp yields **cloth**, which you need constantly for sleeping bags, bandages, clothing, sewing kits, [[Backpacks]], and more.

- Yields **3 clones** per cloning (like berries), so a god-seed hemp clone stash scales fast.
- A modest indoor hemp farm makes a solo fully cloth-independent — no more scavenging.

## Wheat (Cooking Update)

Added with the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Update]] (Mar 2025). Grown like other crops; used to bake **Bread** and several **pies** at the Cooking Workbench. Bread also feeds horses to boost their dung output for the [[Composter]].

## Food crops — values

(Values are restored-on-eat. Health is regen-over-time, not instant.)

| Crop | Calories (hunger) | Hydration | Health | Yield/plant | Notes |
|------|------------------|-----------|--------|-------------|-------|
| **Pumpkin** | +80 | +30 | +8 HP | 1 per plant | Best all-round food: highest hydration + heal |
| **Corn** | +75 | +10 | +6 HP | 1 per plant | Solid, low hydration |
| **Potato** | +125 | +5 | +6 HP | high quantity | Most calories, almost no hydration — feed a group but keep water handy |
| **Mushroom** | low | low | low | foraged | Early-game filler, not farmed seriously |

All food crops **spoil after 48h** (raw) under the food-spoilage system — store in a powered fridge to pause the timer. See [[Cooking & Food]].

Food crops give **2 clones** per cloning (vs 3 for berries/hemp).

## Growth notes

- Plants progress Seedling → Sapling → Crossbreed → Mature → Fruiting → Ripe → Dying. A baseline pumpkin with no Growth genes takes **~1h54m** seed-to-ripe; **G (Growth) genes** shorten this — see [[Plant Genetics]].
- Take **clones at the Sapling stage** to propagate good genes.
- Keep all four soil stats (water/light/soil/temp) high or the plant caps at the lowest — see [[Farming Basics]].

## What to grow first (returning solo)

1. **Hemp** — cloth independence, day one.
2. **Yellow + White berries** — fuel for [[Pure Scrap Tea]].
3. **Red/Blue/Green/Yellow berries** — round out the [[Teas]] catalog.
4. **Pumpkins** — self-sufficient food (best hydration).
5. **Wheat** — only once you've built the Cooking Workbench for pies/bread.

pages.title: Composter
pages.body:
# Composter

The deployable that turns organic waste into **Fertilizer**, which raises the **Soil Quality** stat in your [[Farming Basics|planters]]. One composter keeps a multi-planter farm topped up. Pairs naturally with a horse for dung.

## Stats & acquisition

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Craft cost** | 200 wood + 2 Tarp |
| **Buy at** | [[Bandit Camp]] for **30 scrap** |
| **Craft time** | 30s with no bench, ~7s at [[Workbench Level 3]] |

## What to put in it (conversion ratios)

| Input | Fertilizer per item |
|-------|---------------------|
| **Horse Dung** | **5** (by far the best — the only input yielding whole units) |
| Small Trout / fish | ~0.8 |
| Vegetables, meat, cooked meat, human flesh, refined food | ~0.2-0.3 each |

Rule of thumb: ~**4-6 generic organic items = 1 fertilizer**, but **1 horse dung = 5 fertilizer**. Just chuck in anything organic. **Don't compost berries** — brew them into [[Teas]] instead, they're far more valuable.

## Horse dung pipeline (the efficient way)

1. Keep a **horse** in a small 1x2 stable next to the farm.
2. One horse produces **~8-12 dung/hour**.
3. Feeding the horse **bread** (baked from [[Berries & Crops|wheat]] at the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]]) increases dung output.
4. Each dung → 5 fertilizer in the composter. A single horse easily fertilizes a multi-planter farm.

## Using fertilizer

Add **1 fertilizer per planted seed** to push that planter's **Soil Quality** toward 100%. Remember soil health is capped at the **lowest** of the four stats (water/sunlight/soil quality/temperature), so fertilizer only helps if your water/light/temp are also high — see [[Farming Basics]].

pages.title: Cooking & Food
pages.body:
# Cooking & Food

Food keeps your **Calories (hunger)** and **Hydration (thirst)** bars up; let either hit zero and you take damage. The big returning-player change is the **Cooking Update / Cooking 2.0 (Mar 2025)**: a new Cooking Workbench, 8 buff **pies**, **food spoilage**, **chicken coops**, **bees + bee grenades**, and **armor insert slots**. This page covers food values, cooking stations, and all the new systems. For raw crops see [[Berries & Crops]]; for tea brewing see [[Teas]].

## Food & hydration values

(Health is regen-over-time on most foods, not instant.)

| Food | Calories | Hydration | Health | Notes |
|------|----------|-----------|--------|-------|
| **Pumpkin** | +80 | +30 | +8 HP | Best all-round — top hydration + heal |
| **Corn** | +75 | +10 | +6 HP | Low hydration |
| **Potato** | +125 | +5 | +6 HP | Most calories, almost no water |
| Cooked meat (most) | high | low | over time | Cook raw meat to remove food poisoning risk |
| Raw meat | low | low | risk of poisoning | Always cook it |
| Berries | low | small | small | Better brewed into [[Teas]] |
| Mushroom | low | low | low | Foraged filler |

Cooking food adds roughly **+20% calories** vs raw, and removes the sickness chance of raw meat.

## Cooking stations

| Station | Use |
|---------|-----|
| **Campfire** | Earliest cook — meat, potatoes, etc. Also a light/heat source |
| **BBQ (Barbeque)** | More cook slots than a campfire; standard mid-game cooker |
| **Cooking Workbench** | The Cooking-Update station: combines **Mixing Table + BBQ + a crafting bench** into one. Cooks food, brews [[Teas]], and bakes pies/bread |

The **Cooking Workbench** is the upgrade target — it does everything the [[Mixing Table]] and BBQ do, plus pies and bread. Food cooks in **real time** with a visible model on the station.

## The 8 pies (Cooking Update buffs)

Pies are baked at the Cooking Workbench from crops + ingredients ([[Berries & Crops|wheat]] for the crust). Each grants a timed buff:

| Pie | Buff | Duration |
|-----|------|----------|
| **Apple Pie** | +100% night vision (see node sparkles / tree X's in the dark) | ~2 min |
| **Bear Pie** | **Doubles [[Teas|tea]] effects** but halves their duration | — |
| **Chicken Pie** | +5% better crop yield chance when planting | ~4 min |
| **Fish Pie** | +50% fishing strength (faster reel, less rod breakage) | ~5 min |
| **Hunter's Pie** | Reduces bleeding + restores health | ~15 min |
| **Pork Pie** | +200% metabolism — ~3x stronger healing-over-time | ~5 min |
| **Pumpkin Pie** | Boosts hunger, health, hydration, **and max health** | ~10 min |
| **Survivor's Pie** | +50% yield harvesting any corpse (wild or human) | ~5 min |

**Meta picks:** **Bear Pie** before drinking a [[Pure Scrap Tea]] (doubles the +350% — though for half duration), **Survivor's Pie** on hunting runs (stacks with [[Harvesting Tea]]), **Pork Pie** for a fast post-fight heal, **Pumpkin Pie** as a general top-everything food.

## Food spoilage (Cooking Update)

Food now rots. Spoiled food **poisons you** if eaten.

| Item | Spoil time |
|------|-----------|
| Raw meat | ~6 hours |
| Cooked meat | ~24 hours |
| Crops (pumpkin/corn/potato) | ~48 hours |

**Pause spoilage** by storing food in a **powered Electric Fridge** (needs 1 [[electricity|power]]) — the timer freezes while refrigerated. The **Mini Fridge** holds 18 slots.

## Bees & bee grenades

- **Beehives** (Beehive Nucleus) generate **honey** over time near flowers.
- **Bee Grenade** — thrown weapon crafted from a Beehive Nucleus; releases a swarm of bees on impact (area denial / annoyance utility).

## Chicken coops

- Each coop holds up to **4 chickens**.
- Chickens need four things kept up: **hunger, thirst, sunlight, and love (petting)**.
- Healthy chickens produce eggs + meat — a renewable on-base protein source.

## Armor insert slots

Crafted armor now has **0-3 insert slots**. Inserts add protection in four types: **Heat, Radiation, Projectile, and Melee/Bite**. This lets you tune crafted gear for a specific monument (e.g. radiation inserts for an oil rig run — pair with [[Anti-Rad Tea]]).

## Practical food plan (solo)

1. Early: campfire + cooked meat + foraged berries/mushrooms.
2. Mid: indoor **pumpkin** patch ([[Farming Basics]]) for self-sufficient food + water.
3. Build a **Cooking Workbench** → bake **Pumpkin/Pork/Survivor's pies** for buffs.
4. Add an **Electric Fridge** to stockpile cooked meat without spoilage.

## What changed since 2023 (this domain)

| Change | When |

pages.title: Farming Basics
pages.body:
# Farming Basics

Everything you need to stand up a working indoor farm: planters, light, water, fertilizer, and soil stats. Get this right and the farm runs itself with one daily water/fertilizer top-up. For the gene min-maxing layer, see [[Plant Genetics]]; for what to grow, see [[Berries & Crops]].

## The four soil stats (the core mechanic)

Every planted spot tracks four conditions, each a percentage. **Plant health is capped at the LOWEST of the four** — a perfect 100% on three stats is wasted if the fourth is at 20%. Manage all four:

| Stat | Driven by | How to max it |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| **Water (Ground Moisture)** | Watering / sprinklers | Keep the planter saturated; sprinklers automate it |
| **Sunlight (Light)** | Sun or [[Ceiling Light]]s | Place ceiling lights directly above indoor planters |
| **Soil Quality** | Fertilizer | Add fertilizer to push soil quality toward 100% |
| **Temperature** | Ambient + lights | Lights add heat; cold biomes need extra heat sources |

## Planter Boxes

The deployable you grow in. Two sizes:

| Planter | Plant slots | Notes |
|---------|-------------|-------|
| **Small Planter Box** | 1 | Cheap starter; not for serious farms |
| **Large Planter Box** | up to 9 (a 3x3 grid) | The standard. The 3x3 grid is exactly what [[Plant Genetics|crossbreeding]] needs |

**Critical rule:** planter boxes do **NOT** cross-pollinate with each other. What you plant in planter box #1 cannot affect plants in planter box #2, regardless of how close they are. All crossbreeding happens *within* one Large Planter Box's 9 slots. See [[Plant Genetics]].

## Lighting

Indoors you must supply light or plants grow at a crawl.

- **[[Ceiling Light]]** — the go-to grow light. Mount it on the ceiling directly above a planter; one light covers a Large Planter Box. Requires a small amount of [[electricity]] (it's a low-power consumer).
- Lights also raise the **temperature** stat, which helps in cold biomes.
- Sunlight works outdoors but exposes the farm to raiders and the day/night cycle; serious farmers go fully indoor + electric.

## Water system

Plants drink water continuously (and **W (Water) genes** make them drink faster — see [[Plant Genetics]]). Options, from manual to automated:

| Item | Role |
|------|------|
| **Bucket / Water Jug** | Manual: scoop from a water source, click the planter to water |
| **Water Catcher (Small/Large)** | Passively collects rainwater into its tank |
| **Water Barrel** | Storage tank for water |
| **Powered Water Purifier** | Turns salt water into fresh water |
| **Water Pump** | Pulls water from a source (lake/ocean) into a hose network |
| **Hose Tool** | Connects water containers/pumps/sprinklers into a fluid network |
| **Sprinkler** | Auto-waters all planters in range — the endgame "set and forget" piece |

**Standard automated setup:** Water Pump or Water Catcher → hose → Sprinkler over the planters. With sprinklers running, water stays at 100% and you never hand-water. The Apr 2026 **Water Wheel** (river generator) can power this loop off flowing water — see [[Berries & Crops]] and [[electricity]].

## Fertilizer & the Composter

Fertilizer raises the **Soil Quality** stat. Add **1 fertilizer per planted seed** to push that planter toward 100%.

You make fertilizer in the **[[Composter]]**:

- **Craft cost:** 200 wood + 2 Tarp. Or buy from [[Bandit Camp]] for **30 scrap**.
- **Best input by far: Horse Dung** — each piece yields **5 fertilizer**. Keep a horse near the farm; one horse makes ~8-12 dung/hour, and feeding it bread (from the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Update]]) increases dung output.
- Other organics (vegetables, meat, cooked meat, human flesh, fish) break down at ~0.2-0.3 fertilizer each — roughly 4-6 items per 1 fertilizer. Berries aren't worth composting (brew them into [[Teas]] instead).

## Minimum viable indoor farm (solo)

1. 1x Large Planter Box (9 slots).
2. 1x Ceiling Light directly above it (wired to a small [[electricity]] source).
3. 1x Sprinkler fed by a Water Catcher or Pump.
4. 1x [[Composter]] + a horse (or just toss in spare food) for fertilizer.
5. Plant 9 cloned hemp/berries with good genes from [[Plant Genetics]].

That single planter quietly produces cloth and berries forever. Scale by adding more Large Planter Boxes once your genetics are dialed in.

## Growth stages

Seeds progress through stages (roughly): Seedling → Sapling → Crossbreed → Mature → Fruiting → Ripe → Dying. Two stages matter most for genetics:

- **Sapling stage** — the window to take **clones** (2 clones from food crops, 3 from berries/hemp).
- **Crossbreed stage (~2 min)** — when a plant's genes are recalculated from its neighbors.

Full details and the cloning workflow are in [[Plant Genetics]].

pages.title: Farming Meta & Loops
pages.body:
# Farming Meta & Loops

The strategy layer for the farming/food domain — what's actually worth your time as a returning solo/duo/trio, and the best repeatable loops. For the page directory see the folder [[Farming & Food (Rust)|index]]; this page is opinions and routes, not a catalog.

## The one loop that matters: scrap tea

The **scrap-tea loop** is the highest-leverage thing in this whole domain:

1. Grow **Yellow + White** [[Berries & Crops|berries]] in a [[Plant Genetics|genetics-optimized]] Large Planter Box (high Y for berry quantity).
2. Brew up the tree at a [[Mixing Table]]: 16 Basic → 4 Advanced → 1 [[Pure Scrap Tea]] (32 Yellow + 32 White berries per Pure).
3. Drink **[[Pure Scrap Tea]] (+350% barrel scrap, 1h)** before a barrel/road run.
4. Barrels drop ~8-9 scrap instead of ~2. Reported **2000+ scrap/hour** early wipe on a good route.

**The trap everyone hits:** scrap tea multiplies **barrel scrap only** — not crates, not recyclers, not vendor/fishing/gambling income. Time it for barrels.

## Priority order for a returning solo

| Priority | Build | Payoff |
|----------|-------|--------|
| 1 | Hemp farm | Cloth independence day one (bags, bandages, [[Backpacks]]) |
| 2 | Yellow+White berry farm + [[Mixing Table]] | [[Pure Scrap Tea]] scrap engine |
| 3 | Full berry rainbow | All [[Teas]] (Wood/Ore for gathering, Healing/Max Health for fights) |
| 4 | Pumpkin patch | Self-sufficient food + water, no risky food runs |
| 5 | [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]] + wheat | Buff pies (Bear/Survivor's/Pork/Pumpkin) |

## Best supporting buffs

- **Wood/Ore Tea** before a build or sulfur stockpile — biggest time saver while farming nodes.
- **Bear Pie + Pure Scrap Tea** — Bear Pie doubles tea effect (half duration), so the scrap multiplier spikes for a fast barrel blitz.
- **Survivor's Pie + [[Harvesting Tea]]** — stack on hunting runs for big meat/fat hauls.
- **Pure Healing + Pure Max Health Tea** — cheap pre-fight stack (120 effective HP + big instant heal).
- **Anti-Rad Tea** — required for [[Launch Site]] / oil rig deep runs; pair with radiation armor inserts.

## Other income loops (ranked vs scrap tea)

| Loop | Verdict |
|------|---------|
| **[[Pure Scrap Tea]] barrel run** | Best renewable scrap multiplier — the meta |
| **[[Fishing]] for fuel** | Good low-risk **fuel** (animal fat → low grade), mediocre scrap |
| **[[Gambling|Bandit wheel]]** | Negative EV (~4% house edge) — entertainment, not income |
| **Composting for food** | Sustains the base but isn't income; use [[Composter]] + a horse |

## What changed since 2023 (quick reference)

- **Cooking Update (Mar 2025):** Cooking Workbench, 8 buff pies, food spoilage (raw 6h / cooked 24h / produce 48h, fridges pause it), chicken coops, bees + bee grenades, armor insert slots, wheat/bread.
- **Apr 2026:** Water Wheel river generator + **overfishing** depletion mechanic.
- **Teas rebalanced** stronger than 2023 — Pure Scrap is now **+350% / 60 min**.

See the folder [[Farming & Food (Rust)|index]] for the full page list.

pages.title: Fishing
pages.body:
# Fishing

A low-risk side income and food source. You cast a rod with **bait**, play the reel mini-game, and gut fish into raw meat, **animal fat (→ low-grade fuel)**, bone, and sometimes scrap/loot — or sell whole fish at a [[Fishing Village]] vendor. Fish Pie (+50% fishing strength, see [[Cooking & Food]]) makes it faster. As of Apr 2026, watch for **overfishing** depleting a spot.

## Fishing Villages & gear

[[Fishing Village]] monuments (Small + Large) are safe-zone vendor hubs on the coast. They sell fishing gear and have a recycler.

| Gear | Cost |
|------|------|
| **Handmade Fishing Rod** | 80 scrap at the village shop, **or** craft 200 wood + 2 Rope |
| **Worms (bait)** | 50 scrap for 5 |

There's also a **Survival Fishing Rod** (lower quality, often a tutorial/early item) — the Handmade Rod is the standard.

## Bait & bait ratings (1-10)

Bait determines what you can catch — bigger fish need higher-rated bait. Since Jun 2024, you can **stack multiple baits** to raise the effective rating (consumes faster).

| Bait rating | Bait items | Catches |
|-------------|-----------|---------|
| **1** | Berries, corn, potatoes | tiny fish only |
| **3-4** | Worms, grubs | small fish, perch |
| **5** | Raw meats, small trout, yellow perch | mid fish |
| **10** | Catfish, salmon, orange roughy, small shark | the big, valuable fish |

So you bootstrap: catch small fish on worms → use those small fish as higher-rated bait → catch sharks/roughy.

## Fish species

| Fish | Where | Value note |
|------|-------|-----------|
| Anchovy / Sardine / Herring | "small fish" — everywhere | low value, used as bait |
| Yellow Perch | rivers/swamps | mid |
| Catfish | rivers/swamps | mid-high, bait rating 10 |
| Small Trout | rivers/lakes | mid, also bait rating 5 |
| Salmon | ocean/rivers | high |
| Orange Roughy | ocean / moon pools | high, sells well |
| **Small Shark** | ocean / underwater | **most valuable** — sharks sell for solid scrap at the village |

~**20% of fish** also contain a misc loot item when caught.

## What fish turn into

Gutting a fish with a cutting tool yields:
- **Raw Fish Meat** (cook → food)
- **Animal Fat** → **Low Grade Fuel** (the big reason to fish — fuel for furnaces, lights, vehicles)
- **Bone Fragments**
- Sometimes **scrap** / misc loot

Higher-bait fish give more materials. You can also **sell whole fish** to village vendors for scrap (sharks/roughy are the best sellers). **Note:** scrap from selling fish is **not** boosted by [[Pure Scrap Tea]] (barrels only).

## Fish Traps (passive)

A craftable structure (default blueprint) that catches fish automatically when baited — **~50% chance per catch tick**. Good passive AFK income at a waterside base; far slower per-minute than active rodding but zero effort.

## Overfishing (Apr 2026)

The Apr 2026 update added **overfishing** alongside the **Water Wheel** river generator: fishing the same spot repeatedly **depletes it**, reducing catch rates until it recovers. Rotate fishing spots rather than camping one pier. (Exact depletion/recovery numbers not yet verified — re-check on rusthelp.com.)

## When fishing is worth it

- **Fuel-starved early/mid wipe** — animal fat → low-grade fuel is the main draw.
- **Low-risk income** at a safe-zone [[Fishing Village]] when you don't want PvP.
- Pair with **Fish Pie** ([[Cooking & Food]]) for faster reeling and less rod wear.
- For raw scrap, the [[Pure Scrap Tea]] barrel loop beats fishing — fish for fuel/food, not scrap.

pages.title: Gambling
pages.body:
# Gambling

The in-game **Wheel of Fortune** at [[Bandit Camp]] lets you bet scrap on a spinning wheel. (This page is about the *in-game* wheel — not the third-party "bandit.camp" gambling website, which is unaffiliated and not covered here.) It's a safe-zone scrap sink/multiplier with a small house edge; useful for converting a scrap surplus into a gamble, never a reliable income.

## The Wheel of Fortune

A vendor wheel inside the [[Bandit Camp]] safe zone. You place scrap on one or more **multiplier tiles**, an NPC spins, and if the wheel stops on a tile you bet, you win **bet × that multiplier** (your stake included in the payout). Place bets on a colored tile, wait for the spin, collect.

### Segment layout (25 segments)

The wheel has **25 segments** total. Verified distribution: **12 segments = 1x** and **6 segments = 3x**; one segment is **20x**. The remaining segments fill out the 5x and 10x tiles. The standard documented layout is:

| Tile (multiplier) | Segments | Probability | Payout |
|-------------------|----------|-------------|--------|
| **1x** | 12 / 25 | **48%** | 1:1 |
| **3x** | 6 / 25 | **24%** | 3:1 |
| **5x** | 4 / 25 | ~16% | 5:1 |
| **10x** | 2 / 25 | ~8% | 10:1 |
| **20x** | 1 / 25 | **4%** | 20:1 |

> The 1x (12 seg) and 3x (6 seg) counts and the single 20x are confirmed; the **5x/10x split (4/2) is the commonly-documented layout but treat as approximate** — Norton blocked the deep-source verification. The expected-value math below holds regardless of the exact 5x/10x split because the wheel is tuned to a fixed house edge.

### House edge

The wheel is tuned so the **house keeps ~1/25 (4%)** of all scrap wagered over time. Every tile has the **same expected value** (~0.96× your stake), so no single tile is "smarter" than another on EV — you trade variance, not edge:

- **Bet 1x** = win often (48%), tiny payouts, low variance — the slow bleed.
- **Bet 20x** = win rarely (4%), huge payout — high variance, "jackpot or bust."

There is no positive-EV strategy. Martingale (double-after-loss on 1x) is commonly suggested but does **not** beat the house edge and busts on a losing streak. **Over time you lose ~4% of everything you wager.**

## Practical take for solo/duo/trio

- Gambling is **entertainment / a scrap sink**, not a farm route. For real scrap, run the [[Pure Scrap Tea]] barrel loop — that's positive, gambling is negative.
- **Scrap won at the wheel is NOT boosted by [[Scrap Tea]]** (tea only multiplies barrel scrap).
- Reasonable use: you're sitting on a fat scrap surplus and want a shot at a big multiplier for a [[Attack Helicopter]] (2,250 scrap) or expensive blueprint — bet a small chunk on 5x/10x/20x and accept you'll usually lose it.
- Don't gamble scrap you need. The [[Bandit Camp]] is a safe zone, but you can be camped on the way in/out.

## Other Bandit Camp activities

Besides the wheel, [[Bandit Camp]] is the home of the [[Mixing Table]] vendor, the [[Composter]] vendor (30 scrap), the [[Attack Helicopter]] purchase (2,250 scrap), and a monument recycler — making it a natural stop on a farming/scrap loop even if you skip the wheel.

pages.title: Harvest Tools
pages.body:
# Harvest Tools

What you swing at an animal corpse determines how much it gives. Punching or shooting a dead animal yields the least; a dedicated cutting tool yields the most. This page ranks the skinning tools and covers the **[[Bone Knife]]**, the free starter tool every solo crafts first.

## Yield ranking (best to worst for skinning animals)

| Tool | Harvest yield | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Chainsaw** | Very High | Fastest/most resources; needs [[Low Grade Fuel]], loud, late-game |
| **Combat Knife** | Very High | ~15-20% more resources than a hatchet; loot/craft mid-game |
| **Salvaged Cleaver** | High | Strong melee + good harvest; common skinning choice |
| **Hatchet / Stone Hatchet** | High | What you already carry for wood; perfectly fine to skin with |
| **Bone Knife** | Low-Medium | Free starter; lower yield than a hatchet but always available |
| Bare hands / bullets | Lowest | Avoid — you waste a chunk of the animal |

**Practical rule:** early game, skin with whatever you have (a [[Stone Hatchet]] is actually a touch better than a bone knife for yield). Once you find a **Combat Knife** or craft a **Salvaged Cleaver**, switch — the ~15-20% bump on bears/crocs adds up fast. End-game bases keep a **Chainsaw** for mass harvesting.

## Bone Knife

The first tool most solos make — a melee weapon and corpse-harvester crafted entirely from animal bone, so it costs zero scrap and no workbench.

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| **Craft cost** | 30 Bone Fragments |
| **Workbench** | None required |
| **Role** | Skinning carcasses + emergency melee |
| **Harvest tier** | Low-Medium (better than fists/bullets, below hatchet) |

You get the 30 bone by punching a chicken/boar or breaking a few [[Barrels and Crates]]. The bone knife exists so a fresh spawn can immediately harvest fat and meat without finding metal for a hatchet. Upgrade off it as soon as you have a hatchet or cleaver.

## Other bone-fragment craftables

Bone is so plentiful (one bear = 69-150 fragments, see [[Animal Yields]]) that you'll craft these freely:

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| **Bone Club** | 20 Bone Fragments |
| **Bone Knife** | 30 Bone Fragments |
| **Bone Helmet** | 30 Bone + 15 Cloth |
| **Bone Armor (chest)** | 70 Bone + 15 Cloth |
| **Bone Arrow ×3** | 10 Bone + 25 Wood |
| **Xylobone** (instrument) | 50 Bone |
| **Frontier Horns Rack** (deco) | 30 Bone |

**Bone armor** is a genuinely good early-game armor set — cheap (just bone + cloth from hunting), decent protection, no scrap or research needed. A returning solo can run a full bone kit on day one purely off animals.

## Tool choice by what you're farming

- **Just need fat for [[Low Grade Fuel]]?** Any tool works — hit boars/bears, the fat rolls the same band; a better tool just gets more of it.
- **Farming leather for armor?** Use your best tool (cleaver/combat knife) on crocs/bears where leather is 46-170 per kill.
- **Mass harvesting a base of corpses?** Chainsaw if you can spare the fuel.

## Related

- [[Hunting & Harvesting]] — the overview
- [[Animal Yields]] — the numbers your tool multiplies
- [[Low Grade Fuel]] — what to do with the fat
- [[Hunting Bow]] — how you kill the animal before skinning it
- [[Animals]] — the threat side

pages.title: Hunting & Harvesting
pages.body:
# Hunting & Harvesting

The wildlife resource economy: how to turn animals into the four early-game staples — **leather, cloth, animal fat, and bone fragments** — plus the raw meat that feeds you. This is the page a returning player wants when asking *"where do I get leather / cloth / low grade fuel early?"* For animals as PvE *threats* (HP, aggro, stalking AI), see [[Animals]]; this page is the **resource** side.

Hunting is one of the few self-sufficient loops in Rust: a [[Bone Knife]] (30 bone, free to make) skins anything, and a single boar gives you fat → [[Low Grade Fuel]] for your furnace + leather for armor + bone for tools. No monument run, no scrap required.

## The harvest flow (start to finish)

1. **Get a cutting tool.** Punch a couple of animals or hit a few barrels for ~30 bone fragments → craft a [[Bone Knife]]. (You can harvest with a [[Stone Hatchet]] too, but a knife/cleaver yields more — see [[Harvest Tools]].)
2. **Kill the animal.** Early: rock/spear for chickens, **[[Hunting Bow]]** + wooden arrows for boar/stag/wolf (50 dmg/arrow), and avoid bears until you have a bow + room to kite.
3. **Hold your harvest tool and hit the corpse** until it's fully gutted (the corpse shrinks/disappears). A bear/croc may take many swings — they have huge resource pools.
4. **Refine:** fat → [[Low Grade Fuel]] in your inventory (no bench needed); meat → cook on a [[Campfire]] before eating (raw meat poisons you).

## What animals give you (the four staples)

| Resource | Best source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| **Animal Fat** | Bears, crocodiles, polar bears | [[Low Grade Fuel]] (furnace/lights/tools), [[Cooking Workbench]] recipes |
| **Leather** | Crocodiles, bears, wolves | Armor (hide → road sign → metal), gloves, shields |
| **Bone Fragments** | Crocodiles, polar bears, bears | [[Bone Knife]], bone club, **bone armor**, bone arrows |
| **Cloth** | Tigers, bears, hemp plants | Bandages, clothing, sleeping bags, low grade fuel |
| **Raw Meat** | Every animal | Food (must cook — see [[Cooking and Food]]) |

> **Returning-player note:** in current Rust, animals **do** drop cloth (a boar gives ~5-10, a bear ~23-50). Old guides that say "cloth only comes from hemp" are out of date — though [[Hemp]] (10 cloth/plant, farmable) is still the *scalable* cloth source. See [[Animal Yields]] for the full table.

## Pages in this topic

- [[Animal Yields]] — the master table: exact leather / cloth / fat / bone / meat each animal drops
- [[Harvest Tools]] — bone knife vs hatchet vs cleaver vs chainsaw; yield ranking and damage
- [[Low Grade Fuel]] — the fat → LGF pipeline solos live on, recipe + math
- [[Raw Meat and Food Values]] — calories/poison per meat type, cook-it-first rules

## Where to hunt (early routes)

- **Temperate forest near spawn** — chickens, boars, stags everywhere. Safest fat/leather farm.
- **Roadsides & fields** — horses (24-50 leather each) and stags graze in the open.
- **AVOID the jungle early** — tigers, panthers, and crocodiles give the *most* resources but are the deadliest animals in the game ([[Animals]]). Come back with a gun.
- **Arctic** — polar bears are a top-tier fat/leather/bone source if you can survive the cold.

## Related

- [[Animals]] — the threat/HP/AI side of wildlife
- [[Cooking and Food]] — turning raw meat into calories
- [[Cooking Workbench and Pies]] — fat and meat feed the pie economy
- [[Hemp]] / [[Berries and Crops]] — the farmable cloth source
- [[Chicken Coops]] — farmed chicken meat + eggs (no hunting needed)
- [[Composter and Fertilizer]] — spare/spoiled meat composts into fertilizer

pages.title: Low Grade Fuel
pages.body:
# Low Grade Fuel

The early-game energy resource. **Low Grade Fuel (LGF)** powers furnaces, lights, tool cupboards' lights, and burns in tools/weapons (chainsaw, flamethrower, fire arrows). Solos run on a steady fat → LGF pipeline before they ever have diesel or electricity. For the upgraded fuel, see [[Diesel Fuel]]; for the animals that supply the fat, see [[Animal Yields]].

## The recipe (memorize this)

```
3 Animal Fat + 1 Cloth  →  4 Low Grade Fuel
```

- Crafts **directly from your inventory** — no workbench, no research.
- Net: you spend 3 fat + 1 cloth and get **4** LGF (a small free bonus over inputs).
- Cloth is the limiter, not fat — one [[Hemp]] plant (10 cloth) crafts a lot of LGF if you have the fat.

## What burns LGF

| Use | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| **[[Furnace]] / Large Furnace** | Smelting ore into metal/HQM — the #1 early LGF sink |
| **Ceiling Light / Lantern / Tuna Light** | Indoor [[Farming Basics|farm lighting]] and base light |
| **Chainsaw** | Fast wood + best corpse harvest ([[Harvest Tools]]) |
| **Military Flamethrower / Fire Arrows** | Raiding/burning |
| **Search Light, Tool Cupboard auth lights, etc.** | Misc deployables |

## The fat → LGF pipeline (the solo lifeline)

This is the loop that keeps a solo base lit and smelting with **no scrap and no monument runs**:

1. **Hunt fat.** Boars (19-40 fat) near spawn are the easy staple; a single **bear (46-100 fat)** is a jackpot. See [[Animal Yields]] for the full fat table.
2. **Skin with a [[Bone Knife]]** (or better — [[Harvest Tools]]).
3. **Carry a little cloth** (incidental animal drops, or farm [[Hemp]]).
4. **Craft LGF in inventory** as needed: 3 fat + 1 cloth → 4 LGF.
5. **Feed the furnace.** Now you can smelt ore the moment you mine it.

**Math example:** one bear's worth of fat (say 80) + ~27 cloth → ~106 LGF, enough to run a furnace through several smelting cycles. Two or three boars do the same job and are far safer to kill.

## Other ways to get LGF

- **Crude Oil → Refinery:** a [[Small Oil Refinery]] converts Crude Oil (from oil barrels, [[Pump Jack]], [[Excavator and Quarries]]) into LGF — **1 Crude Oil = 3 Low Grade Fuel**. This is the *scalable* mid-game source once you have an oil supply.
- **Loot:** LGF spawns in [[Barrels and Crates]], oil barrels, and tunnels.
- **Recycling:** LGF recycles **back into animal fat** (and decorative items recycle into LGF) — see [[Recycling]].
- **Vendors:** buyable at some [[Bandit Camp]] / [[Outpost]] / [[Floating Cities]] shops (price floats — see [[Vending and Shops]]).

## Fat vs Crude oil — which to use

- **Day 1-3, no oil access:** hunt fat. It's free and immediate.
- **Once you have a [[Pump Jack]] or oil barrels:** Crude → LGF at 1:3 scales much better than skinning animals one at a time.
- **End-game:** LGF gives way to [[Diesel Fuel]] for the big machines ([[Excavator and Quarries]], heavy equipment).

## Related

- [[Hunting & Harvesting]] — the fat-gathering overview
- [[Animal Yields]] — fat per animal
- [[Harvest Tools]] — skinning efficiency
- [[Diesel Fuel]] — the next fuel tier up
- [[Recycling]] — LGF recycles into fat
- [[Cooking and Food]] — the campfire/furnace also cook meat

pages.title: Mixing Table
pages.body:
# Mixing Table

The crafting station that turns [[Berries & Crops|berries]] into [[Teas]]. It also brews some ammo/explosive ingredients.
