As of the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Update]] (Mar 2025), the **Cooking Workbench** absorbs the Mixing Table's tea functions, so on a modern base you may build the Cooking Workbench instead — but the standalone Mixing Table is cheaper and still the fast way to mass-brew tea.

## Stats & acquisition

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Health** | 500 HP |
| **Buy at** | [[Bandit Camp]] Food Shop for **175 scrap** |
| **Research cost** | 75 scrap |
| **Craft cost** | 200 metal fragments + 100 stone (at [[Workbench Level 1]]) |
| **Storage** | small built-in box for berries + finished teas |

## How brewing works

1. Load berries into the table.
2. Click a recipe name to auto-add the right ingredients; **shift+click** queues the max combination up to the stack limit of **20**.
3. A full batch takes **~1.5 minutes** to complete.
4. Upgrade tiers by feeding **4x lower-tier tea → 1x higher-tier** (see [[Teas]]).

## Beyond teas

The Mixing Table also crafts (once blueprints are learned): **Gun Powder, Low Grade Fuel, Explosives**, and some basic ammo (5.56 Rifle Ammo, Pistol Ammo). It's an early-game crafting hub even before you commit to a full farm.

## Mixing Table vs Cooking Workbench

| | Mixing Table | [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]] |
|--|--------------|------------------|
| Brews teas | Yes | Yes |
| Cooks food / pies | No | Yes |
| Acts as BBQ + furnace-lite | No | Yes |
| Cost | Cheaper (200 metal frags + 100 stone) | More expensive |

For a tea-focused [[Plant Genetics|berry farm]], the Mixing Table is enough. Build the Cooking Workbench when you also want pies and cooked-food buffs.

pages.title: Plant Genetics
pages.body:
# Plant Genetics

The gene system is what separates a casual farmer from a farm that out-produces everything around it. Every plant carries **six gene slots**, each filled by one of five gene types. Through **crossbreeding** you steer random seeds toward a "god seed" (e.g. **GGGGYY** or **GGGYYY**) that grows fast and yields more. This page is the full mechanic; for the physical farm, see [[Farming Basics]].

## The six gene slots

Every plant has exactly **6 gene positions**, read left to right, e.g. `G G Y Y H W`. Positions are fixed — a plant cannot rotate or reorder its own genes. They only change through **crossbreeding**.

## The five gene types

| Gene | Color | Name | Effect |
|------|-------|------|--------|
| **G** | Green | Growth | Faster seed-to-ripe time. More G = quicker harvests |
| **Y** | Green | Yield | More output. For every **2 Y genes**, you get **+1 extra clone** when cloning |
| **H** | Green | Hardiness | Resilience against poor soil conditions (water/light/temp/quality) |
| **W** | Red | Water | **Bad** — forces higher water consumption (mL/min). Drains your tank |
| **X** | Red | Empty/Neutral | **Bad** — does nothing. A wasted slot |

**Good genes:** G, Y, H (green). **Bad genes:** W, X (red). The community-ideal seeds are **GGGGYY**, **GGGYYY**, or **YYYYGG** — heavy growth + yield. H is fine but G and Y are what people chase.

> Yield fractions matter: a yield value of **2.49 gives 2** harvested items, but **2.50 gives 3**. Pushing one more Y gene can cross that threshold.

## Crossbreeding: how genes are inherited

Crossbreeding happens **only during the Crossbreed stage (~2 minutes)**. The instant a plant enters that stage, its new genes are recalculated from its **8 neighbors** in the 3x3 grid of a single Large Planter Box (orthogonal **and** diagonal touch counts).

### The weighting system

Each neighboring gene "votes" for the slot it occupies, with a weight:

- **Green genes (G, Y, H): weight 0.6**
- **Red genes (W, X): weight 1.0**

Red is **dominant** — a single red gene (1.0) beats a single green gene (0.6) in that slot. To overpower a red, you need **multiple greens stacking on the same slot**: two greens (0.6 + 0.6 = 1.2) beat one red (1.0). This is the whole game: surround a target slot with enough green votes to drown out the reds.

### Planter boxes do not cross-pollinate

Crossbreeding is contained **inside one Large Planter Box's 9 slots**. Planter box #1 and planter box #2 never interact, no matter how close. Keep each breeding experiment in its own box.

## Cloning vs. seeds

- **Seeds** (from harvested berries/crops) have **random genes** — that's your raw material.
- **Clones** taken at the **Sapling stage** are **genetically identical** to the parent — that's how you lock in and mass-produce a good seed.
- Clone counts: **2 clones** from food crops, **3 clones** from berries/hemp. More Y genes = more clones per cloning.

## Step-by-step: building a god seed

1. **Gather raw material.** Plant 10-20+ random seeds (hemp or berries). Harvest/inspect their genes. Keep any with **5 of 6 green** (5/6) — these are your near-perfect candidates.
2. **Use a genetics calculator.** Type your candidate genes into a Rust genetics calculator, set the target (e.g. 3G/3Y), and it returns a placement recipe: which plant goes in which of the 9 slots.
3. **Place to avoid stacked reds.** The rule: **never let two neighbors share the same red gene in the same slot.** If two plants both have a W in slot 4, that slot gets a combined red weight of 2.0 and your green votes lose.
4. **Center-plant timing trick.** Plant a "target" specimen in the **center slot slightly later** than the 8 surrounding plants. The center reaches the Crossbreed stage *after* its neighbors are established, so it absorbs their combined green genes. Five greens flanking the center (combined ~1.8+) easily overpower a single red (1.0), passing green into the center slot.
5. **Clone the winner.** Once a plant hits a target like **GGGGYY**, take clones at the Sapling stage and you now have an unlimited supply of that exact seed. Fill all your planters with clones.

## Why genetics is worth it

- **Growth (G):** faster cycles = more harvests per hour of cloth/berries.
- **Yield (Y):** more cloth and more berries per plant — directly feeds the [[Teas]] economy and the [[Pure Scrap Tea]] loop.
- **Water (avoid W):** W genes make a 9-plant farm drink your water tank dry; pure-green seeds barely sip. This is the practical reason to purge reds.

Once you have a god-seed clone stash, you never touch random seeds again — just replant clones forever.

pages.title: Pure Scrap Tea
pages.body:
# Pure Scrap Tea

The top-tier [[Scrap Tea]] and the most important single consumable for a farming-based scrap economy. It gives **+350% scrap yield from barrels for 1 hour**. Drink it before a road/barrel run and barrels that normally drop ~2 scrap drop **~8-9** instead. This is the payoff for running a [[Plant Genetics|genetics-optimized berry farm]].

## The whole scrap tea line

Brewed from **Yellow + White** berries at a [[Mixing Table]]. Tiers stack 4-to-1:

| Tier | Scrap from barrels | Duration | How to brew |
|------|-------------------|----------|-------------|
| Basic Scrap Tea | +100% | 30 min | 2 Yellow + 2 White berries |
| Advanced Scrap Tea | +225% | 45 min | 4x Basic Scrap Tea |
| **Pure Scrap Tea** | **+350%** | **60 min** | 4x Advanced Scrap Tea (= 32 Yellow + 32 White berries total) |

## The critical limitation

**Scrap tea only multiplies scrap that comes out of BARRELS.** It does **not** apply to:

- Crates (military crates, normal crates, elite crates)
- Recycler output (recycling components into scrap)
- NPC vendor sales, fishing rewards, or [[Gambling|gambling]] winnings

So time it for a **barrel-smashing road run**, not a recycling session.

## The farm-to-scrap loop

1. **Grow** Yellow + White berries in a Large Planter Box using god-seed clones from [[Plant Genetics]] (high Y for more berries per harvest).
2. **Brew up the tree** at a [[Mixing Table]]: 16 Basic → 4 Advanced → 1 Pure (each Pure needs 32 Yellow + 32 White berries).
3. **Pop a Pure Scrap Tea** right before hitting a road full of barrels, or a barrel-dense monument exterior.
4. **Smash barrels** for the full hour. ~8-9 scrap/barrel adds up fast.

Players report this pushing **2000+ scrap/hour** early-wipe when combined with a good barrel route (roads, [[Junkyard]], monument perimeters). Lower tiers stack into the same loop — drink whatever tier you have; even Basic (+100%) doubles barrel scrap.

## Why it's S-tier for solo/duo/trio

- Scrap funds [[Blueprint Fragments|tech tree]] unlocks, [[Bandit Camp]] purchases (including the [[Attack Helicopter]] at 2,250 scrap), and recyclables.
- A berry farm is renewable and hidden indoors — no risky food/loot runs needed to sustain it.
- The only cost is farm setup ([[Farming Basics]]) + berry [[Plant Genetics|genetics]], both one-time investments.

See [[Teas]] for the full tea catalog and [[Berries & Crops]] for berry sourcing.

pages.title: Raw Meat and Food Values
pages.body:
# Raw Meat and Food Values

The meat half of the harvest. Every animal you skin ([[Animal Yields]]) drops raw meat — but **eating it raw poisons you**. This page lists the calories/hydration/poison per meat type and the cook-it-first rules. For the cooking stations and broader food/water system, see [[Cooking and Food]]; for the buff-pie economy, see [[Cooking Workbench and Pies]].

## The golden rule: cook it first

**Raw meat does small damage / adds poison over time when eaten.** Always cook on a [[Campfire]], [[Furnace]], or BBQ before eating. Cooking flips the poison to healing and roughly doubles+ the calories.

Watch the cook timing — over-cooking turns meat into **Burnt Meat** (low calories, no poison but wasteful). Pull it at the "cooked" stage, not "burnt."

## Food value table

| Meat | Raw (cal / hydr / poison) | Cooked (cal / hydr / heal) |
|---|---|---|
| **Cooked/Raw Pork** (boar) | 60 cal, +1 hydr, mild poison | **60 cal, +1 hydr, +5 HP** |
| **Bear Meat** | 10 cal, +3 hydr, **+5 poison** | **100 cal, +1 hydr, +5 HP** |
| **Deer Meat** (venison) | small cal, mild poison | ~50 cal, +heal |
| **Wolf Meat** | small cal, mild poison | ~50 cal, +heal |
| **Horse Meat** | small cal, mild poison | ~50 cal, +heal |
| **Chicken Breast** | small cal, mild poison | ~30 cal, +heal |
| **Snake Meat** | small cal, poison | low cal, +heal (also drops 4 Snake Venom) |

> **Cooked Bear Meat is the best raw-meat food in the game at 100 calories** — bears are worth hunting for the meat alone, not just the fat/leather. Cooked Pork (60 cal) is the easy everyday staple since boars are everywhere and safe. Deer/wolf/horse/chicken cooked values aren't all published as clean numbers but sit in the ~30-50 calorie band — fine early-game filler.

## Food spoilage (NEW since 2023 — Crafting Update, Mar 2025)

Meat now **spoils on a timer**, a big change for returning players:

| State | Spoil timer |
|---|---|
| **Raw meat** | ~6 hours → becomes Spoiled |
| **Cooked meat** | ~24 hours → becomes Spoiled |
| **Produce (berries/veg)** | ~48 hours |

- **Spoiled meat** still gives a fraction of its calories but adds **poison** — it can kill you over time. Don't hoard raw meat.
- **A powered fridge pauses spoilage** — store cooked meat in a [[Mini Fridge]] (18 slots) or fridge to keep it fresh. This is why electricity/fridges matter for a food base now.
- **Cook just-in-time** rather than stockpiling raw meat; cooked lasts 4× longer.

## Where the meat goes

1. **Eat it** (cooked) — base calorie/hydration source.
2. **[[Cooking Workbench and Pies|Pies]]** — meat is an ingredient in several buff pies (Crafting Update).
3. **Bait** — fish guts/meat can bait [[Fishing]] traps; bear meat baits some traps.
4. **Compost it** — spare or spoiled meat breaks down into fertilizer in the [[Composter]] (~0.2-0.3 fertilizer each).
5. **Feed animals** — meat/scraps factor into [[Chicken Coops]] and horse care.

## Returning-player summary (2023 → 2026)

- **Food now spoils** (raw 6h / cooked 24h) — the single biggest food change. Get a powered fridge.
- **Cooking Workbench + pies (Mar 2025)** added a whole buff-food layer on top of plain cooked meat.
- Raw meat still poisons you — cook everything, never over-cook into Burnt Meat.

## Related

- [[Hunting & Harvesting]] — how you get the meat
- [[Animal Yields]] — meat amounts per animal
- [[Cooking and Food]] — stations, water, calorie/hydration system
- [[Cooking Workbench and Pies]] — the buff-pie economy
- [[Composter and Fertilizer]] — composting spare meat
- [[Animals]] — the threat side of the animals you're hunting

pages.title: Teas
pages.body:
# Teas

Teas are consumable buff drinks brewed from [[Berries & Crops|berries]] at a [[Mixing Table]] (or the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]], which absorbs the mixing table's functions). They are the single biggest payoff of running a farm: gathering teas multiply your wood/ore/scrap yields, and the scrap tea line drives the best passive scrap multiplier in the game (see [[Pure Scrap Tea]]).

## Tea tiers

Every tea exists in three tiers, each strictly **4-of-the-lower = 1-of-the-higher**:

- **Basic** — brewed from raw berries.
- **Advanced** — brew **4x Basic** (no extra berries needed for the upgrade step itself).
- **Pure** — brew **4x Advanced**.

So a Pure tea = 4 Advanced = 16 Basic = the berry pile for 16 basic brews. All teas also give **+30 Hydration** on drink.

> **Numbers caveat:** different sources report slightly different gathering-tea percentages (e.g. Wood Pure +100% vs +200%, Ore Pure +50% vs +60%). The figures below favor the rusthelp/in-game wiki values; treat the exact % as approximate and re-verify on rusthelp.com after any monthly patch, but the **relative ranking and recipes are stable**.

## Gathering teas (the money makers)

### [[Wood Tea]]
Boosts wood gathered per hit. Recipe: **Red + Blue + Red + Blue** berries.

| Tier | Wood yield | Duration |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Basic | +30% (some sources +50%) | 30 min |
| Advanced | +60% (some +100%) | 30 min |
| Pure | +100% (some +200%) | 30 min |

### [[Ore Tea]]
Boosts ore/sulfur/metal per node hit. Recipe: **Yellow + Blue + Yellow + Blue** berries.

| Tier | Ore yield | Duration |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Basic | +20% | 30 min |
| Advanced | +35-40% | 30 min |
| Pure | +50-60% | 30 min |

### [[Scrap Tea]]
Boosts scrap **from barrels only** — not crates, not recyclers. Recipe: **Yellow + White + Yellow + White** berries. This is the farm meta — see [[Pure Scrap Tea]].

| Tier | Scrap yield (barrels) | Duration | Recipe to brew |
|------|----------------------|----------|----------------|
| Basic | +100% | 30 min | 2 Yellow + 2 White |
| Advanced | +225% | 45 min | 4x Basic Scrap Tea |
| **Pure** | **+350%** | **60 min** | 4x Advanced (= 32 Yellow + 32 White total) |

### [[Harvesting Tea]]
Added Aug 2020. Boosts resources from **harvesting animal corpses** (meat/fat/bone/cloth from skinning). Buff: **+150% corpse resources for 30 min** at the listed tier. Recipe uses berries at the [[Mixing Table]]; great paired with hunting trips and the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Update]] meat economy.

## Survival / combat teas

### [[Healing Tea]]
Instant + over-time health. Recipe: **4x Red** berries (Basic).

| Tier | Effect |
|------|--------|
| Basic | +30 instant health |
| Advanced | +health + restoration over time |
| Pure | +30 instant + ~+75 restoration over time |

### [[Max Health Tea]]
Raises your max HP above 100 temporarily. Recipe: **3x Red + 1x Yellow** (Basic).

| Tier | Max HP bonus | Duration |
|------|-------------|----------|
| Basic | +5 | 20 min |
| Advanced | +12.5 | 20 min |
| Pure | +20 | 20 min |

A Pure Max Health Tea + Pure Healing Tea is a strong pre-fight stack: 120 effective HP and a big instant heal.

### [[Anti-Rad Tea]]
Radiation resistance for monument/oil-rig runs. Recipe: **2x Red + 2x Green** berries (Basic).

| Tier | Radiation resistance | Duration |
|------|---------------------|----------|
| Basic | +5% (+50% exposure resist, 5 min) | 30 min |
| Advanced | +15% | 30 min |
| Pure | +25% (+50% exposure resist) | 30 min |

## Temperature teas (Cooking Update, Mar 2025)

Two climate teas were added with the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Update]], brewed from **Red + Yellow** berries:

### [[Warming Tea]]
Protects against cold (snow biome, night, water).

| Tier | Temp boost | Duration |
|------|-----------|----------|
| Basic | +5°C | 20 min |
| Pure | +15°C (stays warm even at 0°C ambient) | 60 min |

### [[Cooling Tea]]
The inverse — reduces heat damage in the desert biome / hot zones. Same red+yellow berry base, tiered Basic → Advanced → Pure.

## Which teas matter for the meta

| Priority | Tea | Why |
|----------|-----|-----|
| **S** | [[Pure Scrap Tea]] | +350% barrel scrap, 1h — best passive scrap multiplier |
| A | [[Wood Tea]] / [[Ore Tea]] | Halves/triples gather time when building or stocking sulfur |
| A | [[Healing Tea]] + [[Max Health Tea]] | Cheap fight-prep stack (extra HP + instant heal) |
| B | [[Anti-Rad Tea]] | Needed for [[Launch Site]] / [[Military Tunnels]] / oil rig deep runs |
| B | [[Harvesting Tea]] | Big meat/fat boost on hunting runs |
| C | [[Warming Tea]] / [[Cooling Tea]] | Situational biome comfort |

The whole reason to grow a 9-slot berry farm with good [[Plant Genetics]] is to feed this list — especially the [[Pure Scrap Tea]] line.

pages.title: Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters
pages.body:
# Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters

Cheating is the #1 complaint of every returning Rust player, and the honest answer is: **it's real, it's worse on free/high-pop officials, and you cannot fully escape it on vanilla** — but in 2026 you have actual tools to dodge most of it. This page is the survival manual for the cheating problem: how the ban system works, how to tell a cheater from a god-tier player, how to report properly so it actually lands, and the single biggest mitigation a returning solo/duo/trio can use — **[[Premium Servers]]**.

> **The 30-second version:** Play [[Premium Servers]] (Steam inventory ≥ $15) or TPM/Secure-Boot officials, not raw vanilla high-pop. Learn the aimbot/ESP tells so you stop ragequitting on legit deaths. When you do meet a real one: F7 report in-game + a clip + their Steam ID. Don't expect an instant ban — EAC bans in waves.

---

## 1. What anti-cheat Rust actually runs

Rust uses **Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC)**, a Epic Games kernel-level anti-cheat. "Kernel-level" means it loads a driver at boot and monitors memory access, driver behavior, input patterns, and long-term gameplay signatures — not just a scan of the game process. This is why EAC needs **Secure Boot** enabled on many systems and why it's hard to spoof cheaply.

Key facts a returning player should internalize:

- **EAC is the only thing that can actually detect cheats.** Server admins, plugins, and your eyeballs can *suspect*, gather evidence, and *server-ban*, but a global game ban comes from EAC/Facepunch. (See [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] for what admins can spectate.)
- **EAC bans in waves, not instantly.** A blatant cheater you reported today might keep playing for days or weeks, then vanish in a ban wave. Detection-then-delay is deliberate (it stops cheat devs from binary-diffing which build got caught). Do not assume "they're still here = my report was ignored."
- **Detection is a cat-and-mouse arms race.** Paid cheat providers sell "undetected" loaders and HWID spoofers. EAC catches the cheap/public ones fast and the private ones slowly. This is structurally unwinnable on free servers — hence Premium (Section 5).

---

## 2. The ban system: three different "bans" that get confused

This trips up everyone. There are **three distinct bans**, and they have totally different scope and appeal paths.

| Ban type | Issued by | Scope | Shows on Steam? | Appealable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **EAC ban** | Easy Anti-Cheat (Epic) | **Global** — every EAC-protected game session of Rust, permanent | Yes — appears as a **VAC-style "Game Ban"** on the Steam profile | **No.** EAC has a zero-tolerance, no-reversal policy. Appeals are effectively dead-ends. |
| **Game / Developer ban** | Facepunch Studios | All Facepunch games + online services (forums, support) | Yes — counts as a **Game Ban** on Steam | **Sometimes** — you can contact Facepunch support; rare to win unless it was a mistaken-identity / shared-PC case. |
| **Server ban** | An individual community server's admins | **That server only** (some networks share ban lists across their own servers) | **No** — invisible on your Steam profile | Up to that server owner — appeal in their Discord. Officials don't issue these. |

Practical takeaways for *you* (the legit returning player):

- A **Game Ban** badge on a player's Steam profile (visible publicly) is a strong tell they've been caught cheating before — though it could be in any EAC/VAC game, and bans only *appear after* the wave hits. A profile with a fresh game ban + a brand-new account is a closet-cheater signature.
- **Family-share / shared-PC risk:** an EAC ban can hit the *account that ran the cheat*, and Family Sharing of Rust to a cheating friend can get **your** library lending privileges revoked. Don't lend Rust to randos.
- "Get unbanned" services and HWID-spoofer sellers are scams or malware — there is no legitimate EAC unban.

---

## 3. Spotting cheaters: tells by cheat type

The hardest skill for a returning player is **distinguishing a genuinely cracked player from a cheater**, because Rust's PvP skill ceiling is enormous (recoil control, peeker's advantage, pre-aim). Below are the real tells. One tell alone is rarely proof; **a stack of tells across a fight is.**

### Aimbot
- **Inhuman headshot ratio.** Legit players land plenty of bodyshots, especially while running, at range, or against a strafing target. Aimbot users have suspiciously high **headshot %** that holds up *over distance and across multiple kills*. Check the **combat log** (Section 4) for hit locations.
- **Instant snap-on.** The crosshair teleports onto your head the *instant* you peek, with zero acquisition time, even from a flick that started off-target.
- **Tracking through smoke / behind cover.** Aim stays glued to where you are even when you should be unseen.
- **Perfect through recoil.** Full-auto spray that stays pinned on the head with no spread walk-off (combine with ESP and it's lethal at any range).
- **Legit-player look-alike:** a good player *also* gets fast headshots — but they miss, they reset, they bodyshot under pressure, and their aim has human micro-jitter and overcorrection.

### ESP / Wallhacks (the most common, hardest to "feel")
- **Pre-fire / pre-aim on hidden players.** They shoot *before* you round the corner, or their gun is already trained on the exact spot you're about to appear from.
- **Beelining to your stash/base/loot** with no scouting, no hesitation, ignoring decoys.
- **Tracking you through solid walls/rocks** — aim follows your silhouette while you're fully occluded. The classic catch: spectate them (as an admin) or watch a demo and see them aiming at a player through a wall, then act on it.
- **Never gets surprised.** Always pre-positioned for your push, always knows the third-party is coming.
- **Looting only the good box / knowing which wall to raid** (item ESP).
- **Legit look-alike:** game sense, sound whoring (footsteps/reload audio is *loud* in Rust), and map knowledge explain a LOT. A good player who heard your footsteps will pre-aim too. The difference is consistency through *impossible* information (you made no sound, you're fully hidden, there's no line of sight).

### Spinbot
- The most literal: the player **spins their model in rapid 360° rotations** continuously, usually paired with aimbot so they hit you regardless of facing. Unmistakable when active — it's an anti-aim trick to dodge return fire.

### No-clip / Fly / "Spiderman"
- **No fall damage** from heights that should hurt or kill.
- **Passing through walls/floors/rocks**, or appearing inside a sealed base with no raid.
- **Vertical scaling** of walls/cliffs unnaturally ("Spiderman" deliberately scales surfaces to dodge the flyhack height-trigger kick).
- **Aerial teleporting** / hovering. Admins test this by force-teleporting a suspect upward to see if no-clip is toggled.

### Loot / spawn cheats (you'll see this as a survivor)
- A player/base with **stacks larger than the server's default stack size**, or endgame loot inconsistent with hours played that wipe. Often only visible after you raid or an admin inspects their inventory.

### Latency / hit-reg abuse
- In your **combat log**, repeated `Projectile Invalid` entries when you shoot a suspect can indicate lag-switching or hit-registration manipulation (your hits getting rejected).

> **Returning-player reality check:** In 2023 you might have called every death a "hacker." A huge share of those were just better players with recoil scripts banned and skill you'd forgotten. Spectate the kill cam mentally: did they *miss* at all? Did they *react* to sound? If yes, it was probably legit. Reserve the cheater label for the stack-of-tells cases.

---

## 4. The combat log as evidence

The combat log is your built-in black box and the single most useful self-serve forensic tool.

- **Open the [console](Settings and Binds) with `F1`** and type **`combatlog`** (you can also bind it). Each server stores roughly the **last 100 combat events** you were involved in.
- It shows, per event: **attacker, target, weapon, ammo, distance, hit area (head/chest/etc.), damage, and health remaining**.
- **What to look for in a suspected cheater's fight:**
  - Every entry showing **`head`** as the hit area → likely aimbot.
  - Hits landing on you from **distances/angles with no line of sight** → likely ESP+aimbot.
  - **`Projectile Invalid`** spam → possible lag/hit-reg abuse on their end.
- The combat log is *your* log (events involving you), not a global feed — so it's strongest for "how did they kill me?" forensics. Pair it with a video clip for a report.

See [[Settings and Binds]] for binding the console/combatlog and [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] for the admin-side spectate/`combatlog <steamid>` commands.

---

## 5. Premium Servers — the real mitigation (use this)

This is the most important section for a returning solo/duo/trio. **[[Premium Servers]]** are the closest thing Rust has to a cheater filter, and they're free to access if you already own cosmetics.

- **What they are:** an official Facepunch server flavor (launched **March 13, 2025**, still officially "experimental") that **denies entry to accounts whose Steam inventory of Rust items is worth less than ~$15**.
- **Why it works:** cheaters burn through disposable accounts after each ban wave. A $15 inventory requirement adds real **financial friction per throwaway account**, so it's far more expensive to keep re-buying in. Community reports and Facepunch's own framing put cheater density dramatically lower than raw vanilla (commonly cited as roughly **~4x fewer** cheater encounters — directional, not a guaranteed number).
- **What counts toward the $15:** tradable Rust items — **Permanent Store** cosmetics (building skins, décor packs, hazmat skins) and any marketplace-tradable Rust skins. **Excluded:** standalone DLC packs like the Instruments DLC and Voice Props (these aren't tradable inventory value).
- **Cost in practice:** if you've played since ~2018 and own any skins/twitch drops, **you may already qualify for $0**. Otherwise, buy ~$15 of cheap tradable skins off the Steam Community Market — that's a one-time spend, not a subscription. ([[Skins and the Skin Economy]] explains what's tradable.)
- **How to access:**
  - Premium status shows as a badge on your avatar in the main menu.
  - Premium servers **only appear in your browser if you meet the threshold**; new purchases can take up to ~20 minutes to register (manually refresh in the server list if needed).
  - Server owners enable it with the convar `server.premium 1`.
- **Limitations Facepunch is upfront about:** it's experimental and **"won't stop every cheat user."** A determined cheater can fund a $15 inventory. It raises the cost; it doesn't eliminate the problem.
- **Companion mitigation:** some officials also require **TPM 2.0 + Secure Boot** (hardware-bound, harder to spoof). See [[Server Types]] for the full vanilla / Softcore / Hardcore / Primitive / modded / Premium breakdown and how to pick one as a returning solo.

> **Recommendation for a returning solo/duo/trio:** default to **Premium officials** (or a well-moderated community server with active admins) over free vanilla high-pop. The cheater delta is the single biggest quality-of-life upgrade available, and it costs you a one-time ~$15 (or nothing if you have old skins).

---

## 6. Trust factor & account age

There's no public "Steam trust factor" number you can read, but the signals matter:

- **Account age + Rust hours + inventory value** correlate with legitimacy. A 2-week-old account with 0 cosmetics and a recent Game Ban badge is the textbook cheater profile.
- **Premium's $15 inventory requirement is essentially a trust-factor proxy** — it filters on exactly the "fresh disposable account" signature.
- When you suspect someone, **check their Steam profile** (if public): account creation date, Rust playtime, VAC/Game Ban badges, level. A blatant fragger with a private profile + new account + game ban history is your prime report target.
- Keep **your own** profile in good standing: don't run sketchy "FPS booster"/spoofer software (much of it is cheat-adjacent or malware and can get *you* flagged), don't Family-Share Rust to cheaters.

---

## 7. How to report a cheater (so it actually lands)

### In-game F7 report (primary, do this every time)
1. Press **`F7`** in-game.
2. Select the player from the list (you can pick whether it's cheating, abuse, etc.).
3. Fill the form with specifics and submit. On many servers the report **also forwards to the server's Discord** so admins can act locally.
4. F7 feeds the report into the official pipeline that EAC/Facepunch use to prioritize who to investigate. Volume of credible reports matters — report even if you think nothing will happen.

### Strengthen the report with evidence
- **A video clip** is by far the strongest evidence. Use Steam's built-in recording, NVIDIA/AMD instant replay, or [Medal](#)/OBS. Capture the suspicious moment (the wall-track, the spinbot, the impossible flick). See [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] for in-client **demo recording** (`demo.record`/`demo.play`) which lets you re-watch a fight from any angle as proof.
- **The combat log** (Section 4) — screenshot the all-headshot or impossible-distance entries.
- **Their Steam ID / profile** — admins and Facepunch need an identifier, not just a display name (names are changeable). Get it from the F7 menu, the scoreboard, or `players` console list.

### Escalation paths
- **Server ban (community servers):** report to the **server's Discord** with your clip — active admins can spectate (`combatlog <steamid>`, no-clip-test, inventory check) and ban from *their* server immediately, even before any EAC wave.
- **Steam report:** open their Steam profile → **Report → Cheating** as a secondary channel.
- **Facepunch support:** for serious/organized issues; note that EAC bans themselves aren't influenced by appeals, and Facepunch won't give you per-report status updates.

### What NOT to expect
- No instant ban, no confirmation email, no "your report banned X" notification. Bans come in **waves**; success looks like "that guy stopped appearing." Reporting is a numbers game that works in aggregate.

---

## 8. Realistic expectations (read this before you ragequit)

- **You cannot avoid 100% of cheaters on vanilla officials.** Anyone selling you that is lying. The arms race guarantees some slip through between ban waves.
- **Most of your deaths are not cheaters.** Rust's skill gap is brutal; a clan of practiced players will feel like aimbots and ESP because of comms ("he's pushing left"), sound cues, and recoil mastery. Use the *stack of tells* before you accuse.
- **The leverage you DO have:** play [[Premium Servers]] / TPM-Secure-Boot / well-moderated community servers, learn the tells so you don't tilt on legit deaths, keep clips ready, and F7 the blatant ones. That combination removes the large majority of the cheating frustration for a returning solo/duo/trio.
- **Don't fight the meta from a disadvantage:** if a server feels infested and admins are absent, leave. Server choice is your strongest anti-cheat lever — bigger than any in-fight read.

---

## Related pages

- [[Server Types]] — vanilla / Softcore / Hardcore / Primitive / modded / **Premium**, and how to pick one
- [[Premium Servers]] — the $15-inventory cheater filter in depth
- [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] — `combatlog`, `demo.record`, spectate, admin commands
- [[Settings and Binds]] — bind the console / combat log
- [[Skins and the Skin Economy]] — what counts as tradable inventory value for Premium
- [[Wipe Schedule]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[PvP Tips]]

pages.title: Clan Roles and Coordination
pages.body:
# Clan Roles and Coordination

How a group splits labor so a wipe runs on rails instead of chaos. Applies whether you're a trio specializing or a 6+ clan running shifts. For the access mechanics behind all this, see [[Clans and Groups]] and [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]].

## Why roles matter once you pass solo

A solo does everything sequentially. A group's whole advantage is **parallelism** — three people farming, building, and grinding sulfur *at the same time* compress days of solo progress into hours. Roles only pay off if people actually stick to them; "everyone farms whatever" wastes the group's biggest edge.

## The standard role split

| Role | Owns | What they do |
|---|---|---|
| **Farmer / grinder** | Resource economy | Wood, stone, metal, sulfur runs; feeds furnaces; keeps [[Upkeep]] topped. Wants a planter room + bulk storage in the base |
| **Builder / base architect** | The base | Designs and upgrades the [[Building Guide|base]], manages [[Tool Cupboard]]s + [[Upkeep]], runs repairs after raids, places [[Auto Turret]]s and traps |
| **PvP / roamer** | Map control + kills | Holds monuments, fights at [[Oil Rig]]/[[Launch Site]], collects scrap and [[Blueprint Fragments]] from scientists, scouts enemy bases |
| **Tinkerer / tech** | Crafting + electricity | Tech tree path-unlocks, [[Recycler]] runs, electrical/industrial setups, [[Auto Turret]] circuits, cooking buffs |
| **Sulfur / boom maker** | Raid economy | Dedicated sulfur grind → gunpowder → explosives; preps [[Rockets]]/[[C4]] stockpile for raids. See [[Raid Costs]] |

In a **trio** these collapse: typically one farmer, one builder/tinkerer, one PvP/roamer — and everyone helps with sulfur before a raid. In a **6+ clan** you can run two farmers, a dedicated sulfur grinder, and a 2-3 person roam squad.

## Loot rules that prevent group implosion

The #1 cause of clans falling apart is loot drama. The rule that fixes ~90% of it:

> **One shared "team core" box for everyone, plus a personal box per member.**

- **Team core box(es):** medical, ammo, building mats, common guns — anyone can pull what they need for a fight or a build. Lock with the shared **guest code** ([[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]]).
- **Personal box / [[Locker]] per member:** their own kit, skins, hoarded loot — locked with *their own* code only they know. Reduces "who took my AK" fights to zero.
- **Boom and high-value loot** (explosives, keycards, components) lives in a **leader-access room** behind a separate code, not the general team box, so a betrayer or a small breach can't walk off with the raid stockpile.

## Shift scheduling (offline coverage)

Rust has no pause — your base is vulnerable whenever everyone's asleep (offline raids). Bigger groups beat this with **staggered playtime**:

- Try to **never have the base fully empty.** Even one person online deters opportunist offline raids and can defend or call for backup.
- Coordinate timezones: a clan with US + EU members naturally covers more of the 24 h clock.
- Use a **[[Seismic Sensor]]** (raid alarm, May 2026) + [[Rust+ Companion App]] Smart Alarms so offline members get phone notifications when the base takes damage.
- Keep **respawn [[Sleeping Bag]]s spread out** — bags within 50 m share cooldown, so cluster them and a team wipe locks everyone out at once.

## Communication

- **Discord voice is mandatory** for any serious group — in-game voice is proximity-only and the phone/broadcaster systems are toys.
- Use the in-game **ping system** (middle-mouse with binoculars/drone/CCTV) and **map markers** (up to 5, leader markers show to team) for silent callouts — see [[Team System]] and [[Settings and Binds]].
- Pre-agree callout language for raids/defense ("contact south wall", "boom incoming", "core breached") — see [[Raid Bases and FOBs]].

## Returning-player reality check (2026)

Solo/duo/trio team-limited servers have exploded, and the **skill gap between organized groups and casuals has widened**. A coordinated trio with clear roles routinely beats a disorganized 6-stack. Don't over-recruit: a tight, role-disciplined small group is stronger than a sloppy big one, and every extra member is one more person who knows your base code.

Related: [[Clans and Groups]], [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]], [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]], [[Raid Bases and FOBs]], [[Team System]], [[Raid Costs]], [[Upkeep]].

pages.title: Clans and Groups
pages.body:
# Clans and Groups

How a Rust group actually *operates* beyond the 8-player [[Team System]] UI: sharing building privilege across members, running multiple Tool Cupboards in one compound, splitting roles, code-lock and locker etiquette, and coordinating raid bases / FOBs. This is the "how a clan runs a wipe" layer that [[Team System]] (the team UI) and [[Group Bases]] (compounds as threat intel) don't cover.

> **Returning-player note:** the in-game team is capped at 8 (vanilla `maxteamsize`). A "clan" larger than 8 is just *multiple teams cooperating* — they share no green nameplates, no shared map dots, and **no automatic build/TC access**. Everything below (TC auth, locks, turrets) is still **manual and per-player** regardless of team. Being teamed never auths anyone on anything.

## The core truth: team â‰  access

The single most-misunderstood thing for a trio scaling up: **joining a team grants zero base access.** Three separate systems each have their own list:

| System | How members get access | Shared by team? |
|---|---|---|
| **Building privilege** ([[Tool Cupboard]]) | Each player must press *Authorize* on the TC | No — manual per TC |
| **Locks** ([[Code Lock]] / [[Key Lock]]) | Each player must know the code (or hold a key) | No — code-based, not team-based |
| **Auto Turrets** ([[Auto Turret]]) | Each player must be added to the turret's authorized list | No — manual per turret |

So a 6-person clan's onboarding ritual at base is literally: walk every member to the **TC** (auth), give them the **base code** (or guest code), and add them to each **turret**. Miss one and that player can't build, can't open doors, or gets shot by your own defenses.

## Pages in this cluster

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]] | Auth limits, building-privilege radius, why clans run many TCs, spacing, clearing the list, betrayal-proofing |
| [[Clan Roles and Coordination]] | Farmer / builder / raider / PvP split, loot rules, shift scheduling, comms |
| [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]] | Main vs guest code, what each lock secures, who can pick up what, the "team core box + personal boxes" rule |
| [[Raid Bases and FOBs]] | Building a Forward Operating Base, raid roles (rocketeer/breacher/looter/defender), online vs offline, rocket-count math |

## Why scaling past a trio changes everything

- **Upkeep multiplies but so does farming throughput.** A compound burns far more resources per day in [[Upkeep]] than a 2x2, but a 6-stack farming in parallel out-produces it easily — the constraint becomes *organization*, not resources.
- **You become a target worth raiding.** A duo base targets 60-120 rockets soft-side (above opportunist threshold, below serious commitment); a visible clan compound advertises loot and invites the entire server's biggest groups. See [[Group Bases]].
- **Internal security becomes a real threat.** With 6+ people who all know the base code, a single disgruntled member can clear the TC list, change locks, or loot the core. Clans mitigate this with **compartmentalized TCs and guest codes** (below).

## The clan onboarding checklist (do this for every new member)

1. **Party up in the menu** first ([[Team System]] — Party system spawns you within ~100 m and auto-teams).
2. At base: have them **Authorize on the main [[Tool Cupboard]]**.
3. Give them the **guest [[Code Lock]] code** (not the master code) for shared doors.
4. Add them to **[[Auto Turret]]** authorized lists so defenses are friendly.
5. Point them at **their personal box** and the **team core box**, then assign a role (see [[Clan Roles and Coordination]]).

Related: [[Team System]], [[Group Bases]], [[Building Guide]], [[Raid Costs]], [[Upkeep]].

pages.title: Clothing & Environmental Gear
pages.body:
# Clothing & Environmental Gear

This is the **non-combat apparel** reference: the clothing and gear you wear to survive **cold**, **radiation**, **water/oxygen**, and **darkness** — not to win gunfights. Combat protection numbers (projectile/melee/explosion %) live on [[Armor]]; here the job is **warmth, rad-resistance, diving, and utility (light/vision)**.

Rust clothing is **layered per slot**. Each of Head / Chest / Legs has a **Layer 1 (clothing: comfort + cold + rad)** and a **Layer 2 (armor)** slot, so you can wear a hoodie *under* a metal chest plate. **Feet (boots/fins)**, **hands (gloves)**, and **face/mask** are single-slot. Some items (Snow Jacket, Hazmat Suit) are **whole-body or whole-slot hogs** that block the armor layer — that's their big tradeoff.

> Verification note: Facepunch rebalances clothing cold/rad values almost every wipe. The hard numbers below (diving tank seconds, fins speed multiplier, NVG battery minutes, hazmat/lead/gas-mask rad points) are verified Jun 2026. The **cold-protection percentages** for cloth items drift patch-to-patch — treat the *ranking* (which item is warmest) as reliable and the exact % as approximate.

---

## The four jobs of environmental gear

| Job | What it counters | Key gear | Threshold page |
|-----|------------------|----------|----------------|
| **Warmth** | Cold biomes, night, wet penalty | Hoodie, Pants, Snow Jacket, Burlap/Hide sets, Beanie, Candle Hat, Boots, Gloves | [[Temperature and Cold]] |
| **Radiation** | Monument rad zones, reactors | Hazmat Suit, Lead-lined armor, Gas Mask, Burlap+Wood layering | [[Armor]] (rad threshold table) |
| **Diving** | Oxygen + underwater speed | Diving Tank, Fins, Mask, Wetsuit | [[Underwater Labs]], [[Deep Sea Monuments]] |
| **Utility** | Darkness / vision | Miners Hat, Candle Hat, Night Vision Goggles | — |

---

## Slot map

| Slot | Layer-1 (clothing) options | Single-slot specials |
|------|----------------------------|----------------------|
| **Head** | Beanie Hat, Boonie Hat, Bucket Helmet, Candle Hat, Miners Hat, Burlap Headwrap, Hide Helmet | **Night Vision Goggles**, **Gas Mask** (cannot wear with a helmet) |
| **Face / mask** | Bandana Mask, Improvised Balaclava | Gas Mask occupies the face role |
| **Chest** | Hoodie, T-Shirt/Shirt, Tank Top, Burlap Shirt, Hide Shirt/Halterneck | **Snow Jacket** (eats the whole chest slot), **Hazmat Suit** (full-body) |
| **Legs** | Pants, Shorts, Burlap Trousers, Hide Pants | Hazmat Suit covers legs too |
| **Feet** | Boots, Shoes, Burlap Shoes, Hide Boots | **Diving Fins** (water gear) |
| **Hands** | Leather Gloves, Roadsign Gloves, Burlap Gloves, Tactical Gloves | — |
| **Eyes** | — | **Diving Mask** (or NVG) |
| **Back / chest gadget** | — | **Diving Tank** |

---

## Warm clothing

Warmth comes almost entirely from **Layer-1 cloth/leather** items. Metal armor gives **negative** cold (see [[Armor]]) so you layer cloth *under* it. Relative ranking (warmest first within a slot), values approximate:

| Item | Slot | Cold protection | Rad | Notes |
|------|------|-----------------|-----|-------|
| **Snow Jacket** | Chest (whole slot) | **Highest in game (~+20%)** | moderate rad too | Keeps you warm in any biome; **blocks chest armor**; overheats you in the desert |
| **Hoodie** | Chest (Layer 1) | High (~+10%) | tiny | The everyday warm chest; wears under a metal plate |
| **Pants** | Legs (Layer 1) | High (~+10%) | tiny | Pairs with the hoodie; wears under a kilt |
| **Burlap Shirt / Trousers** | Chest / Legs | Good cold + small rad | small rad each | The cheap rad-and-cold layering set; default blueprint |
| **Burlap Headwrap** | Head | Good cold + small rad | small rad | Part of the burlap set; arctic-viable when full set worn |
| **Burlap Shoes** | Feet | Small cold + small rad | small rad | Cheap feet warmth |
| **Burlap Gloves** | Hands | Small cold + small rad | small rad | Cheap hand warmth/rad |
| **Hide set** (shirt/halterneck, pants, boots, helmet) | Various | Good cold | none | Early-game warmth from animal fat/leather; warmer than cloth tier |
| **Beanie Hat** | Head | Good cold | none | Cheap pure-warmth cap; default blueprint |
| **Candle Hat** | Head (top) | **Substantial cold** + ambient light | none | Doubles as a light; low defense but warm |
| **Boots / Shoes** | Feet | Small cold | none | Always wear *something* on feet in snow |
| **Leather Gloves** | Hands | Small cold | none | Hands count toward total warmth |
| **Bandana Mask** | Face | **Best cold-per-scrap cloth item** | tiny | Cheapest way to add warmth in the snow |
| **Improvised Balaclava** | Face | Good cold | tiny | Full face cover; warm + intimidation skins |
| **Bucket Helmet** | Head | **+ slight cold** | none | Rare metal piece that *adds* a little warmth |
| **Wood Armor (jacket/pants)** | Layer 2 | none (warmth) | small rad | Warmth-neutral; included here only because it stacks rad for monument kits |

See [[Temperature and Cold]] for the biome temperatures, the **−7 °C death threshold**, and the **wet penalty** (being soaked drags effective temp far down — dry off by a [[Camp Fire]]).

### Cold vs armor tradeoff (the core layering rule)
- A full metal kit ([[Metal Facemask]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]] + [[Road Sign Kilt]]) carries a **steep cold penalty** (chest plate ~−34%, facemask ~−4%, kilt ~−8%).
- **Layer 1 cancels it:** wear **Hoodie + Pants** under the metal so you don't freeze on a snow night.
- A survivable **snow PvP loadout**: facemask + chest plate + kilt over **hoodie + pants**, plus **beanie/bandana + gloves + boots**. Add a Candle Hat if you'd rather have warmth-plus-light over the boonie.
- The **Snow Jacket** is the no-fuss option for non-combat snow trips: max warmth + decent rad, but you sacrifice the metal chest plate entirely.

---

## Radiation protection

Radiation in Rust is **points-subtracted, not a percentage**: each zone has a strength (rads/sec) and your **total worn rad-protection points** are subtracted from it. If total protection **≥ zone strength**, you take zero. (Full zone-by-zone breakdown and the threshold table live on [[Armor]].)

Key rad-protection values (verified Jun 2026):

| Item | Rad points | Slot | Notes |
|------|-----------|------|-------|
| **Hazmat Suit** | **25** | Full body | Single biggest item; clears low/medium/high monuments alone |
| **Lead-lined armor** (helmet / vest / pants) | **5 each** (set = 15) | Layers over slots | Stacks on top of a hazmat for reactor rooms |
| **Full Burlap set** | **~10–12** combined | Head/chest/legs/feet/hands | The cheap monument kit |
| **Gas Mask** | **2** | Head/face | Small bonus; **can't wear with a helmet** |
| **Snow Jacket** | moderate | Chest | Warmth piece that also helps in low-rad zones |
| **Bandana / Wood armor** | small each | various | Layer them to top up burlap |

### The Hazmat Suit (the workhorse)
A full-body suit giving **25 radiation**, **~+50% cold**, and a flat **~30% to projectile/melee/explosion**. It's the standard **monument-run** outfit: throw it on for [[Power Plant]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Cargo Ship]], the flooded [[Oil Rig]] after the hack, etc. It is **not** a PvP outfit — combat numbers are mediocre and you give up the [[Metal Facemask]] headshot reduction. Keep one in a box and swap into it for pushes.

- **Arctic Hazmat Suit** is a skin variant that **trades some rad for cold** — radiation protection is lower (~17% less than standard, still enough for most monuments) but it shrugs off blizzard/−5 °C cold. Good for snow-edge bases. (Skin only — same item, different stats package.)
- **Scientist / Heavy Scientist suits** are loot-drop body pieces that also carry rad; functionally hazmat-class for monument work.

### The "what passes each rad tier" cheat (full table on [[Armor]])
- **Low (~26):** Full Burlap set.
- **Medium (~52):** Burlap + Wood Armor + bandana, **or** a Hazmat.
- **High (~81):** **Hazmat alone (25)** clears it.
- **Extreme (~100+):** **Hazmat + Lead set (25+15 = 40)** or hazmat + **Anti-Radiation Pills** to outlast the meter. The [[Launch Site]] Vehicle Assembly Building and the [[Power Plant]] cooling tower are the hottest spots — a bare hazmat does **not** fully cover them.

---

## Diving gear

Underwater play needs **oxygen + vision + speed**. Required for [[Underwater Labs]] and useful around [[Deep Sea Monuments]] and seafloor crate dives.

| Item | Slot | Effect | Numbers (verified Jun 2026) |
|------|------|--------|------------------------------|
| **Diving Tank** | Chest gadget | Breathe underwater | **600 s (~10 min)** of oxygen; refill at a **Workbench / Repair Bench**, or top up at **air pockets** inside labs |
| **Double Diving Tank** | Chest gadget | Larger air supply | **~1,080 s (~18 min)** of oxygen |
| **Diving Fins** | Feet | Faster swim | **×1.5 water speed**; **−0.3 land move speed** (terrible on foot — swap back on land) |
| **Diving Mask** | Eyes | Clear underwater vision | No resource cost; removes the murky underwater blur |
| **Wetsuit** | Body | Thermal protection in cold water | Prevents cold-water hypothermia; pairs with tank/fins/mask |

**Oxygen mechanics:** drains at a **constant rate regardless of depth**; **fast swimming drains faster than slow swimming**, so cruise, don't sprint, when air is low. Diving fins reduce effective consumption by getting you there faster. Tanks are **repairable/recyclable** and despawn in ~20 min if dropped.

**Lab kit checklist:** Diving Tank (or Double) + Mask + Fins, plus your monument essentials — **keycards** for the [[Keycards|locked sections]], meds, and a weapon. Surface at **air pockets** inside the lab to refill before the next stretch. Don't forget to **swap fins off** the moment you're inside on foot.

---

## Utility gear (light & vision)

| Item | Slot | What it does | Power / fuel | Craft / source |
|------|------|--------------|--------------|----------------|
| **Miners Hat** | Head | Focused white **flashlight beam**; same defense as the Headset; toggle from inventory | Burns **Low Grade Fuel** (~25 s per 1 LGF) | WB1: 50 Metal Frags, 15 Cloth, 10 Low Grade Fuel |
| **Candle Hat** | Head (top) | **Ambient** torch-like glow; **substantial cold protection** | No fuel (older versions degraded with use) | Cheap default-known recipe |
| **Night Vision Goggles (NVG)** | Head | Amplifies light → see in full dark; lenses glow visibly to others | **Battery lasts ~15 min**; recharge at a **Lvl 2 Workbench**; **cannot be worn with a helmet** | WB2: 10 HQM + 2 Tech Trash (research 60 scrap); or vending at Bandit Camp/Floating Cities for **250 scrap**; or high-tier loot/scientists |

**Light-source tips:**
- **Miners Hat = caves, monuments, base work** — a bright beam, but it eats fuel and **gives away your position** (others see your light). Toggle it off when roaming hostile.
- **Candle Hat = cheap snow nights** — pick it over a beanie when you also want a little ambient light, but it's dim.
- **NVG = the night-roaming meta** — huge advantage on dark servers, but **you can't also wear a helmet** (you trade head armor for vision) and **enemy players can see your glowing lenses**. Budget a spare battery; 15 min goes fast.

---

## "What to wear for X" — quick loadouts

| Situation | Wear this | Why |
|-----------|-----------|-----|
| **Snow biome trip (non-combat)** | Snow Jacket + Pants + Beanie/Candle Hat + Boots + Gloves (or full Hide/Burlap set) | Max warmth; no armor needed if avoiding fights — see [[Temperature and Cold]] |
| **Snow biome PvP** | [[Metal Facemask]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]] + [[Road Sign Kilt]] **over Hoodie + Pants**, + Beanie + Bandana + Gloves + Boots | Keeps combat protection ([[Armor]]) while offsetting the metal cold penalty |
| **Cold night anywhere** | Hoodie + Pants + Beanie + Boots, or stand by a [[Camp Fire]] | Layer-1 warmth; dry off if wet — wet supercharges cold |
| **Deep dive / [[Underwater Labs]]** | Diving Tank (or Double) + Mask + Fins + Wetsuit + keycards | Oxygen + vision + speed; swap fins off indoors |
| **Seafloor crate run / [[Deep Sea Monuments]]** | Diving Tank + Mask + Fins (skip armor) | You're swimming, not fighting — air and speed matter most |
| **Standard rad monument** (Airfield, Water Treatment, Trainyard) | Full **Burlap** set, or just a **Hazmat** | Burlap clears low/med; hazmat is foolproof — see [[Armor]] |
| **High-rad monument** (Power Plant, Mil Tunnels, Cargo) | **Hazmat Suit** | 25 rad clears it alone |
| **Reactor / extreme rad** (Launch VAB, Oil Rig reactor) | **Hazmat + Lead set** (40) and/or Anti-Radiation Pills, get in/out fast | Bare hazmat is short of the hottest zones |
| **Night roaming a dark server** | **NVG** (no helmet) + light armor + bandana | Vision edge; accept the head-armor sacrifice and the visible lenses |
| **Cave farming / base work in the dark** | **Miners Hat** (carry spare Low Grade Fuel) | Bright beam; cheap; toggle off if PvP threat |

---

## Returning-player notes

- **Radiation is much gentler than launch era** — most red monuments are passable in a cheap burlap+wood kit now; truly lethal rad is confined to a few reactor rooms.
- **Armor inserts** (since the Mar 2025 Crafting Update): crafted clothing/armor can roll **0–3 insert slots** for small bonuses — see [[Armor]].
- **NVG and the diving meta are unchanged** in structure but values get nudged each wipe; re-check the [[Built Different Update]] / [[Updates]] before assuming an exact number.
- **The wet penalty is the silent killer** — see [[Temperature and Cold]]. Snow + wet can push effective temp below −40 °C.

---

## Related

[[Armor]] · [[Temperature and Cold]] · [[Underwater Labs]] · [[Deep Sea Monuments]] · [[Comfort and Health Regen]] · [[Camp Fire]] · [[Keycards]] · [[Metal Facemask]] · [[Metal Chest Plate]] · [[Road Sign Kilt]] · [[Built Different Update]]

Sources: wiki.facepunch.com (diving.tank, diving.tank.double, diving.fins, diving.mask, nightvisiongoggles, hat.miner, hat.candle, mask.bandana, mask.balaclava, burlap.headwrap, hazmatsuit), rusthelp.com (night-vision-goggles), wiki.rustclash.com (snow-jacket, miners-hat), falconrust.com underwater diving guide, corrosionhour.com (miners-hat, candle-hat, burlap-headwrap), rust.fandom.com (Hazmat Suit, Snow Jacket, Hoodie), tradeit.gg arctic hazmat, ginx.tv best armor. Cold-% values approximate (rebalanced per wipe); rad points / diving seconds / NVG battery verified Jun 2026.

pages.title: Code Locks and Locker Etiquette
pages.body:
# Code Locks and Locker Etiquette

How a group shares door/box access without anyone being able to lock the others out, and the box-organization rules that keep a clan from imploding. For who-can-build (a separate system), see [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]].

## Code Lock basics (verified)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Craft cost | **100 metal fragments** |
| Workbench level | 0 (craftable from start) |
| Craft time | ~30 s |
| Secures | Doors, garage doors, [[Tool Cupboard]]s, boxes, [[Locker]]s, fridges |
| Failed-attempt lockout | **8 wrong tries → locked out 15 min** (anti-brute-force) |

Set a **4-digit master code** when placed. Holding E gives options to change the code, set a guest code, or remove the lock.

## Master code vs guest code — the clan-sharing trick

A [[Code Lock]] has **two codes**:

- **Master code:** full control. Whoever knows it can open the lock *and change/remove it*. Keep this to **leaders only**.
- **Guest code:** a separate PIN that lets someone **open** the entity but **not change the master code or remove the lock.** This is how you give the clan access to shared doors/boxes without handing anyone the power to lock you out or steal the lock.

> **Rule:** Hand out the **guest code** for shared base doors and the team core box; never give the master code to general members. If a member leaves or betrays, just change the guest code — the master stays yours.

Important: **locks are code-based, not team-based.** Being on the [[Team System]] does *not* add anyone to a lock; each member must be told the code. Conversely, clearing the [[Tool Cupboard]] auth list does **not** change any lock — after a betrayal you must rotate codes separately.

## What auth lets people pick up vs what locks protect

- A box/TC with **no lock** can be **picked up** by anyone who is [[Tool Cupboard|TC-authed]] in that zone. So an unlocked box in your base is wide open to your own clan. **Lock everything you care about**, even inside.
- A **locked** box can't be picked up or opened without the code, even by TC-authed members — this is exactly how you keep personal loot personal inside a shared base.

## Key Lock — the cheap alternative

The [[Key Lock]] is cheaper but worse for groups: it uses **physical keys** instead of a PIN. To share, you craft and hand out keys; anyone with a key can open it. There's no guest tier and keys take inventory slots. Fine for early-wipe twig doors; **clans use Code Locks** for everything that matters.

## Box / locker organization for a group

Pair this with the loot rules in [[Clan Roles and Coordination]]:

| Container | Lock | Who has access |
|---|---|---|
| **Team core box(es)** (meds, ammo, common mats, common guns) | Guest code | Whole clan |
| **Personal box / [[Locker]]** (1 per member) | Each member's own private code | Just that member |
| **Boom / high-value room** (explosives, keycards, components, rares) | Separate leader-only code | Leaders only |
| **[[Tool Cupboard]]** | Code Lock, leader-only code | Leaders (auth is separate; see [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]]) |

The [[Locker]] (28-slot, swap-loadout container) is the clan PvP-kit standard — each roamer keeps a pre-set fight loadout in their own locked locker for instant re-gear after death.

## Etiquette / opsec

- **Never type a code in public chat or say it on proximity voice** — it leaks to enemies. Share via Discord/DM only.
- **Don't reuse the same code everywhere.** If one box gets cracked or a member leaks it, segment so the damage is contained.
- **Avoid trivial codes** (1111, 1234) — they get guessed within the 8-try window.
- After **any roster change**, rotate the guest code on shared containers and re-do the [[Tool Cupboard]] auth list and [[Auto Turret]] lists.

Related: [[Code Lock]], [[Key Lock]], [[Locker]], [[Tool Cupboard]], [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]], [[Clan Roles and Coordination]], [[Clans and Groups]].

pages.title: Comfort and Health Regen
pages.body:
# Comfort and Health Regen

**Comfort** is a positive buff (0–100%) you get from being near comfortable objects. Its job is to **drive passive health regeneration** up to a cap. Understanding the comfort heal is how you go from "always low HP" to "topped up between fights for free."

---

## How passive healing works

Rust heals you slowly over time **only when conditions are met**. The gates:

- **Calories must be above 100.** At/below 100 calories, passive healing stops entirely (see [[Hunger and Thirst]]).
- **Hydration must be above ~50.** Dehydration cancels the comfort heal.
- **Higher comfort = higher heal-to cap.** Comfort doesn't heal faster so much as it raises the **ceiling** the passive regen will carry you to.

### Comfort heal-to caps
With calories above 100 and adequate hydration, the comfort level sets how high passive regen will take you:

| Comfort | Heals you up to |
|---|---|
| **50%** | **81 HP** |
| **75%** | **91 HP** |
| **100%** | **full (100 HP)** |

So sitting at a campfire with food in your gut will passively patch you back toward full — but only to the cap your comfort allows. To top **all the way to 100**, you need **100% comfort**.

---

## What gives comfort

| Source | Comfort | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **[[Camp Fire]]** | High | Also gives warmth ([[Temperature and Cold]]); the staple early heal spot |
| **Furnace** | High | Warmth + comfort while smelting |
| **[[Sleeping Bag]] / Bed** | Comfort while on it | Lie down to heal up safely at base |
| **Rug / chairs / furniture** | Moderate | Deco items add comfort in a built base |
| **Being inside near multiple sources** | Stacks toward 100% | Cluster heat/deco to hit 100% comfort for full heal |

Comfort **decays quickly** once you walk away from the source — it's a "stay near it" buff, not a lingering one.

---

## Putting it together — the free heal loop

After a fight, to recover HP without burning medkits:

1. Get **calories above 100** (eat cooked meat/food — see [[Hunger and Thirst]]).
2. Get **hydration above 50** (drink fresh water).
3. **Sit next to a [[Camp Fire]]** (or in a comfy base) to build comfort.
4. Passive regen ticks you up to the comfort cap (**81 / 91 / 100** depending on comfort %).
5. For a **full** heal, stack comfort to **100%** (multiple sources / lie on a [[Sleeping Bag]]).

This is the cheapest healing in the game — it costs only food and water, which you should have anyway.

---

## Why this matters for combat

- Topping off between fights via comfort saves your **[[Medical Syringe]]** and **[[Large Medkit]]** for actual combat / self-revive (see [[Wounded System]]).
- Keeping food/water high for the comfort heal **also** raises your downed-recovery chance from 20% to 45% — same prep, double benefit.

---

## Related

[[Survival Mechanics]] · [[Hunger and Thirst]] · [[Temperature and Cold]] · [[Wounded System]] · [[Camp Fire]] · [[Sleeping Bag]] · [[Large Medkit]] · [[Medical Syringe]]

pages.title: Console Commands & Streamer Tools
pages.body:
# Console Commands & Streamer Tools

Rust's F1 console is where you tune performance, review fights, record clips, and toggle streamer protections — all client-side, no admin rights needed. This page is the **returning-player cheat sheet for client convars and commands**. It is the companion to [[Settings and Binds]] (which covers keybinds and the in-game options menu) and [[Performance Settings]] (which covers the full FPS-optimization workflow). For reviewing suspicious deaths see [[Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters]].

> **Scope note:** Everything here runs on *your* client and works on any vanilla server you join. **Server admin commands** (spawning items, `noclip`, `teleport`, `kill <playerid>`, weather control, etc.) require ownership/RCON and live on the [[Running a Rust Server]] page — they will not work on servers you don't own and trying them just prints "command requires auth level 2."

> **"Built Different" (Unity 6) status — verify before trusting old guides.** The June 4 2026 wipe moved Rust to Unity 6. Many *graphics-setting* convars (shadow quality, water quality, grass) survived the engine swap unchanged, but the old garbage-collector hitch behaviour changed: Unity 6's incremental GC means the classic `gc.buffer 4096` launch-option trick matters less than it did in Unity 2021, and a couple of stutter-fix convars got renamed/removed between 2021 and 6. Where a value below is engine-sensitive it's flagged. When in doubt, type the command with no value in console — Rust prints the current value and valid range.

---

## Opening & using the console

- **`F1`** — toggle the developer console. (Rebindable; some players move it off F1 to free it for a quickslot — see [[Settings and Binds]].)
- Type a command and press **Enter**. Type a convar **with no value** to read its current value and range (e.g. just `fps.limit`).
- **Up/Down arrows** scroll command history.
- **Tab** autocompletes.
- The console has two tabs: **Console** (output/log) and **Console.log** history. Convars are `category.name value`; commands are usually a verb.
- Almost any command can be **bound to a key** with `bind <key> "<command>"` — see [[Settings and Binds]] for the bind syntax and a full recommended bind set. This page lists *which* commands are worth binding; that page covers *how*.

---

## 1. Performance & graphics convars

These are the ones a returning player actually touches. Full optimization pass (launch options, GPU settings, in-menu sliders) is on [[Performance Settings]] — this is the quick console layer.

| Convar | Range / value | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fps.limit <n>` | `-1` = uncapped, or any number | Caps frame rate. `fps.limit -1` removes the cap; setting e.g. `144` reduces GPU heat/coil whine and can *reduce* stutter on a too-fast CPU. |
| `client.directly.fps` | (read) | Prints current FPS to console. (The `perf 1`–`5` HUD overlay is the usual live readout — see below.) |
| `perf <0-5>` | 0–5 | The on-screen perf overlay. `perf 1` = FPS only; `perf 2` = +frametime/memory; `perf 5` = full graph. `perf 0` off. This is what most players bind. |
| `gc.collect` | (command) | **Manually runs the garbage collector.** Bind it to a key and tap it after looting/before a fight to flush a building memory hitch. The single most useful perf command in Rust. |
| `gc.buffer <MB>` | e.g. `2048`, `4096` | Buffer the GC works with before forcing a collection. Bigger = fewer but heavier collections. Common values 2048 / 4096. *Unity 6 note:* less impactful than in Unity 2021; set via launch option `-gc.buffer 4096` rather than in-session. |
| `pool.clear_memory` | (command) | Clears the entity memory pool after long sessions — run if FPS has slowly degraded over hours. |
| `graphics.shadowdistance <n>` | 50–1000 | Shadow render distance. Lower = big FPS gain in monuments. `0`-ish kills most shadows. |
| `graphics.shadowquality <0-3>` | 0–3 | Shadow resolution. 0 for max FPS. |
| `graphics.shadowcascades <n>` | 1, 2, or 4 | Shadow detail tiers. `1` (no cascades) = fastest. |
| `grass.displacement <0/1>` | 0 / 1 | Grass that bends as you walk. `0` saves frames in grassy biomes (and removes a movement tell). |
| `graphics.grassshadows <0/1>` | 0 / 1 | Shadows cast by grass. `0` for FPS. |
| `water.quality <0-2>` | 0–2 | Wave/ripple detail. `0` for FPS; matters on the [[Coast]] / [[Oil Rig]]. |
| `water.reflections <0-2>` | 0–2 | Reflection detail. `0` for FPS. |
| `mesh.quality <0-200>` | 0–200 | LOD aggressiveness (object detail vs. distance). Lower = props pop in closer but more FPS. |
| `terrain.quality <0-100>` | 0–100 | Terrain detail. Lower for FPS. |
| `graphics.dof <0/1>` | 0 / 1 | Depth of field. `0` — pure performance/clarity win, no downside in PvP. |
| `graphics.vm_fov_scale <0/1>` | 0 / 1 | Weapon (viewmodel) FOV scaling. `graphics.vm_fov_scale 0` shrinks the gun in your view = cleaner sightline. Popular PvP convar. |
| `effects.maxgibs <0-2000>` | 0–2000 | Max debris chunks from destroyed objects. **`effects.maxgibs 0`** recovers ~10–15 FPS during raids (no flying wall fragments). |
| `decor.layer_distance <n>` | distance | Cull small clutter decor sooner. Lower = FPS. |

**Returning-player quick perf bind** (drop into console once; details in [[Settings and Binds]]):
```
bind <key> gc.collect
bind <key> "perf 2"
```
Tap the GC bind whenever you feel a hitch starting.

---

## 2. Combat log — reviewing fights & cheat reports

The **combat log** is your built-in killcam-by-numbers: it lists recent damage you dealt and took with attacker/victim, weapon, body part, distance (in meters), and HP. Essential for "did that guy snap to my head through a wall?" and for filing a report — see [[Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters]].

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `combatlog` | Prints your recent combat events to console. **~10-second delay** — wait ~10s after a fight before reading. |
| `combatlog <n>` | Limit to the last `n` lines. |
| `combatlog_outgoing 1` / `combatlog_incoming 1` | Filter to only the damage you dealt / only what you took. |

**Reading it:** columns are roughly `time | attacker | victim | weapon | ammo | area(body part) | distance | old_hp → new_hp | info`. A `bullet` hit logged at e.g. `0.0m` distance with you fully behind cover, or impossible `head` strings back-to-back, is the kind of thing you screenshot for a report.

**Handy bind** — run combatlog the instant you open console:
```
bind f1 "consoletoggle;combatlog"
```
(Replace `f1` if you've moved your console key.)

---

## 3. Demo recording & playback — clips and evidence

Rust records full **demos** (`.dem` replays of everything around you), not just video. You can replay from any angle, freecam, slow-mo — ideal for montage clips *and* for capturing a cheater in motion. Full official docs: [Facepunch — Demos](https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/Demos).

### Recording
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `record <name>` | Start recording a demo to `<name>.dem`. |
| `demo.recorder` | Opens the recorder **UI** (type a name, hit record). Up-arrow in it reprints the last demo name for quick versioning. |
| `stop` | Stop the current recording. |

### Playback
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `demo.play <name>` | Load and play a recorded demo. (Or use the **playback icon, top-right of the main menu**, to browse/play/delete demos in a UI.) |
| `stop` | Exit playback back to the main menu. |
| `demo.timescale <x>` | Playback speed. `1` = realtime, `0` = pause, `0.25` = slow-mo, `2` = fast. |
| `demo.pause` / `demo.resume` | Pause / resume. |
| `demo.jump <sec>` | Jump to an absolute time (e.g. `demo.jump 120` → 2:00). |
| `demo.skip <sec>` | Skip relative (+/- seconds). |
| `demo.playernames` | List all players in the demo with their SteamID64 — get the offender's ID for a report. |
| `demo.togglehud` (or `demo.hud <0/1>`) | Show/hide the demo HUD (timecode, timescale, filename, date). Worth binding. |

**Where demos save:**
`...\Steam\steamapps\common\Rust\demos\` (`.dem` files). Note: a demo only contains what your client could see — it's not a server-wide recording.

**Workflow for a clip:** `record montage1` before a fight → `stop` after → main-menu playback browser → freecam + `demo.timescale 0.3` for the slow-mo beat → screen-capture with OBS/ShadowPlay.

---

## 4. Streamer mode & privacy

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `streamermode true` / `streamermode false` | **Streamer Mode.** Hides other players' real names (shows generic Rust-themed names), hides server names/IP, and mutes voice-name reveals — protects you from stream-snipers and keeps personal info off camera. |
| `streamermode.enable_voice_overlay 0/1` | Toggle whether the talking-player overlay shows under streamer mode. |

Turn it on **before** going live, not after — server name and your server-list are visible until you do.

---

## 5. Audio convars

All scale `0.00`–`1.00` unless noted. Useful for quickly killing music to hear footsteps, or dropping others' voice volume.

| Convar | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `audio.master <0-1>` | 0–1 | Master volume. |
| `audio.game <0-1>` | 0–1 | Game SFX (footsteps, gunfire, gibs). Keep high for PvP. |
| `audio.voices <0-5>` | 0–5 | **Other players' voice chat** volume. Note the range goes to 5 — you can *boost* quiet teammates above normal. |
| `audio.musicvolume <0-1>` | 0–1 | In-game ambient/event music. Many PvP players set `audio.musicvolume 0` to hear footsteps cleanly. |
| `audio.ambience <0-1>` | 0–1 | Environmental ambience (wind, ocean). |
| `audio.instruments <0-1>` | 0–1 | Playable instruments volume. |

---

## 6. Voice & chat

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chat.say "<text>"` | Send a **global** chat message from console. |
| `chat.teamsay "<text>"` | Send a **team-only** message (see [[Team System]]). |
| `chat.enabled true/false` | Show/hide the chat box entirely (declutter for clips). |
| `voice_loopback 1` | Hear your own mic back to test it before a raid call. (Set `0` after.) |
| `global.textchat 1/0` | Toggle text chat display. |

Push-to-talk key is set in the in-game options (see [[Settings and Binds]]). The **mic input device is NOT set in Rust at all** — Rust uses Steam's VoIP, so the device lives in Steam Settings → Voice → Voice Input Device. See [[Voice Chat and Audio Routing]].

---

## 7. Death, respawn & sleeping bags

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `kill` | **Kills your character.** The reliable way to respawn when you're stuck, glitched in terrain, or want to bag-spawn elsewhere. |
| `respawn` | Respawn at the beach/random spawn. (If `kill` doesn't take, this is the fallback.) |
| `respawn_sleepingbag <id>` | Respawn directly at a specific [[Sleeping Bags & Beds|sleeping bag/bed]] by its ID — useful when the spawn menu is laggy or you're rotating a raid through a [[Raid Bases and FOBs|FOB]]. |
| `respawn_sleepingbag_remove <id>` | Delete a bag by ID from console. |

`kill` does **not** drop you outside your gear — you still drop a lootable corpse with everything on you, so don't `kill` mid-field with a full inventory.

---

## 8. Connecting & utility

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `client.connect <ip:port>` | Connect to a server by IP (faster than the browser if you know the address). |
| `client.disconnect` | Leave the current server to the main menu. |
| `quit` | Close the game immediately. |
| `seed` | Print the current map's seed (for looking it up on [[RustMaps / Map Tools|a map site]]). |
| `world.size` | Print map size. |
| `find <text>` | **Search all convars/commands** containing `<text>` — e.g. `find grass` lists every grass setting. Your in-game discovery tool. |
| `console.clear` | Clear the console output. |

`find <text>` is the most underused command for returning players: type `find audio`, `find graphics`, `find demo` and Rust prints the live, current-patch list — more authoritative than any wiki, including this page.

---

## Quick reference — the binds worth setting

(Set these in console once; bind syntax + a fuller set on [[Settings and Binds]].)

```
bind <key> gc.collect              # flush stutter before a fight
bind <key> "perf 2"                # toggle perf overlay
bind <key> "consoletoggle;combatlog"   # open console straight to combat log
bind <key> demo.togglehud          # clean demo HUD for clips
bind <key> "audio.musicvolume 0"   # mute music to hear footsteps
```

---

## Related pages
- [[Settings and Binds]] — keybinds, options menu, the bind command itself
- [[Performance Settings]] — full FPS optimization (launch options, GPU, sliders)
- [[Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters]] — using combatlog + demos to spot and report cheaters
- [[Running a Rust Server]] — server-side admin commands (spawn, noclip, teleport, weather)
- [[Team System]] — team chat and grouping
- [[Returning Player Changelog]] — what changed in "Built Different" / Unity 6

---

## Sources
- [Facepunch Wiki — Demos](https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust/Demos) (official demo command syntax & save path)
- [Rustafied — Useful Rust Console Commands](https://www.rustafied.com/useful-rust-experimental-console-commands) (kill/respawn, fps.limit, streamermode, vm_fov_scale)
- [Corrosion Hour — Rust Combat Log Command](https://www.corrosionhour.com/rust-combat-log-command/) (combatlog usage, ~10s delay)
- [Steam Guide — All options-menu settings as console commands + values](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3180714936) (graphics/audio convar ranges)
- [IQON — Optimize Rust for Performance (2026)](https://iqondigital.com/learn/games/optimize-rust-performance) (gc.buffer/gc.collect, effects.maxgibs, pool.clear_memory)
- [GameHelper — Fix Rust Lag Spikes 2026](https://www.gamehelper.io/games/rust/articles/how-to-fix-common-performance-issues-in-rust-complete-troubleshooting-guide) (Unity 6 stutter behaviour)
- [Switchblade Gaming — Best Rust PC Settings 2026](https://www.switchbladegaming.com/game-settings/rust-best-settings/)
- [Sportskeeda — Best Rust Graphics Settings for Performance](https://www.sportskeeda.com/mmo/best-rust-graphics-settings-performance-how-get-maximum-fps)
- [LagoFast — Rust Commands 2025](https://www.lagofast.com/en/blog/rust-commands-2025/)

pages.title: First Day Guide
pages.body:
# First Day Guide

Hour-by-hour route for wipe day (or your first day on a fresh server). Assumes vanilla rates, solo. The 2026 twist vs 2023: **scrap alone no longer tiers you up** — you need monument [[Blueprint Fragments]] for WB2/WB3, and research got cheap (15/30/60/120 scrap by tier).

> Brand new or very rusty? **Tutorial Island** (added Mar 2024) is offered on first spawn on supported servers — a safe solo island teaching gather/craft/build/cook. ~30–45 min, worth it once.

## Hour 0–1: Beach to backpack

1. Spawn. Immediately note nearest road, river, and small monuments on the map (G).
2. Punch a tree → rock node. Craft **Stone Hatchet** + **Stone Pickaxe**, then a **Spear**.
3. Farm: ~3,000 wood, ~1,500 stone, hit every barrel on the road (scrap + components).
4. Kill 2–3 animals (boar/deer) for cloth/meat, or pick hemp — you want **~200 cloth** early.
5. Craft **Sleeping Bag** (30 cloth) and drop it the moment you find your build spot — you have a 15-respawn-point cap ([[Sleeping Bag]]), shared cooldown for bags within 50 m.
6. Craft **Hunting Bow** (200 wood + 50 cloth, no workbench) + ~30 arrows. The bow is still the king of day-one fights.

**Build spot criteria (solo):** off the road sightlines, near (not at) 1–2 small monuments with [[Recycler]] (monument recyclers run 5s/120% yield — safe-zone ones only 8s/80%), near a river or lake (rivers are wider/deeper since World Update 2.0 — you swim across now), and NOT in the jungle biome on wipe day (tigers/crocs/snakes will end your naked runs).

## Hour 1–2: The 2x1 and Tool Cupboard

1. Build a **2x1 stone** (or wood→stone upgrade) with airlock: foundation ~200 wood each in twig, upgrade walls to stone (300 stone/wall).
2. Place **[[Tool Cupboard]]** (1,000 wood) FIRST, inside, hidden. Stock it with upkeep wood/stone.
3. Doors: wood door (300 wood) day one, **Sheet Metal Door (150 metal frags)** by tonight. **[[Code Lock]] = 100 metal frags** — get this on ASAP (key locks get you killed).
4. **Furnace** + smelt frags. Place **[[Workbench Level 1]]: 500 wood + 100 metal fragments** (note: **no scrap cost anymore** — removed Nov 2025).
5. Craft a **Small [[Backpack]]** (50 cloth + 5 sewing kits, WB1, 12 slots — it drops on death but doubles your farm runs).

## Hour 2–4: Scrap + the fragment race

Your two currencies now: **scrap** (research/tech tree, vehicle purchases) and **Basic Blueprint Fragments** (the WB2 gate).

**Basic Fragment sources (verified vs rusthelp.com):**
- [[Green Keycard]] puzzle-room pickup = **1 Basic Fragment**; [[Blue Keycard]] puzzle-room pickup = **2 Basic Fragments** (so a green→blue chain is ~3 toward your 5)
- Medium/large monument crates (loot tables reshuffled in the Oct 2025 update — new puzzles at [[The Dome]], [[Ferry Terminal]], [[Radtown]])
- **Supply Drops** ([[Airdrop]])
