- Junkpile/roaming scientists can drop them — roadside scientists alone can carry you most of the way to 5
- Recycling a looted [[Workbench Level 2]] also returns Basic Fragments

**Fragment math (verified):** WB2 needs exactly **5 Basic**; WB3 needs **5 Advanced**. **20 Basic Fragments combine into 1 Advanced** — so in a pinch you can grind green/blue puzzles all the way to WB3, but it's 100 Basic for the 5 Advanced; far faster to loot Advanced directly from elite/hackable crates (see Hour-evening below).

Route: nearest small monument with a green puzzle → grab a [[Green Keycard]] from drawers/desks → run the puzzle → recycle components at the monument recycler (120% yield) → repeat at a second monument. Bow + nail gun or **Handmade SMG** (T1 gun added Nov 2024) is enough for junkpile scientists.

## Hour 4–6: Workbench 2 and first real guns

1. **[[Workbench Level 2]] = 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + 5 Basic Blueprint Fragments.** Place it the moment you have the five fragments — this is the single biggest power spike of the wipe.
2. Research is cheap now: **15 scrap (T0) / 30 (T1) / 60 (T2) / 120 (T3)** per item, and the tech tree is one station with tabs + multi-node path-unlock (Apr 2026) — you can click a target item and pay the whole path.
3. Priority T2 unlocks for a solo: **SAR or Python → garage door → ladder hatch → medical syringes → road-sign armor**. (See [[Solo Survival Guide]] for the full priority list.)
4. Expand the 2x1 → 2x2 or honeycombed core; upgrade core to sheet metal. **Explosive protection caps at 75%** (May 2025) so perfect armor stacking matters less than layers ([[Building Guide]]).

## Evening: bank the wipe

- Hide 2–3 **stash spots** (small stashes) with a gun + meds away from base.
- Pair base with [[Rust+ Companion App]]; place a **Smart Alarm** on your TC room if you have the electricity.
- Food: cook meat; raw food spoils in **6h**, cooked in **24h** (Mar 2025 spoilage system) — a powered fridge pauses it, but day one just cook-and-carry.
- If flush on scrap: **Workbench Level 3 = 1,000 metal frags + 100 HQM + 5 Advanced Blueprint Fragments** (no scrap cost). **Advanced Fragments drop ×2 at 100% from Locked/Hackable Crates** and at [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnel]], [[Nuclear Missile Silo]], and the [[Underwater Lab]]; **Elite Crates only ~10% for ×1** (unreliable). So one hackable crate hack = nearly half a WB3. That's a day-2/3 goal via [[Launch Site]], [[Oil Rig]] (small off-hours), [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] tiers.

## Day-one don'ts (2026 edition)

- Don't roam at night with loot — gunshots are audible at **400/500/600 m** by weapon class (Sep 2025), and wolves/predators use real stalking AI now.
- Don't bother gamma-cheating the night; it's dead (shader nightlight, Mar 2024).
- Don't recycle guns/armor you might use — research is only 15–60 scrap now; researching beats recycling for almost everything usable.
- Don't build on tier-0 jungle edges or directly on new Deep Sea coast event zones ([[Deep Sea]] — no building, elite loot, opens/closes).

Related: [[Solo Survival Guide]], [[Wipe Schedule]], [[Blueprint Fragments]], [[Building Guide]], [[Recycler]], [[Monuments Index]].

pages.title: Getting Started (Rust)
pages.body:
# Getting Started (Rust)

Operations manual for a **returning solo/duo/trio PC player** (last played ~2023). Rust in 2026 is a different game in three big ways:

1. **Progression rework (Oct–Nov 2025).** The scrap-only grind is dead. [[Workbench Level 2]] needs 5 **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]**, [[Workbench Level 3]] needs 5 **Advanced Blueprint Fragments** — found only at monuments, crates, and airdrops. Research is now cheap (15/30/60/120 scrap by tier). You can no longer "buy" your way up with roadside scrap; you must hit monuments.
2. **Blueprints wipe monthly on every official server** (since Nov 2025's "Pivot Or Die"). Everyone restarts at tier 1 each force wipe. Community servers can still keep BPs.
3. **Anti-cheat actually improved.** [[Premium Servers]] (Steam inventory ≥ $15, ~4x fewer cheaters) and optional TPM 2.0 + Secure Boot servers exist. Solo play on officials is more survivable than it was in 2023.

> **Pick your mode deliberately (July 2026, [[Common Ground Update]]).** Official servers come in **Vanilla**, **Softcore**, and **Hardcore** flavors — and as of Common Ground they play very differently:
> - **Vanilla** = the classic full-loss game this whole vault is tuned for (default assumption below).
> - **Softcore** = lower-stress: keep ~50% of your inventory on death, **2x gather** (double ore/wood/food), and **timed raid windows** (structures only breakable 6-9 PM local; an active TC blocks structure raids off-window). Good for a returning/relaxed player; progression is fast and offline-raid fear is low.
> - **Hardcore** = the punishing mode (fog of war, no gun crafting, compass item) — **clans are disabled here**.
> - **Clan system** (Clan Table: roles, clan chat, member map dots) is available on **Vanilla + Softcore**, useful once you're trio+. See [[Clans and Groups]].

## Pages in this folder

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [[Wipe Schedule]] | Force wipe = first Thursday monthly @ 19:00 UTC; map vs BP wipes; weekly/biweekly community cadences |
| [[Server Types]] | Vanilla / Softcore / Hardcore / Primitive / 2x-5x modded / Premium — and how to pick one as a returning solo |
| [[Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters]] | EAC + ban types, aimbot/ESP/spinbot/no-clip tells, combat log evidence, F7 reporting, Premium as the #1 mitigation, realistic expectations |
| [[First Day Guide]] | Hour-by-hour: spawn → farm → 2x1 starter → bow → WB1 → first monument runs |
| [[Solo Survival Guide]] | The 2026 solo meta: fragment-hunting windows, base design, when to fight |
| [[Team System]] | Team UI (max 8), the July 2025 Party system, in-game pings and markers |
| [[Clans and Groups]] | How a clan actually operates: team≠access, onboarding checklist, scaling past a trio |
| [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]] | TC auth limits/radius, why clans run multiple TCs, clearing the list, betrayal-proofing |
| [[Clan Roles and Coordination]] | Farmer/builder/raider/PvP split, loot rules, shift scheduling, comms |
| [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]] | Master vs guest codes, what locks vs auth protect, box organization for a group |
| [[Raid Bases and FOBs]] | Forward Operating Bases, raid roles, online vs offline, rocket-count scouting math |
| [[Settings and Binds]] | Essential keybinds, autorun, gesture wheel (hold B), ping system, combat log |
| [[Map, Grid & Callouts]] | Reading the map (G), the 150 m grid (A0=NW, letter+number), monument icons, death marker, respawn UI, ping wheel, duo/trio comms discipline |
| [[Rust+ Companion App]] | Pairing, Smart Switches, Smart Alarms, map/team from your phone |
| [[Performance Settings]] | FPS tuning for a high-end PC (DLSS, shadow cascades, `-gc.buffer`, Unity 6 mouse-stutter note) |
| [[Survival Mechanics]] | Hub for the survival layer: the four meters, what kills returning players, downed-system overview |
| [[Wounded System]] | **Must-read for returners:** crawling vs incapacitated, 20%/45%/10% recovery, 45s timer, medkit-in-belt revive, give-up |
| [[Hunger and Thirst]] | Calories (max 500), hydration (max 250), starvation < 40 / dehydration < 25, food spoilage, never drink the sea |
| [[Temperature and Cold]] | Cold damage below −7 °C, biome day/night temps, wet penalty, snow-biome death trap, clothing warmth |
| [[Clothing & Environmental Gear]] | Non-armor apparel: warmth/rad/diving/utility — hazmat, snow jacket, burlap/hide, diving tank+fins+mask, NVG, miners hat, "what to wear for X" |
| [[Comfort and Health Regen]] | Comfort heal-to caps (50%→81, 75%→91, 100%→full), the free post-fight heal loop |

## The 60-second version of "what do I do this wipe"

1. Spawn day (Thursday): beach → stone tools → [[First Day Guide]] starter 2x1 with [[Tool Cupboard]] + [[Code Lock]].
2. Craft [[Workbench Level 1]] (500 wood + 100 metal frags — **no scrap cost anymore**).
3. Run [[Green Keycard]]/[[Blue Keycard]] puzzles and junkpile scientists for 5 **Basic Blueprint Fragments** → place [[Workbench Level 2]] (500 frags + 20 HQM + the 5 fragments).
4. Tech-tree/research what you need (research is 15/30/60/120 scrap by tier — cheap).
5. Elite/hackable crates for 5 **Advanced Blueprint Fragments** → [[Workbench Level 3]] (1,000 frags + 100 HQM + fragments).
6. Endgame chase: 9 rare, non-craftable [[Workbench Augmentations]] (added May 2026).

Related (other folders): [[Monuments Index]], [[Weapons Index]], [[Raid Costs]], [[Building Guide]], [[Recycler]], [[Skins and the Skin Economy]], [[Twitch and Kick Drops]].

pages.title: Hunger and Thirst
pages.body:
# Hunger and Thirst

The two consumption meters that drain constantly and will kill you if ignored: **Calories (hunger)** and **Hydration (thirst)**. Keeping both high also doubles your odds of standing back up in the [[Wounded System]], so this isn't just chip damage — it's a combat stat.

---

## Calories / Hunger

- **Max: 500.** The bar drains slowly and continuously; it drains faster when you sprint, fight, or are cold.
- **No penalty for being merely low** — you can run around in the 100–400 range fine.
- **Stop passive healing at â‰¤ 100 calories.** To benefit from comfort healing you must stay **above 100**. This is the most important number to remember.
- **Starvation status applies under ~40 calories.** Below this you take **damage over time** (HP bleed) that continues until you eat or die. Damage ramps the lower you go (worst near ~15).
- **Fix:** eat. Cooked meat, berries, mushrooms, pumpkins, corn, fish, cooked food from a [[Cooking Workbench]]. Cooked food restores more than raw and is safer (no food poisoning).

### Food sources (early → late)
| Source | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Berries / mushrooms / pumpkins | Forage bushes | Tier-0 instant calories; weak |
| Raw meat → **cooked meat** | Hunt animals (chicken, boar, deer, wolf), cook on [[Camp Fire]] | Cook it — raw meat can cause food poisoning |
| Fish | [[Fishing]] / fish traps | Plentiful near water |
| Canned food | Loot crates / monuments | Ready to eat, found loot |
| **Buff pies** | [[Cooking Workbench]] (Mar 2025 update) | 8 pies give stat buffs — endgame food |

---

## Hydration / Thirst

- **Max: 250.** Drains **roughly 5× slower than hunger** — you'll get hungry first.
- **Heat and activity drain it faster.** Desert biome + sprinting + fighting = drink more often.
- **Dehydrated status applies under ~25 hydration** → **damage over time**.
- **Below ~50 hydration you lose the comfort heal** (comfort stops working when thirst is too low).
- **Fully dehydrated = movement penalty:** you slow down, and at the extreme you **cannot run at all** — a death sentence in a fight.
- **Fix:** drink. Hold E on fresh water sources, or carry a [[Water Bottle]] / [[Water Jug]]; collect rain with a [[Water Catcher]].

### Water sources & a critical gotcha
| Source | Drinkable? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Rivers, lakes, ponds (fresh) | âœ… Yes | Free, safe; refill bottles here |
| Rain via [[Water Catcher]] | âœ… Yes | Base water supply |
| Water Bottle / Water Jug | âœ… Yes | Portable; fill at fresh water |
| **Ocean / sea water** | âŒ **No** | **Salt water actively REDUCES hydration** — never drink the sea |
| Radiated water (some monuments) | âš ï¸ | Gives rads; avoid without protection |

> **Returning-player trap:** drinking ocean water to "top up" makes you *more* thirsty. Only drink fresh water.

---

## How the two interact with the rest of survival

- **Recovery odds:** full food + water raises crawl recovery in the [[Wounded System]] from **20% to 45%**. Treat eating/drinking as pre-fight prep.
- **Comfort heal gate:** you need calories **> 100** AND hydration **> 50** for the [[Comfort and Health Regen]] passive heal to do its job near a fire.
- **Temperature link:** being cold and being wet ([[Temperature and Cold]]) interacts with thirst — extreme heat speeds thirst drain.

---

## Food spoilage (Mar 2025 Crafting Update — new since 2023)

Food now **spoils over time** — a major change for returning players:

- **Raw food: ~6 hours** before it rots.
- **Cooked food: ~24 hours** before it rots.
- **Spoilage is PAUSED inside a powered [[Fridge]]** (or [[Mini Fridge]], 18 slots) — store perishables there.

So you can no longer hoard a chest of raw meat forever; cook it, or fridge it.

---

## Practical rules

1. **Keep calories above 100** at all times (enables healing) — eat cooked meat before it dips.
2. **Never let thirst hit 25** — carry a full water bottle.
3. **Never drink ocean water.**
4. **Top off food + water before any fight** — it nearly doubles your wounded-recovery chance.
5. **Cook and/or fridge food** — raw spoils in ~6h now.

---

## Related

[[Survival Mechanics]] · [[Temperature and Cold]] · [[Comfort and Health Regen]] · [[Wounded System]] · [[Camp Fire]] · [[Cooking Workbench]] · [[Fridge]] · [[Water Catcher]] · [[Fishing]]

pages.title: Instruments, Boombox & Social Items
pages.body:
# Instruments, Boombox & Social Items

The non-combat "fun" layer of Rust: the stuff you build to mess with friends, decorate a base, run a shop, sign your turf, or stage a base-party between wipes. None of it wins fights, but on a long solo/duo/trio wipe it's a big chunk of why people keep logging in. This page is the durable catalog of every social / roleplay / cosmetic item: musical instruments, the Boombox + cassettes, the Drone + Drone Marketplace, neon signs and picture frames, the Telephone, the Instant Camera, fireworks, and seasonal cosmetic deployables.

Cross-references: [[Deployables]] (base-interior placeables), [[Vending and Shops]] (the marketplace ordering system and shopfronts), [[Seasonal Events]] (when the festive cosmetics drop), [[Electricity]] (most of these need power).

> **Numbers verified June 2026.** Craft costs and DLC gating below were checked against rusthelp.com and wiki.facepunch.com. Where a number isn't on this page it's because the source didn't list it cleanly — don't assume.

---

## The big picture: what's free vs. paid (DLC)

A lot of the "fun" layer is gated behind cheap one-time **paid DLC**. Important nuance that catches returning players: **if anyone on the server owns the DLC and crafts the item, anyone can use/deploy it** — you don't all need to buy it. You only need the DLC to *craft from the blueprint*.

| Layer | DLC required to craft? | DLC name |
|-------|------------------------|----------|
| **Musical instruments** (10 of them) | Yes | **Instruments Pack** (~$10, Dec 2019) |
| **Boombox / Cassette Recorder / cassettes** | Yes | **Voice Props** DLC |
| **Instant Camera** | Yes | **Sunburn** DLC |
| **Drone + Drone Marketplace** | No | base game |
| **Telephone** | No | base game (tech tree) |
| **Neon signs / picture frames / wood signs** | No (frames base game; some sign *skins* are paid) | base game |
| **Fireworks** | No | base game (craftable) |
| **Party hats / festive cosmetics** | No | seasonal drops / event |

So: instruments, boombox and the instant camera all want a few dollars of DLC; drones, phones, signs and fireworks are free and craftable.

---

## Musical instruments (Instruments Pack DLC)

Ten craftable instruments. You equip one like a tool and play it. Great for base-parties, busking at [[Outpost]]/[[Bandit Camp]] safe zones, or trolling over proximity voice. Each is a held item, not a deployable.

### The roster + craft cost

| Instrument | Type | Craft cost |
|-----------|------|-----------|
| **Junkyard Drum Kit** | Percussion (held drum set) | 100 metal frags + 200 wood |
| **Wheelbarrow Piano** | Keys | 100 metal frags + 200 wood |
| **Sousaphone** | Brass (the "tuba") | 100 metal frags |
| **Plumber's Trumpet** | Brass | 75 metal frags |
| **Shovel Bass** | Strings (bass) | 75 metal frags + 50 wood |
| **Jerry Can Guitar** | Strings (guitar) | 50 metal frags + 25 wood |
| **Xylobones** | Percussion (bone xylophone) | 50 bone fragments |
| **Pan Flute** | Wind (flute) | 20 metal frags + 5 cloth |
| **Cowbell** | Percussion | (cheap; metal frags) |
| **Canbourine** | Percussion (tambourine) | (cheap; metal frags) |

(Cowbell and Canbourine are the joke-cheap ones — more cowbell.)

### How to play — the note keys

Equip the instrument, then play notes on the **numpad** by default:

| Numpad key | Note |
|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | C |
| 2 | D |
| 3 | E |
| 4 | F |
| 5 | G |
| 6 | A |
| 7 | B |

Modifiers:
- **Numpad +** → play the **sharp** of the note
- **Numpad Enter** → shift **down an octave**
- Press **H** to convert your *whole keyboard* into a wider note range (much more expressive than the 7-key numpad — this is the "real piano" mode).

Drum kits map differently (set in **Options > Controls > Instruments**), with each numpad/key bound to a specific drum piece: Floor tom (A#), 2nd tom (G#), Snare right (C), Bass drum 1 (C#), Bass drum 2 (D), Snare left (D#), Broken snare (E), Closed hi-hat L (E#), Loose hi-hat (F), Small tom (F#), Closed hi-hat R (G), Cowbell (B), Ride cymbal (B#), Crash cymbal. You can rebind all of these.

### MIDI and recorded playback (the power-user trick)

- **MIDI input is supported by default** for pianos and drum kits — plug in a real MIDI keyboard/drum pad and play live in-game. (Enable in the experimental options if it doesn't pick up.)
- Rust can **play back `.mid` files natively**: drop a MIDI file in the game's `/instruments` folder and run the console command `instruments.playrecording <filename>`. This is how people get a Jerry Can Guitar to rip a full song automatically. See the [[Commands]] / console reference for syntax.

---

## Boombox, Cassette Recorder & cassettes (Voice Props DLC)

The audio-prop set. Lets you play recorded sound, internet radio stations, or your own voice recordings out loud in the world. **Craft requires the Voice Props DLC; anyone can use a deployed one.**

### Boom Box

A large powered speaker that plays internet radio stations or an inserted cassette.

- **Craft cost:** 200 wood + 100 metal frags + 20 cloth (Workbench 1)
- **Use:** look at it, hold **USE (E)** → menu with **Open** (insert a cassette) and **Radio Settings** (pick a radio station).
- **Audio range:** ~30 meters (about 10 foundations).
- Needs power to stay on as a fixed deployable. There is also a **portable / mobile boombox** form factor used as a held item; both play the same cassettes.

### Cassette Recorder + cassettes

A held recorder you use to *capture* audio (your mic / world sound) onto a cassette, which then plays back through a Cassette Recorder, Boom Box, or portable boombox.

- **Cassette Recorder craft cost:** 75 metal frags (Workbench 1).
- **Controls:** **[attack]** plays the inserted cassette · **[attack2]** records new audio · **[+reload]** throws the recorder.
- **Recording flow:** right-click → short rewind animation → **3-second countdown** → then you record. Press **Esc** to stop early.
- **Cassette types (recording length):**

| Cassette | Length |
|----------|:---:|
| Cassette – Short | 10 seconds |
| Cassette – Medium | 20 seconds |
| Cassette – Long | 30 seconds |

Classic uses: leaving a taunting voice message in a base you raided, a looping ad outside your shop, ambient music in a base-bar, or jump-scares near a loot room. Recycle value of the recorder is ~45 metal frags (radtown) / 30 (safezone).

---

## Drone & Drone Marketplace

The Drone is a small remote-controlled flying camera-bot; the **Drone Marketplace** is the safe-zone ordering terminal that uses courier drones to fetch goods for you. Both are base-game, no DLC.

### The Drone (RC)

- A deployable drone you **control remotely** (pilot it FPV). Used for scouting, recon over a target base, or just messing around.
- Plays into the same RC ecosystem as RC cars / the [[Electricity|computer station]] camera network — you can wire it into a Computer Station and fly it from a chair.

### The Drone Marketplace (safe-zone delivery)

This is the **shop-by-drone** system. Two Marketplace terminals exist, one each at the **[[Outpost]]** and **[[Bandit Camp]]** safe zones.

How it works:
1. At a Marketplace terminal you open a **map of every public vending machine** on the server (both NPC shops and player-run [[Vending and Shops|vending machines]]).
2. Add items to a cart and **place an order**.
3. A **courier drone** flies to that vendor, buys the goods, and returns them to a **pickup container** at the terminal.
4. **Delivery fee: 20 scrap per order**, on top of the item's price.
5. After the drone returns, you have **~5 minutes** to grab the goods before they become free-for-all to anyone at the terminal.

Why it matters: you can buy from a faraway player shop *without crossing the map*, so you never risk the loot in transit — the goods only exist on you once you're standing in the safe zone. Huge for solos buying from distant bulk sellers. Pair this with [[Vending and Shops]] for running your own end of the trade.

---

## Telephone

Call other telephones on the island. Base game, learned from the tech tree.

- **Craft cost:** 50 wood + 100 metal frags + 1 tech trash (Workbench 1).
- **Tech tree:** ~195 scrap total to research (30 to unlock the node + 165). Also loots from Underwater crates (~1.1% on advanced underwater crates) and scientists.
- **Buy it instead:** Outpost vending machines sell one for **~50 scrap** — usually faster than researching.
- **Power:** barely any — a single steady volt into the **power** socket keeps it on. See [[Electricity]].
- **Phone numbers:** each phone gets a **new random phone number every time you place it**. Pick it up and re-place → new number.
- **Use:** look at the phone, dial another phone's number, and talk over voice in real time across the map. There's an in-phone **contacts/phone book** so you can save numbers. Deployable on boats/[[Tugboat|tugboats]] too.

Practical uses: a shop hotline so buyers can reach you, coordinating with allies across the map, or a "front desk" phone for a roleplay/trade base.

---

## Signs, neon signs & picture frames

The drawing/decoration layer. All base-game craftable (frames and wood signs); some neon-sign *skins* are paid, but the canvas is free. You paint directly on them in-game with a paint UI, or auto-paint images with the third-party tool **Rustangelo** (free; PRO tier paid).

| Item | What it is |
|------|-----------|
| **Wooden signs** (small/large, single/double, hanging, post) | Cheap paintable canvases for shop labels, base art, warnings. |
| **Portrait Picture Frame** | Portrait-oriented paintable canvas. |
| **Landscape Picture Frame** | Landscape-oriented paintable canvas. |
| **Neon signs** (pack of 5 sizes) | Paintable signs that **glow when powered** — wire into [[Electricity]]. Great base lighting + nighttime branding. |

Notes:
- Painting is done in an editor when you look at the sign and press USE; you draw, place text, or stamp shapes. Larger signs = more pixels = more detail.
- **Rustangelo** loads any image and auto-paints it onto a sign pixel-by-pixel; complex images take minutes to an hour to paint and work on any server.
- Neon signs are the modern way to light + brand a [[Vending and Shops|shop]] or compound entrance; they need a power feed but draw little.

---

## Instant Camera (Sunburn DLC)

A Polaroid-style camera. Take in-world photos you can mount on walls in a picture frame or gift to other players.

- **Craft cost:** 1 gear + 75 metal frags.
- **DLC:** requires the **Sunburn DLC** to learn the recipe (anyone can use a crafted one).
- **Controls:** **primary fire** = take photo · **secondary fire** = zoom in/out · **reload** = change focus mode.
- The printed photo is a real item you can hand to someone, store, or frame. Memory-lane material for a long wipe, evidence of a raid, or shop decoration.

---

## Fireworks

Craftable pyrotechnics — base game, no DLC. They're a "Fun" category item; you place them and ignite (some are wired to power via the [[Electricity]] system / Rustrician). Despite being associated with [[Seasonal Events|New Year]], they are **permanently craftable**, not seasonal-locked.

### Types

| Type | Effect |
|------|--------|
| **Volcano Firework** (white / red / violet) | A big ground sparkler that shoots a fountain straight up. |
| **Roman Candle** (blue / green / red / violet) | Fires ~10 balls into the air in sequence. |
| **Boomer / Mortar** (blue, green, red, orange, violet, pattern) | Each launches ~10 individual aerial explosions. |
| **Champagne Boomer** | Multi-stage: several large bursts, each trailing ~5 smaller explosions. |

### Craft cost (representative — White Volcano Firework)

- **20 metal frags + 15 gunpowder** (Workbench-dependent craft time; stack size 20).

Other variants follow a similar recipe. Common uses: New Year base-parties, victory celebrations after a big raid, or wiring a mortar volley to a [[Electricity|timer/switch]] for an automated show. (There are also paid **Small / Large Fireworks Pack** *skins* on the item store, ~$3.59–$3.99, purely cosmetic re-skins.)

---

## Party hats & seasonal cosmetic deployables

These rotate in during [[Seasonal Events]] and are mostly **free, time-limited drops** rather than craftables. They have no combat value — pure flair.

| Item | When | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| **Party Hat** | New Year / events | Cosmetic head wearable; spawns around festive events. |
| **Christmas decorations** (lights, stockings, trees, presents, snowman) | Christmas event | See [[Christmas Event]] — Santa sleigh, gift drops, snowballs, decorative deployables. |
| **Easter eggs / bunny ears** | Easter event | See [[Easter Event]] — egg hunt cosmetics. |
| **Halloween cosmetics** (pumpkins, candy, spooky deployables) | Halloween event | See [[Halloween Event]] — wearable masks, jack-o'-lanterns. |
| **Fireworks** (above) | Year-round, themed at New Year | Craftable, not seasonal-locked. |

For exactly when these are live and what drops, the authority is [[Seasonal Events]] plus the individual event pages.

---

## Pets & companions

Rust has **no persistent tameable pet system** for solos in the survival sense — you can't tame a wolf to follow you. The closest things:

- **Chickens / Chicken Coop:** part of the [[Farming]] / industrial-farming layer — a coop produces eggs, not a "pet" companion. (Tie-in to food, not RP.)
- **Horses ([[Horses]]):** the closest to a companion — you tame/claim and ride them, stable them, and they have stamina/breeds. They live in the [[Vehicles]] layer, not here.
- **Frankenstein / "Frankenstein's Monster":** a **Halloween-event** stitched-together companion construct — you assemble body parts and it follows/fights for you during the event window. Seasonal only; see [[Halloween Event]].

So: no year-round pet, but horses are your durable "companion," and Frankenstein is the seasonal novelty.

---

## Quick reference — the whole fun layer

| Item | DLC? | Power? | Headline use |
|------|:---:|:---:|------|
| Instruments (x10) | Instruments Pack | No | Live music / MIDI playback |
| Boom Box | Voice Props | Yes | Radio stations + cassette playback |
| Cassette Recorder + cassettes | Voice Props | No (held) | Record + replay your voice/audio |
| Drone (RC) | No | — | Remote scouting |
| Drone Marketplace | No | (terminal) | Safe-zone shop delivery (20 scrap/order) |
| Telephone | No | 1 volt | Call other phones across the map |
| Wood/neon signs + picture frames | No* | Neon needs power | Paintable art / shop branding |
| Instant Camera | Sunburn | No | Take + frame Polaroid photos |
| Fireworks | No | optional (wired) | Pyrotechnics, base-parties |
| Party hats / seasonal cosmetics | No | No | Festive flair (event-limited) |
| Frankenstein companion | No | — | Halloween-only follower |

\*Some neon-sign and firework re-skins are paid cosmetics on the item store, but the functional item is free/craftable.

---

## See also

- [[Deployables]] — the broader base-interior placeable catalog
- [[Vending and Shops]] — running shops + the marketplace ordering system

pages.title: Map, Grid & Callouts
pages.body:
# Map, Grid & Callouts

How to read the Rust map, name a location precisely, and talk to your team so the right person is shooting the right enemy at the right grid square. For a returning solo/duo/trio player this is the single highest-leverage "soft skill" in the game: a duo with clean callouts beats a disorganized quad. This page covers the in-game map (G), the grid coordinate system, monument icons, map size, the death screen and respawn UI, map markers and the ping wheel, the compass, and a comms-discipline section for small teams.

Related: [[Rust Monuments]] · [[Team System]] · [[Rust+ Companion App]] · [[Settings and Binds]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]]

---

## The in-game map (G)

- **Open it by holding `G`.** The map stays visible only while the key is held — release `G` and it closes. (Default bind; rebindable in [[Settings and Binds]].) Some players bind it to a more comfortable key, or use a toggle bind, because you open the map constantly.
- **While the map is open you are standing still and fully exposed.** You don't go into a safe menu — your body is just sitting there. Open the map behind cover, inside your base, or while crouched in a bush. Players and NPCs will happily kill you mid-map-check.
- **Hardcore game mode disables the map entirely** (no map, no compass, no death marker). On vanilla/softcore/premium servers you have the full map. See [[Server Types]].

### Map controls

| Action | Control |
|---|---|
| Open/hold map | Hold `G` |
| Pan | Hold **right mouse button** and drag |
| Zoom | **Mouse wheel** (up = in, down = out) |
| Recenter on yourself | **Focus** button (top-right of map) |
| Toggle the coordinate grid | **Grid** button (top-right) |
| Your character | **Yellow dot** with a caret showing facing direction |
| Teammates | **Green dots** with names, updated in real time (requires being in a [[Team System|team]]) |

The grid overlay was added all the way back in Devblog 181 and is **off by default** — turn it on once and leave it on. Without the grid you cannot give a coordinate callout.

---

## The grid system

Rust overlays a lettered/numbered grid on the map, exactly like Battleship:

- **Columns** run left→right (west→east) and are **lettered**: `A, B, C, ... Z`, and on bigger maps it continues `AA, AB, AC, ...` after Z.
- **Rows** run top→bottom (north→south) and are **numbered**: `0, 1, 2, 3, ...`.
- A grid square is named **column-then-row**: `D7`, `K12`, `AA3`. Top-left corner of the map is `A0`.
- **Each grid square is 150 m × 150 m**, regardless of map size. So a "4500" map (4500 m wide) has roughly 30 columns × 30 rows; a "3000" map has roughly 20 × 20. The square size never changes — only how many squares there are.

This is *the* unit of communication in Rust. "I died at **F8**" is instantly actionable; "I died near the swamp" is not.

### Reading a grid callout

Because columns are west→east and rows are north→south:

- Moving **right** on the map = moving **east** = letter goes up (`D → E`).
- Moving **down** on the map = moving **south** = number goes up (`7 → 8`).
- `A0` is the **northwest** corner. The highest letter + highest number is the **southeast** corner.

### Precision inside a square

A 150 m square is big enough that "which corner" matters in a fight. Common ways to subdivide verbally:

- **"top/bottom, left/right of D7"** — e.g. "two pushing **bottom-left D7**."
- **Edges as compass:** "**north edge of K11**," "**SE corner of F8**."
- **Relative to a landmark in the square:** "behind the big rock D7," "the cliff side of K11."

---

## Reading monument icons

Monuments appear on the map as labeled icons once the map is generated (you don't have to discover them). Knowing the icon → monument mapping lets you call out "I'm running **Launch**" without opening the legend. Full per-monument detail lives in [[Rust Monuments]]; quick reference:

| On-map appearance | Monument | Callout shorthand |
|---|---|---|
| Large building cluster, NE-ish | [[Launch Site]] | "Launch" |
| Rocket-on-pad / large industrial | [[Launch Site]] | "Launch" / "Sat" (satellite dish is separate) |
| Airstrip + hangars | [[Airfield]] | "Air" |
| Domed reactor | [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] | "Silo" |
| Trainyard cranes/tracks | [[Trainyard]] | "TY" / "Train" |
| Water treatment pools | [[Water Treatment Plant]] | "Water" / "WTP" |
| Power plant cooling towers | [[Power Plant]] | "PP" / "Power" |
| Oil derrick (land) | [[Sulfur Quarry]] / oil monuments | varies |
| Two oil rig platforms (offshore) | [[Large Oil Rig]] / [[Small Oil Rig]] | "Big rig" / "Small rig" |
| Town buildings (safe zone, green) | [[Outpost]] / [[Bandit Camp]] | "Outpost" / "Bandit" |
| Harbor cranes on the coast | [[Harbor]] | "Harbor" |
| Dish array | [[Satellite Dish]] | "Sat" / "Dish" |
| Train tunnel entrances | [[Underground Train Tunnels]] | "Tunnels" / "metro" |

When a monument and a grid square conflict, **lead with the monument** if the enemy is on it, and the grid if they're roaming open field: "geared squad on **Launch**" vs. "lone naked at **F8**."

---

## Map size

Server map size = the map's width in meters. It's set by the server and shown in the browser/title.

| Size (m) | Grid (~) | Feel | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **3000** | ~20 × 20 | Cramped, constant PvP, few monuments | Small/duo/trio servers, high-pop brawl |
| **3500** | ~23 × 23 | Facepunch's recommended default | Many community servers |
| **4000** | ~27 × 27 | Balanced, room for cars/heli | Most **official** servers |
| **4500** | ~30 × 30 | Sprawling, all monuments + vehicles | Large/high-pop servers, 300+ |

Engine default is 4500, but Facepunch recommends ~3500 for most servers, and the **bulk of official servers run ~4000**. Bigger map = more monuments, more roam distance, more relevant [[Vehicles]] (a [[Horse]] or [[Modular Car]] matters far more on 4500 than 3000). Check the size before committing to a base spot — a "far from monuments" base on 3000 is much closer than the same words on 4500.

---

## The death marker

When you die, Rust drops a **death marker** at the spot you died, visible on your map. This is how you (and teammates) navigate back to your loot bag before it despawns.

- Your dropped loot sits in a **bag/backpack on the ground** for a limited time (it despawns — minutes, not hours, and faster if the loot is low-value). Sprint back fast.
- On a team, calling your **death grid immediately** ("died **F8** bottom, body there") lets a teammate grab your kit while you respawn. This is the entire economy of a duo/trio fight — never let a full kit despawn.
- The marker shows where you died, not where the killer is. Assume the killer is **looting your body** at that grid; that's where to retaliate or where to *avoid*.

---

## Respawn / sleeping-bag UI

When you die, the **death screen** shows a map plus a list of your respawn points:

- **Respawn options** = [[Sleeping Bag]]s and **Beds** you've placed. They appear by **name** on the death screen and as icons on the map. Name your bags ("Main," "Raid," "Farm-N") so you pick the right one under pressure.
- **Bag cooldown:** after being placed or used, a **sleeping bag** has a **5-minute** cooldown before you can spawn on it again. Spawning on a bag also triggers the timer for **all bags within a 50 m radius** (so don't cluster all your bags in one room — spread them, or one death locks the whole stack).
- **Beds** have a **drastically shorter** cooldown than bags — upgrade your home spawn to a bed as soon as you can afford it.
- **Limit:** max **15** respawn points (bags + beds) per player.
- **Map management:** a toggle on the right side of the map can **hide bags while alive**, and you can **unclaim** bags you no longer use to free up slots.
- For a duo/trio: place bags near your base, near contested monuments, and near common fight spots so a death isn't a 5-minute run back. Coordinate so you don't all dump bags in one 50 m circle.

---

## Map markers & the ping wheel

Two distinct systems: **persistent markers** you place on the map, and **transient pings** you place in the world.

### Map markers (persistent)

- Open the map (`G`) and click to drop a marker. **Max 5 markers** per player.
- Each marker can have a **color**, an **icon**, and a **text label**.
- Labels are **trimmed to 3 characters** when shown on the **compass**, so name them tersely: `HOM`, `RD1`, `FRM`.
- **Team leaders:** if you are the team **leader**, all your teammates see **all of your markers** in addition to their own. Use this — the leader marks the raid target / rally point, everyone sees it. (Set/transfer leader via the [[Team System]] UI.)
- Returning-player note: 5 is not many. Reserve them for **home, current objective, and rally**, not clutter.

### The ping wheel (transient)

Pings are placed **in the world** (not on the map) using recon tools, and last **10 seconds** unless cancelled. All teammates see your pings.

Pings work while using:
- **[[Binoculars]]** (hold RMB to aim, then ping)
- **[[Drone]]s**
- **[[CCTV Camera]]s**

Ping inputs:

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| **Single tap** ping key | **Contextual ping** — node ping when aimed at an ore node, loot ping at a storage entity, gun ping at a dropped weapon, generic location ping otherwise |
| **Double tap** ping key | **Red hostile/danger ping** — "enemy here" |
| **Hold** ping key | **Radial menu** with all ping options (~6 options) to pick a specific ping type |
| **Single tap** again | **Cancels** the ping early |

For a small team, the binocular danger-ping is the cleanest way to mark a sniper or roamer the moment you spot them through the binos — it puts a world marker your teammate can look at directly, far less error-prone than reading a grid out loud mid-fight.

---

## Compass & north

- The **compass** is a horizontal bar at the top of the screen (toggleable in [[Settings and Binds]] / enabled by default in most modes; disabled in hardcore).
- It reads **0 / 360 = North, 90 = East, 180 = South, 270 = West**. North on the map is **up**; the grid's `A0` corner is the **NW** corner.
- Your **map markers' 3-char labels** show on the compass at their bearing, so you can navigate to "HOM" without reopening the map.
- Bearings are an alternative callout axis: "sniper at **310** off Launch" tells a teammate which way to look without a grid. Combine with grid for the full picture: "**090 from us, holding F8 north edge.**"

---

## Comms convention for duo / trio

Callouts only help if the whole team uses the *same* words. Agree on these before the wipe.

### Callout format (always in this order)

> **[count] [state] [grid/landmark] [direction/detail]**

Examples:
- "**Two geared, D7 Launch, holding the rocket tower.**"
- "**One naked, F8 bottom-left, running NE toward us.**"
- "**Solo sniper, 310 off the dish, prone north edge K11.**"

Count → state → where → detail. This is the order teammates expect; jumbling it costs the half-second that gets someone killed.

### State words (say exactly these)

| Word | Means |
|---|---|
| **Naked / kitted / geared / full kit** | Their gear level (naked = no threat to loot; full kit = high-value target) |
| **One / two / squad / quad+** | How many. "Squad" = unknown 3-4, "quad+" = at least 4 |
| **Spotted / shooting / pushing / holding / repositioning** | What they're doing |
| **Down / dead / killed** | "down" = wounded/crawling (can be revived — see [[Wounded System]]); "dead" = confirmed corpse |

### Target-calling

- **Call the target by position, not just "him":** "I take **left**, you take **right**," or "**focus the rocket guy first.**"
- **Confirm kills:** "left is **dead**," so nobody keeps shooting a corpse while the other enemy flanks.
- **One caller in a fight.** In a trio, the person with the best angle calls targets; the others execute. Two people calling at once = chaos.

### Movement words

| Word | Means | Implied response |
|---|---|---|
| **Pushing** | I am moving onto the enemy now | Cover me / push with me |
| **Holding** | I am staying on this angle, not moving | I rotate around you |
| **Repositioning** | I am moving to a new angle, briefly off-angle | You hold the angle while I move |
| **Rotating [dir]** | Moving to flank | Hold their attention |
| **Falling back / breaking** | Disengaging | Cover the retreat, drop smoke |
| **Reset** | Disengage and recover; fight's over for now | Heal, reposition, regroup |

### Discipline (the part people skip)

- **Brevity over chatter.** Dead air is fine; non-stop talk buries the one callout that matters. If nothing changed, say nothing.
- **One person talks at a time** during contact. Step on a teammate's callout and you both lose information.
- **Update, don't repeat.** "Still two D7" only if it changed; otherwise the team assumes your last callout holds.
- **Call your own death immediately** with grid + body location so a teammate can recover your kit (see death marker above). "Dead F8 bottom, kit's there."
- **Loot calls:** "I have the rockets," "C4 on me," so the team knows who's carrying the raid kit if they go down.
- **Mark, don't describe, when you can.** A binocular **danger-ping** or a leader **map marker** beats reading coordinates aloud — and works when you forget which way is north. See the ping wheel above.

### Out-of-game comms

You'll do almost all of this over Discord/voice, not in-game [[Team System|team chat]]. The [[Rust+ Companion App]] lets you read team chat, see teammate positions, and get [[Smart Alarm]] pings from your phone when you're AFK — useful for a trio where one person steps away.

---

## Quick reference card

- **Open map:** hold `G` (you're exposed — do it safe).
- **Turn on the grid once** (Grid button) and never turn it off.
- **Grid square = 150 m**; named **letter+number**, `A0` = NW corner. Right = east (letter up), down = south (number up).
- **Map size:** 3000 small / ~4000 official / 4500 large — check before basing.
- **Death marker** = where you died; sprint back, your bag despawns.
- **Bags:** 5-min cooldown, 50 m shared-cooldown radius, max 15, beds are faster — spread and name them.
- **Markers:** max 5, 3-char compass labels, leader's markers shared to team.
- **Pings:** binos/drone/CCTV; tap = contextual, double-tap = danger, hold = wheel; last 10 s.
- **Callout order:** count → state → grid → detail. "Two geared D7 Launch holding tower."

---

## Sources

- [Facepunch — "Make Your Mark" devblog](https://rust.facepunch.com/news/make-your-mark) (ping system, map markers, compass labels)
- [Corrosion Hour — RUST Map Guide](https://www.corrosionhour.com/rust-map-guide/) (G key, grid overlay, 150 m squares, icons, focus/grid buttons)
- [Facepunch — "Bags to Battles" devblog](https://rust.facepunch.com/news/bags-to-battles) (respawn UI, bag cooldown, 50 m radius, 15-bag limit, hide-while-alive toggle)
- [BerryByte — Rust Map Sizes Explained](https://blog.berrybyte.net/rust-map-sizes-explained-which-one-is-right-for-your-server/) (3000/3500/4000/4500 sizing)
- [Steam Community — RUST Map Guide](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3350494176) (grid lettering A→Z→AA, column/row orientation)

pages.title: Performance Settings
pages.body:
# Performance Settings

FPS/latency tuning for a high-end PC (a 5090-class GPU, 4K@144 Hz, high-end CPU). Rust moved to **Unity 6 in June 2026** ("Built Different") — generally better frame pacing, plus one new gotcha (below).

## Unity 6 gotcha: high-polling-rate mice

After the Jun 2026 Unity 6 update, **mice polling above 1000 Hz cause stutter** for some players. If you run a 2K/4K/8K-Hz mouse, **drop polling to 1000 Hz** in the mouse software before blaming the GPU. This is the #1 "my FPS is fine but the game feels awful" cause right now.

## Launch options (Steam → Properties)

```
-gc.buffer 2048
```
Rust has a long-documented GC stutter pattern: after 45–60 min the Unity garbage collector triggers frequently on a too-small default buffer. `-gc.buffer 2048` (MB) makes collections rarer. With 32–64 GB RAM this is free. Add `-high` (process priority) optionally; skip ancient `-malloc`/thread-count voodoo from 2020 guides.

## In-game settings — what actually costs frames (2026 measurements)

| Setting | Recommendation (5090-class) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Graphics Quality preset | Custom — never the master slider | Master slider 6→2 recovers 30–50 FPS on mid GPUs; on a 5090 set individual options instead |
| **Shadow Cascades** | **2** | Single biggest win in current builds (18–30 FPS on mid GPUs); visual loss minimal |
| Shadow Distance | 100–150 | Long shadows are pure cost |
| **Draw Distance** | **2000** | Sweet spot — 2500 gives ~5% more visibility for 7+ FPS; below 1500 you lose threat-spotting |
| Anti-Aliasing | **DLSS Quality** (native DLSS 3.7 in the AA dropdown) | ~30–40% FPS gain, near-native image; at 4K even DLSS Balanced looks fine |
| Object Quality / Tree Quality | High is fine on a 5090; drop Tree Meshes if jungle biome chugs | Jungle (May 2025) is the heaviest biome |
| Grass displacement | ON (gameplay) | Shows player trails |
| Water Quality | 1–2 | High water is expensive and rivers/ocean are everywhere post-Naval Update |
| Occlusion Culling | ON | Free frames in bases/monuments |
| Volumetric clouds/fog (Aug 2025) | Medium/off for PvP clarity | Pretty, but fog hides players |
| Max Frame Rate | **Refresh − 5** (139 for 144 Hz) | Kills tearing-induced latency spikes; with G-Sync use the global NVCP cap instead |

## Windows-side (one-time Windows tuning)

- **HAGS ON** (1–5 ms input latency win), Game Mode ON, Ultimate Performance power plan.
- G-Sync + cap below refresh; disable in-game V-Sync.
- Secure Boot + TPM 2.0 enabled also qualifies you for the hardened anti-cheat servers ([[Server Types]]).

## Diagnosing in-game

- `perf 1` = FPS counter; `perf 5` = FPS + frame time + RAM + **GC count** + ping. If GC count ticks up in sync with stutters → the `-gc.buffer` fix above.
- Memory leak pattern: smooth for ~45–60 min then progressive stutter → relog (a full reconnect clears it; map cache makes reconnects fast since Aug 2025's 65% loading improvement).
- Server-side lag (rubber-banding while your FPS is fine): check `ping` in console; populated officials run worst the first hour after [[Wipe Schedule]] force wipe.

## Realistic targets (4K, 5090)

- 4K DLSS Quality, settings above: ~140+ FPS open world, dips at [[Launch Site]]/big bases — frame-cap at 139 makes that invisible.
- For sweaty PvP, some still run 1440p output for higher minimums — at 4K@144 with DLSS the 5090 doesn't need it.

Related: [[Settings and Binds]], [[Server Types]], [[Wipe Schedule]], [[Recording Graphics Settings]] (the quality-max counterpart of this page, for recording at 4K).

> **Jul 2026 note:** the "Common Ground" update (Jul 2) added Contact Shadows improvements, an experimental Shadow Caching option, and an inventory Player Model Definition toggle to the Graphics menu.

pages.title: Raid Bases and FOBs
pages.body:
# Raid Bases and FOBs

How a group stages, defends, and coordinates a raid using a **Forward Operating Base (FOB)** / raid base, and how raid roles are split. Pairs with [[Raid Costs]] (the explosive math) and [[Clan Roles and Coordination]] (who does what).

## What an FOB is

A **Forward Operating Base (FOB)** — also called a raid base — is a small base built *near the target* purely to support a raid. It is **not** a home base: no comfort, no farming, just staging. It exists to:

- **Respawn** raiders near the fight (place [[Sleeping Bag]]s inside) so deaths don't reset the raid.
- **Store loot and boom** so attackers aren't carrying everything on their bodies (which would all drop on death).
- **Provide cover** and a defensible position to push the target from.
- **Mount defenses** ([[Auto Turret]]s, shotgun traps) against the defender's counter-pushes and third-party raiders.

A solid FOB takes **~60-120 seconds with three builders**. Speed matters — the longer it takes, the more time the defender has to wake up / call backup.

## Building an FOB

- Place it **close to the breach path** but with a wall/terrain between it and the target's shooting windows.
- **Lock everything** with a [[Code Lock]] (guest code so the whole raid party can re-gear) — see [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]].
- Spread **[[Sleeping Bag]]s** so the team respawns on-site; remember bags within 50 m share cooldown.
- Add **[[Auto Turret]]s** covering front and rear; allow extra time for the electricity hookup. Authorize all raiders on them so they don't shoot your own team.
- Keep a **boom resupply box** stocked so dedicated runners can re-arm breachers mid-raid.

## Raid roles (a coordinated clan raid)

| Role | Job |
|---|---|
| **Rocketeer / boom team** | Fire [[Rockets]]/[[C4]] in coordinated barrages along the planned path; aim at **wall junctions** to maximize splash |
| **Breacher** | Push through fresh holes, kill defenders, prevent them re-sealing with twig |
| **Looter** | Once core is open, strip valuables fast and ferry to the FOB |
| **FOB defender** | Hold the staging base; man turrets; cover respawns |
| **Outside / counter team** | Suppress third-party raiders drawn by the noise so the inside team stays on objective |
| **Boom runner** | Resupply rocketeers from the FOB so they never stop firing |

Constant **Discord voice** with pre-agreed callouts is non-negotiable. See [[Clan Roles and Coordination]].

## The objective: the Tool Cupboard

The heart of every raid is the enemy's [[Tool Cupboard]] (100 HP, usually buried behind the core). Once you destroy it:

1. The defender **loses building privilege** — they can no longer wall off or rebuild in that zone.
2. You **place your own TC + [[Code Lock]]**, seal the shell with your own doors, and the base is effectively yours to loot at leisure ("loot and scoot," ideally under cover of night).
3. Note: a destroyed TC still gives the *original owner* ~24 h grief-protection upkeep, but with the TC gone they can't claim-build — that protection just delays decay.

## Scouting & the rocket-count math

Before committing, scout and **count the rockets to reach the TC**:

- Each **armored door** on the raid path costs roughly **15 rockets** — every extra door is a real sulfur tax. (See [[Raid Costs]] for the full door/wall explosive table.)
- Count walls + doors along the *shortest* path to core/TC, then **carry an extra 10-20%** for misses, deaths, and misplaced shots.
- Factor external defenses: [[Auto Turret]]s (12-turret / 40 m interference cap means defenders can't infinitely stack active turrets), shotgun/flame traps, and extra walls. Plan boom around clearing those first.

## Online vs offline raiding

| | Offline raid | Online raid |
|---|---|---|
| **When** | Target's group is asleep/away | Defenders present and fighting back |
| **Pro** | No resistance, predictable boom count | Bigger reward; can demoralize/wipe an active group |
| **Con** | Considered cheap; target may have offline-protection bases | Defenders re-seal breaches, respawn from beds, third-parties pile in |
| **Key tactic** | Just breach efficiently | Push **hard and fast in waves**, kill respawning defenders on sight, destroy their twig re-seals, keep the boom flowing |

Seeing defenders forced to respawn repeatedly means you've got them on the back foot. The counter to *being* online-raided is the [[Seismic Sensor]] raid alarm + [[Rust+ Companion App]] Smart Alarms so your offline members get pulled in.

Related: [[Raid Costs]], [[Rockets]], [[C4]], [[Tool Cupboard]], [[Auto Turret]], [[Sleeping Bag]], [[Clan Roles and Coordination]], [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]], [[Group Bases]], [[Clans and Groups]].

pages.title: Recording Graphics Settings
pages.body:
# Recording Graphics Settings

Max-visual-quality settings for **recording 4K gameplay** on a high-end rig (5090-class GPU, 64 GB RAM, 4K@144 monitor), with OBS capturing 4K60 NVENC HEVC on the GPU's dedicated encoders. Target: **stunning on camera, stable ~120 FPS in-game** (`fps.limit 120` so OBS's compositor never starves), without throwing PvP fights. This is the quality-max counterpart to [[Performance Settings]] (which is FPS-min). Current to the **July 2026 "Common Ground"** update.

## The one-principle summary

Video encoders punish **shimmer and flicker** far more than softness — temporal AA (TSSAA) + Sharpen is the correct look for recorded footage even though sweaty PvP players run FXAA. Everything else is "max it, the 5090 eats it," except the three PvP-asymmetry settings flagged at the bottom.

## Graphics tab (punch-in list)

| Setting | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Graphics Quality | **Custom** (start at 6, then set below) | Master slider overrides individual options |
| Draw Distance | **2500** (max) | Distant terrain/monuments on camera; ~5-7 FPS over 2000 |
| Shadow Distance | **400** (cinematic 800+, sweat 150) | TRADEOFF flag below |
| Shadow Cascades | **Four** | Smooth shadow gradients on footage; the 5090 affords it |
| Max Shadow Lights | **3** | Campfires/flashlights cast real shadows — night footage looks incredible |
| Water Quality | **2** (max) | Post-[[Naval Update]] water is a showpiece |
| Water Reflections | **2** (max) | Expensive but gorgeous on camera |
| Shader Level | **600** (max) | |
| Anisotropic Filtering | **16x** | Free on a 5090; sharp ground textures at grazing angles |
| Parallax Mapping | **2** | Terrain depth on camera (drop to 1 if edge artifacts bug you) |
| Object Quality | **200** | |
| Terrain Quality | **100** | |
| Tree Quality / Tree Meshes | **150-200** | TRADEOFF flag below (bush asymmetry) |
| Particle Quality | **100** | Muzzle flash / explosions are the money shots |
| Grass Quality | **~50** (cinematic 100) | TRADEOFF flag below |
| Grass Displacement | **ON** | Trails look good AND are info |
| Grass Shadows | **OFF** (ON only for pure b-roll) | Costy + deepens the grass asymmetry |
| Volumetric Clouds | **High** | Skies carry outdoor shots |
| Volumetric Fog | **Medium** | Fog hides players; High only for b-roll |
| Occlusion Culling | **ON** | Free frames, no visual cost |
| Contact Shadows | **ON** (new/improved Jul 2026) | Viewmodel + player shadow detail, cheap |
| Shadow Caching (experimental, Jul 2026) | **Try ON** | Cheaper shadows; revert if artifacts |
| Player Model Definition (inventory, Jul 2026) | **High** | Inventory paper-doll render quality |
| Max Frame Rate | leave, use `fps.limit 120` | |
| NVIDIA Reflex | **On + Boost** | Native support; input-lag win |

## Anti-aliasing — the on-camera call

Dropdown: Off / FXAA / SMAA / TSSAA / DLSS (Quality/Balanced/Performance).

- **Recording: TSSAA + Sharpen ON.** Temporal AA kills foliage shimmer/edge crawl, which HEVC otherwise turns into flickering blocky noise (shimmer eats bitrate). Slight softness at native 4K is minimal and Sharpen offsets it.
- **Sweat mode: FXAA** (or Off at 4K) — maximum distant-player crispness; TSSAA/DLSS can smear a camo player at 300m. This is the classic "pretty vs alive" fork.
- **DLSS Quality** = the FPS lever, not the quality pick: use it only if 120 doesn't hold. Adds mild foliage ghosting on footage.

## Image Effects tab

| Effect | Value | On camera |
|---|---|---|
| Sun Shafts | **ON** | God rays — biggest single cinematic win, cheap |
| High Quality Bloom | **ON** | |
| Ambient Occlusion | **ON** | Depth/grounding |
| Sharpen | **ON** | Mandatory partner to TSSAA |
| Contact Shadows | **ON** | |
| Depth of Field | **OFF** | Blurs distance = death; looks wrong on gameplay footage. ON only in demo-replay b-roll |
| Motion Blur | **OFF** | Smears compressed footage; 120→60 fps capture is already smooth |
| Lens Dirt | **OFF** | Reads as smudged footage in bright scenes |
| Vignette | **OFF** | Looks like a cheap filter on 4K video |

## FOV

- **90** (menu max) for gameplay and recording both — no conflict; 90 is also the competitive standard.
- For shorts (9:16 crop), 90 still works: the vertical crop takes the low-distortion center.
- Drop to ~70-75 **only in demo playback** for cinematic pulls.
- `graphics.vm_fov_scale`: keep **1** (default) for recording — the gun looks natural on camera. PvP purists set 0 (smaller viewmodel); that reads oddly on footage.

## Console layer (all client-side, official-server safe)

```
fps.limit 120                 # the cap — keeps frametime flat for OBS
graphics.vm_fov_scale 1       # natural viewmodel for camera
bind <key> gc.collect         # flush a hitch before a fight (frametime spikes ruin footage)
bind <key> "perf 2"           # frametime readout
streamermode true             # before going live/recording others' names
record <name> / stop          # demo capture for b-roll (see [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]])
```

Launch option: `-gc.buffer 4096` (less critical under Unity 6 incremental GC, still harmless).

Recording-specific notes:
- **Do NOT set `effects.maxgibs 0`** — the FPS-guide trick deletes flying debris, which is exactly what you want ON camera during raids. Keep default (1000).
- Weather/time convars (`env.time`, `weather.*`) are **admin-only** — nothing to do there on officials. For controlled-light b-roll, record a demo and re-shoot in playback.
- HUD-free b-roll: use demo playback + `demo.togglehud`, not live convars.

## The 3 PvP-honesty tradeoffs (cinematic vs competitive)

1. **Grass Quality + Grass Shadows.** Max grass hides prone/crouched players *from you* while a potato-settings enemy sees them plainly — the worst asymmetry in Rust. Cinematic: 100 + shadows ON. **Recommended: ~50, shadows OFF.** Tree Quality has the same (milder) issue: dense bushes render for you that low-settings enemies see through — hence 150 not 200 if playing sweaty areas.
2. **Shadow Distance.** 800-1000 is gorgeous (long evening shadows) but costs the most frames of any single slider and adds visual noise at range. **Recommended: 400** — shadows still read on camera in the 0-400m band where all fights happen. Sweat: 150.
3. **TSSAA vs FXAA.** TSSAA = beautiful stable footage, slightly softer distant players. FXAA = crisper 300m+ target ID, shimmery footage. **Recommended: TSSAA + Sharpen** — at 4K the softness penalty is small and the footage payoff is huge. Switch to FXAA only for tournament-sweat sessions you aren't publishing.

## Expected FPS (4K, 5090/285K, settings above)

- Open world: **~110-150 FPS** native 4K + TSSAA. Rust is often CPU/streaming-bound, not GPU-bound, so the 5090 has headroom to spare.
- Dips: [[Launch Site]], big compound fights, jungle biome → **80-110**.
- **`fps.limit 120` holds most of the time**; the dips are the exception, not the rule.
- If dips annoy you, lower in this order (best quality-kept per FPS-gained):
  1. AA → **DLSS Quality** (+25-40%, smallest on-camera cost at 4K)
  2. Shadow Distance 400 → 200
  3. Shadow Cascades Four → Two
  4. Water Reflections 2 → 1, then Water Quality 2 → 1
  5. Parallax 2 → 0
  6. Max Shadow Lights 3 → 2
  - Touch Object/Tree/Particle/Terrain quality **last** — they're what the camera sees most.

## Patch history
- **Jul 2026 (Common Ground):** Contact Shadows improvements + experimental Shadow Caching + inventory Player Model Definition toggle added. Page created.

Related: [[Performance Settings]], [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]], [[Settings and Binds]], [[Recoil & Aim Mastery]].

## Sources
- [CorrosionHour — RUST Settings Guide & Options](https://www.corrosionhour.com/rust-settings-guide/) (menu option names, ranges, convar equivalents)
- [CorrosionHour — RUST July 2026 Update Preview](https://www.corrosionhour.com/rust-july-2026-update-preview/) (Common Ground graphics additions)
- [Tradeit — Rust Graphics Settings 2026](https://tradeit.gg/blog/rust-graphics-settings/) (FPS costs per setting)
- [Switchblade Gaming — Best Rust PC Settings 2026](https://www.switchbladegaming.com/game-settings/rust-best-settings/) (DLSS 3.7 native, Reflex, VRAM at 4K)
- [PCOptimizedSettings — Rust Guide](https://pcoptimizedsettings.com/rust-optimized-settings-performance-guide-updated-april-2025/) (AA comparison: FXAA/SMAA/TSSAA/DLSS behavior at 4K)
- [Steam Guide — options menu as console commands](https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3180714936)

# Returning Player Changelog

One-page cheat sheet: everything that changed between ~2023 (last played) and June 2026 ("Built Different" patch), ordered by how much it changes your habits. Details live in the linked pages.

## Tier 1 — relearn or die

| Change | When | What it means for you |
|---|---|---|
| **Blueprint Fragments progression** | Oct–Nov 2025 | WB2 = 5 Basic Fragments, WB3 = 5 Advanced Fragments, monument/crate/airdrop-only. Scrap no longer buys tiers. [[First Day Guide]] |
| **Research costs slashed** | Nov 2025 | 15/30/60/120 scrap by tier (was 20/75/125/500). Research everything; recycle almost nothing usable |
| **Monthly BP wipes on ALL officials** | Nov 2025 | Every force wipe is a full reset now. [[Wipe Schedule]] |
| **Aimcone overhaul** | May 2024 | Movement penalty blends in over ~4 shots — strafe tap-fire meta. Spend an hour on an aim server. [[Server Types]] |
| **Explosive protection capped 75%** | May 2025 | No more unraidable bunkers; build for raid-cost layers. [[Building Guide]] |
| **Monument loot reshuffled + new puzzles** | Oct 2025 | First reshuffle in 5+ years: Dome/Ferry Terminal/Radtown puzzles; [[Blue Keycard]] **no longer sold at Outpost**; [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] is RED card |

## Tier 2 — big new systems

- **Backpacks** (Feb 2024): Small 12 slots (50 cloth + 5 sewing kits, T1), Large 28 (military loot). Drop on death.
- **Recycler split** (May 2024): safe zone 8s/80% vs **monument 5s/120%** — recycle at monuments.
- **Food spoilage + Cooking Workbench + bees + chicken coops** (Mar 2025): raw 6h / cooked 24h, fridges pause it; 8 buff pies. [[Farming and Food]]
- **Armor insert slots** (Mar 2025): crafted armor takes 0–3 inserts tuning protection.
- **Party system** (Jul 2025): menu-invite Steam friends, spawn together ~100 m, auto-team. [[Team System]]
- **Siege weapons + shields** (Feb 2025), **Mortar** (May 2026): catapult/ballista/battering ram/siege tower — raiding has a whole primitive lane now. [[Raid Costs]]
- **World Update 2.0** (Oct 2024) + **Jungle biome** (May 2025) + **Deep Sea / Tropical Islands / Ghost Ships / Floating Cities** (Feb 2026): terrain regenerated, rivers swim-deep, tigers/crocs/snakes in tier-0 jungle, offshore elite event zones.
- **Naval Update** (Feb 2026): player-built modular ships with cannons at Boat Building Stations; PT Boat with two .50 cals. [[Vehicles Index]]
- **New guns since you left:** Handmade SMG (T1), SKS (T3), High Calibre Revolver, Minigun + Military Flamethrower (heavy-scientist loot), Blowpipe/Boomerang, M16A2 burst + Ballistic armor (Jun 2026, loot-only), craftable silencers, 4x/8x/16x variable zoom. [[Weapons Index]]
- **Vehicles:** Attack Heli (2,250 scrap, Bandit Camp), motor/pedal bikes, DPV, Tugboat, parachutes; horses overhauled (swim, tow, 12-slot saddlebags). [[Vehicles Index]]

## Tier 3 — QoL and meta-environment

- **Premium Servers** (Mar 2025; "Premium Access Pass" Jun 2026): $15+ Steam inventory gate, ~4x fewer cheaters; TPM/Secure-Boot servers (Mar 2026). [[Server Types]]
- **Softcore reworked** (Apr 2025): respawn with 50% inventory, −25% PvP damage, team cap 4. **Hardcore reworked** (Aug 2025): fog-of-war map, compass item, no firearm crafting.
- **Ping system** (Apr 2023 — you may have caught this) + map markers ×5. [[Team System]]
- **Sleeping bags capped at 15 respawn points** (Jun 2023).
- **Tech tree**: single station with tabs (Jun 2024) + multi-node path unlock (Apr 2026).
- **Gamma cheating dead** (Mar 2024 shader nightlight); **gunshots audible 400/500/600 m** by class (Sep 2025); **wolves stalk** (Nov 2024).
- **Auto turret 40 m interference cap** (Oct 2023); **handcuffs/prisoner hoods** (Jul 2024).
- **Tutorial Island** (Mar 2024); full menu redesign + 65% faster loading (Aug 2025); daytime +20 min (Mar 2026); Unity 6 (Jun 2026 — set mice to ≤1000 Hz, [[Performance Settings]]).
- **Endgame chase:** 9 rare non-craftable [[Workbench Augmentations]] (May 2026); Cargo docks at harbors with a 60s departure horn (Apr 2024); Oil Rig irradiates 30 min post-hack.
- **Roadmap teased:** cows/sheep/breeding, apartment monuments, "Rust Premium" subscription late 2026.

Related: [[Getting Started (Rust)]], [[First Day Guide]], [[Solo Survival Guide]], [[Wipe Schedule]].

pages.title: Running a Rust Server
pages.body:
# Running a Rust Server

A primer on hosting your own Rust server. This is the **server-operator** view — installing the dedicated server, the convars that shape the world, admin/RCON access, modding frameworks, and wiping. It is distinct from the **client/cheat** convars in [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] (that page is for things you type as a player). If you self-host an ARK server you already know the shape of this: SteamCMD download, a startup batch/script, a config file, port forwarding, RCON.

> Verified June 2026 against Rustafied's host guide, the Steam/Valve dedicated-server docs, XGamingServer, Cybrancee and HostingBuff. Rust runs on **Unity 6** as of the [[Built Different Update]] (June 4 2026); the dedicated server is the same engine bump, so allow a fresh `validate` after that wipe. Numbers below are current but Facepunch changes them — re-verify after a major update.

See also: [[Server Types]] (vanilla vs modded vs premium, picking one to *play*), [[Wipe Schedule]] (official force-wipe cadence you'll want to mirror).

---

## Self-hosted vs rented (GSP)

| | Self-hosted (your PC / VPS) | Rented (Game Server Provider) |
|---|---|---|
| Cost | Free if you own the box; electricity + bandwidth | ~$10–25/mo for a small slot, more for big maps/players |
| Control | Total — files, mods, OS, network | Web panel; varies by host (Pterodactyl/Pelican, LinuxGSM) |
| Setup effort | High (SteamCMD, ports, updates, RCON) | Low — one-click installs, auto-wipe schedulers |
| DDoS protection | You provide it | Usually included |
| Best for | Tinkering, private duo/trio realm, learning | "Just want a server my friends join" |

For a **private solo/duo/trio realm** self-hosting on a spare PC is fine and free. The moment you want it 24/7 and public, a GSP's DDoS protection and uptime usually win — public Rust servers get attacked. (Same logic as your ARK box: LAN/friends-only is easy; public-facing is a different animal.)

**RAM is the real constraint.** Budget roughly **7 GB per server instance** as a baseline; a 4000-size map with 50+ players and Oxide/Carbon plugins will use more. Map generation on first boot or after a wipe takes **5–15 minutes** — the server appears "stuck" but is generating; don't kill it.

---

## Installing with SteamCMD

The Rust dedicated server is a free, anonymous SteamCMD app. **App ID `258550`** (note: that's the *server*, not the game's `252490`).

1. Download SteamCMD, extract to e.g. `C:\steamcmd\`.
2. Run `steamcmd.exe` and enter:

```
force_install_dir "c:\rustserver\"
login anonymous
app_update 258550 validate
quit
```

3. After a major Rust update (and especially after the Unity 6 [[Built Different Update]]), re-run the same `app_update 258550 validate` to patch — the server **must** match the client protocol or nobody can connect.

That gives you `RustDedicated.exe` in `c:\rustserver\`.

---

## The startup script (where most config lives)

In Rust, most "config" is **convars passed on the command line** with `+`, not a separate file you hand-edit (though see `server.cfg` below). A minimal Windows `start.bat` next to `RustDedicated.exe`:

```bat
RustDedicated.exe -batchmode ^
 +server.ip 0.0.0.0 ^
 +server.port 28015 ^
 +server.identity "myserver" ^
 +server.hostname "Fiiish Island | Duo | Monthly" ^
 +server.description "Friends-only, monthly wipe" ^
 +server.maxplayers 50 ^
 +server.worldsize 4000 ^
 +server.seed 1234 ^
 +server.level "Procedural Map" ^
 +server.tickrate 30 ^
 +server.saveinterval 300 ^
 +rcon.ip 0.0.0.0 ^
 +rcon.port 28016 ^
 +rcon.password "CHANGE_ME_LONG_RANDOM" ^
 +rcon.web 1
```

`^` is the Windows line-continuation char (drop them and put it all on one line if you prefer). On Linux it's the same convars with `\` continuations.

### Key convars

| Convar | Range / values | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `server.port` | default **28015** (UDP) | Client connection port |
| `server.ip` | `0.0.0.0` | Bind to all interfaces |
| `server.identity` | string, e.g. `myserver` | Names the save folder `server/<identity>/`. **This is the folder you'll wipe.** |
| `server.hostname` | string | Name shown in the in-game server browser |
| `server.description` | string | Server description (use `\n` for line breaks) |
| `server.maxplayers` | e.g. 10–250 | Player cap. Higher = more RAM/CPU |
| `server.worldsize` | **1000–6000** | Map size. 3000–3500 is "official feel"; 4000 is roomy; 6000 is huge and heavy |
| `server.seed` | **0–2147483647** | Determines the procedural map layout. Change it each wipe for a fresh map |
| `server.level` | `Procedural Map`, `Barren`, `HapisIsland`, `SavasIsland`, `SavasIsland_koth` | Map type; almost everyone uses Procedural |
| `server.tickrate` | default 30 (10–30) | Network tick. Higher = smoother PvP, more CPU. 30 is the practical sweet spot |
| `server.saveinterval` | seconds, e.g. 300 | How often the world auto-saves |
| `server.salt` | int | Combined with seed; some hosts vary this instead of seed |

> Worldsize and seed together define the whole map (monuments, terrain, roads). A given `worldsize` + `seed` is reproducible — useful if your group found a layout you like. To preview a seed before committing, paste it into a third-party Rust map generator (e.g. RustMaps).

### `server.cfg` (the persistent config file)

Beyond startup args, the server reads `server/<identity>/cfg/server.cfg` on boot — a plain text file of convar assignments, one per line, no `+`:

```
server.hostname "Fiiish Island | Duo | Monthly"
server.maxplayers 50
server.gamemode vanilla
decay.scale 1.0
```

There's also `cfg/users.cfg` (auto-generated) which stores your `ownerid`/`moderatorid` and bans — `server.writecfg` writes to it. Edit live convars in the console instead of fighting the file, then `server.writecfg` to persist.

---

## Ports & networking

| Port | Protocol | Purpose | Forward? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **28015** | UDP | Game traffic (clients connect here) | **Yes** — required |
| **28016** | TCP | RCON (web/websocket) | Only to your admin IP, ideally not the public internet |
| 28017 | (varies) | App/Rust+ companion, if enabled | Optional |

Port-forward **28015/UDP** on your router to the server box's LAN IP (exactly like your ARK port-forward). Players connect via `client.connect <your-public-ip>:28015` or by searching the in-game **Community** tab for your hostname. **Do not** expose RCON (28016) wide open — lock it to your IP or a VPN (you already run Tailscale; pointing RCON at a Tailscale IP is the clean move).

---

## Admin access: ownerid / moderatorid

Two auth levels:

- **`ownerid <SteamID64> "name"`** — level 2, full owner: every convar, item spawning, F1 admin tools, RCON.
- **`moderatorid <SteamID64> "name"`** — level 1, moderator: kick/ban/mute/teleport/noclip, but **not** convar changes or item spawning.

Run them in the **server console** (the window/RCON) or via RCON, then **`server.writecfg`** to save to `users.cfg` so they survive a restart:

```
ownerid 76561198000000000 "Josia"
server.writecfg
```

Remove with `removeowner <SteamID64>` / `removemoderator <SteamID64>`.

> **Security:** your SteamID64 grants full server control. Only `ownerid` people you fully trust — owner = ability to spawn anything, ban anyone, and rewrite the world. Never paste your `ownerid` line into a public Discord or a plugin config you didn't read. Keep the RCON password long and random and out of screenshots/streams. This is the same threat model as your ARK admin password: an admin credential leak = the realm is theirs.

---

## In-game admin tools (F1 console)

Once you're an owner, open the **F1 console** in-game and you have the admin toolkit. Many overlap with the player-side stuff on [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]], but these need auth:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `noclip` | Toggle flight + clip through walls (free-cam building/inspection) |
| `god true` / `god 1` | God mode (no damage) — admin god toggle |
| `admintime <0-24>` | Set time for **you only** (scouting in the dark) |
| `env.time <0-24>` | Set time for the **whole server** |
| `weather.rain <0-1>` / `weather.fog` / `weather.wind` | Force weather; `weather.load Clear` to clear |
| `teleport "name1" "name2"` | Teleport player1 to player2 |
| `teleport2me "name"` | Bring a player to you |
| `teleportpos "x y z"` | Teleport yourself to coordinates |
| `inventory.giveto "name" <item> <amount>` | Give item to a named player |
| `inventory.giveall <item> <amount>` | Give item to everyone online |
| `give <item> <amount>` | Give item to yourself |
| `spawn <entity>` | Spawn an entity/NPC/animal |
| `ent kill` / `ent who` | Kill / identify the entity you're looking at |
| `airdrop` / `airdrop.drop` | Trigger a supply drop |
| `find <text>` | Search for convars/commands matching text |

Item shortnames (for `give`/`inventory.giveto`) are on the Facepunch wiki Item list — e.g. `give rifle.ak 1`, `give wood 1000`.

---

## RCON (remote console)

RCON lets you administer without being in-game — from a phone, a web tool, or an automation script.

- Enable with `+rcon.web 1` (websocket mode, recommended), `+rcon.port 28016`, `+rcon.password "..."`.
- Connect with any RCON client: **RustAdmin** (Windows GUI), the web-based **Rcon.io**, or browser console tools. Point it at `ws://<server-ip>:28016/<password>`.
- Anything you can type in the server console works over RCON: `say "wipe in 10m"`, `ownerid ...`, `restart 300`, `serverinfo`, `playerlist`.

Useful server-management commands:

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `save` / `server.save` | Force an immediate world save (do this before a restart/wipe) |
| `server.readcfg` / `server.writecfg` | Reload / write the config |
| `restart <seconds>` | Graceful restart with countdown broadcast |
| `quit` | Shut the server down |
| `serverinfo` | FPS, players, entities, memory |
| `playerlist` / `status` | Who's online + SteamIDs/pings |

---

## Performance & tickrate

- **`server.tickrate 30`** is the practical max and what officials run; it's the biggest lever on PvP feel. Higher than 30 isn't supported and just burns CPU.
- **`fps.limit`** (server-side) caps server frame loop; leave default unless profiling.
- **Worldsize and entity count** drive memory and GC pauses. A 6000 map full of bases will stutter on weak hardware — most private realms are happiest at **3000–4000**.
- Rust's server is mostly single-thread-bound for the main loop; **high single-core clock** matters more than core count. (Your high-end box will host a small private map trivially.)
- Watch for **GC spikes** (players feel them as rubber-banding) on heavily-modded Oxide servers; Carbon's dynamic hooking mitigates this (see below).

---

## Modding frameworks: Oxide (uMod) vs Carbon

Vanilla Rust has **no plugin support** — you need a framework. Two exist; both install over the dedicated server and both run `.cs` plugins dropped into a folder.

| | **Oxide / uMod** | **Carbon** |
|---|---|---|
| Origin | The original (≈2013), mature, huge ecosystem | Newer, performance-focused, actively developed |
| Plugin library | **~1,400+** plugins on uMod | Near-100% Oxide-compatible; some "Carbon-only" plugins exist |
| Hooking | Patches game DLLs heavily; can be slower to boot, more GC | **Dynamic hooking** — boots ~30–40% faster, lighter on GC |
| Update cadence | Maintenance mode; can lag after a Rust patch | Self-updating, patches **faster** after Rust updates |
| Verdict 2026 | Stable, proven, biggest library | Where the community is moving; recommended for new servers |

**For a new private server in 2026, Carbon is the common recommendation** (fast patching after wipes matters — see [[Wipe Schedule]]); plugin compatibility is near-parity so you don't lose the uMod catalog. Oxide remains the safe, battle-tested choice if you value maximum maturity.

**Popular plugins** (work on both frameworks): an admin/permission menu, kits/starter-gear, a TP/home system (`/home`, `/tpr`), a shop/economy, copy-paste (build-saving), a vanish/admin-radar set, RustEdit custom-monument support, a wipe/announcement scheduler, and discord integration (chat relay + RCON-to-Discord). Grab plugins from **uMod (umod.org)** or the Carbon community — read the source/permissions before installing; a plugin runs arbitrary C# on your box.

> Note: installing Oxide/Carbon makes your server **modded** in the browser (and it'll show in the Modded tab). That's a different category from official/vanilla — see [[Server Types]].

---

## Wiping the server

There is **no in-game "wipe" command.** A wipe = stop the server, delete specific save files in `server/<identity>/`, optionally change the seed, restart. Match your cadence to what players expect ([[Wipe Schedule]]: officials force-wipe the **first Thursday monthly at 19:00 UTC**, with weekly/biweekly community variants).

### Map wipe (most common)

Resets the world, all buildings, and inventories; **keeps** learned blueprints. Stop the server, then in `server/<identity>/`:

1. Delete the procedural map saves: **`proceduralmap.*.sav`** and **`proceduralmap.*.map`** (the `*` is the worldsize/seed stamp).
2. *(Optional but recommended)* change `server.seed` (and/or `server.salt`) for a fresh layout.
3. Start the server — it regenerates the map (5–15 min).

### Blueprint (BP) wipe

A map wipe **plus** erasing everyone's learned recipes, forcing re-research from scrap. Do the map-wipe steps **and** additionally delete the blueprint database:

- **`player.blueprints.5.db`**

(Facepunch's monthly force wipes are **map-only by default**; **BP wipes are announced separately and are rarer** — though note officials BP-wipe monthly since "Pivot Or Die," per [[Getting Started (Rust)]]. On your own server you choose.)

### Full wipe

Map + BP + all player data (deaths, states, identities). Delete the procedural map files, `player.blueprints.5.db`, and the other `player.*.db` / state files in the identity folder — effectively wipe the whole `server/<identity>/` save except `cfg/`. Keep `cfg/users.cfg` if you don't want to re-add admins.

> **Before any wipe:** run `save` so you're working from a clean state, announce it (`say` / a scheduler plugin), and back up the identity folder if you might want to roll back. GSPs and LinuxGSM/Pterodactyl panels expose all of this as an **auto-wipe scheduler** so you don't hand-delete files monthly.

---

## Security basics (do these)

1. **Long random RCON password**, never reused, never on-stream/in-screenshots.
2. **Don't expose RCON (28016) to the public internet** — bind it to LAN/VPN/Tailscale or your admin IP only.
3. **`ownerid` only people you'd trust with the literal keys** — owner can spawn, ban, and rewrite the world.
4. **Read plugins before installing.** A malicious or sloppy plugin runs arbitrary C# with full server access. Stick to reputable uMod/Carbon authors.
5. **Keep the server updated** (`app_update 258550 validate` after each Rust patch) — an out-of-date server can't be joined and may carry known issues.
6. **Back up the identity folder** before wipes and before installing/updating a framework.

(Same operational discipline as your ARK server: credentials in a password manager, admin port not public, restart via your scheduled-task path rather than ad-hoc.)

---
