## Related

- [[Server Types]] — vanilla / softcore / hardcore / primitive / 2x–5x modded / premium, and which to *play*
- [[Wipe Schedule]] — official force-wipe cadence to mirror; map vs BP timing
- [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] — the client-side convar reference (player view), distinct from this operator view
- [[Built Different Update]] — current patch (Unity 6); re-validate the server after it
- [[Getting Started (Rust)]] — the player-side operations manual

pages.title: Rust+ Companion App
pages.body:
# Rust+ Companion App

Official free companion app (iOS/Android) — your base's security system and team dashboard when you're not at the PC. As a solo this is your offline-raid early-warning; as a duo/trio it's shared situational awareness. Disabled entirely on Hardcore servers ([[Server Types]]).

## Setup / pairing

1. Install **Rust+** from the App Store / Play Store, sign in with the **same Steam account**.
2. In-game on the server: ESC → **Rust+** tab → **Pair with server** → accept the push notification on the phone.
3. Pairing is **per server, per wipe** — re-pair after every map wipe ([[Wipe Schedule]]) and re-pair each smart device after you rebuild.

## What the app gives you (no devices needed)

- **Live server map** with your teammates' positions, monuments, and map events — [[Cargo Ship]], [[Attack Helicopter]] patrol, crate/airdrop indicators.
- Server status: player count, in-game time, queue.
- **Team chat** from your phone ([[Team System]]).
- Death notifications (you died / your bag situation).

## Smart devices (require electricity — see [[Electricity Basics]])

| Device | Cost ballpark | What it does via Rust+ |
|---|---|---|
| **Smart Switch** | T2 electrical component | Remote on/off toggle from the app — arm turrets, lights, SAM, recyclers (anything wired through it) before you even log in |
| **Smart Alarm** | T2 electrical component | **Push notification to every paired player with building privilege** when powered on; message text fully customizable ("TC ROOM BREACHED") |
| **CCTV Camera** | — | View live (laggy) feeds in-app when wired and paired |
| **Storage Monitor** | — | Tracks a box/TC contents — **upkeep-low warnings** for your TC from the app |

**Pairing a device:** hold **E** on the placed device → **Pair**; accept on the phone. Each teammate must pair their own phone with each device they want notifications from.

## The standard solo alarm chain (2026)

1. Small battery → root combiner as needed.
2. **HBHF sensor or Tin Can Alarm tripline** at your airlock + **Seismic Sensor** (May 2026 — detects nearby explosions, i.e. the raid itself) →
3. → **Smart Alarm** ("RAID IN PROGRESS") and a **Smart Switch** arming interior [[Auto Turret]]s.
4. Result: phone buzzes the moment satchels hit, and you can flip turrets/lights remotely while sprinting to the PC.

## Notes & limits

- Notifications only fire if the device is **powered** and you (still) have **building privilege**.
- Don't put your only alarm on the exterior — wire the **TC/loot room**, that's the notification that matters.
- The app's map shows vending machines and their stock — useful for shopping runs to player bases without leaving spawn.
- Third-party power tools exist (e.g., the open-source `rustplusplus` Discord bot wraps the same API: device control + events in Discord) — community-made, use at your own judgment.

Related: [[Electricity Basics]], [[Solo Survival Guide]], [[Team System]], [[Wipe Schedule]].

pages.title: rusthelp.com
pages.body:
# rusthelp.com

**[rusthelp.com](https://rusthelp.com)** is the de-facto **RustLabs successor** — the authoritative numbers wiki for Rust. When this vault states an exact stat (item cost, raid cost, recycle yield, loot-table drop chance, scrap-per-container), it is verified against rusthelp unless noted otherwise. It is the single most-cited source across the Rust wiki here.

## What it's the source of truth for

- **Item stats** — damage, durability, craft costs, stack sizes (`/items/<name>`).
- **Loot tables** — exact per-slot drop chances for every container (`/world/<container>`). This feeds [[Loot Tables]], [[Barrels and Crates]], and [[Loot Table Reverse Lookup]].
- **Recycle yields** — scrap + material returns per component, with the **safe-zone (80%) vs monument/radtown (120%)** split shown side by side. Feeds [[Recycling]].
- **Raid costs** — explosives needed per wall/door tier. Feeds the raiding pages.
- **Tools** — interactive [tech-tree planner](https://rusthelp.com/tools/techtree) and craft calculators.

## How to read its loot tables (so the percentages make sense)

- Each container has **guaranteed slots** (e.g. scrap) + **random slots** that each independently roll from a weighted pool. The published % is **per-slot**, so the expected count of a high-% item over multiple slots is higher than the listed number. See the explainer in [[Loot Tables]].
- Recycle tables show **two columns**: the higher (monument/radtown, 120%) and lower (safe-zone, 80%) yield — the May 2 2024 "Meta Madness" change. See [[Recycling]].

## Verification convention in this vault

Pages that have been number-checked against rusthelp carry a dated verification note (e.g. *"verified vs rusthelp.com, June 2026, Built Different"*). **Numbers are never stated from memory** — if a value can't be confirmed on rusthelp (or the relevant facepunch devblog for brand-new systems), it's flagged as an estimate.

Secondary/cross-check sources, in order: [wiki.facepunch.com](https://wiki.facepunch.com/rust), [rust.facepunch.com/news](https://rust.facepunch.com/news) (monthly devblogs — the source of truth for *brand-new* mechanics rusthelp hasn't tabled yet), [rustafied.com](https://www.rustafied.com), [corrosionhour.com](https://www.corrosionhour.com), and [rustrician.io](https://www.rustrician.io) for electricity circuits.

## Related

[[Loot Tables]] · [[Barrels and Crates]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Scrap]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Tech Tree]]

pages.title: Server Types
pages.body:
# Server Types

How to read the server browser in 2026 and pick a home as a returning solo/duo/trio.

## Official vs Community vs Modded

| Category | Run by | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Official | Facepunch | Pure vanilla. **BPs wipe monthly** (since Nov 2025). Highest pop, most zergs, best anti-cheat telemetry |
| Community | Independent admins, unmodded | Vanilla gameplay but admin-set wipe cadence/map size; quality depends entirely on the admin |
| Modded | Independent, plugins (Oxide/Carbon) | 2x/5x rates, kits, teleport, clans, arenas — anything goes; separate browser tab |

## Gamemodes (verified June 2026)

### Vanilla / Survival
The default. Team UI max 8 ([[Team System]]). Monthly map+BP wipe on officials. This is the baseline every other mode modifies.

### Softcore (reworked Apr 2025 "Soft Refresh")
- Die **outside building privilege** → automatically **respawn with 50% of your inventory** (50% of total stack counts, so you can't get junk-stack scammed).
- Additional 50% of inventory/hotbar reclaimable at a safe-zone **Reclaim terminal** for up to 2 hours.
- **−25% PvP bullet damage.**
- **Max team/auth size 4.** Can respawn at [[Outpost]]/[[Bandit Camp]] if not hostile.
- Monthly BP wipes. Best "I have a job" mode; genuinely good for a returning solo's first wipe back.

### Hardcore (reworked Aug 2025 "Harder Core")
- **Fog-of-war map**: starts black, reveals as you explore.
- Your position shows on the map **only with a Compass item in your belt** (no direction indicator, no compass HUD).
- **Firearms cannot be crafted or researched** — loot-only (found guns repair without BP). Ammo crafting costs **5x**.
- No safe zones, no team system, no [[Rust+ Companion App]], local-only chat (~100 m), max 5 sleeping bags, bag cooldown 15 min / bed 10 min, **upkeep doubled**, tech tree costs raised (~1.5x T1 / 2x T2 / 4x T3).
- For veterans who want 2014 Rust. Not recommended for your first wipe back.

### Primitive
Bows/melee/siege only — no firearms era. Niche but popular with small groups sick of getting beamed.

### Modded rate servers (2x, 3x, 5x, 10x)
Multiplied gather rates, often shorter wipes, often "max group 2/3" rules. **"Solo/Duo/Trio 2x weekly" servers are the classic returning-player choice** — group-size limits are admin-enforced, so you fight other small groups, not 12-man zergs.

### Aim-train / UKN-style
UKN.gg and similar: instant guns, infinite ammo, arena/target practice. Use one for 30–60 minutes to re-learn recoil before your first real wipe — **recoil and aimcone changed in May 2024** (movement penalty blends in over ~4 shots; strafe tap-fire is meta) and the gun pool has ~8 new weapons since 2023 ([[Weapons Index]]).

### Console
Separate product (Rust Console Edition, older build, separate servers). Irrelevant for PC — you can't cross-play.

## Premium Servers / anti-cheat (verified)

- **Premium** (Mar 2025, renamed **Premium Access Pass** Jun 2026): servers you can only join if your **Rust Steam inventory is worth ≥ $15** (skins, store items — tradable value counts). Facepunch data showed roughly **4x fewer cheaters**; the $15 floor was chosen from analysis of millions of banned accounts. Many officials run premium variants. If you own any old skins from 2023, you likely already qualify — check the Premium tab in the server browser.
- **TPM 2.0 + Secure Boot servers** (Mar 2026): optional server flag requiring hardware attestation — the strongest anti-cheat tier. Enable Secure Boot in BIOS if you want these (high-end hardware supports it).
- A paid **"Rust Premium" battlepass-style subscription** is teased for late 2026 — different thing from the Access Pass, not live yet.

## How to pick, as a returning solo (recommendation)

1. **Wipe 1 (rust removal):** Softcore official, or a low-pop (~100) community vanilla server wiped <24h ago. Learn the [[Blueprint Fragments]] loop without sweats.
2. **Wipe 2+:** "Solo/Duo/Trio" capped 2x community server, weekly/biweekly — the best effort-to-fun ratio for small groups in 2026.
3. **When confident:** Premium vanilla official, monthly, for the full experience with fewer cheaters.
4. Always filter: wiped recently, ping < 80, pop 100–300 (sub-50 is dead, 500+ is zerg land for a solo).

Related: [[Wipe Schedule]], [[Solo Survival Guide]], [[First Day Guide]], [[Team System]].

pages.title: Settings and Binds
pages.body:
# Settings and Binds

Console is F1. Binds entered in console persist (written to `keys.cfg` in `cfg/`). The menu got a full redesign in Aug 2025 (with ~65% faster loading), so options live in new places but binds work the same.

## Essential console binds (verified syntax, May 2026)

| Bind | Command | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Autorun | `bind q forward;sprint` | Hands-free travel; press W/Shift to cancel. THE one bind everyone uses |
| Auto-attack farm | `bind z +attack;+duck` | Hold to crouch-spam melee on nodes/walls (soft-side farming) |
| Crouch toggle | `bind c duck` | Toggle sneak instead of holding Ctrl |
| Auto-swim | `bind 0 forward;sprint;jump` | Rivers are wide/deep everywhere since World Update 2.0 — you swim a lot now |
| Laser/light on ADS | `bind mouse1 +lighttoggle;+attack2` | Flashlight/laser only while aiming |
| Combat log | `combatlog` (in console) | Last 30 damage events: attacker, weapon, distance, HP. First thing to check after a death |
| Perf overlay | `perf 1` (fps) / `perf 5` (fps+RAM+GC+ping) | See [[Performance Settings]] |

Crafting quality-of-life: the tech tree is one station with tabs (Jun 2024) and supports **multi-node path unlock** (Apr 2026) — click the end item, pay the whole path at once. No bind needed.

## Default keys worth re-learning

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| **B (hold)** | Gesture wheel — wave/point/surrender etc. Friendly-ID without voice |
| **Middle mouse** | Ping (with binoculars/drone/cam): tap = contextual, double-tap = danger, hold = 6-option wheel ([[Team System]]) |
| G | Map. Up to **5 personal markers**, colorable/labelable |
| Tab | Inventory + team UI |
| F1 | Console + kill (`kill` command, suicide timer applies) |
| E (hold) | Interaction wheel — pairing ([[Rust+ Companion App]]), rotate, pickup, etc. |
| Left Alt | Free-look (hold while running) |
| H | Toggle HUD info / hoverloot varies — check Options → Controls after the Aug 2025 menu redesign |

## Settings that matter (non-performance)

- **Crosshair:** vanilla has no real crosshair customization; aimcone (May 2024) means hipfire blooms with sustained movement-fire — learn tap-fire instead of taping a dot to the monitor. (Many use the gesture of ADS-only anyway.)
- **Field of View:** 90 is the sweet spot; max FOV helps melee/parkour, hurts long-range spotting.
- **Hover loot / quick loot:** enable in Options — moves stacks on hover, mandatory QoL.
- **Voice volume / mute:** per-player mute from the Tab player list — use it, beach mic spam is eternal.
- **Nightlight:** gamma abuse is dead (Mar 2024 shader nightlight) — there is a built-in low-light shader; nights are fairer but genuinely dark. Don't chase 2023-era gamma guides.
- **Contact list:** the contacts system (friend/enemy tagging with nameplate colors) is in the inventory screen — tag neighbors.

## Useful console commands (not binds)

```
client.lookatradius 20     # widens interact radius (default ~0.2-ish per patch; helps door/loot interaction)
audio.voices 0.5           # voice chat volume
chat.enable false          # hide chat entirely (streamer/no-toxicity mode)
hud.lock true              # prevents accidental HUD scale drags
streamermode 1             # anonymizes names if clipping for the auto-clip pipeline
```

> Note: convar names occasionally change with monthly patches (Unity 6 landed Jun 2026); if a bind errors, check `find <keyword>` in F1 console for the current name.

Related: [[Performance Settings]], [[Team System]], [[First Day Guide]].

pages.title: Solo Survival Guide
pages.body:
# Solo Survival Guide

How a solo survives a populated server in mid-2026. The progression rework cuts both ways for solos: research is dirt cheap (15/30/60/120 scrap), but WB2/WB3 are gated behind contested monument loot ([[Blueprint Fragments]]) — PC Gamer's launch take on "Pivot Or Die" literally called it "a nightmare for solo survivors." It's manageable if you play the timing game below.

## The solo mindset shifts since 2023

| Then (2023) | Now (2026) |
|---|---|
| Grind roadside scrap → tech tree everything | Scrap is cheap; **fragments are the bottleneck** — you must do monuments |
| BPs persist most of the year on officials | **BPs wipe monthly everywhere official** — every wipe is a BP wipe |
| Gamma up at night, farm safely | Night is actually dark; predators stalk; gunshots audible 400–600 m |
| Full-auto spray meta | May 2024 aimcone: **strafe tap-fire / burst** wins; first ~4 shots are accurate while moving |
| 100% splash-proof bunkers possible | **Explosive protection caps at 75%** — everything is raidable, design for cost not immunity |

## Fragment-hunting as a solo: timing windows

You can't out-fight a trio at [[Launch Site]] on wipe day. You can out-time them:

- **Off-peak hours** (server-local 4–9 AM) are the solo's monument window — green/blue puzzles respawn loot and go uncontested.
- **Junkpile scientists** along roads drop Basic Fragments and nobody fights you for them. A bow/Handmade SMG roadside loop can fund WB2 without ever entering a big monument.
- **Supply Drops**: with the airdrop visible map-wide, only chase ones landing near your quadrant; bring the bike (motorbikes/pedal bikes since Jul 2024 — silent-ish, cheap, beats a horse for drop-racing).
- **Advanced Fragments** (elite/hackable crates): as a solo, prefer **[[The Dome]] elite crates** and **small [[Oil Rig]] off-hours** over Launch. Note Oil Rig **floods with radiation 30 min after the crate hack** — get in, get out. [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] is RED-keycard now with 3 extra elite crates — top-tier but trio territory.

## Solo base (2026)

- **2x2 with ladder-hatch core and garage doors**, stone shell / sheet-metal core, external TC honeycomb later. Bunker meta is nerfed by the 75% explosive-protection cap — spend on **layers + spread loot**, not one magic core.
- **15 respawn points max** (bags+beds combined, 50 m shared cooldown): 3–4 at base, 2 near your farm monuments, 1 near water, rest as roam-recovery bags.
- **Hidden external stashes** beat a bigger base. A solo's wealth should be 40% buried.
- Electricity priorities: [[Auto Turret]] (remember the **40 m interference cap** — max ~12 turrets powered in an area before they shut off), **Seismic Sensor** (May 2026 raid alarm — detects explosions nearby) wired to a Smart Alarm → phone push via [[Rust+ Companion App]]. **Tin Can Alarm** (May 2026) is a free tripwire for doorways.
- Food: small planter + **chicken coop** (Mar 2025) + Mini Fridge (18 slots, pauses spoilage) makes you grocery-independent; **Cooking Workbench pies** give real buffs (e.g., farming/loot pies) — see [[Farming and Food]].

## Solo loadout ladder

1. **Bow → Crossbow** (still wins vs early guns at range)
2. **Handmade SMG** (T1, cheap, close-range shredder — new since Nov 2024)
3. **SAR / Python** (T2 staples, unchanged)
4. **SKS** (T3 DMR niche, Nov 2024) → **AK/Bolty** when established
5. Armor: road-sign + coffee can; crafted armor takes **insert slots (0–3)** since Mar 2025 — wood/metal inserts tune projectile vs melee protection. The Jun 2026 **Ballistic armor set** and M16A2 are loot-only chase items.
6. Always carry: 2–4 syringes, bandages, and a **Parachute** in the backpack slot if you roam high ground (T2 craft: 2 tarp + 2 sewing kits + 50 cloth; −20% durability per use).

## Fights to take, fights to skip

- **Take:** nakeds at your monuments, solo farmers, junkpile scientists, anyone counting your base's garage doors.
- **Skip:** wipe-day Launch, anything near a zerg's compound, [[Attack Helicopter]] gunships (it got nerfed Nov 2025 — flares no longer fool homing missiles — but it still deletes solos), Deep Sea event zones at peak hours.
- Disengage tech: gunshot audibility is class-based (400/500/600 m) — a silencer (craftable since Jun 2025) genuinely shrinks your detection bubble while farming.

## When you log off

- TC stocked for 24h+ upkeep; loot split across 2+ rooms + buried stashes.
- [[Rust+ Companion App]] paired: Smart Alarm on TC + Seismic Sensor = you know about the raid in real time.
- On **Softcore** ([[Server Types]]) you keep 50% on death — if you're only half-committed this month, play there and skip the paranoia.

Related: [[First Day Guide]], [[Server Types]], [[Building Guide]], [[Raid Costs]], [[Weapons Index]], [[Electricity Basics]].

pages.title: Survival Mechanics
pages.body:
# Survival Mechanics

The literal survival layer of Rust: the four meters that keep you alive (**health, calories/hunger, hydration/thirst, comfort**) plus the environmental systems that try to kill you (**temperature/cold, radiation, bleeding**) and what happens when you hit 0 HP (**the wounded / downed system**).

If you stopped playing around 2022–23, the single most important thing to relearn is the **[[Wounded System]]** — going to 0 HP no longer always kills you; you usually go *down* (crawling or incapacitated) with a recovery chance and a timer. The other classic killer for returning players is **cold at night**, especially if you wander into the snow biome naked. Both are covered in depth below and in their own pages.

This page is the hub. Deep dives:

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [[Hunger and Thirst]] | Calories (max 500), hydration, starvation/dehydration thresholds and damage, eating/drinking, food spoilage |
| [[Temperature and Cold]] | Body temperature, cold damage thresholds, biome temps day/night, wet penalty, fire/heat, clothing & comfort warmth |
| [[Comfort and Health Regen]] | What gives comfort, the heal-to caps (81 / 91 / 100), passive regen rules, sleeping-bag heal |
| [[Wounded System]] | Crawling vs incapacitated, recovery %, 45s timer, medkit-in-belt revive, give-up, looting effect, instant-death cases |

---

## The four meters at a glance

| Meter | Max | Danger threshold | What happens below it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Health** | 100 | 0 | Go down (wounded) or die — see [[Wounded System]] |
| **Calories (hunger)** | 500 | < ~40 | **Starvation** status; lose HP over time until you eat or die |
| **Hydration (thirst)** | 250 | < ~25 | **Dehydration** status; lose HP, then movement slows; fully dry = can't run |
| **Comfort** | 0–100% | n/a (it's a *buff*) | Drives passive healing up to a cap (see below) |

Key relationships you must internalize:

- **Hunger drains roughly 5× faster than thirst.** You will get hungry long before you get thirsty. Carry food.
- **You stop passively healing when calories drop to/below 100.** Keep food **above 100** to heal from comfort.
- **Comfort stops working when thirst drops to/below ~50.** Dehydration cancels your campfire heal.
- **Heat and activity (sprinting, fighting) drain thirst faster.** Desert + running = drink more.

---

## Death and downed — the headline change

When your health reaches **0**, one of three things happens:

1. **Instant death** — headshots, a second knockdown within a few minutes, drowning fully, or massive overkill.
2. **Wounded / crawling** — the default. You're on your knees, can crawl slowly and open doors, and have a recovery chance.
3. **Incapacitated** — flat on your back, immobile. Triggered by **fall damage**, being **looted while crawling**, or **crawling into deep water**.

Crawling gives a **base 20%** recovery chance (up to **45%** with full food/water). Incapacitated gives a flat **10%**. A **Large Medkit in a belt/hotbar slot** guarantees you stand back up at the 45-second mark (consumed either way). Full details and the exact console-var numbers are in [[Wounded System]].

To stop crawling and just respawn, open the **F1 console** and type `kill` (the "give up" route — there is no dedicated button, you use the kill command).

---

## What kills returning players (and the fix)

| Killer | Why it happens | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Cold at night** | Naked or under-dressed; snow/desert nights hit âˆ’7 °C to âˆ’30 °C+ | Wear Layer-1 clothing, stay near a [[Camp Fire]], don't sleep in the snow naked — see [[Temperature and Cold]] |
| **Starvation while AFK/looting** | Hunger drains fast; you ignore it | Always keep cooked meat / a stack of berries; eat before it hits 40 |
| **Dehydration in the desert** | Thirst spikes from heat + sprinting | Drink from any fresh water source / bottle / [[Water Catcher]] |
| **Not understanding "down â‰  dead"** | Panic when crawling, or finish-bashing teammates wrong | Read [[Wounded System]]; carry a [[Medical Syringe]] to revive teammates instantly |
| **Bleeding out** | Damage applies a bleed DoT you don't bandage | Use [[Bandage]] / syringe / eat to stop/outpace bleed |

---

## Respawn & survival convars (pinned defaults)

These are the **default server values** behind the survival systems — useful for knowing exactly how long you're locked out of a respawn, and for spotting a modded server. (All values verified 2026-06-13; modded servers freely override them.)

### Respawn cooldowns

| Respawn point | Cooldown before you can use it again | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **[[Sleeping Bag]]** | **~300 s (5 min)** | The base respawn point; cheapest (30 cloth) |
| **Bed** (upgraded bag) | **~120 s (2 min)** | Roughly half the bag cooldown — upgrade key bags to beds |
| **Shared-cooldown radius** | **50 m** | Respawning at one bag/bed **resets the cooldown on every other bag/bed you own within 50 m**, so spreading bags ~50 m apart gives you multiple ready spawn points |

> Source note: Corrosion Hour lists **300 s bag / 120 s bed**; some older sources cite 400 s / 200 s. Treat **300 / 120** as current default and remember any server can change it. Sleeping-bag cap is **15** placed bags per player (see [[Sleeping Bag]]).

### Wounded / downed convars

| Convar | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `crawlingminhealth` | **30** | Min HP granted when you drop into the crawling state |
| `crawlingmaxhealth` | **50** | Max HP granted entering crawling |
| `woundedrecoverchance` | **0.2** | Base 20% chance to stand back up from crawling |
| `incapacitatedrecoverchance` | **0.1** | Base 10% chance from incapacitated |
| `woundedmaxfoodandwaterbonus` | **0.25** | +25 percentage points to recovery at full food + water (20% → 45%) |

Full behavior in [[Wounded System]]. The recovery timer is **45 seconds**.

### Metabolism (hunger / thirst) drain

| Meter | Max (spawn) | Drain behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **Calories** | **500** | Drains continuously; faster when sprinting/fighting/cold |
| **Hydration** | **250** | Drains **~5× slower** than calories (≈5:1 hunger:thirst ratio) |

Exact per-second drain rates aren't published as a clean convar (handled by the metabolism component), but the **5:1 hunger-to-thirst ratio** and the **500 / 250** caps are the durable numbers. Heat and activity accelerate thirst. See [[Hunger and Thirst]] for thresholds (starvation < ~40 cal, dehydration < ~25 hydration, healing gate at > 100 cal).

---

## Healing items (quick reference)

| Item | Effect | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [[Bandage]] | Stops bleeding, small instant heal | Cheap (cloth); craftable tier 0 |
| [[Medical Syringe]] | Heal-over-time + can **revive a downed teammate instantly** | The go-to combat heal; T1 craftable |
| [[Large Medkit]] | Large heal-over-time; **in belt = guaranteed self-revive** at timer | Best self-recovery insurance; keep one on your belt always |
| **Cooked food** | Restores calories + small HP, drives comfort heal | See [[Hunger and Thirst]] and [[Cooking Workbench]] |
| **Anti-Radiation Pills** | Reduce radiation over time | For monument runs without a [[Hazmat Suit]] |

---

## Status effects you'll see on screen (HUD icons)

- **Bleeding** — red droplet; damage over time until bandaged or outpaced by healing.
- **Cold / Freezing** — snowflake; the screen frosts at very low temps; DoT below ~âˆ’7 °C. See [[Temperature and Cold]].
- **Hot / Warm** — fire icon; standing too close to a fire or in extreme desert heat burns you.
- **Starving** — applies under ~40 calories; HP bleed.
- **Dehydrated** — applies under ~25 hydration; HP bleed, then movement penalty.
- **Comfort** — the green buff that enables faster passive healing near fires/furnaces/bags.
- **Radiation (rads)** — builds at irradiated monuments; vision distorts ~50+ stacks, can't run ~100+; offset with [[Hazmat Suit]] / pills.

---

## Related

[[Camp Fire]] · [[Sleeping Bag]] · [[Hazmat Suit]] · [[Cooking Workbench]] · [[Bandage]] · [[Medical Syringe]] · [[Large Medkit]] · [[First Day Guide]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[Getting Started (Rust)]]

pages.title: TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases
pages.body:
# TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases

How building privilege is shared across a group, and why clans run multiple [[Tool Cupboard]]s in one compound. This is the durable-mechanics page; for the social/onboarding layer see [[Clans and Groups]].

## What authorization actually grants

Pressing **Authorize** on a [[Tool Cupboard]] (hold E → Authorize) adds *you* to that TC's list. While authorized, within the building-privilege zone you can:

- **Build, upgrade, and rotate** structures.
- **Pick up and place deployables** (boxes, furnaces, the TC itself if it has no lock).
- **Use traps that require TC privilege** (Flame Turret, Shotgun Trap won't fire at authed players).
- **Place external walls / gates** in the claimed area.

Without auth you get the **"Building blocked"** prompt and can't place or remove anything in that zone.

### Key numbers (verified)

| Stat | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [[Tool Cupboard]] HP | **100** | Soft, but usually buried behind the core — destroying it ends upkeep |
| Max authorized players | **~10** (vanilla default) | Some sources cite 8; modded/group-limit servers change it. Officials sit around 10 |
| Building-privilege radius (stated) | "50 m" in-game text | The real claimed zone is much smaller |
| Real effective radius | **~17.5 m** from the outermost foundation | Adapts to base shape — irregular bases get irregular zones |
| Craft cost | 1,000 wood | Cheap; the loss is the *upkeep reset*, not the TC |

The 10-player auth cap is **per TC**, which is one reason a clan larger than ~10 *needs* multiple cupboards even before considering anti-grief.

## Clearing the auth list (the betrayal button)

**Anyone authorized on a TC can hold E → Clear List**, which de-auths *everyone at once* (including the owner). Implications for a clan:

- After a member rage-quits or gets kicked: **clear the list and re-auth only trusted members.** Also rotate any shared [[Code Lock]] codes and re-do [[Auto Turret]] lists — clearing the TC alone doesn't fix locks or turrets.
- A traitor with TC access can clear the list and re-auth themselves to seize the base. This is why high-trust clans **keep the master TC behind a separate locked, low-access room** and only put a handful of leaders on it.

## Why clans run multiple TCs (multi-TC compounds)

A big base does **not** rely on one cupboard. Reasons:

1. **Spread upkeep.** Each TC holds its own [[Upkeep]] resources; splitting the compound across several TCs means no single cupboard runs dry and collapses the whole place.
2. **Anti-grief / anti-build claiming.** Extra TCs on small foundations placed *around* the perimeter extend the no-build zone, stopping enemies from placing a raid base or building into your walls. See [[Group Bases]].
3. **Raid resilience.** If a raider breaches and destroys the **main** TC, the *other* TCs still hold building privilege over their sections — the attacker can't immediately wall off and claim the whole compound, and your team can still rebuild in the still-claimed zones.
4. **Auth-cap workaround.** With a ~10-player cap per TC, a 12-stack physically can't all auth one cupboard.

### Placement rules for multiple TCs

- **TCs cannot overlap.** You must place each one *just outside* the existing privilege zone. In practice that's roughly **16 m apart** (a few foundations of gap); too close and the game refuses placement ("cannot stack tool cupboards").
- A common compound pattern: **one core TC** for the main base, plus **perimeter "claim" TCs** on 1x1 foundations near the corners/gates, each lock-protected.
- **Lock every TC** with a [[Code Lock]]. An unlocked TC can be picked up by anyone who auths — instant base takeover.
- After a TC is destroyed it provides **~24 h of grief-protection upkeep** before structures start to decay, giving the group time to replace it.

## Auth vs. lock — don't confuse them

- **TC auth** = who can *build*. **Lock** = who can *open doors/boxes*. They are independent. A member can be TC-authed but still locked out of the loot rooms if they don't have the code, and vice versa.
- For a clan: auth the whole team on the TC (so anyone can repair/rebuild after a raid), but **compartmentalize loot with separate [[Code Lock]] codes** (see [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]]).

Related: [[Tool Cupboard]], [[Upkeep]], [[Code Lock]], [[Auto Turret]], [[Group Bases]], [[Clans and Groups]], [[Building Guide]].

pages.title: Team System
pages.body:
# Team System

Everything for playing duo/trio: teams, the 2025 Party system, and pings/markers.

## Teams (in-game)

- Default **max team size: 8** on vanilla (server convar `maxteamsize`; Softcore caps it at **4**, [[Server Types]]; Hardcore disables teams entirely).
- Create: open inventory (Tab) → team UI bottom-left → Create Team. Leader invites by looking at a player and using the prompt, or via the team UI.
- Teammates get: **green nameplates and map dots**, shared visibility of team member status (alive/sleeping/dead), and team voice/markers integration. Authorization on TC/turrets/locks is still **per-player and manual** — being teamed does NOT auto-auth anyone.
- Team info also surfaces in [[Rust+ Companion App]] (teammate locations on the phone map, team chat from the app).

## Party system (Jul 2025 "Friends with Benefits" — the big QoL win)

The old misery of "spawn, die, run 2 km, can't find each other" is fixed:

- **Invite friends from the main menu via your Steam friends list** before joining any server. Parties persist across servers.
- When the party joins a server, members **spawn within ~100 m of each other** on first spawn and are **automatically placed on the same in-game team**.
- You can also invite from the chat panel in-game, and add friends who aren't on your server yet.

Returning-player implication: for a duo/trio wipe-day start, form the party in the menu first — you skip the entire "meet up" phase and start the [[First Day Guide]] route together immediately.

## Pings (Apr 2023 "Make Your Mark" — may have missed it leaving in 2023)

- With **binoculars, drones, or CCTV cameras** equipped: **tap middle-mouse (default ping key)** = contextual ping; **double-tap** = red danger ping; **hold** = radial wheel with 6 ping types (enemy, loot, node, go-to, etc.).
- Pings are visible to teammates in-world and on the map.
- **Map markers**: up to **5 personal markers**, with editable colors/labels; team leader markers show to the team.

## Voice + comms

- In-game voice is proximity. Team voice = use Discord like everyone else; the in-game **phone system** and **broadcasters** exist but are toys.
- The chat panel supports team chat (default: toggle with the chat key, team tab).
- Gesture wheel (hold **B**) for silent friendly-ID — see [[Settings and Binds]].

## Duo/trio etiquette that saves wipes

- Auth everyone on **TC, turrets, code locks** the moment they're placed; un-auth (TC "clear list" + lock code changes) instantly when someone gets community-drama'd.
- Set **bag cooldowns** in mind: bags within 50 m share cooldown when one is used — spread team bags so a team wipe doesn't lock everyone out ([[Sleeping Bag]]).
- Loot rules: one shared "team core" box + personal boxes prevents 90% of group implosions.

Related: [[Settings and Binds]], [[Rust+ Companion App]], [[Server Types]], [[First Day Guide]].

pages.title: Temperature and Cold
pages.body:
# Temperature and Cold

Rust simulates a **body temperature** for your character. Let it drop too low and you take **cold damage over time** — the classic way naked, under-dressed, or snow-wandering returning players die overnight. There's also a **heat** side (fire, desert) that burns you. This page covers the thresholds, biome temperatures, the wet penalty, and how clothing/comfort keep you warm.

---

## How body temperature works

Your displayed temperature is the **ambient temperature modified by**: biome, time of day, weather, whether you're **wet**, proximity to **fire/heat**, and your **clothing** (Layer-1 insulation). The HUD shows a thermometer.

### Cold damage thresholds
| Body temp | Effect |
|---|---|
| Above ~5 °C | Safe — no cold damage |
| Below ~5 °C | **Cold** status begins; light damage over time, scaling colder = worse |
| Below ~âˆ’4 °C | Screen edges **frost over** (visual warning) |
| Below ~âˆ’7 °C | **Significant** cold damage over time — you will die without action |

### Heat / fire side
- Standing **too close to a [[Camp Fire]]**, furnace, or in **extreme desert heat** applies a **Hot/Warm/Burning** status and **damages** you. Back off from the fire — proximity gives comfort+warmth, but right in the flames burns.

---

## Biome temperatures (naked, approximate)

| Biome | Day | Night | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Temperate** (grass) | warm | ~1–4 °C | Safe-ish even naked; the default starter zone |
| **Desert / Arid** | up to ~34 °C (drains **thirst** fast) | down to ~âˆ’7 °C (avg under âˆ’2 °C) | **Hot by day, cold by night** — needs clothing or a fire at night |
| **Arctic / Snow** | ~âˆ’11 to âˆ’32 °C | colder still | **Lethal.** Never go naked; full warm kit required |

**Wet penalty:** being **100% wet** (rain, swimming, deep water) drags temperature **way down**. In the arctic, wet can push effective temp to **~âˆ’44 °C day / âˆ’65 °C night**. Getting soaked then standing in cold is a fast death — dry off by a fire.

> **Returning-player trap:** spawning or sleeping in the **snow biome** naked = freeze to death by morning. Start in temperate, gear up before going north.

---

## Staying warm (in priority order)

1. **Wear Layer-1 clothing.** Head/Chest/Legs each have **Layer 1 (comfort + cold resistance)** and **Layer 2 (armor)**. Layer-1 items — **Hoodie, Pants, Bandana, Hide clothing, Burlap shirt/trousers** — provide warmth. Hands/Feet are single-layer (**Boots, Gloves**).
2. **The [[Snow Jacket]]** is the single best warmth piece — keeps you warm "in any climate" and has notably high **radiation protection**, but it **occupies the whole chest slot** (no chest armor under it) and is overkill/harmful in the desert (overheats you).
3. **Stand near a [[Camp Fire]]** — gives warmth **and** comfort (see [[Comfort and Health Regen]]). Don't stand *in* it (burns).
4. **Stay in the temperate biome** when possible — temperature alone rarely kills there.
5. **Dry off** — get out of water/rain and warm up; the wet penalty is huge.

### Cold vs. armor tradeoff
Heavy metal armor ([[Coffee Can Helmet]], [[Metal Facemask]], [[Road Sign Jacket]]) gives no warmth and the metal pieces can make you colder, so layer **Hoodie + Pants underneath** to offset. A common snow loadout (metal faceplate + jacket + hoodie + pants + wood leggings + gloves + boots) gives ~28+ rad protection and enough warmth to survive a snow night.

---

## Quick survival rules

1. **Don't go to the snow biome under-dressed** — it's the #1 cold killer.
2. **Desert: hot by day (drink up), cold by night (dress or light a fire).**
3. **Below âˆ’7 °C you're taking real damage** — get to a fire or put on Layer-1 clothing now.
4. **Being wet supercharges cold** — dry off before nightfall.
5. **Don't stand inside a campfire** — proximity warms, contact burns.

---

## Related

[[Survival Mechanics]] · [[Hunger and Thirst]] · [[Comfort and Health Regen]] · [[Wounded System]] · [[Camp Fire]] · [[Snow Jacket]] · [[Hazmat Suit]] · [[Coffee Can Helmet]] · [[Road Sign Jacket]] · [[Biomes]]

pages.title: Voice Chat and Audio Routing
pages.body:
# Voice Chat and Audio Routing

How Rust's proximity voice actually gets its microphone, and how to point Rust at a **different** input device than Discord (voice-changer on Rust, clean voice on Discord).

## The one fact that matters

**Rust has NO in-game microphone/input device selector.** Rust's voice chat is built on **Steam's VoIP** (Steamworks voice API), so the input device is chosen in **Steam**, not in Rust's Options → Audio menu. Rust's own Audio options only contain volume sliders (`audio.master`, `audio.voices`, `audio.game`, `audio.music`, `audio.instruments`) plus the push-to-talk bind (default **V**).

> Beware SEO/AI-slop guides claiming Rust has an "Options → Audio → Voice Chat → Input Device" dropdown. It does not exist. Voicemod's own official Rust setup doc and the more careful guides both route you through Steam.

## Where the device is actually set

| Layer | What it controls | Path |
|---|---|---|
| **Steam** (authoritative for Rust) | The mic Rust transmits | Steam → Friends & Chat → gear icon → **Voice** → **Voice Input Device** dropdown |
| **Windows default recording device** | Steam's fallback when the dropdown is on "Default Device" | Settings → Sound → Input |
| **Rust in-game** | Nothing (volumes + PTT key only) | Options → Audio |

Steam's dropdown lists every recording endpoint on the system, including **virtual devices** (VB-CABLE, Voicemeeter Out B1/B2, Voicemod Virtual Microphone). Selecting one explicitly is what makes independent routing possible.

### Default Device vs Default Communications Device

When Steam's dropdown is left on **"Default Device"**, Steam follows the Windows **Default Device**, *not* the Windows **Default Communications Device**. This is a long-standing Steam behaviour and a recurring complaint on the Steam Client Beta forums — people who set only the Communications default find Steam ignoring it.

**Practical consequence:** don't rely on the Communications-device split to separate Rust from Discord. Pick the device **explicitly** in Steam's dropdown instead.

## Rust/Steam voice processing (matters for pitch-shifted or autotuned input)

- **Rust itself applies no user-facing noise suppression** to the mic. There are no Rust convars for noise gate / suppression / AGC.
- **Steam does.** Steam → Voice → **Show Advanced Settings** exposes **Noise Cancellation**, **Echo Cancellation**, input gain, and a **voice transmission threshold** (gate). These run on the signal *before* it reaches Rust.
- If you feed Rust an **already-processed** signal (voice changer, pitch shift, autotune), **turn Steam's Noise Cancellation and Echo Cancellation OFF** and lower/disable the transmission threshold. Steam's RNNoise-style suppressor is trained on human speech; a pitch-shifted or formant-shifted voice can get classified as noise and be gated/chopped. Echo cancellation is also known to break odd inputs outright (documented Steam Client Beta bug reports).
- Voice is compressed for transmit (Steam voice / Opus-class codec at low bitrate, historically narrow/wideband). Expect a **noticeable quality drop** on top of any effect — heavily processed voices come through more degraded than clean ones. *(Codec specifics not confirmed for the current client — treat as directional.)*
- Voice used to travel over Steam P2P directly between players; Facepunch moved it to route **through the game server** after players abused P2P to harvest IPs for DDoS.

## Virtual audio devices as Rust's mic

**Yes, they work.** Rust/Steam accept virtual capture devices — Voicemod's official Rust guide is built entirely on pointing Steam at the "Voicemod Virtual Microphone", and the same applies to VB-CABLE Output and Voicemeeter's Out B1/B2 virtual outputs.

Known friction:
- Steam sometimes **fails to switch input devices** from its dropdown until the Steam client (or the game) is restarted — a widely reported Steam issue, not Rust-specific. Restart Steam after changing the device.
- Some guides insist you also set the virtual device as the **Windows default input**. That's blanket advice for the "Default Device" case; if you select the device explicitly in Steam it should not be required — but it's the first thing to try if Rust transmits silence.
- Virtual devices must be **running/fed** (Voicemeeter engine open, voice-changer app open) before Steam/Rust starts, or the endpoint may enumerate but carry no signal.
- `voice_loopback 1` in the Rust F1 console plays your own mic back — **the** way to verify the processed signal is actually reaching Rust. Set `voice_loopback 0` after.

## Split routing: voice-changer in Rust, clean voice in Discord

The split is achievable because the two apps have **independent, explicit device selectors**:

1. Voice-changer chain (e.g. Voicemeeter/FiiishVoice with pitch + autotune) outputs to a virtual bus (Voicemeeter **Out B1**, or **VB-CABLE Input**).
2. **Steam → Voice → Voice Input Device = that virtual device** → Rust proximity chat carries the effect.
3. **Discord → Voice & Video → Input Device = the physical mic** (Wave:3 / hardware interface) → Discord stays clean.
4. In Discord, also disable Krisp/noise suppression only if you route processed audio there — for the clean path leave it as-is.
5. Verify with `voice_loopback 1` in Rust and Discord's own mic test.

Caveat: this means the effect is **always on** in Rust (no in-game bypass). Toggling requires a hotkey in the voice-changer app itself.

See also: [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]], [[Settings and Binds]], [[Team System]], [[Social and Fun Items]] (Cassette Recorder records the mic in-world).

## Sources

- Voicemod Help Center — "How to set up Voicemod on Rust" (Steam Voice Input Device steps)
- Hollyland — "How to Change a Microphone in Rust": "no in-game options to change the mic input exist"
- VoIP Insight — Rust voice chat guide (Steam Friends & Chat → Voice)
- Steam Client Beta forums — "Steam Voice is using 'Default Device' instead of 'Default Communication Device'"; echo-cancellation breakage reports
- Steam Community — Rust discussions on changing in-game mic input
- rust.facepunch.com — voice moved off Steam P2P to server-routed

pages.title: Wipe Schedule
pages.body:
# Wipe Schedule

## Force wipe (the one that matters)

- **When:** First Thursday of every month, **19:00 UTC** (3 PM Eastern / 12 PM Pacific during DST; 2 PM ET / 11 AM PT in winter).
- **What:** Facepunch ships the monthly update; the client patch is **mandatory**, so every server must update. All maps regenerate (new map seed unless the server pins one).
- **2026 force wipes so far:** Jan 1, Feb 5 (Naval Update), Mar 5, Apr 2, May 7, **Jun 4 ("Built Different" — Unity 6, M16A2, Ballistic armor, Premium Access Pass rename)**. Next: first Thursday of July.

## Map wipe vs Blueprint (BP) wipe

| Wipe type | What resets | What survives |
|---|---|---|
| Map wipe | Terrain/seed, all bases, all items, deployed everything, sleeping bags | Learned blueprints (on servers that don't BP-wipe) |
| BP wipe | Every learned blueprint — back to rock + torch tier knowledge | Nothing progression-wise |

**Big 2025 change:** since the **Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die"** update, **all official Facepunch servers wipe blueprints monthly**, synchronized with the first-Thursday force wipe. The old "officials only BP-wipe a few times a year" rule is gone. Rationale: with the [[Blueprint Fragments]] system, a map-wiped server where everyone already knows everything skipped the whole early game.

Community servers choose their own BP policy — "no BP wipe" long-term servers still exist if you hate monthly resets.

## Server wipe cadences (community)

| Cadence | Who it's for | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Monthly (force wipe only) | Builders, casuals, solos who want a long run | Most vanilla officials are effectively this (now with monthly BP wipe too) |
| Biweekly | The most popular middle ground | Map wipes mid-month + at force wipe; BP policy varies per server |
| Weekly | Sweats, PvP-focused, high pop | Constant fresh starts; fastest progression servers (2x/3x) often weekly |
| Twice-weekly / daily | Aim-train, clan-prep, zerg practice | Not really "survival" anymore |

The server browser shows **last wipe time** on every server; "map: Procedural" + recent wipe date = fresh start. Pick a server wiped within the last ~24–48h as a solo or you'll face established AK bases (see [[Server Types]]).

## Practical wipe-day notes for a solo

- Wipe-day pop is the month's highest; the beach is a war zone for ~2 hours. If you hate that, join 1–2 days after wipe — monuments are calmer and the fragment race ([[Blueprint Fragments]]) has spread out.
- BPs now wiping monthly means **wipe-day knowledge is the meta**: the [[First Day Guide]] route matters every single month, not just after the rare BP wipe.
- [[Rust+ Companion App]] pairing resets with each map wipe — re-pair the server and your smart devices after you rebuild.
- Updates land at 19:00 UTC but big patches can have 1–3h of server instability; don't plan a deep [[Oil Rig]] run in the first hour of a patch.

Related: [[Server Types]], [[First Day Guide]], [[Blueprint Fragments]], [[Workbench]].

pages.title: Wounded System
pages.body:
# Wounded System

> **The #1 thing a returning player must relearn.** Going to 0 HP usually does **not** kill you outright anymore — you go *down* into a recoverable state with a percentage chance and a timer. This was reworked in the **August 2023 "Wounding" update** and the UI now shows your recovery odds and the countdown.

When your health hits **0**, the game rolls one of three outcomes: **instant death**, **wounded (crawling)**, or **incapacitated**. Which one you get depends on *how* you went down.

---

## The three outcomes

### 1. Instant death (no recovery)
You die immediately — no crawl, no timer — when:
- The killing blow is a **headshot** (fatal damage still applies to the head).
- You go down a **second time within a few minutes** of getting back up (the game escalates a re-knockdown to a kill).
- You **drown** (fully underwater out of air).
- Overwhelming overkill damage in one hit.

### 2. Wounded / Crawling (the default)
The most common state. You drop to your **knees** and can:
- **Crawl slowly** along the ground.
- **Open and close doors** (hold E) — that's it.
- You **cannot** pick up items, fire weapons, or use most tools. You **immediately drop** whatever item was in your hand.

On entering the crawling state you're given between **30 and 50 HP** — console var defaults **`crawlingminhealth 30`** / **`crawlingmaxhealth 50`** (verified Facepunch convar values 2026-06-13). A **45-second recovery timer** starts.

### 3. Incapacitated
You lie **flat on your back**, unable to move at all. Same 45-second timer, but a much lower recovery chance. You get pushed into incapacitated (instead of crawling) when:
- You go down to **fall damage** (always incapacitated — and **medkits cannot revive a fall-damage downing**).
- Someone **loots your body while you're crawling** (you "roll over" into incapacitated).
- You **crawl into deep water** while wounded.

---

## Recovery chances and the timer

When the **45-second timer** expires, the game rolls your recovery chance. Hit the roll → you stand back up (at low HP). Miss it → you die.

All convar defaults below verified against Facepunch convar list (2026-06-13):

| State | Base recovery chance | With full food + water | Console var (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Crawling (wounded)** | **20%** | up to **45%** (+25% max bonus) | `woundedrecoverchance 0.2` + `woundedmaxfoodandwaterbonus 0.25` |
| **Incapacitated** | **10%** | (limited bonus, same 0.25 cap applies) | `incapacitatedrecoverchance 0.1` |

So **keeping your calories and hydration topped up literally more than doubles your odds of getting back up** (20% → 45%). The bonus is `woundedmaxfoodandwaterbonus = 0.25` (25 percentage points at full food+water), added on top of the base chance. This is a concrete reason to not run around starving.

The HUD (since the Aug 2023 update) displays both your **recovery probability** and the **countdown to recovery or death**, so you can read your odds while down.

---

## Guaranteed self-revive: Large Medkit in your belt

This is the insurance every player should run:

- Keep a **[[Large Medkit]] in a hotbar/belt slot** (NOT just loose in your inventory).
- When the 45-second timer expires, you get back up **guaranteed** — the medkit overrides the random roll.
- The medkit is **consumed** whether you recover naturally or via the medkit, but you **keep** any unused medkits if you stand up before the timer.
- **Exception:** a Large Medkit will **not** save you from a **fall-damage** incapacitation.

Net rule: **always have a Large Medkit on your belt.** It converts a coin-flip into a near-certain second chance (outside of fall deaths and headshots).

---

## Reviving teammates (duo/trio)

- A teammate can use a **[[Medical Syringe]]** or **[[Large Medkit]]** on your downed body to **instantly** pull you up — no need to wait for the timer.
- This is why the **[[Medical Syringe]]** is the standard combat heal in a squad: it doubles as an instant rez.
- Conversely, if you want to **finish an enemy** who's crawling, **loot their body** (rolls them to incapacitated, lower odds) or keep hitting them — a second knockdown kills.

---

## "Give up" — choosing to die

There is **no dedicated give-up button**. To die on purpose while crawling (e.g., you're trapped, no medkit, want to respawn at base):

1. Open the console with **F1**.
2. Type **`kill`** and press Enter.

You'll die instantly and can respawn at a [[Sleeping Bag]] or bed. Useful when the recovery roll is hopeless or you'd just be picked up and farmed.

---

## Practical playbook

- **Always carry a Large Medkit on your belt.** Coin-flip → near-guaranteed second life.
- **Keep food/water high** before fights — it lifts crawl recovery from 20% to 45%.
- **When you go down in a fight:** crawl to cover or a door, hold E to barricade, wait the timer.
- **In a squad:** call it out; a teammate's syringe is an instant rez.
- **Don't get re-downed fast** — the second knockdown inside a few minutes is a guaranteed kill.
- **Fall damage is special:** no medkit save, straight to incapacitated. Don't try to clutch a high fall.

---

## Related

[[Survival Mechanics]] · [[Hunger and Thirst]] · [[Large Medkit]] · [[Medical Syringe]] · [[Bandage]] · [[Sleeping Bag]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[Returning Player Changelog]]

pages.title: Base Defense & Counter-Raid Playbook
pages.body:
# Base Defense & Counter-Raid Playbook

This is the "how to actually defend" layer on top of the reference pages. For the raw numbers — wall HP, C4 counts, sulfur costs — go to [[Raid Costs]]. For build patterns go to [[Bunkers]] and the base-design pages. For device stats go to [[Auto Turrets]] and [[Traps]]. This page is about **sequencing, decisions, and trade-offs**: where to spend your defense budget, what actually stops a raid versus what just looks scary, and what to do the moment someone starts booming your walls.

Verified against the **"Built Different" update (live Jun 4 2026)**, which was a player-model / [[Ballistic Armor]] / [[M16A2]] drop and **changed zero building HP, door HP, explosive damage, or raid costs** — so all the defense math below is current for the June 2026 wipe cycle.

---

## The one principle everything flows from

You cannot build an unraidable base. Everything dies to enough boom. What you *can* do is make **the sulfur cost of reaching your loot exceed the value of your loot.** That's the entire game of defense. A raider does mental math at your wall: "is what's inside worth the C4 I'm about to spend?" Your job is to make the answer "no," or at least "not worth the noise and time."

Three levers move that math, and you should think about every defensive decision as pulling one of them:

1. **Raw cost** — more wall layers between the outside and your loot = more explosives. See raid-cost scaling below.
2. **Time + noise** — a raid that takes 20 minutes and sounds like a war zone invites third-parties (see [[Counter-Raiding]]) and gives you time to log in and fight back.
3. **Uncertainty** — if the raider can't tell whether your loot is even *in there*, or where it is, expensive guesswork eats their booms. Bunkers, multi-TC, and decoy rooms all sell uncertainty.

A returning solo/duo/trio on a populated 2026 vanilla server is not trying to beat a 10-man's online raid — that's unwinnable and you shouldn't try. You're trying to (a) survive **offline** raids from roamers and small groups, and (b) **win or deny** online raids where you're present to fight. Those are two completely different problems and most of this guide splits along that line.

---

## Defensive design philosophy

### Surround the loot, not the base

The single most common mistake is honeycombing the whole base evenly. Don't. Honeycomb (extra wall layers — see [[Soft Side]] and [[Raid Defense]]) is expensive in upkeep and you can't afford it everywhere. **Wrap your core** — the room holding your [[Tool Cupboard|TC]] and your best loot — in layers, and let the outer shell be thinner. A raider who breaks your outer wall should find another wall, then another, before anything worth taking.

The raid-cost scaling is the whole reason this works. Each [[Stone Wall]] is 2 C4 (4,400 sulfur). A loot room behind one stone wall is 2 C4. Honeycomb it with 2 more layers and it's 6 C4 — **13,200 sulfur** — to reach the same box. You didn't triple your wall count over the whole base; you tripled the cost of the *one line that matters*.

### Make the cheapest line still expensive

Raiders find the **softest path**, not the front door. Your defense is only as strong as your weakest line to loot. That means:

- **No exposed [[Soft Side]].** The soft (inner) face of a wall takes ~10x melee and ~2x firearm damage. A soft-sided stone wall gets silently pickaxed down for the price of a few pickaxes — no boom, no noise. The classic version is the **loot room with an exposed soft underside**: a raider gets directly *below* your loot room and breaks upward through the soft floor. Always honeycomb underneath and beside loot, not just around it.
- **Watch the foundation skirt.** Foundation sides/bottoms are soft. A base on a slope or cliff edge can be soft-side raided from below. Pick flat ground or wall off the low side. See [[Base Locations]].
- **Count your doors honestly.** A [[Sheet Metal Door]] is **1 C4** to pop (250 HP). If your loot sits behind a single sheet door, your loot room costs 1 C4 regardless of how many stone walls surround it. The walls are irrelevant if there's a 1-C4 door into the same room. Doors are usually the cheapest line — design around that.

### Layer your doors and use airlocks

Because the sheet door is the cheap line, you never want a single door between outside and loot. Use **airlocks**: two (or three) doors in series with a small dead space between, so a raider has to blow door → walk into a sealed box → blow another door, often under fire from a peek. Each [[Sheet Metal Door|sheet door]] adds 1 C4; a [[Doors and Locks|garage door]] adds 2; an armored door adds 2-3. An airlock of sheet → garage → core is 1+2+3 = ~5-6 C4 just for the door line, before any wall honeycomb.

### Build cost you can actually pay

Every honeycomb wall costs upkeep (see [[Upkeep and Decay]]). A defense you can't feed decays and falls over on its own. As a solo/duo/trio, build a **small, dense, expensive** base, not a sprawling fortress you can't maintain. A 2x2 or 2x1 core wrapped tight beats a 4x4 you can only afford to stone-grade halfway. The [[Solo Bases]], [[Duo Bases]], and [[Trio Bases]] pages have group-appropriate footprints.

---

## Anti-offline measures (the raid you can't be present for)

This is the defense that matters most for returning solo/duo/trio players, because you sleep and they don't. Offline raiders are doing cold cost math — they want cheap, quiet, loot-positive raids. Your goal is to be **above their threshold**.

### The offline checklist

- **Stone minimum, sheet metal core.** Twig/wood is melee/fire-raidable for nothing. Stone is the floor; upgrade your loot-room shell to sheet metal (4 C4 hard side / ~3 C4 soft) as soon as your economy allows.
- **Multi-TC the core.** A single [[Tool Cupboard|TC]] is a single point of failure — pop it and they can remove your walls for free. **Bury extra TCs** behind honeycomb so they can't be reached or de-authed easily. Multiple overlapping TCs mean a raider can't gain building privilege to deconstruct your base even after breaching, so they have to boom *every* wall the hard way.
- **Don't keep all your eggs in one box.** Spread loot across multiple boxes in different honeycomb cells. A raider who blows into one room and finds 6 boxes can't tell which is the kit and which is the rug. Decoy boxes (empty, or full of cheap junk) waste their time and may make them stop early.
- **Hide a respawn outside the loot room.** A [[Sleeping Bag]] inside the loot room just feeds the raider your kit on respawn. Put your bag somewhere they can't camp.
- **Bunker the core.** A [[Bunkers|bunker]] — a sealed room with no walkable door, entered by a hatch or removable block — forces raiders to break the *shell* (lots of boom) instead of picking a lock or door-camping. The garage-door bunker and the **Armored Triangle Ladder Hatch** (added Apr 2026, Spring Clean) are the reliable, no-exploit versions in 2026.
- **Auto-defense that runs while you sleep.** This is the only thing actually *shooting* during an offline raid. See the turret/trap section below.

### Auto-defense for offline (turrets + traps)

[[Auto Turrets|Auto turrets]] are the backbone of automated defense — 1,000 HP, 10 rW to run, 30 m range, up to 1,536 rounds of 5.56. They track and shoot on their own, day and night. The hard rules:

- **Power them off batteries, not just generators.** A turret with no power is a 1,000-HP box that does nothing. Wire turrets to a [[Large Rechargeable Battery|large battery]] (or several) so they keep firing if a raider cuts your [[Electricity Basics|power]] or your generator runs dry. See [[Electrical Circuits]] for the wiring.
- **Respect the interference cap: 12 active turrets per 40 m.** The 13th won't power. Don't overbuild a turret farm that silently disables itself.
- **Protect the turret, not just the loot.** A turret in the open gets sniped or grenaded from outside its 30 m arc. Put turrets **behind glass/embrasures** or in recessed positions so a raider can't kill them before they enter the kill zone. A turret you can shoot from cover is free to disable.
- **Load good ammo.** Turrets shred with 5.56; HV rounds extend reach. A turret loaded with handmade junk barely tickles armored raiders — and in 2026 a raider in full [[Ballistic Armor]] eats a lot more turret fire than the old roadsign/metal sets did, so don't undergun your turrets.
- **Don't authorize the wrong people.** Authorize every base member; a turret will happily mow down an unauthorized teammate.

[[Traps|Traps]] cover the corridors turrets can't see:

- **Shotgun Trap** — 300 HP, **180 damage per shot** (handmade shells), 4 m detection, up to 384 shells. The bread-and-butter hallway trap. Stack several down a 1-tile corridor for a kill hallway. **Wire to an [[HBHF Sensor]]** so it only fires on enemies and doesn't burn 384 shells on you walking past.
- **Flame Turret** — area denial in tight spaces; great over a bunker hatch or breach point but cheap to destroy (300 HP) so use it as a deterrent/tripwire, not a wall.
- The trap principle: **traps don't stop a determined raid, they bleed it and buy time.** A raider who eats 180 damage on a breach has to heal or retreat — and that's seconds for you (if online) or attrition (if offline). Wire traps to [[Pressure Pad|pressure pads]] / sensors at the predictable breach points: the floor below the loot room, the first airlock, the spot a soft-side raider would stand.

### Reading whether you're worth offlining

If you're a fresh wipe duo with three boxes of frags and a workbench, your base costs less to raid than what's inside, and turrets won't save you. **Match your defense spend to your loot.** Early wipe: small, stone, one airlock, a bag outside. Mid wipe with explosives and a workbench: sheet-metal core, multi-TC, a couple of turrets on batteries, a shotgun-trap hallway. Late wipe with a full kit and a [[Excavator and Quarries|quarry]] worth of resources: full bunker, turret farm, honeycombed loot under glass.

---

## Turret + trap layout patterns

Concrete layouts beat abstract advice. These assume a small solo/duo/trio core.

### The kill-hallway airlock

The standard offline+online piece. A 1-tile corridor from the entrance to the core, lined with:

- One [[Shotgun Trap]] on each wall facing into the corridor, wired to an [[HBHF Sensor]] over the entrance so they fire only on enemies.
- A door at each end (sheet → core), forming an airlock. A raider who blows the outer door steps into the corridor and eats stacked shotgun fire while trying to blow the inner door.
- Optional: a peek embrasure from your safe room into the corridor so you can shoot the breacher yourself when online.

### The recessed turret pocket

A turret sees 30 m but dies if shot first. Recess it into a wall behind a [[Windows Shutters and Frames|window frame]] with glass, or into a triangle pocket, so its arc covers the approach/breach but a raider can't line it up from cover. Two turrets covering each other's blind spots beat one turret in the open. Power both off a [[Large Rechargeable Battery|large battery]] bank.

### The breach-floor trap

The soft underside of a loot room is the classic raid line. Put the loot room one floor up over an empty honeycomb cell, and wire a shotgun trap + flame turret to a pressure pad on the floor below, so a raider who tries to soft-side up from underneath gets lit up in the dead space. Combined with honeycomb, this turns the cheap soft-side line into an expensive, fired-upon one.

### The bunker-hatch denial

Over a [[Bunkers|bunker]] hatch, a flame turret or shotgun trap aimed at the hatch opening means a raider who finally breaks the shell and tries to drop in takes fire on entry. The bunker already forced them to boom the whole shell; the trap makes the payoff a fight, not a free loot.

---

## Online defense (when you're home and they raid anyway)

Online raids are won by the defender far more often than people think, because the raider is committed, exposed, and burning resources on a clock. If you're present, your goal flips from "be too expensive" to **"make them lose more than they gain — kill them, bleed their boom, or make them retreat."** Full tactics live on [[Counter-Raiding]]; the decision-making:

### Hold the breach, don't run out the front

Do **not** sprint out your door to fight in the open — that's their PvP, on their terms, and you'll get traded by their off-angle. Instead, **let them break a wall and funnel into the hole.** You have cover and pre-known angles; they're silhouetted in the breach they just made. A pre-placed [[Shotgun Trap]] or turret on the likely breach corridor (see the kill-hallway layout) means the first raider through eats damage before they can shoot. This is the whole point of designing your base around a breach funnel instead of even honeycomb.

### Counter-boom and re-wall

Every wall you replace makes them pay the raid cost again. If they've opened one layer, **build-block behind it** or drop a wall to reset the funnel. A solo who re-walls one breach during an online raid can double the raider's C4 spend and break their cost math mid-raid. Keep stone/sheet building mats and a hammer in your fight kit, not just guns.

### Relocate loot the instant it starts

The moment you hear the first boom, **move the good stuff** — to a hidden box, a bunker cell, or out a back exit — while they're still breaking the shell. Raiders routinely spend full boom to breach a loot room and find it empty because the defender shuffled the kit during the breach. An empty loot room after 8 C4 is a raid the defender won.

### Bag and respawn discipline

If you die, respawn somewhere they **can't bag-camp** — a hidden bag, not the loot room. Don't feed your kit back through the same door repeatedly. A defender who keeps respawning into the same fatal funnel just gear-feeds the raid. Keep a stash of kits/meds at the respawn so you re-enter the fight armed, not naked.

### Call for help and weaponize the noise

Online raids are loud and that's *your* advantage. Call clanmates/neighbors — a 1v2 becomes winnable with a pincer. And the noise that exposes you also attracts **third-parties** who may hit the raiders (see below). Sometimes the best online defense is simply surviving long enough for someone else to punish the raiders' exposed [[Group Bases|FOB]].

### Use your peeks and meds

A base with shooting floors and peek embrasures lets you trade favorably: shoot, drop back into cover, heal. Keep [[meds]] (syringes, bandages, a [[Combat Mechanics|medical syringe]] stack) in your fight kit. The raider in the breach can't heal as safely as you can in your own walls — out-sustain them.

---

## Shooting floors and peeks

A **shooting floor** is a second story over your core with embrasures (slotted windows / [[Windows Shutters and Frames|shutters]]) that let you shoot down onto raiders working your walls while staying behind cover. Design notes:

- **Cover every wall a raider would breach.** If your loot-room shell has a face nobody can peek, that's where they'll set up uncontested.
- **Use shutters/embrasures, not open windows.** You want to open a slot, shoot, and close it. Open frames let raiders shoot back in and grenade through.
- **Watch your own soft sides.** A shooting floor adds walls — make sure the new floor's underside and the room's soft faces are honeycombed, or you've added a new raid line.
- **Pair with [[Auto Turrets|turrets]].** Turrets suppress the breach while you reposition; you clean up what the turret softened. A raider can't focus the turret and dodge your peek at the same time.
- **Don't over-window the ground floor.** Ground-floor embrasures the raider can reach are just holes; keep peeks high or recessed.

---

## Countering an active raid (third-partying)

The flip side of [[Counter-Raiding]]: when *someone else* is raiding, they are the most vulnerable target on the map. They've committed boom, they're focused on the wall, their loot is in an exposed FOB or [[Group Bases|tower]], and they don't expect a third party. As a solo/duo/trio this is one of the highest-value plays on a populated server.

### When to third-party

- **You hear sustained booming** near you and you have a kit you're willing to risk. The raiders are distracted and exposed.
- **Their FOB is reachable.** Their fresh boom, loot, and rockets are often stashed in a flimsy raid tower next to the target. That's the prize — sometimes worth more than the base they're cracking.
- **You can disengage.** Never commit to a third-party you can't run from. Have an escape and a bag.

### How to third-party

- **Hit the FOB, not the raiders, if you can.** While they're breaking a wall, slip into their tower and take the boom/loot. You might never fire a shot and walk away with their whole raid kit.
- **Take high ground / off-angle.** They're focused on the target base's wall; come from the angle they're not watching.
- **Let the raid soften both sides.** Sometimes the best move is to wait for the raiders to breach and fight the *defender*, then mop up whoever's left and loot both.
- **Grab and go.** Third-parties win by speed and surprise, not by winning a prolonged fight against a committed group. Get the boom, get out.

See [[PvP Tips]] and [[Combat Mechanics]] for the gunplay layer, and [[Raid Methods]] for understanding what the raiders are doing so you can predict their next move.

---

## Raid-base denial

Raiders need a **forward operating base (FOB)** near you to stage boom, store loot, and respawn during a raid. Denying them good FOB spots is a real, underrated layer of defense.

- **Pick a base location with no easy raid-tower spots adjacent.** A core on open flat ground with no cliff, rock, or terrain edge within rocket/peek range is harder to set up against. The [[Base Locations]] page covers terrain choice; the defensive version is "where would *I* build a raid base against me?" — and then deny that spot (build over it, or pick somewhere it doesn't exist).
- **Don't leave buildable terrain in your honeycomb gaps.** Raiders love to twig-tower in a gap between your walls. Floor over or wall off any flat surface adjacent to your loot-room shell.
- **Keep external [[Traps|traps]]/turrets covering the obvious FOB ground.** A turret that can see the only good raid-tower spot makes setting up there a fight, not a freebie.
- **Roof peaks and [[Roof Access and Peaks|roof access]] control.** A raider who can land on your roof can ladder/boom down through the top. Use roof peaks and proper roof access so the top isn't a soft entry, and so a raid tower next door can't simply rocket the roof open.
- **Compound walls buy distance.** A [[Expansion and Compound|compound wall]] pushes raiders back, forces them to tower higher (more visible, more exposed to your peeks/turrets), and denies close FOB ground. It doesn't stop a raid but it changes the geometry in your favor.

---

## Putting it together — a defense plan by stage

| Stage | Core | TC | Doors | Auto-defense | Anti-offline |
|-------|------|----|----|--------------|--------------|
| **Day 1 (fresh)** | Small stone 1x1/2x1, [[Soft Side]] checked | 1 TC | 1 sheet door + airlock if possible | none yet | bag outside loot room |
| **Mid (workbench + explosives in economy)** | Sheet-metal loot shell, honeycomb the core | multi-TC, bury spares | sheet → garage airlock | 1-2 turrets on a [[Large Rechargeable Battery|battery]], one shotgun-trap hallway | spread loot, decoy boxes, hidden bag |
| **Late (full kit + quarry)** | Full [[Bunkers|bunker]] core, loot under glass, honeycomb above/below/beside | multi-TC + buried, redundant | sheet → garage → armored airlock | turret pockets (respect 12/40m cap), trap floors, flame turret over hatch | shooting floors, compound wall, FOB-denied location |

The through-line: **spend defense in proportion to loot, always wrap the core not the base, never leave a cheap line (door or soft side) to your loot, and put something that shoots on the breach.** When you're online, fight the breach, re-wall, and relocate loot — most online raids are the defender's to win.

---

## See also

- [[Raid Costs]] — the master explosive/sulfur table (every number cited here)
- [[Raid Defense]] — honeycomb and raid-cost scaling fundamentals
- [[Counter-Raiding]] — mid-raid defense and third-partying tactics
- [[Bunkers]] — sealed-core build patterns (garage-door, hatch, armored triangle hatch)
- [[Soft Side]] — hard vs soft faces and the loot-room-from-below raid
- [[Auto Turrets]] · [[Traps]] — device stats and wiring
- [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Upkeep and Decay]] — multi-TC and feeding your defense
- [[Solo Bases]] · [[Duo Bases]] · [[Trio Bases]] · [[Group Bases]] — group-appropriate footprints
- [[Doors and Locks]] · [[Windows Shutters and Frames]] — airlocks, peeks, embrasures
- [[Electricity Basics]] · [[Electrical Circuits]] · [[HBHF Sensor]] · [[Pressure Pad]] — powering and triggering defenses
- [[Base Locations]] · [[Expansion and Compound]] · [[Roof Access and Peaks]] — terrain and FOB denial
- [[Ballistic Armor]] · [[M16A2]] — June 2026 "Built Different" gear that raiders bring to the breach

pages.title: Duo & Trio Wipe Guide
pages.body:
# Duo & Trio Wipe Guide

This is the **how-to-actually-play** layer for two or three friends running a vanilla wipe on a populated 2026 server. It assumes you already know the mechanics — for the raw numbers it points you at the reference pages ([[Raid Costs]], [[Rust Weapons]], [[Blueprint Fragments]], etc.) instead of re-listing tables. What it adds is **sequencing, role splits, decision-making, and trade-offs**: the stuff a solo can't do, and the stuff that gets a duo or trio rolled if they get it wrong.

If you're coming back after a break, read [[Returning Player Guide]] first — the progression overhaul (fragments gate workbenches, BPs wipe monthly, mortars killed compounds) is assumed knowledge below. Current patch is **"Built Different"** (Jun 4 2026, Unity 6); it added the loot-only [[M16A2]] burst rifle and the [[Armor|Ballistic armor]] set but **changed no building/raid numbers**, so all the raid math here is current.

The core thesis: **a duo is a solo that never has to stop the loop, and a trio is a duo that can hold ground.** Everything downstream — base choice, monument selection, raid logistics — flows from that.

---

## 1. Why a group changes everything (the force-multiplier math)

A solo's hard limit isn't farm rate — it's **simultaneity**. A solo can only do one thing at a time, so every minute spent farming is a minute not progressing the tech tree, and every roam is the base sitting undefended. The whole [[Solo Survival Guide]] is about managing that single-threaded constraint.

A group breaks the constraint:

- **Two parallel loops.** While one player farms sulfur, the other runs monuments for [[Blueprint Fragments]] and components. You hit Workbench T2 and T3 **roughly twice as fast** because the two gates — fragments (monument-farmed) and HQM (node-farmed) — are now worked in parallel instead of serially. See [[Progression Route]].
- **Someone is always home, or always can be.** With [[Rust+ Companion App]] alarms a solo can react to a raid; a duo/trio can actually *be there* and counter it. See [[Counter-Raiding]].
- **You can take fights a solo declines.** A solo third-parties and runs. A trio holds an angle, trades a player, rezzes, and wins the box. This is the single biggest skill jump from solo.
- **You unlock content gated by bodies.** [[Small Oil Rig]], [[Large Oil Rig]], [[Cargo Ship]], the [[Patrol Helicopter]], and contested [[Launch Site]] runs are *possible* solo but *efficient* in a group. A trio clears Small Oil in the time a solo spends dying to the heavy scientists.

The trap is thinking a group means "do solo things, but faster." It doesn't. It means **do different things** — split, parallelize, and hold.

---

## 2. Roles: split, don't clone

The fastest groups assign **soft roles** for the first 6–8 hours, then blur them once everyone's geared. Hard role lock-in all wipe is a mistake (the farmer resents it, the PvP player gets bored), but the **opening** rewards specialization hard. See [[Clan Roles and Coordination]] for the full doctrine; here's the practical split.

### Duo split (2 players)

You don't have enough bodies for a dedicated farmer *and* a dedicated roamer, so you **alternate**:

- **Player A — Builder/Farmer first.** Gathers the stone for the base, places the [[Tool Cupboard]], builds [[Workbench Level 1]], gets furnaces cooking. Stays close to base early.
- **Player B — Scout/Looter first.** Immediately runs the [[Roadside Junk Piles]] + T1 monument ring for scrap, components, and the first fragments. Brings the early income home.
- **Then they swap and rotate.** Once the base is sealed and a sulfur stockpile exists, A farms sulfur/nodes while B pushes [[Keycards|card runs]], and they trade off so neither burns out and the base is never empty for long.

The duo golden rule: **never both be in the same place doing the same thing in the opening.** Two players hitting the same barrel circle is half the income of two circles.

### Trio split (3 players)

Three bodies is where real role specialization pays:

- **Farmer** — owns the resource economy: sulfur runs, HQM/metal nodes, keeps furnaces full, manages the [[Smelting & Furnaces|smelting]] loop. Builds the [[Quarries|quarry]] mid-wipe. Usually the least-PvP-confident player; this is a feature, not a bug — they stay alive and keep the engine running.
- **Builder/Tech** — owns the base and the tech tree: upgrades the [[Open Core vs Closed Core|core]], manages [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]], runs the [[Blueprint Fragments|fragment]] and [[Keycards|keycard]] runs that gate workbenches, researches guns at the [[Research Table]] / [[Tech Tree]]. The "logistics brain."
- **PvP/Roamer** — owns the map: scouts neighbors, contests [[Roadside Junk Piles|roads]] and [[Airdrop|airdrops]], runs the [[Small Oil Rig]] money loop, and is the designated shot-caller in fights. Best mechanical player.

The trio golden rule: **the farmer keeps farming through everything short of an active raid.** The most common trio failure is all three rushing to every airdrop ping and letting the economy stall. Send the roamer, keep the engine on.

### When to blur roles

Once everyone has a primary rifle (AK/SAR/MP5 — see [[Rust Weapons]]), full [[Armor|metal kit]], and the base is at sheet metal, **drop the roles and roam together**. A geared trio moving as a unit is far more than 3× a solo: you cover angles, share meds via [[Meds & Healing|the rez chain]], and can wipe groups twice your size by holding a building. The opening is for splitting; the mid-game is for stacking.

---

## 3. The shared base: one TC, many loot rooms
