This is the biggest structural decision and it's different from solo. A solo hides everything behind one airlock; **a group's design goal is "one breach must not equal a full wipe."**

### Shared TC mechanics — get this right or grief yourselves

- **Authorize every teammate on the [[Tool Cupboard]].** The TC controls building privilege for everyone in radius; auth is per-player, not team-wide. See [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]].
- **Auth is trust.** Anyone on the TC can pick up your deployables, demolish (within the grace window), and clear the auth list. Only auth people you'd hand your whole base to. The [[Team System]] team UI does **not** grant base access — teaming and authing are separate.
- **One person owns upkeep.** Designate who keeps the TC stocked ([[Upkeep and Decay]]). A base that decays because "I thought you were filling it" is the dumbest way to lose a wipe.
- **Master code on the core, guest codes on shared rooms.** Use [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette|code lock]] tiers: the deep loot/BP room on a code only the responsible players know, shared farm/furnace rooms on the guest code. Lockers store per-player kits.

### Picking the base by team size

Use the [[Base Designs]] decision tree, but the short version:

**Duo →** a **2x2** with an [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open core or stability bunker]]. See [[Duo Bases]]. You want:
- A **bunkered or honeycombed core** so the loot doesn't sit one C4 behind the wall.
- **Two loot rooms minimum** on separate code locks, so a partial raid doesn't get everything.
- Enough room for two large furnaces + a [[Workbench Level 3|WB3]] without cramming.

**Trio →** a **2x2–3x3** with **multiple separated loot rooms** and a shooting floor. See [[Trio Bases]]. The current reference designs:
- **The Naxos** — open core grown around a **bunkered starter** (your day-1 cell becomes the permanent deep bunker). Solves the trio's awkward "between starter and main" raidable window.
- **The Frustrator / Aggravator family** — loot rooms behind **drop-down chutes rigged with shotgun traps**; every door raid becomes a trap gauntlet (25+ rockets to TC, ~40 to open all rooms). High upkeep — only viable once your farm sustains it.

### The 2026 design constraints that override everything

These changed since 2023 and they dictate the shape:

- **Mortars lob over walls (Apr 2026).** The tall-wall compound is dead — a high external wall just flags your roof for a mortar crew firing from *outside* your TC bubble. Go **low-profile, roofed walkways, indoor furnaces**, and push any external walls 30m+ off the structure. See [[Roof Access and Peaks]], [[Expansion and Compound Design]].
- **Explosive protection caps at 75% (May 2025).** Nothing is unraidable. Every wall has a finite [[Raid Costs|rocket cost]] — heavy plate no longer tanks rockets. Your defense is *cost and layers*, not invincibility.
- **Open core needs bodies to work.** An [[Open Core vs Closed Core|open core]] (loot in a central pillar, shooting floor around it) is only good if someone's home to shoot from it. A duo that's often both out should lean **closed/honeycombed**; a trio with offline coverage can run open core.

### Honeycomb math is your real defense

Your wall HP is upkeep; your **honeycomb depth** is the raid cost. A raider pays per layer ([[Raid Costs]]: stone wall = 2 C4 / 4 rockets, sheet = 4 C4 / 7 rockets). Two honeycomb layers of stone before the loot = the raider eats 4 C4 just to reach the room, *then* the room wall. A duo can afford 1–2 honeycomb layers; a trio's farm sustains a full triple-honeycomb open core. **Sheet-metal upgrade the raid path, leave honeycomb you'll never expose at stone** to save upkeep.

---

## 4. The opening: hours 0–8, parallelized

Same arc as solo (rock → tools → base → tech → guns → raid) but **run two/three tracks at once.** Here's the concrete trio plan; collapse the farmer+builder tracks into one alternating player for a duo.

**Hour 0 — everyone gathers, one builder.**
All players punch nodes and trees on spawn to bank starting resources. The moment you have ~1,000 wood + ~2,000 stone, the **builder commits to the base** ([[Starter Bases]]: 2x1/2x2 with airlock) and plants the [[Tool Cupboard]] *immediately* — TC-less = instant decay. The other 1–2 keep gathering and feed the builder. Everyone gets a [[Sleeping Bag]] down inside before doing anything risky.

**Hour 1 — split the tracks.**
- **Farmer:** stays near base, banks stone/wood/metal, gets two furnaces lit, starts the sulfur pile.
- **Builder/Tech:** builds [[Workbench Level 1]] (500 wood + 100 metal frags + 50 scrap, default-known), crafts the [[Tool Recipes|tool kit]], then starts the [[Recycling & Economy|component]] hunt.
- **Roamer:** runs [[Roadside Junk Piles]] and the closest T1 monuments ([[Oxums Gas Station]], [[Abandoned Supermarket]], [[Junkyard]]) for scrap + components. Recycle on-site — **monument recyclers are 5s/120%** vs safe-zone 8s/80% ([[Recycling]]).

**Hours 2–4 — race the two gates in parallel.**
The whole point of a group: work **fragments and HQM at the same time**.
- **Roamer/Tech** hunts the **5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]** for [[Workbench Level 2|WB2]] — best sources are [[Power Plant]] / [[Train Yard]] / [[Water Treatment Plant]] (3 each), plus green-puzzle rooms (1 each). While there, grab [[Green Keycard|green cards]] off desks and run a green puzzle for a **[[Blue Keycard]] + a Basic Fragment**.
- **Farmer** banks the **20 HQM** WB2 also needs and keeps sulfur flowing.
- Build **[[Workbench Level 2]]** the instant both gates are met (500 frags + 20 HQM + 5 Basic — no scrap since Nov 2025).

**Hours 4–6 — first guns + the snowball kit.**
At WB2, research the cheap snowball kit at the [[Tech Tree]] (15/30/60/120 scrap by rarity): **[[Semi-Auto Rifle]] + [[Thompson]] + [[Python Revolver]]**. Craft a [[Armor|budget/metal kit]]. Now the roamer can take real fights and the group can defend a counter. Get [[Meds & Healing|syringes]] crafted — the rez chain is what makes a trio win trades.

**Hours 6–8 — push to T3.**
- **Tech/Roamer** runs **red-card monuments** for [[Red Keycard|red cards]] and **5 Advanced Fragments**: blue puzzles at [[Water Treatment Plant]] (no NPCs — safest), [[Train Yard]], [[Power Plant]], [[Airfield]]; Advanced fragments from elite/locked crates at [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Small Oil Rig]]. *Or* shortcut: [[Bandit Camp]] sells all three cards (Green 15 / Blue 40 / Red 80 scrap).
- **Farmer** banks the **100 HQM** for [[Workbench Level 3|WB3]].
- Build **WB3** (1,000 frags + 100 HQM + 5 Advanced) → research the **[[Assault Rifle|AK]]**, **[[Bolt Action Rifle]]**, **[[MP5A4]]**. Full [[Armor|Metal Facemask + Chest Plate + Road Sign Kilt]] kit. You are now a real threat.

A coordinated trio hits WB3 + AKs in the **first evening** of a wipe. That's roughly a half-wipe head start on a solo.

---

## 5. Group roams: how to actually move as a unit

Once geared, roaming together is where a group's edge compounds. A solo roam is a series of declined fights; a group roam is hunting.

- **Spacing.** Don't stack. Move in a loose wedge so one [[Rust Shotguns|shotgun]] blast or [[Explosives|rocket]] can't catch two of you, but close enough to trade and rez. The roamer/shot-caller leads.
- **Comms = callouts, not chatter.** Direction (clock or cardinal), distance, count, and what they're holding. "Two, north ridge, 80m, one bolty" wins fights; "uh, guys, there's a dude" loses them.
- **Trade and rez.** The mechanical core of group PvP: when a teammate goes down (not dead — [[Wounded System|wounded]]), the others trade the kill or suppress, then rez with a [[Meds & Healing|medical syringe]]. A trio that rezzes beats a trio that doesn't, every time.
- **Hold buildings, don't chase.** Your advantage is angles. When you contest a monument or get third-partied, **funnel the fight into a structure** where you cover doors and they can only push one at a time. Chasing into open ground throws away the body advantage.
- **Designate a looter.** After a won fight, one person loots while the others hold security and watch for the third-party (someone *will* push the gunfire). Don't all dive the bodies.
- **One backpack of meds/ammo, not three.** Coordinate so you're not all out of bandages at once. [[Armor|Armor]] and meds drop on death now (backpacks drop too) — a wiped group feeds the enemy a full kit, so fight where you can recover bodies.

---

## 6. Monuments & events: what a group takes that a solo can't

The reference [[Rust Monuments]] page has the full tier table. Here's the **group lens** — which monuments flip from "risky solo" to "efficient group," and how to run them.

### The duo/trio money loop: Small Oil Rig

[[Small Oil Rig]] is *the* standard duo/trio income run. Solo it's a slog (15 scientists + 6 heavies on the Chinook). As a group:
- One player hacks the **locked crate** (triggers the Chinook of heavy scientists ~timer), the other(s) clear scientists and hold the heli pad.
- Split the floors — clear bottom-up, regroup at the crate. You walk away with components, [[Rust Weapons|guns]], and [[Blueprint Fragments|Advanced fragments]] far faster than the [[Locked Crate]] timer.
- Bring [[Meds & Healing|meds]] and a [[Armor|kit]] — and expect to be contested. Half of running Oil is winning the fight for it.

### Large Oil Rig — trio-and-up territory

[[Large Oil Rig]] (27 scientists + a **12-heavy Chinook response**) is genuinely hard solo and clean for a coordinated trio: one hacks, two hold the corridors against the heavy wave. The payout (2 elites, locked crate, multiple puzzles, Advanced fragments) is the best PvE money in the game if you can hold it — but it's the most contested water monument, so treat every run as a potential PvP fight.

### Cargo Ship — needs bodies and a boat

[[Cargo Ship]] docks at [[Harbor]] now (board from land, 60s departure horn) or board at sea via [[RHIB]]. ~12 scientists + 3 locked crates, loot refills then floods radiation. A solo gets swarmed; a duo/trio splits deck-clearing and crate-hacking and clears it before the radiation phase. **Always assume another group is already aboard or inbound** — Cargo is a PvP magnet.

### Patrol Helicopter — the group fight a solo runs from

[[Patrol Helicopter]] (10,000 HP) can be soloed by killing both rotors with a rifle, but a group does it safely: spread out so it can't focus-fire, pour [[Rust Ammo|incendiary/HV rounds]] into a rotor, and have someone on overwatch for the **inevitable third-party** that the heli's gunfire attracts. Drops 4 high-tier gibs ([[Rust Weapons|LMG/heli loot]]). The hard part isn't the heli — it's the other group that heard it.

### Launch Site & Bradley — coordinate or die

[[Launch Site]] is the T3 flagship (77 crates, [[Bradley APC]], Green+Red puzzle). A trio takes Bradley cleanly: 7 HV rockets or 3 C4 ([[Raid Costs]]), with one person tanking aggro while others rocket it, then split the crates. Solo Bradley is a rocket-budget gamble; a trio makes it routine income.

### Underwater Labs — the low-PvP exception

[[Underwater Labs]] is the **lowest-PvP loot source** (random layouts, ~25 crates, sub entry). Good when your group wants loot without a guaranteed fight — send the farmer-type here while the roamer contests the hot monuments. A duo can chain-loot labs all evening with minimal contest.

**General rule:** a group's monument selection should be *parallel*, not *convoy*. Don't all run the same monument unless it requires the bodies (Oil, Cargo, Heli, Bradley). Otherwise split — roamer on hot monuments, farmer/tech on safe loot — and double your hourly income.

---

## 7. Group raiding logistics

Raiding is where a group's coordination either shines or collapses. The explosive math is in [[Raid Costs]] and [[Explosives]]; the craft chains in [[Explosive Recipes]]. This section is the **operational** layer — see [[Raid Bases and FOBs]] and [[Raid Methods]] for the full doctrine.

### Scout before you commit

The cardinal sin is throwing boom blind. Before a raid:
- **Count the cost.** Identify the target's wall grade and door types ([[Soft Side]] matters — soft side is ~25% less boom). Walk the [[Raid Costs|cost]]: a sheet-metal loot room behind a stone wall + an [[Sheet Metal Door|sheet door]] is ~2 C4 (wall) + 1 C4 (door); a honeycombed core is far more. If you can't afford the *whole* path, don't start — a half-raid just arms the defender and feeds them your boom on the counter.
- **Check occupancy.** [[Raid Defense|Online vs offline]] is the single biggest variable. Offline raids are cheap and safe; online raids need enough bodies to breach *and* fight the defenders simultaneously. A duo rarely has the bodies for a contested online raid on a defended base — pick offlines or eco targets.
- **Identify the loot room.** Don't blow the whole base — blow the *path to loot*. [[Soft Side|Soft-side]] the breach where possible.

### The FOB — non-negotiable for anything bigger than a door

For any multi-C4 raid, build a [[Raid Bases and FOBs|Forward Operating Base]] near the target:
- **Sleeping bags inside** so deaths during the raid respawn you *at* the raid, not back home. This is what lets a group push a defended raid — you can afford to die.
- **Store boom and loot in the FOB**, not on your bodies. Everything on your body (and in your backpack) drops on death — a wiped raid party that was carrying all the C4 just gifted it to the defender.
- **Mount [[Auto Turret]]s / shotgun [[Traps|traps]]** facing the likely third-party and counter-push directions. Raids attract crowds.

### Raid roles (the six-role split)

From [[Raid Bases and FOBs]] / [[Clan Roles and Coordination]], scaled to your size:

- **Boom carrier** — holds and places the [[Explosives|C4/rockets]], calls the breach sequence.
- **Security/overwatch** — watches for the defender's counter and the third-party. *This role is mandatory* — the loudest raid in the area always draws a vulture group.
- **Looter** — clears loot fast once the room's open (puzzle resets and gas in monuments are a model: loot fast, leave).

A **duo** runs these as boom+looter / security, swapping. A **trio** runs a clean boom / security / looter split — the trio's whole raiding advantage is that someone is *always* watching the back door while the others work.

### Online vs offline — the group decision

- **Offline raid:** cheaper (no defenders shooting back), the duo/trio bread-and-butter. Scout the target's online hours via [[Rust+ Companion App|Rust+]]/observation, hit when they're asleep. Risk is purely the third-party, so still post security.
- **Online raid:** needs enough bodies to breach *and* win the gunfight. Realistically trio-and-up against a defended base; a duo should only online-raid weaker or distracted targets. The payoff is catching loot before they can hide/scatter it.

### Eco-raiding for the early game

Before you have a C4 economy, [[Eco-Raiding]] is how a group punches up: beancans, [[Eoka Pistol|eoka]] shells, [[Melee & Bows|fire/molotov]] on wood, satchels, landmines on doors. A duo/trio that eco-raids a few naked/wood bases in the first day snowballs into the boom economy that funds real raids. See [[Raid Methods]] for the boom-path ladder.

### Counter-raiding — your group's defensive edge

The flip side: when *you* get raided, a group can [[Counter-Raiding|counter]] in a way a solo can't. With [[Rust+ Companion App|Rust+]] alarms ([[Electrical Circuits|smart alarm chain]]) and bodies at home, you can peek the raiders mid-breach, deny them the loot room, and turn their committed boom into a wipe *for them*. The decision — counter vs bail — comes down to: are you geared, are you home, and can you out-body them? If yes, the raider who committed C4 to your wall is now fighting on your turf with their boom already spent. See [[Counter-Raiding]] and [[Raid Defense]].

---

## 8. Sustain & mid-wipe economy

The opening is parallelized; the mid-wipe is about keeping all engines running so you're always boom-positive.

- **Place a [[Quarries|quarry]] mid-wipe** (Survey Charge anywhere, or run static monument quarries / the [[Giant Excavator]] on [[Diesel Fuel|diesel]]). The farmer owns this. A running sulfur quarry is what turns a trio from "raids occasionally" into "raids on a schedule."
- **Run the [[Pure Scrap Tea]] loop** if someone enjoys [[Farming Meta & Loops|farming]] — it massively boosts barrel scrap and funds [[Bandit Camp|Bandit]] keycard/vehicle purchases.
- **Get a [[Minicopter]] or [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]]** from Air Wolf (750 / 1,250 scrap) the moment you can afford it. Air mobility is a group force-multiplier: fast monument runs, raid insertions, and escape. A trio with a Scrap Heli does in an hour what grounded takes three.
- **Keep furnaces and the [[Smelting & Furnaces|smelt loop]] running overnight** — [[Large Furnace|large furnaces]] batch-smelt while you sleep so the morning starts with metal/HQM banked.
- **Don't let the base outgrow the farm.** Every wall you upgrade and every loot room you add raises [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]]. A trio that builds a Frustrator it can't feed loses the base to decay, not raiders. Match base ambition to sustained farm rate.

---

## 9. Quick reference — duo vs trio cheat sheet

| Dimension | Duo | Trio |
|-----------|-----|------|
| Opening play | Alternate builder/farmer & scout/looter; never both same spot | Hard split: Farmer / Builder-Tech / Roamer |
| Base | [[Duo Bases\|2x2]] honeycombed or stability-bunker, 2 loot rooms | [[Trio Bases\|2x2–3x3]] multi-loot-room + shooting floor (Naxos / Aggravator) |
| Core type | Lean closed/honeycomb if often both out | Open core works if offline coverage exists |
| Money loop | [[Small Oil Rig]], [[Underwater Labs]], [[Cargo Ship]] | + [[Large Oil Rig]], [[Patrol Helicopter]], [[Launch Site]]/[[Bradley APC]] |
| Roaming | Trade-and-rez, pick fights, avoid 3+ groups | Hold buildings, contest monuments, win even-or-down |
| Raiding | Offline & eco; online only on weak/distracted targets | Full FOB + 3-role split; can run contested online raids |
| Biggest failure | Both AFK-farming same circle; base undefended | All three chasing every airdrop; farm stalls |

---

## See also

[[Returning Player Guide]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[Progression Route]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Keycards]] · [[Rust Weapons]] · [[Armor]] · [[Meds & Healing]] · [[Base Designs]] · [[Duo Bases]] · [[Trio Bases]] · [[Open Core vs Closed Core]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Explosives]] · [[Raid Methods]] · [[Raid Defense]] · [[Counter-Raiding]] · [[Eco-Raiding]] · [[Raid Bases and FOBs]] · [[Clan Roles and Coordination]] · [[Small Oil Rig]] · [[Large Oil Rig]] · [[Cargo Ship]] · [[Patrol Helicopter]] · [[Launch Site]] · [[Underwater Labs]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Quarries]] · [[Rust+ Companion App]]

pages.body:
# Farming Empire

This is the **how-to-actually-do-it** layer on top of the farming reference pages. The mechanics live in [[Plant Genetics]], [[Farming Basics]], [[Teas]], [[Composter]], [[Berries & Crops]], [[Pure Scrap Tea]], and [[Cooking & Food]] — go there for the full tables. This page is the **sequence, the decisions, and the loops**: in what order to build, how to grind from random seeds to a GGGGGG/YYYYYY clone stash, how to wire one self-watering planter that runs while you sleep, which teas to mass-produce and why, how to be food-independent, and the single highest-leverage thing a farm does for you — the **scrap-tea barrel loop**.

Written for a returning solo/duo/trio on a populated 2026 vanilla server. As of the **Built Different update (June 2026)** the farming system is unchanged from the Farming 2.0 / Cooking-Update era — genetics, planters, teas, and pies all work as described in the reference pages. Re-verify numbers on rusthelp.com after each first-Thursday patch, but the workflow below is stable.

> **The one-sentence version:** a hidden indoor farm of cloned god-seed berries feeds a [[Mixing Table]] that mass-produces [[Pure Scrap Tea]], which turns a road of barrels into ~2,000 scrap/hour — and the same farm makes you cloth-, food-, and tea-independent so you never have to do a risky food run again.

---

## Why bother (the payoff, up front)

A returning player's instinct is "farming is a tryhard side-quest." On a populated server it's the opposite — it's the **lowest-risk, highest-ceiling economy in the game** because it runs *inside your base* while you're doing other things. Concretely, a finished farm gives you:

1. **A scrap engine.** [[Pure Scrap Tea]] is +350% barrel scrap for an hour. A barrel run that nets ~500 scrap raw nets ~2,000+ with the tea. Scrap funds the [[Blueprint Fragments|tech tree]], [[Bandit Camp]] purchases (the [[Attack Helicopter]] is 2,250 scrap), and recycler feedstock.
2. **Cloth independence, day one.** A hemp planter ends scavenging for cloth — bags, bandages, sleeping bags, [[Backpacks]], clothing, sewing kits all flow from one box.
3. **Food + water independence.** A pumpkin patch feeds you *and* hydrates you, so you stop doing dangerous food runs and stop dying of thirst in the desert.
4. **Gather multipliers.** [[Wood Tea]] / [[Ore Tea]] roughly double-to-triple your wood and sulfur intake when you're building or stockpiling for a raid.
5. **Fight prep.** Pure [[Healing Tea]] + Pure [[Max Health Tea]] = ~120 effective HP and a big instant heal, brewed from berries you already grow.

Everything below is the order to build these in, and how to get the genetics that make them cheap.

---

## Phase 0 — Minimum viable farm (the same day you have a base)

Don't wait for perfect genetics. Stand up a **working** farm immediately with random seeds; you upgrade the genes *while it already runs*. The minimum viable indoor farm (from [[Farming Basics]]) is:

- **1x Large Planter Box** (9 slots, the 3x3 grid genetics needs).
- **1x [[Ceiling Light]]** mounted on the ceiling directly above it — one light covers the whole box and also adds the **Temperature** stat. Low power draw; see [[electricity]].
- **1x Sprinkler** fed by a Water Catcher or Water Pump via the Hose Tool — once running, water sits at 100% and you never hand-water.
- **1x [[Composter]]** for fertilizer (craft: 200 wood + 2 Tarp, or buy at [[Bandit Camp]] for 30 scrap).

**The core rule that trips everyone up:** plant health is **capped at the LOWEST of four soil stats** — Water, Sunlight, Soil Quality, Temperature ([[Farming Basics]]). A perfect 100% water/light/temp is wasted if Soil Quality sits at 20%. So:

- Light handles Sunlight + most of Temperature.
- Sprinkler handles Water.
- Fertilizer handles Soil Quality — add **1 fertilizer per planted seed**.

Get all four green and the box runs itself with one daily top-up. That's Phase 0. Now you start the genetics grind in parallel.

---

## Phase 1 — Genetics min-maxing: random seeds → god-seed clone stash

This is the heart of the empire. The goal is a small library of **cloned "god seeds"** — typically **GGGGYY**, **GGGYYY**, **YYYYGG**, or for a pure-yield berry the all-green **YYYYYY** — that you replant forever and never touch a random seed again. Recap of the gene types from [[Plant Genetics]]:

| Gene | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| **G** Growth | Faster seed→ripe. More G = more harvests per hour. |
| **Y** Yield | More output per plant. **Every 2 Y genes = +1 extra clone** when cloning. |
| **H** Hardiness | Resilience to imperfect soil — fine but not the priority. |
| **W** Water | **Bad.** Forces higher water consumption — drains your tank. |
| **X** Empty | **Bad.** A dead, wasted slot. |

G, Y, H are green (good); W, X are red (bad). G and Y are the two you actually chase. **Why purge reds matters in practice:** W genes make a 9-plant box drink your tank dry; a pure-green box barely sips, which is the whole reason a sprinkler keeps up.

> **Yield threshold trick:** harvest counts round down. A yield value of **2.49 gives 2** items, but **2.50 gives 3**. One more Y gene can flip that threshold and quietly add 50% to a harvest — this is why people grind to 4–6 Y on a dedicated berry strain.

### The crossbreeding mechanic in one paragraph

Crossbreeding only happens during the **Crossbreed stage (~2 minutes)**. The instant a plant enters that stage, each of its 6 gene slots is recalculated by **voting** from its **8 neighbors** in the 3x3 box (orthogonal *and* diagonal). **Green genes vote with weight 0.6; red genes vote with weight 1.0** — so red is *dominant*: a single red (1.0) beats a single green (0.6) in that slot. To win a slot for green you need **multiple greens stacking the same position**: two greens (0.6 + 0.6 = 1.2) beat one red (1.0). That single fact — stack greens to drown reds — is the entire technique. Note: **planter boxes do not cross-pollinate each other** — all breeding happens inside one box's 9 slots.

### Step-by-step to a god seed

**Step 1 — Gather raw material.** Forage wild bushes (each pick gives 1 berry + 1 seed) or harvest your Phase 0 random planting. Plant **15–25 random seeds** and inspect their genes. **Keep every candidate with 5-of-6 green** (e.g. `GGGGGY` with one red, or `GGGYYG`). Discard 3+ red seeds. You want a handful of near-perfect parents.

**Step 2 — Use a genetics calculator.** Don't eyeball it. Type your candidate genes into any Rust gene calculator (e.g. rustrician-style or the Steam-guide calculators), set your target (say 4G/2Y), and it returns a **placement recipe** — which seed goes in which of the 9 slots so that green votes overpower reds in every slot. This turns a stochastic mess into a deterministic plan.

**Step 3 — Place to avoid stacked reds.** The hard rule: **never let two neighbors share the same red gene in the same slot.** If two adjacent plants both carry a W in slot 4, that slot gets a combined red weight of 2.0 and your green votes (0.6 each) can't catch up. Spread your reds across different slots so no single slot is double-red.

**Step 4 — The center-plant timing trick.** This is the pro move. Plant the **8 outer slots first**, let them establish, then plant your "target" specimen in the **center slot slightly later**. The center reaches the Crossbreed stage *after* its 8 neighbors are mature, so it absorbs their combined green votes. Five greens flanking the center sum to ~3.0 in a slot — they obliterate a single red (1.0) and pass green into the center. Repeat, walking the center plant closer to all-green each generation.

**Step 5 — Clone the winner.** The moment a plant reaches a target like GGGGYY, take **clones at the Sapling stage** — clones are *genetically identical* to the parent. You now have an unlimited supply of that exact seed. Berries and hemp give **3 clones** per cloning; food crops give **2**; extra Y genes add more (every 2 Y = +1 clone). One good parent + cloning = a god-seed stash in a couple of cycles.

**Step 6 — Retire random seeds forever.** Fill all your planters with clones. From here you only ever replant clones; the random-seed grind is a one-time tax. Keep a few backup clone seeds in a labeled box per strain (one for high-G hemp, one for high-Y yellow berry, one for high-Y white berry, etc.).

### Two strains to actually build first

You don't need one perfect seed — you need **two specialized strains**:

1. **High-Y berry strain (yield-first):** push to **YYYYYY or YYYYGG**. Yield-maxed yellow and white berries are what make [[Pure Scrap Tea]] cheap (a Pure costs 32 yellow + 32 white berries; more Y per harvest = fewer cycles per Pure).
2. **High-G hemp strain (growth-first):** push hemp toward **GGGGGG or GGGGYY**. Fast hemp turnover keeps cloth flowing for bags/bandages/clothing.

A true all-green **GGGGGG** is the absolute fastest-cycling plant (great for hemp); **YYYYYY** is the absolute highest-output (great for berries you brew). Most farmers settle on **GGGGYY / GGGYYY** as the do-everything compromise — fast *and* high-yield.

---

## Phase 2 — Automating the farm (planter + light + water + composter)

Once genetics are dialed, scale and automate so the farm is genuinely "set and forget."

### Planters
Use **Large Planter Boxes** only for production (Small Planters are 1-slot starters). Each Large box is 9 slots; a serious solo runs 2–4 boxes (one hemp, one yellow berry, one white berry, one mixed-rainbow/food). Remember boxes don't cross-pollinate — keep each strain in its own box, which is convenient because you *want* them separated anyway.

### Light
One **[[Ceiling Light]]** mounted directly above each Large box. It covers the full box, supplies Sunlight, and bumps Temperature (important in snow biomes). It's a low-power consumer — see [[electricity]] for the small solar/battery or generator loop to run it. Indoor + electric beats outdoor sun farming: no day/night dependency, no exposure to raiders eyeballing your crops.

### Water (the automated loop)
Goal: Water stays at 100% with zero manual input. The standard chain from [[Farming Basics]]:

**Water source → Hose Tool → Sprinkler over the planters.**

Source options, in order of convenience:
- **Water Pump** pulling from a lake/ocean (most reliable, constant flow).
- **Large Water Catcher** (passive rain collection) — fine in wet biomes, dry in deserts.
- The **April 2026 Water Wheel** river generator can power this loop off flowing water — see [[Berries & Crops]] and [[electricity]].

Sprinkler math to size your source: a sprinkler consumes ~2 water/sec; a source outputting ~6 water supports ~3 sprinklers, ~12 supports ~6. Plan source output to cover all your boxes plus headroom. **Pure-green seeds barely drink** (no W genes), so a modest source covers a lot of planters — yet another payoff of purging W.

### Fertilizer + the horse-dung pipeline
Soil Quality comes from fertilizer, made in the **[[Composter]]**. The single best input by a mile: **Horse Dung = 5 fertilizer each** (everything else is ~0.2–0.3, i.e. 4–6 items per 1 fertilizer). The efficient pipeline ([[Composter]]):

1. Keep a **horse** in a 1x2 stable next to the farm.
2. One horse makes **~8–12 dung/hour**.
3. Feed it **bread** (baked from [[Berries & Crops|wheat]] at the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]]) to boost dung output.
4. Dung → composter → fertilizer → planters.

A single horse easily keeps a multi-box farm at 100% Soil Quality. **Never compost berries** — they're worth far more brewed into [[Teas]]. Toss in spare meat/veg/fish if you have no horse yet, but the horse loop is the real answer.

---

## Phase 3 — The tea production line (which teas, and why)

Teas are the entire reason the farm exists. All teas brew at a [[Mixing Table]] (or the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]], which absorbs the mixing table). Every tea tiers **4-to-1**: 4 Basic = 1 Advanced, 4 Advanced = 1 Pure. So a Pure = 16 Basic-worth of berries. Full catalog in [[Teas]]; here's the production *priority*:

### S-tier: mass-produce these
| Tea | Recipe (Basic) | Effect | Make in bulk? |
|-----|----------------|--------|---------------|
| **[[Pure Scrap Tea]]** | Yellow + White ×2 | **+350% barrel scrap, 60 min** | **YES — this is the whole point.** Brew Pures constantly. |
| **[[Wood Tea]]** | Red + Blue ×2 | Pure ~+100% wood | Yes, before any build/upkeep run |
| **[[Ore Tea]]** | Yellow + Blue ×2 | Pure ~+50–60% ore/sulfur | Yes, before a sulfur stockpile for raiding |

### A-tier: keep a stock, don't necessarily mass-brew
| Tea | Recipe | Effect | When |
|-----|--------|--------|------|
| **[[Healing Tea]]** | 4× Red | Pure: +30 instant + ~75 over time | Pre-fight stack |
| **[[Max Health Tea]]** | 3× Red + 1× Yellow | Pure: +20 max HP | Pre-fight stack (with Healing = ~120 eff. HP) |
| **[[Harvesting Tea]]** | berries | +150% corpse resources | Hunting runs |

### Situational: brew on demand
- **[[Anti-Rad Tea]]** (2 Red + 2 Green) — required for [[Launch Site]] / [[Military Tunnels]] / deep oil rig. Pair with radiation armor inserts ([[Cooking & Food]]).
- **[[Warming Tea]] / [[Cooling Tea]]** (Red + Yellow) — biome comfort; snow nights / desert days.

### What this means for your berry mix
Because the S-tier list runs on **Yellow, White, Red, Blue** berries (Scrap = Yellow+White, Wood = Red+Blue, Ore = Yellow+Blue), prioritize farming **Yellow and White** first (Scrap Tea), then **Red and Blue** (Wood/Ore + Healing/Max Health). Green and Black are niche (Anti-Rad / minor recipes) — a few plants are enough. See [[Berries & Crops]] for the berry-to-tea map.

### The pie multiplier
At the [[Cooking & Food|Cooking Workbench]], a **Bear Pie doubles tea effects (but halves duration)**. Eat a Bear Pie *then* drink a Pure Scrap Tea and you get a monstrous scrap multiplier for a focused ~30-min barrel blitz. Use it when you've found a barrel-dense route and want to clear it fast.

---

## Phase 4 — Food self-sufficiency

The farm should also end your food/water anxiety so you never log in starving. From [[Berries & Crops]] / [[Cooking & Food]]:

| Crop | Calories | Hydration | Role |
|------|----------|-----------|------|
| **Pumpkin** | +80 | **+30** | **Best all-round** — top hydration + heal. Grow these. |
| **Corn** | +75 | +10 | Solid backup |
| **Potato** | **+125** | +5 | Most calories, almost no water — feeds a group, keep water handy |

**The food plan:**
1. Dedicate part of one Large box (or a whole box for a trio) to **pumpkins** — they cover hunger *and* thirst, so you can ignore water sources on base.
2. Build a **Cooking Workbench** (it's the Mixing Table + BBQ + bench in one). Cook meat to remove poisoning risk and add ~20% calories.
3. Remember **food spoilage** (Cooking Update): raw meat ~6h, cooked ~24h, produce ~48h. A **powered Electric Fridge** *pauses* the spoil timer — stockpile cooked meat and pies there.
4. Optional protein loops: a **chicken coop** (4 chickens → eggs + meat, needs hunger/thirst/sunlight/love) and **beehives** (honey) — see [[Cooking & Food]].

For buffs, bake **Pumpkin Pie** (tops everything + max HP), **Pork Pie** (3× healing-over-time, fast post-fight recovery), and **Survivor's Pie** (+50% corpse yield, stacks with [[Harvesting Tea]] on hunts).

---

## Phase 5 — The best scrap-tea farm loop (the empire's engine)

This is the repeatable money loop the whole farm is built to feed. Detail in [[Pure Scrap Tea]]; here's the operational run-of-show.

### The loop
1. **Grow** Yellow + White berries on your high-Y strain. A Pure Scrap Tea needs **32 Yellow + 32 White berries** (16 Basic → 4 Advanced → 1 Pure), so high Yield genes pay for themselves fast.
2. **Brew up the tree** at the [[Mixing Table]] / Cooking Workbench. Keep a rolling stock of Pures — you want several ready at all times.
3. **(Optional) Eat a Bear Pie** for a doubled-effect blitz.
4. **Pop a Pure Scrap Tea** the moment before you start a **barrel run** — a road, [[Junkyard]], or a monument *perimeter* dense with barrels.
5. **Smash barrels for the full hour.** Barrels that drop ~2 scrap now drop **~8–9**. Reported **2,000+ scrap/hour** early-wipe on a good route.

### The critical limitation — do not waste the tea
**Scrap Tea multiplies BARREL scrap only.** It does **nothing** for:
- Crates (military / normal / elite),
- **Recycler output** (recycling components is unaffected),
- Vendor sales, [[Fishing]] rewards, or [[Gambling]] winnings.

So **never** drink it for a recycling session or a crate-farming monument run. Drink it for *barrels*, period. Pair the run with components for [[Recycling]] back home (recycle is separate income — the tea just doesn't boost it).

### Best routes for the hour
- **Roads** — long stretches of roadside barrels; chain them with a [[Minicopter]] or motorbike to cover ground in the 60-minute window.
- **[[Junkyard]]** — barrel-dense and central.
- **Monument perimeters** — the *outside* barrels at [[Oxum's Gas Station]], [[Mining Outpost]], [[Abandoned Supermarket]], etc. (you're smashing barrels, not doing the puzzle).
- Combine with picking up **components** along the way → recycle at home for a second income stream.

### Where the scrap goes
- **[[Blueprint Fragments|Tech tree]]** unlocks (the fastest way to guns/armor as a returning player).
- **[[Bandit Camp]]** buys — including the **[[Attack Helicopter]] at 2,250 scrap** and the [[Composter]] itself at 30.
- **Recycler feedstock** and component-gated crafts.

---

## Putting it together — a build sequence checklist

A clean order for a returning solo (compress timelines for a duo/trio who can parallelize):

1. **Day 1:** base up → 1 Large Planter Box + Ceiling Light + a Water Catcher/Pump + Sprinkler + Composter. Plant **random hemp** immediately (cloth now).
2. **Day 1–2:** plant 15–25 **random berry seeds** as genetics raw material; inspect, keep 5/6-green candidates.
3. **Day 2–3:** run the **center-plant crossbreeding** workflow → clone a **high-G hemp** strain and a **high-Y yellow + white berry** strain. Retire random seeds.
4. **Day 3+:** scale to 2–4 Large boxes (hemp / yellow / white / mixed-food). Add a **horse + dung composter** loop for hands-free fertilizer.
5. **Ongoing:** build a **[[Mixing Table]]**, then upgrade to a **Cooking Workbench**. Mass-brew **[[Pure Scrap Tea]]**; keep Wood/Ore on hand for build/sulfur days; keep a Healing+Max-Health stack for fights.
6. **Income loop:** Bear Pie (optional) → Pure Scrap Tea → barrel road run → ~2,000 scrap/hr → tech tree + Bandit Camp.
7. **Self-sufficiency:** a pumpkin block + Electric Fridge so food/water never gates your play.

That's the empire: a hidden, automated, gene-optimized berry farm that prints scrap, cloth, food, and combat buffs while you do everything else.

---

## See also

- [[Plant Genetics]] — full gene mechanic, weights, crossbreeding deep-dive
- [[Farming Basics]] — soil stats, planters, water/light/fertilizer setup
- [[Teas]] — complete tea catalog with all tiers and recipes
- [[Pure Scrap Tea]] — the scrap loop reference

pages.title: Full Base Automation
pages.body:
# Full Base Automation

The complete "wire your whole base so it runs itself" guide for a returning **solo/duo/trio** on a populated 2026 vanilla server (current patch: [[Built Different Update|Built Different]], June 2026). This is the *how to actually build it, in what order, and what to do when you can't afford the ideal version yet* layer on top of the reference pages. Read [[Electricity Basics]] for how power flows, [[Electrical Components]] for the parts list, [[Electrical Circuits]] for the canonical wiring recipes, and [[Industrial]] for the item-moving layer — this page sequences all of them into one base.

**The mindset shift for a returning player:** automation in Rust is not an endgame luxury. Every minute you spend hand-feeding furnaces, hand-sorting loot, or babysitting a farm is a minute you're not running monuments, raiding, or holding map control. A solo with a self-smelting, self-sorting, self-defending base plays a fundamentally different game than one who logs in to a chore list. Build the backbone early (often by day 2-3), then bolt modules on as scrap allows.

**Test everything in [[rustrician.io]] first.** Every electrical circuit here can be dragged out in the free simulator before you spend a single HQM. The simulator uses the **Test Generator** (100 rW, infinite) as its source — mentally swap that for your real [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] line.

---

## The build order (read this first)

Don't try to wire everything at once. The dependency chain is:

1. **Power backbone** — sources -> [[Root Combiner]] -> [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] -> distribution. *Nothing else works without this.*
2. **Auto-turret array** — defense first. An automated base that can't defend itself just feeds raiders a tidier loot pile.
3. **Smart alarm + Rust+** — so you know when to log in / repair / fight.
4. **Auto-furnace line** — the single biggest quality-of-life win; ore in, ingots out.
5. **Industrial sorting + auto-crafting** — loot dumps and refines itself.
6. **Auto-door bunker** — a hidden core that survives soft-side raids.
7. **Sprinkler farm** — passive food/cloth/genetics once the rest is humming.

Each section below is a self-contained module with a component list, build order, power budget, and the solo/duo/trio trade-offs. Power budgets accumulate — track your **total continuous draw** against your battery's 100 rW output ceiling as you go.

---

## Part 1 — Power budget planning (do the math before you build)

Everything downstream is a draw on one number: your continuous **rW load**. A single [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] outputs a hard cap of **100 rW** no matter how full it is, and stores **24,000 rWm** (= 100 rW for 240 minutes / 4 hours with zero generation). That 100 rW ceiling is the budget the whole base lives inside. Exceed it and the battery drains faster than it charges; stay under it with margin and you have 24/7 uptime.

### Step 1: tally your continuous load

Add up everything that runs *all the time*. Verified per-component draws (see [[Electrical Components]]):

| System | Per-unit draw | Typical solo/trio count | Subtotal |
|--------|--------------|------------------------|----------|
| [[Auto Turret]] | **10 rW** (11 if wiring signal outputs) | 4-9 | 40-90 rW |
| Electric Furnace | **1 rW** | 3-6 | 3-6 rW |
| Industrial Conveyor | **1 rW** | 4-10 | 4-10 rW |
| Industrial Crafter | **1 rW** | 1-2 | 1-2 rW |
| HBHF Sensor | **1 rW** | 1-3 | 1-3 rW |
| Smart Alarm | **1 rW** (dark until tripped) | 1-2 | ~0 idle |
| Smart Switch (master kill) | **1 rW** | 1 | 1 rW |
| Door Controller (bunker) | **1 rW** | 1-2 | 1-2 rW |
| Ceiling Lights | **1-2 rW** | a few (night only) | 0-10 rW |
| Water Pump (farm) | **5 rW** | 1 | 5 rW |
| Sprinkler | **1 rW** | up to 4/pump | 4 rW |

> **Note on the Electric Furnace:** it draws **1 rW** (verified June 2026 against corrosionhour and the Industrial system docs). If you see "3 rW" quoted in older notes including the current [[Industrial]] reference table, treat 1 rW as correct for the live game — the furnace's cost is its 1 rW operating draw, not 3.

**The headline number for a typical defended trio base:** ~6 turrets (60 rW) + furnace line (~6 rW) + sorting (~6 rW) + sensors/doors (~4 rW) ≈ **76 rW continuous**. That fits one Large Battery's 100 rW output with ~24 rW of headroom — exactly the design target.

### Step 2: size your generation to *charge* the battery, not just match the draw

Batteries charge at **80% efficiency** — 20% of incoming power is lost as heat. So to net-store power you need sources producing meaningfully *more* than your load. Rule of thumb: **size generation ~25% above continuous draw.** A 76 rW base wants ~95+ rW of average daytime generation to both run the load and refill the buffer the night drained.

### Step 3: pick a source mix whose failure modes don't overlap

This is the whole trick to 24/7 power. Each source fails differently; combine them so you're never fully dark:

| Source | Output | Fails when | Best for |
|--------|--------|-----------|----------|
| [[Large Solar Panel]] | up to **20 rW** | Night (~9PM-11AM), shadows | Daytime bulk; cheap; ~940-1,075 rWm/day per panel |
| Wind Turbine | **0-150 rW**, avg ~**93 rW** at 6th-floor height | Calm wind, low placement, choked by cliffs | The 24/7 workhorse if placed high in open air |
| Water Wheel (Apr 2026) | up to **30 rW** passive in flowing water (up to 60 rW hand-cranked) | Not near a river/current | River bases; steady, no day/night dependence |
| Small Generator | **40 rW** steady | Out of fuel (~1 LGF/45s, ~80 LGF/hr) | Burst defense windows, raid nights — too costly 24/7 |

**The canonical solo/trio rig:** stack **2-4 Large Solar Panels + 1-2 Wind Turbines** through [[Root Combiner]]s into your Large Battery. Solar covers the day cheaply; the turbine bridges night and cloudy stretches. If you're on a river, a **Water Wheel** is a fantastic third leg — it doesn't care about sun or wind. Keep a **Small Generator** wired through a [[Root Combiner]] as an emergency leg you flip on during a raid or a long dead-wind night.

> **You cannot wire two sources into the same input.** Every time you add a source, it goes through its own [[Root Combiner]] input (2 inputs -> 1 output, no backflow). Chain combiners: `(Solar + Wind) -> Combiner -> (that + Water Wheel) -> Combiner -> Battery`.

### Step 4: battery sizing

One [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] (24,000 rWm) is the standard core. Its 4-hour full-drain at 100 rW comfortably bridges a Rust night (~10 min) many times over — the battery exists to ride out the *day-long* gap when you're offline and sources underperform, not just one night. If your continuous draw exceeds ~90 rW (lots of turrets), run a **second independent battery on its own source/combiner** rather than daisy-chaining. Two batteries on one line do **not** sum their outputs — each is still capped at 100 rW, and you risk backfeed weirdness. Split your base into two power islands instead (e.g. "defense battery" + "industrial battery").

**Placement:** bury the battery, combiners, and wiring hub **deep inside the base**, ideally inside the [[Tool Cupboard|TC]] core or bunker. Exposed batteries on a roof are a soft raid target — pop the battery and the whole base goes dark.

---

## Part 2 — The power backbone (build this first)

This is [[Electrical Circuits]] circuit #1, the trunk everything plugs into.

**Component list (starter trunk):**
- 2-4x [[Large Solar Panel]] (roof, sun-facing)
- 1-2x Wind Turbine (highest open-air point; remember the **15 m no-build radius**)
- 1-3x [[Root Combiner]] (2 HQM each, WB1)
- 1x [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] (50 HQM, WB2)
- 1x **Smart Switch** (1 rW — your single master kill, remotely flippable from Rust+)
- 1-2x **Splitter** (1 HQM each, WB1) and/or **Electrical Branch**es for distribution
- Wire Tool (1 scrap)

**Build order:**
1. Mount solar panels on the roof facing the sun's arc (in the northern map zone, face south) with clear sky line-of-sight. Mount the wind turbine on your highest tower point in open air.
2. Wire each pair of sources into a [[Root Combiner]]; chain combiners until all sources merge into one output line.
3. Combiner output -> **Large Battery** input. The battery now buffers everything.
4. Battery **Power Out** -> **Smart Switch** -> first **Splitter**. The Smart Switch is your whole-base remote kill / arm from the [[Rust+]] app — invaluable when you want to cut turret power before a teammate walks the perimeter, or restore it remotely.
5. From the Splitter, branch dedicated lines to: turret array, industrial gear, sensors/doors, lights. Use **Electrical Branch**es when you want a *fixed* amount to one device and the remainder onward (a Branch set to N draws N+1 total — budget the extra 1 rW).

> **The 1 rW pass-through tax.** Nearly every component costs 1 rW to operate and passes `input - 1` onward. Chain Splitter -> Branch -> Timer -> Door Controller and you've burned ~4 rW before the door moves. The only common free component is the **AND Switch** (0 rW). Always pad your battery sizing for these losses.

---

## Part 3 — Auto-turret array with backup power

Defense before convenience. This is [[Electrical Circuits]] circuit #2 expanded with the backup-power detail. See [[Auto Turrets]] for placement meta and counters.

**Component list (6-turret defended trio base):**
- 6x [[Auto Turret]] (HQM + Gears + CCTV components, WB2) — each loaded with a real gun + 5.56 ammo (a turret is only as good as its weapon; AK/[[M249]] turrets shred, a Nailgun turret is a speed bump)
- Your power backbone from Part 2 (battery + Smart Switch master kill)
- Enough **Splitter**s/**Electrical Branch**es to fan out 6 clean 10 rW lines (each Splitter = 3 outputs; chain them)
- *(backup leg)* 1x **Small Generator** wired through a spare [[Root Combiner]] input
- *(optional)* 1x Timer for scheduled arming

**Build order:**
1. Battery Power Out -> **Smart Switch** (already in your backbone) -> Splitter tree -> each turret's **Power In**. **A turret draws exactly 10 rW** (11 rW if you also wire its Has Target / Low Ammo / No Ammo signal outputs).
2. **Backup power:** wire a **Small Generator** into a [[Root Combiner]] alongside your renewables, feeding the same battery. During a raid (when you want turrets blazing and might be drawing 60+ rW for an extended fight) or a dead-wind night, flip the generator on. It adds 40 rW steady for ~80 LGF/hr — expensive, so it's an emergency leg, not a baseline.
3. **Interference cap:** never pack more than **12 turrets inside a 40 m radius** — the 13th refuses to power and just sparks. Spread a big wall across the radius or stagger heights.
4. **Mount turrets above eye level** on walls/ceilings so raiders must expose themselves to shoot up at them, and tuck them behind half-wall "nests."

**Power budget:** 6 turrets x 10 rW = **60 rW** + 1 rW Smart Switch = **61 rW** continuous. A single Large Battery (100 rW out) comfortably runs **~9 turrets (90 rW)** before hitting its ceiling; beyond that, second battery / power island.

**Signal-output upgrades (advanced):** wire a turret's **Has Target** output (needs 11 rW) into a **Smart Alarm** or a [[Garage Door]] drop, so target acquisition pings your phone or seals a bunker automatically. Wire **Low Ammo (<=50)** / **No Ammo** outputs into a flasher light or Rust+ alert so you know to resupply.

---

## Part 4 — Smart raid alarm + Rust+ notifications

The cheapest, highest-value automation in the game. This is [[Electrical Circuits]] circuit #3. Costs ~1 rW idle and tells your phone the instant a stranger is at your base — the difference between logging in to defend and logging in to a hole in your wall. Pair with the [[Rust+]] companion app.

**Component list:**
- 1-3x **HBHF Sensor** (1 rW each; ~11 m / 3.5-foundation range; outputs 1 rW *per unauthorized person* detected)
- 1x **Smart Alarm** (1 rW; sirens ~42 m + pushes a named notification to the Rust+ app)
- *(multi-room)* **OR Switch**es (0 rW each) to merge sensors
- *(2026 additions)* a **Seismic Sensor** (signals on nearby explosions — raid detection) and/or a **Tin Can Alarm** (can be rigged with up to 9 throwables to fire when tripped — see [[Built Different Update]] era additions)

**Build order:**
1. Battery line (>=2 rW) -> **HBHF Sensor** Power In. In its menu set **Exclude Authorized = ON, Include Others = ON** so it ignores you and TC-authed teammates and only fires on strangers.
2. HBHF **passthrough output** -> **Smart Alarm** Power In. Because the HBHF only outputs power equal to the number of unauthorized players sensed, the alarm stays dark (0 idle draw) until an enemy is actually present.
3. **Name the alarm** in its menu ("Loot Room", "TC Core", "North Wall") so the Rust+ push tells you *which* zone was breached.
4. **Multi-room:** wire several HBHF outputs into a chain of **OR Switch**es -> one Smart Alarm if you just want "someone's here," or keep one alarm per logical zone if you want room-specific alerts.
5. **Raid detection:** add a **Seismic Sensor** so explosive hits ping you even if no one's standing in an HBHF radius — useful for offline-raid awareness.

**Storage Monitors** also report box contents to Rust+ — bolt one on your sulfur/component boxes so you can check stockpiles from your phone and know whether to log in and farm.

---

## Part 5 — Auto-furnace smelting line

The biggest day-to-day QoL win: dump raw ore, walk away, collect ingots. Built on [[Industrial]] electric furnaces — no wood, no manual ignition, **~40% faster than a regular furnace** (verified 2026), and they self-heat from power. The one trade-off: **electric furnaces produce no charcoal**, so keep a wood furnace or two for gunpowder charcoal (or run the Igniter circuit, [[Electrical Circuits]] #7).

**Component list (3 ore types):**
- 1x **ore input box** (Large Box) + Storage Adaptor
- 3x **Electric Furnace** (1 rW each; **1 Storage Adaptor** slot each; 2 ore slots / 3 output slots) — one furnace per ore type so they don't cross-contaminate
- 1x **ingot output box** + Storage Adaptor
- **Industrial Conveyor**s: minimum 1 in + 1 out; cleaner is 1 in + 1 out per furnace
- *(optional)* **Industrial Splitter** to fan one ore stream to multiple furnaces
- **Pipe Tool** + power from your battery line

**Build order:**
1. **Ore box** (Storage Adaptor) -> **Industrial Conveyor** -> each **Electric Furnace** input. Set the in-conveyor **filter** to route each ore to its own furnace: metal ore -> furnace 1, sulfur ore -> furnace 2, HQM ore -> furnace 3. Use an **Industrial Splitter** if fanning one stream.
2. Power each furnace with **1 rW** (no wood, no Igniter — they self-heat).
3. **Furnace output** (Storage Adaptor) -> **Industrial Conveyor** -> **ingot box**. Set the out-conveyor filter to move **only the finished ingot** (Metal Fragments / Sulfur / HQM) so unsmelted ore stays cooking in the furnace.
4. Net result: dump raw ore into the input box, leave, come back to a box of ingots.

**Power budget:** 3 furnaces (3 rW) + ~4 conveyors (4 rW) = **~7 rW** continuous. Trivial against your 100 rW budget — scale to 6 furnaces (one each for metal, sulfur, HQM, plus spares) for ~13 rW total if you process a lot.

**Charcoal workaround:** keep **2-3 regular Small Furnaces** or a Large Furnace on a separate wood supply for charcoal, since electric furnaces make none and you need charcoal for gunpowder (see Part 6 auto-crafting). Or run [[Electrical Circuits]] #7 (Igniter on a Switch/Timer) to remote-light wood furnaces.

---

## Part 6 — Industrial auto-sorting + auto-crafting conveyor setup

Now the loot room runs itself. Dump everything into one box; it sorts into labeled boxes every 5 seconds, and surplus mats feed auto-crafters that produce gunpowder and ammo while you sleep. This is [[Industrial]] Builds 1 and 3, sequenced and tuned.

### 6a — Auto-sorting loot room

**Component list (sorts into 6 boxes):**
- 1x **dump box** (Large Box) — your input, where you mass-dump on return from a run
- 6x destination boxes (stone, metal frags, sulfur, HQM, components, scrap)
- Storage Adaptors: 1 on the dump box output + 1 on each destination box (a Large Box accepts up to 4 adaptors if you need more pipes)
- 6x **Industrial Conveyor** (1 rW each) — *or* fewer conveyors + **Industrial Splitter**s to fan out
- **Pipe Tool** + battery line

**Build order:**
1. Snap a **Storage Adaptor** onto the dump box and each destination box.
2. Place an **Industrial Conveyor** between the dump box and each destination box. (Conveyor-per-item gives the cleanest filtering; splitters save conveyors at the cost of filter granularity.)
3. On each conveyor's **filter**, add the **one item** that box should receive, mode **ANY ITEM**, and set a **MAX** equal to the cap you want (e.g. cap a stone box so overflow routes elsewhere). You can put up to **16 items** in a single filter (verified 2026 — note older notes saying "12" are out of date).
4. Power each conveyor with **1 rW**. Six conveyors = **6 rW**.
5. **Pipe Tool** every link. First transfer is **5 s** after power-on, then every **5 s**; throughput is up to **60 items from 12 stacks per tick** (unstackables move 12 at a time).

**The filter modes that make it smart** (set per-item on each conveyor):
- **MAX** — stop sending an item once the destination holds X (cap a stone box at a stack count so it never overflows).
- **MIN** — only move the *surplus* above a kept minimum (always leave, say, 100 Low Grade Fuel behind in the source).
- **BUFFER** — move in fixed chunks of X.
- Mode **EXCLUDE LISTED** on one final "overflow" conveyor pointing to a junk box catches any unexpected item so it never clogs the dump box.

**Limits to respect:** max **32 Storage Adaptors per side** of a conveyor, and an **industrial max depth of 32 components** in a chain. Far beyond what a solo/trio base needs, but relevant if you build a mega-sorter.

### 6b — Auto-recycling (returning-player favorite)

Pipe your **components box** straight into a **Recycler** via conveyor, and pipe the recycler's output back into your sorter. Components -> recycler -> scrap + raw mats -> sorted automatically. See [[Economy]] for recycler yields. (Recyclers exist at monuments and can be looted/relocated in some cases; confirm current placement rules on your server.)

### 6c — Auto-crafting (gunpowder, then ammo)

Turn raw sulfur + charcoal into a stockpile of gunpowder, then chain a second crafter to turn gunpowder + metal frags into rifle ammo — entirely hands-free.

**Component list (one craft line):**
- 1x **Industrial Crafter** (1 rW; **max 2 per [[Workbench]]**) attached to the correct workbench
- material box + finished-goods box
- 2x **Industrial Conveyor** + Pipe Tool + battery line

**Build order:**
1. Attach the **Industrial Crafter** to the right **Workbench** (gunpowder/ammo = WB Level 1+; up to 2 crafters per bench).
2. **Material box** (sulfur + charcoal for gunpowder) -> **Conveyor** -> Crafter input.
3. Load the **blueprint** (Gunpowder) into the crafter's blueprint slot.
4. **Crafter output** -> **Conveyor** -> finished-goods box.
5. Chain it: feed the gunpowder box + a metal-frags box into a **second crafter** loaded with the rifle/pistol ammo blueprint. Sulfur + charcoal in one end, **5.56 ammo** out the other — which feeds your turrets and your guns.

**Power budget:** each craft line = crafter 1 rW + 2 conveyors 2 rW = **3 rW**. Two lines (gunpowder + ammo) = ~6 rW.

**The full self-sustaining loop:** ore -> auto-furnace (Part 5) -> ingots; sulfur ore -> furnace -> sulfur -> auto-crafter -> gunpowder -> auto-crafter -> ammo -> hand-loaded into turrets. A returning player who builds this loop logs in to *stockpiles*, not chores.

---

## Part 7 — Auto-door bunker (security core)

A hidden [[Garage Door]] honeycomb bunker that only opens when you stand on a secret spot and auto-closes behind you — the standard way to keep your loot core alive against soft-side raids. This is [[Electrical Circuits]] #4. See [[Building Basics]], [[Soft Side]], and [[Doors and Locks]] for the building side.

**Component list:**
- 1x **Pressure Pad** (1 rW; pulses when stood on; detects players *and* vehicles; works through half floors) **or** 1x **HBHF Sensor** (1 rW, Exclude-Authorized for team-only) for a no-visible-trigger version
- 1x **Door Controller** (1 rW) on the bunker [[Garage Door]]
- 1x **Memory Cell** (latches the open state)
- 1x **Timer** (3-5 s; holds the door open long enough to pass)
- power from your battery line

**Build order (timer auto-close):**
1. **Trigger** (Pressure Pad or HBHF) output -> **Memory Cell SET** input. Stepping on/being sensed latches "open."
2. **Memory Cell** output -> **Door Controller** Power In. While latched, the controller (1 rW) holds the [[Garage Door]] open.
3. **Memory Cell** output also -> **Timer**; **Timer** output (after 3-5 s) -> Memory Cell **RESET**. The door auto-closes a few seconds after triggering, even if you've already walked off the pad.
4. Place the trigger on the **inside** of the honeycomb cell so raiders outside can never trip it. With an HBHF version (Exclude Authorized ON), only you/teammates can open it at all.

**Cheaper always-while-pressed version:** skip the Memory Cell + Timer and wire **Pressure Pad -> Door Controller** directly — open only while you stand on the pad, shut the instant you step off. Less convenient (can't pass fast) but minimal parts.

**Power budget:** ~3-4 rW total. Tiny — wire it off any battery branch.

> **Bunker design note:** the [[Spring Clean]]-era **Armoured Ladder Hatch** (April 2026, T3, square + triangle) is now the top-tier vertical bunker access — pair it with the auto-door garage bunker for a hard-to-soft-side core.

---

## Part 8 — Sprinkler farm (passive food/cloth/genetics)

Once defense and industry hum, automate food. An indoor planter garden watered hands-free. This is [[Electrical Circuits]] #9; see [[Water Systems]] for the plumbing and [[Farming]] for crop genetics, ripeness, and yields.

**Component list:**
- 1x **Electric Water Pump** (5 rW; sockets: 1 power + 2 remote on/off) at/below your water source
- water hose from pump up to the grow room (a powered pump is required whenever sprinklers sit *higher* than the source)
- up to **4x Sprinkler** per pump (1 rW each; each draws ~2 mL/s, sprays ~3 mL/s)
- planters below the sprinklers
- *(optional)* **Electrical Heater** (3 rW) to regulate greenhouse crop temperature; **Ceiling Lights** for indoor growth
- *(optional)* 1x **Timer** to pulse the pump rather than run it 24/7
- power from your battery line

**Build + plumbing order:**
1. Place the **Water Pump** at/below your source (ocean, river, or a fed [[Water Catcher]] / Water Barrel). Collection ~8.5 mL/s, output up to 12 mL/s.
2. Power the pump with **5 rW**.
3. Run a **water hose** from the pump up to the grow room into your **Sprinklers** (4 sprinklers x ~2 mL/s = 8 mL/s draw, inside the pump's 12 mL/s output).
4. Power each **Sprinkler** with **1 rW**; they spray the planters below.
5. *(optional)* Insert a **Timer** on the pump's power leg so it runs in bursts (planters only need topping up) — saves power and water.

**Power budget:** pump 5 rW + 4 sprinklers 4 rW = **9 rW**. For a bigger farm, add a *second* pump rather than overloading one (the 12 mL/s output caps sprinklers per pump). A **Water Wheel** on a nearby river can power the whole farm independently of your main battery — handy for a separate greenhouse outbuilding.

---

## Putting it all together: the worked trio base

A concrete target for a populated 2026 vanilla wipe. Continuous draw:

| Module | Draw |
|--------|------|
| 6x Auto Turret + Smart Switch | 61 rW |
| Auto-furnace line (3 furnace + 4 conveyor) | 7 rW |
| Auto-sorter (6 conveyor) | 6 rW |
| Auto-crafter (gunpowder + ammo, 2 lines) | 6 rW |
| Raid alarm (HBHF + sensors) | ~2 rW |
| Bunker auto-door | 3 rW |
| Sprinkler farm | 9 rW (or off the Water Wheel) |
| **Total** | **~85-94 rW** |

That sits right at the edge of one [[Large Rechargeable Battery]]'s 100 rW output. If you run the full farm off main power, **split into two power islands**: a "defense + industry" battery and a "farm + lights" battery, each on its own source/combiner. Generation target: ~3-4 [[Large Solar Panel]]s + 1-2 Wind Turbines (+ a Water Wheel if riverside), with a Small Generator backup leg for raid nights.

**Sequencing on a fresh wipe:**
- **Day 1-2:** backbone (1 battery, 1-2 solar, 1 turbine) + 2-4 turrets + raid alarm. Defense and awareness first.
- **Day 2-3:** auto-furnace line — stop hand-feeding furnaces immediately, it pays for itself in hours.
- **Day 3-5:** auto-sorter + auto-crafter as components/HQM allow. Add the bunker auto-door once you have a real loot core to protect.
- **Day 5+:** sprinkler farm + second power island + extra turrets, scaling the array toward (but never past) the 12-per-40m interference cap.

**Solo vs duo vs trio scaling:**
- **Solo:** prioritize the alarm + bunker auto-door (you can't be everywhere). Keep turrets modest (4-6) and lean on the auto-door core surviving while you're offline. One battery is plenty.
- **Duo:** add the full auto-furnace + sorter early — two people generate more loot to refine, and the time saved compounds.
- **Trio:** run the full 6-9 turret array, two power islands, and the complete craft loop. With three TC-auths you can afford bigger renewable arrays and a generator backup for raid defense.

---

## Common automation mistakes (returning-player gotchas)

- **Forgetting the 1 rW pass-through tax** — a 10-component chain quietly eats ~10 rW. Test in [[rustrician.io]] and read the live Active Usage on the battery.
- **Exposing the battery/turbine** — roof-mounted batteries die first in a raid and black out the whole base. Bury power deep; only the solar panels and turbine *have* to be outside.
- **Daisy-chaining two batteries expecting summed output** — they don't sum; build power islands.
- **Wiring two sources into one input** — always use a [[Root Combiner]].
- **Electric furnaces for charcoal** — they make none; keep wood furnaces for gunpowder charcoal.
- **Overloading a water pump** — past ~4 sprinklers (12 mL/s output) flow starves; add a second pump.
- **Pipes through walls** — the **Pipe Tool** can't cross building blocks (only deployables like doors); the **Wire Tool** passes through anything. Plan industrial layouts in one contiguous room.
- **Not authorizing turrets** — set every turret to authorize you and all teammates, or your own array shreds you.
- **Filter cap confusion** — a conveyor filter holds **16** items (current), not 12; you have room to consolidate sorting conveyors.

---

## Related

- [[Electricity Basics]] · [[Electrical Components]] · [[Electrical Circuits]] · [[Industrial]] — the four reference pages this guide sequences
- [[Auto Turrets]] · [[Traps]] · [[Water Systems]] — defense and farming subsystems
- [[Large Rechargeable Battery]] · [[Root Combiner]] · [[Large Solar Panel]] · [[Door Controller]] · [[HBHF Sensor]] · [[Garage Door]] — key components
- [[rustrician.io]] — free circuit simulator; build before you buy
- [[Rust+]] — phone notifications for the alarm + Smart Switch master kill + Storage Monitors
- [[Building Basics]] · [[Soft Side]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] — the base the automation lives in
- [[Farming]] · [[Economy]] — what the sprinkler farm and auto-recycler feed into
- [[Built Different Update]] · [[Spring Clean]] · [[Rust Updates 2026]] — current-patch context (Water Wheel, Armoured Ladder Hatch, Seismic Sensor, Tin Can Alarm)

pages.title: Group Base & Compound
pages.body:
# Group Base & Compound

The "how to actually run a quad+ base" layer. [[Group Bases]] catalogs the named clan designs and their published upkeep/raid numbers; [[Expansion and Compound Design]] covers the mechanics of perimeters, shooting floors, and turret arcs. **This page is the playbook that sits on top of both** — sequencing, who-does-what, where the loot lives, how you stage a raid out of the base, and how you actually defend a big footprint when 6–8 people are online and 2 are awake. Numbers verified June 13 2026; the live patch is the **"Built Different" update (Jun 4 2026)** — a player-model/armor/M16A2 drop that **changed no building HP, raid math, or turret rules**, so everything here is current.

> [!warning] Read this honestly
> A clan fortress is an **economy, not a build.** The Osmium-tier reference base in [[Group Bases]] costs **3–4 dedicated farmers per day** just to not decay, and ~**900 rockets / 1.26M sulfur** to raid. If your group can't reliably staff the farm, you don't have a group base — you have a decaying liability that telegraphs "loot here" to the whole server. The honest call for a 4–6 man that isn't online all day is a **fat [[Trio Bases|trio-class]] core + a small compound**, not a fortress. Build to your farm output, not your ambition.

---

## The one rule that governs everything: upkeep is your budget

Every decision below — footprint, honeycomb depth, number of TCs, compound size, turret count — spends from one finite pool: **[[Upkeep]] you can actually farm.** Group bases die far more often to **decay during a dead week** than to boom. The math from real published designs ([[Group Bases]]):

| Tier | ~Upkeep/day | Farmers it implies | Raid cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fat trio core + small compound | ~6–10k stone / 8–15k frags / ~150 HQM | 1–2 part-time | ~30–60 rockets |
| Mid clan (the Prophecy class) | ~20k stone / 15k frags / 160 HQM | 2–3 active | hundreds of rockets |
| Large clan (the Osmium class) | ~32k stone / 101k frags / 340 HQM | **3–4 full-time** | **900+ rockets / ~1.26M sulfur** |

Frag upkeep is the killer at scale — a sheet-metal honeycomb shell (1,000 HP/wall, [[Raid Costs|7 rockets each]]) is the strongest defense per wall but taxes **frags daily, forever.** Reserve sheet for the layers that matter (TC cells, the loot core) and run cheap **stone honeycomb** on the outer shell where the goal is just "more walls to break," not "unbreachable."

**Practical gate before you expand:** can your daily farm refill the TCs *and* leave a surplus for boom and rebuilds? If not, you're over-built. See [[Expansion and Compound Design]] for the over-extension death spiral (running two TCs / two bases is the classic clan starve-out).

---

## Multi-TC honeycomb: why clan bases are different

A solo base has one [[Tool Cupboard]] and dies the moment a raider seals it. A group base **cannot** work that way, because the TC at **100 HP / 8 explo 5.56 (200 sulfur)** ([[Raid Costs]]) is the cheapest thing in the entire base to kill. The whole point of clan construction is that **no single TC pop hands the base over.**

- **3–4 TC zones, each in its own armored/honeycombed cell.** The published Waterloo and Retaliator designs run 4 TCs ([[Group Bases]]). If raiders seal one wing's cupboard, the other wings keep building privilege — you can still re-wall the breach, repair, and place fresh externals.
- **Spread the privilege bubbles** so the TCs overlap your whole footprint but live in *separate* breach corridors. A raider who cracks the loot wing should still be standing inside another wing's build-block.
- **Each TC cell is its own raid.** Wall it off, honeycomb it, hide it deep — never against an outer wall, never in the first room a breach opens into ([[Raid Defense]]).
- **Authorize discipline:** only core/officer accounts on all TCs; rotating members on a single "build" TC. A leaver or a compromised account that's authed on every cupboard can grief the whole base from the inside. This is a [[Team System|team-management]] problem as much as a building one.

The failure mode this prevents is the **online TC rush** — the way clan bases actually die. Raiders don't out-boom an Osmium shell; they wait for a thin online crew, rush a gatehouse or a weak wing, seal a TC, and peel the base from inside. Multi-TC + a defended core buys the time for your offline farmers to log in.

---

## Distributed, role-based storage (where the loot lives)

The other thing that breaks at clan scale: **one big loot room is a single point of failure and a splash gift.** Rocket splash damages multiple adjacent walls at once — the Tycho design's whole pitch is **"splash-separated bunkers"** ([[Group Bases]]), cells spaced so one rocket can't open two.

Run loot as **per-player / per-role cells, splash-separated:**

- **Personal loot cells** — one small honeycombed box-room per member, each its own little raid. An offliner who cracks one gets one player's kit, not the clan bank. Spread them so no two share a wall that splash can double-hit.
- **Role/bank cells** behind the deepest honeycomb: the **boom bank** (rockets, C4, gunpowder), the **build bank** (stone/frags/HQM for upkeep + rebuilds), and the **meds/food** store. These are the raid targets worth the most — bury them deepest, in [[Bunkers|bunker]] cells if you can, so they cost an extra raid (hatch + walls) to reach ([[Raid Defense]]).
- **Decoys.** A clan base has the footprint to afford a fake loot room near a likely breach — empty or low-value boxes that eat boom and waste an offliner's time while your real banks sit untouched.
- **Auth on storage, not just doors.** Lockers and boxes can be locked/authed; the build/boom banks should be officer-auth only. This is your anti-leaver insurance — losing a member shouldn't mean losing the bank.

**Hopper collection (Mar 2025 QoL):** defense literally pays you. Dead raiders drop [[Backpacks]]; hoppers under the shooting floor and in the kill zone auto-collect their boom and kit during a fight. A defended online raid can net you the attacker's entire rocket stack — fund your defense with their offense.

---

## Compound walls & externals (the perimeter)

A compound is the outer ring of [[High External Stone Wall|high external walls]] that forces a breach before anyone touches the base and **stops grubbing** — raiders building twig/honeycomb against your wall to stage [[Satchel Charge|satchels]] or a [[Siege Tower]]. The gap between wall and core is your **kill zone.** Full mechanics in [[Expansion and Compound Design]]; the group-specific calls:

- **High External Stone Wall: 500 HP, 4 rockets to break, ~4 m tall, now craftable** (no longer kit-only). Same HP as a stone wall but you rarely raid them — you ladder over, shoot through, or gate-camp ([[Raid Costs]]).
- **One gate, airlocked, always.** Every extra gate is another breach point and another grub spot. Put an [[Airlock]] *behind* the [[High External Stone Wall|external gate]] — never trust the gate alone.
- **Double-wall the perimeter** at high-value bases so a single rocket line (4 rockets) doesn't open the ring — but only if upkeep allows. A second external ring is real daily tax.
- **External [[Tool Cupboard|TCs]] in the compound footprint are the main reason to run a compound at all.** They deny build privilege in your kill zone, so raiders can't ladder, tower, or honeycomb up to you. Place several in gatehouses and corner cells, each honeycombed into a small armored box so they can't be cheaply popped. (Note these against the upkeep budget above — external TCs are part of why clan upkeep balloons.)
- **Turret pods** — a recessed external box with an [[Auto Turret]] behind a wide gap, hidden in the compound wall — instakill grubbers and laddermen. A current-meta external defense.

> [!warning] The mortar problem killed "stack high walls and hide" (Apr 30 2026)
> [[Mortar]]s (HE + fragmentation) unlock at [[Workbench Level 2]] and **lob shells over a compound wall from outside your TC bubble.** Tall walls no longer hide you — they create a **predictable arc** a mortar crew drops shells into, and they raise your profile on the map. Modern clan compounds are **lower-profile, roofed over every internal walkway, with furnaces/farm stations pulled indoors.** Don't build a tall flat compound full of exposed furnaces and bags in 2026 — you're building a mortar target. Some large clans now *drop* sections of perimeter wall specifically to deny a mortar a clean repeatable arc.

---

## Shooting floors: the heart of group defense

The shooting floor is what makes a group base a **fortress instead of a big box.** It's an elevated platform from which defenders fire **down** into the kill zone and core through floor gaps, with [[Auto Turret]]s below. A raider who spends 20+ rockets into your core and then steps onto open ground under a manned shooting floor has bought the worst fight in the game ([[Expansion and Compound Design]]).

- **Wide gaps:** misaligned floor/wall slots you can shoot through but raiders can't jump through.
- **Peek-downs, inner and outer.** Outer peek-downs cover the compound/kill zone; inner peek-downs cover the core breach. Good clan designs run both — you want eyes on the wall they're booming *and* the room they breach into.
- **Roof floor** above for vertical coverage and anti-siege.
- **Man it by role** (see Roles below) — the shooting floor only works with bodies on it. An empty shooting floor is just more wall to upkeep.

This is the defensive payoff of all that footprint: the compound funnels raiders into open ground, the shooting floor and turrets own that ground, and your honeycomb buys the time for everyone to get on the floor.

---

## Auto turret coverage: arcs, not walls of turrets

Plan turrets **before** you build, because the interference cap makes raw count useless.

- [[Auto Turret]]: **1,000 HP**, costs 10 HQM + targeting computer + CCTV camera, draws **10 power** each, dies to **3 rockets / 106 explo** offline ([[Raid Costs]]). Every one needs an [[Electricity|electrical]] feed.
- **Interference cap: max 12 active turrets within a 40 m radius** (vanilla `sentry.maxinterference` = 12, `sentry.interferenceradius` = 40 m, live since the Oct 5 2023 update). Over the cap, extra turrets glow blue and acquire nothing. **Turret-wall spam is dead** — overlap **arcs**, not bodies.
- **A 3×3 room is too big for one turret.** Budget 2–3 with overlapping arcs per zone, on a single inside toggle so you can power them down to reload/repair without running outside.
- **Switched banks** wired to [[Seismic Sensor]]s / detectors: large bases keep most turrets *off* (under the 12-cap) until a raid trips the sensor, then power on the bank covering that side. This is how a clan base covers a footprint that would otherwise blow the interference cap — you never need 12 *on* at once, just 12 on *where the raid is.*
- A compromised electrical feed kills your turrets; protect the **electricity room** (root combiner / batteries) like a TC cell — it's a soft, high-value disable target.

---

## Roles: a clan base only works if it's staffed

Footprint without bodies is a liability. Assign standing roles ([[Team System]] for the mechanics of teams, auth, and pings):

- **Farmers (2–4, the most important role).** They feed the upkeep budget that makes everything else legal. No farmers = decay = free raid. Rotate so the TCs never run dry.
- **Builder / base lead.** One person owns the build plan, the auth list, and the upkeep watch. Distributed authority on storage and TCs is good; distributed *responsibility* for the build is how bases get half-honeycombed and inconsistent. One lead, one plan.
- **PvP / roam crew.** Hold monuments, run [[Card Run Routes|card runs]], counter-raid, and control the area around the base. They're also your shooting-floor defenders when a raid hits.
- **Boom / raid crew.** Manage the boom bank, plan offensive raids, and run the FOB (below).
- **Auth discipline is a security control.** Core on all TCs; rotating members on a single build TC; officer-only on the boom and build banks. A leaver or a hijacked account authed everywhere can end the base from inside — this is the one threat a fortress wall does nothing against.

Two-awake reality: design the base so **two people can defend it** — concentrated shooting-floor coverage over the most likely breach, switched turrets, and honeycomb depth that buys time for the offline crew to wake up. A base that only survives with 8 online is a base that gets offlined.

---

## FOB / raid-base staging (going on offense)

A group's loot grows fastest by **raiding**, and the staging discipline is the same one third-parties use against *you* ([[Counter-Raiding]]).

- **FOB = forward operating base:** a cheap, fast, disposable base (twig/wood, a TC, sleeping bags, a few boxes) built within **sprint range** of your target. Purpose: respawn point, boom/armor/med resupply, and a defensive position vs third-parties.
- **Keep the boom in the FOB, not your pockets, until you're breaching.** A wiped raid crew shouldn't lose the whole rocket stack to one bad peek.
- **Defend the FOB** — a couple of [[Shotgun Trap]]s or a turret on the door stops a third party rolling your respawns while you're committed to the wall. The most committed raider is the most vulnerable; assume someone is watching your raid.
- **Air staging:** the FOB can be a repad/refuel point, but the **Nov 2025 heli nerf** (no in-flight repair) means a ground FOB can't keep a damaged [[Attack Helicopter]] flying — plan air raids to win fast or not at all.
- **Picking targets:** door-path is always cheaper than wall-path — a [[Sheet Metal Door]] (1 C4 / 2,200) beats a sheet wall (4 C4 / 8,800) every time ([[Raid Costs]]). Scout the cheapest line to loot before you commit boom; raid the lowest-tier obstacle on the path.

Inverted, this is also your **counter-raid radar:** when *you* spot a group's FOB near a base they're cracking, that FOB is softer than the base and holds both crews' loot. A clean third-party can net a whole raid's worth of explosives for one good fight ([[Counter-Raiding]]).

---

## Defending a big footprint (putting it together)

When the raid actually comes:
