1. **Sensors first.** [[Seismic Sensor]]s wired to lights/alarms (and the switched turret banks) tell you which side is hit the instant boom lands — power on the turret bank covering that wall, get bodies to that peek-down.
2. **Hold the breach, don't run the front.** Let them open a wall and funnel into the kill zone; you have the shooting floor, the angles, and the cover — they're exposed in the hole they made ([[Counter-Raiding]]).
3. **Re-wall behind the breach** to reset the funnel and make them pay again — this only works because multi-TC keeps your build privilege alive even if one cupboard is sealed.
4. **Relocate the bank** if a wing is genuinely falling — move boom/build stock to a deeper cell or out a back exit while they're still breaking shell. Splash-separated cells buy you the time.
5. **Pincer.** A defended group base turns a raid into a gunfight on *your* ground — hoppers collect the dead raiders' [[Backpacks]], and a won defense often refunds more boom than the raid cost you.
6. **Offline insurance is depth, not presence.** When nobody's awake, the only thing fighting for you is honeycomb depth + bunker cells + hidden/decoy loot. Make the cheapest line to your real bank still cost an offliner more boom than one dead week is worth ([[Raid Defense]]).

---

## Expansion order for a group (practical sequence)

Build in this order — each step earns the next ([[Expansion and Compound Design]]):

1. **Main core, honeycombed first.** Stone outer honeycomb, sheet-metal mid layers, armored only on TC/bank cells.
2. **Multi-TC + splash-separated loot cells** before any footprint. The internal economy beats raw size.
3. **Shooting floor + inner/outer peek-downs** once you have bodies to man it.
4. **External TCs** in the future compound footprint, to lock build privilege early (and budget their upkeep).
5. **High external wall ring, one airlocked gate** — last, because it's the highest upkeep and the biggest [[Mortar]] liability. Keep it low-profile and roof the internal walkways.
6. **Turrets** wired in with overlapping arcs and switched banks, under the 40 m / 12-turret cap.

> Don't run two full bases. When your starter has done its job, convert it to an external/furnace shack inside the compound or let it decay — paying [[Upkeep]] on two TCs is the over-extension that starves a clan's main into decay during the first quiet week.

---

## Related

[[Group Bases]] · [[Expansion and Compound Design]] · [[Team System]] · [[Raid Defense]] · [[Counter-Raiding]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Open Core vs Closed Core]] · [[Auto Turret]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Seismic Sensor]] · [[High External Stone Wall]] · [[Mortar]] · [[Upkeep]] · [[Forward Operating Base]]

## Sources
RustHelp / RustLabs-successor (wall/door/TC/turret HP, rocket & C4 counts, raw-sulfur anchors); wiki.facepunch + uMod/HostEZ (`sentry.maxinterference` 12 / `interferenceradius` 40 m, Oct 5 2023); rust.facepunch.com/news "Built Different" (Jun 4 2026 — confirmed no building/raid math change); published clan-design upkeep/raid numbers via [[Group Bases]] (Dust, Meano, Evil Wurst); compound/shooting-floor/mortar meta via [[Expansion and Compound Design]]; FOB/counter-raid doctrine via [[Counter-Raiding]].

pages.title: Monument Roam Routes
pages.body:
# Monument Roam Routes

The "how to actually loot the map" layer for a returning solo/duo/trio on a populated 2026 vanilla server. Where [[Card Run Routes]] tells you how to climb the green→blue→red **keycard** ladder, this page is about the broader question: **given my gear and my goal right now, which monuments do I hit, in what order, and when?**

The core idea since the 2025-2026 monument reshuffle and the [[Puzzle System|fragment economy]] is that monuments are no longer interchangeable barrel farms. Each one has a *purpose* — scrap, components, guns, fragments, or pure tech — and the right loop depends entirely on which of those you're short on. Don't roam at random; roam with a shopping list.

> Numbers here are pulled from the reference pages; follow the [[wikilinks]] for full tables. Always sanity-check stats in game after the first-Thursday patch — see [[Rust Updates 2026]] and [[Wipe Schedule]].

---

## Step 0 — Pick your goal before you leave base

Decide which of these you need *most*, then jump to that loop. Trying to do all of them in one trip gets you killed carrying loot you don't want.

| Goal | What you actually need | Go to |
|---|---|---|
| **Bootstrap a fresh wipe** | scrap + low-risk components | [[#Loop A — The scrap-and-components milk run (no cards, no gun)]] |
| **Fund the workbench** | Basic/Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] | [[Card Run Routes]] (the ladder) + [[#Loop B — The component grind]] |
| **Get your first real guns** | elite/military crates | [[#Loop C — The gun run]] |
| **Get rich fast (geared)** | high-density elite + scrap | [[#Loop D — The high-roller circuit]] |
| **Cap a session with an event** | Heli / Cargo / Bradley | [[#Event timing — Cargo, Heli, Bradley]] |

The other axis is **risk tolerance vs. server heat.** On a populated 2026 server every keycard hack and every event puts a **global map marker** up. Loud monuments (Launch, Oil Rig, Cargo) are *contested PvP arenas first and loot piñatas second.* The quiet milk-run monuments are where solos actually make their living.

---

## The risk/reward map (memorize this)

Roughly sorted low-risk → high-reward. The whole skill of roaming is climbing this ladder only as fast as your gear allows.

| Risk | Monuments | What they give | Gear gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **None** (no NPCs, no/low rad) | [[Lighthouse]], [[Oxum's Gas Station]], [[Abandoned Supermarket]], [[Mining Outpost]], [[Junkyard]], [[Abandoned Cabins]] | scrap, low-tier components, free green cards | rock + clothes |
| **Low** (light rad, no NPCs) | [[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], [[The Dome]], [[Radtown]], [[Water Treatment Plant]] | scrap, components, blue puzzle (→ red card) | basic radsuit / hazmat |
| **Medium** (rad + few scientists) | [[Train Yard]], [[Power Plant]], [[Airfield]], [[Arctic Research Base]], [[Harbor]] | components, fragments, red cards | hazmat + a real gun |
| **High** (rad + many scientists) | [[Military Tunnels]], [[Launch Site]], [[Missile Silo]], [[Giant Excavator Pit]] | elite crates, Advanced fragments, scrap | hazmat + rifle + meds + numbers |
| **Apex** (NPC walls + PvP magnets) | [[Large Oil Rig]], [[Small Oil Rig]], [[Cargo Ship]], [[Patrol Helicopter]], [[Bradley APC]] | best non-craftable loot in the game | full kit + a team or nerves of steel |

---

## Loop A — The scrap-and-components milk run (no cards, no gun)

**Goal:** the wipe-day and rebuild-after-death economy. Scrap for the [[Tech Tree]] and [[Bandit Camp]], components ([[Components|gears/springs/pipes/sheet metal]]) for tools and early guns. Zero cards, zero combat, minimal rad.

**Kit:** clothes, a [[Rock]]/hatchet, a [[Salvaged Hammer]] is optional, a horse or [[Roadside Junk Piles|road]] to travel. No hazmat needed.

**The route (chain whatever is nearest):**

1. **Roadside tier-0s** — [[Oxum's Gas Station]], [[Abandoned Supermarket]], [[Mining Outpost]]. Each has a [[Recycler]] (monument recyclers = **5 s cycle, 120% yield**, strictly better than safe-zone recyclers). Smash barrels → recycle metal/components → bank scrap. A free [[Green Keycard]] usually spawns on a desk at the supermarket/gas station (feeds [[Card Run Routes]]).
2. **[[Junkyard]]** — barrels + a magnet crane + the **car shredder** (shred a [[Modular Car|car]] for a big scrap/component dump). Heli crashes here and shredding heli gibs is **200-500 scrap per heli**. Has a recycler on site.
3. **[[Satellite Dish]] / [[Sewer Branch]]** — light rad, no NPCs. Sewer Branch is the **best low-tier loot room on the map** (~9 crates) and has a recycler. Bring a basic radsuit. Satellite Dish doubles as a one-switch [[Green Keycard|green puzzle]] if you have a green card.
4. **Bank, recycle, repeat.** This loop is endlessly repeatable, never flags the map, and is the backbone of a [[Solo Survival Guide|solo's]] economy. Two laps usually buys a [[Workbench|T1 bench]] + first tools.

**Why this loop matters in 2026:** with the [[Blueprint Fragments|fragment overhaul]], the tech-tree scrap tax got steeper, so a clean scrap loop early is more valuable than ever. Don't skip it to rush a puzzle you can't yet defend.

---

## Loop B — The component grind (mid-game, light combat)

**Goal:** [[Components]] (high-quality metal, gears, springs, tech trash, rifle bodies, metal blades) for crafting guns, [[Armored Door|doors]], and tools once your blueprints are unlocking. Also feeds Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]] for the T2/T3 [[Workbench]].

**Kit:** hazmat or a solid radsuit (most of these cap at rad 26-52), a [[Semi-Automatic Rifle|SAR]] or better, meds, 1-2 [[Electric Fuse|fuses]], a blue card if you want the puzzle loot.

**The route:**

1. **[[Power Plant]]** — no scientists, rad up to 52, a green+blue [[Puzzle System|puzzle]] and **3 monument recyclers**. This is the premier component-and-recycle monument: huge barrel/crate density, on-site recyclers so you convert in place, and 3 Basic Fragments from the puzzle. Quiet because it has no NPC wall.
2. **[[Water Treatment Plant]]** — rad 26, **zero scientists**, only needs a blue card + fuse, and prints a **[[Red Keycard]] + 2 Basic Fragments + ~6 crates**. The safest fragment/component source in the game (see [[Card Run Routes]]). Recycler on site.
3. **[[Train Yard]]** — rad to 26, only 4 scientists, blue puzzle → red card + 2 frags + ~9 half-military crates. Strong component density and a recycler.
4. **[[Train Tunnels]]** between monuments — the underground rail network connects many of these; the [[Train Tunnels|tunnel dwellers]] drop components and you can travel monument-to-monument underground, dodging surface PvP. A genuinely under-used solo highway in 2026.

**Sequencing tip:** do the **no-NPC monuments first while ungeared** (Power Plant, WTP), bank, *then* gear up for the scientist monuments. Dying at Train Yard with a full Power Plant haul is the classic mistake.

---

## Loop C — The gun run (you have a red card + a real weapon)

**Goal:** [[Elite Crate]]s and military crates — i.e. **guns, attire, and the components to craft more guns.** This is how you go from one SAR to a kitted [[Assault Rifle]] team.

**Kit:** full hazmat (Military Tunnels rad is mild but Launch is 52), a rifle minimum, **150+ rounds**, multiple medkits/syringes, the cards the monument needs, 1-2 fuses.

**Pick by what your map has and how hot the server is:**

- **[[Military Tunnels]]** — *the best guns-per-run land monument.* **6 elite crates** (the most of any land monument), 2 Advanced Fragments, full Green+Blue+Red ladder + 1 fuse. 33 scientists exist but the puzzle path only forces ~11 fights — leapfrog them as a duo/trio. Rad is only median 11 / max 26, so hazmat is plenty. **This is the trio's bread-and-butter loot run.**
- **[[Launch Site]]** — green+red + 2 fuses, no scientist wall but rad 52, rocket-area parkour, and **[[Bradley APC]] patrolling the runway.** 3 elites + 2 Advanced Fragments. Loud and contested; bring someone to watch for the APC and for third parties.
- **[[Missile Silo]]** — red card only, but **27 scientists and rad 81** make it effectively a raid. Highest red-room density post-Oct-2025 (4 elites + 2 Advanced Fragments + ~20 crates). **Trio-and-up only**; treat it like clearing a base, not a loot stop.
- **[[Giant Excavator Pit]]** — no cards, but 18 scientists guard it; run the excavator for a guaranteed **HQM/sulfur/scrap dump** (great for [[Raiding|raid]] prep) rather than guns.

**The cardinal rule of the gun run:** start the loudest hack/puzzle, then *defend the loot, don't chase it.* The map marker brings company. If you can't hold the room, grab the elites and exfil — a finished gun run you survived beats a full clear you died on.

---

## Loop D — The high-roller circuit (geared team, accept PvP)

**Goal:** the absolute top of the loot table — [[Locked Crate]]s, heavy-scientist guns, the best attire. This is end-of-session, full-kit, expect-to-fight content.

- **[[Small Oil Rig]]** — boat + blue + red. 15 scientists (incl. 6 [[Heavy Scientist|heavies]]), a locked crate + elites. The hack flags the whole server; the rig **floods with radiation ~30 min after the hack starts**, and every boat-rat shows up. Duo-viable but loud. Puzzle resets on ~65 min, not 30.
- **[[Large Oil Rig]]** — the apex PvE-into-PvP monument: 27 scientists + 12 heavies, multiple locked crates, no recyclers. **Trio-minimum**, and even then you're racing other teams. Get a boat there, clear methodically, hold the helipad.
- **[[Cargo Ship]]** — see event timing below. No explosives needed, just boarding + the firepower for ~12 scientists; **3 [[Locked Crate]]s** (15-min hacks each) plus crates that **refill every 10 min up to 3 times.** Post-rework it **docks at a [[Harbor]]**, so you can board from land via a crane container — huge for boatless solos.

**On a populated server, treat Loop D monuments as PvP venues.** The loot is real but the people contesting it are the actual content. Don't bring loot you can't afford to lose, and have an exfil plan (lifeboat at Cargo's stern, boat at the rigs).

---

## Radiation & gear gates per monument

Quick reference so you don't walk into rad 81 in a snow jacket. Verify per patch.

| Rad tier | Monuments | Protection needed |
|---|---|---|
| **None** | tier-0 roadsides, [[Junkyard]], [[Harbor]], [[Ferry Terminal]], [[Lighthouse]] | clothes |
| **Low (≤11)** | [[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], [[Arctic Research Base]], [[Airfield]] | basic radsuit / partial hazmat |
| **Medium (~26)** | [[Water Treatment Plant]], [[Train Yard]], [[Military Tunnels]] | hazmat suit |
| **High (~52)** | [[Power Plant]], [[Launch Site]], [[Underwater Labs]] | full hazmat |
| **Extreme (~81)** | [[Missile Silo]] | full hazmat + rad-removing meds; minimize dwell time |

A full **[[Hazmat Suit]]** covers everything up to ~52 comfortably and trivializes the medium tier. For Missile Silo, carry anti-rad and keep moving — don't AFK in a loot room while the [[Puzzle System|reset purge]] floods it. (Most puzzles purge rad in the last ~10 min of their ~30-min cycle.)

---

## Event timing — Cargo, Heli, Bradley

Events are the highest loot-per-minute plays on the map, but they're **scheduled global markers** — everyone sees them. Time your roam around them.

### [[Patrol Helicopter]] — the best solo/duo event
- Spawns every **~2-4 hours** (server default). Drops **4 crates = 1 elite Heli Crate + 3 Heli Weapon Crates** — no explosives needed.
- **Kill the rotors, not the body:** top rotor 900 HP + tail rotor 500 HP = ~1,400 effective vs. 10,000 for the hull. Tail first (it flies erratically after), then top. Bring **300+ rifle rounds.**
- It won't aggro a near-naked player, so you can **pre-position un-geared, then swap to gear and rifle** when it commits. As of 2026 it tries to **crash at a nearby monument** on death (not at safe zones), so fight it near where you want the wreck.
- Break line of sight to deaggro (~30 s). Peek-shoot-hide off a hard structure; don't stand in the napalm.

### [[Cargo Ship]] — the no-boom payday
- Spawns every **~2-4 in-game days** (a few real hours). ~12 scientists, **3 [[Locked Crate]]s** (15-min hacks), crates **refill every 10 min ×3.**
- Post-rework it **docks at a [[Harbor]]** — board from land by hiding in a crane container. Boatless solos finally have a reliable boarding route.
- **Radiation-respawn trick:** when the departure siren sounds and rad floods the deck, surviving **~2 minutes into the radiation** respawns all 3 locked crates and stops the rad — a free second loot cycle if you can tank it. Lifeboat is at the stern for exfil.
- Start all three hacks early so they finish together; the map marker means you'll likely be contested.

### [[Bradley APC]] — explosives required
- Patrols [[Launch Site]] (and the [[Giant Excavator Pit]] runs). **Needs explosives** ([[C4|timed charges]] / rockets / [[HV Rocket]]s to the tracks/weak points) — this is the one event you can't rifle down.
- Drops elite-tier crates. Worth folding into a **Launch Site gun run** only if you brought the boom and a teammate to spot. Otherwise skip it and take the elites without poking the tank.

---

## Putting it together — sample sessions

**Solo, 90 min, mid-wipe (T2 done, want guns):**
[[Water Treatment Plant]] (blue card from [[Bandit Camp]], 40 scrap → red card + frags + components, no NPCs) → bank → gear up → quiet-hours [[Military Tunnels]] crawl (silenced rifle, leapfrog scientists) for elites → exfil before anyone reads the map marker. Pad with a [[Satellite Dish]]/[[Sewer Branch]] scrap top-up if a [[Patrol Helicopter]] hasn't spawned.

**Duo, 2 hr, "fund the team":**
Split [[#Loop A — The scrap-and-components milk run (no cards, no gun)|Loop A]] roadsides for scrap + green cards (both players, parallel) → converge on [[Power Plant]] (no NPCs, 3 recyclers, components + frags) → [[Train Yard]] blue puzzle for a red card → cap with [[Military Tunnels]] if you both have rifles, or chase a [[Patrol Helicopter]] if one spawns. Bank between every leg — cards and loot drop on death.

**Trio, full kit, "get rich":**
[[Military Tunnels]] full clear (6 elites) → [[Missile Silo]] as a coordinated push (treat as a raid) → end on [[Cargo Ship]] or [[Large Oil Rig]] if one is up. This is a PvP-acceptance session — expect to fight other teams for the apex monuments and don't carry irreplaceable kit you can't re-craft.

---

## Roaming rules of thumb

- **Roam with a shopping list, not a vibe.** Know which goal (scrap / components / guns / fragments / scrap) you're filling before you leave the [[Tool Cupboard|TC]].
- **Climb the risk ladder only as fast as your gear allows.** A dead body at Launch funds the enemy team; a clean Power Plant loop funds you.
- **Bank between legs.** Everything drops on death, including [[Backpacks|backpack]] contents and keycards. Never carry two monuments' worth of loot.
- **Prefer monument recyclers** (5 s / 120%) over safe-zone ones (8 s / 80%) when you can hold the spot — see [[Recycler]].
- **Loud monuments are PvP venues.** Every hack/puzzle/event is a global marker. Solos live on the quiet loops; teams fight for the apex ones.
- **Use the [[Train Tunnels]] as a stealth highway** to move between monuments without exposing yourself on the surface.
- **Time events into your roam** — a [[Patrol Helicopter]] mid-loop or a [[Cargo Ship]] docking at [[Harbor]] is worth detouring for; a [[Bradley APC]] is only worth it if you brought explosives.
- **Read the doors** — an already-open puzzle door means someone looted it; check the next monument instead of wasting a fuse ([[Puzzle System]]).

---

## See also
- [[Card Run Routes]] — the keycard ladder (green→blue→red) this guide sits on top of
- [[Puzzle System]] — fuses, reset timers, the fragment economy
- [[Rust Monuments]] — the master tier table with all radiation/scientist/recycler stats
- [[Solo Survival Guide]] / [[First Day Guide]] — what to do before you can roam
- [[Recycler]] — yield math for converting your haul
- [[Raid Costs]] / [[Raiding]] — where your scrap and HQM eventually go

pages.title: Progression Speedrun
pages.body:
# Progression Speedrun

The **fastest naked-to-AK route** on a populated 2026 vanilla server, written for a returning **solo / duo / trio** player. This is the "how to actually play wipe day" layer that sits on top of [[Progression Route]] (the what) and the reference tables ([[Tech Tree]], [[Workbenches]], [[Recycling]], [[Raid Costs]]). Where [[Progression Route]] lists the phases, this page is about **sequencing and decision-making**: what to do *right now*, what to skip, and where returners waste hours.

> [!important] Read this first — the three gates that actually matter in 2026
> 1. **Scrap is no longer the wall.** Research is dirt cheap now (**15 / 30 / 60 / 120** by rarity — see [[Tech Tree]]). You will never be "scrap-starved" the way you were in 2023.
> 2. **[[Blueprint Fragments]] gate your benches.** A [[Workbench Level 2]] needs **5 Basic Fragments**, a [[Workbench Level 3]] needs **5 Advanced Fragments**. No amount of scrap builds a bench. Fragments come from **monument puzzle runs**, period.
> 3. **The whole game wipes monthly** (first Thursday, 19:00 UTC — see [[Wipe Schedule]]). This route is a *repeatable speedrun*, not a one-time grind. The goal is to compress it tighter every wipe.

The headline: **a returning player's instinct is to hoard scrap and grind metal at base. That is the slow path now.** The fast path is to *leave base early and run monuments*, because monuments are simultaneously your scrap source, your fragment source, and your component source. Every minute spent punching nodes after the first hour is a minute not spent unlocking the bench you actually need.

---

## The mental model: two parallel races

Wipe day is two resource races running at once, and you have to interleave them:

| Race | What you're collecting | Gates it opens |
|---|---|---|
| **Scrap race** | scrap + recyclable [[Components]] | research/tech-tree unlocks (tools, guns, doors) |
| **Fragment race** | Basic then Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] | the benches themselves (WB1 → WB2 → WB3) |

A bench with no unlocked recipes is useless; an unlocked recipe with no bench to craft it is useless. You need **both** to line up. The whole speedrun is about not letting one race lag the other — the classic mistake is teching a full WB2 loadout you can't build because you never grabbed 5 Basic Fragments, or vice versa.

---

## Phase 0 — Spawn to bag (target: first 10 minutes)

The clock starts at the beach. Speed here is mostly muscle memory.

**Checklist:**
- [ ] Spawn, gather wood + stone with the rock until you have **stone tools** (Stone Hatchet + Stone Pickaxe). This roughly triples your gather rate — make these before anything else.
- [ ] Get to **~1,000 wood + ~500 stone + some metal ore**. Hit nodes on the way, don't make a project of it.
- [ ] Place a **[[Tool Cupboard]]** (1,000 wood) — this is your land claim. Authorize on it.
- [ ] Build a minimal **2x1** with a **wooden door**. Skip the code lock for 60 seconds; a key lock (free, 1 wood) holds until you tech a code lock.
- [ ] Place a **Sleeping Bag** (30 cloth). Bag cap is 15 — you'll want several spread around later, but one at home now.
- [ ] Place a **Furnace** (and start smelting any ore you grabbed) before you leave.

> [!tip] Don't over-build on wipe day
> A returner's reflex is to build a "real base" immediately. Don't. On a populated server, a fat early base is a billboard that says "raid me." Build the smallest defensible box that holds a TC + furnace + bench, hidden if you can manage it. See [[Solo Survival Guide]] and [[Base Designs]]. The base grows *after* you have a gun.

**Common Phase 0 mistakes:**
- Punching trees for 20 minutes "to be safe." You need ~1k wood, not 5k.
- Forgetting the bag. Dying naked with no bag on wipe day costs you 15 minutes of beach.
- Building far from a road/monument. You want your base **within a short run of a recycler and a green/blue puzzle monument** — that proximity is the single biggest time-saver of the wipe.

---

## Phase 1 — WB1 + the cheap power spike (target: 30–45 min in)

This is the cheapest, fastest spike in the game post-[[Pivot Or Die]].

**Step 1: Build [[Workbench Level 1]].** Cost is **500 wood + 100 metal frags — no scrap, no fragments** (see [[Workbenches]]). This is the one bench you can build entirely from base materials. Build it as soon as you can smelt 100 frags.

**Step 2: Start the scrap race.** Go run **road barrels + roadside crates** and one small monument. Targets:
- Road barrels = **2 scrap each** + ~15% component chance ([[Scrap]]).
- Hit **[[Oxum's Gas Station]]**, **[[Mining Outpost]]**, **[[Abandoned Supermarket]]**, or **[[Lighthouse]]** — tier-0, no rad suit needed, fast in-and-out, and most have a **monument [[Recycling|recycler]]** so you can convert components to scrap on the spot.
- You want **~150–300 scrap** banked for the first tech round.

**Step 3: Tech-tree the WB1 essentials.** At ~15–30 scrap each these are nearly free now. Priority order:

1. **Code Lock** (secure your base — do this first)
2. **[[Hatchet]] + [[Pickaxe]]** (metal tools = much faster gather than stone)
3. **Sleeping Bag** is default; tech **[[Large Furnace]]** for smelting throughput
4. **[[Small Backpack]]** (carry more on monument runs — huge QoL)
5. **A sidearm** — pick ONE: [[Revolver]] (cheap, reliable), Double Barrel (burst), or [[Crossbow]] (silent, ammo-cheap). The revolver is the standard.
6. **Medical Syringe** (combat sustain) — skip the Large Medkit until WB2 economy.

> [!note] Research Table — only build it if you have a reason
> Build a **[[Research Table]]** (200 metal frags + 20 scrap) **only** if you (a) found a gun you want to clone, or (b) you're a duo/trio and want to hand out shareable paper BPs. For a pure solo teching their own path, the [[Tech Tree]] is cheaper and needs no physical copy. See the trade-off table in [[Tech Tree]].

**End-of-Phase-1 state:** defensible box, metal tools, backpack, a sidearm + a few meds. You're now a real threat to other nakeds and can safely run monuments.

---

## Phase 2 — The Basic Fragment run (target: 1–2 hr in)

**This is the phase returners forget exists.** In 2023 you'd dump scrap into the bench and move on. Now you must physically go get **5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]** before [[Workbench Level 2]] will craft.

**The efficient move: one green/blue puzzle monument gives you almost all of it.**

| Monument | Basic Fragments | Card needed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Power Plant]] | ×3 | [[Blue Keycard]] | also 3 recyclers, big scrap |
| [[Train Yard]] | ×3 | [[Blue Keycard]] | |
| [[Water Treatment Plant]] | ×3 | [[Blue Keycard]] | |
| [[Underwater Labs]] | ~4 | (dive) | strong all-rounder |
| [[Airfield]] | ×2 | [[Green Keycard]] | |

**One ×3 run + a couple of looted fragments = your 5.** You almost never need two full runs. If you're short, the **[[Metal Detector]]** digs a Basic Fragment at **6.1% per dig** (~1 in 16) — a quiet supplement for a low-PvP solo, but slower than a single guaranteed loot room.

**While you're at the monument, multi-task the scrap race:**
- Loot all crates/barrels for scrap + **[[Components]]** (rifle bodies, tech trash, gears, springs).
- Grab a **[[Blue Keycard]]** / [[Green Keycard]] for the [[Puzzle System|puzzle]] (and carry 1–2 [[Fuses]]).
- Recycle low-value components **at the monument recycler** (not at Outpost — monument recyclers pay ~50% more; see [[Recycling]]). **Keep** rifle bodies, springs, and semi bodies — you'll craft from those.

**Bank for the bench:** **20 HQM + 500 metal frags** for the WB2 craft (plus your 5 Basic Fragments). HQM comes from recycling springs/pipes/road signs/sheet metal early, then from smelting later. See [[Refining HQM]].

**Build [[Workbench Level 2]]:** 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + **5 Basic Fragments**.

**Then tech-tree your real loadout at WB2.** Priority for a solo/duo:

1. **[[Thompson]]** — the best T2 cost-to-DPS gun, and your first proper PvP weapon. (Tech this *first*.)
2. **Salvaged tools** (Salvaged Axe / Pickaxe / Hammer / Icepick) — the gather/repair jump that pays for itself fast.
3. **Sheet Metal Door + [[Garage Door]]** — your loot room finally stops being a 1-satchel break.
4. **Metal Facemask + Road Sign armor** (Coffee Can helmet path) — survivability spike.
5. **Mixing Table** — required to make gunpowder/ammo (see Phase 3).
6. **Satchel Charges** — your first raiding tool, for opportunistic eco-raids ([[Eco Raiding]]).

> [!tip] Solo gun call at T2: Thompson over Semi-Auto Rifle
> The [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] is fine, but the [[Thompson]] wins early fights with its fire rate and uses cheaper [[pistol ammo]]. Tech the Thompson first; add the Semi later if you want a ranged option. The [[Custom SMG]] and [[MP5]] are reachable too but cost more nodes — skip them on the speedrun.

---

## Phase 3 — Get the gun actually shooting (runs parallel to Phase 2/4)

A teched gun with no ammo is a club. Do this *in parallel* with the fragment grind, not after.

1. **Mine sulfur** (sulfur nodes / desert + snow biome). You need a steady sulfur stream from here to endgame.
2. **Mixing Table** → **gunpowder**: 30 charcoal + 20 sulfur → 10 gunpowder.
3. Craft ammo for your gun:
   - **Pistol ammo** for the Thompson (cheap, makes the gun usable immediately).
   - **[[5.56 Rifle Ammo]]** once you're on rifles: 10 metal frags + 5 GP → 3 rounds.
4. Carry a few meds and you're **PvP-capable.** Now your monument runs defend themselves and you can counter-roam contested loot.

> [!note] Charcoal bottleneck
> Gunpowder eats charcoal, and charcoal comes from burning wood in furnaces. A [[Large Furnace]] (Phase 1 tech) churns charcoal far faster than the basic furnace — this is *why* the Large Furnace is a Phase 1 priority, not a luxury. See [[Smelting and Furnaces]].

---

## Phase 4 — The Advanced Fragment run → WB3 → AK (target: 3–5 hr in)

The final gate. [[Workbench Level 3]] needs **5 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]**, and those come from **elite / hackable crates at top-tier monuments**.

**Where to get Advanced Fragments:**

| Source | Yield | Access |
|---|---|---|
| [[Locked Crate]] (Oil Rig / Chinook / Ghost Ship) | **2 guaranteed** | hack timer / heli |
| [[Small Oil Rig]] / [[Large Oil Rig]] | hackable crate = 1+ | RHIB/boat, NPCs |
| [[Launch Site]] | elite crates | high rad, [[Bradley APC]] |
| [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] | elite crates | [[Red Keycard]] |
| [[Military Tunnels]] | elite crates | high-rad NPCs |

**The fastest single source is a hackable [[Locked Crate]]: 2 Advanced Fragments guaranteed each.** Two oil rig runs (or one rig + one Launch Site sweep) covers your 5. To *fund* these trips, killing the **[[Bradley APC]]** at Launch Site or the **[[Patrol Helicopter]]** dumps huge scrap + component hauls — but only attempt those once you have rockets/explosives and armor.

> [!warning] Don't brute-force Advanced Fragments
> You *can* convert **20 Basic → 1 Advanced**, meaning 100 Basic Fragments = a WB3. **Never do this.** It's an enormous grind versus a couple of monument runs. The conversion exists for overflow, not as a route.

**Bank for the bench:** **100 HQM + 1,000 metal frags** (see [[Workbenches]] for the exact WB3 cost), plus your 5 Advanced Fragments.

**Build [[Workbench Level 3]], then tech the AK.**

- **[[Assault Rifle|AK-47]]** — the goal. Tech-tree path is ~780 scrap total, or research a looted one for 120 scrap. **Craft cost: 50 [[High Quality Metal]] + 200 wood + 1 Rifle Body + 4 Metal Spring** (35s craft). This is why you *kept* rifle bodies and springs instead of recycling them.
- **[[5.56 Rifle Ammo]]** (if not already) + **Explosive 5.56** (the cheap raid bullet).
- **[[Bolt Action Rifle]]** if you want a sniper option.
- **Satchels → C4 / Rockets** for hard raids (see [[Explosives]] and [[Raid Costs]]).
- High-tier armor crafting (and note the new **Ballistic armor set** from the [[Built Different Update]], June 2026 — see [[Rust Armor]]).

**You now have a full AK kit.** That's the speedrun completed: naked → AK in roughly a focused afternoon if monuments cooperate.

---

## The minimum-scrap path (if you're scrap-starved)

Scrap is rarely the bottleneck now, but if you're playing a high-contest server and getting your monument runs taxed, here's the leanest scrap spend to still reach T3:

1. **WB1 (free of scrap)** — tech only **Code Lock, Hatchet, Pickaxe, Revolver, Syringe** (~5 nodes, mostly 15–30 scrap → ~120 scrap total).
2. **WB2** — tech only **Thompson, Sheet Metal Door, Mixing Table** (~3 key nodes). Skip salvaged tools and armor if truly starved; craft road sign armor later.
3. **WB3** — tech-tree straight to the **AK only** (path nodes, ~780 scrap) OR **research a looted AK for 120 scrap** if you find one (much cheaper — keep an eye on [[Locked Crate]] drops, the AK drops ~28% there).

The fragment cost is fixed (5 Basic + 5 Advanced regardless), so the only scrap you *must* spend is the gun/tool research. **Looting an AK and researching it (120 scrap) is the single cheapest path to a craftable AK** — always check crate drops before grinding the full tech path.

---

## When to research vs tech-tree vs craft directly

A decision a returner gets wrong constantly. The costs are now equal per item (15/30/60/120), so it comes down to *what you physically have*:

| Situation | Best move | Why |
|---|---|---|
| You want a gun you don't own, solo | **[[Tech Tree]]** | no physical copy needed; just buy the path nodes |
| You **found/looted** the item | **[[Research Table]]** | jump straight to it, no upstream path nodes; consumes the copy |
| Duo/trio, want everyone to have it | **[[Research Table]]** | produces a shareable paper BP (one researches, hands out copies) |
| You already learned the BP | **Craft directly** | research is a one-time unlock; after that just build it at the bench |
| You need it *this fight* and have the mats | **Craft** if learned, else loot one | research/tech takes a trip to a bench + scrap |

The pattern for a solo speedrun: **tech-tree the path to your key guns** (Thompson, AK) early, and **research-table anything good you happen to loot** to skip the path. For a duo/trio, **one person research-tables the AK and hands out paper BPs** — that's the single biggest efficiency a team has over a solo.

---

## Workbench timing — the load-bearing decisions

The benches are the spine of the speedrun. Get the timing right:

- **WB1 — build it the moment you can smelt 100 metal frags** (Phase 1). It costs no scrap and no fragments; there is never a reason to delay it. Everything early lives here.
- **WB2 — build it the moment you have 5 Basic Fragments + 20 HQM** (Phase 2). Don't wait to "have more scrap" — scrap doesn't build it. The trigger is the *fragments*, and one puzzle run gets them.
- **WB3 — build it the moment you have 5 Advanced Fragments + 100 HQM** (Phase 4). This is the slow gate because Advanced Fragments require contested top-tier monuments. Everything before WB3 should be funneling toward funding/surviving those runs.

> [!tip] Crafting-speed bonus stacks with bench tier
> Higher benches craft *faster* — a [[Workbench Level 2]] crafts in 15s at WB1, 7.5s at WB2, 3.75s at WB3 (see [[Workbenches]]). Once you have WB3, bulk-craft your ammo and components *standing in the WB3 aura* for the speed bonus. The [[Workbench Augmentations|Accelerated]] augment speeds it further.

---

## The full wipe-day checklist (printable)

**Phase 0 (0–10 min):**
- [ ] Stone tools
- [ ] 1k wood + 500 stone + ore
- [ ] [[Tool Cupboard]] placed + authorized
- [ ] 2x1 + door (key lock), near a road + green/blue monument
- [ ] [[Sleeping Bag]] + Furnace down, smelting

**Phase 1 (10–45 min):**
- [ ] [[Workbench Level 1]] built (500 wood + 100 frags)
- [ ] Road-barrel + small-monument scrap run → ~150–300 scrap
- [ ] Tech: Code Lock → Hatchet/Pickaxe → [[Large Furnace]] → [[Small Backpack]] → sidearm → Syringe
- [ ] Code Lock on base

**Phase 2 (45 min–2 hr):**
- [ ] Green/blue puzzle monument run → **5 Basic Fragments**
- [ ] Loot components (KEEP rifle bodies + springs + semi bodies)
- [ ] Recycle junk at the **monument** recycler
- [ ] Bank 20 HQM + 500 frags → build [[Workbench Level 2]]
- [ ] Tech: [[Thompson]] → Salvaged tools → Sheet Metal Door + [[Garage Door]] → armor → Mixing Table → Satchels

**Phase 3 (parallel):**
- [ ] Sulfur stream going
- [ ] Mixing Table → gunpowder → ammo
- [ ] Gun loaded — you are now PvP-capable

**Phase 4 (2–5 hr):**
- [ ] Oil Rig / Launch Site / Silo runs → **5 Advanced Fragments** (Locked Crate = 2 each)
- [ ] Bank 100 HQM + 1,000 frags → build [[Workbench Level 3]]
- [ ] Tech/research the **[[Assault Rifle|AK]]** (research a looted one for 120 scrap if you find it)
- [ ] Craft AK: 50 HQM + 200 wood + 1 Rifle Body + 4 Metal Spring
- [ ] Ammo + meds + armor → **full AK kit**

---

## Solo vs duo/trio — how the route splits

| | Solo | Duo / Trio |
|---|---|---|
| **Fragments** | farm all yourself; one ×3 run = WB2 | split duties — one runs monuments while another farms/builds |
| **Research** | tech-tree only (cheapest for one player) | one person research-tables key guns → shares paper BPs |
| **Oil Rig** | risky alone; pick low-pop hours | one holds the crate timer, one watches stairs/water |
| **Base** | small + hidden; under the [[Solo Survival Guide]] explosive cap | bigger, more turrets (mind the 40m turret-interference cap) |
| **Raiding** | satchels / explo-ammo on soft side; C4 sparingly | can afford rocket/C4 raids much sooner ([[Raid Costs]]) |
| **AK timeline** | ~4–5 hr realistic solo | ~2.5–3.5 hr with split duties |

The biggest team advantage isn't combat — it's **parallelizing the two races**. One player can run the fragment monuments while another runs the scrap/recycle loop and a third builds + smelts. A solo has to time-slice all three.

---

## Returning-player traps (the things that cost you a wipe)

1. **Hoarding scrap waiting for the old 500-scrap "very rare" wall.** It's **120** now. Spend it.
2. **Trying to grind a bench from base.** Scrap doesn't build benches anymore — only [[Blueprint Fragments]] do, and those only drop at monuments. If your WB2 craft is greyed out, you're missing the 5 Basic Fragments, not scrap.
3. **Recycling rifle bodies + springs.** You craft the AK from those. Keep them.
4. **Dumping components at Outpost out of 2023 habit.** Monument recyclers pay ~50% more ([[Recycling]]).
5. **Over-building wipe-day.** A big early base gets raided. Build small, build hidden, grow after you have a gun.
6. **Skipping the Large Furnace.** It's the charcoal engine that feeds gunpowder. Tech it Phase 1.
7. **Teching guns you can't feed.** Don't unlock five weapons; pick one per tier (Thompson → AK) and fund its ammo.

---

## Related

[[Progression Route]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Research Table]] · [[Scrap]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Assault Rifle]] · [[Thompson]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[First Day Guide]] · [[Pivot Or Die]] · [[Built Different Update]]

pages.title: PvE Mastery
pages.body:
# PvE Mastery

This is the **how to actually run every AI/PvE loot target** layer on top of the [[Rust Events & PvE|Events]] reference pages. The reference pages hold the verified numbers (HP, hack timers, crate counts, kill costs); this guide is about **sequencing, kit, positioning, the go/no-go decision, and how a solo or small team actually pulls each one off** on a populated 2026 vanilla server (current wipe: **"Built Different,"** live since 4 Jun 2026).

The core PvE truth in Rust: **the AI is rarely what kills you.** The map marker, the gunshot audibility, and the burn timer on the loot are what get you killed — by humans. Every plan below is built around *minimizing your exposure window* and *being able to extract or hold*, not just around beating the scientists/Bradley/heli.

Reference index: [[Rust Events & PvE|Events]] · [[Bradley APC]] · [[Patrol Helicopter]] · [[Oil Rig]] · [[Cargo Ship]] · [[Chinook CH-47]] · [[Locked Crate]] · [[NPCs & Scientists]]

---

## The shared rules (read once, applies to all targets)

These four facts govern every PvE target in the game. Internalize them and most of the tactics below become obvious.

1. **Hacks are 15 minutes and announced globally.** Every [[Locked Crate]] (rig, cargo, Chinook drop) puts a marker on the whole server's map for the full **900-second** hack. You are advertising "free loot + a busy player here" to everyone. The clock is your real enemy.
2. **Gunshots are audible by weapon class at 400 / 500 / 600 m** (Sep 2025 change). The moment you open up on a heli or a deck full of scientists, you've rung the dinner bell for everyone within render. Plan for a third party *every time*.
3. **Burn timers gate the loot.** Bradley crates (~4 min), heli gibs (~couple min), and the napalm/fire on both must cool before you can touch the loot. You have to *hold the kill site* through the burn — that's the contested window.
4. **Don't shoot the crate.** Damaging a [[Locked Crate]] **resets the 15-minute timer**. It's the #1 denial troll. If someone's shooting your crate, they're not necessarily pushing — they're stalling you into the open.

**Default PvE kit checklist** (scale up/down per target):
- Primary: [[Assault Rifle]] or [[LR-300]] + **300+ rounds of 5.56** (the universal answer to scientists, heli rotors, and human contesters).
- Sidearm/backup: [[Custom SMG]] or a shotgun for close heavies.
- Long-range opener: [[Bolt Action Rifle]] / [[L96]] with HV ammo for safe rotor/scientist pecking.
- **Meds:** at minimum 2 Medical Syringes + a stack of bandages (see [[Meds & Healing|Meds]]). Heavies and the heli out-damage your regen fast.
- Armor: see [[Armor]] — the new **Ballistic** set (June 2026) is the current top-tier human/scientist protection; remember explosive protection on armor is **capped at 75%** (May 2025), so armor will not save you from Bradley's cannon.
- Mobility/extract: a boat ([[RHIB]]) for naval targets, a horse/[[Vehicles (Rust)|vehicle]] for inland, and ideally a stash or sleeping bag near the objective to respawn-rush if you die mid-fight.

---

## Bradley APC — Launch Site

Full reference + cost table: [[Bradley APC]]. Home monument: [[Launch Site]].

Bradley is the **explosive-gated** target: bullets, melee, fire, and arrows do **zero** damage. **1,000 HP**, drops **3 APC crates**, respawns **~1 hour**. This is a pure "do I have the explosives and the spot" play — there's no clever no-cost trick.

### Go/no-go
- **You need explosives in hand before you go.** No improvising. The single most cost-efficient kill is **High Velocity Rockets** at ~200 sulfur each.
- **The reliable plan: bring 6–7 HV rockets.** Four HV will technically kill it with clean rear/tread hits, but Bradley *moves* and misses happen — the "4 vs 7" spread you'll see online is purely an aim question, not a balance change. Bring 6–7 and you're not gambling. That's **~1,200–1,400 sulfur** total — cheap for 3 high-tier crates.
- Alternative costs (see [[Raid Costs]] / [[Explosives]] for the full table): **8 [[Rocket]]s** (~11,200 sulfur — wasteful), **3 [[C4]]** (~6,600), **~20 [[Satchel Charge]]s** (~9,600). HV is the answer unless you literally have nothing else.

### The kill (positioning is everything)
Bradley has a **main cannon (~25–30 dmg/shell)** that will one-shot most early armor, plus twin auto-cannons. **It cannot shoot what it cannot see** — so the whole fight is "peek, fire, break line of sight."

1. **Pre-position on hard cover.** The rocket-factory building, the giant rocket itself, and container stacks at [[Launch Site]] all block the cannon. Pick a spot where you can step out, fire one HV, and step back behind something solid.
2. **Aim center-mass / turret, not the wheels.** Every explosive hit counts toward the 1,000 HP pool; you just want hits, not "weak points."
3. **One rocket per peek.** Fire, duck, let the cannon volley hit your cover, peek the next gap. Two rockets per peek is greedy and gets you cannoned.
4. **Lead it.** HV rockets are fast and flat (much easier on a moving target than slow standard rockets), but still lead the chassis a hair when it's driving.
5. **Commit — don't chip it.** If you damage Bradley and then walk away for a few minutes, **it heals back to full**. There is no "come back later and finish it." Bring enough to do it in one sitting.

### Looting & extract
- On death it drops **3 APC crates** in **burning wreckage — wait ~4 minutes** for the fire to die. This is the dangerous window: the explosion + smoke is visible across the map and the gunfire-into-rockets drew attention.
- **Solo:** clear immediate area, post up on cover overlooking the wreck, and wait out the burn. Don't stand *on* the crates.
- **Duo/trio:** one holds an overwatch angle on the road/rail approaches while the others loot the instant the fire dies. Split the loot into bags and **leave fast** — Launch Site is a destination for geared players.
- The APC crate pool shares the exclusive **Minigun / Military Flamethrower** chance with the heli. Otherwise expect rifles, [[M249]], explosives, high-tier [[Components]], ammo.

---

## Patrol Helicopter — anywhere it roams

Full reference: [[Patrol Helicopter]]. This is the **best no-explosives PvE play for a solo/duo** — a rifle and enough ammo is the whole shopping list.

Body **10,000 HP**, but the **rotors are the trick**: top rotor **900 HP**, tail rotor **500 HP** — destroy **both** and it crashes regardless of body HP. That's ~1,400 effective HP instead of 10,000. **Always shoot rotors.** Drops **4 crates** (1 elite Heli Crate + 3 Heli Weapon Crates). Spawns roughly **every 2–4 hours** (server default).

### Aggro management (this is how you survive)
The heli engages "geared" players — broadly, **more than two clothing/armor pieces or a weapon better than a bow**. It strafes with accurate door-gun MGs and fires **napalm rockets** that set fire to ground and wooden bases.

- **Break line of sight and it deaggros in ~30 seconds.** Your whole fight is peek-shoot-hide around a wall or into a building, exactly like Bradley.
- **Don't stand in the napalm.** It stacks damage fast and will burn down a wooden base under you.
- Fight near a monument or your base with hard cover and a roof to duck under.

### The kill (rotor order)
1. **Tail rotor first (500 HP).** It's the smaller pool, and once it's gone the heli flies erratically and is easier to keep eyes on.
2. **Then the top rotor (900 HP)** — that's the crash.
3. **Peek during its MG strafe.** When it's committed to a strafing run it's predictable and you have a clean rotor angle; dump rounds, then duck *before* the rocket run.
4. A [[Bolt Action Rifle]] / [[L96]] with HV ammo is great for the **opening pecks at range** to chip a rotor safely and draw it to your chosen ground. Switch to [[Assault Rifle]] / [[LR-300]] for sustained rotor damage up close.
5. Bring **300+ rounds of 5.56.** Body-only kills eat 200+ rifle rounds and are a trap — rotors only.
6. If you happen to own a Minigun or a couple of [[Rocket]]s, a few rockets to the rotors ends it instantly — but those are usually better saved for Bradley/raids.

### Crash looting & extract
- Crashes into **4 crates in burning gibs** — wait for the fire to die (~couple minutes) before looting, and **clear the napalm first** or you'll burn standing on the loot.
- The wreck leaves harvestable **scrap / high-quality metal** too.
- Same third-party warning as Bradley: gunfire + visible smoke = company. **Duo:** one watches approaches while the other waits out the burn and harvests. The **1 Heli Crate is elite tier (guaranteed top-tier weapon)** — prioritize that crate first if you have to grab-and-run.

---

## Small & Large Oil Rig

Full reference: [[Oil Rig]] · [[Small Oil Rig]] · [[Large Oil Rig]]. The scientist event chain is owned by [[Chinook CH-47]]; the reward is a [[Locked Crate]].

Both rigs follow the same loop: **clear blue scientists → hack the top-floor locked crate (15 min) → survive the Chinook heavy-scientist drop → loot.** No explosives needed; no radiation on the rig itself (unlike [[Cargo Ship]]). Reach them by [[RHIB]] (recommended) or swim.

The trap that kills new returners: the **rig's blue scientists are 215 HP** (verified rusthelp) — *tankier than the 150 HP monument blues* — so aim head (5-headshot torso-tank otherwise). And the **heavy scientists are the real fight**, not the patrol scientists.

### Small Oil Rig (the solo-friendly one)
- **~12–15 blue scientists** (215 HP), locked crate on **Level 4**, **15-min** hack, scientist respawn **~24 min**.
- Heavy drop: **5 heavies** via [[Chinook CH-47]].
- Has **3 [[Green Keycard]]-locked rooms** (bring a green card — see [[Card Run Routes]] / [[Green Keycard]]).

**Solo plan:**
1. Approach by RHIB, tie up out of the scientists' sightlines, climb up.
2. **Clear from the bottom up**, using doorways and stair landings as cover — fight one or two scientists at a time, never push into open deck under multiple. Headshots only; bodyshots waste a magazine on 215 HP tanks.
3. Loot the green-card rooms and regular crates *first*, before you touch the locked crate — that way if the heavy drop overwhelms you, you've already banked the easy loot.
4. **Only start the hack when you're stocked and ready to fight 5 heavies.** The hack both starts the 900s timer *and* triggers the Chinook.
5. Hold a chokepoint near the helipad/crate. Heavies fast-rope onto the helipad — funnel them through a doorway and headshot. **300 HP, 5 headshots each**, and they roll **four equal-chance loadouts: [[M249]] / Minigun / Military Flamethrower / [[SPAS-12]]** — the flamethrower denies space, so don't get cornered against it.
6. Crate opens → elite loot ([[Locked Crate]] table: guaranteed ×2 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] + metal armor insert + good gun odds).

### Large Oil Rig (a duo/trio job)
- **23 blue scientists** spread L0→L6 (heaviest cluster: **7 on L6** by the crate), 215 HP each. Locked crate on **Level 6**, **15-min** hack, ~62 loot containers across levels.
- Heavy drop: **10 heavies** — double the Small Rig. **This is not a comfortable solo.** Doable, but you'll be juggling 10 heavies + a 15-minute timer + the chance of boats arriving.

**Team plan:**
1. Board together, **split clearing**: one player sweeps lower levels while another pushes toward L6, so you don't get sandwiched.
2. Bank the lower-level + green-room loot on the way up.
3. **Designate a heavy-fight chokepoint near the L6 helipad before hacking.** Ten heavies in the open is a death sentence; a doorway funnel where two of you can headshot in turns is survivable.
4. Start the hack, fall back to the choke, and grind the 10 heavies down. Keep a dedicated **watcher on the water** — the marker draws RHIBs, and a contesting team boarding mid-heavy-fight is the most common wipe.
5. Loot, then leave.

### The rig-specific dangers
- **Heavies, not blues, are the fight.** Carry a shotgun ([[Shotguns]] / [[SPAS-12]]) for close heavies plus your rifle, and *bring real meds* — door-gun-equivalent damage from heavies chunks you.
- **Post-hack flooding:** on some configs the rig **floods with radiation ~30 min after the crate is hacked** — don't camp the rig indefinitely after looting; grab and go.
- **Extraction is the chokepoint.** You came by water; so does everyone contesting you. Have your RHIB positioned for a fast push-off, and split loot across players' bags so one death isn't the whole run.

---

## Cargo Ship

Full reference: [[Cargo Ship]]. The other big **no-explosives** naval run, and arguably the best value because of the radiation-respawn double-dip.

A roaming freighter with **~12 blue scientists**, **3 [[Locked Crate]]s** (bow / stern / mid, each a 15-min hack), and lots of regular crates that **refill every 10 min up to 3 times**. Spawns every ~2–4 in-game days. Since the **Harbor rework (Apr 2024)** it **docks once at the first [[Harbor]] it passes**.

### Boarding (you have options now)
| Method | When to use |
|---|---|
| **[[RHIB]] / boat → rear ladder** | The reliable classic. Drive alongside the stern, climb up. |
| **Harbor container stowaway** | Post-rework: hide in a dock container before the crane loads it aboard. **Best stealth board for a solo with no boat** — you arrive on deck for free and unannounced. |
| **Parachute / [[Attack Helicopter]]** | Air-drop onto the deck (parachutes lose -20% durability per use). |
| Swim + ladder | Slow and exposed; the ship is moving. Last resort. |

### The run
1. **Clear scientists deck by deck** with corridors and containers as cover (they carry MP5s, shotguns, LR-300s). 12 of them is very manageable for a duo and doable solo.
2. **Start all 3 locked-crate hacks early and close together** so they finish around the same time — each is 15 minutes and the marker is up the whole time regardless, so stagger them as little as possible.
3. While the hacks run, loot regular crates. **They refill every 10 min, 3×** — a defended hold genuinely pays out more than a smash-and-grab, *if* you can keep the ship.
4. **Departure = siren → radiation floods the deck to lethal.** Two responses:
   - **No rad gear:** leave *immediately* via the rear **lifeboat** / your boat / parachute.
   - **Rad gear + meds:** **tank ~2 minutes into the radiation** and the ship **respawns all 3 locked crates and shuts the radiation off** — a clean second loot cycle, usually with everyone else already gone. This is the single best PvE value trick in the game if you can survive it.

### Solo vs team
- **Solo:** the container-stowaway board + a quiet 3-crate hack is very survivable; the risk is a contesting boat seeing the marker. Keep a med kit up and the lifeboat in mind.
- **Duo/trio:** one holds the boarding ladder / watches the water while others clear and hack. The radiation double-dip is much easier to pull off as a team since one person can guard while another tanks rads.
- Note: [[RHIB]]s are still fine for cargo, but they're **banned from the newer [[Deep Sea Event]] zone** — don't confuse the two.

---

## Chinook CH-47 locked crate (free-roaming)

Full reference: [[Chinook CH-47]] · [[Locked Crate]].

Separate from its Oil Rig role, the Chinook occasionally **flies over and drops a single [[Locked Crate]] at a random tier-1+ monument**. It's one of the best **"no explosives, no scientists"** grabs in the game — but it's a pure **hold-a-spot-for-15-minutes** test against the whole server, because the crate's location is **marked globally** the entire hack.

### The play
1. Spot the Chinook circling (it may carry the crate slung underneath before placing it) and note the monument it drops on.
2. Get there fast and **start the hack** — 900s countdown, visible to everyone.
3. **Defend the crate for 15 minutes. Do not shoot it** — damage resets the timer (this is *the* denial trick; if a troll is plinking your crate from range, you have to push them off, not wait).
4. It opens to elite loot — same [[Locked Crate]] table as the rigs/cargo: guaranteed **×2 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]** (fastest path to [[Workbench Level 3]]), metal armor insert, and strong gun odds (AK at ~28%).

### Holding it
- **The 15-minute global marker is the entire difficulty.** Pick your fights: the best holds are when the crate lands somewhere with a defensible building you can wall off line of sight from.
- **Solo:** consider whether you can actually hold *this* monument for 15 minutes against your server's population before committing. Sometimes the right call is to let it go.
- **Duo/trio:** one defends/sits the crate room, the others watch the two or three approach angles. Rotate so nobody's caught reloading.
- You *can* try to shoot the Chinook itself down for a bonus, but it has a big HP pool and the crate is the real prize — don't waste ammo you'll need for contesters.

---

## Putting it together — a wipe sequence for a returning solo/duo

The PvE targets aren't a menu, they're a **progression**. Roughly how to slot them into a wipe:

1. **Early wipe (first day):** scrap runs and the [[Patrol Helicopter]] are your engine. The heli needs only a rifle + ammo, and one kill (especially the elite Heli Crate) can fully kit you and jump-start your guns. Watch the spawn cadence (~every 2–4 h) and be ready when it appears near you.
2. **Once you have a [[RHIB]] + ~300 rounds + meds:** start running **[[Cargo Ship]]** and **[[Small Oil Rig]]**. These hand you elite [[Locked Crate]] loot with **no explosives** — the guaranteed Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] from each crate is your fastest route to [[Workbench Level 3]] (two crates clears it). Cargo's radiation double-dip and the container-stowaway board make it the best value of the two.
3. **Grab free [[Chinook CH-47]] crates of opportunity** whenever one drops somewhere you can realistically hold for 15 minutes.
4. **Mid/late wipe, once you can afford ~6–7 HV rockets:** add **[[Bradley APC]]** at [[Launch Site]] to the rotation — ~1,200–1,400 sulfur for 3 high-tier crates and a shot at the Minigun.
5. **As a duo/trio with kit and coordination:** **[[Large Oil Rig]]** (10 heavies) becomes worth it for the bigger loot density.

Across all of them, the discipline is the same: **minimize your marker/gunfire window, never fight the AI in the open, hold or extract the burn, and always assume a third party is coming.** The scientists and the tank are the easy part.

---

## Related

- [[Rust Events & PvE|Events]] — index of every AI/world event
- [[Bradley APC]] · [[Patrol Helicopter]] · [[Oil Rig]] · [[Cargo Ship]] · [[Chinook CH-47]] — the per-target reference pages
- [[Locked Crate]] — the elite loot/blueprint-fragment source behind rigs, cargo, and Chinook drops
- [[NPCs & Scientists]] — blue (150 / 215 HP) and heavy (300 HP) scientist stats and loadouts
- [[Launch Site]] · [[Harbor]] — the relevant monuments
- [[Raid Costs]] · [[Explosives]] — Bradley kill-cost context
- [[Armor]] · [[Meds & Healing|Meds]] · [[Assault Rifle]] · [[LR-300]] · [[Bolt Action Rifle]] · [[Shotguns]] — loadout pieces
- [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Workbench Level 3]] — why the locked-crate runs matter
- [[Returning Player Guide (2023 → 2026)|Returning Player Guide]] — the broader returning-player overview

pages.title: Raiding Playbook
pages.body:
# Raiding Playbook

The "how to actually pull off a raid" layer that sits on top of the reference pages. [[Raid Costs]] tells you *how much boom* a wall takes; [[Explosives]] tells you *how to make it*; [[Raid Methods]] tells you the *categories* of approach. This page is the **decision engine and the field procedure**: how to pick a target, do the cost-vs-loot math, time the hit, build the staging base, choose your breach path, and get out alive with the loot — written for a returning **solo/duo/trio** on a populated 2026 vanilla server.

> **Patch status (Jun 13 2026):** the live **"Built Different" update (Jun 4 2026)** was a player-model / armor / M16A2 patch and **changed no building HP, door HP, explosive damage, or raid costs** — every number referenced here is current. Recheck the first Thursday of next month (Rust's monthly cadence) before trusting any specific count.

The whole game of raiding is a single sentence: **spend less than you take, and survive the extraction.** Everything below serves that sentence.

---

## 1. The mindset: raiding is an investment, not a power trip

A raid is a trade. You convert **boom + time + risk** into **loot**. Most failed raids fail not because the breach didn't work but because the trade was bad: you spent 4 C4 (8,800 sulfur) on a base whose loot room held a chest of cloth and a bow, or you got third-partied at minute 12 and lost the loot *and* your kit.

Before you throw a single charge, you should be able to answer:

1. **What's likely in there?** (read the base — section 2)
2. **What will it cost to reach it?** (the cost workflow — section 3)
3. **When do I hit, online or offline?** (timing — section 4)
4. **How do I stage so I'm not running across the map?** (FOB — section 5)
5. **What's my breach line and what do I bring?** (pathing + kit — sections 6-8)
6. **How do I get the loot home before someone takes it from me?** (extraction — section 9)

If you can't answer 1-2 confidently, you're gambling, not raiding. Gambling is fine on wipe day with beancans; it's a disaster with a C4 stack mid-wipe.

---

## 2. Target selection — reading a base for loot vs effort

The single most valuable raiding skill is **looking at a base and estimating both its loot and its raid cost without going inside.** You do this by walking (or driving) past dozens of bases and triaging.

### Signals a base is worth raiding (loot signals)

- **Tier of build vs size.** A *small* sheet-metal/armored base is the sweet spot: someone invested upgrade resources but doesn't have the wall count of a clan. High value per C4.
- **Activity markers:** smoke from furnaces, the hum of a working [[Recycling|recycler]] or refinery, vehicles parked ([[Minicopter]], [[Modular Cars|car]], [[RHIB]]) , a [[Quarry|quarry]] or [[Pump Jack|pump jack]] running. Active base = fresh loot.
- **Electricity:** lots of wiring, [[Auto Turret]]s, [[Solar Panels|solar]] — a powered base means an invested player with components, guns, and a good [[Tool Cupboard|TC]].
- **External walls + a compound:** they're protecting *something* (often a tugboat, vehicles, or farm). Compounds also mean the owner has resources to burn.
- **Garage doors, shop fronts, [[Vending Machines|vending machines]]:** a vending machine alone is loot (and tells you they trade — they have scrap/components).

### Signals to skip (effort/empty signals)

- **Big bland stone box, no activity, no upkeep smoke** — likely abandoned and decaying, or a sleeper with nothing. Confirm with [[Upkeep and Decay|decay]] state: a base whose lower blocks are already half-decayed has an empty or near-empty TC.
- **Massive clan compound** — wall-count alone (multiple armored layers + honeycomb + turret lines) means dozens of C4. Not a solo/duo target unless you have intel on a soft side.
- **Naked shacks / 1x1s with no upgrades** — usually a bag spot or a fresh spawn. Nothing inside.
- **Bases mid-online-fight** — someone's already raiding it; you'd be the third party walking into two armed groups.

### The loot-room read

The loot is almost never behind the front door. Learn to spot **where the loot room is** from outside:

- **Center mass / highest internal point.** Loot rooms hide in the geometric center or the top floor, behind the most door/wall layers.
- **Count the layers.** Walk the perimeter and count wall thicknesses (honeycomb). A base that's 1-deep everywhere has a cheap line in; a base with 3-deep honeycomb around one quadrant is telling you exactly where the loot is — and that it'll be expensive to reach *there*. Sometimes the cheap line is the back, not the obvious front.
- **Bunker tells.** A wall with no visible door, a suspicious half-height garage door, a floating room with no stairs — see [[Bunkers]]. If the core is a bunker you must break the **shell**, not pick a path; price it as full-wall breaches.
- **TC location guess.** The [[Tool Cupboard]] is usually adjacent to the loot room (so they can hit "authorize" while restocking). Reaching and popping it (100 HP, ~8 explosive 5.56 = 200 sulfur) lets you place *your own* TC and disassemble the rest for free — that's often the real objective, not the loot boxes directly.

**Triage rule:** for every base you consider, give it a rough **loot grade (A-F)** and a rough **C4-equivalent cost.** Only raid where loot grade clearly beats cost. On a populated server you'll walk past 20 bases to find 1 good target — that's normal and correct.

---

## 3. The raid-cost math workflow

This is the core skill. You're turning "a base I can see" into "a precise shopping list of boom + a sulfur bill," then sanity-checking it against expected loot. Full tables live in [[Raid Costs]]; here's the *workflow*.

### Step 1 — Trace the cheapest line to loot

Walk the loot-bearing path from outside to the loot room and write down each obstacle in order. **Always pick the lowest-HP obstacle on each layer:**

- A **[[Sheet Metal Door]] (250 HP) = 1 C4** beats a **sheet wall (1,000 HP) = 4 C4** *every single time.* Hunt for doors.
- A **garage door (600 HP) = 2 C4** is cheaper than a sheet wall but pricier than a sheet door.
- If a layer is a solid wall with no door, that's where the bill spikes — look for an adjacent door or a soft side first.

### Step 2 — Apply the soft-side discount

Once you're through *any* outer layer, interior walls take **~25% less** from the inside ([[Soft Side]]). Whenever your line goes wall → wall, price the second wall at soft-side cost. Even better: if you can reach the **soft underside of the loot-room floor** (from below) or a soft-sided exterior wall, the *whole* break gets cheaper or even goes melee/tool-only. Always look for an exposed soft side before committing C4.

### Step 3 — Pick the explosive per obstacle (the trade-off table)

The anchors from [[Explosives]] — memorize these six:

| Boom | Raw sulfur | Best for |
|------|-----------|----------|
| C4 | **2,200** (+2 tech trash) | single hard target, doors; fastest |
| Rocket | **1,400** | **splash** — honeycomb / multiple walls at once |
| Satchel | **~480** | pre-T3 doors/early walls; duds |
| Beancan | **120** | cheap doors; duds, random fuse |
| Homemade Landmine | **60** | doors when metal-rich, sulfur-poor; needs floor access to place flat |
| Explosive 5.56 | **25/round** | soft targets — TC (8), turret (106), wood (47); doubles as a weapon |

Decision shortcuts:

- **Doors → C4** when you have it (1 C4 = sheet door, fast and quiet-ish). **Landmines/beancans** when you're sulfur-poor and time-rich.
- **Walls → C4** for a single wall (cheapest per-HP), **rockets** when one shot's blast can hit multiple honeycomb walls (see splash, section 6).
- **Soft targets (TC, turrets, wood, exposed boxes) → explosive 5.56.** Never waste C4 on a 100-HP TC.
- **Wood anything → fire.** Incendiary rocket (300) or molotovs are cheaper than any "real" boom against wood. See [[Eco-Raiding]].

### Step 4 — Total it, add a buffer, sanity-check against loot

Add up the sulfur. **Add ~20%** for misjudged walls, a missed rocket, or a hidden extra door layer — running out of boom one wall short of the loot room is the worst outcome in the game. Then compare:

> **Is the expected loot worth more than [total sulfur + my kit + my time + third-party risk]?**

Rough yardsticks (2026): one C4 = 2,200 sulfur ≈ a solid sulfur-node grind session. A 4-C4 raid (~8,800 sulfur) is *most of a wipe-day's farming.* If the loot room probably holds less than ~2 C4 worth of returnable value (guns, components, scrap, explosives you can recycle back), walk away.

### Step 5 — Recycle-back accounting

Don't price a raid purely on sulfur out. **What comes back?** Components, pipes, tech trash, and weapons recycle into the *next* raid's boom. A base full of components and a few guns effectively refunds part of your C4 bill. Monument [[Recycling|recyclers]] (faster, ~120% yield) beat safe-zone recyclers — extract to a recycler, not just to your box.

---

## 4. Timing — online vs offline

(The full comparison table is in [[Raid Methods]]; here's how to *decide*.)

### Default for solo/duo/trio: offline

You rarely have the bodies to win a sustained online fight against an established group while *also* managing boom and loot. **Offline is the default raid for small groups.** The target is asleep or away; you breach, loot, and leave with nobody shooting back. The cost is **time pressure** (they could log in) and the risk that they've stashed/removed loot before logging.

How to find the offline window:

- **Learn their hours.** Scout the base across a day or two; note when activity (smoke, doors opening, vehicles moving) stops.
- **[[Seismic Sensor]] / decay timing** can hint at activity, but the simplest tool is just patience and observation.
- **Server population dips** (very late local night, weekday mornings) widen the window.

### When online is correct

- **You outnumber or out-gear them** and want *all* their loot present (offline players often log with key loot on them or stashed).
- **The loot is so good** you accept a fight (e.g., you watched them run a heli/cargo and stuff a tugboat).
- **Counter-raid opportunity:** they're *already* mid-raid on someone else, distracted and committed — see [[Counter-Raiding]]. Hitting a group that's spent their boom and attention elsewhere is one of the highest-EV plays in the game.

### Noise and the neighbors

Even an "offline" raid is loud. Explosions carry; gunshots are audible **400/500/600m** by weapon class. On a populated server, **every boom is a dinner bell** that brings third parties. Mitigate:

- **Hit during server-wide events** ([[Patrol Helicopter|heli]], [[Cargo Ship|cargo]], [[Airdrop|airdrop]]) when noise blends in and players are distracted at the event.
- **Crouch-walk** (the only silent movement) on approach.
- **Be fast.** A raid that takes 4 minutes draws fewer third parties than one that takes 20. Pre-plan the breach order so you're never standing around deciding.

---

## 5. The raid base / FOB — staging the operation

Running boom and loot back and forth across the map on foot is how raids die. Build a **Forward Operating Base (FOB)** — a disposable staging structure near the target.

### What a minimum FOB needs

- **A sleeping bag (or twoper person)** so you respawn *at the raid*, not at home. This is non-negotiable — if a defender or third party kills you, you want to be back in 5 seconds, not 5 minutes.
- **A box or two** to dump loot into between trips, so a single death doesn't lose everything you've pulled.
- **A small [[Tool Cupboard]]** to stop someone from instantly griefing/decaying your FOB and to let you build walls.
- **Walls/airlock if online** — even a 1x1 with a code-locked door gives you a fallback to reload, heal, and respawn-defend.

### Placement

- **Close, but not breaching-distance.** Far enough that a defender logging in doesn't immediately see/shoot you while you build; close enough that respawning puts you right back in the fight. ~30-80m, behind cover (a rock, treeline, ridge) with line-of-sight to the breach.
- **On the loot side / extraction side** so your final trips are short.
- **Disposable.** A FOB is twig/wood — you abandon it after the raid. Don't over-invest; it's scaffolding.

### Raid-base variants

- **Solo offline:** often just a bag + a box on the ground behind a rock. Minimal.
- **Online / contested:** a sealed 1x1 or 2x1 with an airlock, a bag each, a box, and ideally an [[Auto Turret]] or shotgun trap facing the approach so you can defend while looting. This is also your **counter-counter-raid** position if the owner logs in.
- **Big raid (trio, armored target):** a 2x2 with a furnace (to smelt looted ore on-site), a small [[Workbench]] (to craft more boom from recycled components), and multiple bags. Effectively a mobile base for a long siege.

---

## 6. Breach pathing — getting through the shell

Knowing the cost is half of it; the *order and physics* of the breach is the other half. Tighten your route so every charge counts.

### Soft-side first, always

Before you spend hard-side prices, check for the cheapest physics:

- **Soft-sided exterior wall** (a build mistake — pale flat-grey face out, see [[Soft Side]]): pickaxe/jackhammer it for a handful of tools, no boom, near-silent.
- **Soft underside of the loot-room floor:** if you can get *directly below* the loot room (a foundation you can stand on, a cave/cliff gap, or by tunneling sideways one layer), you break **upward through the soft floor** for ~10x melee / ~2x firearm damage — sometimes cheaper than any wall. This is the classic "soft-side the loot room from below" raid.
- **Once you breach any layer, soft-side inward.** Every interior wall is ~25% cheaper from inside, and interior walls are often the un-honeycombed weak link.

### Honeycomb and splash damage

**Honeycomb** = the extra ring of walls a defender builds around the loot room so you can't just break two walls to reach it; you have to chew through a maze. This is where **rockets beat C4**:

- A **rocket's blast hits up to four walls of the building "cross" for full damage**, plus partial damage to the two adjacent walls on each side. So one well-placed rocket into a honeycomb pocket damages *multiple* walls at once.
- **C4 is single-target** (it sticks to one surface). It's the cheapest *per single wall*, but useless for the "open many honeycomb walls together" job.
- **Rule:** punch **doors with C4** one at a time; blow **honeycomb walls with rockets** in bulk. Mix your boom accordingly — a typical armored-base raid is "C4 the door line + rockets through the honeycomb."

### Defeating bunkers

A [[Bunkers|bunker]] has **no walkable door into the core** — the only access is a hatch the owner drops through, or a piece they briefly remove and replace. You can't pick a path; you must **break the shell.** Practical implications:

- **Price it as full-wall breaches**, not door breaks. A bunkered loot room behind sheet/armored walls is 4-8 C4 *per wall face* — frequently not worth it for a solo unless the loot is exceptional.
- **Look for the hatch / removed piece.** Some bunkers rely on a floor hatch or a pixel-gap drop; if you can reach the hatch's level you may breach one floor/wall into the core instead of the full shell. Garage-door and ladder-hatch bunkers are the common 2026 patterns.
- **Stability-trick / "God Bunker" cells** are patch-volatile — they sometimes break a floor that the engine then can't restore, but Facepunch tweaks these. Don't *count* on a stability cheese line; price the honest shell break and treat any stability exploit as a bonus.
- See [[Bunkers]] for the build side (how defenders make these) — understanding the build tells you exactly which piece to attack.

### Door stacking and airlocks

Modern solo/duo loot rooms hide behind **stacked sheet doors + airlocks** rather than one fat door, precisely because **1 C4 = 1 sheet door.** So:

- **Count the doors, not the rooms.** A "two-room airlock" might be 3 sheet doors deep = 3 C4 just to walk the hallway. Price every door.
- **Garage doors in the stack** (600 HP = 2 C4) are a deliberate speed-bump — they cost double a sheet door and you can't shoot through them.
- If the door stack is more expensive than blowing **one wall** around it (and soft-siding in), take the wall. Always compare the door line vs a wall flank.

### Take the TC

The strategic objective inside many raids is the **[[Tool Cupboard]] (100 HP).** Eight explosive 5.56 (200 sulfur) destroys it. Once their TC is gone:

- They can no longer instantly repair/upgrade against you.
- You can **place your own TC**, which lets you **remove (pick up) their building blocks** — meaning you can disassemble walls/doors for *free* instead of booming every remaining layer. Reaching the TC early can collapse the rest of the raid cost to near-zero.

---

## 7. Splash, fire, and the "free" damage sources

- **Rocket splash** (above) — your bulk-wall tool; aim at wall intersections, not flat centers, to catch the most surfaces.
- **Fire vs wood:** never boom a wooden structure. Incendiary rocket (300 sulfur) or molotovs (2 = wood wall) are far cheaper and ignore soft/hard side. Fire can also be lobbed *through* windows/embrasures to flush hiders out of a loot room. See [[Eco-Raiding]].
- **Explosive 5.56 splash-free chipping:** great for whittling a turret (106 rounds, or just bait/disable it offline), the TC, and exposed deployables while your booms handle structure.
- **Shoot the turrets first.** An [[Auto Turret]] (1,000 HP) will shred you mid-breach. Offline you can often just walk up and gun it down or rocket it (3 rockets); online, disable power or peek-kill it before committing.

---

## 8. What to bring (the raid kit)

Pack from a checklist, not from vibes. Forgetting your launcher 60m into the raid is a real way to lose one.

### Boom (per your section-3 plan)

- The exact explosives from your cost workflow **+20% buffer.**
- A **[[Rocket Launcher]]** if you're bringing rockets (don't forget the launcher).
- A stack of **explosive 5.56** for the TC, turrets, and soft cleanup.

### Combat kit (one per person, more on contested raids)

- Your main rifle ([[Assault Rifle]]/[[M16A2]]/[[SKS]]/etc.) + ammo, plus your sidearm.
- **Armor:** at least a [[Armor|coffee can helmet + roadsign/metal chest]]; full kit if you expect a fight. The new ballistic armor set (Built Different) is an option if you've farmed it.
- **Meds:** [[Meds|syringes / medical syringes / bandages]]. You *will* take damage breaching and from third parties.

### Utility

- **Building plan + hammer + ~enough resources** for the FOB (bags, a box, a TC, a few walls/doors).
- **Sleeping bag(s)** — the most-forgotten item; without it you can't respawn at the raid.
- **A [[Hammer]]** to place/pick up and to upgrade the FOB.
- **Building tool for soft-siding:** a **jackhammer or salvaged pickaxe** in case a soft side or floor opens a cheap line.
- **A vehicle** for offline raids far from home — [[Minicopter]] for boom in, loot out; [[Horses|horse]] or [[Modular Cars|car]] for ground hauling.
- **Codes pre-set** on your FOB doors so you're not fumbling a keypad mid-fight.

### Pre-raid checklist (run it every time)

1. Boom counted + 20% buffer, launcher packed.
2. Explosive 5.56 for TC/turrets.
3. Full combat kit + meds per person.
4. FOB kit: bags, box, TC, walls/doors, hammer.
5. Soft-side tool (pickaxe/jackhammer).
6. Vehicle fueled if needed; bag set at home in case you die en route.

---

## 9. Extraction — getting the loot home

You haven't won until the loot is in a box you own that nobody's raiding. Extraction is where greedy raiders lose everything.

- **Stage loot to your FOB box first**, not all the way home. One death mid-haul shouldn't lose the whole take.
- **Prioritize what you grab.** If you might get rushed: guns, components, tech trash, explosives, and scrap first; bulk resources (stone, wood, low-grade) last and only if safe. Don't die holding a stack of frags.
- **Recycle on-site or en route.** Components and broken guns are worth more as recycled metal/pipes/tech trash you can re-roll into next raid's boom. Hit a monument [[Recycling|recycler]] (faster + ~120% yield) on the way home.
- **Watch for the bag-camp.** If you offline-raided, the owner may log in to a destroyed base and respawn angry. Either be gone, or hold your FOB and bag-camp *them* (you have the position and the loot; they have nothing). Counter-counter-raiding from a prepared FOB is very winnable — see [[Counter-Raiding]].
- **Vary your route home.** Don't run a straight line that a watcher can intercept; use cover, and split loot across players if it's a duo/trio so one death isn't catastrophic.
- **Leave nothing reusable behind.** Abandon the twig FOB (it'll decay), but don't leave a stocked box or your spare boom for the next person.

---

## 10. Worked examples

### Example A — solo, mid-wipe, small stone base, offline

You spot an active small stone base: smoke, a [[Minicopter]] parked, no turrets. You scout: front is a sheet door, then a hallway with one more sheet door into a loot room next to the TC. **Two sheet doors = 2 C4 (4,400 sulfur)** + 8 explosive 5.56 (200) for the TC. Add buffer: bring **3 C4** in case of a hidden third door. Loot grade B (active base, components likely). Plan: build a bag + box behind the parked-mini rock, wait for the offline window (no smoke for an hour), C4 door one, C4 door two, explosive-5.56 the TC, place your own TC, pick up the loot-room walls for free if there's more behind, haul to the FOB box, mini home. **Net:** ~4,600 sulfur out, likely components + a gun + scrap back — good trade.

### Example B — duo, late wipe, bunkered armored base

A neat armored base, no visible loot-room door — a [[Bunkers|bunker]]. The core is behind **one armored wall face (2,000 HP = 8 C4 = 17,600 sulfur)** with honeycomb. That's ~8 sulfur-grind-sessions for a *maybe*. **Verdict: skip it** unless you have hard intel (watched them stash heli/cargo loot) — and even then, look for the hatch level to breach one floor instead of the full shell, or eco-raid a softer neighbor. The math, not the ego, makes this call.

### Example C — trio counter-raid (highest EV)
