You see a group **already raiding** a third base — booms going off, their boom and attention spent. They've left their own base lighter and they're standing in the open at the breach. This is a [[Counter-Raiding]] play, not a wall-break: skip the explosives, bring **combat kit**, FOB up nearby, and **take the loot off their bodies and out of the base they just opened.** You let someone else pay the C4 bill. Bring meds and armor, not C4.

---

## 11. Quick decision rules (the cheat sheet)

1. **Raid the lowest-HP obstacle on the path to loot.** Doors > walls. Soft-side > hard-side. (Sheet door = 1 C4 vs sheet wall = 4 C4.)
2. **Soft-side every interior wall** (~25% off) and **soft-underside the loot-room floor** when you can reach it (~10x melee).
3. **C4 for single targets/doors; rockets for honeycomb splash; explosive 5.56 for soft (TC/turrets/wood); fire for wood.**
4. **Take the TC** (100 HP, 8 explo) — then place your own and disassemble the rest for free.
5. **Offline is the default** for solo/duo/trio; **online/counter-raid** only when you out-gear or they're distracted/already-committed.
6. **Always FOB:** bag + box + TC near the target. Respawn at the raid, dump loot between trips.
7. **+20% boom buffer.** Running one wall short of loot is the worst outcome.
8. **Total cost (sulfur + kit + time + third-party risk) must clearly beat expected loot,** counting recycle-back.
9. **Be fast and hit during events** — every boom is a third-party dinner bell.
10. **The raid isn't over until the loot is in your box.** Extraction is half the raid.

---

## Related

[[Raid Costs]] · [[Explosives]] · [[Raid Methods]] · [[Eco-Raiding]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Soft Side]] · [[Counter-Raiding]] · [[Raid Defense]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Auto Turret]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Seismic Sensor]] · [[Bradley APC]]

pages.title: Recoil & Aim Mastery
pages.body:
# Recoil & Aim Mastery

The single biggest skill gap in Rust is **landing bullets**. Two players with the same [[Assault Rifle]] kit can have a 5:1 K/D difference purely on spray control and crosshair placement. This guide is the "how to actually aim" layer that sits on top of the per-weapon stat pages in [[Rust Weapons]] and the systems math in [[Combat Mechanics]]. If you're a returning player who last touched Rust before the **May 2024 aimcone overhaul**, your old muscle memory is partly wrong — the modern system rewards a different rhythm. Read this whole page once, then go do the train-server routine at the bottom.

This page covers the *technique*. For raw numbers (damage, RPM, recoil values) follow the [[wikilinks]] to the weapon pages; for the underlying hit/aimcone math see [[Combat Mechanics]].

---

## The modern recoil system (what changed, and why your old habits are wrong)

Rust recoil is **not** a single memorizable pattern anymore. Since the post-2022 rework it is three layers stacked on top of each other:

1. **Recoil pattern (deterministic):** every shot kicks the muzzle in a *direction* — mostly up, with a per-weapon horizontal drift. This part is learnable and is what you counter with mouse movement.
2. **Aim cone (random spread):** even with a perfectly still crosshair, bullets land somewhere inside a cone. The cone is small when you start firing and **bloom**s wider the longer you hold the trigger.
3. **Bloom + movement penalty:** sustained full-auto and movement widen the cone further.

The mantra from every modern recoil guide: *"Spray isn't pattern memorization. It's fighting bloom, aim cone, and some RNG."* You can control the pattern perfectly and still miss at range because of the cone. That is intentional — it's why **bursting beats holding the trigger** outside of point-blank.

### The May 2024 aimcone overhaul — the rule that changed everything

Before May 2024, **any** movement instantly maxed out your aim-cone penalty, so "run-and-gun" was punished and people stood still to shoot. Facepunch changed it ([[Meta Madness Update]]):

> The movement penalty now starts at **zero** and blends up to full only **after ~4 rapid-fire shots**.

Practical consequences — internalize these:

- **Tap-firing and 2–4 round bursts while strafing are now accurate.** You can dodge *and* shoot. This is the core of modern Rust PvP.
- **Full-auto while standing still sprays the widest** by the end of the mag. Holding the trigger is a close-range-only tool.
- **The cone resets between bursts.** Stop firing for a beat and your next burst starts tight again. This is why "burst → reset → re-peek" works.

If you came back and your sprays feel worse than you remember, it's because you're holding the trigger like it's 2021. Switch to bursts.

### Crouch

Crouching **shrinks the base aim cone** (tighter grouping) and shrinks your hitbox — but it does **not** remove bloom or recoil, and it slows you to a crawl. Crouch for the *last* precise shots or to hold a static angle, never as a blanket accuracy button. Crouch-spamming ("crouch peeking") is a real technique for poking a head over cover, but standing-and-bursting wins most open fights because mobility dodges the enemy's bullets.

---

## Sensitivity, FOV & settings (do this before you train)

Recoil control is muscle memory tied to a fixed sensitivity. **Pick a sensitivity and never change it.** Every time you change it you reset your spray muscle memory to zero. Full settings live on [[Settings and Binds]]; the combat-relevant ones:

- **FOV:** Set to **90** (the max) and lock the viewmodel scale so ADS doesn't warp: console `graphics.fov "90"; graphics.vm_fov_scale false`. Above 90 isn't available; pushing viewmodel FOV makes the gun feel shaky and targets smaller — **85–90 is the sweet spot** for tracking and spray. Wider FOV also means you see more peripherally, which matters more than a slightly smaller target.
- **Mouse sensitivity / DPI:** There's no "correct" number, but a common comfortable range is roughly **30–55 cm/360** (the physical distance to spin a full circle). Lower = steadier sprays, more desk space needed; higher = faster flicks, twitchier spray. DPI directly affects how big your counter-movements are, so **practice at the exact DPI + in-game sens you'll play at.** Use a cm/360 converter if you're matching a setup from another game.
- **ADS sensitivity:** Keep the ADS multiplier (mouse aim sensitivity scalar) at **1.0** so hipfire and ADS feel like the same physical motion — this keeps one set of muscle memory. Lower ADS sens helps long-range scope work but splits your muscle memory; most players keep it at 1.
- **Raw input ON:** console `input.rawinput true` — bypasses Windows mouse acceleration/smoothing. Non-negotiable.
- **Kill motion blur and weapon FX clutter:** `graphics.motionblur 0` so you can see your tracers and the target.
- **Unity 6 mouse caveat (Jun 2026):** since the engine move, **1000Hz+ polling mice can cause stutter/input hitches**. If your aim feels inconsistent post-update, drop your mouse polling rate to **500Hz** until Facepunch patches it (see [[Combat Mechanics]] and [[Performance]]).

---

## Crosshair placement & the rules that beat raw mechanics

Mechanical spray control is maybe half of aiming. The other half is **where your crosshair already is** when the enemy appears. Good players "pre-aim" so they barely have to move.

- **Keep your crosshair at head height, always.** Headshots do **2x damage** ([[Combat Mechanics]]) — an [[Assault Rifle]] body shot of ~50 becomes ~100 to the head. Walk corners, doorways, and monument hallways with your dot already where a head will be. You should be *correcting onto* a head, not *finding* one.
- **Pre-aim the angle, not the open space.** Hold your crosshair tight on the edge of the cover the enemy will peek from, so the moment they appear you're already on them.
- **Wide-swing vs shoulder-peek:** shoulder-peek (expose one pixel of shoulder) to *bait/gather info* when you're not ready; wide-swing (full strafe out) only when you've committed and want to use the [[#The peeker's advantage]] timing edge.
- **Don't ego-spray a held angle.** If someone is pre-aiming a doorway, the worst thing you can do is walk straight into their crosshair. Jiggle, bait the shot, then swing on their reload/reset.

---

## Hipfire vs ADS vs crouch — when to use each

| Mode | Cone | Move speed | Use it for |
|------|------|-----------|------------|
| **Hipfire** | Wide | Full | Point-blank shotgun/SMG brawls, surprise close kills. A coin flip past ~10m. |
| **ADS, standing** | Tight base, blooms with spray | Reduced | The default for everything past short range. Strafe + burst. |
| **ADS, crouched** | Tightest base | Crawl | The last precise long-range shots; holding a static sniper/angle. |

The decision tree in a fight: **close (<10m) → hipfire or spray**; **mid (10–60m) → ADS strafe-burst 3–5 rounds**; **long (60m+) → ADS, slow taps, crouch for the final shots, wait for the cone to fully shrink between shots.**

---

## Per-weapon spray patterns & how to compensate

Patterns below are *tendencies* — a direction to counter, plus irreducible cone scatter on top. Numbers and craft/unlock details are on each weapon's page; this is the muscle-memory layer. **Universal compensation rule: move the mouse the opposite direction of the kick.** Almost everything kicks **up first**, so the dominant motion is always a firm downward pull; the horizontal drift is the part that differs per gun.

### [[Assault Rifle]] (AK) — *Hard. The skill ceiling.*
The hardest but most rewarding spray in the game. The muzzle **climbs sharply straight up for the first ~6–8 rounds**, then **drifts** (the classic "S-curve" tendency — a snake left in the mid-mag, then a pull back). 
- **Compensate:** pull **straight down hard** during the opening vertical climb, then ease the pull and **counter the horizontal drift** (nudge against whichever way it's snaking) in a shallow zigzag-down motion that mirrors the muzzle.
- **Practical doctrine:** **burst 4–6 rounds**, reset, re-peek. Reserve the full-mag spray for point-blank where the cone doesn't matter. Mastering the AK is the single biggest investment that pays off — it's the craftable end-game gun.
- Attachments: [[Holosight]] + [[Muzzle Brake]] (tames vertical) for spray fights; [[8x Scope]]/[[16x Scope]] + [[Silencer]] for stealthy mid-long. See [[Weapon Attachments]].

### [[LR-300]] — *Easy. Best-in-class AR (loot-only).*
After the May 2024 buffs Facepunch literally called it "the best in class AR" — **reduced horizontal recoil, higher bullet velocity, less damage falloff.** The spray is the **cleanest vertical with only a slight zigzag.**
- **Compensate:** mostly a smooth **downward pull**, minimal horizontal correction. If you can control an AK you'll feel like you're cheating on the LR.
- **Doctrine:** can be sprayed harder than the AK at mid-range; still burst at distance. The catch — it's **not craftable** (loot/tech-tree only), so the AK stays your reliable ceiling. Excellent long-range AR when you find one.

### [[MP5A4]] — *Easy. The training wheels and a real close-mid gun.*
Low recoil, a **minimal leftward Z-shape.** 
- **Compensate:** light downward pull, keep tracking the center. Very forgiving.
- **Doctrine:** the gun to **learn burst control on first** — fast feedback, low bloom. Strong close-to-mid weapon in its own right; tap/burst it and it's laser-accurate. Skip the muzzle brake (unnecessary); run [[Holosight]] + laser.

### [[Thompson]] (Tommy) — *Medium. Cheap close-range workhorse.*
**Vertical climb with a random zigzag** — more horizontal chaos than the MP5, and bloom-heavy at distance.
- **Compensate:** strong **downward pull**, and accept that the horizontal is partly random — don't over-correct sideways, just keep it centered and let bursts do the work.
- **Doctrine:** a **close-proximity** gun. It's cheap and effective in tight base/monument fights but falls apart past mid-range as bloom opens up. One of the best early-wipe power-spikes (see [[Solo Survival Guide]]).

### [[Custom SMG]] — *Easy. The hose.*
After its buffs (30-round mag, tightened aimcone, more center-fire hits) it's a brutal close-range SMG. Spray climbs **up and drifts fast to the right.**
- **Compensate:** **down + slightly left** to counter the up-right drift. Fast fire rate means you correct quickly.
- **Doctrine:** **point-blank spray** weapon. High DPS in your face; bloom kills it at range. Run laser + handmade/holo sight.

### [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] (SAR) — *Medium. Pure tap-fire skill.*
Semi-auto: **no spray pattern to fight.** Each pull kicks up; the gun recovers and you re-aim for the next shot. It's a **rhythm + crosshair-placement** test, not a spray test.
- **Compensate:** small downward correction after each shot to bring the dot back onto the head, then fire again. Find the fastest cadence where each shot is still *accurate*, not the fastest you can click.
- **Doctrine:** mid-range headshot machine on a budget; the bridge weapon between primitives and a full AR. Run a [[Holosight]] and focus on consistent taps. Great for solos who can't yet control an AK.

### [[M249]] — *Medium. Sustained-fire angle holder (loot-only).*
100-round belt. Recoil is comparatively **mild — slight straight-down with a minor right pull.**
- **Compensate:** small **downward** adjustment, minimal horizontal correction. The recoil is easy; the challenge is that it's heavy and loot-only.
- **Doctrine:** best for **holding a static angle / suppressing** (raids, defending) where the huge belt and low recoil shine; clumsy for aggressive roaming. You can't craft it, so treat it as a found bonus, not a plan.

**Quick reference — dominant correction by gun:**

| Weapon | Difficulty | Spray tendency | Primary correction |
|--------|-----------|----------------|--------------------|
| [[Assault Rifle]] (AK) | Hard | Up, then S-drift | Hard down + zigzag against drift |
| [[LR-300]] | Easy | Clean vertical, slight zigzag | Smooth down |
| [[MP5A4]] | Easy | Minimal left Z | Light down |
| [[Thompson]] | Medium | Vertical + random zigzag | Strong down, center it |
| [[Custom SMG]] | Easy | Up-right fast drift | Down + slightly left |
| [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] (SAR) | Medium | N/A (semi) | Small down between taps |
| [[M249]] | Medium | Slight down, minor right | Small down |

---

## Peeking, jiggle-strafing & movement in a fight

The May 2024 change means **you can shoot while moving** — so the best players are never standing still in the open.

### Jiggle-strafing (A-D spam)
Tap A then D (and back) to make your model jerk side to side. This **breaks the enemy's tracking** — their crosshair lags behind your model, so their bullets land where you *were*. Combine with **tap-firing** (which stays accurate while moving) so you're dodging *and* dealing damage. Against a player holding still and full-auto'ing, a controlled jiggle-strafe burst will usually win.

### The peeker's advantage
The player who initiates the peek sees the held player **before** the held player sees them (network/latency favors the mover). Use it: **wide-swing** a held angle when you're ready to commit, get your first burst off, then **re-peek** rather than sitting in their crosshair. Don't hold angles passively against an aggressive peeker — bait their swing, then punish the reset.

### Crouch-peek vs jump-peek
- **Crouch-peek:** poke a head over cover, tap, drop back — minimal exposure, good for SAR/snipers and trading.
- **Jump-peek:** vault out to gather info on a held angle without committing your feet to open ground. Don't try to *shoot* mid-jump (cone is wide); use it to *spot*, then swing properly.

### Sound cues — fight with your ears
Per the Sep 2025 change, gunshots carry a **fixed range by weapon class** (~400m quiet / ~500m rifles / ~600m loud — see [[Combat Mechanics]]). You are **louder than you think**: one AK burst can pull roamers from two grids over and invite a third party. Practical habits:

- **Wear a headset** and learn to triangulate footsteps, reloads, eating, and building sounds. Half of winning a fight is knowing where the enemy is before you see them.
- **Use [[Silencer]]s** (craftable since Jun 2025) when you want to take a fight without summoning the whole server — a major solo/duo tool for avoiding third parties.
- Listen for the enemy's **reload** — that's your free re-peek window.

---

## The train-server practice routine

You don't learn recoil in real fights — you lose kits doing that. Learn it on an **aim/recoil training server** (search the server browser for "ukn", "aim", "aimtrain", or "ffa"; UKN.gg and "Perfect Aim Train"-style ranges are the standard). These give you free guns, recoil walls, dummies, fixed-distance duels, and FFA.

**Why a train server:** instant kits, a wall to read your own bullet holes, stat tracking, and consistent reps — none of which a vanilla wipe gives you.

### Daily warm-up (15–25 min before you play your real server)
1. **5 min — spray walls.** Empty mags into a wall at a fixed distance and *look at the grouping*. Adjust your downward/horizontal pull until the holes cluster tight. Do MP5 → LR → AK.
2. **5 min — burst control.** Same wall, but practice **4–6 round bursts with a reset** between each. This is the rhythm you'll actually use in fights.
3. **5 min — duels / fixed-distance.** Apply it under pressure on moving targets.
4. **5–10 min — FFA.** Real movement, peeking, jiggle-strafe reps, target acquisition.

### Skill-progression ladder (over weeks)
1. **[[MP5A4]]** — learn burst control and reset rhythm (low bloom, fast feedback).
2. **[[LR-300]]** — clean vertical tracking; build the "pull down smooth" motion.
3. **[[Assault Rifle]] (AK)** — the hard vertical + S-drift; this is the real grind.
4. **[[Thompson]] / [[Custom SMG]]** — chaos/close-range reps so you're comfortable when a fight collapses to point-blank.
5. **[[Semi-Auto Rifle]] (SAR)** — tap-fire cadence + headshot consistency on a separate day.

### What "good" looks like
- You can put an AK burst into a tight head-height group at ~30m **while strafing.**
- Your crosshair is *already* at head height when targets appear; you correct onto heads, not search for them.
- You instinctively **burst-and-reset** at range and only hold the trigger point-blank.
- You jiggle while you shoot instead of standing still.

---

## Returning-player cheat sheet

If you only remember five things:

1. **Burst, don't hold.** The cone blooms after ~4 shots; tap/burst stays accurate, full-auto is point-blank only. (May 2024 overhaul.)
2. **Crosshair at head height, always.** 2x headshot damage is the whole game.
3. **Move while you shoot.** Movement no longer wrecks tap accuracy; jiggle-strafe to dodge.
4. **Lock one sensitivity + FOV 90 + raw input, then grind a train server.** 20 min warm-up before every session.
5. **You're loud — use silencers and your ears** to control who joins your fights.

---

## Cross-links

[[Rust Weapons]] · [[Combat Mechanics]] · [[PvP Tips]] · [[Weapon Attachments]] · [[Ammo]] · [[Armor]] · [[Settings and Binds]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[Meta Madness Update]]

Sources: rust.facepunch.com/news/meta-madness (aimcone overhaul specifics), rustmods.com/rust-recoil-patterns (per-weapon patterns + current-system framing), wiki.facepunch.com, rustafied.com, aim-training-server guides (UKN/training routines), Rust sensitivity/FOV community references. Numbers cross-referenced to the [[Rust Weapons]] and [[Combat Mechanics]] reference pages — see those for full stat tables.

# Rust Guides

The strategy/how-to layer on top of the reference wiki.

## Wipe Playbooks
- [[Solo Wipe Guide]] — A comprehensive full-wipe-arc strategy guide for solo (scaling to duo/trio) PC players on a populated 2026 vanilla server — the decision/sequencing layer on top of the existing Rust reference pages, current to the June 2026 "Built Different" update.
- [[Duo & Trio Wipe Guide]] — A long, decision-focused strategy guide for 2-3 players on a 2026 vanilla server — role splits, shared-TC base design, parallelized tech-tree rush, group roams/monuments/events a solo can't take, and full group-raiding logistics — cross-linked heavily to existing reference pages instead of re-listing tables.

## Combat
- [[Recoil & Aim Mastery]] — New long-form strategy guide teaching the modern Rust recoil/aimcone system, per-weapon spray compensation, settings, peeking/movement, and a train-server practice routine for returning solo/duo/trio players.

## Raiding
- [[Raiding Playbook]] — New comprehensive end-to-end raiding strategy guide for returning solo/duo/trio players, built as the decision/execution layer on top of the existing raid reference pages.
- [[Base Defense & Counter-Raid Playbook]] — A long-form strategy guide on the "how to actually defend" layer for solo/duo/trio players: defensive design philosophy, anti-offline measures, turret/trap layouts, online breach-holding, third-partying, and raid-base denial, cross-linked heavily to existing rust reference pages.

## Economy
- [[Scrap & Economy Optimization]] — New in-depth strategy guide on maximizing scrap + components per hour and sequencing a wipe-long economy, current to the June 2026 "Built Different" wipe.
- [[Monument Roam Routes]] — A returning-player strategy guide for which monuments to hit, in what order, and when — organized by goal (scrap, components, guns, riches, events) for solo/duo/trio on a populated 2026 vanilla server, sitting on top of the existing reference pages and the [[Card Run Routes]] keycard ladder.
- [[Progression Speedrun]] — A long, sequencing-focused wipe-day strategy guide taking a returning solo/duo/trio from naked spawn to a full AK kit, built on the vault's established 2026 "Built Different" canon (cheap research, Blueprint-Fragment-gated benches) and cross-linked heavily to existing reference pages.

## Base Building
- [[Full Base Automation]] — A long, end-to-end strategy guide for wiring a solo/duo/trio base to run itself on a 2026 vanilla server: power budgeting, source mix, auto-turrets with backup power, smart alarm + Rust+, auto-furnace line, industrial sorting + auto-crafting, bunker auto-door, and a sprinkler farm — sequenced into one build order with per-module power budgets and a worked trio example.
- [[Group Base & Compound]] — A long quad+ group-basing strategy guide (compound walls/externals, shooting floors, multi-TC honeycomb, role-based storage/auth, FOB staging, and defending a big footprint), layered on top of the existing reference pages with heavy [[wikilinks]] and verified June-2026 numbers.

## Lifeskill
- [[Farming Empire]] — A long, sequenced strategy guide for self-sufficient farming — genetics min-maxing to a god-seed clone stash, an automated planter/light/water/composter loop, the tea production priority line, food independence, and the scrap-tea barrel loop — built for a returning solo/duo/trio on a 2026 vanilla server and cross-linked heavily to existing reference pages.

## PvE
- [[PvE Mastery]] — A long, decision-focused strategy guide for soloing/duoing every Rust AI loot target (Bradley, Patrol Heli, both Oil Rigs, Cargo Ship, free-roaming Chinook crate), built as the "how to actually play" layer on top of the existing event reference pages, with a wipe-progression sequence at the end.

pages.title: Scrap & Economy Optimization
pages.body:
# Scrap & Economy Optimization

The "how to actually play the economy" layer that sits on top of the reference pages. This is about **sequencing and decision-making**: which route to run at which hour of wipe, what to recycle vs craft vs sell, and how to turn a pile of [[Components]] into a [[Tech Tree]] timeline that gets you to guns and explosives before the server's groups do.

Numbers here are pulled in for context, but the **full tables live on the reference pages** — [[Scrap]], [[Recycling]], [[Components]], [[Scrap Runs]], [[Barrels and Crates]], [[Vending and Shops]] — and those are the ones verified against rusthelp.com / rustmods (June 2026, "Built Different" wipe). When a number and a reference page disagree, trust the reference page.

> **The one mental model that matters:** scrap is not the goal. Scrap is the *throttle* on three timelines running in parallel — your **bench timeline** (WB1 → WB2 → WB3, gated by [[Blueprint Fragments]]), your **gun timeline** (rock → bow → revolver → SAR/Thompson → AK), and your **boom timeline** (eoka shells → satchels → C4/rockets). Every hour you should know which of the three is your current bottleneck and farm the input that unblocks it. Farming scrap with no plan for what it unblocks is the #1 returning-player mistake.

---

## Part 1 — The two currencies, and why "scrap/hr" lies

A returning player thinks in raw scrap. The 2026 economy actually runs on **two** currencies that you farm from the same containers:

1. **Scrap** — buys [[Tech Tree]] unlocks, keycards, vehicles, and safe-zone gear. The currency of *progression speed*.
2. **Components** — the *physical* gate on crafting. You can have 5,000 scrap and still not be able to craft an AK if you have no [[Rifle Body]] and no springs. Components also recycle *into* scrap, so they're a convertible reserve.

The trap in every "best scrap farm" YouTube title is that the highest scrap/hr route is often **not** the route that unblocks your current timeline. A [[Junkyard]] crane loop prints scrap but almost no rifle bodies or tech trash. The [[Train Tunnels]] dweller loop prints components (springs, blades, semi bodies) that *are* AK and SAR inputs. Pick the route by **what you need next**, not by the headline number.

See [[Scrap]] for the full "what scrap buys" sink list and [[Components]] for the recycle-yield table.

---

## Part 2 — Ranked scrap-run routes (solo vs group)

These are relative rankings. Per-hour figures are community estimates (rustmods 2026, mirrored on [[Scrap Runs]]) — treat them as a ladder, not a guarantee. **Every route below assumes you end at a monument recycler**, which pays ~50% more than a safe-zone recycler (the May 2024 split — see [[Recycling]]).

### Solo ladder (lowest risk → highest)

| Rung | Route | ~Scrap/hr | What it actually gives you | When to run it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Road + [[Roadside Junk Piles]] loop | 800–1,500 | Scrap + early components + frags; near-zero PvP | Hour 0–2, and any time you're under-geared |
| 2 | Sea trash / ocean barrel run | 800–1,200 | Scrap + low-tier comps; safest on a populated server | When the roads are camped |
| 3 | [[Junkyard]] crane shred loop | 800–1,500 | Pure scrap + frags; almost no top comps | Mid-wipe when you have LGF to spare and need scrap, not parts |
| 4 | [[Train Tunnels]] dweller + crate loop | 1,500–2,000 | **The component workhorse** — springs, blades, semi bodies, mil crates | Once you have a SAR/revolver + 100 rounds |
| 5 | Passive [[Fishing]] traps (overnight) | 1,500–2,000 (overnight) | Scrap via gutting fish (~20% × scrap) | Set before logout; free money while you sleep |
| 6 | [[Missile Silo]] (red-card) | 1,200+ | Scrap + Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] | When you hold a red card and a hazmat |

**Solo doctrine:** rungs 1–3 keep you alive and fund the early bench climb. The jump to rung 4 (tunnels) is the single biggest solo income upgrade once you can defend yourself, because it converts directly into gun parts. Avoid [[Launch Site]] and Arctic solo on a populated 2026 server unless it's dead hours — you'll get third-partied and lose the run *and* the kit.

### Duo ladder

| Rung | Route | ~Scrap/hr | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Monument triangle (Harbor → [[Ferry Terminal]] → local radtown) | ~1,500 | One loots, one guards the recycler. The duo classic. |
| 2 | [[Launch Site]] barrel yard + crates | 1,500–2,000 | 28 yellow + blue barrels, big crate density; now efficient post-rework but high PvP |
| 3 | [[Train Tunnels]] split (one clears, one carries) | ~2,000 | Doubles tunnel throughput; carry mil crates to surface recycler |
| 4 | [[Small Oil Rig]] | event-tier | Treat as a PvP event, not a farm — locked crate + elite, ~scrap-dense but contested |

**Duo doctrine:** the recycler-guard split is the whole game. The bottleneck on every duo run is *recycle time standing still at a public recycler*; one player holding the angle while the other feeds the machine roughly doubles safe throughput. Buy a [[Minicopter]] (750 scrap) the moment you can — it converts the triangle loop from 20 min into 8 and lets you contest airdrops.

### Trio ladder

| Rung | Route | ~Scrap/hr | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [[Arctic Research Base]] | 2,500–3,000 | Highest sustained farm in the game for a coordinated trio; also a free Snowmobile + red card |
| 2 | Locked-crate contests (Cargo / Oil Rig / Chinook) | event-tier | A trio can actually hold these. 33% chance of 140–159 scrap per locked crate + Advanced frags |
| 3 | [[Launch Site]] full clear (Bradley → crates → puzzle) | very high | Needs the firepower to kill [[Bradley APC]] (7 HV rockets / 3 C4); pays the most loot in the game |

**Trio doctrine:** a trio's edge isn't scrap/hr on barrels — it's the ability to **hold contested space**. Once you can clear Arctic and contest a locked crate, your scrap income stops being the bottleneck and your *boom* timeline becomes the limiter. Shift farming effort toward sulfur (see Part 6).

---

## Part 3 — Component priorities: the "never recycle these" list

The recycle-yield numbers are on [[Components]] (monument vs safe-zone columns). Here's the *decision layer* on top of them — what to hoard, what to feed the machine, and why.

### Tier S — hoard, almost never recycle early/mid wipe
- **[[Rifle Body]]** — the gate on the AK (1 body + 50 HQM + 200 wood + 4 springs) and bolt action. Also the single highest scrap component (30 at a monument recycler) — so it's your "emergency cash" reserve, but recycling one is recycling an AK. Hold until you have a confirmed surplus.
- **[[Metal Spring]]** — every spring gun needs them (AK ×4, MP5/SKS ×2, SAR/Thompson ×1). Springs are the quiet bottleneck that stalls more gun timelines than rifle bodies do. Hoard hard.
- **Tech Trash** — gates night-vision, the industrial line, and the timed-explosive chain. 24 scrap each at a monument (best scrap-per-slot of the common comps), so it's also great cash — but if you're heading to C4, you'll want a stack. Recycle only your surplus.
- **Gears** — armored doors and ladder hatches need 5–6 each; you'll burn a shocking number making your base raid-resistant. Also feeds turrets/traps later.

### Tier A — situational; recycle once your craft needs are met
- **SMG Body / Semi-Auto Body** — keep enough to build the SMG/SAR you want, recycle the rest. Semi bodies also dump 90 frags on recycle, handy for frag-starved early wipe.
- **Metal Pipe** — rockets, salvaged tools, bolt action. Cheap to also just *buy* at [[Outpost]] (30 scrap), so don't over-hoard; recycle spares.
- **Sheet Metal** — high external walls + heavy armor. Recyclable for 120 frags, which is real metal-frag income early.

### Tier B — recycle on sight (unless a specific build is queued)
- **Metal Blade, Road Signs, Empty Propane Tank, Sewing Kit** — niche craft uses. Recycle for scrap/cloth/frags unless you're actively building roadsign armor or a flamethrower.
- **[[Electric Fuse]]** — the eternal *exception*. Worth 24 scrap recycled, but fuses are the bottleneck for green/blue keycard puzzle runs. **Never recycle a fuse until you're done puzzling for the session.** A fuse you recycle is a Blue Keycard puzzle you can't run.

### Tier C — convert, don't hold
- **Rope / Tarp** — recycle into cloth (tarp = 60 cloth at a monument, the best cloth-per-slot source in the game). Cloth feeds bandages, hazmat, sleeping bags.

---

## Part 4 — Recycle vs craft vs sell: the decision rules

This is the heart of "playing the economy." Three rules cover ~90% of decisions:

**Rule 1 — Recycle when the scrap value beats the craft value *and* you don't need the part.**
A [[Rifle Body]] recycles for 30 scrap. If you don't need an AK *and* you don't need 30 scrap toward a specific [[Tech Tree]] unlock, you're just hoarding clutter — recycle it. But if 30 scrap doesn't unblock a timeline, the body is more valuable *as a body* (an AK is worth far more than 30 scrap). The test: **"Does this exact scrap amount finish something I'm waiting on?"** If yes, recycle. If no, hold the component — it's a more flexible reserve.

**Rule 2 — Craft when you have the components *and* the recipe is cheaper than buying the equivalent.**
Buying a [[Minicopter]] is 750 scrap and you can't craft one — clear case for buying. But buying components at [[Outpost]] (Gears 125, Spring 60, Pipe 30) is almost always worse than looting them; use Outpost component buys only to *finish* a craft you're one part short on, never as a primary source. Buying a Spring for 60 scrap to complete an AK you're otherwise sitting on is correct; buying 4 springs at 60 each is throwing money away.

**Rule 3 — Sell (or trade) when the item is demand-priced *above* its scrap value, or when scrap is your bottleneck.**
The classic 2026 arbitrage is the **Bandit Camp scope/HQM cycle**: buy a Scope, recycle it for ~48 HQM, sell the HQM back at Bandit for ~192 scrap — net ~+42 scrap per ~30-second cycle (rustmods 2026). It's tedious but it's the highest scrap/hr in the game if you have nothing better to do and need pure scrap. More generally: NPC prices **float with demand** since July 2024 (see [[Vending and Shops]]) — the [[Outpost]]/[[Bandit Camp]] core catalog is stable, but the **Travelling Vendor** and **Floating City** shops swing widely. Comparison-shop the floaters; rely on Outpost/Bandit for predictable buys.

> **The recycle-everything-on-site rule:** standing at a public monument recycler with a full inventory of components is the most dangerous you'll be all wipe. Recycle *as you go* — feed the machine the moment you pass one — so you're never carrying a wipe's worth of loot through a contested monument. Scrap stacks to 1,000 and is forgettable to lose; a backpack of un-recycled rifle bodies is a kill someone will fight for.

---

## Part 5 — Vending-machine flipping (the player economy)

Once you have a base and a couple of vending machines, you become a node in the **Drone Marketplace** (terminals at [[Outpost]] and [[Bandit Camp]] let any player buy from any vending machine map-wide — see [[Vending and Shops]]). This is passive scrap income while you're offline.

**What sells reliably (in rough order):**
1. **Bulk resources** — stone, wood, frags, sulfur, HQM in round stacks at a small markup over the Outpost exchange rate. Boring, always sells, zero risk.
2. **Components** — pipes, gears, springs. Other players hate farming these as much as you do.
3. **Ammo and gunpowder** — mid-wipe, geared players buy ammo by the stack. High margin if you have a sulfur engine.
4. **Low grade fuel / diesel** — vehicle and excavator fuel; steady demand.
5. **Keycards / fuses** — convenience buyers who don't want to puzzle.

**Flipping mechanics:**
- **Buy low at floating vendors, resell at your machine.** When a Travelling Vendor dumps Jackhammers below the 150 Outpost price (~92 on a good day), buy and resell.
- **Price just under Outpost** on anything Outpost sells (tools, components) so the Drone Marketplace routes buyers to you instead — you undercut the safe-zone monopoly.
- **Run the machine near a monument you control** so you can restock it on your normal loop; a vending base nobody can reach by drone marketplace still works, but one near foot traffic also gets walk-up sales.
- **Don't overstock single items** — vending machines have limited slots; spread across 3–4 high-velocity goods rather than 30 stacks of one.

The casino at [[Bandit Camp]] is a **scrap sink, not income** — the wheel and slots have a house edge (~4%); the only +EV game is player poker if you're the better player (it's a scrap *transfer*, not generation). Treat gambling as entertainment you pay for, never as an economy plan.

---

## Part 6 — The wipe-long economy plan (tied to tech-tree goals)

This is the sequencing layer — what your scrap and components should be *funding* at each phase. It dovetails with [[Progression Route]] (the full naked-to-T3 path) but focuses on the *economic* decisions. The bench gates are the spine: [[Workbench Level 1]] → [[Workbench Level 2]] (needs 5 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]) → [[Workbench Level 3]] (needs 5 Advanced Fragments).

### Phase 0 — Hour 0 to first TC (first ~30 min)
**Goal:** base down, [[Tool Cupboard]] placed, sleeping bag.
**Economy:** road + [[Roadside Junk Piles]] barrels for instant scrap and the resources to build. Use the [[Outpost]] resource-exchange machines as a shortcut — recycle a road run's components, buy 1,000 stone for 50 scrap rather than hand-mining it. Don't tech-tree anything yet; everything you need (WB1, basic tools) is default-known.

### Phase 1 — WB1 up, Basic Fragments rolling (hour ~0.5–2)
**Goal:** WB1 (500 wood + 100 frags), then start banking **Basic Fragments** toward WB2's 5-fragment gate.
**Economy:** Basic Fragments drop from green/blue puzzle rooms and several monuments — **run green-card puzzles for the free fragments + the Blue Keycard they award**, rather than buying cards. A [[Green Keycard]] is 15 scrap at Bandit if you must, but [[Abandoned Cabins]] gives a free non-respawning one and most desks spawn them. This phase is **fragment-limited, not scrap-limited** — route toward monuments that pay fragments, not toward raw barrel scrap.

### Phase 2 — WB2 + first real gun (hour ~2–5)
**Goal:** WB2 unlocked, a [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] or [[Thompson]]/[[Custom SMG]] in hand.
**Economy:** now you need **components**, so the route shifts to [[Train Tunnels]] (springs, semi bodies, blades) and monument crates. Tech-tree costs are slashed (15/30/60/120 scrap per rarity tier — see [[Tech Tree]]), so unlocking the SAR/Thompson path is cheap; the limiter is the *physical* component + HQM. This is where you buy a **Jackhammer (150 at Outpost)** — the single biggest farming-speed upgrade, before you tech-tree better tools. A [[Minicopter]] (750) here transforms a duo's loop.

### Phase 3 — WB3 + AK/boom (hour ~5–12+)
**Goal:** WB3 (needs 5 **Advanced** Fragments + 100 HQM), AK online, sulfur engine running.
**Economy:** Advanced Fragments come from the hard monuments — [[Missile Silo]] (2 per run), Locked Crates, [[Launch Site]]. This is the phase where **solo and trio economies diverge hardest**: a solo grinds tunnels + silo and tech-trees carefully; a trio holds Arctic/locked crates and floods in fragments. Once WB3 is up, **sulfur becomes the master currency** — your scrap income is now mostly there to fund a [[Giant Excavator Pit]] / [[Quarries]] diesel run (Diesel = 300 LGF at Outpost) that prints the sulfur for [[Explosives]]. The boom timeline (~2,200 sulfur per C4 — see [[Raid Costs]]) replaces scrap as your limiter.

### Phase 4 — Established / sulfur economy (mid-to-late wipe)
**Goal:** raid income, defense, surplus.
**Economy:** at this point scrap is *abundant* and the questions become: how much sulfur per night can I refine (overnight furnace + quarry loop), how many turrets/SAMs can I fund for defense (Auto Turret 400, SAM 500 at Outpost), and what's my raid budget. Convert surplus scrap and components into a **vending engine** (Part 5) so your downtime earns. The wipe is now won on *boom volume and base defense*, not scrap/hr — but a thin scrap reserve is still what lets you re-kit after a death without re-grinding from naked.

---

## Part 7 — Multipliers and force-multipliers worth buying first

In rough ROI order for a returning solo/duo:

1. **[[Pure Scrap Tea]] (+barrel scrap)** — drink before **barrel/road runs** (it boosts *barrel* scrap, not recycler yield — don't waste it on a recycle loop). Cheap, big early multiplier. See [[Teas]].
2. **Jackhammer (150)** — doubles+ your gather speed across stone/metal/sulfur; buy before tech-treeing tools.
3. **[[Minicopter]] (750)** — converts every farm route's travel time; the duo game-changer.
4. **Recycler proximity** — build near a 2–3 recycler monument ([[Power Plant]] has 3, [[Sewer Branch]] has two 120% recyclers) so your loop ends at a recycler you control, not a camped public one.
5. **[[Giant Excavator Pit]] diesel run** — once you control the area; turns scrap → diesel → bulk sulfur/HQM faster than mining by hand.

---

## Quick-reference decision flowchart

```
Got loot at a monument?
  -> Recycle EVERYTHING except: rifle bodies, springs, tech trash,
     gears (hoard), and fuses (if still puzzling). Do it on-site.

Need scrap fast, nothing better to do?
  -> Bandit scope/HQM flip (~+42/cycle) or Junkyard crane loop.

Need GUN PARTS (springs, bodies)?
  -> Train Tunnels dweller loop, not the Junkyard.

Need BLUEPRINT FRAGMENTS (bench gated)?
  -> Run green/blue/red puzzles + hard monuments, not barrels.

Bench is up, AK is up?
  -> Pivot scrap into a diesel/quarry SULFUR engine. Boom is the limiter now.

Got a base + downtime?
  -> Run vending machines on the Drone Marketplace for passive scrap.
```

---

## Related
