pages.title: Solo Wipe Guide
pages.body:
# Solo Wipe Guide

The complete playthrough of a single wipe as a solo (the doctrine scales down to duo/trio — see the team notes throughout). This is the **decision layer** that sits on top of the reference pages: not "what does a sheet door cost" (that's [[Raid Costs]]) but *when do you stop farming and go contest a monument, when do you take a fight, when do you hide, and what do you actually do with the last 36 hours of the wipe.*

If you want the raw hour-0 checklist, read [[First Day Guide]] first and the dry tier-by-tier path in [[Progression Route]]. This page assumes you've skimmed those and want the **why and when**.

Current to the June 2026 **"Built Different"** update (player-model/armor/M16A2 drop — it changed no building HP, door HP, explosive damage, or raid costs, so every number cited below is live). Patches land the first Thursday monthly — re-verify against [[Rust Update History]] each wipe.

> [!important] The one mental model for the whole wipe
> Your wipe has **two currencies and one clock.** Scrap (cheap research, vehicles) and **Basic/Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]** (the only thing that unlocks WB2/WB3). The clock is the wipe length — typically 7 days on a monthly official, 3.5 on a biweekly. **Everything below is "where should I be on the clock."** A solo who is still farming barrels on day 3 has already lost; a solo who rushed AK on day 1 and got offlined on day 2 also lost. The art is the pacing.

---

## The wipe-arc at a glance

| Phase | Clock | Goal | Single most important thing |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Day 1** | first 0–6 hr | starter base + WB2 + first real gun | survive the spawn rush; lock a TC |
| **Day 1–3** | tech tree + T2 + monuments | fragment economy running, sulfur banked | get to WB3 before the server's geared players do |
| **Mid wipe** | ~day 3–5 | T3, AK, raiding *up*, defended base | turn your loot lead into someone else's loot |
| **Late wipe** | ~day 5–end | defense, hoarding, end-wipe plays | don't lose the wipe in the last night |

The rest of this page walks each phase as decisions, not just tasks.

---

## Day 1 — spawn to first roam (hour by hour)

Day 1 is a race against two things: the **spawn rush** (everyone is naked and aggressive, eokas and bows everywhere) and the **fragment gate** (you cannot tier up without monuments, so the sooner your base is safe the sooner you can leave it).

### Hour 0–1: don't die, get tools, mark the map

The literal opening is in [[First Day Guide]] — rock → [[Tool Recipes|stone tools]] → spear → bow, ~3,000 wood / ~1,500 stone, hit road barrels, ~200 cloth, drop a [[Deployables|Sleeping Bag]] at your build spot. The **decisions** that matter here:

- **Spawn beach triage.** If you spawn into a cluster of other nakeds farming the same nodes, *leave*. The first 20 minutes are kill-on-sight and you have nothing worth dying for. Run inland one grid square. A quiet spot beats a rich spot at hour 0.
- **Pick your biome deliberately.** Temperate/forest is the default safe solo home. **Avoid the jungle biome on wipe day** — tigers/panthers/crocs/snakes ([[Jungle Update]]) will end naked runs and the loot isn't worth it yet. **Avoid snow** unless you have clothing (cold is a real killer now — see [[Temperature and Cold]]). Coast near a [[Fishing Villages|fishing village]] gives a safe-zone recycler fallback.
- **Build near, not on, 1–2 small monuments** with a [[Recycling|monument recycler]] (monument recyclers = 5s cycle / ~120% yield; safe-zone ones are slower and 80%). [[Oxum's Gas Station]], [[Abandoned Supermarket]], [[Mining Outpost]] are ideal solo neighbors. See [[Base Locations]] for the "T1-monument ring" concept.

### Hour 1–2: the 2x1, the TC, the lock

Build the [[Starter Bases|2x1 stone with airlock]], TC inside and hidden, sheet-metal door + **[[Doors and Locks|Code Lock]] (100 metal frags)** as fast as humanly possible. Key locks get you killed; a code lock is non-negotiable. Furnace going, **[[Workbench Level 1]] (500 wood + 100 metal frags, no scrap)** placed.

Decision: **how much base on day 1?** Answer for a solo: *the minimum that holds your TC and one loot box through a casual offline.* You will rebuild and expand later. Over-building hour 2 is wasted stone you should be turning into a gun. A [[Solo Bases|2x1 → 2x2]] is plenty until you have something worth raiding.

### Hour 2–4: the fragment race begins

This is the phase returners get wrong. The instinct from old Rust is "grind scrap, tech-tree everything." **Scrap is no longer the gate.** Your two parallel jobs:

1. **Scrap** for research (15/30/60/120 by tier — see [[Tech Tree]]) and eventually a [[Minicopter]]/vehicle.
2. **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]** for WB2 — you need exactly **5**.

Basic Fragment sources (verified): a [[Green Keycard]] puzzle room = 1 fragment, a [[Blue Keycard]] room = 2, so a green→blue chain nets ~3 toward your 5. Plus medium/large monument crates, [[Airdrop|supply drops]], and — the solo's secret weapon — **roadside/junkpile scientists**, who drop fragments and whom *nobody fights you for.* See [[Card Run Routes]] for the optimized chains.

> [!tip] The solo's quietest path to WB2
> A bow + [[Handmade SMG]] roadside loop hitting junkpile scientists and a single green→blue puzzle at an off-peak hour can fund WB2 **without ever walking into Launch or Oil Rig.** You don't have to win the contested monuments to tier up — you have to avoid them.

### Hour 4–6: WB2 and your first real gun

**[[Workbench Level 2]] = 500 metal frags + 20 HQM + 5 Basic Fragments.** The moment you place it is the single biggest power spike of the early wipe. Tech-tree priority at WB2 for a solo (in order):

1. **[[Semi-Auto Rifle]]** or **[[Thompson]]** — your first reliable gun. SAR is the best-value mid-wipe snowball rifle; Thompson is the classic CQC kit-stealer. **[[Python Revolver]]** is the best sidearm and cheap.
2. **[[Doors and Locks|Sheet Metal Door]] + Garage Door + ladder hatch** — your base actually becomes a base.
3. **[[Medical Recipes|Medical Syringe]]** — staying alive in fights is loot.
4. **Road-sign + coffee-can armor** — see [[Armor]]; crafted armor takes 0–3 insert slots ([[Crafting Update]]) to tune projectile vs melee.

### First roam

Your first roam should be **defensive and opportunistic**, not a hunt. Hit your local monuments off-peak, take the free kills (nakeds at your monuments, lone farmers, anyone counting your garage doors), and *bank the loot in a stash before you push your luck.* The single most common day-1 death is the geared-too-early solo who roams with everything he owns and donates it to the first SAR he meets. See [[PvP Tips]] for fight selection.

---

## Day 1–3 — tech tree, T2 consolidation, monument farming

By now you have a defended starter base and a gun. The goal of this stretch is to **build the engine** — the income loop and tech base that gets you to WB3 before the server's tryhards.

### Tech tree priorities (what to unlock and in what order)

Research is cheap; the constraint is **scrap throughput, not scrap cost.** Don't tech-tree everything — tech-tree the path to power. Rough solo priority after the WB2 essentials above:

- **Salvaged tools** (Salvaged Pickaxe/Axe/Hammer) — 2–3x your farm speed; pays for itself in one farm session.
- **[[Explosive Recipes|Satchel Charges]]** — your first raiding tool and your first eco-raid entry. A satchel is your "I found a juicy 2x1" button.
- **[[Large Furnace]]** — overnight smelting; stops the metal-frag bottleneck.
- **[[Recipes-medical|Large Medkit]]** — solos who can full-heal mid-roam win attrition fights.
- **Vehicle scrap** banked toward a **[[Minicopter]] (750 scrap from Air Wolf)** — a solo's single best force multiplier for monument and airdrop racing.

### Monument farming as the income engine

Your scrap-per-hour ranking (community estimates, from [[Scrap Runs]]) — pick by what your gear and the server population support:

- **[[Train Tunnels]] + recycler loop (~1,500–2,000/hr, solo)** — the solo workhorse. Tunnel dwellers + wagon crates, ride the workcart, surface at a monument recycler. Bring 100+ rounds; dwellers rush in melee packs.
- **[[Junkyard]] shredder (800–1,500/hr)** — magnet-drop vehicles into the shredder; a stolen [[Attack Helicopter]] shreds for 500 scrap. Low-risk, has its own recycler.
- **Passive [[Fishing|fish traps]] overnight (~1,500–2,000)** — set traps before you log, collect at login. Free scrap while you sleep.
- **Local 3-monument triangle** ([[Harbor]] → [[Ferry Terminal]] → [[Radtown]]) — barrels on the way, crates inside, fragments and components, recycle on-site.

The duo/trio difference: a partner unlocks the **recycler guard** pattern (one loots, one holds the recycler) and makes Arctic Research Base (~2.5–3k/hr) and [[Cargo Ship|Locked Crate]] contests viable. See [[Scrap Runs]] for the full breakdown.

### Fragment timing — the off-peak doctrine

You can't out-fight a trio at [[Launch Site]] on wipe day. You out-*time* them. **Server-local 4–9 AM** is the solo's monument window: puzzles have reset, loot has respawned, and the geared players are asleep. If your real-life schedule lets you play a morning session, that's worth more than any gun. This is the single biggest lever a solo has and it's free.

### Sulfur, in parallel

Start mining **sulfur** the moment you have a gun to defend yourself with. Run a [[Mixing Table]] for gunpowder (30 charcoal + 20 sulfur → 10 GP) and bank a stack of **5.56** (10 frags + 5 GP → 3 rounds via [[Ammo Recipes]]). Sulfur is the late-wipe currency that decides whether you raid or get raided — start the pile early even if you don't spend it yet.

---

## Mid wipe (~day 3–5) — T3, the AK, and raiding up

This is where the wipe is won or lost. You have an income loop and a defended base; now you convert that lead into **other people's loot** before the server's groups outscale you.

### Advanced Fragments → WB3

**[[Workbench Level 3]] = 1,000 metal frags + 100 HQM + 5 Advanced Fragments.** The fragment math (verified): Advanced Fragments drop **×2 at ~100% from Locked/Hackable Crates** and at [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Missile Silo]], and [[Underwater Labs]]; Elite Crates only ~10% for ×1 (unreliable). **20 Basic combine into 1 Advanced** — possible but brutal (100 Basic for the 5 you need), so loot Advanced directly.

The solo plays for Advanced fragments, ranked by safety:

1. **[[Underwater Labs]]** — the lowest-PvP loot source in the game. Modular layouts, ~25 crates, sub entry. If you have a [[Submarines|sub]] or even a [[Diver Propulsion Vehicle|DPV]], this is the safest WB3 path.
2. **Small [[Oil Rig]] off-hours** — one hackable crate guarantees Advanced fragments, but **it floods with radiation ~30 min after the crate hack** ([[Pivot Or Die Update]]) — get in, hack, get out.
3. **[[The Dome]]** elite crates + the new green-card puzzle — climbable, often quiet.
4. **[[Launch Site]]** — top loot density but trio territory; only off-peak and only if you can leave fast.

### The AK and the kit ladder

**[[Assault Rifle]] (AK-47) = 50 HQM + 200 wood + 1 rifle body + 4 metal springs** at WB3 (rusthelp). It's the S-tier all-round roaming gun (50 dmg / 450 RPM). But the AK is not automatically your first WB3 craft — think about what you actually need:

- If you're **raiding**, the AK can wait; prioritize the boom (below).
- If you're **roaming/defending**, AK or **[[Bolt Action Rifle]]** (craftable T3 sniper, ~150 to the head + bleed) first.
- The **recoil is real** — the May 2024 aimcone means the first ~4 shots are accurate while moving, then it climbs. **Strafe-and-tap / burst beats spray.** See [[Combat Mechanics]] and [[PvP Tips]]. If you haven't practiced AK spray, the **SAR/Bolty/Thompson** may net you more kills than an AK you can't control.
- Chase items (loot-only): **[[LR-300]]** (lower recoil than AK), **[[MP5A4]]**/[[M249]]/[[L96]], and the new **[[M16A2]]** burst rifle + **[[Armor|Ballistic armor]]** from the Jun 2026 drop.

### Raiding up — the solo's raid doctrine

Raiding as a solo is about **picking targets you can crack cheaply and clear before the owner logs in.** The boom math you live by (full table in [[Raid Costs]], craft chains in [[Explosives]]):

- **Sheet metal door = 1 C4 (2,200 sulfur).** The most common target in the game.
- **Stone wall = 2 C4 (4,400) / 4 rockets.** Sheet metal wall = 4 C4. Always raid the *lowest-tier obstacle on the path to loot* — a sheet door beats a sheet wall every time.
- **TC = 100 HP = 8 explosive 5.56 (200 sulfur).** Most of a raid's cost is just *reaching* the TC; take it and you place your own and peel the base from inside.
- **Soft-side everything.** Inner walls cost ~25% less from inside.

Solo raid target selection:

1. **Eco-raid the soft ones first.** [[Eco-Raiding]] — eoka/satchel/fire/beancan entries on a 2x1 or an exposed door net you free loot at a fraction of C4 cost. A solo lives on eco-raids in the early-mid wipe.
2. **Scout before you commit.** Count the garage doors / external TC honeycomb to estimate the boom you'll need (rocket-count scouting). If you can't afford the whole path, don't start — a half-raid just arms the defender.
3. **Online vs offline.** As a solo, **offline raid** almost always. Online-raiding a base you can't out-DPS gets you third-partied. Use [[Rust+ Companion App]] alarms to learn a target's offline window over a day or two, then hit it.
4. **[[Bradley APC]] for the PvE bank.** 4–7 **HV rockets** to the rear/treads (1 metal pipe + 100 GP each) drops 3 crates of M249/L96-tier loot. The canonical cheapest Bradley kill — fund your WB3 trips with it.

> [!warning] The committed-raid trap
> The most expensive mistake a solo makes is starting a raid he can't finish. If the base is bigger than your scout estimate, **walk away with your sulfur.** A wasted raid is two losses: the sulfur *and* the loot you didn't get. Discipline on target selection is the whole game.

---

## Late wipe (~day 5 to end) — defense, hoarding, end-wipe plays

By late wipe the server has settled: the zergs have compounds, the dead have un-installed, and the survivors have boom. Your job flips from *acquiring* to *not losing what you have* — and then, in the final hours, spending it all.

### Defense — make yourself not worth raiding

A solo can't out-tank a group; you make your base **cost more to raid than it contains.** This is the [[Raid Defense]] doctrine:

- **Layers and spread loot, not one magic core.** Explosive protection caps at 75% ([[Crafting Update]]/[[Raid Methods]]) — there is no splash-proof bunker anymore. **Honeycomb** your loot rooms so the attacker has to break multiple stone walls (2 C4 each) just to reach boxes.
- **Spread your wealth.** A raider who pops your loot room and finds 1/3 of your stuff often leaves the rest unbroken. Keep ~40% of your wealth in **hidden external stashes** away from the base entirely — a buried stash with a gun + meds + sulfur is your insurance against a total offline.
- **Electricity** ([[Electricity Basics]]): [[Auto Turrets]] (mind the **12-per-40m interference cap**), a **Seismic Sensor** raid alarm (May 2026) → Smart Alarm → phone push via [[Rust+ Companion App]], and the free **Tin Can Alarm** tripwire on doorways. A solo who *knows* he's being raided can race home or counter; a solo who logs in to a hole in his wall has already lost. See [[Counter-Raiding]].
- **Bunkers** that still work: garage-door and ladder-hatch bunkers ([[Bunkers]]); classic stability bunkers are patched. Don't rely on a bunker as your only defense — it buys time, not immunity.

### Offline protection — the log-off checklist

Every time you log off late wipe:

- TC stocked for **24h+ upkeep** (exact brackets in [[Upkeep and Decay]]).
- Loot split across **2+ honeycombed rooms** + buried external stashes.
- [[Rust+ Companion App]] paired; Smart Alarm on the TC + Seismic Sensor armed.
- A **recovery bag** outside the base near a stash, so if you're raided you respawn *armed and outside* rather than naked in the rubble.
- On **Softcore** servers ([[Server Types]]) you keep 50% on death — if you're only half-committed this month, this is where to play and skip the paranoia entirely.

### Hoarding vs spending — read the clock

The classic late-wipe error is **hoarding boom you never spend.** Sulfur in a box on the last day of wipe is worthless — it vanishes at force wipe. The discipline:

- **Mid-late wipe:** keep a defensive reserve (enough boom to counter-raid or re-secure) and spend the rest on offense.
- **Final 36 hours:** stop hoarding. Convert everything to raids. The loot you take in the last night you don't even have to keep — you just have to *deny it to others* and have fun doing it.

### End-wipe plays — go out swinging

The last day is the most fun day if you stop playing scared:

- **Spend all your boom.** Raid the bases you scouted all wipe. End-wipe defenders are often AFK or checked-out — your offline-raid intel pays off now.
- **Contest the events you avoided all wipe.** [[Launch Site]] / [[Bradley APC]] / [[Patrol Helicopter]] / [[Cargo Ship]] — at end wipe the contest is thinner and a death costs you nothing.
- **Group bases as targets.** A solo with 20 rockets and nothing to lose can take a real bite out of a [[Group Bases|zerg compound]] on the last night. You won't crack the core, but the outer loot rooms are real.
- **Burn the chase items.** That [[L96]] or [[M249]] you've been hoarding "for the right fight" — the right fight is now. It wipes in a few hours either way.

---

## Risk management — the solo's decision rules

The thread through the whole wipe is **fight selection.** A solo loses by dying with loot, not by failing to find loot. The rules:

**Fights to take:**
- Nakeds and lone farmers at *your* monuments.
- Junkpile/roadside scientists (free fragments, no PvP risk).
- Anyone scouting/counting your base.
- A fair 1v1 where you have the gear and the angle — but only if losing it won't end your wipe.

**Fights to skip:**
- Wipe-day [[Launch Site]] and anything near a zerg compound.
- [[Attack Helicopter]] gunships (nerfed Nov 2025 but still deletes solos), [[Patrol Helicopter]] unless you can crash it cleanly.
- [[Deep Sea Event|Deep Sea]] event zones at peak hours.
- Any fight you're taking *because you're bored* while carrying loot you can't afford to lose.

**Disengage tech:**
- Gunshots are audible at **400/500/600 m** by weapon class ([[Combat Mechanics]]). A **silencer** (craftable since Jun 2025) genuinely shrinks your detection bubble while farming — it's a stealth tool, not a damage tool.
- **Don't roam at night with loot.** Night is actually dark now (the shader nightlight killed gamma cheating, [[Lighting The Way Update]]) and predators stalk. Bank before dark.
- **The bank-it reflex.** Every time you have loot and a stash within reach, *bank it.* The solo who banks twice as often as he thinks he needs to is the solo who still has gear on day 5.

---

## When to hide vs when to fight (the whole game in one table)

| Situation | Solo move | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Spawn rush, hour 0 | **Hide / relocate** | Nothing to gain, easy death |
| Junkpile scientist on the road | **Fight** | Free fragments, no real risk |
| Geared player at a contested monument, peak hours | **Avoid** | You can't win the third-party |
| Same monument, 5 AM server time | **Take it** | Off-peak is your window |
| Found a juicy undefended 2x1 | **Eco-raid it** | Cheap loot, your bread and butter |
| Big base, can't afford the full boom path | **Walk away** | Half-raids just arm the defender |
| Raid alarm fires while you're online | **Race home / counter** ([[Counter-Raiding]]) | Knowing = the whole advantage |
| Last 36 hours of wipe | **Spend everything, fight everyone** | Hoarded boom wipes to zero |

---

## Solo → duo → trio scaling

Everything above is the solo baseline. What changes with bodies (see [[Duo Bases]], [[Trio Bases]], [[Team System]]):

- **Duo:** one farms while one defends; recycler-guard farming; [[Research Table]] to share BPs (one researches the AK, hands out paper BPs). Arctic and Locked Crate contests become viable. Build a [[Duo Bases|2x2 open-core or stability-bunker]].
- **Trio:** twin-bunker or open-core [[Trio Bases|trio base]] with a shooting floor; you can offline-raid mid-size bases, hold a recycler indefinitely, and run two monuments at once. Mind the **40m turret interference cap** when you scale defenses.
- **The constant:** the *pacing* (day-1 base → fragment race → WB3 → raid up → defend → end-wipe spend) is identical at every team size. More bodies just compress the clock.

---

## Related

[[First Day Guide]] · [[Solo Survival Guide]] · [[Progression Route]] · [[Scrap Runs]] · [[Card Run Routes]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Raid Methods]] · [[Eco-Raiding]] · [[Raid Defense]] · [[Counter-Raiding]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Assault Rifle]] · [[Armor]] · [[PvP Tips]] · [[Combat Mechanics]] · [[Auto Turrets]] · [[Rust+ Companion App]] · [[Solo Bases]] · [[Base Locations]] · [[Wipe Schedule]] · [[Server Types]]

pages.title: Blue Keycard
pages.body:
# Blue Keycard

> "A keycard with medium level clearance."

The mid-tier card. Blue puzzle rooms hold the **[[Red Keycard]]** plus 2-3 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]], the best crate density per minute of any puzzle tier, and (since Oct 2025) they are the natural stepping stone to [[Workbench]] T2.

**Returning-player alert:** the Blue Keycard is **no longer sold at [[Outpost]]** (removed with the Meta Shift update, Oct 2025). It moved to [[Bandit Camp]].

## Item stats (rusthelp.com)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Short name | `keycard_blue` |
| Stack size | 1 |
| Despawn time (on ground) | 40 min |
| Swipes before breaking | ~4 (loses ~25% condition per swipe) |
| Item ID | -484206264 |

## How to get one

### Buy it
- **[[Bandit Camp]] vending machine — 40 [[Scrap]]** (10 s restock).

### Green puzzle rooms (100% spawn, the standard way)
One Blue Keycard sits in each of these green-card rooms (bring 1 [[Green Keycard]] + 1 [[Electric Fuse]]):

| Monument | Room also contains |
|---|---|
| [[Satellite Dish]] | 2 normal crates + 1 Basic Fragment |
| [[Sewer Branch]] | 9 crates (80/20 normal/military) + 1 Basic Fragment |
| [[The Dome]] | 2 normal crates + 2 diesel + 1 Basic Fragment (puzzle new Oct 2025) |
| [[Ferry Terminal]] | 2 normal crates + 1 Basic Fragment (new Oct 2025; no radiation) |
| [[Radtown]] | 2 **military** crates + 1 Basic Fragment (new Oct 2025) |
| [[Harbor|Harbor (Large)]] | 2 normal crates + 1 Basic Fragment |
| [[Harbor|Harbor (Small)]] | 1-2 crates + 1 Basic Fragment |

### Gutting fish (20% chance each)
Catfish, Orange Roughy, Salmon, and Small Shark each have a 20% chance to contain a Blue Keycard when gutted — a real alternative if you're [[Fishing]] off a [[Tugboat]] anyway.

## Where to use it

| Monument | What's behind the blue door | See |
|---|---|---|
| [[Water Treatment Plant]] | [[Red Keycard]] + 2 Fragments + 6 crates — **no green door, no NPCs** | best solo run |
| [[Train Yard]] | Red Keycard + 2 Fragments + 9 crates (50% military) | no green needed |
| [[Power Plant]] | Red Keycard + 3 Fragments + 8 crates + 5 barrels | needs green first |
| [[Airfield]] | Red Keycard + 2 Fragments + 7 crates | 2 fuses, 3 scientists |
| [[Arctic Research Base]] | 4 crates; Red Keycard on a box in the garage (no fuse needed) | 10 scientists |
| [[Military Tunnel]] | mid-stage door on the way to the red room | |
| [[Oil Rig]] / [[Large Oil Rig]] | 4 military crates (Large); antechamber to red room (Small) | reset ~65 min |
| [[Underwater Labs]] | blue rooms (most common lab puzzle tier) | layout procedural |

Full mechanics in [[Puzzle System]]; run order in [[Card Run Routes]].

## Tips

- 40 scrap at Bandit is cheap insurance; a failed green run (contested room, wasted swipes) costs more in time.
- Blue rooms **adjacent to red keycards** guarantee **2× Basic Fragments** — two Water Treatment/Train Yard runs nearly finishes your 5-fragment [[Workbench]] T2 requirement.
- Carry it in your hotbar, swipe only powered readers — 4 swipes per card.

pages.title: Card Run Routes
pages.body:
# Card Run Routes

Efficient green→blue→red chains for a solo and a duo, tuned for the **2026 fragment economy** (see [[Puzzle System]]). The goal of a card run is no longer just crates — it's **Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]] (5 = [[Workbench]] T2)** and **Advanced Fragments (5 = T3)**.

## The two golden shortcuts (know these first)

1. **[[Bandit Camp]] sells everything.** Green 15 / Blue 40 / Red 80 [[Scrap]], 10 s restock. **135 scrap = full card set.** If you have scrap, skip the ladder entirely. ([[Outpost]] no longer sells blue — changed Oct 2025.)
2. **Two blue puzzles need NO green card:** [[Water Treatment Plant]] (1 fuse + blue, zero NPCs) and [[Train Yard]] (1 fuse + blue, 3 switches). Buy a 40-scrap blue → walk out with a free [[Red Keycard]] + 2 Basic Fragments + 6-9 crates.

---

## SOLO ROUTE — "WTP loop" (lowest risk, ~1 hour to T2 materials)

**Kit:** 1 [[Blue Keycard]] (buy, 40 scrap) or run one green puzzle first; 2 [[Electric Fuse|fuses]]; burlap/wood armor; bow or pistol. Minimal rad gear (WTP max rad 26 — a snow jacket + pants tier is fine).

1. **Free green card:** hit [[Oxum's Gas Station]] / [[Lighthouse]] / [[Abandoned Supermarket]] / [[Abandoned Cabins]] — 100% desk spawns, no NPCs. (Skip if buying blue directly.)
2. **Green puzzle — pick the closest of:** [[Satellite Dish]] (1 switch, fastest), [[Ferry Terminal]] (no radiation, green card spawns on-site — a self-contained starter monument), or [[Radtown]] (2 *military* crates). Take: **[[Blue Keycard]] + 1 Basic Fragment** + crates.
3. **[[Water Treatment Plant]]:** wheel up the blast door, slot fuse upstairs, run the timer to the blue door. Take: **[[Red Keycard]] + 2 Basic Fragments + 6 crates + 3 diesel**. No scientists. This is the safest red-card printer in the game.
4. **Bank the red card** (despawns in 1 h on ground, forever in a box). Repeat steps 2-3 on the ~30 min [[Puzzle System|reset clock]] — **two loops = 6 Basic Fragments = T2 with one spare.**
5. **Spend the red(s)** once geared: solo-friendliest red room is **[[Nuclear Missile Silo]]'s hatch only if you're confident** (23 scientists, rad 81 — honestly a trio monument now); realistic solo picks are [[Underwater Labs]] red rooms (bring 2 fuses, fight 4ish dwellers, take 2-3 [[Elite Crate]]s + Advanced Fragments) or a quiet-hours [[Military Tunnel]] crawl (11 scientists on path — doable solo with a silenced gun and meds, all 3 cards + 1 fuse required).

**Scrap math if buying:** 40 scrap (blue) + ~0 (fuses from roadside barrels/crates) → red card worth 80 + ~6 crates + 2 fragments per 30-min loop.

## SOLO ALT — "Fisherman's blue"
Gutting Catfish/Salmon/Orange Roughy/Small Shark = 20% blue card each. If you're coastal with a rod, you can skip green entirely and feed the WTP loop with fish. Pairs naturally with a [[Tugboat]] life.

---

## DUO ROUTE — "Split ladder" (~90 min to a red room hit)

**Kit:** 2 green cards (30 scrap) + 1 blue (40) from [[Bandit Camp]], 4 fuses, rad gear for max-52 monuments, guns for the red leg. One player banks loot mid-route at base.

**Leg 1 — parallel greens (minute 0-20).** Split up: Player A runs [[Sewer Branch]] (9 crates — best green room), Player B runs [[The Dome]] or [[Satellite Dish]]. Yield: **2 blue cards + 2 Basic Fragments** + crates.

**Leg 2 — twin blues (minute 20-50).** Converge on the rail line: A hits [[Train Yard]] (blue only: red card + 2 frags + 9 half-military crates), B hits [[Water Treatment Plant]] (blue only: red card + 2 frags + 6 crates). Now holding: **2 red cards + 6 Basic Fragments → T2 done**, fragments to spare.

**Leg 3 — red room (minute 50-90).** Pick by server temperature:
- **[[Military Tunnel]]** — best duo value: 1 fuse + green + blue + red, 11 scientists you can leapfrog as a pair → **3 [[Elite Crate]]s + 2 Advanced Fragments**.
- **[[Launch Site]]** — 2 fuses + green + red, no NPC wall but rad 52 and the rocket-area parkour; 3 elites + 2 Advanced Fragments; watch for [[Bradley APC]].
- **[[Airfield]] add-on** — if you only got one red, run Airfield's blue puzzle on the way (2 fuses + green + blue) for a second red + 7 crates; 3 scientists die fast to a duo.
- **[[Oil Rig|Small Oil Rig]]** (boat + blue + red) — locked crate + elite, but the hack calls 6 [[Heavy Scientist]]s and every beach rat with a boat; duo-viable, loud. Rig floods with radiation 30 min after the hack starts.

**Leg 4 — optional silo.** With leftover reds and full kits, [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] is the highest-density red room in the game post-Oct-2025 (**4 elites + 2 Advanced Fragments + ~20 crates**) but budget for 23 scientists and rad 81 — treat it as a raid, not a loot run.

---

## Chaining rules of thumb

- **Respect the swipe budget:** green/blue = 4 swipes, red = 2. One card per planned monument + 1 spare green for the team.
- **Fuses:** carry 2× what the route needs ([[Airfield]] and [[Launch Site]] each eat 2 by design). Roadside barrels/normal crates restock you en route — see [[Electric Fuse]].
- **Read the doors:** open puzzle door = looted; check the next monument instead of burning the fuse ([[Puzzle System]]).
- **Reset clock:** ~30 min from first-loot, rad purge in the last 10 — never AFK inside a loot room.
- **[[Arctic Research Base]] cheese:** if your map has one, a single blue card (no fuse) opens the garage where a **free red card sits on a box** — 10 scientists, but a stealth grab is solo-viable.
- **Cards drop on death** like everything else (including from [[Backpacks|backpacks]]) — bank progress between legs.

pages.title: Electric Fuse
pages.body:
# Electric Fuse

> "An unreliable electric fuse. Will allow electrical passthrough for a period of time."

The consumable that powers every monument puzzle. No fuse = no power = the card reader does nothing (but **still eats keycard durability if you swipe it** — the #1 rookie mistake).

## Item stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Short name | `fuse` |
| Stack size | 10 |
| Despawn time (on ground) | 40 min |
| Burn time in an active fuse box | **~3 minutes (180 s)** of flowing current |
| Recycler yield | ~20 [[Scrap]] (one of the best single-item yields; monument [[Recycler]]s give 120%, safe-zone 80%) |
| Item ID | -629028935 |

The fuse is destroyed when its timer runs out. If you dawdle mid-puzzle the circuit dies and you need a fresh fuse — bring **2 minimum** for multi-stage monuments ([[Airfield]] and [[Launch Site]] *require* 2 by design; [[Underwater Labs]] red rooms need 2).

## Where to find them (rusthelp.com drop table)

| Source | Chance | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| [[Underwater Labs]] Tier 2 component crates | 26.53% | 1-2 |
| Normal crates (incl. wagon crates, underwater advanced crates) | 14.29% | 1 |
| Tunnel / Underwater Lab Dwellers | 7.43% | 1-3 |
| Scientists (various) | ~4.73% | 1 |
| Yellow / blue roadside loot barrels | 1.43% | 1 |

In practice: **road farming and train tunnels rain fuses** — most players have a stack by the time they have their first [[Green Keycard]]. They also show up constantly in sunken chests if you're diving.

## Used at

15 monuments wire fuses into their puzzles, including every monument in the [[Keycards & Monument Puzzles]] master table: [[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], [[The Dome]], [[Ferry Terminal]], [[Radtown]], [[Harbor]], [[Junkyard]], [[Train Yard]], [[Power Plant]], [[Water Treatment Plant]], [[Airfield]], [[Military Tunnel]], [[Launch Site]], [[Oil Rig]]s, and [[Underwater Labs]]. ([[Arctic Research Base]] and the [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] main doors are card-only — no fuse.)

## Fuse etiquette / tactics

- **Place the fuse, flip switches, THEN swipe.** Swipe order doesn't pause the 180 s burn.
- After looting, you can pull a still-live fuse back out of the box at some monuments — but the timer keeps whatever it burned; treat fuses as single-use.
- Recycling spare fuses at ~20 scrap each is real money early wipe — but always keep 2-4 in your base for [[Card Run Routes]].
- Fuse boxes are a known ambush point. Listen before you slot — the box hum and door motors are audible to campers.

pages.title: Green Keycard
pages.body:
# Green Keycard

> "A low level clearance card granting access to basic areas."

The entry ticket to the [[Puzzle System]]. A Green Keycard plus one [[Electric Fuse]] opens a green puzzle room, and **every green puzzle room contains a [[Blue Keycard]] and a guaranteed Basic [[Blueprint Fragments|Blueprint Fragment]]** — making green runs the standard early-wipe progression loop since the Meta Shift update (Oct 2025).

## Item stats (rusthelp.com)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Short name | `keycard_green` |
| Stack size | 1 |
| Despawn time (on ground) | 20 min |
| Swipes before breaking | ~4 (loses ~25% condition per swipe) |
| Item ID | 37122747 |

**Swiping an unpowered card reader still consumes durability.** Place the fuse and power the circuit *before* you swipe.

## How to get one

### Buy it (fastest)
- **[[Bandit Camp]] vending machine — 15 [[Scrap]]** (restocks every 10 s). At 15 scrap it is almost never worth detouring for a free one if you're already near Bandit.

### Free desk/table spawns — where greens actually drop (verified vs rusthelp, Jun 2026)
Greens spawn on desks/tables at **tier-0 and tier-1 monuments** — the safe, no-scientist places you visit anyway as a fresh spawn. This is the key returning-player fact: **you don't need to buy greens; the small monuments hand them out.**

| Monument | Tier | Count | Safety |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Oxum's Gas Station]] | 0 | ×1 (desk inside) | NPC-free, the classic fresh-spawn grab |
| [[Abandoned Supermarket]] | 0 | ×1 (back office) | NPC-free |
| [[Lighthouse]] | 0 | ×1 (top floor) | NPC-free |
| [[Abandoned Cabins]] | 0/1 | ×1 | NPC-free |
| [[Ferry Terminal]] | 1 | ×1 (also a puzzle reward) | no radiation, no scientists |
| [[Junkyard]] | 1/2 | ×1 (puzzle-tied — respawns on puzzle reset; **no reader to swipe**) | no radiation, no scientists |
| [[Power Plant]] | 3 | ×1 | no scientists (radiation instead) |
| [[Underwater Labs]] | mixed | ~×2 per lab | ~4 dwellers; needs a sub/DPV |
| [[Oil Rig|Small Oil Rig]] / [[Large Oil Rig]] | 2/3 | ×1 each (also re-appears in their green rooms) | heavy NPC presence |

**Easiest free green:** [[Oxum's Gas Station]], [[Abandoned Supermarket]], or [[Lighthouse]] — all NPC-free tier-0 monuments. Loot one on the way out of spawn and you have your first card before you've built a base. At 15 scrap a green is also trivially cheap at [[Bandit Camp]], so the rule is: grab the free one if a tier-0 is on your route, buy one otherwise.

### Scientist drops
| NPC | Chance | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| [[Military Tunnel]] / PT Boat / RHIB scientists | 36.34% | 1-3 |
| Outbreak Sprayer / Road scientists | 23.61% | 1-2 |

## Where to use it

Green doors/puzzles exist at: [[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], [[The Dome]], [[Ferry Terminal]], [[Radtown]], [[Harbor]] (both), [[Junkyard]], [[Train Yard]] (side route), [[Power Plant]] (first stage of the blue puzzle), [[Airfield]] (first stage), [[Military Tunnel]] (first stage), [[Launch Site]] (silo-area door), [[Oil Rig]]s, and [[Underwater Labs]].

The Dome, Ferry Terminal, and Radtown puzzles are **new since Oct 2025** — they didn't exist when you last played. See the master table in [[Keycards & Monument Puzzles]] and the run order in [[Card Run Routes]].

## Tips

- Buy 2 cards if you plan to chain green rooms — 4 swipes goes fast when half of them get wasted on unpowered readers.
- A green card on the ground despawns in 20 minutes; in your inventory it lasts forever (it drops on death like everything else, including from a [[Backpacks|backpack]]).
- Don't recycle keycards — their value is the doors.

pages.title: Keycards & Monument Puzzles
pages.body:
# Keycards & Monument Puzzles

The keycard system gates the best monument loot in Rust behind a three-tier color ladder: **[[Green Keycard]] → [[Blue Keycard]] → [[Red Keycard]]**, plus [[Electric Fuse|fuses]] to power the door circuits. Since the **Meta Shift update (Oct 2025)**, puzzle rooms are also the primary source of **[[Blueprint Fragments]]** — the items that gate [[Workbench]] Tier 2 and Tier 3 — so card running is now the backbone of progression, not just a loot grind.

## Pages in this folder

- [[Green Keycard]] — tier 1 card: spawns, vending, what it opens
- [[Blue Keycard]] — tier 2 card: green-room rewards, fish drops, vending
- [[Red Keycard]] — tier 3 card: blue-room rewards, endgame doors
- [[Electric Fuse]] — the consumable that powers every puzzle
- [[Puzzle System]] — how circuits, timers, resets, and the post-2025 radiation lockout work
- [[Card Run Routes]] — efficient solo and duo green→blue→red chains

## The ladder at a glance

| Tier | Get it from | Buy ([[Bandit Camp]]) | Swipes | Despawn (ground) | Opens doors at |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Green Keycard]] | Desk spawns at small monuments; scientists | 15 [[Scrap]] | ~4 (25%/swipe) | 20 min | Green puzzles (tier-1/2 monuments) |
| [[Blue Keycard]] | Green puzzle rooms; gutting fish (20%) | 40 [[Scrap]] | ~4 (25%/swipe) | 40 min | Blue puzzles (tier-2 monuments) |
| [[Red Keycard]] | Blue puzzle rooms | 80 [[Scrap]] | 2 | 60 min | Red rooms (tier-3 endgame) |

**Full buy-out: 135 scrap gets you one of each card at [[Bandit Camp]]** (10s restock each). [[Outpost]] no longer sells the Blue Keycard (removed with Meta Shift, Oct 2025).

## Master puzzle table (verified vs rusthelp.com, June 2026)

### Green puzzles — bring 1 [[Electric Fuse]] + 1 [[Green Keycard]]

All reward **1× [[Blue Keycard]] + 1× Basic [[Blueprint Fragments|Blueprint Fragment]]** plus crates; reset ≈30 min.

| Monument | Switches | Extra rewards | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Satellite Dish]] | 1 | 2 normal crates | Easiest first run |
| [[Sewer Branch]] | 1 | 9 crates (80% normal / 20% military) | Best crate count for a green run |
| [[The Dome]] | 1 | 2 normal crates + 2 diesel | Puzzle NEW Oct 2025 |
| [[Ferry Terminal]] | — | 2 normal crates | Puzzle NEW Oct 2025; no radiation; green card also spawns on-site |
| [[Radtown]] | 1 | 2 **military** crates | Puzzle NEW Oct 2025 |
| [[Harbor|Harbor (Large)]] | 1 | 2 normal crates | [[Harbor|Small Harbor]] has its own green puzzle + blue card too |
| [[Junkyard]] | 1 | crates + 2 diesel (no blue card) | Shredder building; green card spawn is puzzle-tied |
| [[Train Yard]] (green route) | 3 | 1 crate + 3 barrels + 1 fragment (no blue card) | Side route; resets ~immediately |

### Blue puzzles — yield the [[Red Keycard]]

All reward **1× [[Red Keycard]] + 2-3 Basic [[Blueprint Fragments]]**; reset ≈30 min.

| Monument | Bring | Extra rewards | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Water Treatment Plant]] | 1 fuse + **blue only** | 6 crates (80/20) + 3 diesel | **No green door, no NPCs** — best solo red-card source |
| [[Train Yard]] | 1 fuse + **blue only** | 9 crates (50% military) | 3 switches; rad max 26 |
| [[Power Plant]] | 1 fuse + green + blue | 8 crates (60/40) + 5 barrels + 3 diesel + **3 fragments** | 3 switches + timer; rad max 52 |
| [[Airfield]] | **2 fuses** + green + blue | 7 crates + 1 barrel + 3 diesel | 3 scientists on the route |
| [[Arctic Research Base]] | blue only (no fuse) | 4 crates; **red card sits on a box in the garage** | 10 scientists; 2nd blue door = snowmobile garage |
| [[Large Oil Rig]] (blue door) | blue only | 4 military crates | Reset ~65 min |

### Red rooms — endgame

| Monument | Bring | Rewards | Hazards |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[Military Tunnel]] | 1 fuse + green + blue + red | 3 [[Elite Crate]]s + 5 crates + **2 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments|Fragments]]** + 2 diesel | 11 scientists on the puzzle path |
| [[Launch Site]] | 2 fuses + green + red | 3 Elite Crates + ~24 crates + 2 Advanced Fragments | Rad max 52; 8 scientists; [[Bradley APC]] on road |
| [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] | red + button (hatch opens 20 s) | 4 Elite Crates + 2 Advanced Fragments + 20 military + 11 normal crates | **Red card since Oct 2025** (was blue); **23 NVG (heavy-class, ~300 HP) inside + 4 regular outside = 27**; rad max 81 |
| [[Oil Rig|Small Oil Rig]] | blue + red | [[Locked Crate]] + 1 Elite + 1 military crate + green card | 6 [[Heavy Scientist]]s on hack |
| [[Large Oil Rig]] (level 6) | red only | Locked Crate + 2 Elite + 4 military crates | 12 Heavy Scientists on hack; reset ~65 min |
| [[Underwater Labs]] (red rooms) | red + 2 fuses | 2-3 Elite Crates + Advanced Fragments | Lab dwellers; layout procedural |

## Why this matters for progression (2026)

- [[Workbench]] T2 = 5 **Basic** Fragments → green rooms guarantee 1 each, blue-rooms-next-to-red-cards guarantee 2 each. **Three green runs or ~two blue runs = T2.**
- Workbench T3 = 5 **Advanced** Fragments → red rooms, [[Elite Crate]]s (10%), hackable [[Locked Crate]]s (guaranteed), [[Cargo Ship]], CH47 drops.
- 20 Basic Fragments convert to 1 Advanced (fallback).
- Almost every monument's loot was **moved to new locations** in Oct 2025 — pre-2023 farming muscle memory is wrong.

pages.title: Puzzle System
pages.body:
# Puzzle System

How monument keycard puzzles actually work under the hood — circuits, timers, resets, and the **anti-camping radiation lockout added Nov 2025** (new since you last played).

## The components

Every puzzle is a small electrical circuit made of some mix of:

| Component | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Fuse box** | Takes 1 [[Electric Fuse]]; powers the circuit for **~180 seconds**, then destroys the fuse |
| **Switch** | Routes power down a branch; some puzzles need 1, [[Train Yard]]/[[Power Plant]] need 3 |
| **Timer switch** | Powers a branch for a short window, then cuts out — the "hurry up" element |
| **Button** | Momentary trigger (e.g. opens the [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] hatch for 20 s) |
| **Card reader** | Opens its door when powered AND swiped with the right [[Green Keycard|green]]/[[Blue Keycard|blue]]/[[Red Keycard|red]] card |

### Keycard durability per swipe
- Green/Blue: ~4 swipes (≈25% condition per swipe)
- Red: **2 swipes**
- **A swipe on an UNPOWERED reader still consumes durability.** Power first, swipe second. This is the single most expensive mistake in the system.

## Door state = loot intel

Puzzle doors **stay open until the puzzle resets**. Walking up to a monument:
- Door closed → room is probably stocked.
- Door open → someone beat you to it; loot respawns only on reset.

## Reset rules (reworked Oct-Nov 2025 — important)

The old behavior (timer freezes while players are nearby, 60 s cooldown after they leave) was abused by fragment campers after the Meta Shift update, so **Pivot Or Die (Nov 2025)** rewrote it:

1. **The refresh timer only starts once a player loots a container in the puzzle room.** Untouched rooms stay stocked indefinitely.
2. **The timer ticks down even if players stay in range** — you cannot body-block a reset anymore.
3. Standard reset time is **~30 minutes** after first loot (rusthelp lists ~30 m for nearly every puzzle; [[Oil Rig]]/[[Large Oil Rig]] rooms are **~65 minutes**; a few side-rooms like [[Train Yard]]'s green route and [[Water Treatment Plant]]'s secondary area reset near-instantly).
4. **10 minutes before the refresh**, the loot rooms and puzzle elements flood with **severe, unsurvivable radiation** (with a milder buffer zone around it) — the room is force-evacuated.
5. Once that radiation is active, the puzzle only resets after it has been **clear of players for a total of 5 minutes**. Then doors close, fuses/switches reset, and loot respawns.

Net effect: you can farm a puzzle on a ~30-minute loop, but you cannot live inside it.

## Fragment economy hook (why puzzles matter in 2026)

Since Meta Shift (Oct 2025), puzzle rooms are the progression path:

| Room type | Guaranteed [[Blueprint Fragments]] |
|---|---|
| Green puzzle rooms | 1× Basic |
| Blue rooms containing a [[Red Keycard]] | 2× Basic (3 at [[Power Plant]]) |
| Hackable [[Locked Crate]]s | 1× Advanced (guaranteed) |
| [[Elite Crate]]s | Advanced, 1-in-10 |
| Red rooms ([[Military Tunnel]], [[Launch Site]], [[Nuclear Missile Silo]], [[Underwater Labs]]) | 2× Advanced each |

[[Workbench]] T2 = 5 Basic, T3 = 5 Advanced; 20 Basic convert to 1 Advanced.

## General puzzle-running discipline

1. **Stage your kit:** card(s) + fuse(s) + rad protection (check the monument's max rad in [[Keycards & Monument Puzzles]]) + a weapon. [[Military Tunnel]] wants all three cards and serious gear.
2. **Scout the door state** before committing.
3. Slot fuse → flip every switch → run the timed leg → swipe. 180 s is generous if you know the route, brutal if you're reading switch labels.
4. Loot fragments and the next-tier card FIRST — if you get jumped, the card is the run.
5. Note the time; come back at reset +30 min. Solo loops in [[Card Run Routes]] are built around this clock.

## History

Puzzles arrived in the June 2018 "Puzzle Update" ([[Rustafied]] coverage). The Oct 2025 **Meta Shift** added new green puzzles at [[The Dome]], [[Ferry Terminal]], and [[Radtown]], moved the [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] to red clearance, reshuffled nearly every monument's loot positions, and removed the [[Blue Keycard]] from [[Outpost]]. Nov 2025 **Pivot Or Die** added the loot-triggered reset + radiation lockout described above.

pages.title: Red Keycard
pages.body:
# Red Keycard

> "A keycard with advanced clearance, grants access to top level areas."

The endgame card. Red rooms hold [[Elite Crate]]s, [[Locked Crate]]s, and **Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]]** — the items that unlock [[Workbench]] T3 (5 needed). Since Oct 2025 the [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] also requires red (it was blue when you last played).

## Item stats (rusthelp.com)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Short name | `keycard_red` |
| Stack size | 1 |
| Despawn time (on ground) | 1 hour |
| Swipes before breaking | **2** (half the green/blue durability) |
| Item ID | -1880870149 |

**Only 2 swipes.** A wasted swipe on an unpowered reader at [[Launch Site]] can end the run. Power first, swipe second.

## How to get one

### Buy it
- **[[Bandit Camp]] vending machine — 80 [[Scrap]]** (10 s restock). Full card set (green+blue+red) = 135 scrap total.

### Blue puzzle rooms (100% spawn)
| Monument | Bring | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|
| [[Water Treatment Plant]] | 1 fuse + blue card | **Easiest — no NPCs, no green door** |
| [[Train Yard]] | 1 fuse + blue card | 3 switches, rad max 26 |
| [[Power Plant]] | 1 fuse + green + blue | 3 switches + timer, rad max 52 |
| [[Airfield]] | 2 fuses + green + blue | 3 scientists on route |
| [[Arctic Research Base]] | blue card only — red sits **on a box in the garage** | 10 scientists, snow |

## Where to use it

| Monument | Red room loot | Hazards |
|---|---|---|
| [[Military Tunnel]] | 3 [[Elite Crate]] + 5 military/normal crates + **2 Advanced Fragments** + 2 diesel | 11 scientists on the path (33 on monument) |
| [[Launch Site]] | 3 Elite Crates + ~24 crates total + 2 Advanced Fragments | Rad max 52, 8 scientists, [[Bradley APC]] |
| [[Nuclear Missile Silo]] | 4 Elite Crates + 2 Advanced Fragments + ~20 crates + 3 diesel | 23 scientists inside + 4 outside, rad max 81; swipe + button opens the hatch for **20 s** |
| [[Oil Rig|Small Oil Rig]] | [[Locked Crate]] + 1 Elite + 1 military crate (+1 green card) | hack summons 6 [[Heavy Scientist]]s |
| [[Large Oil Rig]] (level 6, no fuse needed) | Locked Crate + 2 Elite + 4 military crates | hack summons 12 Heavy Scientists; reset ~65 min |
| [[Underwater Labs]] | 2-3 Elite Crates + Advanced Fragments (red rooms need **2 fuses**) | lab dwellers |

Oil Rig reminder: the rig floods with radiation **30 minutes after** the locked-crate hack starts — loot and leave.

## Strategy notes

- **Red ≠ rush.** The card despawns from the ground in 1 h but keeps forever in a box. Bank it at base, gear up properly (rad suit, guns, meds), then run [[Military Tunnel]] or the Silo.
- One fresh red card (2 swipes) covers a single red monument run; bring a second card if you intend to chain Small Oil Rig (blue door + red door) plus anything else.
- [[Military Tunnel]] needs **all three cards + 1 fuse** in one trip — pack everything before you commit.
- Cheapest pipeline for a solo: buy blue (40 scrap) → [[Water Treatment Plant]] → free red + 2 Basic Fragments. Repeatable every ~30 min reset. See [[Card Run Routes]].

pages.title: Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)
pages.body:
# Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)

**The "what's strong right now" snapshot for the June 2026 wipe cycle.** Patch = **[[Built Different Update|Built Different]]** (live Thursday June 4 2026). This page is written for a returning solo/duo/trio PC player and consolidates the weapon, armor, base, raid, and economy meta into one place.

> **Staleness gate:** Rust force-wipes the **first Thursday of every month**. The next force wipe is **Thursday July 2 2026**. Anything in this page tagged "meta verdict" should be re-checked after that wipe — but note Built Different changed **no building HP, door HP, or explosive damage**, so raid/base numbers carry forward until Facepunch ships a balance patch. All hard numbers below were verified June 13 2026 against rusthelp / wiki.facepunch.com / Rustafied.

---

## TL;DR — the meta in six lines

- **Run the same meta kit as before:** [[Metal Facemask]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]] + [[Road Sign Kilt]] + hoodie/pants. Ballistic gear is loot-only and *not* worth re-planning your wipe around.
- **[[AK-47|Assault Rifle]] is still king.** M16A2 is a fun loot find, not a meta-shifter — lower damage, burst-locked, can't be crafted.
- **Early game is still fragment-gated:** scrap is cheap, [[Blueprint Fragments]] are the bottleneck. Go to monuments early.
- **Cheapest raids unchanged:** 1 C4 = [[Sheet Metal Door]], 2 C4 = [[Stone Wall]]. Eco-raid with beancans/satchels solo.
- **Bunkers and honeycomb still standard** for solo/duo base survivability; nothing nerfed them this patch.
- **Watch out for:** Unity 6 mouse-polling FPS bug (drop to 1000Hz), and recalibrating headshots on the new player models.

---

## 1. What Built Different actually changed (and the meta impact)

Built Different is fundamentally a **feel / visual / loot patch**, not a balance patch. Full detail lives in [[Built Different Update]]; here's only what affects how you play *this wipe*.

### New player models + animations
- First full rebuild of the player rig in ~10 years: new proportions, faces, hair, re-fitted clothing, and a more natural angled aim stance (less robotic forward-facing pose).
- **Meta impact:** hitboxes feel slightly different and silhouettes read differently at range. The community is **still recalibrating headshots** — your muscle memory for "where the head sits" on a crouched/strafing target is off by a hair. Expect a few wipes of jank. This is the single biggest *PvP* consequence of the patch even though no stat changed.

### M16A2 (new rifle)
| Stat | M16A2 | [[LR-300]] (for comparison) |
|------|-------|------|
| Damage | **35** | 40 |
| Fire mode | **3-round burst only** | Full auto |
| Fire rate | 600 RPM | 500 RPM |
| Magazine | 30 | 30 |
| Ammo | 5.56 | 5.56 |
| Accuracy (lower=tighter) | 5 | 4 |
| Range | 368 | 422 |
| Attachment slots | 4 | 4 |
| Source | **Loot-only** (end-game crates) | Craftable |

**Meta verdict:** Strong mid-range *if you find one*, but it does **not** displace the [[AK-47]] or LR-300. Lower per-shot damage + a forced burst means it punishes whiffs harder and can't sustain spray duels. Treat it as a lucky pickup, not a build target. Detail: [[M16A2]].

### Ballistic armor set + BDU clothing (new, loot-only)
None of these can be crafted or researched — you only find them. Values verified vs the craftable standard:

| Piece | Projectile | vs craftable standard | Verdict |
|-------|-----------|----------------------|---------|
| Ballistic Helmet | **60%** | [[Metal Facemask]] = 50% | +10% head, but loot-only & can't replace reliably |
| Ballistic Vest | **35%** | [[Metal Chest Plate]] = 25% | +10% chest |
| Ballistic Leg Armour | **30%** | [[Road Sign Kilt]] = 20% | best legs in game |
| BDU Shirt | 23% proj | slightly > cloth tier | minor |
| BDU Pants | 17% proj | slightly > cloth tier | minor |

**Meta verdict — is it worth it?** As a *find*, yes — a full Ballistic kit is straight-up better than the metal meta kit and gives you the best legs available. But because it is **loot-only and non-replaceable**, you **cannot build your wipe around it**. The moment you die in it, it's gone and you're back to crafting metal. So: **wear it if you loot it, but the planned, repeatable meta kit is still [[Metal Facemask]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]] + [[Road Sign Kilt]].** See full breakdown in [[Armor]].

### Unity 6 + navmesh
- Engine upgraded to Unity 6; opt-in `-useNewNavmesh` gives smarter scientist pathing and lets **animals path into bases** (close your base properly).
- **Known bug with meta impact:** high-polling mice (1000Hz+) cause CPU overhead → frame drops/stutter. **Fix: drop your mouse to 1000Hz or below** in its software until Facepunch patches it. This is a real competitive disadvantage if you don't.

### Community backlash (context)
Built Different triggered a **1,604% review surge** (peak ~211 reviews/hour vs ~12 baseline) — driven by three things at once: forced face/identity changes, the loot-only gating of new gear (no craft path), and the Unity 6 mouse bug. None of this changes optimal play; it's sentiment, not balance. Most of it will settle by the July wipe.

---

## 2. Weapon meta tier list (this wipe)

Built Different changed no weapon stats except adding the M16A2. The tier list below is the **current verdict** — pull full stats from [[Rust Weapons]] and the per-gun pages.

| Tier | Weapon | Why this wipe |
|------|--------|---------------|
| **S** | [[AK-47\|Assault Rifle]] | Still the best all-round gun: 50 dmg, ~375 DPS, highest skill ceiling, end-wipe value. Wins fights in good hands. |
| **S** | [[Bolt-Action Rifle]] / [[L96]] | Long-range king. L96 if you find/research it; bolt is the craftable standard sniper. |
| **S** | [[Shotguns\|Pump Shotgun]] / M4 Shotgun | Close-range in-base Rust is still close-range Rust — rules base defense and breach. |
| **A** | [[LR-300]] | Tighter recoil / better velocity than AK; many prefer it for mid-range consistency. Loses per-shot to AK. |
| **A** | [[MP5A4]] | Best craftable SMG; strong mid/close once you hit WB3. |
| **A** | [[M249]] | Loot-only LMG; monster if you find it, can't plan around it. |
| **A** | [[M16A2]] | **NEW.** Strong mid-range *if looted*; burst-locked + 35 dmg keep it below AK/LR. |
| **B** | [[Thompson]] | Best cost-to-performance Tier-2 gun (~300 DPS, forgiving). The wipe-day workhorse. |
| **B** | [[Custom SMG]] / [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] | Solid bridge guns before AK. |
| **C** | [[Revolver]] / [[Python Revolver]] / [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] | Roam/early kits and tier-1 fights. |
| **D** | [[Eoka Pistol]] / [[Bows and Primitives\|bow]] | Naked-day RNG and stealth raids only. |

**Practical read:** craft toward AK + bolt + pump as your wipe goal. Run [[Thompson]]/Custom SMG in the meantime. Don't chase the M16A2 — let it find you.

---

## 3. Armor meta

**The meta kit is unchanged by Built Different:**

> [[Metal Facemask]] (head) + [[Metal Chest Plate]] (torso) + [[Road Sign Kilt]] (legs) + hoodie + pants underneath.

- The **facemask is still the single highest-value piece** — it directly cuts the 2× headshot multiplier (see [[Combat Mechanics]]). Nothing craftable beats it for the head.
- Ballistic gear (above) is better but loot-only and non-replaceable → it's a **bonus when found, not the plan**.
- **Don't forget the cold penalty:** metal chest is **-34% cold** — wear cloth underneath or freeze at night/in snow.
- Heavy Plate set still exists for raid-defense / turret-tanking but the move-speed penalty keeps it out of roaming PvP.

Full per-piece table + radiation tiers: [[Armor]].

---

## 4. Base / building meta

Nothing in Built Different touched building HP, stability, or upkeep, so the established meta holds:

- **Solo/duo:** [[Bunkers|bunker base]] + honeycomb is still the standard for surviving offline raids — wall-stacking (honeycomb) multiplies the explosive cost to reach loot, and bunkers add a near-uncounterable loot stash if built right. See [[Bunkers]] and [[Soft Side]].
- **Open-core vs honeycomb:** honeycomb (double/triple-walled core) remains the meta for raid cost-efficiency on small bases; pure open-core is only for big group bases that defend online. For solo/trio, **honeycomb every wall touching loot.**
- **Always orient the [[Soft Side]] inward** — stone/sheet/armored walls take ~25% less boom from inside, so never leave a soft side exposed to the outside.
- **Siege/mortar threat:** mortars and battering rams (siege weapons) remain a group-raid tool, not a solo concern — but they let groups breach high external [[High External Stone Wall|stone walls]] cheaply, so don't over-rely on a wall compound vs organized groups.
- **Close your base for the new navmesh** — animals can now path indoors on servers running `-useNewNavmesh`.

Building fundamentals: [[Building Basics]], [[Stability]], [[Upkeep and Decay]].

---

## 5. Raiding meta (cheapest effective entries)

Built Different **changed no raid costs**. Cheapest verified entries (raw sulfur), from [[Raid Costs]]:

| Target | Cheapest entry | Raw sulfur | Note |
|--------|---------------|-----------|------|
| [[Sheet Metal Door]] | **1 C4** | 2,200 | The #1 raid target in the game. 18 beancans (2,160) is marginally cheaper but slow/loud. |
| Garage Door | **2 C4** | 4,400 | Or 29 [[Explosives\|landmines]] (1,740) if you have the time/cover. |
| Armored Door | 3 C4 | 6,600 | 48 landmines (2,880) is cheapest but situational. |
| [[Stone Wall]] | **2 C4** | 4,400 | Soft side drops cost; breach from inside if reachable. |
| Sheet Metal Wall | 4 C4 | 8,800 | ~3 C4 soft side. |
| [[Tool Cupboard]] | 8 explosive 5.56 | 200 | Pop the TC to stop upkeep/repair. |

**Solo/duo eco-raiding meta:** [[Eco-Raiding]] with **beancans + satchels** against twig/wood/early-stone bases is the most cost-effective way to fund a wipe early. Save C4/rockets for sheet-metal loot rooms. Full method: [[Raid Methods]], [[Explosives]]. Defending: [[Raid Defense]], [[Counter-Raiding]].

---

## 6. Economy / progression meta

The dominant progression mechanic is still **fragment gating** ([[Blueprint Fragments]]) — Built Different did not touch it:

- **Scrap is cheap to spend; fragments are the bottleneck.** WB2 needs 5 Basic Fragments; WB3 needs 5 Advanced. You only get fragments by **leaving home** for monuments, puzzle rooms, and hackable [[Locked Crate|locked crates]]. (Conversion: 20 Basic → 1 Advanced.)
- Workbench crafting costs **no scrap** anymore — scrap goes to **research** (15/30/60/120 by rarity) and tech-tree unlocks.

**Fastest meta route this wipe:**
1. Wipe-day naked → tools → [[Building Basics|2×1 or starter base]] + [[Tool Cupboard]].
2. [[Scrap Runs|Scrap-run]] roads/barrels/[[Recycling|recyclers]] for [[Components|components]] + scrap.
3. Hit easy monuments ([[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], outpost-adjacent) for **Basic Fragments** → WB2 → [[Thompson]]/[[Custom SMG]] + [[Metal Facemask]].
4. Push higher monuments + hackable crates for **Advanced Fragments** → WB3 → [[AK-47]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]].
5. Farm sulfur → [[Explosives|gunpowder/explosives]] → eco-raid to snowball.

See [[Pivot Or Die]] and [[Meta Shift]] for the fragment-system origin, and [[Getting Started]] / [[Returning Player Guide]] for the full early loop.

---

## 7. What's OP / overused / what to avoid

**Overpowered / strongest right now**
- [[AK-47]] in trained hands — unchanged, still the gun that wins wipes.
- Full **Ballistic kit** *when you find it* — best armor in the game, but you can't rely on it.
- [[Bolt-Action Rifle]] / [[L96]] for long-range control of monuments.

**Overused / expect to face it**
- Metal facemask + chest "meta kit" on every geared player — aim for legs/exposed lower body, or land the head.
- Bunkers + honeycomb on solo/duo loot rooms — bring enough boom or skip it.
- [[Shotguns|Pump shotgun]] in base/airlock fights — pre-aim doorways.

**What to avoid**
- **Don't build your wipe around the M16A2 or Ballistic gear** — loot-only, non-craftable, gone when you die.
- **Don't run 1000Hz+ mouse polling** until the Unity 6 bug is patched — you'll stutter in fights.
- **Don't trust your old headshot muscle memory** on the new models — recalibrate at the range.
- **Don't leave a [[Soft Side|soft side]] facing out** or your base raids ~25% cheaper.
- **Don't hoard scrap expecting to craft up** — spend it on research; chase [[Blueprint Fragments|fragments]] instead.

---

## Re-check after the July 2 2026 wipe

This snapshot is accurate for the **June 4 → July 2 2026** cycle. After the next first-Thursday force wipe, re-verify: (1) any balance patch changing weapon/armor/raid numbers, (2) whether the Unity 6 mouse bug is fixed, (3) whether Facepunch makes Ballistic/M16A2 craftable (community is pushing for it). Until then, this is the current "what's strong" page.

**Related:** [[Built Different Update]] · [[Rust Weapons]] · [[Armor]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Returning Player Guide]]

pages.body:
# Current Meta — Common Ground (July 2026)

**The "what's strong right now" snapshot for the July 2026 wipe cycle.** Patch = **[[Common Ground Update|Common Ground]]** (live Thursday July 2 2026). Written for a returning solo/duo/trio PC player.

> **Staleness gate:** Rust force-wipes the **first Thursday of every month**. Next force wipe = **Thursday August 6 2026** — re-check any "meta verdict" after it. Common Ground changed **no weapon/armor/building/explosive numbers**, so the entire combat + raid + base meta from the June [[Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)|Built Different snapshot]] carries forward. This page focuses on **what's actually new: modes.** Numbers verified July 11 2026 against rust.facepunch.com / Rustafied / rusthelp.

---

## TL;DR — the meta in six lines

- **Combat/raid/base meta is unchanged from June.** Same [[AK-47|AK]] king, same [[Metal Facemask]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]] + [[Road Sign Kilt]] kit, same raid costs. If you play **vanilla**, nothing about your wipe changes except a new safe-zone stop and a clan tool.
- **Softcore is now a different tempo:** **2x gather** + **6-9 PM local raid windows**. If your server is softcore, progression is fast and your base is only breakable in that 3-hour window.
- **Clan system is live** on standard + softcore (disabled in hardcore): Clan Table, roles, clan chat, member map dots. Useful for trio+.
- **New Apartment Complex safe-zone monument:** rentable furnished rooms (bed/storage/furnace/T1 bench) + player shops + master-key plays.
- **Raid costs still: 1 C4 = [[Sheet Metal Door]] (2,200 sulfur), 2 C4 = [[Stone Wall]] (4,400).** Nothing rebalanced.
- **Carry-over gotchas from June:** Unity 6 high-polling-mouse FPS bug (drop to 1000Hz), and recalibrated headshots on the new player models.

---

## 1. What Common Ground actually changed (and the meta impact)

Common Ground is a **modes + monument** patch, not a balance patch. Full detail: [[Common Ground Update]]. Only what affects how you play *this wipe*:

### Softcore: 2x gather + raid windows (softcore servers only)
- **Meta impact (softcore only):** Both levers are **Softcore defaults — vanilla is untouched.** On softcore, 2x gather compresses the early game hard (twig-to-stone-to-first-gun is much faster), and **structures are only raidable 6-9 PM local server time** while an active TC (>=1h old) protects the base outside that window. Deployables and an unprotected/fresh TC are still vulnerable 24/7.
  - **How it changes softcore play:** offline-raid fear drops massively — you plan defense around a known 3-hour window instead of 24/7. Do NOT leave loot on deployables (external boxes, turrets) or a sub-1-hour TC exposed; those are the only things attackable off-window.
  - **If you play vanilla:** ignore all of the above — your gather and raid timing are exactly as they were in June.

### Clan system (standard + softcore; off in hardcore)
- Craftable **Clan Table** unlocks a real clan UI: member management, roles, announcements, logs, score, clan chat, name-on-nameplate, and **clan member map dots**.
- **Meta impact:** genuinely useful at **trio and up** — the map dots + roles/announcements streamline coordination past the raw team UI. Solo/duo can skip it. See [[Clans and Groups]], [[Team System]].

### Apartment Complex (new safe-zone monument)
- Rentable furnished rooms (bed, storage, furnace, phone, **T1 workbench**) for an upfront + daily scrap fee; player-run shops; a ~1000-scrap **master key** that opens an occupied room/shop for ~5 min; a basement guard dropping location hints.
- **Meta impact:** a new **safe-zone econ/loot node** — cheap rentable stash + crafting inside protection, plus master-key raiding-lite and shop flipping. Low-risk scrap sink and trading hub, not a power spike.

### Animations (feel only)
- New rifle sprint animations + torch-style one-hand hold extended to the Hatchet. **No gameplay/stat impact** — purely visual polish on the June player-model rework.

### Carry-over from Built Different (still true)
- **High-polling mice (1000Hz+) still cause the Unity 6 FPS bug** — keep your mouse at 1000Hz or below.
- **New player-model silhouettes/hitboxes** — keep recalibrating headshots at the range.

---

## 2. Weapon meta tier list (this wipe)

**Unchanged from June** — Common Ground added no weapons and changed no stats. Full detail: [[Rust Weapons]] and the per-gun pages; the June breakdown in [[Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)]] still applies verbatim.

| Tier | Weapon | Why this wipe |
|------|--------|---------------|
| **S** | [[AK-47\|Assault Rifle]] | Still the best all-round gun; end-wipe value, highest skill ceiling. |
| **S** | [[Bolt-Action Rifle]] / [[L96]] | Long-range king. |
| **S** | [[Rust Shotguns\|Pump Shotgun]] / M4 Shotgun | Rules base defense and breach. |
| **A** | [[LR-300]] | Tighter recoil / better velocity than AK. |
| **A** | [[MP5A4]] | Best craftable SMG at WB3. |
| **A** | [[M249]] / [[M16A2]] | Loot-only; great when found, can't plan around them. |
| **B** | [[Thompson]] / [[Custom SMG]] / [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] | Wipe-day / bridge guns. |
| **C-D** | [[Revolver]] / [[Python Revolver]] / [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] / [[Eoka Pistol]] | Early kits / naked-day RNG. |

---

## 3. Armor meta

**Unchanged:** [[Metal Facemask]] + [[Metal Chest Plate]] + [[Road Sign Kilt]] + hoodie/pants is still the repeatable meta kit; Ballistic set is still the best-but-loot-only find. Full table: [[Armor]].

---

## 4. Base / building meta

Building HP, stability, and upkeep are **untouched**, so the June meta holds — bunker + honeycomb for solo/duo, [[Soft Side]] inward, close your base against the navmesh animals. See [[Bunkers]], [[Building Basics]].

**Softcore-only overlay:** with raid windows, base-defense priorities shift — your walls/doors are only breakable 6-9 PM, so the biggest softcore leak is **exposed deployables and a fresh (<1h) TC**. Tuck external boxes/turrets and let your TC age past an hour before you stash real loot.

---

## 5. Raiding meta (cheapest effective entries)

**No raid costs changed.** Cheapest verified entries (raw sulfur), from [[Raid Costs]]:

| Target | Cheapest entry | Raw sulfur |
|--------|---------------|-----------|
| [[Sheet Metal Door]] | **1 C4** | 2,200 |
| Garage Door | **2 C4** | 4,400 |
| Armored Door | 3 C4 | 6,600 |
| [[Stone Wall]] | **2 C4** | 4,400 |
| Sheet Metal Wall | 4 C4 | 8,800 |
| [[Tool Cupboard]] | 8 explosive 5.56 | 200 |

**Softcore timing overlay:** on softcore you can only break those structure targets **6-9 PM local** — plan the raid for the window. TCs, turrets, and boxes (deployables) can still be popped anytime. On vanilla, raid whenever as before. Methods: [[Raid Methods]], [[Eco-Raiding]]. Defense: [[Raid Defense]], [[Counter-Raiding]].

---

## 6. Economy / progression meta

Still **fragment-gated** ([[Blueprint Fragments]]) — WB2 = 5 Basic, WB3 = 5 Advanced, crafting costs no scrap, research is 15/30/60/120. Route unchanged (see [[Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)]] section 6 and [[Progression Route]]).

**New this patch:** the **Apartment Complex** is a fresh safe-zone econ node — rentable furnished room as a forward stash/craft spot, and player shops for trading. On **softcore**, 2x gather means the sulfur/HQM grind for boom and tools is roughly half the time — economy snowballs faster.

---

## 7. What's OP / overused / what to avoid

**Strongest right now:** [[AK-47]] (unchanged), Ballistic kit *when found*, [[Bolt-Action Rifle]]/[[L96]] for range. On softcore, whoever exploits the 2x-gather early lead + defends the 6-9 PM window best.

**Avoid:**
- **Don't assume raid windows / 2x gather apply on vanilla** — they're **softcore-only**. Check your server mode.
- **On softcore, don't leave loot on deployables or a <1h TC** — that's the only thing raidable off-window.
- Don't run 1000Hz+ mouse polling (Unity 6 bug); don't trust old headshot muscle memory on the new models; don't leave a [[Soft Side|soft side]] out; don't hoard scrap instead of chasing [[Blueprint Fragments|fragments]].

---

## Re-check after the August 6 2026 wipe

Accurate for the **July 2 -> August 6 2026** cycle. After the next force wipe, re-verify any balance patch, whether the Unity 6 mouse bug is fixed, and any softcore/clan/apartment tuning. Until then, this is the current "what's strong" page.

**Related:** [[Common Ground Update]] · [[Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)]] · [[Rust Weapons]] · [[Armor]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Server Types]] · [[Rust Companion App (Web)]]
