2. Clear the 15 scientists **bottom-up**, looting green (L1) and fuse rooms as you climb.
3. Top level: swipe Blue then **Red**, start the **15-minute locked crate hack**.
4. **6 heavy scientists** rope in from the Chinook onto the helipad. Hold the staircase below the crate room; pick off heavies as they funnel.
5. Loot crate + elite at 0:00 and leave. Radiation floods 30 min after hack start; counter-boats are the real threat from minute ~8 onward.

**Worth it for a solo?** Yes — this is the standard solo/duo money run once you hold a [[Red Keycard]]. 15 scientists then only 6 heavies (half of Large Rig's 12) is manageable solo if you hold the staircase chokepoint and kill minigun/flamethrower variants at range. The map-wide hack notification means you're racing counter-boats — bring a fast exit and don't over-commit if a team is already on. Pair it with a [[Underwater Labs]] dive in the same trip.

## PvP notes

- Small Rig is the most counter-rushed event on most servers — the map-wide hack notification plus short boat ride makes it a magnet. A cheap "rat slot" is swimming under the deck legs and ambushing looters on their way down.
- If a team is already on when you arrive, do not ladder up the announced side; take the legs opposite the dock.
- After the [[Attack Helicopter]] nerf (Nov 2025: flares no longer fool homing missiles), boat counters are more common than air counters — watch the water line.

## Cross-links

[[Large Oil Rig]] · [[Locked Crate]] · [[Heavy Scientist]] · [[Red Keycard]] · [[Underwater Labs]]

pages.title: The Dome
pages.body:
# The Dome

The giant geodesic "golf ball" — a climbable steel-frame sphere with a spiral exterior ramp. Historically just a recycler stop, **the 2025/2026 monument reshuffle gave it a real green-card puzzle room**, so it's now a worthwhile destination, not just a landmark. No median radiation (max ~11 in pockets).

## Loot & facilities

| Thing | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Normal crates | 11 | 9 respawning + 2 puzzle-locked |
| Military crates | 4 | |
| Barrels | 20 | one of the highest barrel counts of any minor monument |
| Recycler | 1 | **Radtown type: 5 s/item, 120% yield** ([[Safe Zones]]) |
| Small Oil Refinery | 2 | turn crude into low grade on-site |
| [[Diesel Fuel]] | 2 | for [[Quarries]] / [[Giant Excavator Pit]] |
| Radiation | Median 0 / max 11 | basically safe |

## Green-card puzzle

Bring **1 [[Electric Fuse]]** + **1 [[Green Keycard]]**: insert fuse, flip the switch, swipe the card to open the puzzle room.

**Reward (resets ~30 min):** **1 [[Blue Keycard]]**, **1 Basic [[Blueprint Fragment]]**, **2 [[Diesel Fuel]]**, 2 normal crates. Takes under a minute once you know the fuse-box spot. (rusthelp spec, Jun 2026: 1 fuse + 1 green card, **1 switch**.)

**Worth it for a solo?** Yes — no scientists, rad basically nil (max 11), 1 switch, and the only green run that also hands you **2 diesel + 2 on-site refineries**, making it the one-stop "fuel up before a quarry run" green monument. 20 barrels for early scrap on top. Run it when you need diesel as much as a blue card.

## Climbing for apex loot

After the puzzle, run the spiral exterior ramp up the dome — the apex platform holds extra loot (military crate + ammo box on most maps). The climb is the main reason to know this monument: vertical, exposed, good vantage but easy to get sniped on.

## Returning-player tips

- The 2 diesel + 2 refineries make Dome a one-stop "fuel up before a quarry run" spot.
- 20 barrels = strong early scrap/component farm even if you skip the puzzle.
- No scientists — purely a PvP-risk monument.

Related: [[Keycards]], [[Blueprint Fragments]], [[Diesel Fuel]], [[Quarries]].

pages.title: Train Tunnels
pages.body:
# Train Tunnels

The underground rail network (a.k.a. the Metro / Freight Transit Line) — a map-spanning tunnel system you ride with **Workcarts** to cross the map fast, dotted with loot rooms and [[Tunnel Dweller]] NPCs. Distinct from the surface [[Train Yard]] monument (which has its own keycard puzzles); Train Yard and several other monuments simply contain **tunnel entrances** down into this network.

## How to enter

Entrances are marked on the map by a **small white circular icon with a train-car emblem**. Some are built into monuments ([[Outpost]], [[Train Yard]], etc.); others spawn procedurally in the open world. Each entrance drops via a **huge spiral staircase**, with a faster (riskier) **central elevator shaft**. A default map has roughly **20 underground stations**.

## Tunnel Dwellers (NPCs)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | **125** |
| Weapons | M92 pistol or M39 rifle |
| Gear | Jumpsuit + gas mask |
| Per platform | ~5 dwellers |
| Between platforms | groups of ~3 |

Loot improves the deeper / further along a platform you push. They have real stalking AI in tight corridors — don't sprint blind.

## Loot

Stations and alcoves hold a mix of lower/mid-tier loot: **Military Crates, normal Loot Crates, and Tool Boxes**, plus components, electrical parts, ammo, and the occasional bear rug. No keycard puzzle — it's a kill-and-loot run. Reliable for components and scrap without monument-tier PvP exposure (though tunnels are a known ambush spot).

## Workcarts

- **Surface/aboveground workcart:** two spawn per Freight Transit station, facing opposite directions on the tracks. Run on **Low Grade Fuel** (put fuel in the storage behind the driver cabin, mount the seat, drive). Can pull a few cars.
- **Underground Workcart:** spawns only in side-station "Maintenance Room" cubbies. **1000 HP**, mostly-uncovered engine, pulls very few cars.

Workcarts are the fastest free way to traverse the map — far cheaper than fuel-hungry vehicles for long crossings.

## Returning-player tips

- The tunnels are a top **component farm** for solos/duos: kill dwellers, loot tool boxes and crates, ride a workcart to the next station.
- Take the spiral stairs over the elevator if you suspect someone's camping the shaft — the elevator is a death funnel.
- Tunnels connect most of the map; learn one entrance near your base for fast escapes and roams.

Related: [[Tunnel Dweller]], [[Train Yard]], [[Workcart]], [[Low Grade Fuel]].

pages.title: Train Yard
pages.body:
# Train Yard

Tier 2 industrial monument built around a huge coaling tower. Solid all-purpose farm: blue puzzle yields a [[Red Keycard]] + 2 Basic Blueprint Fragments, light NPC presence (4 scientists), and good vertical PvP terrain.

## Vital stats (verified vs rusthelp.com, Jun 2026)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Type / Tier | Large / Tier 2 |
| Radiation | median 11, max 26 — Hazmat covers everything |
| Scientists | 4 Trainyard Scientists (respawn with puzzle) |
| Recyclers | 1 (monument recycler) |
| Facilities | Repair Bench, Small Oil Refinery, elevator, Pump Jack, 1 motorbike spawn |
| Events | tunnel entrance, Chinook drop zone, Patrol Heli crashes |
| Puzzle reset | ~30 min |

## Loot summary

- 15 open crates (50% Military / 50% Normal, 30-36 min respawn) + 5 Medical/Food
- 10 puzzle-locked crates (50/50 Military/Normal) + 4 puzzle barrels
- 11 open barrels
- **3 Basic Blueprint Fragments total** (2 in blue puzzle, 1 in green) — T2 [[Workbench]] fuel
- **1 [[Red Keycard]]** in the blue puzzle room

**Scrap value of a run (est.):** ~150-250 scrap/lap with components recycled on-site.

## Puzzle walkthroughs

### Blue puzzle (the coaling tower) — the main one
**Bring:** 1 [[Electric Fuse]], 1 [[Blue Keycard]].
1. Go to the base of the **giant concrete coaling tower** (the tallest structure). Insert the fuse in the ground-level fuse box.
2. Flip the **3 switches** that route power (base of the tower + adjacent control shack — learn them once, they're steps apart).
3. Climb the tower stairs (or ride the elevator) to the **top-floor card room**; swipe **Blue**.
4. Loot: 9 crates, **Red Keycard**, 2 Basic Fragments. Descend via the external ladders if the stairs feel camped.

### Green puzzle (instant reset)
**Bring:** 1 fuse, 1 [[Green Keycard]]. Same **3-switch** power routing; the green room (1 crate, 3 barrels, 1 Basic Fragment) sits in the two-story office building. Reset ~0 min — re-runnable immediately. (rusthelp spec, Jun 2026: both puzzles = 1 fuse + 3 switches; blue yields the red card + 2 fragments + 9 crates, green yields 1 fragment + 1 crate + 3 barrels.)

**Worth it for a solo?** Yes. Only 4 scientists, rad max 26 (Hazmat covers it), and the blue puzzle hands a free [[Red Keycard]] + 2 fragments. Slightly riskier than [[Water Treatment Plant]] because of the 4 NPCs and the contested coaling-tower overwatch, but the instant-reset green side-puzzle makes it a strong fragment-farm loop for [[Workbench]] T2. Good solo pick when WTP is taken.

## PvP notes

- The coaling tower top is the best overwatch on the monument and sees the recycler — assume it's occupied.
- Tower stairwell fights heavily favor whoever is above; throw grenades/F1s up, never push blind.
- The long train sheds give cover to cross the yard; the open rail lines are sniper lanes.
- Motorbike spawn makes TY a quick smash-and-grab for roamers — loot rooms get cleaned fast after wipe.

## Cross-links

[[Power Plant]] · [[Airfield]] · [[Water Treatment Plant]] · [[Blue Keycard]] · [[Red Keycard]] · [[Workbench]]

pages.title: Underwater Labs
pages.body:
# Underwater Labs

Procedurally-assembled research stations on the ocean floor — **every lab's layout is random**, built from modular rooms (moonpools, corridors, labs, living quarters). Quiet, loot-dense, and ignored by most of the server. The best "nobody bothers me" farm for solos with a [[Submarine]] or [[DPV]].

## Vital stats (verified vs rusthelp.com, Jun 2026 — counts vary per lab)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Type / Tier | Offshore / Tier 1-2-3 |
| Radiation | median 0, max 52 (isolated hot rooms only) |
| NPCs | ~4-6 "Lab Dwellers" (tough scientist variant, shotguns/SMGs in close quarters) |
| Recyclers | none |
| Crates | ~25 per lab, including **~2 Elite Crates** |
| Puzzles | up to 9 keycard-door configs (Green/Blue/Red + 1-2 fuses), ~30 min resets |
| CCTV | up to 14 feeds (e.g. LAB, OPERATIONS, SECURITYHALL) |
| No-build zone | 1,024 m² |

## Typical loot per lab

- ~2 Elite Crates (usually behind Red doors)
- ~6 Normal, ~3 Ammunition, ~3 Medical, ~3 Food, ~2 Tools, ~1 Fuel crates
- Plus poker table, arcade games, computer stations in the living modules

**Value of a run:** a full lab clear rivals a mid-tier land monument with a fraction of the PvP risk. rusthelp (Jun 2026, per-lab averages, "numbers vary, layout is random"): **~25 crates incl. ~2 Elite Crates, ~4 Basic + ~2 Advanced Blueprint Fragments, ~2 green keycards, ~4 Lab Dwellers, no recyclers, median rad 0 (max 52 in isolated hot rooms).**

**Worth it for a solo?** **Yes — the best solo farm in the game.** Lowest-traffic loot source on most servers (often untouched for hours after a ~30 min reset), no map-wide event to draw counters, ~2 Elite Crates and Advanced Fragments behind red doors, and the only ambush point is the moonpool you arrive through. The single requirement is transport — a [[Submarine]] or [[DPV]] from a [[Fishing Village]]. Carry green+blue+red + 2 fuses to open every door config.

## How to get in and out

1. **Transport:** Submarine (solo or duo, from [[Fishing Village]]) or [[DPV]] underwater scooter (since Oct 2024); strong swimmers can dive with a diving tank for shallow labs.
2. **Entry:** drive the sub up into a **moonpool** (the wet docking bays — surface inside the lab) or climb the exterior ladder shafts.
3. Clear the dwellers room-by-room — close quarters, so shotguns rule here. They hit hard for "scientists"; do not facetank doorways.
4. Run the keycard doors you have cards for (carry Green+Blue+Red and 2 fuses to open everything).
5. Loot, return to the moonpool, and sub home. Check the moonpool before surfacing — that's the only ambush point.

## PvP notes

- Labs are the lowest-traffic loot source in the game; mid-wipe they're often untouched for hours after reset (~30 min puzzle cycles).
- The moonpool is the chokepoint both ways: a parked enemy sub means company inside.
- Sound carries through the modules — sprinting in a lab announces your room position to anyone inside.
- Labs pair naturally with [[Small Oil Rig]] runs (same neighborhood, same boat).

## Cross-links

[[Submarine]] · [[DPV]] · [[Fishing Village]] · [[Small Oil Rig]] · [[Red Keycard]] · [[Electric Fuse]]

pages.title: Water Treatment Plant
pages.body:
# Water Treatment Plant

Low-risk Tier 2 monument: no scientists, mild radiation, a one-card Blue puzzle that pays a [[Red Keycard]] + 2 Basic Blueprint Fragments, and (since the 2026 loot pass) **4 motorbike spawns** behind the puzzle. Great early-wipe blue-card target.

## Vital stats (verified vs rusthelp.com, Jun 2026)

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Type / Tier | Large / Tier 2 |
| Radiation | median 0, max 26 — Hazmat covers the hot pockets |
| Scientists | none |
| Recyclers | 1 (monument recycler) |
| Facilities | 2 Repair Benches, 2 Small Oil Refineries, elevator, Pump Jack, 3 ziplines |
| Events | tunnel entrance, Chinook drop zone, Patrol Heli crashes |
| Vehicles | 4 motorbikes (puzzle-locked garage) |
| Puzzle reset | ~30 min (secondary puzzle: instant) |

## Loot summary

- 15 open crates (80% Normal / 20% Military) + 5 Medical/Food + 13 barrels
- 10 puzzle-locked crates (80/20)
- Puzzle rewards: **1 [[Red Keycard]], 3 Basic Blueprint Fragments total, 3 Diesel Fuel**

**Scrap value of a run (est.):** ~100-200 scrap/lap — loot skews Normal-crate, so WTP is more about the red card, fragments, and bikes than raw scrap.

## Puzzle walkthroughs

### Primary (Blue)
**Bring:** 1 [[Electric Fuse]], 1 [[Blue Keycard]]. (rusthelp spec, Jun 2026: 1 fuse + 1 blue card; no green door, no switches — the simplest red-card puzzle in the game.)
1. **Fuse shack**: the small utility building near the big water towers — insert the fuse and press the **timer** button.
2. The timer raises a **garage door** at the main building; sprint there before the window closes.
3. Swipe **[[Blue Keycard|Blue]]** inside: loot room = 6 crates, **[[Red Keycard]]**, 2 Basic Fragments, 3 Diesel — and the bike garage (4 motorbikes).

### Secondary (free)
One **garage door** activation (no card, no fuse) opens a side room: 4 crates + 1 Basic Blueprint Fragment, **instant reset (~0 min)**. Learn this one — it's free T2-fragment income every pass.

**Worth it for a solo?** **Yes — this is the #1 solo red-card source in the game.** No scientists, median rad 0 (max 26, covered by Hazmat), one fuse + one blue card = a guaranteed [[Red Keycard]] + 2 Basic Fragments + 4 motorbikes every ~30 min. Buy a blue card at [[Bandit Camp]] for 40 scrap, convert it here, repeat. The free secondary garage adds a fragment every lap with no card cost at all.

## PvP notes

- WTP's big open settling tanks are dead ground — move along the building line.
- The tall water towers are climbable overwatch over the puzzle shack and recycler.
- Because it's NPC-free and beginner-friendly, WTP is heavily trafficked early wipe; the fuse-shack-to-garage sprint is the ambush moment.
- A motorbike out of the puzzle garage is the fastest loot-extraction tool in the game — ride out, don't walk.

## Cross-links

[[Train Yard]] · [[Power Plant]] · [[Blue Keycard]] · [[Red Keycard]] · [[Motorbike]] · [[Workbench]]

pages.title: Armor
pages.body:
# Armor

Armor in Rust is **per-piece and per-damage-type**: each piece protects a hit-location, and the protection that applies is decided by *where the bullet lands*, not an averaged whole-body number. A head shot is reduced by your head armor only; a chest shot by your chest piece only. This is why a [[Metal Facemask]] (head) is the single highest-value item in a kit — it directly cuts the 2x headshot multiplier (see [[Combat Mechanics]]).

All protection values below are the raw % damage reduction for that damage type, verified against the official wiki.facepunch.com item pages (June 2026). Negative cold = the piece makes you colder.

## Head armor

| Piece | Projectile | Melee | Bite | Explosion | Cold | Craft / Source |
|-------|-----------|-------|------|-----------|------|----------------|
| [[Metal Facemask]] | **50%** | 70% | 8% | 50% | -4% | 50 Leather, 15 HQM, 6 Sewing Kit (WB3) |
| Coffee Can Helmet | 35% | 50% | 8% | 50% | — | 60 Metal Frags, 15 Cloth, 1 Sewing Kit (WB2) |
| Bucket Helmet | 20% | 50% | 8% | 50% | +6% | 35 Metal Frags (WB1) |
| Heavy Plate Helmet | **90%** | 80% | 13% | 100% | -16% | Loot/craft; **-0.1 move speed** |
| Ballistic Helmet | 60% | 70% | 10% | 13% | -3% | **Loot-only** (Jun 2026) |

The **Metal Facemask is the standard** — its 50% projectile head protection means a [[AK-47|standard rifle]] headshot does ~half its 2x-multiplied damage. The Coffee Can Helmet is the budget bridge before HQM. Heavy Plate Helmet has the best raw numbers but slows you and is rarely worn in roaming PvP.

## Chest armor

| Piece | Projectile | Melee | Bite | Explosion | Cold | Craft / Source |
|-------|-----------|-------|------|-----------|------|----------------|
| [[Metal Chest Plate]] | **25%** | 20% | 13% | — | -34% | 50 Leather, 18 HQM, 8 Sewing Kit (WB3) |
| Road Sign Jacket | 20% | 20% | 40% | — | -34% | Road signs + leather + sewing kit |
| Wood Chestplate | 10% | 40% | 20% | 30% | — | Wood + metal frags |
| Hazmat Suit (full body) | 30% | 30% | 50% | 30% | +50% | Loot; radiation 50% |
| Heavy Plate Jacket | ~90% | high | — | ~100% | negative | Loot/craft; heavy move penalty |
| Ballistic Vest | 35% | 20% | 3% | 3% | -3% | **Loot-only** (Jun 2026) |

The **Metal Chest Plate** is the torso standard — 25% projectile is the best of the craftable chests. It does NOT cover the lower body, so it pairs with a kilt. Note the steep **-34% cold**: wear a hoodie/pants underneath or you'll freeze at night and in snow.

## Leg / lower armor

There is **no metal leg armor**, which is the whole reason the meta kit uses a kilt for the lower body:

| Piece | Projectile | Melee | Bite | Cold | Notes |
|-------|-----------|-------|------|------|-------|
| [[Road Sign Kilt]] | 20% | 20% | 10% | -8% | Standard lower-body PvP piece |
| Wood Armor Pants | ~10% | high | — | — | Cheap melee/early protection |
| Ballistic Leg Armor | 30% | — | — | -3% | **Loot-only** (Jun 2026), best legs in game |

## Hazmat & radiation

The **Hazmat Suit** is a full-body slot that gives 50% radiation, 50% cold, and a flat 30% to projectile/melee/explosion. It's worn for monument runs and irradiated zones (e.g. flooded [[Oil Rig]] 30 min after the hack), NOT for PvP — its combat numbers are mediocre and you give up the facemask's head protection. The newer **Heavy Scientist / NVG / Tactical gloves** loot items also carry radiation. Keep a hazmat in a box for monument pushes.

### How radiation protection actually works

Radiation is **points-subtracted, not a percentage**: each radiation zone has a strength (rads/sec), and your total radiation-protection points are **subtracted from that incoming rate**. If a zone is rated 30 and you have 25 protection, you still take ~5 rads/sec and your radiation meter climbs; when the meter is high enough you lose health. So the rule is simple: **carry total protection >= the zone's radiation level** and you take zero. Anti-Radiation Pills slow the meter's climb (a stopgap, not a substitute for gear), and the [[Mining Quarry]]/monument puzzle areas are usually the worst spots.

Key per-item radiation-protection values (verified Jun 2026):

| Item | Rad protection |
|------|---------------|
| **Hazmat Suit** (full body) | **25** (single biggest item) |
| Lead-lined armor piece (helmet / vest / pants) | **5** each (full lead set = 15) |
| Full **Burlap** set (headwrap + shirt + trousers + shoes + gloves) | ~10-12 combined |
| Wood Armor (jacket + pants) | small each; stacks with burlap |
| **Gas Mask** | 2 |
| Bandana mask | small |
| Metal Facemask / Coffee Can / Road Sign gear | minimal-to-none (these are *combat* armor, not rad gear) |

Protection **stacks across all worn pieces**, so the cheap monument kit is a layered cloth+wood set, NOT combat armor.

### Radiation protection threshold table (what passes each tier)

This is the table that was missing. Match your **total** protection to the zone strength; the columns below are the common environmental radiation levels (rads/sec) you'll meet at monuments:

| Zone strength | Tier | Example monuments | Protection needed | Cheapest kit that passes |
|--------------|------|-------------------|-------------------|--------------------------|
| **~26** (low) | Low rad | [[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], Harbor, gas/super outskirts | **~10-15** | Full **Burlap** set (headwrap, shirt, trousers, shoes, gloves) |
| **~52** (medium) | Medium rad | [[Airfield]], [[Trainyard]], [[Water Treatment Plant]] | **~15-20** | Burlap + **Wood Armor** + bandana, OR a Hazmat |
| **~81** (high) | High rad | [[Power Plant]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Cargo Ship]] | **~25** | **Hazmat Suit** (25) clears it on its own |
| **~100** (extreme) | Extreme rad | [[Oil Rig]] reactor, [[Underwater Labs]] reactor cores, [[Launch Site]] Vehicle Assembly Building | **~30-40+** | **Hazmat + lead set** (25+15=40), or hazmat + **Anti-Radiation Pills** to outlast the meter |

The **Launch Site Vehicle Assembly Building** and the **Power Plant cooling tower** carry the single hottest zones in the game — a Hazmat alone (25) does NOT fully cover them, so you either stack lead, chug Anti-Radiation Pills, or get in and out fast. For everything below high tier a **Hazmat is overkill but foolproof**: it clears low/medium/high on its own, which is why most players just keep one hazmat in a box and skip the cloth-layering math.

> Returning-player note: radiation is far gentler than the launch-era game. Most red monuments (Airfield, Water Treatment, Trainyard) are now passable in a cheap burlap+wood kit, and the truly lethal radiation is confined to a handful of endgame reactor rooms.

## The meta kits

### Solo/duo roaming kit (the standard) — BEST overall
**Metal Facemask (50% head) + Metal Chest Plate (25% chest) + Road Sign Kilt (20% legs)**, with a hoodie + pants underneath for the -34%/-8% cold penalties. This is the most common kit you'll see from wipe day 3-4 onward and the **best craftable PvP combo**: it maximizes head + torso projectile protection while keeping full movement speed (no heavy-plate penalty). Net projectile profile: **50/25/20** head/chest/legs. Cost is dominated by the **33 HQM** across facemask + chestplate. Add a Boonie Hat or Bandana over the facemask only if you need a touch of rad/cold; it doesn't stack head armor.

### Budget / early kit
**Coffee Can Helmet + Road Sign Jacket + Road Sign Kilt** (or Wood set). Gets you respectable melee protection and ~20-35% projectile before you have HQM. Wood armor is specifically strong vs **melee** (spears, machetes) and weak vs bullets — good for early roam where everyone is on bows and tools.

### Heavy raid / anchor kit
**Heavy Plate Helmet + Heavy Plate Jacket**, projectile ~90%, explosion ~100%. Used by a defender holding a doorway or tanking during a raid, NOT for chasing — the -0.1 move speed and cold penalty make it a turtle kit. Remember **explosive protection is capped at 75%** (May 2025), so even heavy plate no longer fully eats rockets.

### Endgame loot kit (Jun 2026)
**Ballistic Helmet + Vest + Leg Armor** — loot-only from elite/locked crates, cannot be crafted, researched, or bought. The leg armor (30% projectile) is the best lower-body protection in the game; the set is a chase item rather than a baseline. See [[Built Different Update]].

## Armor inserts (since Mar 2025 Crafting Update)

Crafted armor can have **0-3 insert slots**. Inserts add small protection or utility bonuses on top of the base piece. This is a returning-player change — armor you craft now is slightly customizable. Higher-tier crafted pieces roll more slots.

## Cross-links

[[Combat Mechanics]] (why head armor matters) · [[Meds & Healing]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Built Different Update]]

Sources: wiki.facepunch.com (metal.facemask, metal.plate.torso, coffeecan.helmet, bucket.helmet, roadsign.jacket, roadsign.kilt, heavy.plate.helmet, wood.armor.jacket, hazmatsuit), rusthelp.com, rustafied.com, falconrust.com + cobaltlab.tech + physgun.com radiation guides, gameplay.tips monument radiation list, pinehosting Built Different preview.

pages.title: Assault Rifle
pages.body:
# Assault Rifle

The **Assault Rifle** (universally called the **"AK"**) is the best all-round weapon in Rust and has topped essentially every tier list since launch. High damage, full-auto, long effective range, and — crucially — **craftable** at Workbench Tier 3. It is the standard end-of-progression roaming gun. See [[Rust Weapons]] for the full meta.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **50** |
| Headshot damage | ~100 (2x) |
| Fire rate | **450 RPM** (full-auto) |
| DPS | ~375 |
| Magazine | **30** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ HV / Incendiary / Explosive variants) |
| Effective range | medium–long (~150-250 m practical, falloff beyond) |
| Aim cone | moderate; opens with sustained movement |
| Recoil | **high** — strong upward "S" pattern |

## Recoil pattern

The AK has the **hardest but most rewarding** recoil in the game. The spray shape is a **sharp vertical climb for the first ~6-8 rounds, then a drift right, then a kick back left** (the old "flexible lightning bolt" / S-curve shape lives on as a tendency, not a fixed pattern) — but since the post-2022 rework this is a **direction plus aim-cone/bloom randomness**, not a memorizable spray.

**How to compensate:** pull your mouse **straight down hard during the opening vertical climb**, then ease the pull and **counter the right drift by nudging left, then nudge back right** as the pattern reverses — a shallow zigzag-down motion that mirrors the muzzle. The aim cone adds irreducible scatter on top, so even perfect control won't land every bullet at range. Because of the [[May 2024 aimcone overhaul]], **tap-firing 2-4 round bursts while strafing** is highly accurate (the cone only opens after ~4 sustained shots); full-mag sprays are reserved for close range where the cone doesn't matter. Controlling the AK is still the single biggest skill gap in Rust PvP.

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T3** |
| Craft cost | 50 [[High Quality Metal]], 200 Wood, 1 Rifle Body, 4 Metal Spring |
| Craft time | 35 s |
| Research cost | 120 scrap (after BP wipe; see [[Pivot Or Die]]) |
| Tech-tree path cost | ~780 scrap total |

To even reach craftability you need a [[Workbench Level 3]], which now requires 5 Advanced [[Blueprint Fragments]] (farmed at monuments) on top of scrap — the core 2025 progression change.

## Ammo options

- **[[5.56 Rifle Ammo]]** — standard.
- **HV 5.56** — flatter trajectory, faster bullet, easier long-range tracking.
- **Incendiary 5.56** — fire DoT, lights wooden builds, great for area denial.
- **Explosive 5.56** — does chip damage to structures; the cheap "boom" raid bullet (rocket alternative on wood/sheet).

## Attachments (4 slots)

Common loadouts (see [[Weapon Attachments]]): [[Holosight]] + [[Muzzle Boost]] for close-range DPS, or [[16x Scope]] / [[8x Scope]] + [[Silencer]] for stealthy mid-long fights. A [[Muzzle Brake]] tames the spray for spray-fights.

## Where it drops

Craft it — but it also drops from [[Locked Crate]]s (~28% chance, 1-2x), [[Elite Crate]]s (~4%), and the heli crate (~2%). Recycling one in a monument [[Recycler]] returns 30 HQM, 2 metal springs, 120 wood.

## Meta verdict — **S tier**

The default best weapon. Every serious roam kit ends in an AK. Its only real competitors are the loot-only [[LR-300]] (smoother) and [[M249]] (more sustained), but neither is craftable, so the AK is the reliable ceiling for solos/duos.

pages.title: Bolt Action Rifle
pages.body:
# Bolt Action Rifle

The **Bolt Action Rifle** ("Bolty") is the **craftable sniper** — the standard long-range rifle for players who can't loot an [[L96]]. Big per-shot damage and bleed, slow bolt-cycle between shots, and a tiny magazine. At Workbench T3 it's the reliable way to threaten long-range duels.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **80** (+ bleed) |
| Headshot damage | ~160 (+ bleed) — kills most armor levels in 1-2 shots |
| Fire rate | ~25 RPM (bolt-cycled, slow) |
| Magazine | **4** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | **350–500 m** |
| Recoil | severe per shot (irrelevant at sniper cadence) |

## Playstyle

You fire, **cycle the bolt** (a forced delay), and re-aim — so each shot must count. A headshot drops most players; a body shot + bleed forces them to retreat. Pair with a [[16x Scope]] for long-range and a [[8x Scope]] for flex range. The slow cycle means a missed shot can be punished, so it rewards patient, pre-aimed peeks.

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T3** |
| Craft cost | ~20 [[High Quality Metal]], 1 Rifle Body, 3 Metal Pipe, 1 Metal Spring |
| Research cost | 120 scrap |

## Meta verdict — **S/A tier**

The best **craftable** long-range option and a staple of every serious roam kit (AK for spray + Bolt for range). It loses to the loot-only [[L96]] (faster handling, one-shot potential) but you can make a Bolt every time. Mandatory for open-terrain servers and anti-sniper duels. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Bows and Primitive Weapons
pages.body:
# Bows and Primitive Weapons

The lowest rung of Rust ranged combat — bows, crossbow, nailgun, and the new blowpipe/boomerang. These are wipe-start and stealth tools. All are silent or near-silent (no gunshot audibility), which is their main appeal once guns exist.

## Comparison

| Weapon | Body dmg | Head dmg | Mag | Reload/cadence | WB tier | Ammo |
|--------|---------|----------|-----|----------------|---------|------|
| **Hunting Bow** | ~50 (+bleed) | ~80 (+bleed) | 1 | ~60 RPM draw | T1 | [[Arrows]] |
| **Compound Bow** | 50–100 (charge-dependent) | high | 1 | slow, chargeable | T1 | Arrows |
| **Crossbow** | ~60 | ~102–121 | 1 | 3.6 s reload | T1 | Arrows |
| **Nailgun** | ~18 | ~36 | 16 | 400 RPM | T1 | Nails |
| **Blowpipe** (2025) | low + poison | — | 1 | slow | T1 | Poison Darts |
| **Boomerang** (2025) | melee/throw | — | — | thrown, returns | T0/T1 | none |

---

## Hunting Bow

The **first ranged weapon** most players craft. Cheap, silent, +bleed. Charge the draw for full damage. **D tier** but essential wipe-start — kills animals for food and ambushes nakeds. Uses [[Arrows]] (Wooden, Bone, High Velocity, Fire).

## Compound Bow

**Strongest bow on paper** — full charge hits very hard (up to ~100), and you can hold a nocked arrow. The risk is the long charge/draw leaves you exposed. **C tier**, a skilled stealth-killer's tool.

## Crossbow

**King of primitive precision** — fires a flat, fast bolt with a built-in sight, big headshot damage (~102-121), but a slow 3.6 s reload means one shot must count. Silent. The best **early-wipe sniper** before you have a real rifle. **B tier**.

## Nailgun

Ultra-cheap **panic blaster** — 16-round mag of nails at 400 RPM, very low damage and short range. The "I have nothing else and someone's in my base" gun. **C tier**, cheap defensive spam.

## Blowpipe (May 2025)

New primitive that fires **poison darts** — low direct damage but applies a poison DoT. A stealthy harassment/finishing tool. Niche.

## Boomerang (May 2025)

New thrown weapon that **returns to you** if it misses — a melee/throwing novelty more than a serious PvP pick.

See [[Rust Weapons]] and [[Arrows]].

pages.title: Combat Mechanics
pages.body:
# Combat Mechanics

The systems that decide whether your bullets land and how much they hurt. Per-gun stats (damage, RPM, recoil pattern) live in the weapons folder; this page is the math underneath all of them. Verified against rust.facepunch.com devblogs and wiki.facepunch.com (June 2026).

## Hit-location damage multipliers

Damage is scaled by **where you hit**. Center mass is baseline; the head is the prize; limbs are punished.

| Hit location | Multiplier (approx) |
|--------------|---------------------|
| **Head** | **2.0x** |
| Chest / torso | 1.0x (baseline) |
| Stomach | ~1.0x |
| Arms / hands | < 1.0x (reduced) |
| Legs | ~0.5x (reduced) |
| Feet / extremities | far less |

- **Headshots do 2x damage** — an [[AK-47]] body shot of 50 becomes ~100 to the head. This is the entire reason aim is about crosshair height (see [[PvP Tips]]).
- The **neck is no longer a headshot** (a balance change) — you have to hit the actual head box.
- Limb shots are why a fleg-tagged opponent can still cross open ground; aim **upper chest/head**, not "the body."

### How head armor interacts
A [[Metal Facemask]] gives **50% projectile protection on the head**, so it cuts the 2x-multiplied headshot down to roughly a normal body shot's worth of damage. Practically: with a facemask you can survive **2 standard rifle headshots past ~30m**, whereas a bare head dies to far fewer. This is why the facemask is the highest-value piece in any kit ([[Armor]]).

## Aim cone, bloom & the May 2024 overhaul

Rust bullets are not perfectly accurate — they spread inside an **aim cone**, and rapid/moving fire adds **bloom** on top of recoil.

- **May 2024 aimcone overhaul:** the movement/spray accuracy penalty now **blends in gradually over ~4 shots** rather than being binary. Practical effect: **tap-firing and short bursts stay tight**, full-auto-while-standing sprays the widest, and strafing tap-fire is viable.
- **Crouching shrinks the aim cone** (tighter base spread) but does **not** remove bloom or recoil — you still pull down. Crouch for the last precise shots, not as a magic accuracy button.
- **Recoil is pattern + randomness.** Post-2022 recoil mixes a learnable pattern with per-shot randomness, so pure rote memorization isn't enough — you compensate the pattern and accept some scatter.

### The modern spray rule of thumb
**Tap → burst → crouch → reset.** Close range: go fast (spread matters less). Mid range: 3-5 round bursts, let the cone settle between. Long range: single taps, wait for the cone to shrink fully between shots.

## Hipfire vs ADS

- **ADS (aim down sights)** = tighter cone, slower movement, the default for any shot past short range.
- **Hipfire** = wider cone but full move speed; only reliable in point-blank shotgun/SMG brawls. At range, hipfire is a coin flip.

## Sound & detection (Sep 2025 change)

Gunshots are now audible at a **fixed range by weapon class**:

| Class | Audible range |
|-------|---------------|
| Quiet (pistols/SMG-ish) | ~400m |
| Mid (rifles) | ~500m |
| Loud (snipers/explosives/high-power) | ~600m |

You are **louder than you think** — a single AK burst pulls roamers from a base or two over. **Craftable silencers (Jun 2025)** reduce your gunshot range/signature, which is a meaningful solo/duo tool for taking fights without summoning third parties (see [[PvP Tips#Third-partying|third-partying]]). Footsteps, reloads, eating, and building/upgrading also make positional sound — wear a headset and use it.

## Optics

- **Variable zoom scope** toggles **4x / 8x / 16x** on a single optic — one scope now covers mid-to-long range instead of swapping holosight/8x.
- Holosight/reflex for close-mid; the variable scope or 16x for sniping.

## Movement & combat states

- **Crouch:** tighter aim cone, smaller hitbox, slower — for holding angles and precise shots.
- **Jump-peeking / strafing:** breaks the enemy's tracking (see [[PvP Tips]]); the May 2024 cone change rewards moving-but-controlled fire.
- **Gamma exploit is dead (Mar 2024):** a shader-based "nightlight" replaced gamma abuse, so you can't cheat darkness anymore — nights are genuinely dark; consider a flashlight/laser or NVGs.

## What changed in mechanics since 2023

| Change | When | Effect |
|--------|------|--------|
| Aimcone overhaul (gradual blend) | May 2024 | Tap/burst-fire rewarded; full-auto standing punished. |
| Neck no longer a headshot | — | Must hit the head box for 2x. |
| Craftable silencers | Jun 2025 | Suppress your own shots; changes the sound meta. |
| Gunshot ranges 400/500/600m | Sep 2025 | Positioning/third-party awareness matters more. |
| Variable zoom scope | — | One optic spans 4x/8x/16x. |
| Shader nightlight (anti-gamma) | Mar 2024 | Darkness can't be cheated away. |
| Unity 6 engine | Jun 2026 | 1000Hz+ mice can stutter (known issue). |

## Cross-links

[[Armor]] · [[Meds & Healing]] · [[PvP Tips]] · [[Melee & Bows]]

Sources: rust.facepunch.com devblogs (aimcone, sound, headshot/neck changes), wiki.facepunch.com, rusthelp.com, rustmods.com recoil guide, rustafied.com.

pages.title: Counter-Raiding
pages.body:
# Counter-Raiding

Counter-raiding is **fighting back while your base is being raided** — turning a raid into a graveyard for the attackers and ideally recovering what they spent. This page covers the combat/defense side; offensive raid costs and explosives live in [[Raid Costs]] / the raiding folder. As a solo/duo you rarely out-gun a clan, so counter-raiding is about **traps, angles, and timing**, not a fair fight.

## The principle

Raiders are **committed and exposed**: they've spent boom (rockets/C4 cost a fortune — see [[Raid Costs]]), they're standing in your loaded killzone, and every second they're shooting walls they're not shooting you. If you make the raid cost more than your loot is worth, they leave — and you keep the base.

## Automated defenses

### Auto Turret
- Shoots intruders automatically; load it with a gun + ammo and power it.
- **40m interference cap (Oct 2023):** turrets within 40m of each other interfere — you **cannot stack a wall of turrets** in a tiny area anymore. Space them out across the base/compound.
- Set to **authorized-only** (whitelist your team) or it shoots you; peacekeeper vs. attack mode matters.
- Turrets need **power** (see [[Electricity]]) — a raider cutting your external solar/battery can disable them, so wire defensively.

### Shotgun Trap & Flame Turret
- **Shotgun Trap:** cheap, loads handmade shells, mounted in hallways/airlocks — shreds anyone funneling through a doorway.
- **Flame Turret:** area denial in a corridor; cheap fuel.
- **Tip:** put traps **behind the wall they'll breach into**, so the first thing through the hole eats a trap.

### New alarm/sensor tech (May 2026)
- **Seismic Sensor** — raid alarm that detects explosions/structure damage; pings you (or triggers electricity) when a wall is being hit. Lets a solo know *exactly* when and where to peek.
- **Tin Can Alarm** — throwable/riggable tripwire alarm for early warning around the compound.
- **Digital Clock alarms** — timed triggers.

Wire these into your [[Electricity]] so the base tells you it's being hit before you even see it.

## Manual counter-raiding (you, with a gun)

### Peeking the raiders
- Raiders breaching a wall are **looking at the wall, not at the gaps** — peek a window/murder-hole/roof angle they aren't watching and tap their head ([[Combat Mechanics]]).
- **Don't peek the same hole twice** — they'll pre-aim it. Rotate between peeks; use height (roof, second floor).
- Time peeks to their **reload or boom-throw animation** (you'll hear it) when they can't instantly return fire.

### Counter-raid kit
- Best armor you have ([[Armor]] — facemask is non-negotiable), [[Meds & Healing|tea to 120 HP]], rifle/AK or shotgun for close peeks, plenty of meds.
- Keep this kit **in a separate hidden box / TC room**, not on your body — so a raid that breaks your loot room doesn't also take your defense kit.

### Sealing & rebuilding
- **Re-wall behind them:** if they breach into a hallway, drop a fresh wall/door behind the breach to trap them in your killzone or cut them off from the loot room.
- **Honeycomb** (double-walled) construction buys time and wastes their boom — every extra wall is more rockets they didn't budget for.
- Keep **building materials + a Building Plan / Hammer** on you to rebuild walls mid-raid.

## Defensive base-design notes (combat-relevant)

- **Airlocks** on every entrance so a peek/raid can't run straight in; pair with a shotgun trap.
- **Loot spread** across multiple TC'd compartments so one breach â‰  everything.
- **Turret coverage** of the most likely raid wall, spaced past the 40m interference cap.
- **External base / decoy** to make raiders guess which structure has loot.
- **Bag spawns** (capped at 15 since Jun 2023) placed so you respawn *near but not in* the killzone to re-peek.

## When to counter-raid vs. when to bail

- **Counter-raid** when: you have a kit ready, the base is honeycombed (time on your side), and a defended peek angle exists. The math favors you — they're spending boom; you're spending bullets.
- **Bail / offline-grab** when: it's a large group, you're under-geared, or they've already cracked the loot room. Sometimes the play is to grab what you can from a hidden stash, log the location, and rebuild/counter-raid later rather than feed kills.

## Cross-links

[[PvP Tips]] · [[Armor]] · [[Meds & Healing]] · [[Combat Mechanics]] · [[Electricity]] · [[Raid Costs]]

Sources: corrosionhour.com defense guide, rustafied.com, rust.facepunch.com news (Seismic Sensor / Tin Can Alarm May 2026; turret interference Oct 2023), r/playrust.

pages.title: Custom SMG
pages.body:
# Custom SMG

The **Custom SMG** is the cheap, ultra-high-fire-rate 9mm spray gun — the budget SMG craftable at Workbench T2. It has a fast, easy-to-form spray pattern but weak accuracy at range, so it lives and dies in close quarters. The classic "I have HQM but no MP5 yet" gun.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | ~30 |
| Headshot damage | ~60 |
| Fire rate | **720 RPM** (highest of any SMG) |
| DPS | ~300 |
| Magazine | **24** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm) |
| Effective range | short (~200 m falloff but poor accuracy) |
| Recoil | low climb but wide aim cone |

## Recoil pattern

The **spray pattern is extremely easy to form** — minimal vertical climb. The limiting factor isn't recoil, it's the **wide aim cone**: bullets scatter, so the gun is only reliable up close. Hold-and-spray at point-blank, don't try to reach out.

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T2** |
| Craft cost | ~8 [[High Quality Metal]], 1 SMG Body, 1 Metal Spring |
| Ammo | cheap 9mm |

## Meta verdict — **B/C tier**

A solid stopgap between the [[Thompson]] and [[MP5A4]]. Cheaper than the MP5 and fine for base defense and close ambushes, but the MP5 outclasses it the moment you reach T3. Good budget pick for solos who can't sustain rifle ammo. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Eoka Pistol
pages.body:
# Eoka Pistol

The **Eoka Pistol** is the cheapest, jankiest gun in Rust — a flintlock-style improvised pistol that **doesn't fire reliably**. You hold left-click and it *might* go off (random ignition chance per click). The ultimate gamble / naked-raiding weapon.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | ~180 (point-blank, like a shotgun) |
| Head dmg | ~210 |
| Magazine | **1** |
| Ammo | [[Shotgun Ammo]] (Handmade Shell) |
| Fire | **unreliable** — random ignition each click |
| WB tier | **T1** (craftable from primitive resources) |

## Why people use it

- **Naked offline raiding** — Eoka + Handmade Shells is the cheapest way for a naked to one-tap a sleeping/AFK player and start a raid.
- **Wipe-day ambush** — if it fires, it one-taps a low-armor target.

The unreliability is the whole meme: you can click 10 times before it goes off, which gets you killed against anyone alert.

## Meta verdict — **D tier (meme/utility)**

Effectively free, occasionally hilarious, mostly a liability in a real fight. Its niche is **offline/sleeper kills** and absolute wipe-start poverty. See [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] for the reliable-but-still-cheap alternative, and [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Handmade LMG
pages.body:
# Handmade LMG

The **Handmade LMG** (HMLMG) is the **craftable** belt-fed light machine gun — a crude alternative to the loot-only [[M249]]. High damage and fire rate with a large belt, but poor accuracy in sustained bursts. Added in the June 2022 combat update.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | ~57.5 |
| Fire rate | **480 RPM** (full-auto) |
| Magazine | **60** (belt) |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | short–mid (accuracy degrades fast) |
| Recoil | **high**, wide cone on sustained fire |

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T3** |
| Notable | the only craftable belt-fed LMG; expensive to feed |

## Meta verdict — **B/A tier**

A **craftable bullet hose** for base defense when you can't loot an M249 — the big belt means no reload window for pushers. Inaccurate at range and ammo-hungry, so it's situational rather than a roam staple. See [[Rust Weapons]] and compare to the [[M249]].

pages.title: Handmade SMG
pages.body:
# Handmade SMG

The **Handmade SMG** is a **Tier-1 craftable automatic** added in **November 2024** — a primitive bullet hose that gives early-wipe and low-tech players a true full-auto option before they reach a workbench T2. It's crude and inaccurate but cheap, and it bridges the gap between primitive weapons and the [[Thompson]]/[[Custom SMG]].

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | ~30 |
| Fire rate | ~480 RPM (full-auto) |
| Magazine | **30** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm; also takes Handmade Shell on some builds) |
| Effective range | short |
| Recoil | high climb, wide cone |

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T1** |
| Notable | first full-auto you can make; very cheap |

## Meta verdict — **C tier (early wipe)**

A genuine quality-of-life addition for the **wipe-day economy** — a naked-to-geared transition gun that doesn't need a T2 bench. Inaccurate and outclassed by every proper SMG, but for the first hour of a wipe a full-auto in your hands beats a [[Revolver]]. New since you last played (Nov 2024). See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: L96
pages.body:
# L96

The **L96** is the strongest gun in Rust — a loot-only bolt sniper that can **one-shot-headshot fully geared players**, with faster handling and bullet velocity than the [[Bolt Action Rifle]]. It is the apex long-range weapon and the dream loot of any wipe.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **80** (+ bleed) |
| Headshot damage | ~160 (+ bleed) — **one-shots geared players** |
| Magazine | **5** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | **450–1000 m** (highest in game) |
| Bullet velocity | very high — least drop/lead of any sniper |
| Recoil | severe per shot |

## Why it's #1

Versus the Bolt Action: **+1 mag capacity, far higher bullet velocity** (easier long-range hits), and **faster aim/cycle handling**. The high velocity means minimal lead on moving targets at range — the single biggest advantage in sniper duels. A headshot ends the fight against any armor tier.

## Acquisition (loot-only)

**No craft recipe.** Drops from [[Elite Crate]]s, the heli/bradley crate, and top-tier monument loot ([[Launch Site]], [[Oil Rig]]). One of the rarest and most valuable items per wipe.

## Meta verdict — **S tier (best gun)**

If you loot an L96, it is your single most valuable item — protect it, don't lose it in a coinflip. Loot-only access is the only reason the craftable [[Assault Rifle]] is the "default" best gun; in raw power the L96 is #1. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Loot-Only Heavy Weapons
pages.body:
# Loot-Only Heavy Weapons

The rarest, most spectacular guns in Rust — none craftable, all from elite loot or Heavy Scientist kills. Covers the [[Minigun]], [[Military Flamethrower]], plus the loot-only revolvers/pistols ([[High Calibre Revolver]], [[Prototype 17]]). For the [[M16A2]] see its own page.

---

## Minigun

A 300-round rifle-ammo hose with a brief **spin-up** before it fires.

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body damage | ~37.5/round |
| Fire rate | **600 RPM** |
| Aim cone | 0.8 deg |
| Magazine | **300** |
| Reload | ~3.5 s |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] |

Drops from Military Crates, [[Elite Crate]]s, and high-tier monuments ([[Oil Rig]], [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]]). Eats ammo absurdly fast — best for **area denial** and overwhelming a pushed defense. The spin-up delay punishes panic-firing. **Spectacle / situational A tier**.

## Military Flamethrower

Heavy-Scientist drop. Streams fire with a large fuel tank (uses [[Low Grade Fuel]]).

- **Eco-raiding** — burns wood foundations, tool cupboards, sleeping bags; a cheap way to grief/clear wood bases.
- **Area denial / base defense** — fills a hallway with fire.

Not a duel weapon (short range, no precision) but excellent utility. Looted from Heavy Scientists at [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], etc.

---

## High Calibre Revolver (Oct 2024)

A loot-only revolver chambered in **5.56 rifle ammo** (not 9mm) — a hard-hitting wheelgun novelty.

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] |
| Magazine | 5 |
| Role | high-damage sidearm |

Hits harder than the [[Python Revolver]] but is loot-only and rifle-ammo-hungry. **C/B tier**, fun find. New since you last played.

## Prototype 17 (burst pistol)

An extremely rare loot-only **burst-fire pistol**.

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Damage | ~40/round |
| Fire rate | ~533 RPM |
| Magazine | **18** |
| Fire mode | toggleable burst |

Strong on paper but **extreme rarity** keeps it a curiosity. **B tier (access-limited)**.

See [[Rust Weapons]] for the full roster and [[Ballistic Armor]] for the matching June 2026 loot-only gear.

pages.title: LR-300
pages.body:
# LR-300

The **LR-300** is the loot-only "cooler cousin" of the [[Assault Rifle]]. It hits slightly softer per shot but has a **flatter, more vertical recoil pattern** and **higher bullet velocity**, making it many players' favorite for consistent mid-to-long range accuracy. The catch: you cannot craft it — it only drops from high-tier loot.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **40** |
| Headshot damage | ~80 |
| Fire rate | ~500 RPM (full-auto) |
| DPS | ~333 |
| Magazine | **30** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | long (~422 m falloff, higher than AK) |
| Recoil | **low–moderate**, mostly vertical |

## Recoil pattern

A **mostly vertical pattern with minor horizontal sway** — much easier to control than the AK's S-curve, especially at range. Combined with higher muzzle velocity, the LR is more forgiving for tracking moving targets at distance. Controlled bursts are deadly. This is why high-skill players who *have* an LR often prefer it over the AK despite the lower per-shot damage.

## Acquisition (loot-only)

There is **no craft recipe and no tech-tree entry**. Find it in [[Locked Crate]]s, [[Elite Crate]]s, and Heavy Scientist drops at high-tier monuments ([[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Oil Rig]]). Because it's loot-gated, it's a "found treasure" gun rather than a kit staple.

## Attachments (4 slots)

Pairs beautifully with a [[Holosight]] or [[16x Scope]]; its low recoil makes a [[Muzzle Boost]] (which increases aim cone slightly) more tolerable than on the AK. See [[Weapon Attachments]].

## Meta verdict — **A tier**

Mechanically arguably *better* than the AK for many players (lower recoil, higher velocity, more range), but its **loot-only access** keeps it below the AK in the practical meta — you build your wipe around the gun you can reliably make. If you loot one, it's an upgrade to your roam kit. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: M16A2
pages.body:
# M16A2

The **M16A2** is a **new June 2026** ("Built Different" update) loot-only military rifle that fires in **fast 3-round bursts**. It trades the [[LR-300]]'s per-shot damage for higher accuracy and a faster fire rate, making it a precise burst weapon for mid-range. Brand new since you last played.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Damage (per round) | **35** |
| Fire mode | **3-round burst only** |
| Fire rate | **600 RPM** (within burst) |
| Magazine | **30** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | ~368 m |
| Accuracy | high (5 — better than AK/LR) |
| Recoil | 3.5 (same as LR-300) |
| Attachment slots | **4** |

## Stat comparison vs LR-300

| | M16A2 | [[LR-300]] |
|---|------|-------|
| Damage | 35 | 40 |
| Accuracy | 5 (higher) | 4 |
| Fire rate | 600 | 500 |
| Range | 368 | 422 |
| Recoil | 3.5 | 3.5 |
| Fire mode | 3-round burst | full-auto |

## Acquisition (loot-only)

No craft/research. Drops from [[Locked Crate]]s (~12%), Ghostship and Oilrig locked crates (~12% each) — "end-game loot." Despawns after 1 hour on the ground.

## Meta verdict — **B tier (new)**

A precise burst rifle that excels at controlled mid-range tap-fights — the burst mechanic enforces accuracy. Loot-only access and lower damage than the AK/LR keep it niche, but the high accuracy + 4 attachment slots make it a fun, viable found gun. Pairs naturally with the new loot-only [[Ballistic Armor]] from the same update. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: M249
pages.body:
# M249

The **M249** is the loot-only light machine gun with the **best raw stats in the game** — high damage, full-auto, and a massive **100-round belt**. It's the king of **base defense and sustained fights** where you can dump a belt without reloading. You only get it from the highest-tier loot.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **65** |
| Headshot damage | ~130 (2x) |
| Fire rate | **500 RPM** (full-auto) |
| DPS | ~542 (highest in the game) |
| Magazine | **100** (belt) |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | mid–long |
| Recoil | **highest in the game** — fire in intervals |

## Recoil pattern

The M249 has the **harshest recoil of any gun** — a violent **bottom-to-top vertical climb** that quickly outruns your downward pull, with heavy bloom on top. You cannot reasonably hold a full 100-round spray on a distant target. The technique is **interval fire**: short 4-6 round bursts, drag the mouse straight down through each burst, then pause to let the cone reset before the next. Up close, just hold it down — the sheer volume of fire overwhelms before recoil matters. Treat it as a suppression/defense hose, not a precision rifle.

## Acquisition (loot-only)

No craft recipe. Drops from [[Elite Crate]]s, the heli/bradley crate, and top monument loot. Reloading 100 rounds is slow, so it shines when you can pre-load and never reload mid-fight (base defense, online-raid hold).

## Meta verdict — **S/A tier**

Best **defensive** weapon in the game — 100 rounds means no reload window for an attacker to push. Less ideal for roaming (heavy, recoil-harsh, slow reload). The craftable alternative is the [[Handmade LMG]]. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: M39 Rifle
pages.body:
# M39 Rifle

The **M39 Rifle** is the loot-only military upgrade to the [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] — same semi-auto playstyle, but higher fire rate, bigger magazine, and better range. You can't craft it; it drops from high-tier crates. Think of it as the SAR's "found upgrade."

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **50** |
| Fire rate | ~343 RPM (semi-auto) |
| Magazine | **20** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | mid–long |
| Recoil | moderate per shot |

## Acquisition (loot-only)

No craft/tech-tree entry. Drops from [[Locked Crate]]s, [[Elite Crate]]s, and Heavy Scientist kills at high-tier monuments ([[Launch Site]], [[Oil Rig]], [[Military Tunnels]]).

## Meta verdict — **B/A tier**

A direct stat upgrade over the SAR — more damage, bigger mag, longer range — but **loot-gated**, so it's not a kit you plan around. With the craftable [[SKS]] now filling a similar role at T3, the M39's appeal is narrower than it used to be, but it's still a great find. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: M92 Pistol
pages.body:
# M92 Pistol

The **M92 Pistol** is the best **sidearm** in Rust — a loot-only military pistol with very low recoil, a 15-round magazine, and a fast fire rate. Effectively a mini-SMG you can hold in your off-slot.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **45** |
| Headshot damage | ~90 |
| Fire rate | ~400 RPM (semi-auto, very fast) |
| Magazine | **15** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm) |
| Effective range | short–mid (~90 m) |
| Recoil | **very low** |

## Acquisition (loot-only)

No craft recipe. Drops from [[Locked Crate]]s, [[Elite Crate]]s, and scientists. A common-ish military drop, so you'll see it more than an L96.

## Meta verdict — **B/A tier**

The best **backup gun** in the game — 15 rounds, low recoil, fast trigger. It out-DPSes the [[Python Revolver]] in a sustained close fight thanks to the bigger mag, at the cost of lower per-shot damage. The premium roam-kit sidearm. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Meds & Healing
pages.body:
# Meds & Healing

Base player health is **100** (push to ~120 with [[Meds & Healing#Healing teas|Max Health Tea]]). Healing in Rust is split between **instant** health (a chunk on use) and **heal-over-time** (HoT, ticks over a few seconds). Most meds also do double duty as **bleed** and **poison** cleanse. Numbers below are verified against wiki.facepunch.com (June 2026).

## Healing items

| Item | Instant | Heal-over-time | Bleed | Poison | Craft | Use on others? |
|------|---------|----------------|-------|--------|-------|----------------|
| **Bandage** | +5 | — | -50 | -2 | 4 Cloth (no WB) | Yes (right-click) |
| **Medical Syringe** | +15 | +20 over ~5s | — | -5 | 15 Cloth, 10 Low Grade Fuel, 10 Metal Frags (WB2) | Yes (right-click) |
| **Large Medkit** | +10 | +100 over time (heals to max) | -100 (stops all bleed) | -10 | 10 Low Grade Fuel + 2 Medical Syringe (WB2) | No (self only) |
| **Anti-Radiation Pills** | — | — | — | — | slows radiation meter climb | Self |

_Pinned (verified Jun 2026 vs wiki.facepunch.com): Bandage +5 heal / -50 bleed; Syringe +15 instant + 20 HoT (also -10 radiation, -5 poison); Large Medkit +10 instant + 100 HoT to full / -100 bleed. Anti-Rad Pills do NOT remove rad gear need — they only slow the buildup; pair with a Hazmat for hot zones (see [[Armor]] radiation table)._

### How to read this in a fight

- **Bandage** is your bleed-stopper. +5 health is trivial — you craft it almost free (4 cloth) and the real job is **-50 bleed**, which stops most bullet bleeds in one or two. Always carry a stack.
- **Medical Syringe** is the **combat heal**: +15 instant then +20 over 4 seconds = 35 total. The instant 15 is what saves you mid-fight; pop one behind cover and keep peeking. Cheap to mass-craft (cloth + LGF + frags).
- **Large Medkit** is the **post-fight / full reset**: +10 instant then heals you all the way to max over time and **instantly stops all bleeding**. The catch is a longer use animation and you can't apply it to a teammate — it's a self-only "I survived, now top off" item. Made from 2 syringes, so it's a HQM-free but syringe-expensive item.

### Healing priority sequence in a fight
1. **Bandage** to stop the bleed (otherwise HoT is fighting the bleed).
2. **Syringe** for the instant +15 to get back over a one-shot threshold.
3. **Large Medkit** only when you're safe — the animation is too long to use while being shot.

## Bleed and the wounded state

- Bullet hits apply **bleed** (damage over time) on top of impact damage. Bandages/medkits cleanse it; syringes do NOT stop bleed.
- At 0 HP you may enter the **wounded/crawling state** rather than dying outright (server-dependent, and skipped on headshots / massive overkill). A teammate can revive you, or you bleed out. A **Large Medkit** taken before you go down guarantees you out of the wounded threshold.

## Healing teas (combat-relevant)

Teas are brewed at a **Mixing Table** (200 Metal Frags + 100 Stone, WB1) in three tiers — 4 basic → 1 advanced, 4 advanced → 1 pure. Only one tea of a given type is active at once; the strongest tier wins; **all tea effects clear on death**. Combat-relevant ones:

| Tea | Effect | Duration |
|-----|--------|----------|
| **Basic Healing Tea** | +20 health over time | (consumed) |
| **Advanced Healing Tea** | +40 health over time | (consumed) |
| **Pure Healing Tea** | **+60 health** over time (heals while running) | (consumed) |
| **Basic Max Health Tea** | **+5 max HP** (~105 cap) | ~20 min |
| **Advanced Max Health Tea** | **+12.5 max HP** (~112 cap) | ~20 min |
| **Pure Max Health Tea** | **+20 max HP** (**120 cap**) + 30 hydration | ~20 min |

**Pre-fight ritual:** drink a **Pure Max Health Tea** before roaming or raiding — 120 HP changes how many shots you survive (e.g. it can be the difference between dying and living to a rifle burst). Carry a **Pure Healing Tea** as an extra emergency heal that also works while running. Because effects clear on death, re-drink after every respawn.

## What changed since 2023

- The **Mar 2025 Crafting Update** added the Cooking Workbench and **food spoilage** (raw food 6h, cooked 24h, paused in powered fridges) plus 8 buff pies — food now matters more for sustained roaming, though core med items (bandage/syringe/medkit) are unchanged in function.
- Mixing Table tea system is the same loop a returning player remembers; the durations and the 120 HP cap still hold.

## Cross-links

[[Armor]] · [[Combat Mechanics]] · [[PvP Tips]] · [[Farming & Food]]

Sources: wiki.facepunch.com (bandage, syringe.medical, largemedkit), rusthelp.com (pure-max-health-tea), corrosionhour.com tea guide, rustafied.com mixing table guide, gamerant tea ranking.

pages.title: Melee & Bows
pages.body:
# Melee & Bows

Pre-gun and silent-kill weapons. These win the **first hour of wipe** (everyone is naked-to-bow) and stay relevant as **quiet finishers** all wipe. Headshots still apply the **2x multiplier** (see [[Combat Mechanics]]). Numbers verified against wiki.facepunch.com (June 2026).

## Melee weapons

| Weapon | Damage/hit | Notes | Craft |
|--------|-----------|-------|-------|
| Rock | ~10 | Starting tool, last resort | Spawn item |
| Stone Spear | **35** (70 headshot) | Throwable, 2.8m reach, 0.7 atk/s | 20 Stone + 1 Wooden Spear |
| Wooden Spear | ~25 | Cheap throwable | 300 Wood |
| Bone Knife | ~20 | Fast, cheap | 35 Bone Frags |
| Combat Knife | ~30 | Fast, high bleed | Metal frags |
| Machete | high + **bleed** | Fast attack, strong bleed; good range | 100 Wood + 40 Metal Frags |
| Salvaged Cleaver | high slash | Slow, big hit | Salvaged loot |
| Salvaged Sword | very high | Can one-hit-head many targets; top melee | WB-tier |
| Longsword | **highest per-hit** | Slow; WB2 | Metal frags + HQM tier |
| Mace / Salvaged Hammer | high blunt | Anti-wood-armor (blunt beats wood's high melee res) | — |

### How to use melee
- **Stone Spear** is the wipe-day king: 35 melee or **thrown for a ~70 headshot**, made from stone you already have. Throw it, pick it back up, or keep a stack to throw.
- **Machete** is the roam knife: fast swings + heavy **bleed** means a couple of hits and they bleed out even if they run. Cheap (100 wood, 40 frags).
- **Salvaged Sword / Longsword** are the burst-melee finishers — high enough per-hit to kill low/wounded targets silently, no gunshot to pull third parties.
- Wood armor has **high melee resistance** (40% on the chest), so against wood-armor naked-rushers, **blunt** weapons (mace) or just shooting them works better than slashing.

## Bows & non-gun ranged

| Weapon | Dmg (wood arrow) | RoF | Notes | Craft |
|--------|-----------------|-----|-------|-------|
| Hunting Bow | **50** | ~60 rpm equiv | Cheap, silent, drop/velocity | 200 Wood + 50 Cloth |
| Crossbow | **60** | ~17 rpm | More dmg, slower, scoped feel | WB tier |
| Compound Bow | scalable (draw) | variable | Hold-draw for more dmg/velocity; best bow | WB tier |
| Nailgun | low, fast | high | Spray close-range, cheap ammo | metal |

### Arrow types
- **Wooden arrows** — cheapest, baseline damage (above).
- **High Velocity arrows** — less damage, much flatter/faster trajectory; easier to land at range.
- **Bone arrows** — cheap early.
- **Fire arrows** — set things alight; area denial / soft-side raiding.

### How to use bows
- Bows are **silent at range** (no 400-600m gunshot ping) — the solo's tool for taking a fight or finishing a runner without summoning third parties.
- They have real **bullet drop and travel time**: aim above and lead moving targets. The **compound bow** holds its draw for more velocity (flatter, faster) — the best for actual PvP archery.
- **Hunting Bow headshot (50 x2 = 100)** can drop a bare-headed naked in one — huge on wipe day.

## New thrown/exotic (May 2025)

- **Blowpipe** — silent dart weapon, applies effects; very quiet harassment tool.
- **Boomerang** — thrown, returns; novelty + silent.

## When melee/bow beats guns

- **Wipe hour:** nobody has guns; spear + bow decide early bases.
- **Silent kills:** finishing a wounded player or sentry without a gunshot (see [[Combat Mechanics#Sound & detection|sound]]) avoids third parties.
- **Ammo-starved:** bows run on wood/cloth, infinitely sustainable vs. gunpowder economy.
- **Anti-wood-armor:** blunt melee ignores wood's melee resistance.

## Cross-links

[[Combat Mechanics]] · [[PvP Tips]] · [[Armor]]

Sources: wiki.facepunch.com (spear.stone, machete, bow.hunting), rust.fandom.com, wiki.rustclash.com, rustafied.com.

pages.title: MP5A4
pages.body:
# MP5A4

The **MP5A4** is the premier **craftable SMG** — a high-fire-rate 9mm bullet hose that dominates close-to-mid-range fights and indoor/raid combat. At Workbench T3 it's the natural CQC counterpart to the [[Assault Rifle]]. Cheaper to feed than a rifle (uses [[Pistol Ammo]]) and shreds at the ranges most PvP actually happens.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **37.5** |
| Headshot damage | ~75 (2x) |
| Fire rate | **600 RPM** (full-auto) |
| DPS | ~375 (highest sustained of craftable SMGs) |
| Magazine | **30** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm; + HV / Incendiary variants) |
| Effective range | short–mid (~72 m practical) |
| Recoil | medium, tighter & more vertical than rifles |

## Recoil pattern

A **tight, mostly vertical pattern** that's easier to control than the AK at close-mid range. The standard technique is to **fire 4-5 rounds, pause ~1 second, fire 4-5 more** — letting the cone reset (per the [[May 2024 aimcone overhaul]]) keeps your bursts accurate. At true close range you just hold and melt.

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T3** |
| Craft cost | ~15 [[High Quality Metal]], 1 SMG Body, 2 Metal Spring |
| Ammo | uses cheap 9mm — far easier to sustain than 5.56 |

## Meta verdict — **S tier**

The best **craftable** close-range gun and a genuine top-tier pick. In the tight spaces where most fights happen (base defense, monument interiors, online raids) the MP5's fire rate beats the AK. Pair an MP5 (CQC) with a Bolt or AK (range) for a complete kit. Its loot-only competitor is the [[Custom SMG]]'s big brother role — but MP5 outclasses every other SMG. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: PvP & Combat
pages.body:
# PvP & Combat

The combat fundamentals hub for Rust — armor, healing, hit mechanics, melee, and the soft skills that win fights. For individual gun stats (damage/RPM/recoil per weapon) see the weapons folder; this folder covers the systems those guns operate inside.

## Pages in this folder

- [[Armor]] — every armor piece and the best set combos, with exact projectile/melee/explosion protection numbers.
- [[Meds & Healing]] — bandage / syringe / medkit numbers, bleed/poison cleanse, healing teas in combat.
- [[Combat Mechanics]] — headshot multipliers, hit-location damage scale, aim cone, hipfire vs ADS, sound ranges, crouch.
- [[Melee & Bows]] — knives, spears, machete, bow/crossbow/compound, blowpipe, boomerang.
- [[PvP Tips]] — peeking, jiggle-strafing, crosshair placement, sound reading, third-partying, solo fight selection.
- [[Sound & Audio Cues]] — identify weapons/footsteps/raids by ear, surface loudness, crouch-walk silence, silencers, audio settings for awareness.
- [[Counter-Raiding]] — defending your base while it's being hit: turrets, shotgun traps, peeks, retakes.

## The one-screen combat summary (verified June 2026)

- **Base HP is 100.** [[Meds & Healing|Max Health Tea]] can push it to ~120.
- **Headshots deal 2x damage.** A [[Metal Facemask]] cuts incoming headshot damage roughly in half (50% projectile protection), which is why it's the single most important piece in a kit.
- **The meta kit is** Metal Facemask + Metal Chest Plate + [[Road Sign Kilt]] (no metal leg armor exists). See [[Armor]].
- **Explosive protection is capped at 75%** (May 2025) — you can no longer fully tank rockets in heavy armor.
- **Aim cone (May 2024 overhaul):** the movement/spray penalty blends in over ~4 shots, so tap-firing and short bursts stay accurate; full-auto standing sprays the most.
- **Gunshots are audible at 400/500/600m** by weapon class (Sep 2025) — you are louder than you think.

## What changed in combat since 2023 (returning player)

| Change | When | Why it matters |
|--------|------|----------------|
| Aim cone overhaul | May 2024 | Movement penalty blends in over ~4 shots; strafe tap-fire is viable, full-auto standing is punished. |
| Explosive protection cap 75% | May 2025 | Heavy armor no longer hard-counters rockets. |
| New guns | 2024-2026 | [[Handmade SMG]] (T1), [[SKS]] (T3), High Calibre Revolver (5.56), M16A2 3-round-burst, Minigun, Military Flamethrower. |
| Craftable silencers | Jun 2025 | You can suppress your own gunshots; changes sound game. |
| Gunshot audible ranges | Sep 2025 | 400/500/600m by class — positioning/sound discipline matters more. |
| Variable zoom scope | — | 4x / 8x / 16x toggle on one optic. |
| Ballistic armor + M16A2 | Jun 2026 | Loot-only endgame gear set (see [[Armor]]). |
| Wolves + stalking AI predators | Nov 2024 | PvE threats while roaming; jungle adds tigers/panthers/crocs/snakes (May 2025). |
| Siege weapons | Feb 2025 | Catapult/Ballista/Battering Ram/Siege Tower change base assault; Mortar (May 2026). |

Sources: wiki.facepunch.com item pages, rusthelp.com, rustafied.com, rust.facepunch.com/news.

pages.title: PvP Tips
pages.body:
# PvP Tips

The soft skills that decide fights once your gear and aim are even. Written for a returning **solo/duo/trio** player — the recurring theme is: *you will be outnumbered, so you fight on your terms or you don't fight.* Mechanics referenced here (aim cone, sound, headshot) are detailed in [[Combat Mechanics]].

## Crosshair placement (the #1 fix)

- **Keep your crosshair at head height, always** — pre-aimed where a head will appear, not at the floor. Headshots are **2x** ([[Combat Mechanics]]); the player whose crosshair is already on the head when the peek happens wins.
- Pre-aim the **edge of cover / doorway** the enemy must come around, not the open middle.
- Lower your sensitivity if you over-flick; consistent micro-adjustments beat wild swings.

## Peeking

- **Jiggle / shoulder peek:** expose only a sliver, bait a shot, learn their position, retreat — without committing your whole body.
- **Pre-fire peeks:** if you know where they are, start firing *as* you peek so your first bullet lands instead of being the one who reacts.
- **Wide vs. shoulder peek:** wide-swing only when you have the HP/armor advantage and want to force the duel; shoulder-peek when gathering info.
- **Don't re-peek the same angle twice** — they're now pre-aimed there. Change height (crouch/stand), change the corner.

## Jiggle-strafing & movement in a fight

- **Strafe-tap:** the May 2024 aim cone blends the move penalty over ~4 shots, so **A-D strafing while tap/burst-firing** keeps you accurate *and* hard to track. Standing still full-auto is the worst of both.
- **Crouch for the last precise shots** (tighter cone, smaller hitbox) but don't crouch-camp in the open.
- **Unpredictable > fast:** change direction, jump occasionally, don't run in a straight line across an opening.

## Sound reading

- Wear a headset. You can hear **footsteps, reloads, eating, building/upgrading, doors, and gunshots** — most kills start with a sound, not a sight.
- Your **own gunshots carry 400/500/600m** by class ([[Combat Mechanics#Sound & detection|sound ranges]]). Every fight you take is an invitation. **Craftable silencers (Jun 2025)** cut that — worth it as a solo.
- Use sound to **count enemies** (multiple reloads/footsteps = group; disengage) and to **time peeks** (peek right after you hear them reload).

## Third-partying (and avoiding being the third-partied)

- A fought-out player is a free kill; expect a **third party** on any loud fight near a monument or compound. Conversely, *you* can win by letting two groups fight and cleaning up.
- As a solo/duo: **fight fast and leave**, or relocate after a kill — the gunshot already broadcast your position. Don't loot leisurely in the open.
- **Silenced weapons + bows** let you take fights without ringing the dinner bell.

## When to take a fight as a solo

Take it when:
- You have **gear/HP advantage** (better armor, full HP, [[Meds & Healing#Healing teas|tea'd to 120]]) and they don't.
- You have **the angle/height** and they're in the open or distracted.
- It's a clean **1v1** with no third-party risk nearby.
- You can **disengage** if it goes wrong (cover/escape route behind you).

Avoid it when:
- You hear **multiple players** (count the footsteps/reloads).
- You're **low/no meds**, low ammo, or carrying loot you can't afford to drop on death (backpacks drop on death since Feb 2024).
- You're **in the open** with no cover and they have the range advantage.
- It's near **their compound** — turrets, [[Counter-Raiding|defenders]], and respawns favor them.

**Solo rule of thumb:** don't fight to fight — fight to *win and leave*. Every avoided fight is loot kept.

## Pre-engagement checklist

1. **Tea up:** Pure Max Health (120 HP) before roaming/raiding; effects clear on death so re-drink.
2. **Meds loaded:** bandages (bleed), syringes (instant +15), one large medkit.
3. **Ammo + a spare gun** if you can.
4. **Escape route** identified before you peek.
5. **Sound check:** stop, listen, count, *then* decide.

## Gear-fear vs. send-it

- **Gear fear** (not fighting because you're scared to lose your kit) loses more loot to caution than to deaths — but as a solo, **dying to a group is real loss** (your backpack drops). The balance: fight winnable fights aggressively, refuse unwinnable ones without hesitation.
- Keep a **second kit in a box** so a death isn't a wipe-ending event; this is what lets you play aggressive.

## Cross-links

[[Combat Mechanics]] · [[Armor]] · [[Meds & Healing]] · [[Melee & Bows]] · [[Counter-Raiding]]

Sources: rustafied.com, corrosionhour.com defense guide, rustmods.com, r/playrust meta sentiment, rust.facepunch.com (aimcone/sound devblogs).

pages.title: Python Revolver
pages.body:
# Python Revolver

The **Python Revolver** is the hardest-hitting **craftable pistol** — a high-damage 9mm wheelgun craftable at Workbench T2. It's the standard sidearm for mid-late wipe, big enough to win close fights outright and the natural backup to a rifle.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **55** (+ bleed) |
| Headshot damage | ~110 (+ bleed) |
| Fire rate | **400 RPM** (semi-auto, click-limited) |
| Magazine | **6** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm) |
| Effective range | short–mid (~72 m) |
| Recoil | high per shot but resets fast |

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T2** |
| Notable | best craftable sidearm; cheap 9mm ammo |

## Meta verdict — **A/B tier**

The best **sidearm** in the game outside the loot-only [[M92 Pistol]]. Huge per-shot damage means a couple of headshots ends a fight — great as a backup when your rifle runs dry, or as a primary in tight CQC. The go-to secondary for serious roam kits. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Revolver
pages.body:
# Revolver

The **Revolver** is the first real gun most players craft — a dirt-cheap Tier-1 8-shot 9mm pistol. It's the bridge out of bows and melee into actual gunplay on wipe day.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | ~35 |
| Headshot damage | ~70 |
| Fire rate | ~343 RPM (semi-auto) |
| Magazine | **8** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm) |
| Effective range | short |
| Recoil | snappy, manageable |

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T1** |
| Notable | very cheap; the canonical wipe-start gun |

## Meta verdict — **C tier (early wipe)**

The classic **first gun**. Cheap, 8 rounds, real lethality against nakeds and early-armor players. You make it, kill someone with a [[Thompson]], and upgrade. Outclassed the moment you reach T2. First rung of the gun ladder: Revolver → [[Semi-Auto Rifle]]/[[Thompson]] → AK/MP5. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Rust Ammo
pages.body:
# Rust Ammo

Reference for every ammunition family and its variants. Ammo type matters as much as the gun: HV for range, Incendiary for area/anti-wood, Explosive for cheap structure damage. Cross-references [[Rust Weapons]].

## Families

| Family | Guns | Base craft (per batch) |
|--------|------|------------------------|
| **5.56 Rifle Ammo** | [[Assault Rifle]], [[LR-300]], [[M249]], [[M16A2]], [[M39 Rifle]], [[SKS]], [[Semi-Auto Rifle]], [[Bolt Action Rifle]], [[L96]], [[Minigun]], [[High Calibre Revolver]] | 10 Metal Fragments + 5 Gun Powder -> 3 rounds (10 s) |
| **Pistol Ammo (9mm)** | [[MP5A4]], [[Thompson]], [[Custom SMG]], [[Handmade SMG]], [[Python Revolver]], [[Revolver]], [[M92 Pistol]] | Metal Fragments + Gun Powder |
| **Shotgun Ammo (12-gauge)** | [[Pump Shotgun]], [[Spas-12]], Double Barrel, [[M4 Shotgun]], [[Waterpipe Shotgun]], [[Eoka Pistol]] | Handmade Shell (cheap) up to slug/incendiary |
| **Arrows** | [[Hunting Bow]], Compound Bow, [[Crossbow]] | Wooden/Bone/HV/Fire |
| **Rockets / 40mm / Nails / Darts** | launchers, [[Nailgun]], [[Blowpipe]] | various |

---

## 5.56 Rifle Ammo variants

| Variant | Effect | Use |
|---------|--------|-----|
| **5.56 Rifle Ammo** | standard | default |
| **HV 5.56** | faster bullet, flatter trajectory, **same damage**, less drop — more expensive | long-range tracking; sniper duels |
| **Incendiary 5.56** | slower bullet, **fire DoT**, **drops off at shorter range than any other 5.56** | area denial, anti-wood-armor, lighting builds. ~10 s to craft 2 |
| **Explosive 5.56 (HE)** | lower projectile speed + less direct damage, **explodes on contact** for fragmentation damage to structures | cheap raiding on wood/sheet metal; chip damage. 125 scrap to research; ~10 s to craft 2 |

> Returning-player note: **Explosive 5.56 is the budget raid bullet** — an AK/SAR full of HE chews through wood and sheet doors far cheaper than rockets. Capped by the May 2025 change that **explosive protection is capped at 75%** (so HE always does at least 25% through armor/structures it's rated against).

## Pistol (9mm) variants

Standard, HV, and Incendiary equivalents exist (same logic: HV = flatter/faster, Incendiary = fire DoT). Far cheaper to mass-produce than 5.56 — a big reason SMGs are economical.

## Shotgun (12-gauge) variants

| Variant | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| **Handmade Shell** | cheapest, wipe-day, lower damage |
| **12-Gauge Buckshot** | standard multi-pellet, max close damage |
