| **12-Gauge Slug** | single projectile — "shotgun sniping," anti-armor at range |
| **12-Gauge Incendiary** | fire DoT, melts wood armor, lights targets |

## Arrows

| Arrow | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| Wooden Arrow | cheap, low damage |
| Bone Arrow | slightly stronger |
| High Velocity Arrow | faster/flatter, less drop |
| Fire Arrow | fire DoT (also lights/burns) |

---

## Practical loadout rules

- **Roaming AK/MP5:** carry standard rounds + a stack of HV for range and Incendiary for finishing/anti-wood.
- **Sniping (Bolt/L96):** **HV 5.56** is standard — flatter trajectory makes long shots far easier.
- **Cheap raiding:** **Explosive 5.56** on an AK/SAR for wood/sheet; rockets for stone/armored. See [[Raiding]].
- **Anti-armor CQC:** **Slug** or **Incendiary** shotgun shells.

See [[Rust Weapons]] and [[Weapon Attachments]].

pages.title: Rust Shotguns
pages.body:
# Rust Shotguns

Rust's shotguns all use [[Shotgun Ammo]] (Handmade Shell, 12-Gauge Buckshot, 12-Gauge Slug, 12-Gauge Incendiary). They deal enormous close-range burst damage but fall off hard past ~10-15 m. This page covers all five; the meme [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] and [[Eoka Pistol]] have their own pages.

## Stat comparison

| Shotgun | Body dmg (buckshot) | Head dmg | RPM | Mag | WB tier | Notes |
|---------|--------------------|----------|-----|-----|---------|-------|
| **Double Barrel** | ~180 | ~210 | ~120 | 2 | T1 | Two barrels, fire both for a one-shot |
| **Pump Shotgun** | ~210 | ~280 | — | 6 | T2 | The workhorse CQC shotgun |
| **Spas-12** | ~157.5/shell | — | 240 | 6 | T3 / loot | Semi-auto, fastest follow-ups |
| **M4 Shotgun** | — | — | semi-auto | 8 | loot-only | Military semi-auto, 8-round mag |
| [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] | ~180 | ~210 | ~13 | 1 | T1 | Wipe-start one-tap |

_Shotgun damage is the sum of many pellets at point-blank; it scatters and drops off rapidly with range. Slugs convert to a single high-damage projectile for "shotgun sniping."_

---

## Double Barrel Shotgun

T1, 2 shells. You can fire **both barrels at once** for a devastating point-blank one-shot, then reload. The classic **early-wipe ambush tool** — peek a corner, dump both, run. Cheap (~175 Metal Fragments, 2 Pipes). **C tier**, brutal in the first hour of a wipe.

## Pump Shotgun

T2, 6 shells, pump-action. **Dominates close-range fights** — high per-shell damage and 6 rounds means you can fight multiple targets without reloading. The go-to base-defense and CQC shotgun for most of a wipe. **B tier**.

## Spas-12

Semi-automatic, 6 shells — the **fastest follow-up shots** of any shotgun (240 RPM). Shreds at close range and stays useful slightly further out. Higher-tier than the Pump. **B tier**.

## M4 Shotgun

Loot-only military semi-auto shotgun, **8-round magazine**, fast follow-ups. The premium shotgun — biggest mag, semi-auto, best for clearing rooms in raids/base defense. **A/B tier** (access-limited). Found in [[Locked Crate]]s and [[Elite Crate]]s.

---

## Ammo choice

- **Handmade Shell** — cheapest, wipe-day.
- **12-Gauge Buckshot** — standard, max close-range pellet damage.
- **12-Gauge Slug** — single projectile, "shotgun sniping" at range, anti-armor.
- **12-Gauge Incendiary** — fire DoT, melts wood armor / lights builds.

See [[Shotgun Ammo]] and [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Rust Weapons
pages.body:
# Rust Weapons

Master index of every firearm and ranged weapon in Rust, with a current-patch (**Built Different**, June 4 2026) meta tier list. Each gun has its own page with damage, fire rate, recoil, craft cost, ammo, attachments, and drop sources. See also [[Rust Ammo]] and [[Weapon Attachments]].

> Returning-player note: the gun roster itself is largely unchanged since 2023, but **how you unlock guns changed completely**. Scrap-only research is gone — you now hunt [[Blueprint Fragments]] at monuments to tier up workbenches, then research is cheap (15/30/60/120 scrap). The AK is still king. New since 2023: [[SKS]], [[Handmade SMG]] (T1), [[High Calibre Revolver]], [[M16A2]], [[Blowpipe]], [[Boomerang]], plus loot-only [[Minigun]], [[Military Flamethrower]] and the [[Ballistic Armor]] set.

---

## How recoil works now (post-2022 + 2024 aimcone)

Since the **June 2022 combat update**, recoil is **no longer a fixed, memorizable spray pattern**. It's now a **hybrid**: a mostly-predictable recoil *direction* (the muzzle climbs mostly vertical with some pull) layered on top of an **aim cone + bloom** that adds genuine per-shot randomness. You compensate the general direction by pulling your mouse the opposite way, but the cone is irreducible randomness on top — "skill, not rote memorization." Facepunch made this change on purpose to kill recoil scripts and lower the skill floor; the trade-off (and the controversy) is that aim cone takes some outcomes "out of your hands." Burst-firing and resetting between bursts is how you fight the bloom.

The **May 2024 aimcone overhaul** changed the movement penalty: instead of an instant accuracy hit when you move, the penalty now **blends in gradually over ~4 shots**. Practical effect — you can **strafe and tap-fire** (1-4 shots) almost as accurately as standing still; only sustained full-auto-while-moving sprays open the cone up. This made tap-firing and "strafe peeking" the dominant gunplay.

Gunshots are now audible at **400 / 500 / 600 m** depending on weapon class (Sep 2025) — pistols/SMGs quietest, rifles loud, snipers loudest. A [[Silencer]] cuts this and removes the muzzle flash.

---

## Meta tier list — Built Different (June 2026)

Ranked for **solo/duo/trio** PvP. "Access" reflects the 2025-2026 fragment progression (craftables are far more reliable than loot-only guns).

### S — best in slot
- [[Assault Rifle]] (AK) — the backbone of high-level PvP; best all-round roaming gun, craftable at T3.
- [[MP5A4]] — craftable T3 SMG, melts at close-mid range; best CQC craftable.
- [[L96]] — strongest gun in the game; one-shot headshots geared players. Loot-only.
- [[Bolt Action Rifle]] — craftable sniper; the durable long-range pick.

### A — excellent
- [[LR-300]] — "the AK's cooler cousin," lower recoil + higher velocity, loot-only.
- [[M249]] — best raw stats in the game, 100-round belt; loot-only, defense king.
- [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] (SAR) — cheap T2 snowball rifle, the workhorse of early-mid wipe.
- [[Thompson]] — low-recoil T2 SMG, the classic snowball weapon.
- [[SKS]] — accurate T3 semi-auto, a craftable M39 substitute (overhauled, now T3).
- [[Python Revolver]] — hardest-hitting craftable pistol.

### B — situational / strong
- [[M39 Rifle]] — loot-only military SAR upgrade.
- [[M92 Pistol]] — best sidearm, military loot.
- [[Custom SMG]] — cheap T2 high-fire-rate spray gun.
- [[Pump Shotgun]] / [[Spas-12]] — close-range craftable / semi-auto.
- [[M4 Shotgun]] — semi-auto military shotgun.
- [[Crossbow]] — primitive precision, early-wipe sniping.
- [[Handmade LMG]] (HMLMG) — craftable belt-fed bullet hose.

### C — early wipe / niche
- [[Revolver]] — first real gun, dirt cheap T1.
- [[Double Barrel Shotgun]] — early ambush burst.
- [[Nailgun]] — ultra-cheap panic gun.
- [[Compound Bow]] — high charged damage, awkward.
- [[High Calibre Revolver]] — 5.56 wheelgun, loot-only novelty.
- [[Prototype 17]] — burst pistol, extreme rarity.

### D — desperation / meme
- [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] — wipe-start one-tap.
- [[Eoka Pistol]] — gamble weapon, naked offline raiding.
- [[Hunting Bow]] — first ranged weapon.
- [[Blowpipe]] — poison dart primitive.

### Loot-only spectacle (rare crate drops)
- [[Minigun]] — 300-round rifle hose, area denial.
- [[Military Flamethrower]] — eco-raid / area denial, Heavy Scientist drop.
- [[M16A2]] — burst-fire military rifle, new June 2026.

---

## Quick stat comparison (key guns)

| Weapon | Body dmg | RPM | Mag | Ammo | WB tier | Craftable |
|--------|---------|-----|-----|------|---------|-----------|
| [[Assault Rifle]] | 50 | 450 | 30 | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] | T3 | Yes |
| [[LR-300]] | 40 | ~500 | 30 | 5.56 | — | Loot |
| [[M249]] | 65 | 500 | 100 | 5.56 | — | Loot |
| [[M16A2]] | 35 (burst) | 600 | 30 | 5.56 | — | Loot |
| [[M39 Rifle]] | 50 | ~343 | 20 | 5.56 | — | Loot |
| [[SKS]] | 42.5 | 400 | 15 | 5.56 | T3 | Yes |
| [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] | 40 | ~343 | 16 | 5.56 | T2 | Yes |
| [[Bolt Action Rifle]] | 80 | ~25 | 4 | 5.56 | T3 | Yes |
| [[L96]] | 80 | — | 5 | 5.56 | — | Loot |
| [[MP5A4]] | 37.5 | 600 | 30 | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm) | T3 | Yes |
| [[Thompson]] | 37.5 | ~462 | 20 | 9mm | T2 | Yes |
| [[Custom SMG]] | 30 | 720 | 24 | 9mm | T2 | Yes |
| [[Handmade SMG]] | 30 | ~480 | 30 | 9mm | T1 | Yes |
| [[Python Revolver]] | 55 | 400 | 6 | 9mm | T2 | Yes |
| [[M92 Pistol]] | 45 | ~400 | 15 | 9mm | — | Loot |
| [[Revolver]] | 35 | ~343 | 8 | 9mm | T1 | Yes |

_Body dmg = chest/torso. Headshots multiply (roughly 2x for rifles; snipers/shotguns higher). Numbers verified vs rusthelp.com, corrosionhour.com, and 2026 community tier lists; exact values fluctuate per patch._

---

## Where guns drop

Late-wipe geared guns ([[L96]], [[M249]], [[M39 Rifle]], [[M16A2]], [[Minigun]]) come almost entirely from high-tier crates — [[Locked Crate]]s (the brown "hackable" crate), [[Elite Crate]]s, and Heavy Scientist drops at monuments like [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], and the [[Oil Rig]]. The [[Military Flamethrower]] and [[Minigun]] are Heavy-Scientist / elite-crate exclusive. See [[Rust Monuments]] for loot tables.

pages.title: Semi-Auto Rifle
pages.body:
# Semi-Auto Rifle

The **Semi-Auto Rifle** (SAR) is the workhorse mid-wipe rifle — a cheap, accurate, semi-automatic 5.56 gun craftable at Workbench **T2**. It's the first "real rifle" most players reach and the single best **snowball weapon** in the game: cheap to make, cheap to feed, and lethal in skilled hands well into late wipe.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **40** |
| Headshot damage | ~80 |
| Fire rate | ~343 RPM (semi-auto, click-limited) |
| DPS | ~120 (limited by your click speed) |
| Magazine | **16** |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | mid (~150 m) |
| Recoil | medium, manageable per-shot |

## Recoil

Semi-auto, so there's no spray to learn — each shot has a vertical kick you reset between clicks. Accuracy is excellent if you let the cone settle. It rewards calm, deliberate fire over panic-clicking.

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T2** |
| Craft cost | ~4 [[High Quality Metal]], 1 Semi Automatic Body, 1 Metal Spring (cheap) |
| Add-on | **Semi-Automatic Pistol** uses the same body — the SAR is the rifle upgrade |

## Meta verdict — **A/S tier (value)**

Pound-for-pound the **best value gun in Rust**. It carries you from your first workbench all the way to fighting AK players — a headshot-heavy SAR player beats a sloppy AK player. Cheap enough to never feel bad losing. Upgrades to the loot-only [[M39 Rifle]] and craftable [[SKS]]. The mandatory mid-wipe rifle for solos/duos. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: SKS
pages.body:
# SKS

The **SKS** is an accurate, mid-damage semi-automatic rifle. It received a **significant overhaul** and was **bumped from Workbench T2 to T3** — so it now sits between the [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] (T2) and the loot-only [[M39 Rifle]] as a **craftable** military-grade marksman rifle. New since you last played (added Nov 2024, reworked since).

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **42.5** |
| Fire rate | **400 RPM** (semi-auto) |
| Magazine | **15** (extendable to **19** with an [[Extended Magazine]]) |
| Ammo | [[5.56 Rifle Ammo]] (+ variants) |
| Effective range | mid–long, very accurate |
| Recoil | low–moderate per shot |

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T3** |
| Craft cost | 12 [[High Quality Metal]], 200 Metal Fragments, 1 Semi Automatic Body, 2 Metal Spring |
| Craft time | 30 s |
| Research cost | 120 scrap |

## Drop sources (also loots)

[[Locked Crate]]s (~5.6%), Ghostship/Oilrig locked crates, Scientist PT Boat drybox (~3%), [[Elite Crate]]s (~2%).

## Attachments

Loves a scope — its accuracy and 400 RPM make it a strong [[8x Scope]]/[[16x Scope]] DMR. The +4-round [[Extended Magazine]] is a meaningful upgrade given the small base mag.

## Meta verdict — **A tier**

A **craftable semi-auto DMR** that splits the difference between the cheap SAR and the loot-only M39. Higher per-shot damage and fire rate than the SAR with comparable accuracy — a great pick for players who like deliberate, headshot-focused rifle play and don't want to gamble on M39 loot. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Sound & Audio Cues
pages.body:
# Sound & Audio Cues

Sound is half of Rust. The other half is shooting, and you only get to shoot the people you heard first. Every meaningful action in this game makes a positional, identifiable sound — a gunshot tells you the weapon class and rough distance, a footstep tells you direction and surface, a hammer-thunk a kilometre away tells you someone is upgrading or being raided. A returning solo/duo/trio who learns to *read* audio will win fights against better aimers who don't, because you choose every engagement and never get the surprise peeked on you.

This page is the "what does that noise mean" manual. For the systems behind it see [[Combat Mechanics]] (the sound-detection section) and [[PvP Tips]] (how to weaponise sound discipline in a fight). For per-weapon stats see the [[Weapons]] folder.

> **Headphones are not optional.** Rust's audio is fully positional (3D HRTF). Speakers collapse left/right and destroy front/back distinction. Cheap wired headphones beat expensive speakers for this game every time. If you take one thing from this page: **wear a headset, and turn your master volume up enough that footsteps are audible.**

---

## 1. Identifying weapons by gunshot

Two things to extract from a gunshot before you do anything else: **what is it** (tells you the threat level and their gear tier) and **roughly how far** (tells you whether to fight, hide, or third-party).

### Sound range by weapon class (Sep 2025 audio overhaul — verified)

The September 2025 update tied a gun's *audible range* to its class, and removed the old trick where shooting from inside cover masked the sound. You are now louder than you think.

| Class | Example weapons | Audible range |
|-------|-----------------|---------------|
| Pistols & SMGs | [[M92 Pistol]], [[Python Revolver]], [[Custom SMG]], [[MP5A4]], [[Thompson]], [[Handmade SMG]] | **~400 m** |
| Assault rifles | [[Assault Rifle]] (AK), [[LR-300]], [[SKS]], [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] | **~500 m** |
| Heavy / long range | [[Bolt Action Rifle]], [[L96]], [[M249]] LMG, [[Handmade LMG]], M16A2 | **~600 m** |

That means a single AK burst pulls roamers from two grid squares away. Sound discipline (silencers, picking fights away from your base, not test-firing in the open) is now a real solo/duo skill, not a nicety. See the **silencer** section below to cut that range to a fraction.

### Telling guns apart by ear

You learn these by playtime, but here are the distinguishing fingerprints:

| Weapon | Sound fingerprint |
|--------|-------------------|
| [[Eoka Pistol]] | A *click* (misfire) then occasionally a flat *pop*. The click without a bang = someone trying to eoka-raid a door near you. **Drop everything and check your loot room.** |
| [[Waterpipe Shotgun]] / [[Shotguns#Double Barrel\|Double Barrel]] | Deep, slow, wet *boom*. One or two then a long reload. Means early-game / low gear. |
| [[Revolver]] | Sharp, dry, slightly tinny crack, slow cadence. |
| [[Python Revolver]] / [[M92 Pistol]] | Snappy, higher-pitched pistol crack; M92 can dump fast. |
| [[Custom SMG]] / [[MP5A4]] | Fast, light, "rippy" full-auto buzz; MP5 is smoother and faster. Means a P2 player is committed. |
| [[Thompson]] | Lower, "chuggier" full-auto than the SMGs; slower RPM, meatier per-shot. |
| [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] (SAR) | Punchy single cracks, medium pitch, can fire fast semi. Classic mid-tier. |
| [[SKS]] | Similar to SAR but a touch deeper/heavier — a T3 semi. |
| [[Assault Rifle]] (AK) | The iconic deep, chunky full-auto *brap*. Means you are fighting a geared player. |
| [[LR-300]] | Crisper, slightly higher-pitched and "tighter" than the AK. |
| [[Bolt Action Rifle]] | A single loud *CRACK* then the unmistakable *cha-chunk* bolt cycle. The bolt sound is your tell to peek — they can't shoot during it. |
| [[L96]] | Like the bolt but louder and deeper; sniper threat at very long range. |
| M39 / [[M39 Rifle]] | Fast, sharp semi-auto, distinctive rapid "tink" cadence. |
| [[M249]] / [[Handmade LMG]] | Sustained heavy full-auto roar that doesn't stop reloading — loot-room or roof defender. |
| M16A2 | Distinctive 3-round-**burst** pattern (brrp … brrp), then a pause. New "Built Different" rifle. |

**Crack-thump for distance & direction.** A supersonic bullet makes two sounds: the *crack* of it passing you, then the *thump* of the muzzle. The longer the gap between crack and thump, the farther away the shooter. The **thump** points at the shooter; the **crack** points at where the bullet went. If you only hear the thump (no crack), the round didn't pass near you — you're not the target yet.

---

## 2. Footsteps — direction, distance, intent

Footsteps are the single richest source of intel in Rust. They tell you presence, direction, distance, movement speed, and what surface someone is standing on (which often tells you *where* in your base they are).

### Movement state vs noise

| Movement | Key | Noise level | When you'll hear it |
|----------|-----|-------------|---------------------|
| **Sprint** | default while moving | **Loudest** — audible the farthest | Roamers, pushes, someone running to your door |
| **Walk** | Sprint toggle off / holding walk | Medium | Cautious approach, holding angles |
| **Crouch-walk** | hold Crouch + move | **Near-silent on most surfaces** | The stealth standard — see below |
| **Crouch idle** | Crouch, stationary | Silent | Holding an angle, waiting in a bush |

### The crouch-walk silence trick (the most important movement habit in Rust)

**Crouch-walking removes essentially all footstep sound on most surfaces.** This is the core stealth mechanic: when you approach an enemy base, a contested monument, or a possible loot room, you crouch-walk so you generate no positional audio. The trade-off is you're slow and your hipfire/jiggle options shrink — but you arrive unheard.

Conversely, **assume any competent enemy is crouch-walking when hunting you.** Silence does not mean empty. Inside your own base during a defend, expect the attacker to be crouching toward your TC — watch for the *other* cues (door sounds, building hits) rather than footsteps.

> Some surfaces and edge cases still leak a faint sound when crouched. Treat crouch-walk as "very quiet," not "guaranteed inaudible," and don't crouch-walk directly onto a metal floor next to someone's headset and expect zero risk.

### Surfaces — loud vs quiet

The surface you (or they) stand on changes the footstep timbre *and* loudness. This is how you locate someone inside a base without seeing them.

| Surface | Loudness | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------|
| Metal / sheet-metal floor & roofs | **Loud, hollow "clang"** | The loudest common surface — running on a metal roof telegraphs a roof-camp or a counter from above |
| Wood floors / [[Building#Tiers\|wood building]] | Loud-ish, "thunky" | Distinct hollow wood knock; tells you they're on a wooden tier |
| Stone / concrete (monuments) | Medium, sharp | Hard footstep crack; common at [[Monuments\|monuments]] |
| Gravel / road | Medium, "crunchy" | Roads carry sound well |
| Dirt / sand | Quieter, softer | |
| Grass / forest floor | **Quietest natural surface** | Approach through grass, not across roads/rocks |
| Water (shallow) | Loud splashing | Swimming/wading is very audible — see vehicles below |
| **Rugs / [[Furniture\|deployed rug]]** | **Silences footsteps** | Players carpet loot rooms and roofs so defenders/raiders can't hear them move inside |

**Practical use:** if you hear a hollow metal clang above you mid-fight, someone is on your roof. A "thunk-thunk" on wood while you're raiding means a defender is moving on the floor above. Match the surface sound to your mental map of the base.

### Other body sounds that give position away

- **Reloads** — distinct mechanical sound; a reload is your cue to peek and trade.
- **Eating / drinking** — audible chewing/gulp; people heal up between fights and get peeked.
- **Healing** — bandage/syringe/medkit use makes noise (see [[Meds & Healing]]).
- **Jumping / landing** — a landing thump, especially from height.
- **Vomiting** (overeating), bleeding groans, taking damage — all positional.

---

## 3. Building & raid sounds — "you are being raided"

This is the category that saves your loot. Rust's building actions are loud and carry far, so you can often hear a raid begin from across the map and decide whether to defend, log, or counter.

### Construction / interaction cues

| Sound | What it means |
|-------|---------------|
| **Hammer "thunk" (repeated)** | Someone is **upgrading or repairing** a wall/door. Near your base = a raider opened a wall and is now sealing themselves in, OR a teammate building. Far = someone establishing nearby. |
| **Building plan placement / "snap"** | A structure being placed — a foundation, a ladder, a raid base going up next to you. |
| **Rotation wheel / radial open** | The upgrade/rotate radial — minor, close-range only. |
| **Ladder placement & climbing** | The wooden ladder creak. Hearing a ladder on your wall = **someone is ladder-raiding into your compound or onto your roof right now.** |
| **Door open / close** | Distinct creak + latch. Hearing your *own* doors open when you didn't = an intruder is inside, or your door got blown and they're walking through. |
| **Code lock beep** | The keypad *beep-beep* on entry, and the rejection buzz on a wrong code. Hearing beeps in your base = someone with the code (teammate) — or someone brute-forcing/has the code. |
| **Garage door / drawbridge / electric** | Heavy motorised grind — large doors and [[Electricity\|powered]] doors cycling. |

### Raid sounds (audible from very far — this is your early warning)

| Sound | Tool / threat |
|-------|---------------|
| **Deep repeated *BOOM* (explosions)** | [[Raid Costs\|Rockets / C4 / explosives]] hitting walls. The flagship "someone is being raided" sound — carries across grids. Count the booms to gauge how deep they are. |
| **Hissing fuse then *pop*** | [[Raid Costs#Satchel Charges\|Satchel charge]] or beancan — cheaper raids, common on doors/twig. |
| **Repeated heavy whacks on a wall** | **Hammering a soft-side wall** or [[Raiding\|melee/jackhammer raid]] — someone found your weak side. |
| **Sustained drilling / sawing** | [[Raiding#Jackhammer\|Jackhammer]] cutting through. |
| **Eoka click (no bang) at a door** | Early-game eoka door raid — cheap but real; check loot. |
| **[[Events#Patrol Helicopter\|Heli]] / siege weapon impacts** | See sections 4 & 5. |

When you hear explosions near home as a solo/duo: don't sprint blind to your TC. Sound-read the *count* and *direction* first, then decide — many raids are baited to draw the owner out. See [[Counter-Raiding]] for the full defend playbook and [[PvP Tips#Third-partying|third-partying]] for cashing in on someone else's raid.

---

## 4. Vehicles, animals & environment

| Sound | Meaning / range cue |
|-------|---------------------|
| **[[Modular Cars\|Car]] / [[Vehicles\|vehicle]] engine** | Loud, carries far — a car rolling up is rarely friendly. Sedan/modular engines and horns are very audible. |
| **[[Minicopter]]** | High, buzzy rotor whine — audible a long way; air threat or someone fleeing. |
| **[[Scrap Transport Helicopter\|Scrap Heli]]** | Deeper, heavier rotor than the mini. |
| **[[Boats\|Boat / RHIB]] motor** | Water-borne approach to coastal/oil bases. |
| **[[Horses\|Horse]] gallop / hooves** | Distinct clip-clop; a horse roamer or escape. |
| **Swimming / wading** | Loud splashes — never approach a coastal base through deep water expecting stealth. |
| **Wolf growl / [[Wolves\|wolf]]** | PvE threat while roaming (added Nov 2024); jungle adds tigers/panthers/crocs/snakes. A growl behind you mid-loot can get you killed. |
| **Bear / boar** | Heavy animal noises; bears especially. |

### Event audio (free intel about the server)

| Event | Audio cue | Why it matters |
|-------|-----------|----------------|
| **[[Events#Patrol Helicopter\|Patrol Helicopter]]** | The unmistakable heavy, ominous rotor + minigun *brrrt* | Heli is on the map — loot opportunity and a danger zone; everyone nearby hears it and may converge. |
| **[[Events#Cargo Ship\|Cargo Ship]]** | Distant ship horn / engine on the coast | Cargo has spawned — geared PvP destination. |
| **[[Events#Bradley APC\|Bradley APC]]** | Tank engine + cannon *boom* at [[Launch Site]] | Bradley is alive/being fought; expect players there. |
| **[[Events#CH47 Chinook\|Chinook (CH47)]]** | Twin-rotor heavy thrum | Locked-crate drop incoming — a hot PvP magnet. |
| **[[Events#Supply Drop\|Supply Drop]] plane** | Prop-plane drone overhead | A cargo plane / airdrop is passing — loot falling somewhere. |
| **[[Siege Weapons\|Siege weapons]]** (Catapult/Ballista/Battering Ram/Mortar) | Heavy launch *thunk* + impact | Group base assault in progress nearby. |

---

## 5. Direction, distance & occlusion (how to actually locate a sound)

Rust's audio engine gives you real directional and distance information if you let it:

- **Direction (panning + HRTF):** with headphones, sound pans left/right and front/back. Front-vs-back is the hardest axis — when unsure, **turn your character slightly and listen for the sound to shift sides.** If it moves to your left when you turn right, it was behind you.
- **Distance (volume + clarity):** far sounds are quieter *and* muffled/reverberant; close sounds are sharp and dry. A crisp footstep is *right there*; a dull, echoey one is across the room or outside.
- **Occlusion:** walls, floors and terrain muffle and lower sounds. A footstep that suddenly gets sharp and loud = they just stepped into your room / line of audio. Use the muffle-to-clear transition as your peek trigger.
- **The crack-thump gap** (section 1) is your best long-range distance estimator for gunfire.

In a fight, **stop moving for a half-second to listen** — your own footsteps and reloads drown out theirs. Many players lose 1v1s simply because they never stopped making noise long enough to hear the flank.

---

## 6. Silencers — controlling *your* signature

Going quiet is as valuable as hearing. Suppressors let a solo/duo take fights or raid without summoning every roamer and third-party on the grid.

| Attachment | Tier | Effect (verified) |
|-----------|------|-------------------|
| **Military Silencer** | T3 (loot / craft) | **−25% damage and −25% projectile velocity**; **removes muzzle flash and bullet tracers**; reduces recoil slightly; collapses gunshot audible range to a fraction of the unsuppressed value (on the order of tens of metres vs the 400–600 m class ranges above). |
| **Oil Filter Silencer** | T2 (craftable) | The craftable mid option — stealth + flash/tracer removal with a damage trade. Superior to the soda-can. |
| **Soda Can Silencer** | T1 (craftable) | Cheapest, most fragile suppressor; low durability but functional early stealth. |

Note Facepunch added **craftable silencers (Jun 2025)** so you no longer need to loot one — this materially changed the sound meta for solos. The exact suppressed sound radius isn't published as a single official number across sources, but the design intent and community testing put a suppressed shot's range at a small fraction of the unsuppressed class range. See per-attachment detail in [[Attachments]].

**Practical silencer play:**
- Roaming solo/duo: silencer + no muzzle flash means you can open fire from cover without broadcasting your position to the whole grid or pulling a third party.
- Raiding: suppressed shots while clearing a base reduce the "free intel" you hand to nearby roamers — though the **explosions** still give the raid away.
- Cost: the damage/velocity penalty means longer time-to-kill and more drop at range, so it's a trade, not free.

---

## 7. Audio settings to maximise awareness

Tune the game so footsteps and shots are loud and clear and nothing drowns them out.

**In-game (Options → Audio):**

| Setting | Recommendation | Why |
|---------|----------------|-----|
| **Master Volume** | High enough that footsteps are clearly audible | The whole point — don't run it so low you miss approaches. |
| **Game / Effects Volume** | High | Footsteps, gunshots, building sounds live here. Keep it up. |
| **Ambient / Wind / Environment** | **Lower** | Wind, water, and ambient nature mask footsteps. Turning ambience down raises the signal-to-noise on threats. |
| **Music** | **Off / minimal** | In-game music has no tactical value and masks cues. |
| **Voice / Voice Chat Volume** | Balance *below* effects | If proximity/team voice is louder than footsteps, you'll talk over the flank you needed to hear. Keep voice present but not dominant. |
| **Instruments** | Low | Other players' instruments are noise pollution. |

**Hardware / OS:**
- **Use headphones, not speakers** — positional audio (front/back, left/right) only works on headphones. This is the biggest single upgrade to your game-sense.
- **Stereo, not virtual-surround upmixers** — Rust already does HRTF positional audio in stereo. Third-party "7.1 virtual surround" often *muddies* it. Plain stereo headphone output is usually best; test both.
- **Optional EQ:** community guides boost the **~1–4 kHz** band where footstep transients live to make steps pop. Helpful but secondary — get the in-game balance right first.
- **Windows volume mixer:** make sure Rust isn't ducked by other apps; keep Discord/voice apps balanced so a loud Discord doesn't drown footsteps.

---

## Quick reference — "what does that sound mean?"

| You hear… | It probably means… | Do this |
|-----------|--------------------|---------|
| Eoka *click* (no bang) at a door | Someone eoka-raiding nearby | Check loot room, peek the door |
| Hammer *thunk thunk* near home | Upgrading/sealing — possibly a raider walling in | Investigate cautiously; sound-read direction |
| Deep repeated **BOOM** | Rocket/C4 raid in progress | Count booms + direction; defend, log, or third-party |
| Hiss + *pop* | Satchel/beancan raid (cheaper) | Likely a door/twig — check soft side |
| Ladder creak on your wall | Ladder-raid into compound/roof | Get to a peek/turret angle fast |
| Door open you didn't open | Intruder inside or blown door | Treat as a breach; ready a weapon |
| Hollow metal clang above | Player on your roof | Look up / hold the roof access |
| AK *brap* within ~500 m | Geared player fighting nearby | Decide: avoid, position, or third-party |
| Bolt *CRACK* + *cha-chunk* | Sniper — and they can't shoot mid-cycle | Peek on the bolt sound |
| Ominous heavy rotor + *brrrt* | Patrol Heli on the map | Loot chance / danger zone — others converge |
| High buzzy rotor | Minicopter inbound/fleeing | Air threat; take cover or AA it |
| Sudden *silence* near you | Enemy crouch-walking | Don't assume empty — hold and listen |

---

## Related

- [[PvP Tips]] — sound discipline, third-partying, fight selection
- [[Combat Mechanics]] — the sound-detection system, crouch, aim cone
- [[Counter-Raiding]] — defending when you hear the boom
- [[Attachments]] — silencer stats in detail
- [[Weapons]] — per-gun damage/RPM/recoil
- [[Events]] — heli/cargo/Bradley/Chinook audio
- [[Vehicles]] — engine/rotor signatures

Sources: rust.facepunch.com news/devblogs (Sep 2025 sound range overhaul, Jun 2025 craftable silencers), wiki.facepunch.com (Military Silencer item page), rusthelp.com (silencer −25% damage/velocity), gamer.org (400/500/600 m class ranges), corrosionhour.com (silencer behaviour, muzzle flash/tracer removal), community footstep/audio-settings guides (surface loudness, crouch-walk silence, EQ). Verified June 2026.

pages.title: Thompson
pages.body:
# Thompson

The **Thompson** is the classic **snowball SMG** — a low-recoil, high-close-range-damage 9mm gun craftable at Workbench T2. It's the gun you make right after your first [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] or [[Revolver]] to start killing geared players and stealing kits. Forgiving recoil makes it the best SMG for newer/returning players.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | **37.5** |
| Headshot damage | ~75 (2x) |
| Fire rate | **~462 RPM** |
| DPS | ~289 |
| Magazine | **20** |
| Ammo | [[Pistol Ammo]] (9mm) |
| Effective range | short–mid (~250 m falloff) |
| Recoil | **low–medium**, very controllable |

## Recoil pattern

**Very easy to use** — a low, mostly **vertical climb with slight horizontal wobble** and a gentle slope, far flatter than the MP5 or AK. Compensation is little more than a soft, steady downward pull; the slower fire rate gives you time to correct between shots. This is the Thompson's whole identity: you trade the MP5's fire rate for a recoil pattern almost anyone can hold on target. Great for run-and-gun early-wipe roaming.

## Craft & unlock

| | |
|------|-------|
| Workbench tier | **T2** |
| Craft cost | ~10 [[High Quality Metal]], 100 Wood, 1 SMG Body, 1 Metal Spring |
| Ammo | cheap 9mm |

## Meta verdict — **A tier**

The ultimate **snowball weapon**: low skill floor, low cost, cheap ammo, real lethality. Once you have an AK/MP5 it's outclassed, but as a wipe-day kit-stealer it's one of the best value guns in the game. See [[Rust Weapons]] and the early-game gun ladder ([[Revolver]] → [[Semi-Auto Rifle]] → [[Thompson]] → [[MP5A4]]/[[Assault Rifle]]).

pages.title: Waterpipe Shotgun
pages.body:
# Waterpipe Shotgun

The **Waterpipe Shotgun** is the cheapest gun in Rust — a single-shell, Tier-1 improvised shotgun that's the **wipe-start one-tap** weapon. Massive point-blank damage, then a long single-shell reload.

## Core stats

| Stat | Value |
|------|-------|
| Body (chest) damage | ~180 (point-blank) |
| Head dmg | ~210 |
| Fire rate | ~13 RPM (one shell, slow reload) |
| Magazine | **1** |
| Ammo | [[Shotgun Ammo]] (Handmade Shell) |
| Effective range | very short |
| WB tier | **T1** |

## Meta verdict — **D/C tier (wipe start)**

The classic wipe-day weapon: cheap, lethal at point-blank, but **one shot then you're vulnerable**. You ambush a naked or low-armor player, one-tap, and grab their stuff. Pairs with melee for the second target. Outclassed instantly by any real gun. See [[Rust Shotguns]] and [[Eoka Pistol]] (the even-cheaper gamble alternative).

pages.title: Weapon Attachments
pages.body:
# Weapon Attachments

Reference for weapon mods (attachments) — sights, muzzles, and barrel mods that slot into a gun's attachment rail. Most rifles have **4 slots**; pistols/SMGs fewer. Each gun page lists its slot count. Cross-references [[Rust Weapons]] and [[Rust Ammo]].

## Sights (aim/zoom)

| Attachment | Effect | Best on |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| **Holosight** | clean red-dot reticle, minor zoom, fast target acquisition | [[Assault Rifle]], [[MP5A4]], [[LR-300]] — close-mid |
| **8x Zoom Scope** | strong magnification | [[Bolt Action Rifle]], [[SKS]], [[M39 Rifle]] — mid-long |
| **16x Zoom Scope** | max magnification, long-range | [[L96]], Bolt — sniping |
| **Variable Zoom Scope (4x/8x/16x)** | adjustable magnification in one optic (newer) | flex DMR/sniper builds |
| **Simple Handmade Sight** | crude T1 iron sight | early-wipe guns |

> The **Variable Zoom Scope** (toggle 4x / 8x / 16x) is a quality-of-life addition since you last played — one optic covers all ranges instead of swapping scopes.

## Muzzle attachments

| Attachment | Effect | Trade-off |
|-----------|--------|-----------|
| **Muzzle Boost** | **increases fire rate / DPS** | widens aim cone slightly (worse accuracy) |
| **Muzzle Brake** | **reduces recoil** (tames the spray) | slightly reduces damage |
| **Silencer** | **removes muzzle flash + greatly reduces gunshot audibility**; no tracer | small velocity/damage penalty |

> **Craftable silencers** arrived **June 2025** — previously loot/research only. A silencer now matters more because **gunshots are audible at 400/500/600 m by weapon class** (Sep 2025); suppressing your AK is real stealth. The **Silencer** is the single most valuable mod for solo roamers who don't want to broadcast their position.

## Barrel / under-barrel

| Attachment | Effect |
|-----------|--------|
| **Laser Sight** | tightens **hip-fire** aim cone | good on SMGs/[[Custom SMG]] for CQC |
| **Extended Magazine** | **+ magazine capacity** (e.g. [[SKS]] 15 -> 19) | slightly slower ADS |
| **Flashlight** | lights dark areas | situational; gives you away |
| **Weapon Lasers / others** | minor utility | niche |

## Recommended loadouts

- **AK roam (range):** [[Holosight]] or 8x Scope + Silencer + Muzzle Brake.
- **AK roam (DPS):** Holosight + Muzzle Boost (accept the wider cone for close fights).
- **MP5/SMG CQC:** Holosight + Laser Sight + Muzzle Boost.
- **Bolt/L96 sniping:** 16x Scope (no muzzle boost — preserve accuracy).
- **SKS/SAR DMR:** 8x or Variable Scope + Extended Magazine + Silencer.

Remember the [[May 2024 aimcone overhaul]]: a Muzzle Boost's accuracy penalty matters less if you **tap-fire**, since the cone resets between bursts. See [[Rust Weapons]].

pages.title: Counter-Raiding
pages.body:
# Counter-Raiding

Two meanings, both covered here:
1. **Defending mid-raid** — fighting back when someone is actively raiding *your* base.
2. **Third-partying a raid** — hitting a group while *they* are raiding someone else (they're committed, distracted, and their loot is in a vulnerable FOB).

## Defending your own base mid-raid

You logged in (or were online) and someone's booming your walls. Goals: kill them, make them retreat, or at least bleed their resources.

- **Hold the breach.** Don't run out the front — let them break a wall and funnel into your kill zone. You have angles and cover; they're exposed in the hole they made. Pre-place a [[Shotgun Trap]]/turret on the likely breach corridor (see [[Raid Defense]]).
- **Counter-boom their entry.** If they've opened one layer, you can re-wall behind it (build block) or drop a wall to reset the funnel. Every wall you replace makes them pay again.
- **Stash/relocate loot** the instant a raid starts — move the good stuff to a hidden box or out a back exit while they're still breaking the shell. Raiders often spend full boom to reach an empty room.
- **Call neighbors / clanmates.** Even a 1v2 becomes winnable if you can pincer them in the breach.
- **Bag management:** if you die, respawn somewhere they can't bag-camp (a hidden bag, not the loot room). Don't feed them your kit repeatedly through the same door.

## Third-partying a raid (counter-raiding others)

A group raiding a base is the most profitable target in Rust: they've sunk thousands of sulfur into the raid, their loot + the victim's loot is concentrated, and they're focused on the wall, not on you.

- **Identify the FOB.** Raiders set up a [[Forward Operating Base]] (sleeping bags + boxes + a TC) within walking distance to respawn and store loot. The FOB is softer than the base being raided — hit *it* and you starve their respawns and grab the spoils.
- **Attack from the side/back** while they're committed to the breach. A flank from your own FOB stops them holding both you and the raid.
- **Wait for the open base.** Sometimes the cheapest counter-raid is to let them finish, kill them on the way out, and walk into the now-doorless base they already opened — you pay zero boom.
- **Bring a fight kit, not a raid kit.** This is a gunfight, not a wall break: armor, a good rifle, meds, and re-supply at your bag. Backpacks drop on death (since Feb 2024), so winning the fight literally hands you their boom.

## Raid bases / FOBs (your offensive infrastructure)

A **raid base / FOB** is a small throwaway base you build next to your target before a raid:

- **Purpose:** respawn point (sleeping bags), boom storage, armor/med resupply, and a defensive position vs counter-raiders/third parties.
- **Build it cheap and fast** — twig/wood, just enough to hold a TC, bags, and a few boxes. It's disposable.
- **Place it within sprint range** of the target so deaths cost seconds, not a cross-map run.
- **Defend it:** a couple of [[Shotgun Trap]]s or a turret on the door stops a third party from rolling your respawns while you're inside the raid.
- For air raids, the FOB can also be a repad/refuel point — though the **Nov 2025 heli nerf** (no in-flight repair) makes ground FOBs less able to keep a damaged [[Attack Helicopter]] flying.

## Key takeaways

- The most committed player in a raid is the most vulnerable — **patience beats boom.**
- Whoever controls respawn (closest bag / FOB) usually wins the attrition fight.
- Loot concentrates during raids; a clean third-party can net you a whole raid's worth of explosives for one good fight.

## Related
[[Raid Methods]] · [[Raid Defense]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Forward Operating Base]] · [[Shotgun Trap]] · [[Auto Turret]] · [[Attack Helicopter]]

pages.title: Eco-Raiding
pages.body:
# Eco-Raiding

"Eco" raiding = breaking in with the **cheapest possible resources**, usually before you have C4 or even a T3 workbench. This is the solo/duo/trio bread and butter on wipe day and against wood/stone bases. The whole idea: spend less in materials than the loot is worth, even if it takes longer and more hits. Compare against the full table in [[Raid Costs]].

## The eco toolkit (cheapest to most)

| Tool | Cost | WB | What it breaks | Notes |
|------|------|----|----------------|-------|
| Salvaged Axe (soft-side) | wood only | none | wood walls/doors (soft side) | 20-30 hits soft side; free but slow + loud |
| Spear (throw, soft-side) | wood only | none | wood, soft-sided roofs | the most "eco" tool — wood only |
| Eoka + Handmade Shells | ~5 sulfur/shell | none | wood doors | **45 shells = wooden door = 225 sulfur**; handmade shells craft with stone, no metal/WB |
| Molotov / fire | low (cloth + low grade) | none | wood walls/doors | **2 molotovs = wood wall**; fastest cheap wood raid, spreads |
| [[Incendiary Rocket]] | 300 sulfur | 2 | wood structures | 1 burns a wooden door; can't touch stone+ |
| Beancan Grenade | 120 sulfur | 1 | doors/TC | duds; 18 = sheet door |
| [[Homemade Landmine]] | 60 sulfur | 2 | doors | cheapest sulfur/door if you can place them flat; 12 = sheet door (720) |
| Satchel Charge | ~480 sulfur | 1 | doors, early walls | the pre-C4 wall option; duds |

## Wipe-day playbook (day 1-2)

Bases are wood and twig. Targets are soft and full of hoarded loot.

1. **Look for twig.** 10 HP — melee straight through any exposed twig wall/foundation. Free.
2. **Burn wood.** Molotovs (2 = wood wall) or a single [[Incendiary Rocket]] on a wooden door. Fire is the cheapest fast wood raid and ignores soft/hard side.
3. **Eoka the doors.** If you've got nothing else, 45 handmade shells (stone-crafted, no WB) pop a wooden door for ~225 sulfur. Slow and loud but needs zero progression.
4. **Soft-side roofs with spears.** Aim a thrown spear at the soft side of a roof tile to break in from above on cheap bases — costs only wood.
5. **Take the TC.** Once inside, the [[Tool Cupboard]] is 100 HP — a few melee hits or 8 explosive rounds. Owning the TC lets you tear the rest down for free.

## Mid-wipe eco (stone bases)

Fire and eoka stop working on stone. Now eco means **landmines, beancans, and satchels** instead of C4:

- **Doors:** Homemade Landmines are the sulfur king — 12 for a [[Sheet Metal Door]] (720) vs 1 C4 (2,200). You trade time + metal for sulfur. Great for solos who farm more metal than sulfur.
- **Walls:** satchels (10 = [[Stone Wall]], ~4,800 sulfur) get you through stone without a T3 bench, but C4 (2 = 4,400) is actually cheaper *and* faster once you can craft it — so eco-walling stone is usually a stopgap, not a plan.
- **Soft-side everything.** Get through one layer cheaply, then the inner walls cost ~25% less.

## When eco-raiding is worth it

- You have **time** (offline target, no third-party pressure).
- You're **sulfur-poor but resource-rich** (lots of wood/metal/cloth, few sulfur nodes farmed).
- The target is **wood/stone**, not armored — eco tools fall off hard vs sheet metal and are useless vs armored.
- The loot is **modest** — don't burn an hour of beancans for a base that's clearly empty.

## When to stop and just use C4

- Target is **online** (slow eco raids get you killed; you need speed).
- Walls are **sheet metal/armored** — satchels/beancans become more sulfur than C4 anyway.
- You're being **third-partied** — every minute you're booming, someone's coming for the loot.

## Returning-player note

The Oct/Nov 2025 progression rework (Blueprint Fragments + cheap research) means you reach satchels/beancans fast, but **C4 still needs Tech Trash** (monument loot), so the eco window where you have boom-but-no-C4 is real. Landmines (WB2, May-2026-era item per the index) are the standout new eco door tool — cheapest sulfur per door in the game.

## Related
[[Raid Costs]] · [[Explosives]] · [[Raid Methods]] · [[Eoka Pistol]] · [[Homemade Landmine]] · [[Incendiary Rocket]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Tech Tree]]

pages.title: Explosives
pages.body:
# Explosives

Everything that breaks a wall in Rust traces back to **sulfur**. You mine sulfur ore, smelt it into sulfur, burn it (with charcoal) into [[Gunpowder]], then craft gunpowder up into the boom. This page is the full craft chain with the sulfur math so you know exactly what to farm. Costs feed directly into [[Raid Costs]].

## The base chain

### Gunpowder (Workbench 1)
- **30 Charcoal + 20 Sulfur -> 10 Gunpowder**
- So **1 gunpowder = 2 sulfur + 3 charcoal**. Charcoal is basically free (burns out of wood in any furnace/campfire), so gunpowder cost ~= 2 sulfur each.
- Crafted at a Mixing Table much faster/cheaper than by hand — always use a Mixing Table for bulk.

### Explosives (the component, Workbench 3)
- **50 Gunpowder + 3 Low Grade Fuel + 10 Sulfur + 10 Metal Fragments -> 1 Explosives**
- Raw sulfur per Explosives = 50 gp x 2 + 10 = **110 sulfur** (plus the LGF/metal).
- "Explosives" is just an ingredient — you never use it directly; it goes into C4 and rockets.

## The booms

### Timed Explosive Charge (C4) — Workbench 3
- **20 Explosives + 5 Cloth + 2 Tech Trash**
- Raw sulfur = 20 x 110 = **2,200 sulfur** each.
- New since 2023: the **2 Tech Trash** requirement gates C4 behind monument loot (Tech Trash comes from recycling/monument crates), not just sulfur. You can have a mountain of sulfur and still be C4-starved.
- Best single-target breaker. 1 C4 = 1 [[Sheet Metal Door]]. 2 = [[Stone Wall]]. Sticks to the surface (no aiming a flight path) and detonates on a timer.

### Rocket — Workbench 3
- **2 Metal Pipe + 150 Gunpowder + 10 Explosives**
- Raw sulfur = 150 x 2 + 10 x 110 = 300 + 1,100 = **1,400 sulfur** each.
- Fired from a [[Rocket Launcher]]. Splash damage means one rocket can hit multiple honeycomb walls — better than C4 for opening bulk walls, worse per-HP on a single target.

### Incendiary Rocket — Workbench 2
- **2 Metal Pipe + 150 Gunpowder + 75 Low Grade Fuel**
- Raw sulfur = 150 x 2 = **300 sulfur** each.
- Sets fire to wooden structures; CANNOT destroy stone or armored. The cheapest answer to a wood base or a wooden door (1 incendiary rocket burns a wooden door for 300 sulfur). Can also start fires *through* walls to flush hiders.

### High Velocity Rocket — Workbench 3
- **1 Metal Pipe + 100 Gunpowder** -> raw sulfur = **~200 each** (100 gp x 2). Cheaper, faster, flatter-flying than a standard rocket but does much less structure damage.
- Used for shooting [[Auto Turret]]s and players at range, NOT for breaking walls. Don't raid bases with these.
- **The one big PvE exception: HV is the cheapest [[Bradley APC]] kill** — **4 minimum (bring 6–7)** into Bradley's rear/treads, vs 8 standard rockets or 3 C4. At ~200 sulfur each, 4–7 HV is far cheaper than the C4 route. Full count table in [[Raid Costs]].

### Satchel Charge — Workbench 1
- **4 Beancan Grenades + 1 Small Stash + 1 Rope**
- Raw sulfur = 4 x 120 = **~480 sulfur** each.
- The classic no-T3 raid tool: you can satchel a base before you ever unlock C4. Downside: has a **dud chance** (can fail and need a re-throw) and you need more of them (4 satchels = 1 sheet door vs 1 C4).

### Beancan Grenade — Workbench 1
- **60 Gunpowder + 20 Metal Fragments**
- Raw sulfur = 60 x 2 = **120 sulfur** each.
- Cheapest craftable throwable. Unreliable (random fuse length, can dud). 18 beancans pop a sheet door. The feeder ingredient for satchels.

### Homemade Landmine — Workbench 2
- **50 Metal Fragments + 30 Gunpowder**
- Raw sulfur = 30 x 2 = **60 sulfur** each.
- The cheapest sulfur-per-damage door breaker in the game if you have TC/floor access to place them: lay them flat against a door and detonate. 12 = sheet door (720 sulfur), 48 = armored door (2,880). Metal-heavy, sulfur-light — great when you're swimming in metal frags but short on sulfur.

### Explosive 5.56 Rifle Ammo — Workbench 3
- **~25 sulfur per round** (crafted from gunpowder + sulfur + metal).
- Not a "boom" — you shoot it out of a rifle. Great for soft targets: [[Tool Cupboard]] (8 rounds), [[Auto Turret]] (106), wood walls (47). Terrible against stone+. Doubles as a weapon, so it's never wasted.

## Sulfur-per-boom summary

| Explosive | Raw sulfur | WB | Notes |
|-----------|-----------|----|----|
| Beancan Grenade | 120 | 1 | duds |
| Homemade Landmine | 60 | 2 | needs placement access, metal-heavy |
| Satchel Charge | ~480 | 1 | duds, no T3 needed |
| Incendiary Rocket | 300 | 2 | wood only |
| Rocket | 1,400 | 3 | splash |
| C4 | 2,200 | 3 | + 2 tech trash; best single target |
| Explosive 5.56 | 25/rd | 3 | soft targets, also a weapon |

## Farming-it math (rough)

- Sulfur ore -> sulfur: smelt 1:1-ish in a furnace. A full night of sulfur fields/quarry gets a duo a few thousand sulfur.
- **One C4 = 2,200 sulfur ~= a solid sulfur-node grind session.** Cracking even a small base (say 4 sheet doors deep = 4 C4) is **~8,800 sulfur** — that's the real "raid cost" most people underestimate.
- Always recycle components: a recycler gives back metal frags, pipes, and tech trash you can re-roll into the next batch. Monument recyclers (5s / 120% yield since May 2024) beat safe-zone recyclers.

## Related
[[Raid Costs]] · [[Gunpowder]] · [[Sulfur]] · [[Mixing Table]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Workbench]] · [[Eco-Raiding]] · [[Raid Methods]]

pages.title: Raid Costs
pages.body:
# Raid Costs

The master reference: how many of each explosive it takes to break every common obstacle, and what that costs in **raw sulfur**. Counts re-verified June 13 2026 against RustLabs-successor data and cross-checked against the current **"Built Different" update (live Jun 4 2026)** — that patch was a player-model / armor / M16A2 drop and **changed no building HP, door HP, explosive damage, or raid costs**, so every number below is current. For the craft chains behind these explosives see [[Explosives]].

## How to read this

- **Raw sulfur** = total sulfur burned all the way down the chain (sulfur -> gunpowder -> explosive). The per-boom anchors are: **C4 = 2,200**, **Rocket = 1,400**, **Satchel = 480**, **Beancan = 120**, **Homemade Landmine = 60**, **Explosive 5.56 = 25/round**.
- **Soft vs hard side:** Stone, sheet metal and armored walls take ~25% less boom from the *inside* (soft side). Numbers below are the **hard side** (worst case) unless noted. Doors, garage doors and external walls have no soft side.
- Counts are rounded UP to whole explosives — you always overpay slightly because you can't throw a fraction of a C4.

## Walls (hard side)

| Wall | HP | C4 | Rockets | Satchels | Beancans | Explo 5.56 | Cheapest sulfur |
|------|----|----|---------|----------|----------|-----------|-----------------|
| Twig Wall | 10 | — | — | — | — | 1 | melee / 1 round |
| Wood Wall | 250 | 1 | 1 | — | — | 47 | fire / 47 explo (1,175) |
| [[Stone Wall]] | 500 | 2 | 4 | 10 | 46 | 185 | **2 C4 = 4,400** |
| Sheet Metal Wall | 1,000 | 4 | 8 | 23 | 131 | 400 | **4 C4 = 8,800** |
| Armored Wall | 2,000 | 8 | 15 | 46 | 223 | 799 | **8 C4 = 17,600** |

Sheet metal & armored walls: the soft (inside) side drops to ~3 C4 (sheet) / ~6 C4 (armored) — always breach from inside if you can reach it.

## Floors & foundations

Floors and foundations share the **exact HP of the wall of the same tier**, so the raid counts are identical to the Walls table. A floor has a "soft" (top) and "hard" (underside) side, but for satchels the count **rounds to the same number on both sides** — soft-side makes no practical difference on a stone floor. You almost never raid floors/foundations directly (walls and doors are the path of least resistance); the main exceptions are ceiling/floor breaches into a loot room or splitting a bunker.

| Tier | HP | C4 | Rockets | Satchels | Beancans | Explo 5.56 |
|------|----|----|---------|----------|----------|-----------|
| Twig | 10 | — | — | — | — | 1 |
| Wood | 250 | 1 | 1 | — | — | 47 |
| **Stone** | **500** | 2 | 4 | **10** | 46 | 185 |
| Sheet Metal | 1,000 | 4 | 8 | 23 | 131 | 400 |
| Armored | 2,000 | 8 | 15 | 46 | 223 | 799 |

**Stone floor = 500 HP = 10 satchels (either side).** Raw cost for 10 satchels: **4,800 sulfur** + 2,400 gunpowder (7,200 charcoal) + 800 metal fragments + 10 rope + 100 cloth. Note that 4 rockets (5,600 sulfur) or 2 C4 (4,400 sulfur) break the same floor — **2 C4 is cheaper and far faster than satchels** on stone, and satchels have a 20% dud chance on top of that. Satchels are only the "cheap" pick when you're sulfur-starved early wipe and can't yet craft C4.

## Doors

| Door | HP | C4 | Rockets | Satchels | Beancans | Landmines | Explo 5.56 | Cheapest sulfur |
|------|----|----|---------|----------|----------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| Wooden Door | 200 | — | — | 2 | 5 | 4 | 16 | fire (1 incendiary rocket / arrows) — 2 satchels = 960 if you already have them |
| [[Sheet Metal Door]] | 250 | 1 | 2 | 4 | 18 | 12 | 63 | **12 landmines = 720** (1 C4 = 2,200 is faster) |
| Garage Door | 600 | 2 | 3 | 9 | 42 | 29 | 150 | **29 landmines = 1,740** |
| Armored Door | 1,000 | 3 | 5 | 15 | 69 | 48 | 250 | **48 landmines = 2,880** (3 C4 = 6,600 faster) |

The sheet metal door is the single most common raid target in the game: **1 C4 pops it.** That 1-C4 break point is why most solo/duo loot rooms hide behind multiple sheet doors + airlocks rather than one fat door.

## External walls & gates

| Structure | HP | Craft cost | C4 | Rockets | Satchels |
|-----------|----|-----------|----|---------|----------|
| High External Wood Wall | 500 | 1,000 wood | 1 | 2 | — (2 incendiary rockets is cheapest — wood burns) |
| High External Wood Gate | 500 | 1,500 wood | 1 | 2 | — (2 incendiary rockets is cheapest) |
| [[High External Stone Wall]] | 500 | 4,000 stone (3 walls / 1 sheet metal) | 2 | 4 | 10 |
| High External Stone Gate | 500 | 3,000 stone + 5 gears | 2 | 4 | 10 |

External stone walls share the **same HP as a stone wall (500)** but you usually don't raid them — you ladder over, shoot through, or gate-camp. Wood external walls burn.

## Deployables & defenses

| Target | HP | C4 | Rockets | Explo 5.56 | Cheapest |
|--------|----|----|---------|-----------|----------|
| [[Tool Cupboard]] | 100 | — | — | 8 | **8 explo = 200** |
| Auto Turret | 1,000 | 2 | 3 (+7 explo) | 106 | 3 rockets or shoot it offline |
| Sleeping Bag | 50 | — | — | melee | melee |
| Large Wood Box | 250 | — | — | — | melee/explo |
| Locker | 100 | — | — | — | melee |
| Vending Machine | 1,250 | 5 | — | — | 5 C4 |
| Workbench T3 | 1,000 | — | — | — | melee once inside |

The **Tool Cupboard at 100 HP** is the soft underbelly of every base — 8 explosive 5.56 rounds (200 sulfur) destroys it. Take the TC and you can place your own, then peel the base apart from inside for free. Most of the raid cost is just *reaching* the TC.

## Bradley APC (PvE explosive target)

Bradley is **explosive-only** — bullets, fire and melee do nothing to its hull. **1,000 HP**, and it **regenerates** if left undamaged for 5 minutes (regen takes ~60s to fully heal), so commit fully once you start.

| Method | Count to kill | Notes |
|--------|--------------|-------|
| **HV Rocket** | **4 minimum** (bring 6–7) | Cheapest viable kill. Aim the **rear/treads**; the front armor and a missed shot waste rockets, which is why guides quote a **4–7** range. 4 hit cleanly = dead; bring spares for misses. |
| **Rocket (regular)** | **8** | Works but ~2x the sulfur of HV for the same job — HV is strictly more sulfur-efficient on Bradley. |
| **C4** | **3** | Fast and reliable but expensive (6,600 sulfur). Use only if you have boom to burn and want a guaranteed instant kill. |
| **Explosive 5.56** | ~500–600 rounds | Technically works, never worth it. |
| **F1 Grenade** | ~40–50 | Cheap-metal option; risky to land enough. |

**Verdict for a solo/duo:** craft **4–7 HV rockets** (1 metal pipe + 100 gunpowder each), peek from cover at Launch Site, dump them into the rear. HV is the canonical cheapest Bradley kill in 2026 — the "4 vs 7" spread is purely about your aim, not a balance change. Drops 3 crates (M249/L96 tier). See [[Explosives]] for the HV craft chain and [[Bradley APC]] for the fight itself.

## Decision rules (sulfur-efficiency)

1. **Always raid the lowest-tier obstacle on the path to loot.** A sheet door (1 C4) beats a sheet wall (4 C4) every time.
2. **Soft-side walls.** Get inside any layer and the inner walls cost ~25% less.
3. **Landmines/beancans for doors when you have time and metal but little sulfur** (early/mid wipe).
4. **C4 for speed, rockets for splash.** C4 is the cheapest per-HP for a *single* target; rockets are better when one shot's blast radius damages multiple walls (honeycomb open-ups).
5. **Explosive 5.56 for soft targets** — TC, turrets, wood, exposed deployables. Awful against stone+.

See [[Raid Methods]] for how to actually execute, [[Eco-Raiding]] for the cheap early-wipe paths, and [[Raid Defense]] for how bases drive these costs up.

pages.title: Raid Defense
pages.body:
# Raid Defense

Making your base expensive enough that raiders walk past it. You can't make a base unraidable — everything dies to enough boom — but you can make the **sulfur cost of reaching your loot exceed the value of your loot**. That's the whole game of defense. Costs raiders pay are in [[Raid Costs]].

## The core principle: raid-cost scaling

Every wall layer between the outside and your loot multiplies the C4 count. A loot room behind:
- 1 [[Stone Wall]] = 2 C4 (4,400 sulfur)
- honeycombed by 2 more layers = 6 C4 (13,200 sulfur)

You want raiders to do the math and decide you're not worth it. Make the **cheapest line to loot still expensive.**

## Honeycomb

Honeycomb = extra walls placed around your core so each one must be broken before reaching loot. Key rules:

- **Surround the loot, not the whole base.** Honeycomb the inner core; the outer shell can be thinner.
- **Stagger walls so rockets can't "mill through" in a straight line** — offset layers so one rocket's splash doesn't damage two layers at once.
- **Combine horizontal and vertical honeycomb** (wall rings AND ceiling/floor layers) so the cheapest path isn't through the roof or floor.
- Cost to you: stone is cheap, but **upkeep scales with building** — a heavily honeycombed base burns a lot of stone/hour in the TC. Balance defense vs upkeep.

## Tool Cupboard protection

The [[Tool Cupboard]] is your weakest point — **100 HP, dies to 8 explosive 5.56 (200 sulfur).** If raiders reach and destroy it, they place their own and disable your decay protection / building privilege.

- **Hide the TC** deep in the core, behind the loot, or in a bunker — never near an outer wall.
- **Backup TCs** (multiple in privilege range) so popping one doesn't hand them building rights.
- Wall the TC off separately so it's not in the same room they breach first.

## Bunkers

A bunker is a sealed compartment (usually below the base) that must be raided **twice** — once to get in, once to reach the bunker loot — for little extra build cost. The classic is a **2x1 with a hatch bunker**: cheap, low upkeep, and your best loot sits behind an extra raid the attacker has to pay for. Bunkers extend defense depth downward for the price of a hatch + a few walls. See [[Bunker Bases]].

## Turrets and traps

| Defense | Power? | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| [[Auto Turret]] | Yes (10 power) | Most powerful. Craft WB2 + 50 HQM. Shoots authorized-exempt targets automatically. **40m interference cap (Oct 2023)** — turrets too close to each other interfere, so you can't stack a wall of them. 1,000 HP, but a raider can kill it offline with 3 rockets/106 explo. |
| Shotgun Trap | No | Fires 12-gauge at anyone unauthorized in a funnel. Great in narrow corridors/airlocks. No friend/foe — authorize yourself. |
| Flame Turret | No (low grade fuel) | Sprays napalm in tight corridors; continuous damage, excellent in choke points. |
| [[Seismic Sensor]] (2026) | Yes | Detects nearby explosions and outputs a signal — wire to lights/alarms for an offline-raid alarm. |
| Tin Can Alarm (2026) | No | Throwable tripwire rigging — early warning. |

Turrets/traps don't stop a determined raid but they **tax online raiders and slow offliners**, buying you time to log in or counter. Put them where raiders are forced to funnel (airlocks, the breach corridor).

## Anti-offline design

Solos/duos lose most loot to offline raids. Defenses that work while you sleep:

- **Depth + honeycomb** so an offliner can't crack the whole base before you wake.
- **Hidden loot:** small spread-out boxes / a hidden bunker box, not one big loot room. Raiders may breach and miss the real stash.
- **Decoy loot rooms** to make them spend boom on empty space (misdirection).
- **Seismic Sensor -> phone/Discord-style alarm** (via electricity) so you know the moment a raid starts.
- **Premium / TPM 2.0 servers** (2025-26) cut cheaters who'd otherwise wallhack to your loot room — a meta-level "defense."
- Keep the **base small.** A solo base that's cheap and deep beats a big base that's expensive to upkeep and full of breach angles.

## What NOT to do

- Don't put your TC or best loot against an outer wall.
- Don't build a single fat door — multiple sheet doors + airlocks cost more total C4 than one armored door, and create kill funnels.
- Don't over-honeycomb past what you can afford in upkeep — a decayed base is a free raid.
- Don't rely on external walls alone; they're laddered/gate-camped, not raided.

## Related
[[Raid Costs]] · [[Counter-Raiding]] · [[Bunker Bases]] · [[Auto Turret]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Seismic Sensor]] · [[Base Building]] · [[Raid Methods]]

pages.title: Raid Methods
pages.body:
# Raid Methods

How to actually execute a raid once you know the [[Raid Costs]]. Methods break down by *when* you hit (online vs offline) and *how* you get in (boom path vs no-boom tricks).

## Online vs offline raiding

| | Online raid | Offline raid |
|---|---|---|
| **When** | Target is logged in | Target is asleep/away |
| **Pro** | All their loot is there; satisfying | No defenders shooting back; relaxed |
| **Con** | They shoot back, can counter-raid, may stash loot | They may have hidden/removed loot; bag-camp risk on return |
| **Risk** | High — bring a fight kit per person | Low combat, high time pressure (they could log in) |

Solo/duo/trio reality: **offline is the default.** You rarely have the numbers to win an online raid against an established group. Scout the base, learn their online hours (or use a [[Seismic Sensor]]/decay timing), and hit when they're gone. Bring exactly the boom from your raid-cost plan plus ~20% buffer for misjudged walls.

## The boom path

1. **Scout first.** Walk the base, count wall layers and doors, find the loot room (usually center or top). Note TC location — popping the [[Tool Cupboard]] (100 HP, 8 explo) lets you place your own and disable theirs.
2. **Pick the cheapest line to loot** (see decision rules in [[Raid Costs]]). Doors > walls. Soft-side > hard-side.
3. **Open the shell, then soft-side inward.** Once inside any layer, interior walls cost ~25% less.
4. **C4 the doors, rocket/satchel the walls.** Use explosive 5.56 to mop up the TC, boxes, turrets.
5. **Loot fast and leave a bag plan** — you'll likely have to make trips; place a sleeping bag nearby or use your [[Forward Operating Base]] (FOB).

## No-boom / cheap tricks

These get you in without (much) sulfur:

- **Soft-siding (raid tools/melee):** Walls take far more damage from the soft (inside) side and from tools than the hard outside. Jackhammer/explosives on the soft side of a roof or floor can be cheaper than a wall break. **Spears soft-side roofs** on cheap early bases (see [[Eco-Raiding]]).
- **Ladder raiding:** A [[Wooden Ladder]] placed inside an open compound or against a low wall lets you climb into an unfinished base or over external walls. Cheap, silent, and doubles as an escape route out of a blast radius. You need a foothold (you can't ladder a flush exterior wall).
- **Twig raiding:** If a base has any **twig** building blocks exposed (10 HP), you can melee straight through them, or place your own twig steps/foundations to climb. Common against rushed wipe-day bases.
- **Open doorways / unfinished bases:** Wipe day, half the map has a missing wall or an un-upgraded twig section. Just walk in.
- **Window/embrasure shooting:** Not entry, but you can kill defenders or shoot the TC through an open window/[[Embrasure]] before committing boom.

## Silent raiding

Footsteps and explosions alert online defenders and neighbors (gunshots are audible **400/500/600m** by weapon class since Sep 2025; explosions trigger [[Seismic Sensor]]s). To stay quiet:

- **Crouch-walk** — the only fully silent movement.
- **Jackhammer/satchel-free entries** where possible; beancans and C4 are loud.
- **Garage door + key tricks**, lockpicking-style soft entries on misbuilt bases.
- Hit during **server-wide events** (heli, cargo, airdrop) when the noise blends in and players are distracted.

## Raid timing

- **Early wipe (day 1-2):** bases are wood/twig — fire, spears, beancans. Cheap and high-value (people hoard wipe-day loot). See [[Eco-Raiding]].
- **Mid wipe:** stone bases, satchels/landmines/early rockets. The grind sweet spot for solos.
- **Late wipe:** armored bunkers, you need C4 stacks and a real plan. Often not worth it for a solo — eco-raid weaker neighbors instead.
- **Pre-wipe:** people dump loot or go offline; good for cleanup raids but loot may be spent.

## Vehicle & siege raiding (returning-player note)

- **Siege weapons** (Catapult, Battering Ram, Ballista, Siege Tower, Mortar — added 2025-26) give a whole no-C4 raid path at WB2: lob boulders/propane bombs at stone, ram doors, climb with a tower. Slower and louder but sulfur-light.
- **Attack Helicopter** (2,250 scrap at Bandit Camp) can rocket-pod a base from the air — but the **Nov 2025 nerf** removed in-flight repair and made flares useless vs homing missiles, so heli raids are riskier. A defender with a [[Homing Missile Launcher]] can swat you.

## Related
[[Raid Costs]] · [[Explosives]] · [[Eco-Raiding]] · [[Raid Defense]] · [[Counter-Raiding]] · [[Tool Cupboard]] · [[Tech Tree]]

pages.title: Raiding
pages.body:
# Raiding

Raiding is Rust's endgame: breaking into another player's base to take their loot. Everything in a raid reduces to **sulfur math** — every explosive is ultimately crafted from sulfur (via [[Gunpowder]]), so raid planning means comparing the sulfur cost of each path into the base against the expected loot.

This folder is the raiding reference for the vault. All numbers verified against rusthelp.com (the RustLabs successor); the July 2026 **[[Common Ground Update]]** changed **no** building HP or explosive damage, so every sulfur cost below is still current.

> **Softcore raid windows (July 2026, [[Common Ground Update]]):** on **softcore servers only**, building blocks and doors (walls/floors/roofs/doors/ladder hatches) can by default **only be damaged 6-9 PM local server time** — outside that window an active TC (>=1h old) blocks structure raids. **Deployables (TC not yet protecting, turrets, boxes, external walls) stay raidable 24/7.** The sulfur costs per wall/door/deployable are **unchanged** — this only gates *when* you can apply them. Vanilla servers are unaffected (raid anytime). Server-configurable.

## Pages

- [[Raid Costs]] — THE reference table: exact explosive counts + sulfur for every wall grade, door, external wall, and deployable
- [[Explosives]] — full craft chains (gunpowder → explosives → C4/rockets), workbench tiers, sulfur-per-boom math
- [[Raid Methods]] — online vs offline, door camping, ladder/twig raiding, silent raiding, landmine stacking
- [[Siege Weapons]] — Catapult, Battering Ram, Ballista, Siege Tower, Mortar (all new since Feb 2025)
- [[Raid Defense]] — honeycomb, turrets, traps, raid alarms, anti-offline design
- [[Counter-Raiding]] — defending mid-raid, third-partying, raid bases
- [[Eco Raiding]] — cheapest entries for fresh wipe: fire vs wood, landmines, beancans

## What changed since 2023 (raiding-relevant)

If you last raided in ~2023, these are the load-bearing changes:

| Change | When | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Armored Door buffed to 1,000 HP** (was 800) | by 2026 | Now 3 C4 / 5 rockets / 250 explo ammo |
| **Homemade Landmine added** (WB2, 60 sulfur) | 2026 | New cheapest door-breaker: 12 break a sheet door for 720 sulfur |
| **Siege weapons** (Catapult, Battering Ram, Ballista, Siege Tower + shields) | Feb 2025 | Whole WB2 no-C4 raid path; propane bombs + boulders vs stone |
| **Mortar artillery** | May 2026 | Indirect-fire raiding from range; shells are WB2, 300 sulfur each |
| **Explosive protection capped at 75%** | May 2025 | Defenders can no longer face-tank splash in stacked kits |
| **Vending machine buffed to 1,250 HP** | by 2026 | 5 C4 — no longer a cheap "door" to go through |
| **Seismic Sensor + Tin Can Alarm** | May 2026 | Defenders get electrical raid alarms; explosions have detectable "vibration levels" |
| **Wolves/predator AI, party system, backpacks** | 2024–25 | Backpacks drop on death — raid casualties now drop their boom in a backpack |
| **Blueprint Fragments progression** | Oct–Nov 2025 | T3 boom requires monument fragment grinding first — see [[Tech Tree]] |
| **Attack Helicopter flare nerf** | Nov 2025 | Heli raids: flares no longer fool homing missiles, no in-flight repair |

## The 10-second cheat sheet

Cheapest practical "boom" cost per common obstacle (full table with all methods in [[Raid Costs]]):

| Obstacle | HP | Cheapest sulfur path |
|---|---|---|
| Wooden Door | 200 | 1 Incendiary Rocket — **300 sulfur** |
| Sheet Metal Door | 250 | 12 Homemade Landmines — **720 sulfur** |
| Garage Door | 600 | 29 Homemade Landmines — **1,740 sulfur** |
| Armored Door | 1,000 | 48 Homemade Landmines — **2,880 sulfur** (or 250 explo ammo, 6,250) |
| Stone Wall | 500 | 2 C4 — **4,400 sulfur** (4 catapult propane bombs = 3,600) |
| Sheet Metal Wall | 1,000 | 7 rockets + 15 explo — **10,175 sulfur** |
| Armored Wall | 2,000 | 8 C4 — **17,600 sulfur** |
| Tool Cupboard | 100 | 8 explo ammo — **200 sulfur** |
| [[Bradley APC]] (PvE, 1,000 HP) | — | 4 HV rockets (bring 6–7) — ~**800–1,400 sulfur**; vs 8 rockets or 3 C4 |

Rule of thumb: **doors are almost always cheaper than walls** of the same tier — raid through doors when the base design lets you. Garage doors and armored doors have **no soft side**.

## Related

[[Tech Tree]] · [[Workbench]] · [[Sulfur]] · [[Mixing Table]] · [[Base Building]] · [[Bunker Bases]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Bradley APC]] · [[Airdrop]]

pages.title: Rust Cheat Sheet
pages.body:
# Rust Cheat Sheet

The "I just need the number, now" page. Every figure here is the headline number pulled from its full wiki page, re-verified June 13 2026 against rusthelp / wiki.facepunch.com / rustmods and cross-checked against the live **[[Built Different Update]]** (Jun 4 2026) — that patch was a player-model / armor / M16A2 drop and **changed no building HP, door HP, explosive damage, raid costs, or vendor prices**, so everything below is current for the June 2026 wipe.

Each section links to the page that has the full context. If you need the *why*, follow the link. If you just need the *number*, it's here.

---

## 1. Raid costs (raw sulfur) — [[Raid Costs]]

Counts rounded **up** to whole explosives; sulfur is the **total burned down the whole chain**. Walls shown **hard side** (worst case); soft/inside side is ~25% cheaper.

### Walls
| Wall | HP | C4 | Rockets | Satchels | Beancans | Cheapest sulfur |
|------|---:|---:|--------:|---------:|---------:|-----------------|
| Wood Wall | 250 | 1 | 1 | — | — | fire / 47 explo 5.56 (~1,175) |
| [[Stone Wall]] | 500 | 2 | 4 | 10 | 46 | **2 C4 = 4,400** |
| Sheet Metal Wall | 1,000 | 4 | 7 | 23 | 131 | **4 C4 = 8,800** |
| Armored Wall | 2,000 | 8 | 15 | 46 | 223 | **8 C4 = 17,600** |

### Doors
| Door | HP | C4 | Rockets | Satchels | Beancans | Landmines | Cheapest |
|------|---:|---:|--------:|---------:|---------:|----------:|----------|
| Wooden Door | 200 | — | — | — | — | — | fire / 16 explo (400) |
| [[Sheet Metal Door]] | 250 | **1** | 2 | 4 | 18 | 12 | **1 C4 = 2,200** (12 mines = 720 cheaper, slower) |
| Garage Door | 600 | 2 | 3 | 9 | 42 | 29 | 29 mines = 1,740 |
| Armored Door | 1,000 | 3 | 5 | 15 | 69 | 48 | 48 mines = 2,880 (3 C4 faster) |

### Soft targets & misc
| Target | HP | Cheapest break |
|--------|---:|----------------|
| [[Tool Cupboard]] | 100 | **8 explo 5.56 = 200** (the soft underbelly — take it, place yours) |
| Auto Turret | 1,000 | 3 rockets, or shoot it while offline |
| High External Stone Wall/Gate | 500 | 2 C4 / 4 rockets (usually ladder over instead) |
| High External Wood Wall/Gate | 500 | 2 incendiary rockets (it burns) |
| [[Bradley APC]] | 1,000 | **4 HV rockets** (bring 6–7), or 8 rockets, or 3 C4 |

> Rule: always raid the **lowest-tier obstacle on the path to loot**. A sheet door (1 C4) beats a sheet wall (4 C4) every time. Get inside one layer and inner walls cost ~25% less.

---

## 2. Explosive craft costs (raw sulfur each) — [[Explosives]]

| Explosive | Raw sulfur | Workbench | Note |
|-----------|-----------:|:---------:|------|
| Explosive 5.56 | **25 / round** | 3 | soft targets, also a weapon |
| Homemade Landmine | **60** | 2 | metal-heavy, needs placement access |
| Beancan Grenade | **120** | 1 | duds; feeds satchels |
| High Velocity Rocket | **~200** | 3 | turrets/Bradley, NOT walls |
| Incendiary Rocket | **300** | 2 | wood only |
| Satchel Charge | **~480** | 1 | no-T3 raid tool, duds |
| Rocket | **1,400** | 3 | splash (2 pipe + 150 gp + 10 explosives) |
| **C4 (Timed Explosive)** | **2,200** | 3 | best single-target; **+2 Tech Trash** gate |

Chain anchors: **1 Gunpowder ≈ 2 sulfur** (30 charcoal + 20 sulfur → 10 gp) · **1 Explosives = 110 sulfur** (50 gp + 3 LGF + 10 sulfur + 10 frags). C4 = 20 Explosives; rocket = 150 gp + 10 Explosives.

---

## 3. Smelting & furnaces — [[Smelting & Furnaces]]

| Question | Answer |
|----------|--------|
| Ore → refined ratio | **always 1:1** |
| Metal / sulfur smelt time | **2.5 s** each |
| HQM smelt time | **10 s** each (4x slower — your bottleneck) |
| Wood per 1,000 metal ore (small furnace) | **~500 wood** (~0.5 wood/ore) |
| Wood → charcoal | **~75%** — 1,000 wood → ~750 charcoal |
| Small furnace slots | **6** (1 fuel / 1–2 output / ~3 ore) |
| Large furnace slots | **18** (T2; ~40% the wood of small for metal, ~1/3 for HQM) |
| Electric furnace | **3 rW, 0 wood, 0 charcoal**, can NOT smelt HQM |
| Where to refine HQM | a normal **furnace** (NOT the oil refinery) |
| Oil Refinery ratio | 1 Crude Oil → **3 Low Grade Fuel** |

> More furnaces never costs more wood — splitting ore across 5 furnaces uses the same total wood as 1, just **5x faster**. Build a furnace bank.

---

## 4. Radiation thresholds — what to wear — [[Armor]]

Radiation is **points subtracted** from the zone rate, not a percent. Carry **total protection ≥ zone strength** → take zero rads. Protection stacks across all worn pieces.

| Zone strength | Tier | Example monuments | Protection needed | Cheapest kit |
|--------------:|------|-------------------|------------------:|--------------|
| **~26** | Low | [[Satellite Dish]], [[Sewer Branch]], Harbor | **~10–15** | Full **Burlap** set |
| **~52** | Medium | [[Airfield]], [[Trainyard]], [[Water Treatment Plant]] | **~15–20** | Burlap + Wood Armor, or a Hazmat |
| **~81** | High | [[Power Plant]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Cargo Ship]] | **~25** | **Hazmat Suit** (25) alone clears it |
| **~100** | Extreme | [[Oil Rig]] reactor, [[Underwater Labs]] core, Launch VAB | **~30–40+** | **Hazmat + lead set** (25+15=40) or hazmat + Anti-Rad Pills |

Key item rad values: **Hazmat = 25** · lead piece = 5 each (set = 15) · gas mask = 2 · burlap set ≈ 10–12. A Hazmat alone clears low/medium/high — most players just keep one in a box.

---

## 5. Upkeep brackets — [[Upkeep and Decay]]

Daily upkeep = sum of each block's build cost × its bracket rate (game averages across all blocks). TC consumes the **same material the block is made of**.

| Bracket | Block count | Tax / day |
|--------:|-------------|----------:|
| 0 | blocks 1–15 | **10%** |
| 1 | blocks 16–65 | **15%** |
| 2 | blocks 66–190 | **20%** |
| 3 | blocks 191+ | **33.3%** |

Decay timers (empty/no TC): Twig ~1h · Wood **3h** · Stone **5h** · Sheet **8h** · Armored **12h**. TC-destroyed grace = **24h** before decay starts. Lesson: **stay under ~65 blocks** to keep cheap brackets, and over-stock the TC before logging off.

---

## 6. Vendor prices (scrap)

### Keycards — [[Keycards & Monument Puzzles]] · all at [[Bandit Camp]]
| Card | Scrap | Swipes |
|------|------:|-------:|
| [[Green Keycard]] | **15** | ~4 |
| [[Blue Keycard]] | **40** | ~4 |
| [[Red Keycard]] | **80** | 2 |
| **Full set (G+B+R)** | **135** | — |

[[Outpost]] no longer sells the Blue Keycard (removed Oct 2025). Fuses + cards bought at Bandit, not Outpost.

### Vehicles — Airwolf vendor at [[Bandit Camp]] (air) / Boat vendor at [[Fishing Villages|Fishing Village]] (sea)
| Vehicle | Scrap | HP | Where |
|---------|------:|---:|-------|
| [[Minicopter]] | **750** | 750 | Airwolf |
| [[Scrap Transport Helicopter\|Scrap Heli]] | **1,250** | 1,000 | Airwolf |
| [[Attack Helicopter]] | **2,250** | 850 | Airwolf |
| [[RHIB]] | **300** | 500 | Boat (Fishing Village) |
| [[Rowboat]] | ~125 | 400 | Boat (Fishing Village) |

All helis: 30 LGF/min, 500 tank → ~16 min 39 s flight; explode on death; decay 8h outside / 48h inside. RHIB: 15 LGF/min, 500 tank → ~33 min.

---

## 7. Recycler yield rule — [[Recycling]]

| Recycler | Yield | Speed |
|----------|------:|-------|
| **Safe-zone** ([[Outpost]], [[Bandit Camp]]) | **~40%** of full | slower |
| **Monument** (Harbor, [[Ferry Terminal]], radtowns, [[Junkyard]], etc.) | **~100%** (~60% *more* than safe zone) | faster |

Always end a [[Scrap Runs|scrap run]] at a **monument recycler** — same loot in, more scrap and components out. Worth carrying loot a little farther to a hot recycler than dumping it at Outpost.

---

## 8. Workbench costs + fragment gates — [[Workbenches]]

No scrap at any tier since "Pivot Or Die" (Nov 2025). Gate is now **[[Blueprint Fragments]]**.

| Bench | Wood | Metal Frags | HQM | Fragments | Needs |
