|-------|-----:|------------:|----:|-----------|-------|
| [[Workbench Level 1\|WB1]] | 500 | 100 | — | — | none (default) |
| [[Workbench Level 2\|WB2]] | — | 500 | 20 | **5 Basic** | WB1 |
| [[Workbench Level 3\|WB3]] | — | 1,000 | 100 | **5 Advanced** | WB2 |

Fragment math: **T2 = 5 Basic** (green rooms give 1 each → ~3 green runs; blue-near-red rooms give 2 → ~2 runs). **T3 = 5 Advanced** (red rooms / [[Elite Crate]]s / hacked [[Locked Crate]]s / [[Cargo Ship]]). **20 Basic → 1 Advanced** fallback. Higher bench = faster craft (each tier ~halves the time).

---

## 9. Key HP values

| Structure | HP | | Item | HP |
|-----------|---:|---|------|---:|
| Twig wall/floor | 10 | | [[Sheet Metal Door]] | 250 |
| Wood wall | 250 | | Wooden Door | 200 |
| [[Stone Wall]] | 500 | | Garage Door | 600 |
| Sheet Metal wall | 1,000 | | Armored Door | 1,000 |
| Armored wall | 2,000 | | Wood Box (large) | 250 |
| High External (wood) | 500 | | [[Tool Cupboard]] | 100 |
| High External (stone) | 500 | | Auto Turret | 1,000 |

Furnace HP: small **500** / large **1,500** / electric **500**. [[Minicopter]] 750 · [[Scrap Transport Helicopter\|Scrap Heli]] 1,000 · [[Attack Helicopter]] 850 · [[RHIB]] 500 · [[Bradley APC]] 1,000.

---

## See also

The full pages behind every number above:
[[Raid Costs]] · [[Explosives]] · [[Smelting & Furnaces]] · [[Armor]] · [[Upkeep and Decay]] · [[Keycards & Monument Puzzles]] · [[Recycling]] · [[Workbenches]] · [[Scrap Runs]] · [[Building Basics]] · [[Tech Tree]] · [[Built Different Update]]

> [!note] Verification
> All numbers re-verified June 13 2026 against rusthelp.com, wiki.facepunch.com, rustmods.com, and the source wiki pages listed in each section. The Built Different update (Jun 4 2026) touched the player model, the Ballistic armor set, and the M16A2 — it did **not** change any structure HP, explosive damage, raid cost, smelt rate, upkeep bracket, or vendor price. Re-check the explosive/HP tables at the next progression-affecting patch; vehicle prices float slightly with vendor demand since Jul 2024.

pages.title: Rust Glossary
pages.body:
# Rust Glossary

An A-Z reference for the slang, jargon, and abbreviations you'll hear in global chat, on streams, and in guides. Rust's community has a dense vocabulary and most of it is never explained in-game — this page is the decoder ring. Terms are grouped by category; within each category they're roughly alphabetical. Where a full vault page exists, the term links to it.

> Sulfur and raid numbers cited here are verified against the **"Built Different" update (live Thu June 4 2026)** and the current [[Raid Costs]] page. Built Different was a player-model / armor / [[M16A2]] drop and changed **no** building HP, explosive damage, or sulfur costs — so all raid anchors below are current. Per-boom sulfur anchors: **C4 = 2,200 · Rocket = 1,400 · Satchel = 480 · Beancan = 120 · Explosive 5.56 = 25/round.**

---

## Player states & gear

- **Naked** — A fresh, ungeared player wearing nothing (or near-nothing). Often used as a verb/insult ("got killed by a naked"). The default sleeper/spawn look.
- **Fresh spawn** — A player who just (re)spawned on the beach with a [[Rock]] and a torch. Has nothing to lose, so they're aggressive and annoying ("fresh spawn rushed me with a rock"). Spawning on the coast with starter gear is "spawning fresh."
- **Kit** — A loadout. As a noun it's "a kit" (gun + armor + meds + ammo); as a verb, "kit up" = grab a full set of gear. A "full kit" usually means rifle + good armor + meds.
- **Geared** — Wearing strong gear: a top-tier rifle ([[Assault Rifle|AK]], [[LR-300]]) plus metal/[[Roadsign|roadsign]] or [[Armor|Ballistic]] armor. Opposite of naked. "Geared player" = high-value kill, high risk to engage.
- **Prim / primitive** — Low-tier gear: burlap/leather armor, bows, [[Eoka Pistol|eokas]], [[Revolver|revolvers]], crossbows. Common early-wipe and on no-workbench servers. "Prim and proper" = a wipe-start where everyone is in prim gear.
- **Gear fear** — The reluctance to fight or take risks because you're carrying good loot you don't want to lose. The #1 reason geared players play passively. "I had gear fear so I logged."
- **Sleeper** — Your character's body when you log off — it lies down where you disconnected and is fully lootable/killable by anyone who finds it. "Got killed in my sleep" = murdered offline. The basis of [[#Server, meta, and play styles|offline raiding]].
- **Bag / sleeping bag** — A [[Sleeping Bag]] or bed; your respawn point. "Set a bag here" = place a respawn near where you're working/raiding so you can come back fast. Bags have a respawn cooldown. Raiders place bags near the target ("bag in") so deaths don't cost them the trip.
- **Roof camper** — A player who sits on their (or a tall) roof and snipes passers-by from relative safety. Mildly derogatory; roof camping is safe but low-effort.
- **Door camp** — Lying in wait outside a base (or inside a doorway) to ambush occupants when they come or go. Common during a raid or to catch a sleeper logging in.

## Base & building

- **TC** — [[Tool Cupboard]]. The block that claims your building area and stores [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]] resources. "Got TC'd / found the TC" = located/destroyed the cupboard, which lets a raider place their own and take over (or stop decay protection). "TC access" = authed on the cupboard.
- **Twig / wood / stone / metal / armored** — The five [[Stability|building grades]], cheapest to strongest. **Twig** (free, placeholder, dies to one bullet) → **Wood** (250 HP, burns) → **Stone** (500 HP) → **Sheet Metal / metal** (1,000 HP) → **Armored** (2,000 HP, top tier). You upgrade walls through these with a [[Hammer|hammer]]. See [[Raid Costs]] for HP and boom per grade.
- **Soft side** — The [[Soft Side|inside]] face of a stone/metal/armored wall, which takes ~25% **more** damage from explosives than the outside (hard) side. Raiders hunt for an exposed soft side (a window, a wall facing into a compound) to breach cheaper. "They left a soft side" = a build mistake.
- **Honeycomb** — Layering extra triangle/square walls around your loot room so a single breached wall opens into another empty cell instead of your loot. Named for the cell pattern. More honeycomb = more boom to reach loot. The core of solo/duo defense.
- **Open core** — A base design where the central rooms are connected/open rather than each individually walled, trading [[Open Core vs Closed|raid cost for build cost and convenience]]. Opposite of a "closed core." Cheaper to build, easier to raid once the shell is cracked.
- **Bunker** — A [[Bunkers|sealed compartment]] (often a foundation/wall "skip" or shotgun-trap room) with no normal door, accessible only via a building trick (e.g., un-deploying a wall, twig-and-rotate). Hides loot from raiders who can't reach it without massive extra boom. See [[Bunkers]].
- **Airlock** — A small double-door chamber at the entrance so opening the outer door doesn't expose your interior. Stops [[#Server, meta, and play styles|door camping]] / shooting straight into your base. "Run an airlock" = build one.
- **Loot room / core** — The innermost room holding your boxes, TC, and crafting. The "core" is what every defense is built to protect and what every raid is trying to reach.
- **Deployables** — Player-placed objects: boxes, furnaces, [[Workbenches|workbenches]], beds, [[Auto Turrets|turrets]], [[Traps|traps]], etc. "Deploy" = place one. Many can't be placed on twig.
- **Decay** — Passive HP loss on structures over time when [[Upkeep and Decay|upkeep]] isn't paid. Wood decays fastest, armored slowest. A base with no resources in the TC "decays out."
- **Upkeep** — The resource cost (in the [[Tool Cupboard|TC]]) to keep your base from decaying. Bigger/higher-tier bases cost more upkeep per period. "Upkeep is killing me" = base too big to feed.
- **Shotgun trap** — A [[Traps|deployable trap]] that fires a shotgun blast at unauthed players in front of it; classic bunker/loot-room defense. See [[Traps]].
- **Turret** — An [[Auto Turrets|Auto Turret]] (powered, AI-targeting) or shotgun trap. "Turret'd up" = base has active turrets. Needs [[Electricity Basics|power]].
- **Peek down / peek** — Looking out from an elevated firing slot (e.g., a triangle floor over an entrance) to shoot raiders below. "Peek down" = the defender's angle from above the door.

## Raiding

- **Raid base / FOB** — A [[Raid Defense|throwaway structure]] thrown up next to a target to store explosives, place [[#Player states & gear|bags]] for respawns, and craft. **FOB** = "forward operating base," same idea for a bigger group op.
- **Online raid** — Raiding a base while the owners are home and defending. High risk, high reward — you fight and raid simultaneously. See [[Raid Methods]].
- **Offline raid** — Raiding when the owners are logged off (sleepers). Safer, the most common solo/duo raid. The reason people build for "offline protection."
- **Eco raid** — A cheap, sulfur-efficient [[Eco Raiding|raid]] using the lowest-cost tools ([[#Weapons & combat|satchels]], beancans, fire, explosive ammo) and accepting more hits/time to save resources. Opposite of full-sending C4. See [[Eco Raiding]].
- **Bean / beancan** — [[Explosives|Beancan Grenade]]. The cheapest craftable explosive (**120 sulfur**), can dud (fail to explode) and must be re-thrown. Stacked for eco raids on sheet doors/stone. "Bean it" = beancan it open.
- **Satch / satchel** — [[Explosives|Satchel Charge]] (4 beancans + small stash + rope). **480 sulfur** each, also can dud. The workhorse eco explosive — best sulfur-per-damage on many targets. "Satch the door."
- **C4 / timed explosive** — [[Explosives|Timed Explosive Charge]]. The premium raid tool: **2,200 sulfur**, sticks and detonates on a timer, never duds. **1 C4 pops a [[Sheet Metal Door|sheet metal door]]**, 2 break a [[Stone Wall|stone wall]]. The benchmark raid currency.
- **Rocket** — Fired from a [[Loot-Only Heavy Weapons|Rocket Launcher]]. **1,400 sulfur** each; faster than satchels, used for walls and Bradley/heli. **Splash** damage hits adjacent structures. Variants: HV rocket (anti-vehicle/door), incendiary (burns wood/loot).
- **Splash** — Area/spillover damage from rockets (and to a lesser degree C4) that damages multiple structures around the point of impact. Good raiders aim to splash a TC or a second wall for free.
- **Insta / instability** — Triggering a structural collapse by destroying a [[Stability|support]] block, so connected blocks fall without being individually boomed. "Insta-raid / floor insta" = bring down a whole section by hitting one load-bearing piece. Cheap when the build allows it.
- **HV rocket** — High-velocity rocket: cheaper, flatter trajectory, low structure damage. Used vs doors, players, and [[Bradley APC|Bradley]]/vehicles rather than walls.
- **Raid cost** — How much boom (and thus [[Scrap|sulfur]]) it takes to reach loot. Always reference the [[Raid Costs]] table before committing.

## Weapons & combat

- **AK** — [[Assault Rifle]]. The top-tier general rifle; "AK" is universal even though the in-game name is Assault Rifle. The gear-tier benchmark.
- **MP5 / MP5A4** — [[MP5A4]]. Workbench-3 SMG, strong mid-range, high fire rate.
- **Bolt / bolty** — [[Bolt-Action Rifle]]. The standard sniper rifle (one-shot to the head with most ammo). The [[L96|L96]] is the higher-tier bolt-action.
- **Tommy** — [[Thompson]]. WB2 SMG, the cheap-and-effective ranged option; staple early/mid gun.
- **SAR** — [[Semi-Auto Rifle]]. The accessible semi-auto, common mid-game before AK. Don't confuse with [[SKS|SKS]] (also semi-auto, scoped sniper-ish).
- **Eoka** — [[Eoka Pistol]]. The infamous cheapest gun: a flint-and-steel pipe pistol that fires on a random click chance. "Eoka'd" = killed by the worst gun in the game (peak humiliation).
- **Custom / SMG** — [[Custom SMG]]. WB2 close-range bullet hose.
- **Splash / spray transfer** — In combat, "spray transfer" = moving your full-auto burst from one target to the next; not to be confused with raid splash.
- **Third party / third-partied** — A fight between two players/teams interrupted by a third group who swoops in to clean up both. "Got third-partied" = killed by someone who showed up mid-fight. Endemic at monuments and roads.
- **Peek / jiggle peek** — Briefly exposing yourself around cover to shoot, then retreating. A **jiggle peek** is a rapid in-and-out (often A-D strafe) to bait shots or check an angle without committing. Core PvP technique; see [[Combat Mechanics]] and [[PvP Tips]].
- **Spray pattern / recoil** — The fixed recoil path a full-auto gun "draws"; controlling it (pulling the mouse opposite the pattern) is the main PvP skill. See [[Combat Mechanics]].

## Progression & resources

- **WB / T1 / T2 / T3** — [[Workbenches|Workbench]] and its tech tiers. **T1 / WB1** ([[Workbench Level 1]]) unlocks basic gear; **T2 / WB2** ([[Workbench Level 2]]) unlocks SMGs, [[#Server, meta, and play styles|semis]], explosives entry; **T3 / WB3** ([[Workbench Level 3]]) unlocks AK, [[Loot-Only Heavy Weapons|rockets]], C4, top armor. "Get to T3" = the standard wipe progression goal.
- **BP / blueprint** — [[Blueprints|Blueprint]]. The unlock that lets you craft an item; learned by spending [[Scrap|scrap]] at the [[Tech Tree|tech tree]] / [[Research Table|research table]]. On a "BP wipe" everyone loses their learned blueprints, not just the map.
- **Tech tree** — The [[Tech Tree|per-workbench unlock tree]]; spend scrap to walk a path to the item you want. Cheaper/more predictable than RNG research.
- **Frags — metal vs blueprint (disambiguation)** — "Frags" alone usually means **[[Components|Metal Fragments]]** (the crafting metal from smelting metal ore). But **BP frags / [[Blueprint Fragments|Blueprint Fragments]]** are a separate currency used to unlock blueprints. Context decides: "I need 200 frags for a gun" = metal fragments; "out of BP frags" = blueprint fragments.
- **HQM** — [[Refining HQM|High Quality Metal]] (and HQ Ore). The premium metal for armored building, top-tier guns, and [[Armor|Ballistic armor]]. Slow to farm; the real late-wipe bottleneck.
- **LGF** — [[Low Grade Fuel]]. Burns in lanterns, [[#Vehicles|vehicles]], furnaces (as fuel), and crafts into explosives. Made from animal fat + cloth.
- **Scrap** — [[Scrap]]. The universal currency: research blueprints, [[Tech Tree|tech tree]], buy from [[Outpost]]/[[Bandit Camp]] and [[Vending and Shops|vending machines]], gamble. Farmed from [[Barrels and Crates|barrels/crates]], [[Recycling|recycling]] components, and [[Scrap Runs|monument runs]].
- **Comp / component** — [[Components|Components]] (gears, springs, pipes, sheet metal, tech trash, rope, etc.) found in barrels/crates. [[Recycling|Recycle]] them into raw materials + scrap, or use them in recipes. "Comp run" = looting roads/monuments for components.
- **Recycle / recycler** — The [[Recycling|recycler]] machine (at [[Outpost]], [[Bandit Camp]], some monuments, and craftable). Breaks items/components down into raw materials + scrap. "Run it through the recycler."

## Server, meta, and play styles

- **Wipe (map vs BP vs force)** — A server reset. **Map wipe** = new map + cleared bases, blueprints kept. **BP wipe** = blueprints also wiped (everyone starts from scratch). **Force wipe** = the mandatory wipe Facepunch pushes on the **first Thursday of every month** when a [[Updates|major update]] drops, which BP-wipes essentially every server (modded servers can defer some BP resets but must take the protocol/map update). Built Different's force wipe was **Thu June 4 2026**.
- **Vanilla / modded / 2x** — **Vanilla** = official-rules servers (default gather, team size 8, no plugins). **Modded** = community servers with plugins (kits, TP, shops, etc.). **2x / 3x / 5x / 10x** = multiplied gather/craft/component rates — higher number = faster wipe. "Vanilla solo only" describes a play style and server type.
- **Group limit / team limit** — The max players a server allows in one team (default **8** on vanilla; many servers run **solo / duo / trio / quad** limits, sometimes enforced by anti-group plugins). "Trio server" = max 3. The context for the whole solo/duo/trio meta.
- **Zerg** — An oversized, often loosely organized group (10s of players) that wins by numbers rather than skill. Roaming zergs dominate monuments and offline whole grids. Vanilla's team limit of 8 doesn't stop "unofficial" zergs allying.
- **Roam / roaming** — Leaving base to fight for kills, loot, and map control rather than to farm. "Going for a roam" = a PvP outing.
- **EAC** — Easy Anti-Cheat, Rust's anti-cheat. "EAC kicked me / EAC disconnected" is a common crash/kick. Cheaters are "EAC'd" (banned).
- **Rust+** — The official **companion mobile app**: pairs with a server to show your map, get raid/turret/[[Electricity Basics|smart-device]] alerts, chat with your team, and remotely control [[Industrial|smart switches]]. "Rust+ pinged me" = the app warned a structure was attacked.
- **Raidable** — A base worth raiding (loot value > raid cost), or generally "able to be raided." On modded servers, "Raidable Bases" is also a specific plugin spawning AI-defended lootable bases.
- **Safe zone** — [[Safe Zones|Monuments]] ([[Outpost]], [[Bandit Camp]], [[Fishing Villages]]) where turrets kill anyone who pulls a weapon. "Hostile in safe zone" = flagged, can't trade, turrets will engage if you stay.

## Monuments & access (colors, keycards, tiers)

- **Monument** — A [[Monuments|named POI]] (Outpost, [[Launch Site]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Large Oil Rig|Oil Rig]], etc.) with loot, NPCs, and/or puzzles. The map's PvE/PvP hotspots and [[Scrap Runs|scrap-run]] destinations.
- **Green / blue / red (keycards)** — The three [[Keycards|access cards]], easiest to hardest puzzle: **[[Green Keycard|green]]** (low-tier monuments), **[[Blue Keycard|blue]]** (mid), **[[Red Keycard|red]]** (high-tier: Launch Site, Oil Rig, Military Tunnels). You feed cards into card readers, sometimes after powering [[Fuses|fuses]]. "Need a red for Launch."
- **T1 / T2 / T3 monuments** — Loosely, monument tiers by danger/loot and which [[Workbenches|workbench]] their crates can roll. Don't confuse with workbench tiers — context matters ("it's a T3 monument" = high-end like Launch Site).
- **Key / keycard** — A [[Keycards|keycard]] (green/blue/red), not a base lock key. "Grab a key" near a monument means a keycard.

## Vehicles

- **Mini** — [[Minicopter]]. The cheap 2-seat helicopter; the everyday flying machine. "Mini'd in" = arrived by minicopter.
- **Scrappy / scrap heli** — [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]]. The bigger 4+ seat transport copter.
- **Heli (the event) vs heli (your vehicle)** — Careful: "heli" can mean the [[Patrol Helicopter|Patrol Helicopter]] event (the attack heli that strafes you) or just your [[Minicopter|mini]]. "Heli's on me" almost always means the event. The roaming combat version is the [[Attack Helicopter]].
- **RHIB / boat** — [[RHIB|RHIB]] (armed/armored boat) or [[Rowboat|rowboat]]; "boat" usually the small one. [[Tugboat|Tugboat]] is the floating-base boat.

## Events & misc

- **Bradley / Brad** — [[Bradley APC]], the tank at [[Launch Site]] (and [[Giant Excavator Pit|Excavator]]). "Bradley camp" = farming it for high-tier loot with rockets/C4.
- **Cargo** — [[Cargo Ship]], the loot-laden ship circling the map; "cargo's up" = it spawned.
- **Airdrop / drop** — [[Airdrop|Supply drop]] (called by a cargo plane). "Drop incoming" = loot parachuting in, contested. The [[Locked Crate|locked (hackable) crate]] from [[Oil Rig|Oil Rig]]/[[Chinook CH47|Chinook]] is a separate, timed loot prize.
- **Gut / gutting (fishing)** — Cutting open a caught fish (via the [[Fishing|fishing]] system) for [[Cooking and Food|food]], fish oil, and occasional loot. "Gut the fish."
- **Tea** — A [[Teas|crafted buff potion]] from the [[Mixing Table|mixing table]] (e.g., [[Pure Scrap Tea|scrap tea]], healing, ore, wood, harvesting teas). Drink before a run for a temporary boost. See [[Teas]].
- **Genetics / clone / cloning** — The [[Plant Genetics|plant gene system]]: read seed genes (G/Y/H/W/X), breed for the best traits, then **clone** a top plant so every copy is identical. The backbone of high-yield [[Berries and Crops|farming]]. "Good genes" = a plant worth cloning.

---

## See also

- [[Raid Costs]] — the authoritative boom/sulfur tables behind every raiding term here
- [[Eco Raiding]] · [[Raid Methods]] · [[Raid Defense]] — raiding in depth
- [[Soft Side]] · [[Stability]] · [[Bunkers]] · [[Open Core vs Closed]] — building terms in depth
- [[Tech Tree]] · [[Blueprints]] · [[Workbenches]] — progression terms in depth
- [[Combat Mechanics]] · [[PvP Tips]] — combat terms in depth
- [[Returning Player Guide]] — if these terms still feel foreign, start here

> **Sources:** corrosionhour.com (The RUST Glossary), rust.fandom.com (Jargon), rustmods.com (Terms, Slang & Lingo), rusthelp.com + the vault's verified [[Raid Costs]] (sulfur anchors), wiki.facepunch.com (team-size convar / wipe protocol), rustafied.com (force-wipe schedule). Numbers re-checked 2026-06-13 against the Built Different patch.

pages.title: Returning Player Guide (2023 → 2026)
pages.body:
# Returning Player Guide (2023 → 2026)

You last played around **2023**. The game you're coming back to in **June 2026** (current patch: **"Built Different,"** live June 4 2026, on **Unity 6**) is meaningfully different — not in its bones, but in three or four systems you will absolutely trip over if nobody warns you. This is the front door. Read the TL;DR, then dive into the linked deep pages.

The single biggest thing to internalize: **the scrap-only research grind is dead, and Blueprint Fragments now gate Workbench tiers.** If you sit at your base waiting to farm 500 scrap to unlock the AK like 2023, you will never tier up. You tier up by *going to monuments*. See [[Progression & Tech Tree]].

---

## 1. TL;DR — the 10 changes that matter most

1. **Progression is monument-driven now.** Workbench T2 needs **5 Basic Blueprint Fragments**, T3 needs **5 Advanced Fragments** — dropped only at monuments/crates/airdrops, not craftable from scrap. Research itself is dirt cheap now (**15/30/60/120 scrap** by rarity, down from 20/75/125/500). See [[Progression & Tech Tree]], [[Blueprint Fragments]].
2. **Blueprints force-wipe with the map every month** (since Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die"). No more permanent BP collection carrying across wipes.
3. **Mortars (Apr 30 2026) killed the tall-wall compound.** HE/frag mortars unlock at **Workbench T2** and lob shells *over* compound walls from *outside* your TC bubble. High external walls now just mark your roof for a mortar crew. Modern bases are low-profile with roofed walkways and indoor furnaces. See [[Base Building & Raid Defense]].
4. **Explosive protection is capped at 75%** (May 2025). There is no longer such a thing as a functionally unraidable wall — every wall has a finite rocket cost.
5. **The world was regenerated.** World Update 2.0 (Oct 2024) rebuilt all terrain (new cliffs, canyons, lakes, oases). A full **Jungle biome** arrived (May 2025) and a **Naval / Deep Sea** layer (Feb 2026). Your 2023 map memory is gone.
6. **Aim cone overhaul (May 2024):** the movement/spray penalty now blends in over ~4 shots, so **strafe tap-firing (1-4 shots) is nearly as accurate as standing still.** This defines current gunplay. See [[Weapons & Gunplay]].
7. **Backpacks exist (Feb 2024):** Small (12 slots, T1 craft) and Large (28 slots, military loot). They **drop on death** — extra loot, extra risk.
8. **Bandit Camp now sells ALL THREE keycards** (Green 15 / Blue 40 / Red 80 scrap). **Outpost no longer sells the Blue Keycard.** Red used to be unbuyable — now you can shortcut the whole ladder for 135 scrap. See [[Keycards]].
9. **Food spoils now (Mar 2025):** raw 6h / cooked 24h, paused only in a powered fridge. Cooking Workbench + buff pies + bees + chicken coops all new. See [[Farming & Cooking]] (if present) / [[Food & Comfort]].
10. **Vehicles exploded into a whole category:** player-built modular ships with cannons (Feb 2026 Naval Update), Attack Helicopter, motorbikes with sidecars, DPV underwater scooter, overhauled swimming horses. See [[Vehicles]].

---

## 2. What's new, by system

### Combat
- **Aim cone overhaul (May 2024)** — see TL;DR #6. Tap-fire and short bursts stay tight; full-auto-standing sprays widest. Crouching shrinks the cone but doesn't remove recoil/bloom. **Recoil is still a fixed learnable pattern** per gun (since June 2022) layered over the random cone. See [[Weapons & Gunplay]].
- **New guns since 2023:** Handmade SMG (T1) + **SKS bumped T2→T3** (Nov 2024); **High Calibre Revolver** (5.56, Oct 2024); Minigun + Military Flamethrower (heavy-scientist drops, Apr 2024); Blowpipe + Boomerang (May 2025); **M16A2 3-round-burst rifle** + **Ballistic armor set** (loot-only, Jun 2026 "Built Different").
- **Craftable silencers (Jun 2025)** — previously loot-only. Matters because **gunshots are now audible at 400/500/600m** by weapon class (Sep 2025). Silencers remove muzzle flash and cut your audio signature — essential for solo third-party avoidance.
- **Ballistic armor (Jun 2026):** Helmet 60% / Vest 35% / Leg Armor 30% projectile — **best legs in the game** — but loot-only, not craftable/researchable/buyable. The craftable meta kit is still **Metal Facemask + Metal Chest Plate + Road Sign Kilt**. See [[Armor & Healing]].
- **Variable zoom scope** (4x/8x/16x). **Headshots are 2x; the neck no longer counts as a headshot** — you must hit the head box.
- **Siege weapons (Feb 2025):** Catapult, Ballista, Battering Ram, Siege Tower + Shields; **Mortar artillery (May 2026)**. **Handcuffs + prisoner hoods (Jul 2024).**
- **Predators got real stalking AI:** Wolves (Nov 2024); jungle tigers/panthers/crocodiles/snakes (May 2025).

### Building
- **Mortars killed the tall external wall** (Apr 30 2026) — see TL;DR #3.
- **Explosive protection capped at 75%** (May 2025) — see TL;DR #4.
- **Auto turrets have a 40m interference cap** (Oct 2023): max ~12 active turrets within a 40m radius. No more turret-wall spam; overlap arcs instead.
- **High External Stone Wall is now craftable and fire-resistant** (Jan 2026, 500 HP, ~4m, 4 rockets to break); wooden high walls/gates upgrade to stone in place.
- **Bunker status 2026:** garage-door bunkers and (Apr 2026) Armored-Triangle ladder-hatch bunkers **work**; triple-honeycomb/wall-stack open-core is current meta; classic stability/pickup bunkers are mostly **patched**. TC-less bases decay immediately.
- **Wallpaper (Sep 2024)**, water-wheel river generator, Digital Clock alarms, Seismic Sensor raid alarm, Tin Can Alarm tripwire (May 2026). See [[Base Building & Raid Defense]] and [[Electricity]] (if present).

### Monuments
- **Loot reshuffled for the first time in 5+ years** (2025/26). New green-card puzzles added at **The Dome, Ferry Terminal, and Radtown**.
- **Nuclear Missile Silo** (itself new, May 2023) upgraded from blue to **RED keycard**: 4 elite crates, 27 scientists, **highest radiation in game (median 26 / max 81)**, 2 Advanced Fragments. See [[Missile Silo]].
- **Puzzle resets reworked (Nov 2025 "Pivot Or Die"):** the ~30-min timer starts only once a player loots a container, ticks down even with players present (no body-blocking), and floods the room with unsurvivable radiation in the final 10 minutes. **Loot fast and leave.**
- **Cargo Ship docks at Harbors** (Apr 2024) — board from land, 60-second departure horn. **Oil Rig floods with radiation 30 min after the crate hack starts.** See [[Launch Site]], [[Large Oil Rig]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Radtown]].

### Vehicles
- **Naval Update (Feb 2026):** full player-built modular ships — hull blocks, sails, engines, code-locked helms, anchors, **CANNONS**, ramps — built at water-placed Boat Building Stations; since March they support electricity/industrial IO. **PT Boat with two .50 cals.**
- **Attack Helicopter** (Sep 2023, 2,250 scrap at Bandit Camp; nerfed Nov 2025 — flares no longer fool homing missiles, no in-flight repair). **Homing Missile Launcher** counters air.
- **Motorbikes + pedal bikes with sidecar/trike variants** (Jul 2024); **DPV underwater scooter** (Oct 2024); **Tugboat** buildable boat (Jul 2023); **Parachutes** (backpack-slot, -20%/use).
- **Horses overhauled (Feb 2025):** swim, tow siege weapons, 12-slot saddlebags. See [[Vehicles]].

### Progression
- See TL;DR #1, #2 and the dedicated [[Progression & Tech Tree]] / [[Blueprint Fragments]] pages. **Workbenches no longer cost scrap to use** (Nov 2025). Tech-tree browsing is now one station with tabs (Jun 2024) plus multi-node path-unlock (Apr 2026). **9 rare loot-only Workbench Augmentations** (May 2026) are the new endgame chase.

### Quality of Life
- **Tutorial Island** (Mar 2024) — genuinely worth a 10-minute run to relearn UI.
- **Party system auto-teams friends on join** (Jul 2025).
- **Full menu redesign + 65% faster loading** (Aug 2025).
- **Sleeping bags capped at 15 respawn points** per player (Jun 2023).
- **Gamma cheating is dead** — shader nightlight (Mar 2024). You can't bright-night anymore.
- **Recyclers split (May 2024):** safe-zone = 8s cycle / 80% yield; monument = 5s / 120%. Building in the T1 monument ring is faster *and* more efficient than running to Outpost. See [[Recycling & Economy]].
- **Premium Access Pass** (Mar 2025, ~$15 via Steam inventory, ~4x fewer cheaters; rebranded Jun 2026); optional TPM 2.0 + Secure Boot servers (Mar 2026). **Softcore** (respawn with 50% inventory, -25% bullet dmg) and **Hardcore** (fog-of-war map, compass item, no firearm crafting) game modes reworked.

---

## 3. What got nerfed or removed since 2023

- **Permanent blueprints are gone** — BPs force-wipe with the map every month (Nov 2025).
- **Scrap-only progression is gone** — fragments gate workbenches now.
- **Outpost no longer sells the Blue Keycard** (moved to Bandit Camp).
- **Functionally unraidable walls are gone** — explosive protection capped at 75% (May 2025); heavy plate no longer fully tanks rockets.
- **The tall external-wall compound is dead** — mortars lob over walls from outside your TC bubble (Apr 30 2026).
- **Turret-wall spam is dead** — 40m interference cap, max ~12 turrets in radius (Oct 2023).
- **Attack Heli flare-cheese nerfed** — flares no longer fool homing missiles; no in-flight repair (Nov 2025).
- **Gamma/brightness cheating is dead** — shader nightlight (Mar 2024).
- **Neck shots no longer count as headshots.**
- **Classic stability/pickup bunkers** mostly patched; **TC-less bases decay immediately** (24h grief-protection buffer only if the TC was *destroyed*).
- **Food is no longer free calories forever** — raw spoils in 6h, cooked in 24h unless in a powered fridge (Mar 2025).
- **Unity 6 regression to know about (Jun 2026):** 1000Hz+ polling-rate mice can cause CPU overhead / frame stutter. If your FPS tanks, drop your mouse polling rate.

---

## 4. Your first wipe back — a concrete day-1 plan

The macro shape of a wipe is the same (rock → tools → base → guns → raid), but the *route* changed. Here's a solo/duo/trio day-1 that respects the new progression:

1. **Spawn, gather, build a starter base.** Stone Spear (20 stone + 1 wooden spear) is the wipe-day weapon; Hunting Bow for range. Build a **1x1 or 2x1** (~1,600-2,000 stone, ~5,600 sulfur to raid) and plant a **Tool Cupboard** (1,000 wood) immediately — TC-less = instant decay. See [[Base Building & Raid Defense]].
2. **Build Workbench T1** (500 wood + 100 metal frags + 50 scrap — default-known). Make tools (Hatchet/Pickaxe = 125 frags + 100 wood).
3. **Run the T1 monument ring for scrap, components, and recyclers.** Hit Gas Station / Supermarket / Junkyard / minor monuments — recycle barrels and components (monument recyclers are 5s/120%). Components (Metal Springs, Gears, weapon Bodies, Tech Trash) are loot-only and gate guns *more than scrap does*. See [[Recycling & Economy]].
4. **Hunt Basic Blueprint Fragments to unlock Workbench T2.** You need **5 Basic**. Reliable sources: **Power Plant / Train Yard / Water Treatment (3 each)**, Airfield / Arctic (2 each), green puzzle rooms (1 each). See [[Blueprint Fragments]].
5. **Start the keycard ladder for blue cards.** Run a **green-card puzzle** (1 Electric Fuse + 1 Green Keycard) at **Satellite Dish, The Dome, Sewer Branch, Radtown, Harbor, or Ferry Terminal** → rewards a **Blue Keycard + 1 Basic Fragment** on ~30-min resets. Green cards spawn 100% on desks at ~10 monuments. *Or* just buy the set at Bandit Camp (135 scrap for all three). See [[Keycards]].
6. **Build WB2** (500 frags + 20 HQM + 5 Basic Fragments — no scrap). Research the **Semi-Auto Rifle + Thompson** snowball kit cheaply (15/30/60/120 scrap at the Research Table / tech tree).
7. **Push to red cards + Advanced Fragments for WB3.** Blue puzzle rooms at **Water Treatment Plant** (safest solo red-card printer — no NPCs, just 1 fuse + blue), Train Yard, Power Plant, Airfield, Arctic each yield a **Red Keycard**. **Advanced Fragments** come from elite/locked crates at **[[Launch Site]], [[Missile Silo]], [[Military Tunnels]], [[Large Oil Rig]]**. You need **5 Advanced** for WB3.
8. **Build WB3** (1,000 frags + 100 HQM + 5 Advanced — no scrap) → research the **AK** (50 HQM + 200 wood + 1 rifle body + 4 metal springs) and **Bolt Action / SKS / MP5**. Kit up: Metal Facemask + Metal Chest Plate + Road Sign Kilt. See [[Weapons & Gunplay]], [[Armor & Healing]].
9. **Sustain:** place your own quarry with a **Survey Charge** anywhere, or run static monument quarries / the **Giant Excavator** on diesel (Outpost: 300 LGF per diesel). See [[Quarries & Excavator]] / [[Recycling & Economy]].

---

## 5. Habits from 2023 that are now WRONG

- âŒ **"Grind 500 scrap, research the AK."** → âœ… Research is cheap (120 scrap top tier); the real gate is **fragments farmed at monuments** to unlock the workbench at all.
- âŒ **"Hoard blueprints across wipes."** → âœ… BPs wipe monthly with the map. Plan around a fresh start every wipe.
- âŒ **"Buy the Blue Keycard at Outpost."** → âœ… Outpost dropped it; buy at **Bandit Camp** (40 scrap) or run a green puzzle for it free.
- âŒ **"Red Keycard is unbuyable, must puzzle for it."** → âœ… Bandit Camp sells **Red for 80 scrap** now.
- âŒ **"Stand still and laser-spray for accuracy."** → âœ… The aim-cone overhaul means **strafe tap-firing** is the accurate playstyle; standing full-auto is the *widest* cone.
- âŒ **"Build a giant compound with tall external walls."** → âœ… **Mortars lob over them.** Go low-profile, roofed walkways, indoor furnaces, walls pushed 30m+ off your structures.
- âŒ **"Stack turrets on a turret wall."** → âœ… 40m interference cap, max ~12; spread them with overlapping arcs.
- âŒ **"Heavy plate tanks rockets."** → âœ… Explosive protection caps at 75%; nothing fully tanks explosives anymore.
- âŒ **"Body-block a puzzle room so nobody else can loot."** → âœ… Reset timer ticks with players present and gasses the room before reset. Loot fast, leave.
- âŒ **"Stockpile cooked meat for the week."** → âœ… Cooked food spoils in 24h unless in a **powered fridge**.
- âŒ **"Brighten my gamma to see at night."** → âœ… Shader nightlight kills this; use actual light sources / NVGs.
- âŒ **"My loot is safe on my body."** → âœ… Backpacks drop on death too — more to lose now.
- âŒ **"Outpost recycler is the best recycler."** → âœ… Monument recyclers (5s/120%) beat safe-zone (8s/80%); recycle in the T1 ring.

---

## See also

[[Progression & Tech Tree]] · [[Blueprint Fragments]] · [[Keycards]] · [[Weapons & Gunplay]] · [[Armor & Healing]] · [[Base Building & Raid Defense]] · [[Recycling & Economy]] · [[Vehicles]] · [[Launch Site]] · [[Large Oil Rig]] · [[Military Tunnels]] · [[Missile Silo]] · [[Radtown]] · [[Quarries & Excavator]]

pages.body:
# Rust Companion App (Web)

Companion web app built from this vault's Rust knowledge base. A searchable, offline-capable reference you can pull up on a second monitor or phone mid-wipe.

- **Live:** https://bluefiiish.github.io/rust-companion/
- **Source:** `projects/rust/app/` (data in `app/data/items.json`, item art in `app/img/items/`, build/scrape tooling in `app/tools/`)
- **Type:** offline **PWA** (installable, works without a connection once loaded)

## What it does

- **Searchable item DB** — every Rust item with stats/costs, backed by `app/data/items.json`.
- **Raid tool** — sulfur/explosive cost per wall grade and door (mirrors [[Raid Costs]]).
- **Recycle tool** — component/scrap yields per item.
- **Genetics tool** — plant gene crossbreeding helper (see [[Plant Genetics]]).

## Keeping it current

The app's data is a snapshot; when a monthly patch changes numbers, the vault pages are updated first (source of truth = rusthelp.com), then the app data is re-generated from `app/tools/`. As of the July 2026 [[Common Ground Update]], **no item stats or raid costs changed**, so the item DB and raid numbers remain accurate.

**Related:** [[Rust Wiki]] · [[Raid Costs]] · [[Loot Tables]] · [[Plant Genetics]]

pages.title: Rust Wiki
pages.body:
# Rust Wiki

Master index for the Rust (game) knowledge base. Built from live web research, current to the **July 2026 "Common Ground"** update. Returning-player oriented: most pages flag what changed since 2023.

> **Companion web app:** [[Rust Companion App (Web)]] — searchable item DB + raid/recycle/genetics tools, offline PWA. Live at https://bluefiiish.github.io/rust-companion/ (source in `projects/rust/app/`).

> **Start here if you're back after a break:** [[Getting Started (Rust)]] then [[Returning Player Changelog]].

---

## Getting Started

- [[Getting Started (Rust)]] — Folder overview + 60-second wipe checklist; the three big 2026 changes
- [[Returning Player Changelog]] — One-page cheat sheet of every 2023→2026 change ranked by habit-impact
- [[Returning Player Guide]] — Full returning-player walkthrough of what changed and what to relearn
- [[rusthelp.com]] — Source-of-truth reference for the RustLabs-successor numbers wiki; how the vault reads its loot/recycle tables and the verification convention
- [[First Day Guide]] — Hour-by-hour wipe-day route: beach to backpack, 2x1 + TC, scrap+fragment race, first guns
- [[Solo Survival Guide]] — 2026 solo meta: fragment-hunting windows, base design under the explosive cap, loadout ladder
- [[Wipe Schedule]] — Force wipe = first Thursday monthly @ 19:00 UTC; map vs BP wipe; community cadences
- [[Server Types]] — Official vs community vs modded; Vanilla/Hardcore/Primitive/2x-5x; Premium Access Pass anti-cheat gate
- [[Team System]] — Team UI (max 8), the Jul 2025 Party system, ping wheel and map markers, duo/trio auth etiquette
- [[Settings and Binds]] — Essential console binds, gesture wheel, ping system, gamma-is-dead nightlight, useful convars
- [[Rust+ Companion App]] — Pairing, live map/team chat, Smart Switch/Alarm/CCTV, the standard solo alarm chain
- [[Rust Companion App (Web)]] — This vault's own companion web app (offline PWA): searchable item DB + raid/recycle/genetics tools; live at bluefiiish.github.io/rust-companion
- [[Performance Settings]] — FPS tuning for a 5090/4K rig: Unity 6 stutter fix, -gc.buffer, shadow cascades, DLSS
- [[Recording Graphics Settings]] — Quality-max 4K settings for recording with OBS: full punch-in list, TSSAA-vs-FXAA on-camera call, PvP-asymmetry flags, fps.limit 120 doctrine
- [[Map, Grid & Callouts]] — Reading the map + 150m grid (A0 = NW), monument icons, ping wheel, and duo/trio callout discipline
- [[Clothing & Environmental Gear]] — Non-armor apparel: warmth, radiation gear, diving gear, NVG + a "what to wear for X" table
- [[Voice Chat and Audio Routing]] — Rust has NO in-game mic selector: it uses Steam VoIP (Steam → Voice → Voice Input Device); virtual-cable routing, Steam noise suppression vs voice changers, Rust-effect/Discord-clean split
- [[Console Commands & Streamer Tools]] — Client F1 convars: perf tuning, combatlog, demo recording, streamer mode, useful binds
- [[Anti-Cheat, Reporting & Spotting Cheaters]] — EAC + ban types, aimbot/ESP tells, the F7 report flow, Premium as the #1 mitigation
- [[Running a Rust Server]] — Self-host primer: SteamCMD, server.cfg convars, admin/RCON, Oxide vs Carbon, map/BP wipe files
- [[Instruments, Boombox & Social Items]] — The non-combat layer: instruments, boombox/cassettes, drone marketplace, signs, telephone

### Survival mechanics
- [[Survival Mechanics]] — Hub for the survival layer: the four meters, environmental killers, downed-system overview
- [[Wounded System]] — Crawling vs incapacitated vs instant death, recovery chances, the self-revive medkit rule
- [[Hunger and Thirst]] — Calories and hydration caps/gates, the drain ratio, never-drink-the-sea, food spoilage
- [[Temperature and Cold]] — Cold-damage thresholds, biome temps, the wet penalty, the snow-biome death trap, clothing warmth
- [[Comfort and Health Regen]] — Comfort heal-to caps, the calories+hydration gates, the free post-fight heal loop

### Clans & groups
- [[Clans and Groups]] — How a group operates beyond the team UI: team≠access, per-member onboarding, scaling past a trio
- [[TC Authorization and Multi-TC Bases]] — Building-privilege mechanics, ~10-player cap, the Clear-List button, multi-TC compounds
- [[Clan Roles and Coordination]] — The role split, the team-core-box loot rule, offline-coverage shifts, comms
- [[Code Locks and Locker Etiquette]] — Master vs guest codes, the lockout, what locks protect vs TC auth, locker tiers
- [[Raid Bases and FOBs]] — Building/defending a FOB, the six raid roles, rocket-count scouting math, online vs offline

---

## Meta

- [[Current Meta — Common Ground (July 2026)]] — **CURRENT** dated meta snapshot (July 2 → Aug 6 2026 wipe): combat/raid/base meta carries over unchanged; softcore 2x gather + raid windows, clans, and the Apartment Complex are the new levers
- [[Current Meta — Built Different (June 2026)]] — previous-wipe snapshot: weapon/armor tier lists, base/raid/economy meta (superseded; still the source for unchanged combat detail)

---

## Reference

- [[Rust Cheat Sheet]] — One-page at-a-glance card: raid-cost sulfur, explosive costs, smelt ratios, rad thresholds, upkeep, vendor prices, recycler yields
- [[Rust Glossary]] — A-Z slang and jargon (naked, kit, honeycomb, eco raid, satch/C4, BP vs metal frags, third party, jiggle peek, zerg, EAC)

---

## Guides

Strategy / decision-layer guides that sit on top of the reference pages above. Current to the June 2026 "Built Different" update.

- [[Solo Wipe Guide]] — Comprehensive full-wipe-arc strategy for solo (scaling to duo/trio) on a populated 2026 vanilla server; the decision/sequencing layer over the reference pages
- [[Duo & Trio Wipe Guide]] — Decision-focused 2-3 player strategy: role splits, shared-TC base design, parallelized tech-tree rush, group roams/monuments/events, and full group-raiding logistics
- [[Recoil & Aim Mastery]] — The modern recoil/aimcone system, per-weapon spray compensation, settings, peeking/movement, and a train-server practice routine
- [[Raiding Playbook]] — End-to-end raiding decision/execution layer for solo/duo/trio, built on top of the raid reference pages
- [[Base Defense & Counter-Raid Playbook]] — The "how to actually defend" layer: defensive design, anti-offline measures, turret/trap layouts, online breach-holding, third-partying, and raid-base denial
- [[Full Base Automation]] — Wiring a base to run itself: power budgeting, source mix, auto-turrets w/ backup power, smart alarm + Rust+, auto-furnace, industrial sorting + auto-crafting, bunker auto-door, sprinkler farm — one sequenced build order
- [[Scrap & Economy Optimization]] — Maximizing scrap + components per hour and sequencing a wipe-long economy
- [[Monument Roam Routes]] — Which monuments to hit, in what order, and when — organized by goal (scrap, components, guns, riches, events) for solo/duo/trio
- [[Farming Empire]] — Self-sufficient farming: genetics min-maxing to a god-seed clone stash, automated planter/light/water/composter loop, tea priority line, food independence, scrap-tea barrel loop
- [[PvE Mastery]] — Soloing/duoing every AI loot target (Bradley, Patrol Heli, both Oil Rigs, Cargo Ship, Chinook crate), with a wipe-progression sequence
- [[Progression Speedrun]] — Wipe-day sequencing from naked spawn to a full AK kit on 2026 "Built Different" canon (cheap research, fragment-gated benches)
- [[Group Base & Compound]] — Quad+ group-basing: compound walls/externals, shooting floors, multi-TC honeycomb, role-based storage/auth, FOB staging, and defending a big footprint

---

## Updates

- [[Rust Update History]] — Master table of every monthly update Jun 2023 – Jun 2026 + a returning-player crib sheet
