pages.title: Rust Updates 2023
pages.body:
# Rust Updates 2023

June–December 2023, the first stretch Josia missed. Context: May 2023 ("R.U.S.T") had just added the **Nuclear Missile Silo** monument, so that may also be new to a 2023-era player. See [[Rust Update History]] for the master table.

## June 1 — Bags to Battles

- **Sleeping bag cap: 15 respawn points max per player** (bags, beds, shelters all count; `max_sleeping_bags` convar). Respawn points show on the map while alive; "bag gifting" settings prevent bag-griefing.
- Shipping Container building skin (16 randomizable colors, repaint via spray can RMB).
- Building upgrade animation (1-second construction effect), ping system polish, hammer radial skin switching.

## July 6 — [[Deep Sea Update|Deep Sea]]

Tugboat (mobile buildable base boat), [[Ferry Terminal]] monument, full ocean wave/water system rewrite. Full page: [[Deep Sea Update]].

## August 3 — Wounded

- **Wounded screen now shows recovery probability and a countdown** to recover/die. Full food + water improves odds; using a **Large Medkit while downed guarantees 100% recovery**.
- Chat **emoji system** (`:` autocomplete; servers can add custom 256px emojis).
- Brick building skin (stone tier). **Burst module buffed** (faster refire, less recoil/aimcone).
- C4/satchels placeable on vehicles again; crafting queue persists through server shutdowns.

## September 7 — [[Airborne Update|Airborne]]

The big one of 2023: **Attack Helicopter** (2,250 scrap at [[Bandit Camp]]), **Parachutes** (T2 craft, backpack slot), **Homing Missile Launcher**, hot air balloon armor, and experimental global base rendering (300m → 1,500m). Full page: [[Airborne Update]].

## October 5 — Solid Foundations

- **Auto turret interference**: only a limited number of turrets can be active within a **40m radius**; extras glow blue and won't target (anti-turret-stacking). See [[Auto Turret]].
- MP5 damage up + less bullet drop; Thompson/Custom SMG center-hit buffs.
- [[Tool Cupboard]] consolidated to one page with +1 tool slot; water catchers fill much faster in rain; Small Battery capacity/output up; weather events more frequent.
- Servers moved to Unity 2021 LTS (fixed crashes dating to 2019). [[Launch Site]] main-building loot increased.

## November 2 — Coupling The Rails

- **Above-ground and underground rail networks connected** via tunnels on 4250+ size maps — trains can travel both seamlessly. Working **train signals** underground (green/yellow/red block occupancy).
- Wire tool: reconnect existing wires, hold RMB to clear — electrician QoL.
- Frontier Base Decor DLC (10 items: weapon racks, storage barrels, planters, trophies).
- **Horse saddlebags 6 → 12 slots**; jackhammer refillable at repair bench.

## December 7 — 10 Years Of Rust

- **Legacy Shelter** (2013-style wooden shelter with key lock + building privilege) and **M4 Shotgun** (uncraftable military drop).
- **Ragdoll overhaul**: corpses fully server-side, collide with vehicles.
- **[[Oil Rig]] change: radiation floods the rig 30 minutes after the hacked crate unlocks**, forcing rotation (anti-camping).
- Bandages can now revive downed players; ore nodes harvestable without crouching; pinata + confetti cannon birthday items.
- **Hardcore mode and Barren maps retired** from official servers (Hardcore returns reworked in Aug 2025 — see [[Rust Updates 2025]]).

## Meta takeaways for 2023

- Air superiority meta arrived: attack heli rockets + parachute drops onto roofs changed base defense (SAM coverage matters more).
- Turret-farm bases nerfed by interference; bag spam nerfed by the 15-bag cap.
- Tugboats became the nomad/solo playstyle of choice for a while.

pages.title: Rust Updates 2024
pages.body:
# Rust Updates 2024

The QoL-and-vehicles year: backpacks, tutorial island, the harbor/cargo rework, bikes, wallpaper, and a full world-generation overhaul. See [[Rust Update History]] for the master table.

## February 1 — [[Bags To Riches Update|Bags To Riches]]

**Backpacks** (Small 12 slots craftable, Large 28 slots loot-only) plus the Metal Detector. Also: plant ripeness window extended 4 → 14 hours, **wooden shelters limited to 1 per player**, death markers on compass. Full page: [[Bags To Riches Update]].

## March 7 — [[Lighting The Way Update|Lighting The Way]]

**Tutorial Island** onboarding, shader-based "nightlight" that kills gamma-cheating, vendor UI redesign, attack heli flares limited to 1 per 30s. Full page: [[Lighting The Way Update]].

## April 4 — [[Waves Of Change Update|Waves Of Change]]

**Harbor rework + Cargo Ship now docks at harbors** (board it from land!), **Minigun**, Military Flamethrower, electricity logic-gate power costs removed, Patrol Helicopter AI rework, Bradley deploys scientists. Full page: [[Waves Of Change Update]].

## May 2 — [[Meta Madness Update|Meta Madness]]

Combat + economy rebalance that still defines the modern game: gradual movement aimcone, **safe-zone recyclers nerfed to 8s/80% while monument recyclers buffed to 5s/120%**, tech tree scrap tax (+10% at WB2, +20% at WB3 — later removed Nov 2025), LR-300 made "best in class". Full page: [[Meta Madness Update]].

## June 6 — Seismic Shift

- **Seismic Sensor**: powered deployable detecting explosions 1–30m away; outputs power per blast type (F1 grenade = 1, rocket/C4 = 3) — the offline-raid alarm component. See [[Electricity]].
- **Monument barricades**: wood/stone/concrete barricades + sandbags placeable on monument terrain; 15-minute decay, 8–10 melee hits to break. Changed monument PvP (instant cover).
- **Tech tree consolidation: one workbench station shows all tiers via tabs** (no more visiting separate benches to browse).
- Instant rejoin within 5 minutes after kick/crash (no queue). Code locks 250% faster to use. Anti-rad tea rebalanced to 15/30/45. Patrol Helicopter lifetime 15 → 30 min.

## July 4 — [[Road Renegades Update|Road Renegades]]

**Motorbikes (+ sidecar), pedal bikes (+ trike)**, **handcuffs + prisoner hoods**, the roaming **Travelling Vendor**, and dynamic NPC vendor pricing. Full page: [[Road Renegades Update]].

## August 1 — Stay Alert

- **Tin Can Alarm**: cheap tripwire that rattles when crossed (later upgraded May 2026 to throw rigged grenades — see [[Upgrade Hard, Raid Harder Update]]).
- **Bush rustle sounds now replicated to other players** (speed-dependent) — bush camping got riskier.
- Ziplines: max length 150 → 185m, picks furthest destination. Underwater dropped items sink with bubble trails.
- NPC vendor price recalc every 5 real hours.

## September 5 — Time To Kill

- **Wallpaper** added: interior wall covering, default blueprint 10 cloth for 2; 4 default colors + DLC skins (floor/ceiling wallpaper followed June 2025). Purely cosmetic, no protection.
- **Digital Clock**: T2 craft, 100 metal frags, 1 power; shows server time and drives **up to 5 alarms that trigger circuits** (automation, timed traps, lights).
- Gas Compression Overdrive attachment (experimental: +damage/velocity, +recoil, −fire rate for Thompson/SAR/SAP/M92/M39/Custom SMG).
- Colorblind accessibility options; building errors moved to toasts.

## October 3 — [[World Update 2.0]]

Terrain generation overhauled (new coastal/inland cliffs, canyons, lakes, oases, longer/wider rivers), **[[Radtown]] monument returns**, Diver Propulsion Vehicle, High Calibre Revolver, water wells with NPC vendors, 3 new dive sites. Full page: [[World Update 2.0]].

## November 7 — Armed and Animated

- **Handmade SMG**: T1 tech-tree automatic — gave early game an auto weapon.
- **SKS**: T3 rifle slotting between SAR and M39 (balanced damage/accuracy mid-tier).
- **Wolf AI overhaul**: wolves hunt as coordinated packs, fear torches/fire, stalk instead of beelining ("less landmine, more tactical"). Further balanced in December.
- Gesture pack DLC incl. Rock Paper Scissors minigame; IO arrows show inputs/outputs on deployables; radioactive water buffed.

## December 5 — Polish and Progress

- **Variable Zoom Scope**: one scope with 4x/8x/16x levels, replacing the old fixed 16x.
- **High External Walls/Gates upgradable wood → stone with a hammer** (no more demolish-and-replace).
- **Helicopter shredding** at [[Junkyard]]: drive a heli onto the shredder for **200–500 scrap** depending on type/health.
- Vending machine sales statistics; landmines disarmable (15% explode chance); fridge 48 slots; dropbox input 4 slots; elevators 50% faster.
- Tesla Coil power draw 35 → 25; anti-rad pills buffed (75 rad reduction); modular car radios.
- Built-in server profiler; native ARM64 Mac support.

## Meta takeaways for 2024

- Backpacks + bikes massively raised solo loot mobility; farm runs carry far more.
- Recycler split moved the early-game grind from Outpost AFK-recycling to contested monuments.
- Cargo docking made Harbor the new hot PvP monument every cargo cycle.
- Worldgen 2.0 maps look different from 2023 maps — relearn cliff lines and river crossings (rivers must be swum now, since May 2025 even more so).

pages.title: Rust Updates 2025
pages.body:
# Rust Updates 2025

The systems year: siege warfare, farming/cooking, the jungle biome, then a controversial progression overhaul in the fall. 2025 set records: **peak 259,646 concurrent players, 5.8M+ unique players**. See [[Rust Update History]].

## February 6 — [[Primitive Update|Primitive]]

**Catapult, Ballista, Battering Ram, Siege Tower** (a whole new raid path), **Shields**, a horse overhaul, the Primitive limited-tech gamemode, and a 4-shot mini crossbow. Full page: [[Primitive Update]].

## March 6 — [[Crafting Update]] (+ Premium Servers, March 13)

**Cooking Workbench + 8 stat pies, food spoilage (raw meat 6h / cooked 24h, paused in powered fridges), Chicken Coop, bees + bee grenades, armor insert slots (0–3 random slots), Engineering Workbench, hoppers** (auto-collect dropped items). Drones: range 300 → 600m, HP 100 → 200. Full page: [[Crafting Update]].

**Premium Servers** (Mar 13): opt-in servers requiring a **$15+ Steam inventory** — anti-cheap-cheat-account friction. By April, Facepunch reported **4x fewer cheater encounters** on Premium.

## April 3 — Soft Refresh

Softcore mode overhauled (the mode, not the whole game):
- Respawn with **50% of your inventory automatically** (Reclaim Terminal removed).
- Destroyed containers/TCs leave repairable "debris" retaining 50% contents; destroyed TCs keep authorization 48h.
- **Bullet damage −25%** in Softcore; door upkeep ~90% for large bases (anti-honeycomb pressure).
- Game-wide: area-of-effect visualizations for sprinklers/heaters/sensors/turrets/traps; HackerOne bug bounty formalized.

## May 1 — [[Jungle Update]]

**First new biome since procedural maps**: jungle (tier-0 spawn zones), tigers, panthers, crocodiles, snakes (venom), vine swinging, **Blowpipe** (4 dart types), **Boomerang**, Ziggurat + Jungle Ruins monuments. Rivers everywhere got longer/wider/deeper. **Armor explosive protection capped at 75%** (was 93% — no more near-rocket-immunity). Full page: [[Jungle Update]].

## June 5 — Nerfed, Buffed, Balanced?

- Jungle polish: ore node spawns up massively (Excavator +45%, Trainyard +34%, Airfield +37%); players no longer spawn in jungle.
- **Craftable silencers**: Soda Can (40 frags, ~12 shots) and Oil Filter (10 HQM, ~48 shots); Military Silencer now loot-only.
- **Indoor lighting overhaul** — interiors no longer darken the whole world (fixed unfair sightlines).
- Wooden barricade stack 10 → 5; incapacitate dart nerfed (6s → 4s); teas got Advanced/Pure variants; produce spoils into Spoiled Produce (48h fridge timer).
- Loot scaling convar caps spawn acceleration at 300 pop.

## July 3 — Friends with Benefits

- **Party system**: invite from main menu, friends join the same server together and are **auto-placed on the same team**. Big for duo/trio.
- **Deployable snapping** (hold Shift): wall/corner alignment for furniture and IO.
- **Permanent Outpost spawn point** unlocked via a Fishing Village mission (30-min cooldown; not in Softcore).
- Patrol Helicopter flee behavior capped at 1 grid; flee location shown on map.

## August 7 — Harder Core

- **Hardcore mode returns, reworked**: map fog-of-war until explored, **Compass item** required to see position, **firearms cannot be crafted or researched**, ammo crafting 5x cost, bag cooldown 15 min, upkeep doubled.
- **Full main-menu/UI redesign**; **loading up to 65% faster**; 10–20% less memory.
- Volumetric clouds + biome fog with god rays; batched projectile updates (2x faster).
- Heavy armor movement penalty moved: 20% chest / 10% legs (was 10/20).

## September 4 — Maintenance

- **Gunshot audibility now scales by weapon class: pistols/SMGs 400m, AK/LR 500m, bolty-class 600m** (was a flat 350m). You hear distant fights — and others hear yours.
- Team sleeping-bag labels (hammer shows whose bag is whose); minicopter damage indicators at 45%/20% HP.
- Famous fix: "players' eyes sometimes appeared closed — fixed."

## October 2 — [[Meta Shift Update|Meta Shift]]

**Blueprint Fragments**: Workbench Tier 2 needs **5 Basic Fragments**, Tier 3 needs **5 Advanced Fragments**, found at monuments/crates/airdrops — progression gated behind leaving base. Monument loot reshuffled after 5+ years; new puzzles at Dome/Ferry Terminal/Radtown; **Nuclear Missile Silo upgraded to red keycard + 3 elite crates**. Crosshair customization. Full page: [[Meta Shift Update]].

## November 6 — [[Pivot Or Die Update|Pivot Or Die]]

Doubling down on Meta Shift: **full blueprint wipe** (first in years), research costs slashed (**common 15, uncommon 30, rare 60, very rare 120 scrap** — down from 20/75/125/500), **scrap cost removed from crafting workbenches**. Fragments stayed. Solo players were loudly unhappy (PC Gamer ran multiple pieces). Also: Mini Fridge (18 slots), storage-adapter box sorting, **patrol heli flares no longer counter homing missiles**, elevators 3 → 5 m/s. Full page: [[Pivot Or Die Update]].

## December 3 + 18 — Getting It Right / Silent Night, Violent Night

The planned **Naval update was delayed to Feb 5, 2026** ("we took on too much"). Dec 4 was a wipe-only patch; Dec 18 brought the Christmas event + the smaller content. Naval testing opened on Staging.

## Meta takeaways for 2025

- Raid meta widened: siege weapons give a sulfur-free (but telegraphed) raid path.
- Food/farming became a real subsystem — spoilage means fridges and logistics matter.
- Premium servers + (later) TPM-secured servers became the cleanest places to play.
- Oct–Nov progression changes are THE thing to understand returning: fragments gate workbenches; research is cheap once you have them.

pages.title: Rust Updates 2026
pages.body:
# Rust Updates 2026

January–June 2026 (current as of 2026-06-12). The naval half-year: player-built boats, a deep-sea endgame zone, then base/QoL catch-up and a full player-model overhaul. See [[Rust Update History]].

## January 1 — Surviving 12 Years (recap + roadmap)

2025 recap (peak 259,646 players). **2026 roadmap announced**: Naval update (Feb 5), new player models & animations (shipped June), **cows, sheep, and an animal breeding system** (pending as of June), new monuments including **apartment complexes** (pending), Rust Mobile global release, a third-party anti-cheat layer, and a battlepass-style "Rust Premium" monetization experiment (separate team; due late 2026).

## February 5 — [[Naval Update]]

The biggest update of the era: **player-built modular boats** (Boat Building Station: hull blocks, sails, engines, helms, anchors, cannons, ramps), the **Deep Sea** offshore event zone (opens/closes like a world event; no building; first-come loot), **Tropical Islands**, **Ghost Ship** monuments, **Floating Cities** (4 variants with vendors, recyclers, casino), **PT Boat** (two .50 cal turrets), RHIB refresh, smarter naval scientists that can't see through walls. Full page: [[Naval Update]].

## February 17 — Lunar New Year 2026

Seasonal event (Year of the Horse cosmetics: Ornate Horse Mask, horse armor skins). No system changes.

## March 5 — Shipshape (naval polish)

- **Electricity, industrial, and water IO now work on player boats**; wallpaper on boats; deployable snapping on boats.
- Deep Sea rework: loot **respawns slowly** (was never), random spawn locations, initial fill ~70%, **RHIBs banned from entry**, network range 300 → 640m, open-notification sound.
- **Boat combat**: cannon hits slow vessels to 30% speed; aim sway when firing from a moving boat. Boat decay delay 12 → 24h.
- Naval scientists rebalanced: can't see through smoke, hazmat protection 5% → 30%, full metal 25% → 50%, miss more but everyone takes less burst damage.
- **Daytime extended ~20 minutes** (night unchanged at ~10 min).
- Anticheat: servers can opt in to require **TPM 2.0 + Secure Boot**.

## April 2 — Spring Clean

- **Armoured Ladder Hatch** (T3, square + triangle variants): direct upgrade from Metal Ladder Hatch — top-tier vertical access for bunker bases.
- **Water Wheel**: river-placed renewable electricity (tidal/inconsistent in ocean); can be manually run like a hamster wheel (yes, you can put handcuffed players in it).
- **Tech tree multi-unlock**: click any node, see the path, unlock the whole path in one press.
- **Overfishing**: heavily fished spots yield junk until they repopulate; deep-sea fishing loot buffed.
- Plant ripeness window 14 → 24h; shield hitboxes fixed; Salvaged Axe + Medical Syringe remodeled after 12 years.
- New GPU-driven terrain renderer (~1,000 fewer drawcalls); secure (TPM) servers measured at **1 cheater per 63 players vs 1 per 42** on regular servers.
- Easter event Apr 2–16.

## May 7 — [[Upgrade Hard, Raid Harder Update|Upgrade hard, raid harder]]

**Workbench Augmentations** (9 rare non-craftable drops that bolt bonus effects onto your workbench) and the **Mortar** (long-range indirect-fire raid/anti-personnel weapon, 2 shell types, no aiming guide). **Tin Can Alarm can be rigged with 9 throwables** (F1, molotov, bee grenade, beancan, flashbang, smoke, supply signal, flare, firecracker) and throws them when tripped. Binoculars remodeled with 3 zoom levels; Computer Station now needs power; vending machine admin UI redesigned. Full page: [[Upgrade Hard, Raid Harder Update]].

## June 4 — [[Built Different Update|Built Different]] (current patch)

**Player model overhaul** (new rig, proportions, faces, hair — first in ~10 years; your race/gender seed kept), **M16A2** (loot-only 3-round-burst rifle, lower per-shot damage than LR-300), **Ballistic Vest/Helmet/Leg armor + BDU clothing** (loot-only, slightly better than existing top tier), **Unity 6 engine upgrade** (known issue: 1000Hz+ mice need polling lowered), new opt-in navmesh (animals can path into bases when enabled). Full page: [[Built Different Update]].

## Still on the 2026 roadmap (not yet shipped as of June)

- Cows, sheep, animal breeding/farming expansion
- Apartment-complex monuments
- "Rust Premium" battlepass-style system (late 2026)
- Rust Mobile global launch

pages.title: Upgrade Hard, Raid Harder Update
pages.body:
# Upgrade Hard, Raid Harder Update

**May 7, 2026** — official post: rust.facepunch.com/news/upgrade-hard-raid-harder.

## Workbench Augmentations
- **Nine distinct workbench upgrade modules**, each a **rare, non-craftable drop** (monument/loot chase items).
- Each augmentation bolts a unique bonus effect onto your [[Workbench]] (mix-and-match; each has its own visual). Collecting all nine = fully upgraded bench.
- New late-game chase layer on top of the [[Meta Shift Update|fragment]] progression.

## Mortar
- Deployable **indirect-fire siege weapon**: lobs shells long distances from flat ground.
- **No aiming guide** (unlike cannons) — range-finding is trial and error, best with [[Binoculars]] + a spotter. Recoil bumps the mortar and adds shot variance.
- **Two shell types: anti-personnel and anti-structure.** Joins the [[Primitive Update]] siege arsenal as the long-range bombardment option for raids/sieges.

## Tin Can Alarm rigging
- The Tin Can Alarm (Aug 2024) can now be **rigged with 9 throwables**: F1 Grenade, Molotov, Bee Grenade, Beancan, Flashbang, Smoke Grenade, Supply Signal, Flare, Firecracker.
- Tripping the wire throws the rigged item on the spot — cheap boobytraps for bases, compounds, or monument puzzle camping. (Supply Signal rig = troll airdrop beacon.)

## Other changes
- **Binoculars remade**: new model/UI, cheaper craft, 3 zoom levels.
- **Computer Station now requires electricity** (CCTV/drone bases need power budget).
- Vending machine admin UI rebuilt (sell from inventory, per-skin listings, reorder).
- Server browser region system (IP-geolocation, anti ping-spoofing); Discord shop partnership (20% off pre-2026 DLC); Crypt Stone building skin; deep-sea loot + scientist boats toned down; flat-bow boats slowed.
- Windows Server 2016 support ended; min Windows 10 build 19043.

## Meta impact
Mortars added true artillery to online raids — flat ground near a target base is now a threat vector. Rigged tin cans made cheap "claymore-style" perimeter defense standard for solos.

pages.title: Waves Of Change Update
pages.body:
# Waves Of Change Update

**April 4, 2024** — official post: rust.facepunch.com/news/waves-of-change. Reworked [[Harbor]] + [[Cargo Ship]] into a single PvP event and overhauled electricity costs.

## Harbor & Cargo Ship docking
- Both harbor variants visually/gameplay reworked.
- **Cargo Ship now docks at harbors it passes** — board it from land, no boat needed. **60-second horn warning** before departure.
- Harbor island becomes a "stronghold" while docked (access via rotating bridge or crane jumps); cranes load openable containers onto the deck (hide inside!).
- Loot refreshes **up to 3 times every 10 minutes**, one refresh triggered on docking.
- May 2024 tweak: docks at **both** harbors; containers spawn 100m out.

## New weapons (Heavy Scientist drops)
- **Minigun**: rare drop from Heavy Scientists; 1.5s spin-up, slows movement while spinning; ammo needs WB2. Not craftable.
- **Military Flamethrower**: Heavy Scientist tier, huge damage to ~12m, lays area-denial fire walls.

## Electricity overhaul
- **15 logic components no longer consume power**: Splitter, Blocker, RAND/XOR/AND/OR switches, Timer, Counter, Memory Cell, Smart Switch, Pressure Pad, Button, Root Combiner, Electrical Branch.
- Circuits got dramatically cheaper to power — complex bases need fewer batteries. See [[Electricity]].
- Deploy guides align components to walls (Shift to align).

## AI changes
- **[[Patrol Helicopter]] rework**: randomized rocket counts/turn speeds, orbital attack phase, damage "zones" — it focuses whoever is hurting it and **flees from areas that burst it down** ("No-Go Zones"), encouraging chases.
- **[[Bradley APC]] deploys scientists** when engaged at [[Launch Site]] and on roads.

## Other
- Retro Tool Cupboard DLC skin with live upkeep monitor display.
- Oil Rig "saturation tube" underwater entrance to Level 3 + CCTV desk on both rigs.
- SRV DNS server support; anti-cheat: ~27k bans in April, 84,753 YTD.

## Meta impact
Cargo became a land-accessible monument event every cycle — harbor control at dock time is one of the biggest recurring fights on the map. Electricity-heavy base designs (turrets + smart alarms) became much easier to run.

pages.title: World Update 2.0
pages.body:
# World Update 2.0

**October 3, 2024** — official post: rust.facepunch.com/news/world_update_2. Procedural maps were regenerated from the ground up — a 2023-era player's map knowledge is partly obsolete.

## World generation overhaul
- **New cliff systems** (coastal + inland), rebuilt rock formations (fan favorites like "god rock" and "arch rock" return).
- **New terrain features: canyons, lakes, oases** scattered across proc-gen maps.
- **Rivers**: longer, flow more naturally, widen toward the mouth (further widened/deepened May 2025 — most rivers must be swum).
- Old rock/cliff assets removed the following month (custom maps had to update).

## Radtown returns
- The Legacy-era **[[Radtown]]** monument came back as a refreshed small/mid monument: original blocky garage proportions, modernized pathing and cover. Got a puzzle room in Oct 2025 ([[Meta Shift Update]]).

## New items
- **High Calibre Revolver**: single-action revolver firing **5.56 rifle ammo**, T2 unlock — hard-hitting budget pistol.
- **Diver Propulsion Vehicle (DPV)**: handheld underwater scooter, low-grade fuel, deployable in 1m+ water. (Later purchasable at Fishing Village, Nov 2025.)
- **Legacy Woodpiles**: harvestable wood nodes in snow/temperate biomes.
- **Radioactive Water**: kills plants instantly, irradiates carriers — a griefing/area-denial liquid (buffed Nov 2024).

## Water/ocean
- **3 new dive sites** (6 crates each), remodeled buoys, better underwater visibility.
- **Water Wells** got NPC vendors (teas/farming gear, 30-min refresh) + auto-filling planters with high-quality genes.

## Events
- Charitable Rust 2024 (Oct 12–19, Direct Relief); 40% sale.

## Meta impact
Maps simply look and play differently than 2023: new cliff lines change roam routes and base spots; lakes/oases are new farm/water bases; Radtown is a new tier-0/1 hotspot. Combined with the May 2025 jungle, "map sense" needs a full refresh.

pages.title: Attack Helicopter
pages.body:
# Attack Helicopter

Player-flown gunship added September 2023 ("Airborne" update). Pilot flies, gunner runs a nose turret and rocket pods. The apex air-PvP vehicle — and the main target of the November 2025 air-combat rebalance.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | 850 |
| Seats | 2 — pilot + gunner |
| Cost | **2,250 scrap** — Airwolf Vendor, [[Bandit Camp]] |
| Starting fuel | 100 [[Low Grade Fuel]] |
| Fuel use | 30 LGF/min; tank 500 → ~16 min 39 s |
| Repair (0→full) | 500 metal fragments, hammer (17 swings) — **ground only** |
| Decay | 10 min idle trigger; 8 h outside, 48 h inside |
| Explodes on death | Yes |

## Armament

| Weapon | Capacity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Nose turret | 1 (built-in style, like an [[Auto Turret]]) | gunner-controlled, fed with 5.56 rifle ammo |
| HV Rockets | up to 36 | side pods; HV and incendiary only — no standard rockets |
| Incendiary Rockets | up to 36 | area denial / soft-side burning |
| Flares | up to 30 | built-in launcher, spoofs [[Homing Missile Launcher]] |

Loading happens via the side pods while landed. The gunner gets a dedicated targeting view.

## November 2025 nerfs (current state)

- **Hand-thrown flares no longer fool homing missiles** — only the built-in flare launcher works.
- **No in-flight repair** — you must land to hammer-repair.
- **Pilot cannot eat/heal while flying.**
- (Compensation: [[Minicopter]] and [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]] received their own built-in flare launchers.)

Net effect: attack helis no longer perma-loiter over bases. Strafe, leave, land, repair.

## Meta use

- **Raid support**: incendiary rockets + turret suppress roof campers while the ground team works. Rocket pods can't breach like real raid explosives — it's anti-player, not anti-base.
- **Air superiority**: the only vehicle that reliably kills other helis in flight.
- **Counters**: [[SAM Site]]s, Homing Missile Launchers (force flare dumps — 30 max), and massed turret fire. 850 HP is less than a scrap heli; it wins by damage, not by tanking.
- For a solo this is a luxury; it really needs a dedicated gunner — premier duo toy.

## Related

[[Minicopter]] · [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]] · [[Homing Missile Launcher]] · [[SAM Site]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Diver Propulsion Vehicle
pages.body:
# Diver Propulsion Vehicle

The **DPV** (added October 2024) is a handheld underwater scooter — a quiet, pocketable alternative to a [[Submarines|submarine]] for moving around underwater. You craft it, **keep it in your inventory**, deploy it when you hit the water, and pick it back up when done.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Power | [[Low Grade Fuel]] (burns a lot) |
| Top speed | ~**21 km/h** underwater |
| Seats | 1 |
| Storage | none (it's a tool, not a boat) |
| Craft | **15 HQM + 1 Tech Trash** |
| Research | **75 scrap** to unlock the blueprint |
| Stowable | yes — carry it in your inventory, deploy/retrieve on demand |
| Features | forward flashlight, fuel + speed gauges, two handlebars |

## How to get one

Research the blueprint for **75 scrap**, then craft with **15 High Quality Metal + 1 Tech Trash**. No vendor purchase.

## Notes

- **Stealth over speed**: far quieter than a submarine, and you can't be spotted as a big vehicle silhouette — but it has no weapons and no storage.
- Burns Low Grade Fuel quickly despite the modest top speed.
- Great for the [[Deep Sea]] and underwater labs where a sub is overkill or too loud.
- Has a flashlight for navigating dark underwater spaces.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Stealthy Deep Sea / underwater loot travel** — slip past [[PT Boat|PT boats]] and divers without engine noise.
- **Pocket escape tool**: drop into water during a chase, deploy, and scoot away submerged.
- Pair with diving gear for extended underwater operations; carry a spare can of LGF since it drinks fuel.

## Related

[[Submarines]] · [[Kayak]] · [[Deep Sea]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Horses
pages.body:
# Horses

The fuel-free mount. Horses cost no [[Low Grade Fuel]] — they eat food — and after the **February 2025 rework** they **swim, auto-avoid trees, can be led/towed, and tow [[Siege Weapons]]**. That makes them the go-to overland vehicle for the wide rivers and [[Jungle]] of the post-[[World Update 2.0]] map, where a [[Modular Cars|car]] would get stuck.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | **400** (all breeds) |
| Stamina | max **30** |
| Fuel | none — eats food (corn, pumpkin, mushrooms, berries, grain) to restore stamina/health |
| Saddlebags | **+6 slots each**, up to 2 bags (slight speed penalty) |
| Swims | yes, while it has stamina — **runs out of stamina in water = the horse drowns** |
| Tows | [[Siege Weapons]] (catapult, ballista, siege tower) since Feb 2025 |
| Heal | **Medical Syringe** restores 60 HP instantly + ~5s speed boost (Nov 2025) |
| Decay | ~3 h (180 min) if left without food; feed at a Hitch & Trough |

## Speed by breed

Faster breeds matter for roaming. Horseshoes (Basic / High Quality) add speed.

| Breed | Default | Basic shoes | HQ shoes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black / White Thoroughbred | 58.5 | 63.9 | **67.5** km/h |
| Chestnut / Piebald | 51.5 | 56.9 | 60.5 km/h |
| Appaloosa, Bay, Buckskin, Pinto | 46.8 | 52.2 | 55.8 km/h |
| Dapple Grey / Red Roan | 42.1 | 47.5 | 51.1 km/h |

For comparison a [[Motorbikes and Bicycles|motorbike]] tops ~92 km/h — horses are slower but go anywhere and need no fuel.

## How to get one

1. **Tame a wild horse**: spawn naturally in **Temperate and Desert** biomes (not Arctic, not water/snow/tunnels/monuments). Mount and ride one you find.
2. **Buy a saddle at a stable**: the **Stable Shopkeeper** at the **Ranch** or **Large Barn** monument sells:
   - Single Horse Saddle — **75 scrap**
   - Double Horse Saddle (2 riders) — **90 scrap**
3. Keep it at a **Hitch & Trough** at your base — feed it so it doesn't decay, and it heals up to 400 HP there.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Fuel-free farming/roaming**: no scrap or LGF outlay; the cheapest sustainable transport in the game.
- **River and jungle crossing**: swims the wide rivers that now split the map; threads trees automatically.
- **Siege logistics**: tow a catapult/ballista to an enemy base for a primitive raid (see [[Siege Weapons]]).
- **Watch the stamina bar in water** — sprinting across a deep river with an empty bar kills the horse and dumps you.
- Saddlebags (+12 slots with two) make it a decent loot mule on a budget.

## Related

[[Siege Weapons]] · [[Motorbikes and Bicycles]] · [[Modular Cars]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Hot Air Balloon
pages.body:
# Hot Air Balloon

Slow, silent, wind-pushed flight platform. You control altitude (burner) — the wind controls direction. Niche but beloved for cheap drop-raids and early-wipe aerial scouting, especially with the armor upgrade.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | 1,500 (**2,500 with Hot Air Balloon Armor**) |
| Capacity | open basket — whole team can stand in it (0 mounted seats) |
| Storage | 18 slots |
| Cost | **150 scrap** — Airwolf Vendor, [[Bandit Camp]] (comes with 75 [[Low Grade Fuel]]); also world spawns in fields |
| Fuel use | 12 LGF/min; tank 500 → ~41 min 40 s |
| Repair (0→full) | 100 cloth, hammer (25 swings) |
| Decay | starts 10 min after abandonment; ~3 h outside; doesn't decay indoors |
| Explodes on death | No |

## Hot Air Balloon Armor

| | |
|---|---|
| Effect | basket side-walls, max HP 1,500 → **2,500**, adds doorway opening |
| Buy | 70 scrap at [[Bandit Camp]] |
| Learn | Tech tree T1 (150 scrap total) or research table 75 scrap; common in roadside brown crates |
| Equip | balloon must be grounded — face the burner button, hold E → Upgrade Armor |
| Caveat | the doorway **cannot be locked** |

## Operation

- Hold the burner (red button) to rise; release to sink. Drift direction = current wind. No steering — plan with the wind or don't fly.
- Toggleable anchor rope keeps it parked.
- [[SAM Site]]s and [[Auto Turret]]s target it; without armor the basket gives almost no cover.

## Meta use

- **Drop raids**: float over a base at night, [[Parachute]] or drop the team onto the roof. Armored balloon + shields made this a real archetype again post-2025.
- **Cheapest flight in Rust**: 150 scrap vs 750 for a [[Minicopter]] — great first-day aerial recon for a solo.
- Low fuel burn (12/min vs 30/min for helis) means long loiter time for map scouting.
- Terrible escape vehicle — anyone with a bolty will pop you out of the basket.

## Related

[[Minicopter]] · [[Parachute]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Kayak
pages.body:
# Kayak

The fuel-free, silent watercraft. A kayak needs no [[Low Grade Fuel]] — you paddle it by alternating **left-click / right-click** with the Paddle. Slow, but completely free to run and quiet enough to sneak.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | ~200–300 |
| Capacity | 1–2 (driver + 1) |
| Power | manual paddling (no fuel) |
| Cost | cheap blueprint (~50 scrap to research) + craft; also sold at Boat Vendor |
| Craft | wood + cloth + a small amount of metal fragments |
| Storage | minimal |

## How to get one

- **Craft it** after unlocking the blueprint (researchable cheaply), or
- **Buy** from the **Boat Vendor** at a [[Fishing Village]].

## Notes

- Paddle by alternating mouse buttons — rhythm matters for speed.
- **Silent and fuel-free** — great for stealth approaches and for crossing the **wider rivers** of the post-[[World Update 2.0]] map without burning fuel.
- Can navigate shallower water than a [[Rowboat]]/[[RHIB]].
- No protection and slow — a sitting duck if spotted in open water.

## Meta use (solo)

- **First-minute traversal**: cross rivers and reach a nearby island before you have any scrap or fuel.
- **Quiet infiltration**: paddle up to a coastal base without the engine noise of a motorboat.
- **Naked beach spawn escape**: cheap and craftable from gathered resources.

## Related

[[Rowboat]] · [[RHIB]] · [[Diver Propulsion Vehicle]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Minicopter
pages.body:
# Minicopter

The workhorse of Rust air travel: a cheap two-seat helicopter that turns any monument run, roof camp, or counter-raid into a 60-second commute. Still the best scrap-per-utility vehicle in the game.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | 750 |
| Seats | 2 (pilot + side passenger) |
| Cost | **750 scrap** — Airwolf Vendor, [[Bandit Camp]] |
| Starting fuel | 100 [[Low Grade Fuel]] |
| Fuel use | 30 LGF/min (1,800/hour) |
| Tank | 500 LGF → ~16 min 39 s of flight |
| Repair (0→full) | 250 metal fragments, hammer (15 swings) |
| Decay | starts after 10 min idle; **8 h outside**, 48 h inside a base |
| Explodes on death | Yes — bail before it pops |
| Flares | built-in flare launcher, max 5 flares (added Nov 2025) |

## How to get one

1. Buy at the Airwolf hangar in [[Bandit Camp]] (heli pad on the river side) for 750 scrap. Prices float with vendor demand since Jul 2024, so it can run slightly higher on busy servers.
2. Rarely found as a world spawn / stolen off careless players' roofs.

## Flying notes

- W/S = pitch, A/D = yaw, mouse = cyclic. Hover tax is real: you burn the same 30 LGF/min hovering as cruising, so land instead of hovering.
- The passenger can shoot freely; the pilot cannot.
- **Nov 2025 air rebalance**: no repairing while flying, no eating/medding as pilot, hand-thrown flares no longer spoof [[Homing Missile Launcher]] missiles — only the built-in flare launcher works (5 flares max).
- [[SAM Site]]s lock on at range and at monuments ([[Launch Site]] has them); [[Auto Turret]]s shred a mini fast — 750 HP melts in seconds of 5.56.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- Cheapest force-multiplier in the game: do a [[Cargo Ship]] chase, hit [[Large Oil Rig]] (land on the helipad), or hop between monuments hunting Blueprint Fragments.
- Park it **inside** your base footprint (48 h decay vs 8 h outside) on a mini pad above shooting-floor height.
- Carries exactly a duo — for trios take the [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]].
- Counter-raid taxi: 750 scrap is cheap enough to treat as disposable mid-wipe.

## Related

[[Scrap Transport Helicopter]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Hot Air Balloon]] · [[Parachute]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Modular Cars
pages.body:
# Modular Cars

The most customizable land vehicle in Rust. You don't buy a car — you find a rusted **chassis** on the roadside, drag it onto a **Modular Car Lift**, bolt on **modules** (cockpit, storage, passenger, engine, etc.), then repair a small engine with **engine parts**. The result is a code-lockable land rig that hauls a duo/trio plus loot across the post-[[World Update 2.0]] road network.

## Chassis

Chassis spawn already-built (with random modules) or empty on roads — roughly **3 modular cars per km** by default. They can't be crafted.

| Chassis | Module slots | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Small | 2 | nimble runabout |
| Medium | 3 | balanced workhorse |
| Large | 4 | full loot/transport rig |

## Modules

Each module occupies 1 or 2 slots and has its own HP — the car only dies when the **whole chassis** is destroyed, but individual modules can be shot off.

| Module | Max HP | Slots | Function |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cockpit | 360 | 1 | driver cockpit, 2 seats |
| Cockpit w/ Engine | 425 | 1 | cockpit + built-in small engine, 2 seats |
| Armored Cockpit | 700 | 1 | armored cockpit, 2 seats |
| Engine | 300 | 1 | engine only, no seats |
| Passenger | 525 | 2 | 4 seats, no cockpit |
| Armored Passenger | 675 | 1 | armored, 2 seats |
| Rear Seats | 275 | 1 | 2 seats |
| Storage | 275 | 1 | 48-slot lockable storage |
| Fuel Tank | 325 | 2 | 200,000 mL extra fuel storage |
| Flatbed | 250 | 1 | flat cargo bed |
| Large Flatbed | 325 | 2 | bigger flat bed |
| Camper | 525 | 2 | 4 seats + bed/amenities |
| Taxi | 295 | 1 | 2 seats + metal shopfront face |

A working car needs at least one **engine** module (or a Cockpit w/ Engine) and one cockpit to drive.

## Engine parts

The engine is empty when you find a chassis. Each engine module has slots for **5 part types**, each in **3 quality tiers** (low / medium / high). You need at least one of each type for the engine to run; higher tier = more power/top speed and better fuel efficiency.

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| Carburetor | air/fuel mix |
| Crankshaft | power transfer |
| Pistons | compression |
| Spark Plugs | ignition |
| Valves | airflow |

Parts come from loot (blue boxes, components), the tech tree, or are **sold by the second-floor vendor at [[Bandit Camp]]** (medium quality). You can also craft low/medium parts.

## Fuel, lift, lock

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Fuel | [[Low Grade Fuel]] only; tank holds up to 500 (more with Fuel Tank module) |
| Lock | Vehicle Key Lock — **75 metal fragments** + 4-digit code |
| Module swaps | only on a powered **Modular Car Lift** |
| Modular Car Lift | crafted, must be wired to power; **[[Junkyard]] has a free permanently-powered lift** |
| Repair | hammer + cloth in inventory; ~61 damage healed per swing |
| Decay | ~864 minutes (~14.4 h) default if left out; park inside |

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Cheapest serious transport** if you can't afford a [[Minicopter]] — no scrap cost, just looted parts.
- A Large chassis with Cockpit w/ Engine + Storage + Storage + Armored Passenger is the classic loot-run/raid car: code-locked storage, 4 seats, armor up front.
- Roads are dangerous — cars are loud and visible; good for crossing the map fast, bad for stealth.
- Use the [[Junkyard]] free lift to set up your build, then drive home and code-lock it.

## Related

[[Motorbikes and Bicycles]] · [[Horses]] · [[Junkyard]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Motorbikes and Bicycles
pages.body:
# Motorbikes and Bicycles

Added in the **July 2024 update**, bikes are the cheap personal-mobility tier: a single rider's answer to "I don't have 750 scrap for a [[Minicopter]] and the roads are too dangerous on foot." Four variants — two pedal (free, no fuel) and two motorized (fast, [[Low Grade Fuel]]).

## The four variants

| Variant | Power | Seats | Max HP | Top speed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pedal Bike** | calories (no fuel) | 1 | ~250 | slow, uphill drains you |
| **Trike** (pedal + rear car) | calories | 2 | ~275 | slow but carries a passenger |
| **Motorbike** | [[Low Grade Fuel]] | 1 | 300 | 0–180 km/h dial, ~92 km/h practical |
| **Motorbike with Sidecar** | [[Low Grade Fuel]] | 2 | 350 | similar, slightly slower loaded |

Pedal bikes consume your **food/calories** instead of fuel — bring meat or you'll exhaust climbing hills. Motorbikes sip Low Grade Fuel and are loud.

## How to get one

- **Find them**: spawn on roadsides and at road-adjacent monuments all over the map (same kind of spawn logic as [[Modular Cars]]).
- **Craft them**: bikes are craftable once you've unlocked the blueprints via the tech tree.
- **Scrap value**: a motorbike shredded at the [[Junkyard]] scrapper is worth about **40 scrap** — cheap, treat as disposable.

## Riding notes

- Wheelie / lean control: you can pop the front wheel; bad landings damage the bike and you.
- Motorbikes are excellent **drive-by** platforms — the rider can use one-handed weapons, and the sidecar passenger can fire freely.
- Off-road handling is rough; they're road/flat-terrain vehicles. For rivers and the [[Jungle]] you'll want a [[Horses|horse]] or boat.
- No code lock — anyone can hop on an unattended bike. Park it inside.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Early-wipe taxi**: the pedal bike costs nothing and needs no fuel — perfect first-hour map traversal before you have scrap.
- **Sidecar duo**: driver + gunner is a legitimate roaming kit for jumping unsuspecting farmers on roads.
- Far cheaper than a [[Modular Cars|car]] and far quieter than a heli, but offers zero protection — one bullet to the rider ends the trip.

## Related

[[Modular Cars]] · [[Horses]] · [[Snowmobiles]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Junkyard]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Parachute
pages.body:
# Parachute

Not a vehicle so much as an **aerial deployment item** — but it's core to the air game. Added in the September 2023 "Airborne" update, the parachute was the **first item to use the new backpack equipment slot**. Equip it, jump from height, and deploy to glide down safely — the backbone of balloon and helicopter **drop-raids**.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Craft | **2 Tarp + 2 Sewing Kit + 50 Cloth** at a **Tier 2 [[Workbench]]** |
| Slot | the **backpack / clothing slot** (not a hand item) |
| Durability | ~**20% lost per use → ~5 uses** before it breaks (repairable) |
| Minimum deploy height | needs altitude (~15 m+) to open — won't save a short fall |
| Steering | hold direction keys to glide; flare/cut to drop faster |

## How to use

1. Craft it (T2 Workbench) and **equip it in the backpack slot**.
2. Get height — jump from a [[Hot Air Balloon]], [[Minicopter]], cliff, or tall monument.
3. Press the deploy key mid-air to open the canopy, then steer toward your target.
4. Each deployment chews ~20% durability; carry spares or repair.

## Notes

- **Drop-raid enabler**: the classic play is an armored [[Hot Air Balloon]] floating over a base at night, then the team parachutes onto the roof.
- You're vulnerable while gliding — slow and predictable; a bolt-action ends a parachutist.
- Works from any sufficient height, not just vehicles — handy for escaping a cliff-edge fight.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Roof access**: parachute onto bases that are otherwise hard to climb.
- **Heli bailout**: jump from a burning [[Minicopter]]/[[Attack Helicopter]] before it explodes and chute to safety.
- Cheap insurance once you have a T2 bench — keep one equipped whenever you fly.

## Related

[[Hot Air Balloon]] · [[Minicopter]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Player-Built Boats
pages.body:
# Player-Built Boats

The headline of the **February 2026 [[Naval Update]]** — the biggest content drop in years. Instead of buying a fixed boat, you now **build a fully custom ship** on the open water: place a **Boat Building Station**, lay down a hull, then bolt on **sails, engines, a helm, cannons, ramps, planks, and an anchor**. This system **replaced the [[Tugboat]]** (which was vaulted) as Rust's mobile sea base.

## How to build one

1. **Place a Boat Building Station** in deep/shallow water (it's the water-placed equivalent of a building planner for boats).
2. Insert a **Boat Plan / Building Plan** and place a **hull**.
3. Attach modular components on/around the hull.
4. Lock the **helm** with a code lock; drop an **anchor** to keep it from drifting.

Boats are assembled and edited at the station, similar to how [[Modular Cars]] are edited on a car lift.

## Hull types

| Hull | Strength |
|---|---|
| **Speed** | fastest, lightest, least armored |
| **Cargo** | holds large storage boxes — the loot/base hull |
| **Armored** | tankiest, slowest, best for combat/raiding |

There are also four **NPC/world ship variants** that spawn: **Clipper, Lander, Galleon, Trawler**.

## Components

| Component | Function |
|---|---|
| **Sails** | wind propulsion — free, no fuel; placement affects handling/speed |
| **Engines** | run on [[Low Grade Fuel]] and burn it **fast**; tiers from **T1 Outboard → T2 → T3 Industrial Marine Engine** |
| **Helm / steering wheel** | steers the ship; **built-in code lock** secures the vessel |
| **Anchor** | holds position, stops drift |
| **Cannons** | naval gun, loaded with **cannonballs**, for sinking other boats |
| **Harpoon Launcher** | added with the cannons for naval combat |
| **Ramps & Planks** | bridge gaps, enable boarding and loading vehicles |

**Electricity + Industrial IO support** was added in **March 2026** — you can now wire power and run conveyor/industrial systems on your ship (turning it into a powered mobile base).

> Careful engine + sail placement matters: a badly balanced ship handles poorly. Mix sails (free) with engines (fuel) for range vs. speed.

## Deep Sea access

- The big **modular ships cannot enter the [[Deep Sea]]** event zone, and neither can [[RHIB|RHIBs]] in some readings — verify per-server; **[[PT Boat|PT boats]] and RHIBs are the craft that reach Deep Sea** per the official notes.
- The Deep Sea forbids building and respawning — your modular base-ship stays in normal waters.

## Meta use (solo/duo/trio)

- **Mobile sea base**: a Cargo hull with boxes, sleeping bags, and (post-March) electricity = a floating home that's hard to find and can relocate.
- **Naval raiding**: an Armored hull with cannons can sink enemy ships and shell coastal bases.
- **Logistics**: ramps + planks load a [[Motorbikes and Bicycles|bike]] or loot onto the deck.
- Expensive in materials and fuel (engines drink LGF) — a project for an established team, not first-day.

## Related

[[Naval Update]] · [[Tugboat]] · [[PT Boat]] · [[RHIB]] · [[Deep Sea]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: PT Boat
pages.body:
# PT Boat

Heavily armed **AI patrol craft** added in the February 2026 [[Naval Update]]. Crewed by scientists, the PT Boat aggressively engages players in open and deep water. It's not bought — it's a **threat you fight and then steal**, similar to claiming a [[Cargo Ship]]'s loot.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | high — tankier than an [[RHIB]] |
| Crew (AI) | a coordinated group of scientists |
| Speed | **slower than the RHIB** |
| Fuel | [[Low Grade Fuel]] — consumes **more than the RHIB** |
| Where | primarily the **[[Deep Sea]]** and open ocean patrols |
| Storage | onboard loot boxes |

## Armament

| Weapon | Notes |
|---|---|
| **Turret with dual .50 cal machine guns** | one twin-gun mount |
| **Turret with single .50 cal** | second mount |
| Ammo | both reload with standard **5.56 rifle ammo** |

The .50 cals shred unarmored boats and players — engaging a PT boat in a rowboat is suicide.

## How to "get" one

- **Clear the AI scientists** crewing it, then board and pilot it / loot its boxes.
- It's one of the few craft (with the [[RHIB]]) that operate in the **[[Deep Sea]]** zone.

## Meta use (solo/duo/trio)

- **Loot target**: PT boats carry good loot and the .50 cal mounts are powerful if you capture the boat.
- **Naval threat**: when sailing your [[Player-Built Boats|modular ship]] or RHIB through patrol waters, PT boats are the main PvE danger — flee or out-gun them.
- High risk for a solo; better tackled as a duo/trio with one driver and gunners.

## Related

[[Naval Ships|Player-Built Boats]] · [[RHIB]] · [[Deep Sea]] · [[Cargo Ship]] · [[Naval Update]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: RHIB
pages.body:
# RHIB

The Rigid Hull Inflatable Boat — the standard team sea-transport. Six occupants, more storage and speed than a [[Rowboat]], and the boat you take to the [[Large Oil Rig]] or to chase the [[Cargo Ship]]. Got a **full visual + functional rebuild in the Feb 2026 [[Naval Update]]** (new model, mounted headlight, compass + map display screens, better storage).

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | 500 |
| Capacity | 1 driver + 5 passengers (6 total) |
| Cost | **300 scrap** — Boat Vendor at [[Fishing Village]] |
| Starting fuel | 50 [[Low Grade Fuel]] |
| Fuel use | **15 LGF/min** (900/hour) |
| Tank | 500 LGF → ~33 min |
| Storage | larger built-in box (~36 slots) |
| Headlight | yes (added Feb 2026) for night/storm navigation |
| Compass + map screens | yes (added Feb 2026) |
| Repair | hammer + metal fragments |

## How to get one

Buy from the **Boat Vendor** at a [[Fishing Village]] for 300 scrap (50 LGF included).

## Notes

- Faster and tankier than a rowboat, but burns 2.5x the fuel (15 vs 6/min).
- **Can still enter the [[Deep Sea]]** event zone (along with [[PT Boat|PT boats]]) — but the [[Naval Ships|big modular ships]] cannot, and the old [[Tugboat]] is gone.
- All 5 passengers can fire — a crewed RHIB is a mobile gun platform for oil rig and cargo takes.

## Meta use (solo/duo/trio)

- **The default monument boat**: take it to [[Small Oil Rig]] / [[Large Oil Rig]], board the [[Cargo Ship]], island-hop.
- Holds the whole trio plus loot; the rebuilt storage box carries a full rig haul.
- Park it ashore or in a boathouse — it decays in open water and is easy to steal.

## Related

[[Rowboat]] · [[Submarine]] · [[Naval Ships]] · [[Deep Sea]] · [[Fishing Village]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Rowboat
pages.body:
# Rowboat

The cheap starter boat. A 4-occupant motorized rowboat for crossing the ocean, hitting coastal monuments, and running early-game [[Oil Rig]] or fishing trips before you can afford an [[RHIB]].

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | ~300–400 |
| Capacity | 1 driver + 3 passengers |
| Cost | **125 scrap** — Boat Vendor at [[Fishing Village]] |
| Starting fuel | 50 [[Low Grade Fuel]] |
| Fuel use | **6 LGF/min** (360/hour) |
| Tank | 500 LGF → ~1 h 23 m |
| Storage | small built-in box (~18 slots) |
| Repair | hammer + wood/metal fragments |
| Decay | decays in open water; pull it ashore or into a boathouse |

## How to get one

Buy from the **Boat Vendor** at any [[Fishing Village]] (they ring the coast) for 125 scrap. Comes with 50 LGF.

## Notes

- Ocean-only — can't go up shallow rivers far; for rivers use a [[Kayak]] or [[Horses|horse]].
- Slow and low-profile; passengers can shoot from it.
- Very fuel-efficient (6/min) — long range on one tank.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **First-wipe water transport**: 125 scrap is the cheapest way to reach offshore monuments or a coastal base.
- Fishing trips, small [[Oil Rig]] runs, island-hopping.
- Upgrade to the [[RHIB]] (300 scrap, 6 seats, faster) once you have the scrap and need more capacity/speed.

## Related

[[RHIB]] · [[Kayak]] · [[Submarine]] · [[Fishing Village]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Scrap Transport Helicopter
pages.body:
# Scrap Transport Helicopter

The flying truck. Two cockpit seats plus an open cargo bay that fits your whole team, loot boxes, even a [[Motorbikes and Bicycles|motorbike]] or [[Modular Cars|car module]] if you're brave. Slower and fatter than a [[Minicopter]] but far tankier.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | 1,000 |
| Seats | 2 mounted (pilot + co-pilot) + open cargo bay (stand/sit unrestricted) |
| Cost | **1,250 scrap** — Airwolf Vendor, [[Bandit Camp]] |
| Starting fuel | 100 [[Low Grade Fuel]] |
| Fuel use | 30 LGF/min |
| Tank | 500 LGF → ~16 min 39 s |
| Repair (0→full) | 750 metal fragments, hammer (20 swings) |
| Decay | starts after 10 min idle; 8 h outside, 48 h inside |
| Explodes on death | Yes |
| Flares | built-in flare launcher, max 5 (added Nov 2025) |
| Headlights | Yes |

Destruction reference (don't park it in the open): 1 C4 (12 s), 2 rockets, or sustained incendiary 5.56 from an M249 kills it.

## How to get one

Airwolf hangar at [[Bandit Camp]], 1,250 scrap (demand-floating price). Also spawns crashed/abandoned at some monuments on certain servers, but vendor purchase is the reliable route.

## Flying notes

- Heavy and sluggish — long spool-up, wide turns. It will lose any race with a [[Minicopter]] but survives turret fire that would delete one.
- Cargo bay passengers can shoot 360°, making a crewed scrap heli a legitimate gunship for [[Cargo Ship]] and [[Large Oil Rig]] takes.
- Same Nov 2025 rules as all helis: no in-flight repair, no pilot healing, built-in flares only vs [[Homing Missile Launcher]].
- Junkyard trick: the magnet crane + shredder at [[Junkyard]] turns surplus helicopters into roughly **200–500 scrap** — stealing and shredding enemy helis is real income.

## Meta use (solo/duo/trio)

- The trio+ monument bus: drop the whole team on [[Launch Site]] or Oil Rig at once.
- Base relocation: the bay hauls boxes — move your loot room in two trips.
- Counter air: its 1,000 HP frame can body-block; some crews use it as a flying shield while the [[Attack Helicopter]] does damage.
- For a solo it's usually overkill — a Minicopter does the same job for 500 less scrap.

## Related

[[Minicopter]] · [[Attack Helicopter]] · [[Hot Air Balloon]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Siege Weapons
pages.body:
# Siege Weapons

Wheeled **primitive raiding machines** added in the **February 2025 "Primitive" update**. They're vehicles in the sense that you build, move, and crew them — and crucially they're **towable by [[Horses]]** — so they live alongside the vehicle pages even though their purpose is raiding without explosives. A budget, gunpowder-free way to crack a base.

## The four machines

| Weapon | Role | Setup cost (placement) | Craft/parts |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Battering Ram** | drive into walls/doors to break them | 1,000 Wood + 500 Frags | 1,000 HQM, 500 Wood, 4 Sheet Metal, 1 Tarp |
| **Catapult** | lobs boulders / firebombs over walls | 1,000 Wood + 250 Frags | 500 Wood, 20 HQM, 2 Rope, 2 Gears |
| **Ballista** | fires large bolts at walls/players | 750 Wood | 250 Frags, 2 Gears, 2 Sheet Metal |
| **Siege Tower** | mobile staircase to scale walls | 1,000 Wood | 500 Wood, 250 Frags, 1 Gear |

(Costs vary slightly by source/patch; these are the launch recipes.)

## How they work

- Built at a **Tier 1–2 [[Workbench]]** from wood/metal/gears — **no gunpowder or explosives needed**, so they unlock early and dodge the [[Raiding|explosive economy]].
- The **Battering Ram** is driven; you ram it repeatedly into a wall or door to break it.
- The **Catapult** and **Ballista** are crewed artillery — load ammo and fire at structures from range.
- The **Siege Tower** is rolled against a wall so attackers can climb over.
- **Shields** were added alongside them for the attackers pushing behind the machines.
- **[[Horses]] can tow** the catapult, ballista, and siege tower to the target — the main reason these appear on the vehicle index.
- **Mortar artillery** (May 2026) extended this primitive-siege line with longer-range bombardment.

## Meta use (solo/duo/trio)

- **No-boom raiding**: crack a base before you can afford C4/rockets — huge for early-wipe and low-pop servers.
- **Tow logistics**: horse-tow a ballista or catapult across the map to a target, set up, and bombard.
- Slow and exposed during setup — best with a crew watching for defenders.
- Countered by base design (layered walls), turrets, and defenders shooting the crew.

## Related

[[Horses]] · [[Raiding]] · [[Workbench]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Snowmobiles
pages.body:
# Snowmobiles

The snow-biome land vehicle. A snowmobile only reaches full speed on **snow or sand** — on grass and rock it crawls — so it's a specialist for Arctic operations rather than a general-purpose ride.

## Stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | 500 |
| Seats | 1 (driver) — some variants seat 2 |
| Fuel | [[Low Grade Fuel]]; burns ~**1 LGF every 7 seconds** (~8.6/min) |
| Tank | 500 LGF |
| Best surface | snow / sand (full speed); slow elsewhere |
| Storage | small built-in inventory |
| Repair | hammer + metal fragments |

The **Tomaha** is the special cosmetic snowmobile skin (Arctic Pack item-store DLC); mechanically identical to the standard snowmobile.

## How to get one

- Complete the **blue keycard puzzle at the [[Arctic Research Base]]** monument — a snowmobile spawns there.
- Occasionally found parked in the snow biome on some servers.

## Riding notes

- Treats snow and sand as its racetrack; expect sluggish handling the moment you leave white terrain.
- Loud and exposed — no cover for the rider.
- Excellent for crossing the open Arctic snowfields where on-foot travel is slow and cold-exposed.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- Niche. If your base or your loot run is in the Arctic (e.g., around [[Arctic Research Base]]), it's the fastest fuel vehicle on that terrain.
- Otherwise a [[Motorbikes and Bicycles|motorbike]], [[Horses|horse]], or [[Modular Cars|car]] beats it everywhere off the snow.

## Related

[[Arctic Research Base]] · [[Motorbikes and Bicycles]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Submarines
pages.body:
# Submarines

Personal underwater attack craft, rented from the **Boat Vendor at [[Fishing Village]]**. Two models: a fast, nimble **solo sub** with one torpedo tube, and a tankier **duo sub** with two crew stations (one pilots, one fires). The stealthy way to reach underwater loot crates, sink boats, and (historically) attack [[Tugboat|tugboats]].

## Stats

| Stat | Solo Submarine | Duo Submarine |
|---|---|---|
| HP | 500 | ~600 |
| Crew | 1 (pilot + fires) | 2 (pilot + gunner) |
| Cost | **100 scrap** | **200 scrap** |
| Starting fuel | 50 [[Low Grade Fuel]] | 50 LGF |
| Torpedo tubes | 1 | 2 |
| Storage | small built-in box (~18 slots) | larger box |
| Oxygen | limited — surface to refill | limited |

Both rent from the **Boat Vendor at any [[Fishing Village]]** and come with 50 LGF.

## Torpedoes

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| Damage | **150 HP per hit** |
| Fire rate | 1 torpedo / **4 seconds** per tube |
| Range | ~**500 m** |
| To sink a [[Tugboat]] (historical) | ~4–6 torpedoes (some sources cite 12) |

Torpedoes are crafted/looted ammo. The duo sub doubles output (2 tubes), which is why it was the tugboat-hunting meta before tugboats were vaulted.

## Notes

- Submarines have a **sonar/ping** to spot nearby underwater entities and players.
- Watch your **oxygen** — you must surface periodically.
- The **[[Diver Propulsion Vehicle]]** is quieter and cheaper for pure travel; subs are for combat and carrying torpedoes.
- Excellent for raiding underwater labs / reaching submerged crates that the [[Naval Update]] and earlier underwater content added.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Cheapest combat watercraft**: 100 scrap for a torpedo platform.
- **Boat ambush**: torpedoes one-shot-chunk rowboats and threaten RHIBs from 500 m.
- **Stealth underwater loot runs**: dive to underwater crate spots others can't reach quickly.
- Duo sub is the coordinated-fire option; solo is the budget/escape pick.

## Related

[[Diver Propulsion Vehicle]] · [[RHIB]] · [[Rowboat]] · [[Deep Sea]] · [[Fishing Village]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Trains and Rail
pages.body:
# Trains and Rail

Rust's rail network runs both **underground** (the Train Tunnels dungeon) and **above-ground** (surface tracks linking monuments). You drive **workcarts** and **locomotives**, couple **wagons** behind them, and use the network for fast monument-to-monument logistics and for the [[Trainyard]] unloading event.

## Vehicle types

| Vehicle | HP | Seats | Fuel/min | Tank | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Workcart** | 1,000 | 1 (+ standing) | ~4 LGF | 500 → ~2 h | the basic driveable engine, found on rails |
| **Locomotive** | 2,000 | 1 | ~6 LGF | 500 → ~1h 23m | twice the HP, pulls ~17 wagons; above-ground |
| **Wagons** | per-type | — | none | — | coupled cargo/storage/seating cars |

Workcart engines take [[Low Grade Fuel]] and burn about **4 LGF/min at top speed** — extremely fuel-efficient compared to helicopters (30/min).

## Coupling

- **Coupling is automatic** when two train cars collide at low-to-moderate speed.
- **High-speed collisions do NOT couple** — they deal damage instead. Approach slowly.
- **Uncoupling is manual**: interact with the coupling point between cars.
- A locomotive can pull roughly **17 wagons** without losing speed; a workcart pulls about half that.
- Throttle has fixed target speeds (low/medium/high); acceleration and pulling power are affected by **gravity** (uphill = slower) and how many cars are coupled.

## Where to find / use

- **Above-ground rails**: surface tracks loop the map connecting monuments; workcarts and locomotives spawn on them.
- **Train Tunnels**: the underground dungeon network — workcarts spawn here; also home to the **Underground Loot** and tunnel dwellers.
- **[[Trainyard]]**: the monument tied to the rail system; the **Trainyard unloading** event has you drive a loot wagon to the unloading bay for rewards.
- No purchase — trains are found on the tracks, not bought from a vendor.

## Riding notes

- Driving controls: W/S throttle, the cart follows the track (no steering), brake to stop.
- Rails pass through tunnels and past monuments — a great way to move loot without exposure on roads, but ambush-prone at tunnel chokepoints.
- Code-lock options are limited; an unattended workcart can be commandeered.

## Meta use (solo/duo)

- **Bulk logistics**: couple a storage wagon behind a workcart to haul a base's worth of loot cheaply (4 LGF/min).
- **Tunnel travel**: move between underground entrances/exits fast, avoiding surface PvP.
- **Trainyard farm**: the unloading event is a reliable mid-tier loot source for a small team.

## Related

[[Trainyard]] · [[Low Grade Fuel]] · [[Modular Cars]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

pages.title: Tugboat
pages.body:
# Tugboat

> **STATUS: VAULTED / REMOVED in the February 2026 [[Naval Update]].** The tugboat was the test-bed that led to the player-built boat system; once [[Naval Ships|modular ships]] shipped, Facepunch disabled tugboat spawns and removed it from vanilla Rust. This page is kept for returning-player context — **you cannot get a tugboat on a current vanilla server.** It may return in modified form; treat as historical.

## What it was (July 2023 – February 2026)

The tugboat was a large, drivable steel boat and the **first vehicle in Rust you could build and deploy structures on** — effectively a **mobile floating base**. Players bolted down sleeping bags, boxes, turrets, and a Tugboat Tool Cupboard, then sailed their base around the ocean.

## Historical stats

| Stat | Value |
|---|---|
| HP | ~2,000–3,000 (very tanky) |
| Crew | 1 driver + anyone aboard the deck/cabin |
| Fuel | [[Low Grade Fuel]], heavy consumption (~5–19/min depending on source/era) |
| Features | sonar (spot nearby threats), buildable interior, code-lockable |
| How you got it | found floating in the ocean; claim by deploying a Tugboat Tool Cupboard |
| Raid to sink | ~4–6 [[Submarines|submarine]] torpedoes, or explosives on the hull |

## Why it was removed

The Feb 2026 [[Naval Update]] replaced the single fixed-design tugboat with a **full modular boat-building system** ([[Naval Ships]]) — players now build custom hulls with sails, engines, cannons, helms, and ramps at a **Boat Building Station**. The tugboat had proven the "mobile sea base" concept; the modular system superseded it.

## If you're a returning player

- Don't go looking for tugboats — they no longer spawn.
- The successor is the **[[Naval Ships|player-built modular boat]]**: more work to build, far more customizable, and capable of carrying a real base.
- For a quick mobile platform today, an [[RHIB]] (storage + 6 seats) is the closest off-the-shelf option.

## Related

[[Naval Ships]] · [[Naval Update]] · [[RHIB]] · [[Submarines]] · [[Vehicles (Rust)]]

# Vehicles (Rust)

Master reference for every player-usable vehicle in Rust as of the **June 2026 "Built Different" patch**. Each row links to a full page with purchase locations, fuel math, repair costs, and meta notes.

## Quick comparison table

| Vehicle | HP | Seats | Cost (where) | Fuel use | Full tank (500 LGF) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [[Minicopter]] | 750 | 2 | 750 scrap ([[Bandit Camp]] Airwolf) | 30 LGF/min | ~16m 39s | Fastest A→B in the game; explodes on death |
| [[Scrap Transport Helicopter]] | 1,000 | 2 + open bay | 1,250 scrap (Airwolf) | 30 LGF/min | ~16m 39s | Team/cargo hauler; can carry a vehicle in the bay |
| [[Attack Helicopter]] | 850 | 2 | 2,250 scrap (Airwolf) | 30 LGF/min | ~16m 39s | Gun turret + rocket pods; nerfed Nov 2025 |
| [[Hot Air Balloon]] | 1,500 (2,500 armored) | basket | 150 scrap (Airwolf) | 12 LGF/min | ~41m 40s | Wind-drifting; armor upgrade exists |
| [[Parachute]] | 5 uses | 1 | craft @ T2 (2 tarp, 2 sewing kits, 50 cloth) | — | — | Backpack slot; deploy >15 m height |
| [[Motorbikes and Bicycles\|Motorbike]] | 300 (350 sidecar) | 1 (2 sidecar) | free world spawn | 7 LGF/min | ~1h 11m | Spawns at road monuments |
| [[Motorbikes and Bicycles\|Pedal Bike]] | 250 (275 trike) | 1 (2 trike) | free world spawn | calories | — | Everywhere on roadsides |
| [[Horses]] | 400 | 1–2 | saddle 75/90 scrap (Ranch / Large Barn) | food | — | 42–58.5 km/h; tows [[Siege Weapons]] |
| [[Modular Cars]] | per-module | up to 6+ | free chassis on roadsides; parts vendored | varies w/ engine | varies | Needs engine parts + [[Modular Cars\|car lift]] |
| [[Snowmobiles]] | 300 | 2 | free ([[Arctic Research Base]], blue card) | ~8.6 LGF/min | ~58 min | Full speed only on snow/sand |
| [[Trains and Rail\|Workcart]] | 1,000 | 1 | free (rail network) | 4 LGF/min | ~2h 5m | Underground + above-ground rails |
| [[Trains and Rail\|Locomotive]] | 2,000 | 1 | free (above-ground rail) | 6 LGF/min | ~1h 23m | Pulls wagons; [[Trainyard]] unloading |
| [[Rowboat]] | 400 | 4 | 125 scrap ([[Fishing Village]]) | 6 LGF/min | ~1h 23m | 18-slot storage |
| [[RHIB]] | 500 | 6 | 300 scrap (Fishing Village) | 15 LGF/min | ~33m | 36-slot storage; can't survive [[Deep Sea]] anymore |
| [[Kayak]] | 200 | 2 | BP 50 scrap; craft 600 wood/100 cloth/75 frags | none (paddle) | — | Silent, free travel |
| [[Submarines\|Solo Sub]] | 500 | 1 | 100 scrap (Fishing Village) | 7 LGF/min | ~1h 11m | 1 torpedo tube, 18 slots |
| [[Submarines\|Duo Sub]] | ~600 | 2 | 200 scrap (Fishing Village) | 9 LGF/min | ~55m | 2 torpedo tubes; bigger box |
| [[Diver Propulsion Vehicle]] | — | 1 | craft @ T2: 15 HQM + 1 tech trash | LGF | — | Stealth underwater scooter (Oct 2024) |
| [[Player-Built Boats]] | per-block | unlimited mounts | Boat Building Station: 200 wood + 1 tarp @ T1 | engine LGF / sails free | — | Feb 2026 Naval Update; cannons, helms, anchors |
| [[PT Boat]] | high | multi | steal from scientists ([[Deep Sea]]) | heavy | — | Three .50 cal turrets fed by 5.56 ammo |
| [[Tugboat]] | 3,000 | crew | **REMOVED Feb 2026** | 19 LGF/min | ~26m | Vaulted by the Naval Update; may return |
| [[Siege Weapons]] | 250–1,000 | 0–1 | craft @ T1–T2 | ram uses LGF | — | Catapult, Ballista, Battering Ram, Siege Tower |

## Vendors at a glance

- **Airwolf Vendor, [[Bandit Camp]]** — Minicopter 750, Scrap Heli 1,250, Attack Heli 2,250, Hot Air Balloon 150 (all include ~75–100 starting [[Low Grade Fuel]]). Second floor sells medium-quality engine components for [[Modular Cars]].
- **Boat Vendor, [[Fishing Village]]** (small + large) — Rowboat 125, RHIB 300, Solo Sub 100, Duo Sub 200 (each with 50 LGF), Kayak blueprint 50 scrap.
- **Stable Shopkeeper, Ranch / Large Barn** — Single Horse Saddle 75 scrap, Double Saddle 90 scrap (claims a horse).
- NPC vendor prices **float with demand** since July 2024 — listed prices are baseline and can drift up on busy servers.

## Universal mechanics

- **Fuel**: everything motorized burns [[Low Grade Fuel]]; tank capacity is 500 (one stack) on nearly every vehicle.
- **Decay**: most vehicles start decaying after 10–45 min idle; outside decay is fast (3–24 h), inside a base most ground vehicles don't decay and helis last 48 h. Exact timers on each page.
- **Repair**: hammer + metal fragments (boats sometimes wood/cloth), 30 s after last damage. Helicopters **cannot be repaired in flight** since Nov 2025.
- **Shredding**: drive unwanted vehicles to the [[Junkyard]] magnet crane shredder for scrap — helicopters give roughly 200–500 scrap; bikes give 25–40.
- **Air defense**: [[SAM Site]]s and [[Auto Turret]]s target helicopters, balloons, and parachutists. The [[Homing Missile Launcher]] hard-counters air vehicles; since Nov 2025 only built-in flare launchers (not hand-thrown flares) can spoof it.
